Other Applicable Definitions

"Calculation Agent Determination of USD/IDR Reference Rate" means that the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner

"Cumulative Events" means that except as provided below, in no event shall the total number of consecutive calendar days during which either (i) valuation is deferred due to an Unscheduled Holiday, or (ii) a Valuation Postponement shall occur (or any combination of (i) and (ii)), exceed 14 consecutive calendar days in the aggregate. Accordingly, (x) if, upon the lapse of any such 14 day period, an Unscheduled Holiday shall have occurred or be continuing on the day following such period that otherwise would have been an IDR Business Day, then such day shall be deemed to be a Valuation Date, and (y) if, upon the lapse of any such 14 day period, a Price Source Disruption shall have occurred or be continuing on the day following such period on which the USD/IDR Reference Rate otherwise would be determined, then Valuation Postponement shall not apply and the USD/IDR Reference Rate shall be determined in accordance with the next disruption fallback.

"Fallback Reference Price" means SFEMC IDR Indicative Survey Rate (IDR02).

"Fallback Survey Valuation Postponement" means that, in the event that the Fallback Reference Price is not available on or before the 3rd IDR Business Day (or day that would have been a IDR Business Day but for an Unscheduled Holiday) succeeding the end of either (i) Valuation Postponement, (ii) Deferral Period for Unscheduled Holiday, or (iii) Cumulative Events, then the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined in accordance with the next applicable disruption fallback on such day. For the avoidance of doubt, Cumulative Events, if applicable, does not preclude postponement of valuation in accordance with this provision.

"IDR Business Day" means a day on which commercial banks and foreign exchange markets settle payments in Tokyo, New York, Singapore and Jakarta.

"IDR JISDOR" means for an IDR Valuation Date the IDR/USD weighted average spot rate in the interbank market based on traded IDR/USD spot foreign exchange transactions during a specified time period which are captured on a real time basis, expressed as the amount of Indonesian Rupiah per one USD, for settlement in two IDR Business Days, published by Bank Indonesia at approximately 10:00 a.m., Jakarta time, on that IDR Valuation Date as the Jakarta Interbank Spot Dollar Rate USD - IDR on Bank Indonesia's website (www.bi.go.id) or otherwise made available by Bank Indonesia (or its successor as administrator).

In the event that no such quotation appears on Bank Indonesia's website (www.bi.go.id("http://www.bi.go.id")) or otherwise is made available by Bank Indonesia (or its successor as administrator), (the "Price Source Disruption"), the USD/IDR Reference Rate shall be determined by the Calculation Agent applying the following disruption fallbacks in the order listed below:


   1)         Valuation Postponement; 
   2)         Fallback Reference Price; 
   3)         Fallback Survey Valuation Postponement; 
   4)         Calculation Agent Determination of USD/IDR Reference Rate. 

"IDR/JPY Rate" means, in respect of an IDR Valuation Date, the IDR/JPY exchange rate, expressed as the amount of JPY per one IDR, which is calculated by the Calculation Agent in accordance with the following formula and rounded to the nearest five decimal places with 0.000005 being rounded up:

USD/JPY Reference Rate divided by USD/IDR Reference Rate

"IDR Valuation Date" means the day that is five (5) Relevant Business Days prior to the relevant Fixed Rate Interest Payment Date or the Maturity Date, as applicable (a "Scheduled IDR Valuation Date"), or, if such day is an Unscheduled Holiday, the immediately following Relevant Business Day, in which case the related Fixed Rate Interest Payment Date or the Maturity Date, as applicable, shall be postponed to fall five (5) Relevant Business Days after such deferred IDR Valuation Date; provided that, if the IDR Valuation Date has not occurred on or before the fourteenth (14(th) ) consecutive day after the Scheduled IDR Valuation Date, then the next day after such fourteenth (14(th) ) day that would have been a Relevant Business Day but for the Unscheduled Holiday shall be deemed to be the IDR Valuation Date ("Deferral Period for Unscheduled Holiday").

"Maximum Days of Postponement" means 14 calendar days.

"Reference Dealers" means five banks active in the USD/JPY currency and foreign exchange market as selected by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

"SFEMC IDR Indicative Survey Rate (IDR02)" means the SFEMC IDR Indicative Survey Rate is determined pursuant to the SFEMC IDR Indicative Survey Rate Methodology updated as of March 4, 2014.

[Noteholders should note that the Calculation Agent acting directly or through a branch or an affiliate may be requested to provide a quotation or quotations from time to time for the purpose of determining the SFEMC IDR Indicative Survey Rate and such quotation may affect, materially or otherwise, the settlement of the Notes.]

"Unscheduled Holiday" means a day that is not a Relevant Business Day and the market was not aware of such fact (by means of a public announcement or by reference to other publicly available information) until a time later than 9:00 a.m. local time in the principal financial centre(s) of IDR five (5) Relevant Business Days prior to the Scheduled IDR Valuation Date.

"USD" means United States dollars.

"USD/IDR Reference Rate" means IDR JISDOR

"USD/JPY Reference Rate" means the mid rate of USD/JPY, expressed as the number of JPY per one USD, published on the Reuters Screen "JPNU" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate) as of 12:00 p.m., Tokyo time on the applicable IDR Valuation Date, as determined by the Calculation Agent.

In the event that no such quotation appears on the Reuters Screen "JPNU" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate), the USD/JPY Reference Rate shall be determined by the Calculation Agent by requesting quotations for mid rate of USD/JPY foreign exchange rate at or about 12:00 p.m. Tokyo time on the first (1st) IDR Business Day following the relevant IDR Valuation Date from Reference Dealers.

If five or four quotations are provided as requested, the USD/JPY Reference Rate will be the arithmetic mean of the remaining three or two such quotations, as the case may be, for such rate provided by the Reference Dealers, after disregarding the highest such quotation and the lowest such quotation (provided that, if two or more such quotations are the highest such quotations, then only one of such quotations shall be disregarded, and if two or more such quotations are the lowest quotations, then only one of such lowest quotations will be disregarded).

If only three or two such quotations are provided as requested, the USD/JPY Reference Rate shall be determined as described above except that the highest and lowest quotations will not be disregarded.

If none or only one of the Reference Dealers provides such quotation, the USD/JPY Reference Rate will be determined by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

"Valuation Postponement" means, for purposes of obtaining the USD/IDR Reference Rate, that the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined on the IDR Business Day first succeeding the day on which the Price Source Disruption ceases to exist, unless the Price Source Disruption continues to exist (measured from the date that, but for the occurrence of the Price Source Disruption, would have been the IDR Valuation Date) for a consecutive number of calendar days equal to the Maximum Days of Postponement. In such event, the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined on the next IDR Business Day after the Maximum Days of Postponement in accordance with the next applicable disruption fallback.

title: EM ASIA  FX -Rupiah hits 2-month peak after Jokowi wins presidential election
text:
(Updates prices. For earlier report, click on )               

SINGAPORE, July 23 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah rose to its highest level in two months on Wednesday after Joko "Jokowi" Widodo was declared the winner of the presidential election, although its gains were tempered by suspected intervention.               

The rupiah rose more than 0.9 percent at one point and touched a high of around 11,485 versus the dollar  , its strongest since late May, according to Thomson Reuters data.               

As the currency rallied, a spokesman for Indonesia's central bank said it will intervene in the foreign exchange market to stabilise the rupiah.               

Traders said the central bank was detected intervening to buy the dollar versus the rupiah, helping to limit the currency's gains.               

The rupiah last stood at 11,510 to the dollar, still up around 0.7 percent on the day.               

The election result could spur an extended relief rally and eventually buoy the rupiah to levels around 11,300 or 11,400, said Mirza Baig, head of foreign exchange and interest rate strategy Asia for BNP Paribas in Singapore.               

"But I would expect that the Bank Indonesia appetite for dollars will be there. Bank Indonesia likely wants to rebuild its FX reserves," Baig said, adding that the rupiah may return to a range of 11,500 to 11,800 in a few months.               

Indonesia's Elections Commission, known as KPU, said on Tuesday that Jokowi had won the July 9 presidential election over his rival, former general Prabowo Subianto.               

The head of Prabowo's legal team said on Wednesday that Prabowo plans to challenge the result in the Constitutional Court. The challenge had been widely expected, but many analysts believe it would be near impossible for Prabowo to overturn the result of the election.               

"Jokowi's margin of over 8 million votes should serve as a substantial buffer in any court dispute," Wellian Wiranto, an economist for OCBC Bank, said in a research note.               

Other Asian currencies also mostly pushed higher, including the Malaysian ringgit and the Philippine peso .               

Investor interest in relatively high-yielding assets has been seen as a source of support for emerging Asian currencies recently, despite lingering worries about geopolitical tensions.

title: Indonesia  c.bank says it will  intervene  in  forex  market to stabilize rupiah
text:
JAKARTA, July 23 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank spokesman says Bank Indonesia (BI) will intervene in the foreign exchange market to stabilize the rupiah a day after Joko "Jokowi" Widodo was named winner of this month's presidential election.

"BI will intervene so the fluctuations due to election sentiment are not too sharp," Peter Jacobs, BI spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.

The rupiah strengthened to as much as 11,485 rupiah per dollar compared to its Tuesday close of 11,590. (Reporting by Gayatri Suroyo and Adriana Nina Kusuma, Editing by Jonathan Thatcher and Richard Borsuk)

title: Indonesia  c.bank says ready to  intervene  if rupiah fall is "outside fundamentals"
text:
JAKARTA, July 22 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank is ready to intervene in the market if the weakening of the rupiah currency is "outside fundamentals", a spokesman said on Tuesday.

The rupiah is currently trading around 11,590, down 0.2 percent on the day.

Indonesian shares fell more than 2 percent early Tuesday afternoon on worries after the likely loser in presidential elections attempted to delay announcement of the official result, due later in the afternoon. (Reporting by Adriana Nina Kusuma; Writing by Eveline Danubrata; Editing by Richard Borsuk)

1. The EU has adopted a Directive regarding the taxation of savings income (the "Savings Directive"). The Savings Directive requires Member States (as defined below) to provide to the tax authorities of other Member States details of payments of interest and other similar income paid by a person to an individual in another Member State, except that Austria and Luxembourg will instead impose a withholding system for a transitional period unless during such period they elect otherwise.

The Bank undertakes that it will ensure that it maintains a paying agent in a country which is a member of the European Union (a "Member State") that will not be obliged to withhold or deduct tax pursuant to the Savings Directive.

The following supplements the discussion under the "Tax Matters" section of the Prospectus regarding the U.S. federal income tax treatment of the Notes, and is subject to the limitations and exceptions set forth therein. Any tax disclosure in the Prospectus or this pricing supplement is of a general nature only, is not exhaustive of all possible tax considerations and is not intended to be, and should not be construed to be, legal, business or tax advice to any particular prospective investor. Each prospective investor should consult its own tax advisor as to the particular tax consequences to it of the acquisition, ownership, and disposition of the Notes, including the effects of applicable U.S. federal, state, and local tax laws and non-U.S. tax laws and possible changes in tax laws.

Due to a change in law since the date of the Prospectus, the second paragraph of "-Payments of Interest" under the United States Holders section should be read as follows: "Interest paid by the Bank on the Notes constitutes income from sources outside the United States and will, depending on the circumstances, be "passive" or "general" income for purposes of computing the foreign tax credit."

Information with Respect to Foreign Financial Assets. Owners of "specified foreign financial assets" with an aggregate value in excess of $50,000 (and in some circumstances, a higher threshold) may be required to file an information report with respect to such assets with their tax returns. "Specified foreign financial assets" may include financial accounts maintained by foreign financial institutions (which may include the Notes), as well as the following, but only if they are not held in accounts maintained by financial institutions: (i) stocks and securities issued by non-United States persons, (ii) financial instruments and contracts held for investment that have non-United States issuers or counterparties, and (iii) interests in foreign entities. Holders are urged to consult their tax advisors regarding the application of this reporting obligation to their ownership of the Notes.

Medicare Tax. A U.S. holder that is an individual or estate, or a trust that does not fall into a special class of trusts that is exempt from such tax, will be subject to a 3.8% tax (the "Medicare tax") on the lesser of (1) the U.S. holder's "net investment income" for the relevant taxable year and (2) the excess of the U.S. holder's modified adjusted gross income for the taxable year over a certain threshold (which in the case of individuals will be between $125,000 and $250,000, depending on the individual's circumstances). A holder's net investment income will generally include its gross interest income and its net gains from the disposition of Notes, unless such interest payments or net gains are derived in the ordinary course of the conduct of a trade or business (other than a trade or business that consists of certain passive or trading activities). If you are a U.S. holder that is an individual, estate or trust, you are urged to consult your tax advisors regarding the applicability of the Medicare tax to your income and gains in respect of your investment in the Notes.

Investors intending to purchase the Notes should consult with their tax and financial advisors to ensure that the intended purchase meets the investment objective before making such purchase.

There are various risks associated with the Notes including, but not limited to, exchange rate risk, price risk and liquidity risk. Investors should consult with their own financial, legal and accounting advisors about the risks associated with an investment in these Notes, the appropriate tools to analyze that investment, and the suitability of the investment in each investor's particular circumstances. Holders of the Notes should also consult with their professional tax advisors regarding tax laws applicable to them.

Payment of each Interest Amount and the Redemption Amount will be based on the Applicable Rate, which is a measure of the rate of exchange between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD. Currency exchange rates are volatile and will affect the holder's return. In addition, the government of Indonesia can from time to time intervene in the foreign exchange market. These interventions or other governmental actions could adversely affect the value of the Notes, as well as the yield (in USD terms) on the Notes and the amount payable at maturity or upon acceleration. Even in the absence of governmental action directly affecting currency exchange rates, political or economic developments in Indonesia or elsewhere could lead to significant and sudden changes in the exchange rate between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD.

The Indonesian Rupiah is an emerging market currency. Emerging market currencies may be subject to particularly substantial volatility, as well as to government actions including currency controls, devaluations and other matters which could materially and adversely affect the value of the Notes.

The methodologies for determining the Applicable Rate may result in a Redemption Amount (or Early Redemption Amount, as the case may be) of the Notes, or an Interest Amount on the Notes, being significantly less than anticipated or less than what an alternative methodology for determining the IDR-USD exchange rate would yield.

0341 GMT [Dow Jones] Gold appears to be facing resistance at $1,323/oz, while support sits at $1,312/oz in the short-term, writes Howie Lee, an investment analysts with Phillip Futures, in a report. Both the upper and lower bands were tested overnight, he says. Based on technical indicators, there is a "chance that gold may exhibit a huge breakout in the near future," Lee says. Dovish comments last week from U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen about U.S. economic growth, downbeat economic data from the U.S. overnight and geopolitical tensions in Iraq, could help provide a floor to precious metal prices. Spot gold is at $1,316.20/oz, down $2.20 from its previous close. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com; Twitter: @ArpanMukherjee)

0339 GMT [Dow Jones] Political risk consultancy Trusted Sources is skeptical that a strong rally in Thailand equities is justified after the May 22 coup, while narrowing polls in Indonesia's presidential race is reason to go neutral on the country, says chief economist Larry Brainard. "If Prabowo prevails and wins we would see a lot of people taking money off the table, particularly in the fixed income area. If Jokowi wins people will still be cautious but you'll see certain sectors doing well" such as infrastructure, Mr. Brainard says, referring to Indonesia's two presidential candidates. However, he is not fazed by recent falls in the rupiah triggered by oil price rises following a conflict in Iraq. "It's basically a short-term trade and I think we should just look through that," said Mr. Brainard. (jake.watts@wsj.com; @jmwatts_)

0323 GMT [Dow Jones] Thailand's benchmark stock index will likely trade sideways in the short term but as Thailand's economic fundamentals begin to catch up with expectations about a recovery in 2014 and 2015, the longer term outlook is more positive, KGI Securities says. "SET has no near-term conviction and may continue to consolidate, amid slowing foreign equity inflows and [the] absence of fresh local macro news," the brokerage says. It recommends investors to accumulate stocks on any dips, forecasting a 1500-1550 range for the third quarter of 2014. The SET trades 0.3% higher early Thursday at 1473, or 4.1% higher in the month-to-date. (jake.watts@wsj.com; @jmwatts_)

0317 GMT [Dow Jones] Narrowing polls in Indonesia support the case for shorting the rupiah, Nomura says in a note. "The latest surveys highlight an increasing uncertainty regarding the presidential election outcome," it says. "In our view, this most recent increase in political uncertainty also raises the risk of capital outflows, especially given the considerable accumulation of foreign bond and equity positioning since end-2013." Nomura says Bank Indonesia may step up its foreign exchange intervention to stop the rupiah falling much further, but with weak reserves, BI will likely adopt "a relatively light-handed approach." The rupiah has depreciated 3.7% against the U.S. dollar in the month-to-date, far more than most other regional currencies, which are mostly stronger or flat. (jake.watts@wsj.com; @jmwatts_)

0308 GMT [Dow Jones] As the rupiah weakens, investors can be expected to show interest in companies earning U.S. dollars, says Trimegah Securities. It is most bullish on oil and gas services stocks, such as PT Wintermar Offshore Marine (WINS.JK), PT Logindo Samudramakmur (LEAD.JK) and PT Elnusa (ELSA.JK). It recommends investors exercise caution with companies with rupiah earnings but U.S. dollar or Euro debt, such as PT Japfa Comfeed (JPFA.JK). The rupiah trades 0.2% stronger against the U.S. dollar Thursday, but has lost 3.5% in the month to date. This comes as oil price increases due to conflict in Iraq turn investors away out of concern that import costs will rise and Indonesia's current-account deficit will become more of a drag on growth. (jake.watts@wsj.com; @jmwatts_)

0306 GMT [Dow Jones] Australian job vacancies rose for the second quarter in a row in the three months to the end of May, which should lend some encouragement to the Reserve Bank of Australia which, recently, has been downbeat on the outlook for job creation. Job vacancies rose 2.5% over the quarter, building on a 2.8% rise in the prior three months, according to government statistics. RBA Assistant Governor Chris Kent said last week he expects unemployment to remain elevated for the next two years. (james.glynn@wsj.com)

0305 GMT [Dow Jones] The Nikkei is up 0.3% at 15314.74 midday. Volume is relatively light, under 1.0 billion shares. "The speech by Prime Minister Abe (made Tuesday evening) turned out to be a total 'non-event', and so post-event activity (Wednesday and Thursday) is also very subdued," says an equity trading director at a European brokerage. "Abe's economic revitalization plan lacked a lot of detail, so investors are keen to see, for example, the exact amount by which corporate tax rates will be lowered, how the revenue will be made up elsewhere, and by precisely how much the government pension body (GPIF) will increase its exposure to stocks. Valuation-wise, Japan shares still lag their overseas counterparts, so this kind of incremental buy pressure could continue for weeks or more." (bradford.frischkorn@wsj.com)

0257 GMT [Dow Jones] China Gas Holdings' (0384.HK) full-year earnings released late Wednesday contained few surprises but its bullish long-term guidance, such as a forecast for a 24% increase in natural gas sales this year, has investors abuzz. "Growth prospects remain bright," Jefferies says, noting two pipelines are set to be operational this year, boosting volumes. Analysts back their buy rating on the stock and raise their price target by about a quarter, to HK$15.90. Shares rise 3.5% to HK$14.36. (mia.lamar@wsj.com)

0250 GMT [Dow Jones] Southeast Asian stocks trade mostly higher early Thursday, led by the Philippines PSEi, which heads for a fresh 12-month high and is up 0.4% in line with improved sentiment in the wider region. Gainers include Philex Mining Corp. (PX.PH) and Jolibee Foods Corp. (JFC.PH), up 2.3% and 1.8% respectively. Elsewhere, Indonesia's JSX and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index gain 0.3% each. Malaysia's KLCI is down 0.2%. On the data front, Singapore reports industrial production data for May later in the day. "We are forecasting a slower growth rate of 3.9% year-on-year in Singapore's May IP, compared to the average of 8.4% year-on-year in the first four months of this year," UOB says. "The unexpected contraction in Singapore's May non-oil domestic exports is likely to show up in the manufacturing numbers today." (jake.watts@wsj.com; @jmwatts_)

0245 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/CNY falls slightly to track a lower central parity set by the PBOC. The pair is at 6.2314 vs 6.2344 at Wednesday's close, after the central parity is set at 6.1538 vs 6.1555 Wednesday, tracking the dollar's broad weakness overseas. "There are still substantial amounts of dollar purchases from importers, but they failed to support the dollar's prices today," says a Shanghai-based foreign bank trader. Offshore, one-year USD/CNY NDFs are down at 6.2390/6.2440 from 6.2412/6.2458 late Wednesday. (wynne.wang@dowjones.com)

0244 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan government bonds are higher in thin trade, mostly reflecting overnight gains in U.S. Treasurys, says a local trader. Market participants are focussed on the local central bank's quarterly policy meeting later Thursday. Most people don't expect the central bank to change its monetary policy, but will seek cues from the central bank governor's comments about the outlook for inflation. "We will watch whether the governor thinks the rising inflationary pressure is temporary or not," the trader adds. The five-year bond yield is at 1.1825% vs 1.2020% late Wednesday, the trader tips the yield to trade between 1.1800% and 1.2000% for the session. The 10-year bond yield is at 1.6000% vs 1.6200% Wednesday. (fanny.liu@wsj.com)

The persistent biddish tone in USD/IDR is likely to keep the Indonesian central bank on its toes, ready to intervene. title: Rupiah Drops:  Central Bank  Support, Prabowo Closes Gap -- Barron's Blog
text:
The Indonesian rupiah fell to the lowest level since February today, trading at 12,135 per dollar this morning. The iShares MSCI Indonesia ETF (EIDO) fell 0.8%.

The decline is partly explained by Bank Indonesia's decision to temporarily "undervalue" rupiah to boost exports. But the newest election polls are also at play. Presidential candidate Prabowo Subianto is narrowing his lead and may even be slightly ahead of the frontrunner Joko Widodo, known as "Jokowi", two weeks ahead of the presidential election on July 9.

The PolComm survey, released yesterday, shows that the margin of victory for Jokowi has shrunk to just 3.1%. About 10.3% of voters were still undecided. Jokowi earlier in the year had a 20% lead.

Oddly, and unique in Indonesia, some of the election polls have been withheld from publication, for fear that Jokowi voters may shift away to Mr. Prabowo. The Sydney Morning Herald reports:

A number of sources contacted by Fairfax Media have confirmed that three credible polling organisations have now measured the gap between the two candidates at either within the margin of error, or with Mr Prabowo in the lead.

A Prabowo win may trigger capital outflow and put pressure on rupiah, which Bank Indonesia will tolerate anyhow, according to Nomura Securities:

This most recent increase in political uncertainty also raises the risk of capital outflows, especially given the considerable accumulation of foreign bond and equity positioning since end-2013. We note that foreign investors have invested about USD3.8bn in local equities and an additional USD7.5bn in local government bonds since the beginning of 2014. Having said that, there is a risk that Bank Indonesia (BI) could step up its FX intervention to arrest further IDR depreciation. However, given the relatively weak FX reserves adequacy ratios (about six months of import coverage, or 2x short-term external debt), we think BI is likely to adopt a relatively light-handed approach to lean against IDR depreciation rather than attempting to stem it. This is also consistent with yesterday"s comments from BI officials that the central bank is comfortable with the recent IDR weakness, as it supports exports competitiveness while curbing imports demand.

0148 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/IDR has breached the round-figure trading barrier at 12,000, fuelled by broad U.S. dollar strength arising from risk aversion. Currently at a 4-month low of 12,040 to the greenback, the rupiah may weaken further on stoploss orders being activated. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0147 GMT [Dow Jones] The difficulties facing mining services companies amid a broad decline in commodity prices could get worse if financiers take fright at the number of corporate failures in the sector, says Deloitte. Forge Group was among the highest-profile casualties, calling in insolvency specialists and laying off 1,300 workers in February after losing the support of its lenders in the wake of cost overruns and profit warnings on two power projects. Deloitte says financiers may soon start to review the structure of performance guarantee facilities in place with mining services firms. "Cash-backed guarantees may emerge and create working capital pressures," Deloitte says. Its Mining Service Index fell by 2.05 points in 1Q 2014 to 85.62 versus 4Q 2013, underperfoming the top 200 companies listed on Australia's share market. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)

0117 GMT [Dow Jones] The Nikkei is down 0.5% at 15295.57 on light volume, following an overnight Wall Street selloff and on the back of a slightly weaker dollar. "Stocks are long overdue for consolidation," says CSLA equity strategist Nicholas Smith. He downplays any link between this and Prime Minister Abe's 'Third Arrow' economic revitalization speech delivered last evening. "Most of what was said had long been factored into the market, including general talk of cutting corporate taxes and boosting public pension fund investment in stocks. What Abe did not mention was detail, for example, on how the 72% of companies that do not pay taxes will be treated to offset the revenue fall, or over what time frame the GPIF (Government Pension Investment Fund) will move into equities. I suppose we'll just have to wait to find out." (bradford.frischkorn@wsj.com)

0116 GMT [Dow Jones] The final investigative report about the fatal 2013 crash of an Asiana Airlines Inc. (020560.SE) plane while trying to land at San Francisco international Airport is likely to renew debate about evacuation delays and mistakes by emergency crews. The National Transportation Safety Board on Tuesday concluded that a controversial, 90-second delay in evacuating the fiery wreck was partly due to the captain's initial order to wait for the arrival of emergency responders. The board also found that the cabin crew's "disorientation and confusion" contributed to the delay. In describing the actions of emergency responders--whose vehicles repeatedly rolled over the body of a victim on the tarmac--the safety board concluded that crews needed more specialized training. Investigators called for more training to help firefighters use certain equipment designed to pierce aircraft fuselages. The NTSB also urged creation of specific guidance or protocols intended to prevent victims from being inadvertently run over by rescue vehicles. Amid the confusion and turmoil in San Francisco, firefighters failed to check on the condition of the sole victim sprawled on the tarmac. In other accidents, according to the board, there may be many more injured people near the airplane "at risk of being struck or rolled over by a vehicle" during rescue operations. (andy.pasztor@wsj.com)

Dovish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairwoman Janet Yellen about the pace of economic growth last week boosted gold prices above the psychological $1,300/oz level. Escalating violence in Iraq has also helped to support gold prices. Spot gold is at $1,318.77/oz, down 23 cents from its previous close, and silver is at $20.91/oz, down 2 cents. "Rio currently sees diamond demand running at roughly double mined supply," Fagan says in a note. "Little detail was given on how this shortfall is expected to be met, although it would imply material upside to current prices given our belief that stockpiles at De Beers and Alrosa are relatively modest," he says. 17:36 EDT - An "unexpected bout of risk aversion" has caused short-term damage to AUD/USD and NZD/USD, says Westpaccurrency strategist Imre Speizer. He says initial optimism fueled by some strong US data were reversed later in the session on geopolitical concerns after over Iraq hit nerves. Speizer notes the only thing on the local calendar is Australia's RBA Deputy Governor Lowe's speech in Melbourne and China's consumer confidence survey. AUD/USD last at 0.9369 from 0.9412 late Tuesday in Sydney. NZD/USD at 0.8676 from 0.8720 late Tuesday in Wellington. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com; @lucy_craymer)

17:23 EDT - The New Zealand Debt Management Office's plan to issue a new 2027 government bond helps steepen the yield curve, says BNZ strategist Kymberly Martin. The yield on New Zealand 2023 bonds push up 2 bps to 4.46%. Ten-year swap push 4 bps higher to 4.90%. Martin says the increase in interest rate swaps may also have been "assisted by a lull in the recent flurry of Kauri sovereign, supranational and agency issuance." Martin adds the firm continues to see hedging value in 2- to 4-year swaps. "We see current 'fair value' on 2-year swap around 4.40%, some 20 bps above current levels." Five-year swap sits at 4.58%. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com; @lucy_craymer)

17:05 EDT - NZD/USD is lower as the greenback performs well overnight following upbeat consumer confidence and new home sales report, says ANZ. "The US data trend remains broadly strong, and some USD strength should be expected." ANZ adds, however, that despite the trend, the third reading on 1Q US GDP and May durable goods orders due later in the global day are both expected to remain subdued. Pair is at 0.8673 from 0.8720 late Tuesday in New Zealand. ANZ expects the pair to trade in a short-term range of 0.8660 to 0.8725. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com; @lucy_craymer)

title: Bank  Indonesia  Hints at No  Intervention  -- Market Talk
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0516 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia views the current USD/IDR level as good for both exports and imports, suggesting the central bank won't intervene in the market. "The 11,300-11,800 level is the appropriate level that will provide incentive for both exporters and importers," senior deputy governor Mirza Adityaswara says. USD/IDR is now at 11,790. The pair has been creeping up since last month due to a combination of political uncertainties ahead of next month's presidential election and seasonal dollar demand. But the central bank is seldom suspected of selling dollars to curb the pair. (Farida.husna@wsj.com)

0514 GMT [Dow Jones] The bullish technical bias for USD/IDR - a negative indicator for the rupiah - will persist if the dollar manages to stay above 11,800 by the end of the day. Unless this technical floor for the dollar is broken, the rupiah will struggle to recoup from sharp losses - amounting to as much as 4.7% against the U.S. dollar - sustained since May 19. Economists have recently warned on Indonesia's weakening economic fundamentals - which could hurt foreign investors' appeal for Indonesian assets. Last week, the Indonesian central bank governor said there will be no change in its tight policy stance this Thursday. USD/IDR is now 11,800 from its Tuesday close of 11,805. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0509 GMT [Dow Jones] Barclays says the gain in Malaysia's April industrial production is consistent with the turnaround in exports, which surged 19% on-year in April, and supports the view that economic growth will remain strong in 2014. The house notes that the industrial production indicator points to sustained growth in Malaysia's GDP, for which it recently raised its forecast to 5.7% in 2014 from 5.4% previously; this compares with 2013's 4.2% growth. Barclays forecasts 2Q GDP at 5.7%. April IP grew 4.2% on-year, propped up by a pickup in mining sector, which cushioned slower growth in electricity generation and manufacturing output. Exports surged . (jason.ng@wsj.com)

0503 GMT [Dow Jones] Vietnam said Wednesday its borrowing from China is not significant and its economy doesn't rely on Chinese loans. Chinese investors hold only 0.33% of Vietnamese stocks, Finance Minister Dinh Tien Dung said in response to lawmakers' call to reduce Vietnam's reliance on Chinese capital. Tension between Vietnam and China has risen to the highest level in years following the deployment early last month of a Chinese oil rig in contested waters near Vietnam's coast. (trong-khanh.vu@wsj.com)

0450 GMT [Dow Jones] Hong Kong stocks decline in lockstep with most other markets in Asia as the World Bank trims global growth expectations, cutting its China forecast for this year from 7.7% to 7.6% - which "will depend on the success of rebalancing efforts." China's reform efforts are having the right effect on growth but their piecemeal approach is harming sentiment, says Goldman Sachs: "Although a number of important policy actions have been adopted, reform measures have not been rolled out as aggressively as many had hoped," the bank says. However, Goldman expects a turning point has been reached. The Hang Seng Index is down 0.3% at 23238.88, with China Mobile (0941.HK) leading declines on the index. Casino stocks rally as Barclays and Credit Suisse say some companies in the sector look undervalued. (gregor.hunter@wsj.com; Twitter: @gregorhunter)

0439 GMT [Dow Jones] Base metals are trading mixed after the World Bank overnight cut its global economic growth forecast to 2.8% for the year, compared with a 3.2% forecast in January. The bank says that emerging markets are expected to face headwinds due to an unwillingness to put in place policy changes in many countries. Slower global economic growth could weigh on demand and price outlook for metals. In copper, the market awaits further news on the ongoing probe by Chinese authorities into fraudulent metal financing deals. LME 3-month copper prices have fallen 2.5% since the start of the month as Chinese authorities investigate whether companies used the same copper stocks held in the port of Qingdao as collateral for obtaining multiple loans. LME 3-month copper is at $6,703/ton, up $28, while nickel is at $18,700/ton, down $75 from its previous close. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com; Twitter: @ArpanMukherjee)

0435 GMT [Dow Jones] A bidding war is brewing on Aquila Resources (AQA.AU) after sources confirmed to the Wall Street Journal that Mineral Resources (MIN.AU) bought at least a 12.1% stake at A$3.75/share, well above the A$3.40/share cash bid from Boasteel and Aurizon (AZJ.AU). Aquila says it welcomes recognition that the value of the company's shares is well in excess of the current bid from Boasteel/Aurizon. Mineral Resources may lack the firepower on its own to purchase Aquila, but it would make sense to have a seat at the table, particularly given its mining services, contracting and processing operations. Odds are the Baosteel/Aurizon bid will need to be sweetened considerably to get it across the line. MIN last down 2.2% at A$10.14. AQA last up 3.2% at A$3.60. (david.rogers@wsj.com; Twitter: @DavidRogersWSJ)

0431 GMT [Dow Jones] Expectations that crude supplies in the U.S. declined in the week to June 6 remains the key fundamental support for prices, Timothy Evans, energy futures specialist at Citigroup, says in a report. The closely watched survey from the Energy Information Administration is due at 1030AM EDT. Analysts expect the EIA to report that supplies fell by 1.7 million barrels in the week ended June 6, a Wall Street Journal survey shows. However, if the EIA reports a surprise rise in supplies, the data could "spark" some profit taking. July Nymex crude is at $104.48/bbl, up 13 cents from its previous close. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com; Twitter: @ArpanMukherjee)

0427 GMT [Dow Jones] Chinese government plans to link trading between the Hong Kong and Shanghai stock exchanges have caught the attention of global investors, who will be watching carefully to see whether access to Chinese capital markets is becoming more straightforward, said Chin-Ping Chia, MSCI's head of equity research and managing director for Asia Pacific. "Investors would prefer simpler ways to access the market and a simpler system," he said. "We do believe that there's continuous momentum, and the Hong Kong-Shanghai connection is one prime example of this." However, the mechanism only covers a fraction of Chinese stocks, and does not include the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, so MSCI will watch how the scheme is expanded over time, he added. MSCI said it would exclude Chinese A-shares from its Emerging Markets Index today after consulting with fund managers. (gregor.hunter@wsj.com; Twitter: @gregorhunter)

0421 GMT [Dow Jones] The New Zealand dollar is pushing higher against the USD, the AUD and the EUR ahead of Thursday's central bank rate decision. "It's hard to see the Kiwi going lower given negative deposit rates in Europe while we are hiking," says Tim Kelleher, ASB's head of FX institutional sales. The market is widely expecting the central bank to lift interest rates by 25 bps to 3.25% so the main focus will be on the accompanying statement and any clues about when the next rate increase might come. Kelleher notes the RBNZ in March indicated more aggressive interest rate increases than what the market is now expecting, so if it doesn't change that track the Kiwi will likely gain. If that's the case, the NZD/USD could head to 0.8650 or 0.8710, Kelleher says. The pair is at 0.8548. (rebecca.howard@wsj.com; Twitter: @FarroHoward)

0419 GMT [Dow Jones] Spotty hedge-fund performance hasn't stopped investors from ploughing cash into the strategy this year--May marked the fourth straight month of positive inflows of investor cash, according to industry tracker Eurekahedge. It estimates that nearly $60 billion has been added so far this year even as hedge funds globally are sitting on just a 1.9% gain year-to-date. The MSCI World index, by comparison, is up 2.6% through May. (mia.lamar@wsj.com)

0417 GMT [Dow Jones] Palladium prices are poised for a "steep pullback" in the coming weeks on profit-taking once it reaches $860/oz, ANZ says in a report. Spot palladium, which rose 1.4% overnight and has risen around 19% since the start of the year, is at its highest level since February 2011. Wage talks overnight to resolve a five-month old strike in South Africa ended in a deadlock. South Africa produces about 40% of the world's supply of the metal, which is mainly used in automobile exhaust filters. Palladium net long positions, or bets that prices will rise, are at historical highs, ANZ says. Total holdings in palladium ETFs stood just shy of 2.8 million ounces at the end of May, exceeding the annual production of Russia, Commerzbank says. Spot palladium is at $850/oz, down $2 from its previous close. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com; Twitter: @ArpanMukherjee)

title: EM ASIA  FX -Won near 6-year high on inflows, rupiah NDFs up as elections start
text:
* Won jumps on stocks inflows, offshore funds short-covering
    * S.Korea intervention spotted, but not so strong - traders
    * Indonesia kicks off parliament vote, PDI-P may win
    * Taiwan dollar near 3-month high on inflows, exporters

 (Adds text, updates prices)
    By Jongwoo Cheon
    SINGAPORE, April 9 (Reuters) - The South Korean won hit a
near six-year high on Wednesday thanks to capital inflows,
leading gains among emerging Asian currencies, while the
Indonesian rupiah rose in offshore markets as parliamentary
elections started.
    The won rose as much as 1.2 percent to 1,040.1
per dollar, its strongest since August 2008.
    Foreign investors extended a buying spree in Seoul's main
stock market to an 11th consecutive session, purchasing
a net 2.5 trillion won ($2.4 billion) worth of stocks during the
period, according to Korea Exchange data. Offshore funds dumped
dollar holdings to stop losses.
    South Korea's foreign exchange authorities were suspected of
buying dollars to prevent the won from strengthening past 1,040,
but the intervention was not seen as strong, traders said.
    Investors had built up short positions in the won on caution
that the authorities may keep the currency weaker than 1,050,
but the finance ministry or the central bank had not been
spotted intervening, traders said.
    "It is less necessary to keep the won weaker as the
government is seeking a balanced development in exports and
domestic consumption," said Jeong My-young, research head at
Samsung Futures in Seoul.
    South Korean President Park Geun-hye promised to shift
economic policy away from supporting big exporters towards
lifting domestic-market-oriented industries and household
income.
    Korea Inc. is also now less vulnerable to foreign exchange
rates than in the past as major exporters such as Samsung
Electronics Co Ltd and Hyundai Motor Co 
are producing part of their goods outside the country.
    Big exporters have focused more on expanding overseas
production bases than local factories. Hyundai plans to build
its fourth plant in China for about 1 trillion won, a source
said last month. 
    In 2013, the won rose 1.4 percent thanks to a sustained
current account surplus and capital inflows, while most emerging
Asian currencies fell on worries that the Federal Reserve's
stimulus reduction may cause fund outflows from the region.
    The won's outperformance last year boosted caution over
possible intervention and some investors took profits in 2014.
    Some analysts have said that the caution had been excessive,
given data showing South Korea's exports were still fine and the
current account remained in surplus.
    Technically, the won is seen having room to strengthen to
1,032, its low in March 2008, analysts said.
    Still, the won is considered overbought with the 14-day
dollar/won relative strength index at 28.3, prompting some
investors to look for chances to book profits. A reading below
the 30 threshold indicates the dollar has been sold excessively.
    
    RUPIAH NDFS
    The rupiah rose in non-deliverable forwards (NDFs)
 markets as Indonesians began voting for a new
parliament. 
    The rupiah's one-month NDFs rose 0.5 percent
to 11,195 per dollar, the strongest since Nov. 1.
    The opposition Indonesian Democratic Party-Struggle (PDI-P)
is likely to dominate in the elections, opinion polls showed.
    That bolstered the chances of a victory by its popular
candidate, Jakarta Governor Joko Widodo, widely know as Jokowi,
in a presidential election. 
    Potential wins by the PDI-P and Jokowi are likely to attract
more foreign funds, analysts have said.
    
    TAIWAN DOLLAR
    The Taiwan dollar rose as much as 0.8 percent to
30.030 to the U.S. dollar, its strongest since Jan. 14, tracking
the won's strength.
    The island's currency found more support from inflows from
foreign financial institutions and as local exporters bought it
around 30.100 for settlements.
    The central bank was spotted intervening to keep the Taiwan
dollar weaker than 30.000, but the intervention was not that
strong, traders said.
    That came as U.S. dollar purchases by South Korea's foreign
exchange authorities were not very large.
    Taiwan's central bank looks closely at the won's movements
to intervene in the foreign exchange market as the two compete
in some exports markets such as semiconductors, traders and
analysts said.

title: Morgan Stanley Bullish on Rupiah Ahead of July Polls -- Market Talk
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0338 GMT [Dow Jones] Morgan Stanley expects Indonesia's rupiah to outperform its regional peers, particularly within the period up to the July presidential election. It signifies a vote of confidence in the region's worst-performing currency in 2013 amid still-wobbly sentiment on emerging markets and reflects how banks now have to consider emerging-market economies on an individual basis rather than as a broad category. It cites recent improvement in Indonesia's trade balance and attractive yields of the government's rupiah bonds as the reasons for its constructive view and marks the first time the bank has turned bullish on the rupiah since before last summer. It forecasts the USD/IDR to fall to 11,800 in the second quarter vs 12,115 currently. (I-made.sentana@wsj.com)

0337 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/JPY will likely try to rise above 104.00 on Thursday if the FOMC later in the day meets market expectations by further shrinking its bond-buying program, says a senior dealer at a major bank in Tokyo. "For equity players, such an decision would be no surprise so the market won't react to it too much," he says, adding "but some bond players had expected that the Fed may not taper this time due to confusion in emerging markets," which could mean higher rates on U.S. Treasurys if the Fed does indeed taper, which in turn should benefit the USD/JPY. The pair is at 103.21.(takashi.mochizuki@wsj.com)

0331 GMT [Dow Jones] The NZD/USD has moved higher over the session "on a further lessening of emerging market contagion risk," says Imre Speizer, senior strategist at Westpac Bank. The pair is at 0.8279 versus 0.8262 early in New Zealand. Emerging market jitters receded after Turkey's central bank increased interest rates in an attempt to shore up its currency. Markets are now looking ahead to the results of the Federal Reserve's first policy-setting meeting of the year, due early Thursday New Zealand time. The Fed is expected to continue scaling back its monthly bond-buying program by another $10 billion to $65 billion--Speizer says anything over $10 billion will be "U.S. dollar positive and will weigh on the Kiwi." The FOMC announcement will be followed by the New Zealand central bank's rate decision where there is a 30% chance of a rate hike, he says. (rebecca.howard@wsj.com; @FarroHoward)

0316 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/JPY could fall to as low as 102.50 in Asia, as Japanese exporters are expected to continue selling the pair on this end-of-month trading day for the spot market, says a senior dealer at a major bank in Tokyo. He adds trading is likely to be quiet ahead of the FOMC's announcement later in the day. The pair is at 103.16.(takashi.mochizuki@wsj.com)

0235 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/JPY daily chart indicates technical support is growing for the dollar, reinforcing demand for the greenback as the U.S. Federal Reserve meets to decide on monetary policy. The daily Ichimoku Cloud support--a technical charting tool that forecasts support and resistance levels--now props up the dollar at 102.88. Investors, who are bullish on the dollar but are waiting for a chance to buy it cheaper might place their orders near this technical support level. If the Cloud support holds up Wednesday, USD/JPY could rally off this base and toward the 20-day Bollinger mid resistance line at 104.00 in the days ahead. The Fed may decide later today to again reduce the amount of bonds it purchases; many analysts expect a gradual but consistent pullout from quantitative easing through the rest of this year. In December, the Fed announced a $10 billion reduction of its $85 billion a month bond purchase program. USD/JPY is now 103.16 versus Tuesday's close of 102.95. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0228 GMT [Dow Jones] China shares are higher as banks extend gains in bargain hunting following recent losses, say analysts. The Shanghai Composite Index is up 0.3% at 2044.71, with analysts tipping the index to hover around 2050. "The range-bound pattern may extend into the last two sessions before a week-long holiday," says Guo Feng, chief investment adviser with Northeast Securities. Shares of companies listed on the ChiNext board, a marketplace for startups, stabilize following the recent pullback, which may lend support to market sentiment, Guo adds. Among actives, banks have risen more as China avoided a potentially destabilizing hit to its financial system after a major shadow lender Monday arranged a bailout for buyers of an investment product that was on the verge of going bust; China Minsheng Banking (600016.SH) adds 1.5% to CNY7.30 while AgBank (601288.SH) gains 0.8% to CNY2.39. The Shenzhen Composite Index is up 0.1% at 1080.60 amy.li@dowjones.com)

0217 GMT [Dow Jones] The Turkish lira may have bounced back spectacularly after the central bank hiked the overnight lending rate by a jaw-dropping 4.5 percentage points to 12.0%, but some traders are turning skeptical that this is the answer to Turkey's problems. The issue at heart is Turkey's wide current account deficit, said one emerging markets currency trader in Singapore. At nearly 8% of economic output, the country's debt is at levels that Greece was at before its economic collapse. For an Asia perspective, India, another emerging market that recently has been dogged by current account deficit woes, is expected to see its deficit reduced to 2.5% of GDP for the current financial year. The India rupee has managed to sustain its recovery from its record lows seen in August 2013 because the government implemented policies to clamp down on gold and oil imports in order to fix the current account deficit - which is what Turkey now needs to do. Unless more concrete steps are taken to bolster the stopgap measure of hiking interest rates to prevent outflows, the Turkish lira could surrender its gains and head back toward the record low of 2.3900 notched on Monday. USD/TRY is now 2.2485 versus its Monday close of 2.2800. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0157 GMT [Dow Jones] The Philippine peso is up alongside other Asian currencies as these currencies recover across the board following Turkey's central bank hiking rates sharply to stem its currency's slide. USD/PHP may head back down toward the base of the daily Bollinger uptrend channel at 44.93 as risk appetite improves. Investor panic may have subsided for now, which could allow the peso to recover losses, but traders are still cautious as the U.S. Federal Reserve meets later in the day to decide on whether to reduce quantitative easing again. If the Fed announces another reduction in bond buying, U.S. bond yields would rise and lift the greenback as well. USD/PHP is now 45.14 from Tuesday's close of 45.23. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0154 GMT [Dow Jones] The rupiah soared to 12,115 versus the U.S. dollar early Wednesday--its strongest since Jan. 21--as emerging market jitters ease. USD/IDR has now rejected the bullish technical signal that had appeared Monday as emerging market currencies stage a global rebound on the back of the Turkish lira rocketing higher after Turkey's central bank announced massive interest rate hikes to stem losses for its currency. Investors had been worried that the Indonesia rupiah could be the next target for speculative investors looking to profit from the emerging market currencies rout. Suspected central bank intervention this week by Bank Indonesia has helped to prevent the rupiah from falling much and has also helped avert investor panic, says an onshore trader. But a U.S. dollar rebound in the near term cannot be ruled out as the U.S. Federal Reserve meets later in the day to decide on whether to reduce quantitative easing again. If the Fed announces another reduction in bond buying, U.S. bond yields would rise and lift the greenback as well. USD/IDR is now 12,120 from Tuesday's close of 12,185. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0144 GMT [Dow Jones] The Malaysia ringgit rallies 0.4% Wednesday in sync with other emerging-market currencies in Asia as investors respond to the recovery of the Turkish lira overnight. USD/MYR has now fallen out of the daily Bollinger uptrend channel--negating the previous bullish-dollar bias and may soon head for the trading barrier at 3.3000. Malaysia's central bank meets today for its interest-rate policy decision. Most analysts expect no change on rates. The U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting later on Wednesday may be more influential on USD/MYR as the street expects the Fed to announce another reduction in bond buying. If the Fed buys fewer bonds the benchmark U.S. Treasury yields will rise and lift the dollar. USD/MYR is now 3.32220 from its Tuesday close of 3.3340. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0142 GMT [Dow Jones] Gold is set to lose a major price support as China winds down for the Lunar New Year and its gold demand remains absent in ensuing weeks, Victor Thianpiriya, commodity strategist at ANZ says in a report. "We are cautious of chasing rallies in this environment," he says. Spot gold is under pressure and is now at $1,253/oz, down $2.70 from its previous close. After rising to a 10-week high Monday, the sharp pullback in prices "highlights how precarious rallies are in the short-term," he says. Also, premiums in China over the global prices which have declined to $7/oz on Monday from $20/oz in early January indicates "a loss of interest," he says. Besides, easing of import restrictions on gold by India is unlikely before the end of February, when the country's federal budget is presented in Parliament, he says. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com)

0138 GMT [Dow Jones] Australia's S&P/ASX 200 is up 0.6% at 5207 as emerging markets jitters receded after Turkey's central bank hiked interest rates to stem exchange rate depreciation. Cyclical stocks are reversing Tuesday's under performance, while high-dividend yield and defensive stocks are lagging. "Recent concern about emerging markets is eerily similar to last May, when we had a falling Aussie dollar, worries about China's shadow banking system and expectations of Fed tapering," says Morgans investment adviser Christopher Macdonald. "The big difference this time is that the IMF and the World Bank have upped their expectations for global growth. All the major economies are pulling in the right direction." He expects the weaker Aussie dollar to attract offshore support for Australian blue chips. BHP (BHP.AU) gains 1.2%, while CBA (CBA.AU) is up 0.4% and Telstra (TLS.AU) falls 0.5%. Focus turns to President Obama's State of the Union address and the FOMC meeting later Wednesday. (david.rogers@wsj.com)

0612 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia's ban on export of unprocessed ore should be "increasingly bullish" for nickel and prices could stabilize before rallying in 3Q, a key demand period, Bank of America-Merrill Lynch says in a report. "Ore inventories give NPI (nickel pig iron) producers some breathing space, but given the ban on nickel ore exports, we believe China's NPI output growth is set to gradually tail off," the bank says, adding that this should help reduce global market surpluses. It maintains a price target for nickel at $17,000/ton in 4Q. However, for copper, exports of concentrates could continue for three years as long as the shipments meet minimum processing requirements. It says the copper physical market may turn weak in 2H, while prices could remain above $7,500/ton in 1H. The slowing pace of economic growth in China, the world's biggest consumer of industrial metals, is likely to weigh on metal demand, analysts say. LME 3-month copper is at $7,193.50/ton, up $13.50, while nickel is at $14,441/ton, down $44 from its previous close. (arpan.mukherjee@wsj.com)

0513 GMT [Dow Jones] A slowdown in last week's manufacturing data from China was the trigger for a global wave of selling that first hit emerging-market currencies and is now taking its toll on stocks. HSBC's Frederic Neumann, co-head of Asia economic research, says the risk is great, but this is "no Lehman moment." A credit crunch in China won't reverberate in the same way, the bank says. It could be bad news for commodities, since China is such a big consumer, but the country has a strong current-account surplus and is still a relatively closed economy, which minimizes the impact of incremental slowing. "A sudden jolt would hurt," says HSBC. "A gradual slowdown, by contrast, might leave global growth little interrupted." HSBC forecasts China growth to slow to 7.4% in 2014 from 7.7% a year earlier and adds that even after that slowdown China will still add more to global demand this year than last, equivalent to another two Malaysias. "Expectations veer too far between boom and bust, distracting from calmer deliberations about what a slowing China might mean," HSBC says. (jake.watts@wsj.com)

On Friday, the Indian rupee--a currency that bears similar traits to the rupiah because of their high-yielding nature--tumbled sharply. The rupee and rupiah were both attractive currencies to hold at a time when there was an abundance of investment inflows related to U.S. quantitative easing. But as the U.S. Federal Reserve reduces its pace of bond buying, these currencies have been losing their appeal. The main reason the rupiah hasn't weakened much so far is central bank intervention. Bank Indonesia is known to intervene in the market to prevent excessive rupiah weakness in order to avert investor panic. Punters, however, will be placing their bets on the USD/IDR nondeliverable forward contracts, which are beyond the influence of Bank Indonesia, and in this way reflect better market sentiment for the currency. The labour market's demand-supply ratio edged up to 1.10 in the fourth quarter from 1.07 in the third, so for every 100 job seekers there are 110 jobs available, suggesting that the nation's job market remains robust, official data show. Economic growth will likely slow to 7.5% in the first quarter and 7.1% in the second quarter, the economists say, adding that the government is likely to loosen monetary policy in the second quarter by cutting the reserve requirement ratio by 50 basis points to boost growth. (liyan.qi@dowjones.com)

0435 GMT [Dow Jones] Asia bolstered North Sea crude-oil markets in 2013 directly through purchases of North Sea barrels by South Korea and China, and indirectly by diverting the former Soviet Union's crude oil production, also called Urals, towards Asia from Europe, Citi Research says. South Korea and China bought around 100,000 bbl/day of North Sea crude last year via arbitrage last year, and are expected to continue buying this year with three cargoes of Forties crude oil already headed towards South Korea in January. Citi says increasing flows of FSU crude towards the east are tightening the structurally short Northwest European crude market and "the loss of FSU flow west contributes to the ongoing resilience of Brent structure and flat price." 0457 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR could rally much higher as the Indonesian rupiah becomes the next target for speculative investors looking to profit from the emerging-market currency rout. Signs of increased volatility for the rupiah are appearing as the currency fell 0.5% Monday--its biggest drop since early January. The rupiah has the potential to fall much more, possibly to 12,390, if USD/IDR ends the day above 12,220 and thereby inside the daily Bollinger uptrend channel--a bullish technical signal for the dollar. On Friday, the Indian rupee--a currency that bears similar traits to the rupiah because of their high-yielding nature--tumbled sharply. The rupee and rupiah were both attractive currencies to hold at a time when there was an abundance of investment inflows related to U.S. quantitative easing. But as the U.S. Federal Reserve reduces its pace of bond buying, these currencies have been losing their appeal.

 The main reason the rupiah hasn't weakened much so far is central bank intervention. Bank Indonesia is known to intervene in the market to prevent excessive rupiah weakness in order to avert investor panic. Punters, however, will be placing their bets on the USD/IDR nondeliverable forward contracts, which are beyond the influence of Bank Indonesia, and in this way reflect better market sentiment for the currency. title: Indonesia's  forex  reserves rise to $99.4 bln as of December
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 8 (Reuters) - Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves rose to $99.4 billion at end-December, Bank Indonesia said on Wednesday, despite central bank interventions to calm the sharply falling rupiah.

Reserves in November were $96.96 billion and are likely to rise again in January with the proceeeds from a $4 billion global bond issuance on Tuesday.

The central bank spent a total of $13.4 billion in 2013 to help shore up the ailing rupiah, Asia's worst-performing currency in the year and down more than 20 percent against the dollar on rising concerns over the country's vulnerability to sudden capital outflows and a large current-account deficit. The rupiah fell on corporate dollar demand. Offshore funds continued to cut bullish positions in the won both against the dollar and the yen.     The Philippine peso eased as December inflation was faster than expected.     The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six major currencies, edged up in Asia even though December U.S.

"It is inevitable for Asian currencies to fall against the dollar as the Fed starts tapering. What matters is 'which one would fall more?'" said Park.     The won is experiencing a correction after last year's strong performance, but it is unlikely to underperform Southeast Asian peers, given South Korea's better economic fundamentals, she added.     The South Korean currency was the second-best performing Asian currency with a 1.4 percent gain to the dollar, while most regional units saw losses.

title: EM ASIA  FX  -Rupiah hits 5-year trough after Fed trims stimulus
text:

For earlier story, double click on ) SINGAPORE, Dec 19 (Reuters) - Emerging Asian currencies fell and the Indonesian rupiah hit a five-year low versus the dollar on Thursday, after the U.S. Federal Reserve announced it would start scaling back its massive monetary stimulus. The rupiah slipped to 12,225 versus the dollar, its lowest level since December 2008, according to Thomson Reuters data. Emerging Asian currencies fell broadly. The U.S.

central bank on Wednesday modestly trimmed the pace of its monthly asset purchases, by $10 billion to $75 billion, and sought to temper the long-awaited move by suggesting its key interest rate would stay at rock bottom even longer than previously promised. Traders said the rupiah came under pressure due to dollar-buying by banks on behalf of their corporate customers.

text:

0659 GMT [Dow Jones] IG chief market strategist Chris Weston says he's seen "no panic at all" ahead of the Fed's policy meeting later Wednesday, reporting "good, orderly two-way business from clients." Investors aren't expecting a disaster in the U.S. market either, with over two-thirds of new positions on S&P futures being long, Weston adds.(mia.lamar@wsj.com)

0534 GMT [Dow Jones] Currently at a 3-month low of 3.2580 to the U.S. dollar, the Malaysia ringgit could be the strongest candidate amongst Asian currencies for a post-FOMC rebound rally in the event the U.S. Federal Reserve keeps the pace of its bond buying unchanged. The ringgit has lost 1.6% of its value against the greenback since a week ago, but the daily Bollinger chart suggests weakness in the Malaysia ringgit may be slightly overdone. USD/MYR is now overextended past the upper Bollinger band (standard deviation 2), which indicates that the currency's value has fluctuated beyond the typical amplitude of the last 20 days - the parameter most often used for this charting tool. This technical overshoot is usually followed by a pullback toward the Bollinger band standard deviation 1, which is currently at 3.2380. USD/MYR is now 3.2580 from Tuesday's closing of 3.2470. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0522 GMT [Dow Jones] The spot USD/SGD is trading with a buoyant tone Wednesday on the prospect that the Federal Reserve could begin dialing down its $85 billion-a-month bond-buying program as early as at tonight's meeting and on spillover strength from the spot USD/JPY, which saw the yen weakening 0.37% to as low as 103.04 on speculation that Japan's Prime Minister Shinzo Abe may make a growth-strategy announcement in a speech on Thursday. The technical bias on the spot USD/SGD daily chart is positive as the MACD and slow stochastic indicators are bullish, while the five-day moving average is rising above the 15-day moving average. The overnight rise in spot USD/SGD to a two-month high of 1.2593 has stalled just below the 50% Fibonacci retracement of the decline from the Aug. 22 high of 1.2859 to the Oct. 23 low of 1.2336. As long as support at the Dec. 10 reaction low of 1.2465 is not breached, the spot USD/SGD looks on course to advance further in coming days 1.2659, the 61.8% retracement level, and then to the Sept. 13 minor reaction high of 1.2712. The spot USD/SGD was recently at 1.2583, up from 1.2571 in late New York trade Tuesday.(jerry.tan@wsj.com)

[Dow Jones] PREVIEW: India's central bank is likely to raise its repo rate on Wednesday to keep the recent surge in food prices from spilling over to other products, a poll shows. Fourteen of the 15 economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expect the RBI to raise its repo rate to 8.0% from 7.75%. The remaining economist predicts that the RBI will leave the rate unchanged. Analysts note that both wholesale and retail prices are rising faster than previously anticipated. "Although most of the inflation pressure is supply driven, we think that the RBI would still want to maintain a hawkish stance to ensure that inflation expectations [which are firmly in double-digit territory as per recent surveys] do not rise further," say analysts from Deutsche Bank. RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan has already established himself as an inflation hawk by raising rates twice since he took over in September, even though economic growth is at a 10-year low, analysts say. The policy outcome is due at 0530 GMT on Wednesday. (sudeep.jain@wsj.com)

0517 GMT [Dow Jones] Copper falls in Asia but remains comfortably in its recent range. Investors stay on the sidelines, awaiting the outcome of a key U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting later Wednesday. Investors are looking for clues as to when the Fed may start trimming its commodity-friendly stimulus program. Standard Bank says it has raised its 2013 forecasts for China demand for copper and aluminum as physical and financial demand have exceeded expectations, which provides "a firmer footing" for next year. Credit conditions remain tight in China in 2H as the central bank refrains from pumping money into the money market - the latest evidence coming from Wednesday's money-market rates, which surged to their highest levels since June. LME three-month copper is down 0.5% at $7,242.50/ton. (yue.li@wsj.com)

0500 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysian shares recoup some of their early losses but remain weak at the midday break. The benchmark KLCI is down 0.1% at 1848.86. "Local funds started selective stock picking, but the overall caution ahead of the (U.S.) Federal Reserve's policy decision will keep the index subdued," says a dealer, tipping immediate support at 1840. In the broader market, gainers trail laggards 234 to 364, while 304 shares remain unchanged. Among the index shares, Petronas Gas (6033.KU) leads gains with a 2.1% rise to MYR23.68 and heavyweight Malayan Banking (1155.KU) adds 0.2% to MYR10.04, while Petronas Chemicals (5183.KU) falls 0.7% to MYR6.78 and IOI Corp.(1961.KU) sheds 0.9% to MYR5.76. (abhrajit.gangopadhyay@wsj.com)

0436 GMT [Dow Jones] The rupee is slightly stronger Wednesday before the 0530 GMT policy decision announcement by the Reserve Bank of India. The odds that the central bank might raise interest rates became stronger after higher-than-expected November inflation data released Monday. The rupee is the outperformer in South Asia this week as all other currencies in the region depreciate against the dollar ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve policy decision later today. India's benchmark inflation rate was 7.5% in November versus expectations for 7.0% -- raising the possibility that the RBI could hike interest rates again, which would make it a third time in four months. A rate hike could lift the rupee due to the larger interest rate differential which implies rupee-denominated assets would yield more attractive returns than dollar-denominated ones. USD/INR is now 61.89 from Tuesday's closing of 62.01. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

0434 GMT [Dow Jones] The NZX-50 closes down 1.1% at 4675.878 as the market remains soft due to strength in the NZD/AUD seeing Australian funds selling to take currency profits, says Macquarie Private Wealth Associate Director Rob Gwyther. He adds there is also little else in the market to drive buying and this was resulting in light volumes exacerbating moves. Large-cap stock Fletcher Building (FBU.NZ) closes down 2.2% at NZ$8.35, Contact Energy was down 2.4% at NZ$4.87 and Skycity (SKC.NZ) closes down 1.8% to NZ$3.75. Summerset (SUM.NZ) is the one standout performer, ending up 1.3% at NZ$3.23 after announcing it was purchasing two Christchurch sites on which to build villages. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com)

0404 GMT [Dow Jones] Australia's central bank Governor Glenn Stevens is keeping his options open. He won't rule out intervention to lower the Australian dollar, cutting interest rates further or introducing new regulatory tools to slow lending to keep house prices in check, he tells a parliamentary economics committee on Wednesday. Policy adjustments will be made if the conditions warrant, Stevens says. Stevens says "watch this space," hinting the Reserve Bank of Australia might soon publish research into new clamps on home lending. Prices are rising because of record-low interest rates. "On occasion intervention can be quite useful. It still is," Stevens says. But the central bank alone can't revive a flagging economy, he says and calls on other policy makers to build confidence in the economy. (james.glynn@wsj.com)

0331 GMT [Dow Jones] The NZD/USD has traded sideways over the course of the session, with the market focus all on the FOMC decision later in the global day and the potential for it to announce it will start to taper its bond-buying program, says Chris Hunter, corporate dealing manager at Western Union Business Solutions. "Tomorrow morning is going to provide the direction if not for the next quarter, then for the rest of the year as to what the market is going to do with the U.S. currency." The pair is at 0.8264 vs 0.8271 early this morning. Hunter adds that NZ 3Q GDP, due Thursday, is expected to be a strong number and "this may reduce the impact of a U.S. dollar positive announcement by the Fed or it might just boost the New Zealand dollar higher." He puts support ahead of the FOMC at 0.8235, with resistance at 0.8285. (lucy.craymer@wsj.com)

0307 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/CNY is steady after central parity is moved a fraction only. The pair is at 6.0715 vs 6.0710 Tuesday close after the fixing is set at 6.1105 vs 6.1108 Tuesday. Traders said the yuan will likely have strong support at 6.0700. "I don't expect the [U.S.] Federal Reserve to surprise the market with a tapering decision and the yuan is unlikely to get any incentive from the U.S. side," a Shanghai-based foreign bank trader says. Offshore, one-year USD/CNY NDFs are at 6.1290/6.1320 from 6.1279/6.1322 late Tuesday. (wynne.wang@dowjones.com)

0211 GMT [Dow Jones] The dollar's routing of the Indonesia rupiah continues after yet another near five-year record was hit on Tuesday. The rupiah is back at Tuesday's 12,150 low against the greenback as traders, emboldened by a lack of willingness by the Indonesia central bank to intervene against rupiah weakness, bought the dollar on a bet that the U.S. Federal Reserve might decide to reduce bond-buying at its policy meeting today. The rupiah is widely seen as one of the more vulnerable currencies in the event the Fed decides to cut back on bond purchases - which could trigger foreign outflows that will further weaken the rupiah. The Indonesia central bank has been conspicuously absent in the spot market except for recent verbal intervention to talk the dollar down. Even the Monday announcement of raising foreign-investment limits in certain sectors of the economy, such as airports and railways, didn't help the rupiah to recoup losses. USD/IDR is now at 12,150, against Tuesday's closing of 12,110. (ewen.chew@wsj.com)

title: EM ASIA  FX  -Asian  currencies  mixed; baht rises on short-covering
text:
* Previous day's rise in gold, position squaring lift baht * Rupiah eases on onshore dollar demand (Adds text, updates prices) By Masayuki Kitano SINGAPORE, Dec 11 (Reuters) - The Thai baht rose on short-covering on Wednesday, pulling away from a three-month low set last week on concerns over political tensions, while the Indonesian rupiah fell on dollar-buying by onshore players. Moves in Asian currencies were mixed, with currencies such as the baht and the Philippine peso getting a respite after a recent selloff, while those like the rupiah and the Indian rupee retreated. Although there is caution that emerging Asian currencies could come under pressure if the U.S. Federal Reserve were to announce a scaling back of its monetary stimulus at its Dec. 17-18 policy meeting, some market players say a big shock is unlikely. The market already seems to have priced in the impact of the Fed eventually tapering its bond-buying stimulus, said a trader for a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.

 "Market is long the U.S. dollar because of this and we now see dollar selling to adjust positions," the trader said. While there had been expectations for a big outflow from emerging Asian markets at one point, that doesn't seem to be happening right now, he added.


    
    THAI BAHT
    Traders said long liquidation in the dollar gave a lift to
the baht, which rose as high as around 31.90, from a
three-month low of 32.34 set last Friday.
    A Bangkok-based trader said the previous day's


short-covering rise in gold helped trigger some dollar-selling, adding that the market had been caught long the dollar. The precious metal is popular among Thai investors, and rises in gold prices often prompt some to sell physical gold or futures. Investors might then sell the dollars they gained from such transactions to buy the baht. Other traders said stop-loss dollar selling was triggered at levels below 32.05 and 32.00.


    
    INDONESIAN RUPIAH
    The Indonesian rupiah fell as low as 12,012,


nearing a low of 12,035 set last Thursday, the rupiah's weakest level versus the dollar since March 2009, according to Thomson Reuters data. Traders said Indonesia's central bank was spotted intervening to sell the dollar, which rose on the back of demand from onshore players. One trader said the dollar was likely to remain on the bid against the rupiah going into the month-end, supported by demand from local companies. title: Indonesia's Nov  forex  reserves little changed - c.bank
text:
JAKARTA, Dec 6 (Reuters) - Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves stood at $96.96 billion at end-November, marginally lower than $97 billion the previous month, Bank Indonesia said on Friday.

The central bank last week said that it would not hesitate to intervene in foreign exchange and debt markets to help prop up the ailing rupiah, which has fallen nearly 20 percent against the dollar so far this year.

Governor Agus Martowardojo earlier urged exporters to sell dollars to help balance supply and demand in the market.
