The Indonesia central bank has been urging local exporters to sell their U.S. dollar earnings at these elevated levels - likely an attempt to help buffer the rupiah from further weakness. text:
* Offshore funds sell baht; intervention caution cuts losses * Indonesia sees $50 mln trade surplus in Oct * Philippine peso edges up on remittance inflows (Adds text, updates prices) By Jongwoo Cheon SINGAPORE, Dec 2 (Reuters) - Thailand's baht cratered to a 12-week low on Monday as anti-government protesters vowed to topple Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra, while the Indonesian rupiah outshone emerging Asian currencies after posting a surprise trade surplus. The baht earlier lost as much as 0.5 percent to 32.26 per dollar, its weakest since Sept 11, as offshore funds sold the currency amid the political turmoil. It recouped some of the losses as traders kept a wary eye over possible dollar-selling intervention by the central bank. Traders in Bangkok, however, said they have not spotted official sales of dollars yet.

 Thai protesters took to the streets to renew their fight to topple Shinawatra, prompting riot police to fire teargas and stun grenades for a second day outside her fortified office compound to keep them at bay. On Sunday, three people were killed in street clashes in Bangkok. The dollar/baht forward rates jumped with the one-month rate up 43.5 percent to 17.00, indicating more investors are trying to buy dollar forwards. "We may see more capital outflows on escalating political tensions. If the Fed tapering fears emerge again, the outflows may accelerate," said Yuna Park, a currency and bond analyst at Dongbu Securities in Seoul. . "The issue was initially purely political. But now it may hurt economic growth," Park said, adding the bath may test this year's low of 32.46. In November, foreign investors sold a combined net 84.2 billion baht ($2.62 billion) in Thai stocks and bonds. The growing political tensions saw the baht become the second-worst performing emerging Asian currency in November with a 3.1 percent loss against the dollar, Thomson Reuters data showed. Most emerging Asian currencies advanced as final HSBC/Markit Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) showed China's factory activity maintained steady growth momentum in November. Still, the gains were tempered as investors awaited key U.S. economic data including November jobs on Friday for clues on when the Federal Reserve would start scaling back its stimulus. Nonfarm payrolls for November are expected to show an increase of 185,000 jobs last month, down from 204,000 in October, according to a Reuters survey of economists. "If a better number on nonfarm materializes, it may be the catalyst for a higher USD/JPY which adds to the upside in USD/Asia here," said Andy Ji, Asian currency strategist for Commonwealth Bank of Australia in Singapore.


    Ji said he would sell emerging Asian currencies on rallies.
    
    RUPIAH
    The rupiah rose in both onshore and offshore markets as
Indonesia reported a trade surplus of $50 million in October,
led by unexpected growth in exports. 
    Earlier, spot rupiah in the local market gained with the


central bank spotted selling dollars to support the ailing currency and as foreign banks bought the Indonesian currency on dips, traders said. In offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) markets, the rupiah extended gains after the data. The official Jakarta Interbank Spot Dollar Rate (JISDOR) , which the central bank introduced in May as part of a bid to manage exchange rate fluctuations, was fixed at 11,946 rupiah per dollar, compared with Friday's 11,977. Jakarta shares rose more than 1 percent, outperforming most regional stocks.

overseas Filipino workers.
    "If all other things remain quiet, the inflows may drive
dollar/peso lower in coming sessions," said a senior Philippine
bank trader in Manila.
    The Philippine currency may strengthen to 43.50 per dollar,
the trader added.

title: Southeast Asian Markets End Week Slightly Higher; Rupiah Pushes 4.5-Year Low
text:
Southeast Asian markets ended Friday mostly higher, with Thailand and Indonesia making strong gains in the last part of the day, while Indonesia's rupiah retreated from a 4.5-year low against the U.S. dollar on suspected intervention from the central bank.

Thailand's SET closed up 0.9%, recovering from a 0.5% fall during morning trading. Indonesia's JSX closed up 0.5%, while the Philippines' PSE Composite gained 0.6%--its fourth straight day of gains after over a week of declines triggered by the landfall of Typhoon Haiyan on Nov. 8.

Elsewhere, Vietnam's benchmark closed flat, Malaysia's KLCI added 0.3% and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times bucked the trend with a fall of 0.3%.

Central bankers in both the Philippines and Indonesia attempted to reassure investors Friday. Governor Amando Tetangco in the Philippines said that the impact of Typhoon Haiyan on the economy would be manageable and domestic growth should hit targets of this year and next without central bank intervention. The government is targeting 6.5%-7.5% growth in 2014.

Bank Indonesia governor Agus Martowardojo said that the rupiah, which is hovering near a 4.5%-year low of 12,000 against the U.S. dollar, reflected economic fundamentals despite heavy falls this year of almost 20%. He said the central bank would prioritize stabilizing the economy rather than boosting growth. There was some speculation among traders that Bank Indonesia may have intervened Friday to keep the rupiah from breaching the 12,000 mark.

Among other currencies in the region, Malaysia's ringgit strengthened 0.3% and Thailand's baht lost 0.1% against the U.S. dollar.

Thai real-estate developer Central Pattana Public Co., a volatile large-cap stock, added 2.4%, while telecoms provider Total Access Communications Public Co.--also known as DTAC--ended up 5%.

Philippine stocks continued to recover from a blip in investor sentiment following the typhoon. Telecoms provider Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co. added 2.1%, while property investor SM Investments Corporation gained 0.8%.

In Malaysia, conglomerate Genting Bhd., which has interests in casinos, power, plantations and other businesses, lost 1.4% a day after it reported third-quarter results that Kenanga Research said came in below expectations. Genting said its core net profit for the nine months to September was 1.29 billion ringgit (US$400 million). The group's earnings are expected to be better in the fourth quarter of 2013 as it is entering the busy festive year-end season, Kenanga said in a note, maintaining its "outperform" rating.

title: *Bank Indonesia Gov: Rupiah Level Reflects Economic Fundamentals
text:
29 Nov 2013 01:10 EDT *Bank Indonesia Gov: To Prioritize 'Stability Over Growth'

29 Nov 2013 01:11 EDT *Bank Indonesia Gov: To Intervene if Necessary

29 Nov 2013 01:39 EDT  Bank Indonesia Governor: Rupiah Level Reflects Economic Fundamentals


 
   By Farida Husna 
 

JAKARTA--The rupiah's current level against the U.S. dollar reflects Indonesia's economic fundamentals, Bank Indonesia Governor Agus Martowardojo said Friday, reiterating that the central bank will continue to pursue policies to stabilize the economy rather than boosting growth.

"Our problem is the current account deficit, which needs to be fixed first," Mr. Martowardojo told reporters.

The rupiah is hovering near a 4.5-year low of IDR12,000 against the dollar, falling nearly 20% so far this year on jitters that Indonesia's huge current account deficit will keep the country vulnerable to capital outflows if the U.S. Federal Reserve starts tapering its bond-buying program.

Mr. Martowardojo said the central bank will closely monitor the rupiah's movements and intervene if necessary.

Two dealers said they suspect that the central bank had earlier Friday sold around $25 million around IDR11,990 to prevent the local currency from falling too fast.

Despite this, dealers don't think Bank Indonesia is trying to resist the rupiah's weakness but is merely smoothening its decline to avoid panic among businesses and the public.

title: PREVIEW-Indonesia's trade gap to narrow a bit, but pressure still on rupiah
text:
JAKARTA, Nov 29 (Reuters) - Indonesia is expected to post a slightly narrower trade deficit in October, as aggressive rate rises start to subdue demand for imports, while November's annual inflation may pick up on high food prices, a Reuters poll showed on Friday.

The poll's median projection was for the trade deficit in Southeast Asia's largest economy to come in at $650 million, slightly less than the $660 million gap of the previous month.

Imports in October were forecast to fall 8.11 percent year-on-year, from September's 0.77 percent rise, as a weakening exchange rate crimped demand, while higher interest rates also tempered borrowing and affected importers.

Exports showed some signs of improvement bolstered by a recovery in commodity prices, but stayed weak. October exports were estimated to fall 2.75 percent from a year earlier, against a drop of 6.85 percent the previous month.

"Strong domestic consumption has sustained, while export growth is unlikely to see a strong boost until 2014 - and that is also dependent on how well the global economy picks up," said Gundy Cahyadi, economist at DBS in Singapore.

Indonesia has been struggling to stabilise its external balance, as a large current-account deficit and weak structural reforms have turned foreign investors bearish.

Bank Indonesia, under pressure from the rupiah's steep fall, has raised its benchmark reference rate a total of 175 basis points since June to ease concerns over the country's vulnerability to capital outflows ahead of the Federal Reserve's expected tapering in monetary stimulus.

The poll of 14 analysts projected that November's rate of inflation quickened to 8.48 percent, versus October's 8.32 percent, on stubbornly high prices for foodstuff and pass-through costs from a depreciation in the rupiah.

On a monthly basis, the consumer price index was seen up 0.20 percent, higher than the central bank's forecast of 0.05-0.1 percent.

MORE RATE HIKES SEEN

Weakness in trade and further declines in the rupiah could give the central bank more reason to increase the benchmark reference rate at its December policy meeting or after.

"Bank Indonesia will continue to raise the benchmark rate until there are imminent signs of optimism that the current-account deficit eases to below 3 percent of GDP. Thus, we see BI lifting the rate up to 8.5 percent in Q1-2014," said Arga Samudro, economist at Bahana Securities in Jakarta.

The rupiah hit its support level of 12,000 per dollar on Thursday due to increasing dollar demand from Indonesian firms. Asia's worst-performing currency has lost nearly 20 percent to the dollar this year.

Earlier, Governor of Bank Indonesia Agus Martowardojo said the bank will not hesitate to intervene in the forex market and considers the recent slide temporary.

The finance ministry estimates the current-account deficit to narrow in the fourth quarter to $7 billion, compared with $8.4 billion in the previous quarter.

In April-June, the current-account deficit was $9.9 billion or the equivalent of 4.4 percent of GDP.

title: India, Indonesia  Currencies  Continue to Slide
text:
Indian and Indonesian currencies were battered Wednesday, with both the rupee and the rupiah continuing a recent downtrend, reflecting investors' concerns over growing trade imbalances and slowing emerging-market economies.

India's currency slumped to within a whisker of a record low before the central bank--according to traders--aggressively intervened, while Indonesia's currency fell to its lowest level in more than four years.

The two countries have taken the brunt of a selloff in Asia, as their widening trade deficits and rising inflation leave them especially vulnerable to the impact of global fund managers withdrawing investments from Asia amid signs of accelerating growth in the U.S. and Europe. The Reserve Bank of India and Bank Indonesia have pursued a variety of strategies to reverse the trend, including raising interest rates and intervening in foreign-exchange markets, but so far they have failed to stem the slide.

India's rupee was at 67.10 to the U.S. dollar on Wednesday afternoon after reaching 68.60 earlier in the day--close to a record 68.80 hit on Aug. 28.

Dealers said India's central bank has sold dollars several times in recent weeks. The RBI says it intervenes in the currency market only to curb volatility and not to target a particular exchange rate.

The rupee's slide--it is down 19% in the year to date--comes amid a change in leadership at the Reserve Bank of India, with former International Monetary Fund Chief Economist Raghuram Rajan set to commence his duties as governor on Thursday. His first order of business will likely be to stabilize the currency.

Indonesia's rupiah reached 11,125 against the dollar in the interbank market on Wednesday, its lowest level since April 2009. It is down 14% in the year to date, and the outlook is for the downtrend to continue, with one-month non-deliverable forwards pricing in a further 6% decline.

For people looking to buy dollars from money changers and banks, the rupiah is looking even weaker. The difference between the levels that banks use with each other and posted rates at exchange counters have widened to as high as an extra 900 rupiah per dollar compared with about 200 under normal conditions. Analysts say this is a sign of fear that the supply of U.S. notes is low and indicative of a large appetite to exchange rupiah for dollars.

Signs on Wednesday that the U.S. is moving closer to military action against Syria could make the situation worse for both India and Indonesia's currencies. Although crude-oil prices have slipped since President Barack Obama said over the weekend that he would seek Congress's approval for a strike, support from key political players increases the likelihood of congressional assent, which could spur prices higher. That is bad news for both India and Indonesia, as it threatens to boost their already-high energy-import bills.

Outflows from Asia, especially Indonesia and India, picked up last week to the most since June, when markets were roiled by the first signs that the Federal Reserve was poised to end aggressive bond buying sooner than previously anticipated. Global investors withdrew $104 million from Indonesia's bond markets in the week ending Aug. 28, the most of any Asian debt market, according to research from Australia & New Zealand Banking Group Ltd. In India, fund managers have been exiting stock markets in greater numbers, with $213 million leaving the nation's equities over the same period.

--Ashutosh Joshi and Andreas Ismar contributed to this article.

title: DJ  Emerging Markets Hope to Get Some Attention at G-20, Too
text:
Leaders from the Group of 20 economies have been preoccupied by Syria ahead of their summit this week, but some are still hoping to find a way to steady the suddenly shaky fortunes of emerging markets.

In recent years, most of the economic threats tackled by the G-20 have stemmed from large flows of capital from developed countries to developing ones in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis. But now that flow has begun to reverse, posing new challenges to the global recovery.

The turnaround has accelerated in recent weeks as investors anticipate an end to the U.S. Federal Reserve's period of extraordinary monetary stimulus this year. The result has been sharp falls in developing-country currencies.

The central banks of three G-20 members-Brazil, Indonesia and Turkey-have raised interest rates, intervened in currency markets or both in recent weeks to try to stem the declines.

In India, where the rupee has suffered the most-precipitous decline among large Asian economies, the central bank has also taken the step of selling dollars to state-run oil refiners via a commercial bank to shift demand for dollars away from the open market.

The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development on Tuesday warned that an already subdued recovery in global economic growth could be weakened further if the outflow of capital from developing economies intensifies.

Some leaders are hoping that the issue can still be addressed, even if the meetings in St. Petersburg on Thursday and Friday are dominated by the crisis surrounding the alleged use of chemical weapons in Syria's civil war.

For instance, a person familiar with Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff's thinking said she hopes the summit will produce agreement on ways to ease the impact of the anticipated change in Fed policy.

"The tone of her speech [at the summit] will show how upset she may be with U.S. policies," said a Brazilian government official.

Brazilian officials say they have the backing of other developing countries in seeking moves to address recent currency volatility, although they are unclear about which among the G-20 members will be offering support. In particular, they want the Fed to improve the way it communicates its intentions to reduce market swings.

With the U.S. government focusing on efforts to boost support for its approach to Syria, those developing economies may be left frustrated. But even without Syria, the U.S. would have been unlikely to make major concessions, economists say.

"Other than a vague commitment to take into account the effects of its monetary policy on other countries, the Fed is in practice likely to make no concessions to developments elsewhere," said Capital Economics, a London-based research firm.

title: UPDATE 1-Rupiah weakens past 11,000 for first time since early 2009
text:
(Adds comments, details and background)

* Corporate dollar demand keeps weighing on rupiah

* Record trade deficit in July is latest worry

* Central bank continues to intervene - traders

By Jongwoo Cheon

SINGAPORE, Sept 3 (Reuters) - Indonesia's rupiah weakened past the psychologically important level of 11,000 per dollar on Tuesday, for the first time in more than four years, as the market fretted after the government reported a record monthly trade deficit.

The rupiah's indicative prices lost 0.7 percent to 11,050 per dollar, its weakest since April 2009.

Monday's announcement that Indonesia's trade deficit in July soared to $2.31 billion, nearly triple the June level, was the latest in a series of blows to the currency, which has shed nearly 13 percent against the dollar this year.

The July deficit makes some analysts and traders worry that Indonesia's current account deficit, which widened sharply in the second quarter, could get bigger this quarter, even though the central bank expects it to narrow.

While the rupiah slipped again on Tuesday, Indonesia's benchmark stock index rose 1.5 percent, erasing most of Monday's decline.

The latest fall for the rupiah, which shed 0.6 percent on Monday, stemmed from dollar demand from local companies in thin liquidity.

Forward markets on Tuesday pointed to further depreciation in the rupiah, with one-month non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to the dollar weakening to 11,720.

The spread between the spot rate and the NDFs widened to 655 basis points. The one-month offshore/onshore forward spread increased to 610 bps.

Tuesday's spreads were the highest since Aug. 27, when they reached their widest since the global finance crisis in 2008.

Scotiabank, in a client note, said the rupiah still faces "significant negative speculative strain", adding that the currency "is not yet out of the woods by any stretch of the imagination."

According to traders, the rupiah has periodically traded weaker than 11,000 since late August, as banks in Indonesia bought dollars above that for their local corporate clients. However, Bank Indonesia often discouraged dealers from posting on electronic trading platforms price levels weaker than 11,000.

SCREEN SHOWINGS

On Tuesday, screens showed 11,050 rupiah to the dollar, but the rupiah was traded weaker than that level, according to dealers.

"BI cannot fight the market," said a Jakarta-based trader, referring to Bank Indonesia letting the rupiah weaken below 11,000 in the interbank market.

The central bank has been providing dollar liquidity and, since June, has raised its benchmark interest rate by 125 basis points to support the rupiah.

But deteriorating economic fundamentals could not stop foreign outflows, putting pressure on the currency.

The rupiah, along with the Indian rupee, are seen as especially vulnerable to anticipated reduction in the Federal Reserve's quantitative easing. Both India and Indonesia are struggling with growing current account deficits, slowing economic growth and resistance to implementing much-needed reforms.

Foreign investors have dumped a net 5.9 trillion rupiah ($538.08 million) of Indonesian stocks between Aug. 1 and Sept. 2, according to Thomson Reuters data.

During August, foreigners also reduced bond holdings by 1.8 trillion rupiah, the government data showed. (Editing by Richard Borsuk)

title: Leaders Seek Balm for Emerging Markets at G-20 Summit
text:
Leaders from the Group of 20 economies have been preoccupied by Syria ahead of their summit this week, but some are still hoping to find a way to steady the suddenly shaky fortunes of emerging markets.

In recent years, most of the economic threats tackled by the G-20 have stemmed from large flows of capital from developed countries to developing ones in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis. But now that flow has begun to reverse, posing new challenges to the global recovery.

In India, where the rupee has suffered the most-precipitous decline among large Asian economies, the central bank has also taken the step of selling dollars to state-run oil refiners via a commercial bank to shift demand for dollars away from the open market.

The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development on Tuesday warned that an already subdued recovery in global economic growth could be weakened further if the outflow of capital from developing economies intensifies.

Some leaders are hoping that the issue can still be addressed, even if the meetings in St. Petersburg on Thursday and Friday are dominated by the crisis surrounding the alleged use of chemical weapons in Syria's civil war.

For instance, a person familiar with Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff's thinking said she hopes the summit will produce agreement on ways to ease the impact of the anticipated change in Fed policy.

"The tone of her speech [at the summit] will show how upset she may be with U.S. policies," said a Brazilian government official.

Brazilian officials say they have the backing of other developing countries in seeking moves to address recent currency volatility, although they are unclear about which among the G-20 members will be offering support. In particular, they want the Fed to improve the way it communicates its intentions to reduce market swings.

With the U.S. government focusing on efforts to boost support for its approach to Syria, those developing economies may be left frustrated. But even without Syria, the U.S. would have been unlikely to make major concessions, economists say.

"Other than a vague commitment to take into account the effects of its monetary policy on other countries, the Fed is in practice likely to make no concessions to developments elsewhere," said Capital Economics, a London-based research firm.

In an effort to exercise more control over their currencies, the governments of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa have been working on a joint proposal to set up a $100 billion Contingency Reserve Arrangement by pooling central-bank reserves.

Leaders may make some progress in St. Petersburg, since that doesn't require input from the U.S. or other developed countries, although the new fund is unlikely to be launched until next year.

In March, finance ministers of the five "Brics" countries signed an agreement to kick-start the arrangement during their annual meeting in South Africa. China will contribute $41 billion, followed by Brazil, Russia and India with $18 billion each, and South Africa with $5 billion.

The focus on Syria will also probably mean that developed-country members of the G-20 pay less attention to a long-running dispute over whether to set binding deadlines for stabilizing their budget deficits and beginning to cut their debts.

In recent months, German officials have pushed the G-20 nations to agree to hard targets for reducing debt after the current deficit-cutting agreement expires in 2016. But the effort ran into strong U.S. opposition when finance ministers met in Moscow in July, with Treasury Department officials insisting that the priority had to be boosting jobs and growth as opposed to reducing debt.

Rather than a hard target, the G-20 countries are expected to lay out "medium-term fiscal strategies" to show how they will achieve "sustainable growth" after 2016, a German official told reporters in Berlin on Monday.

"This is better than no strategy, but these aren't binding targets," the official said.

G-20 leaders are also set to produce a plan for supporting growth and creating jobs.

A U.S. administration official said an overriding U.S. goal at the summit is persuading other nations that they need to help boost demand world-wide. Global demand is "improving," but "remains weak," the official said.

"We need to rededicate ourselves to promoting a lasting rebalancing of global demand," the official said. "We welcome signs that Europe's long recession is ending and their critical steps to restore financial stability. But important challenges remain, including boosting demand and addressing record-high unemployment levels."

Beyond that, the U.S. wants to make progress toward another goal: cracking down on tax evasion.

That issue was front-and-center at a separate meeting of the Group of Eight nations in Northern Ireland in June.

"We will also be working in St. Petersburg to get support globally for the kinds of measures that we have laid out for countries to close tax loopholes and avoid a race to the bottom where tax competition leads countries to lose revenue and companies to make inefficient decisions when they locate where they pay the lowest tax, rather than where it's most productive for them to produce," an Obama administration official said.

--Peter Nicholas and Anton Troianovski contributed to this article. [ 09-03-13 1333ET ]

The dollar is slightly firmer after U.S. data on Friday reaffirmed that the U.S. economy is indeed on a solid footing, which could thus convince the Federal Reserve to start withdrawing QE this month. Without any catalyst, and without any strong chart signals, the baht may consolidate within a narrow range for now. One domestic front to watch could be the dissent arising from Thai rubber farmers who are demanding the government buys from them at artificially high prices, as it does from the rice growers. A mass protest is planned for Sep. 3. China PMI released Sunday showed an improvement over its previous month, as did South Korea's HSBC PMI released earlier Monday. The USD/PHP could slip back down to the upper Bollinger band (standard deviation 2) at 44.38 and then consolidate. But analysts think that immediate concern that plagues the rupiah in the open market is the lack of transparency and price discovery, which is why the NDF market still prices the USD/IDR at an exorbitant premium - a sign of poor investor confidence. The premium that the 1-month USD/IDR NDF contract commands over the spot price came down sharply - in reaction to Bank Indonesia's move - to IDR500 from almost IDR800 Wednesday, but it still remains very elevated considering it trades at around IDR20-IDR40 in stable market conditions. The latest move, which traders deem could be the most effective immediate measure to boost the rupee, has removed the main source of USD demand from the open market - the state-run oil companies. The RBI will now sell dollars directly to the 3 state-run oil firms, and thus eliminate their buying in the spot market which drives the USD/INR higher and thus depresses the INR. The dollar is close to the base of the weekly Bollinger downtrend channel, and also the entrance to the monthly Bollinger downtrend channel. The coincidence of these two support levels at around 1,190-1,191 could impede gains for the KRW. The Bank of Korea Thursday highlighted the country's robust export growth despite external headwinds, which could add to bullish sentiment for the won. Immediate resistance is at 1,100 (psychological resistance), then at 1,105 (top of weekly Bollinger downtrend channel), before 1,106 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel).

USD/SGD - consolidation. As the greenback slipped overnight, USD/SGD finds itself still trapped within the 1.2738-1.2800 span for now, bound by the 20-day Bollinger mid support and the psychological barrier above - which is also the entrance to the Bollinger uptrend channel. The next cue for a larger move in USD/SGD could come from USD/CNY - where punters expect a much stronger yuan valuation ahead of the G-20 summit that begins today. But on the flipside, if USD/JPY breaks above 100.00, USD/SGD may follow higher. Immediate resistance is at 1.2800 (psychological resistance and daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 1.2866 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/MYR - consolidation lower. Ratings agencies Fitch and Moody's have both noted that the Malaysia government's attempt at fiscal correction via cutting of the fuel subsidy may not be enough; though Moody's said it was a step in the right direction. The government's decisive response to the recent spotlight on its dwindling current account deficit may be reason to expect the ringgit to recover further. Punters are betting on further action from the Malaysia government to improve the country's fiscal situation, with the possibility of a consumption tax to be introduced at the October budget announcement. Traders expect Malaysia's central bank will likely keep the benchmark interest rate unchanged at its policy meeting today. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 3.2640 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 3.2500 (psychological support), before 3.2420 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 3.2800 (psychological resistance), then at 3.2860 (20-day Bollinger mid), before 3.3000 (psychological barrier).

USD/THB - consolidation. USD/THB may continue to hover between 32.00-32.20, balanced by U.S. dollar strength arising from higher U.S. Treasury yields, and improving investor sentiment in Asia. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose back above 2.90% as bonds got sold again due to increasing likelihood of the Fed tapering quantitative easing this month. But Asia is looking up as the currencies which have been under immense selling pressure lately pull back from the brink of multi-year lows, as a string of improving manufacturing PMIs boost confidence. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 32.00 (psychological support), then at 31.80 (psychological support), before 31.79 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 32.20 (psychological resistance), then at 32.28 (last Wednesday's 3-year high), before 32.49 (monthly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP - consolidation lower. USD/PHP slips back inside the confines of the Bollinger uptrend channel, after having spent the most part of last week in overbought territory. The peso is likely to recover further Thursday, helped by improving investor sentiment in the region. But a dollar dip could stall at the base of the Bollinger uptrend channel at 44.09. As long as the pair remains above this level, an upside bias remains in the near term. As the G-20 summit begins, markets will be awaiting news on the U.S.-Syria situation developing for hints of risk aversion once more. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 44.20 (psychological support), then at 44.09 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 44.00 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is likely at 44.50 (psychological resistance), then at 44.51 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 44.75 (3-year high).

USD/IDR - consolidation lower. Spot USD/IDR still appears buoyant as long as it stays above the 11,000 psychological barrier, but the USD/IDR NDF market may selloff slightly due to improving market sentiment. The rally in U.S. stocks and improving global manufacturing PMIs this week have been helping to offset fears of military escalation in Syria, and the Fed tapering of quantitative easing. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for spot USD/IDR is at 11,000 (psychological support), then at 10,900 (psychological support), before 10,800 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 11,500 (psychological resistance), before 12,000 (psychological resistance).

USD/INR - upside bias. The India rupee jumped Wednesday on fresh measures announced by the new Reserve Bank of India governor. USD/INR could be on its way to 66.00 and possibly lower as investors react to the announcements. Raghuram Rajan, in his first speech as governor, announced that banks which receive dollars into foreign-currency deposits from Indians living abroad now will be able to swap those dollars for rupees from the RBI, and banks can now raise double the previous amount that was allowed via the issuing of overseas bonds. The dollars received can then be exchanged for rupees at cheaper-than-market rates with the RBI. The new policies, in place till Nov. 30, increase dollar liquidity in the system, thus USD/INR fell sharply in anticipation of more USD supply to hit the market soon. USD/CNY - consolidation. The PBOC's USD/CNY parity rate could be set higher on account of the stronger greenback, but the spot USD/CNY may not follow higher. The yuan is likely to find support from the official China August PMI, released Sunday, which continues to affirm an improving economy that is transitioning toward a more sustainable growth pattern. The HSBC August China PMI will be released today, which could confirm that improving trend in the official index. As the China economy stabilizes, investors will expect further financial liberalization this year, which will add to demand for the yuan. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for the USD/CNY is at 6.1127 (base of Bollinger downtrend channel), before 6.1090 (record low). Immediate resistance is likely at 6.1200 (psychological resistance), then at 6.1212 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 6.1300 (20-day Bollinger mid and psychological resistance).

USD/TWD - consolidation, downside bias. The USD/TWD continues to look rangebound on the charts, and likely to remain within the consolidation range of 29.900-30.100 despite the broadly stronger USD. Taiwan August manufacturing PMI to be released slightly later will reveal if the Taiwan economy is gaining ground along with the recent improvement in China's manufacturing sector. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 29.950 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 29.900 (psychological support), before 29.830 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is likely at 29.940 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 30.000 (psychological resistance), before 30.060 (20-day Bollinger mid).

USD/KRW - consolidation with downside bias. The USD/KRW slips to the bottom of the daily Bollinger downtrend channel, which ought to support the pair for now, as the HSBC August PMI comes in at 47.5 versus 47.2 in July. The improved reading is helping to mitigate the disappointing industrial output data released last week, and thus helping the won to strengthen again in spite of a broadly stronger USD. As long as the USD/KRW stays under 1,112, the Bollinger downtrend channel will continue to guide it lower. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 1,108 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 1,100 (psychological support), before 1,095 (base of weekly Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1,112 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 1,116 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance), before 1,120 (psychological resistance).

USD/SGD - consolidation, possible bounce. The USD/SGD has found an interim base at the 20-day Bollinger mid at 1.2720, and could bounce higher toward the Bollinger uptrend channel at 1.2790 as the greenback gains on Syria tensions and the looming decision by the Federal Reserve to withdraw QE. The Sing dollar could suffer slightly with risk sentiment likely to be shaky as the U.S. contemplates a Syria airstrike, with or without its allies. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.2721 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before 1.2700 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 1.2790 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1.2800 (psychological resistance), before 1.2865 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/MYR - possible bounce. The USD/MYR has hit the 20-day Bollinger mid support at 3.2800 and could turn firmer from here due to buying on dips with the increased likelihood of the U.S. Federal Reserve tapering quantitative easing this month. The dollar is slightly firmer after U.S. data on Friday reaffirmed that the U.S. economy is indeed on a solid footing, which could thus convince the Federal Reserve to start withdrawing QE this month. The USD/MYR could bounce off the 20-day Bollinger mid and head back toward the Bollinger uptrend channel at 3.3070. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 3.2800 (psychological support and 20-day Bollinger mid), then at 3.2570 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 3.2500 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 3.3000 (psychological barrier), then at 3.3070 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 3.3350 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/THB - consolidation. The USD/THB is likely to drift about in a 32.00-32.20 range as investors sit on the sidelines watching Syria and awaiting the Federal Reserve decision this month on the possible withdrawal of QE. Without any catalyst, and without any strong chart signals, the baht may consolidate within a narrow range for now. One domestic front to watch could be the dissent arising from Thai rubber farmers who are demanding the government buys from them at artificially high prices, as it does from the rice growers. A mass protest is planned for Sep. 3. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 32.00 (psychological support), then at 31.80 (psychological support), before 31.69 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 32.20 (psychological resistance), then at 32.28 (Wednesday's 3-year high), before 32.49 (monthly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP - possible pullback lower. The USD/PHP may pullback slightly as risk sentiment improves on uplifting regional economic data. China PMI released Sunday showed an improvement over its previous month, as did South Korea's HSBC PMI released earlier Monday. The USD/PHP could slip back down to the upper Bollinger band (standard deviation 2) at 44.38 and then consolidate. The peso has been wilting recently due to broad dollar strength, despite healthy 2Q Philippines GDP data released last week meeting expectations at 7.5%. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 44.50 (psychological support), then at 44.38 (daily Bollinger band standard deviation 2), before 44.20 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is likely at 44.80 (psychological resistance), then at 45.00 (psychological resistance), before 45.21 (monthly Ichimoku Cloud resistance).

USD/IDR - consolidation. The USD/IDR appears to be stabilizing, after the Indonesia central bank, in a special meeting last week, hiked the benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to 7.0%. The move was seen as an attempt to pull the currency from its recent plunge, and also to address rising inflation pressures. But analysts think that immediate concern that plagues the rupiah in the open market is the lack of transparency and price discovery, which is why the NDF market still prices the USD/IDR at an exorbitant premium - a sign of poor investor confidence. The premium that the 1-month USD/IDR NDF contract commands over the spot price came down sharply - in reaction to Bank Indonesia's move - to IDR500 from almost IDR800 Wednesday, but it still remains very elevated considering it trades at around IDR20-IDR40 in stable market conditions. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for the spot USD/IDR is at 10,900 (psychological support), then at 10,800 (psychological support), before 10,500 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 11,000 (major psychological barrier), then at 11,500 (psychological resistance).

USD/INR - consolidation lower. The USD/INR could drift lower as the rupee finally reacts to the government's piecemeal attempts to shore up the currency. The latest move, which traders deem could be the most effective immediate measure to boost the rupee, has removed the main source of USD demand from the open market - the state-run oil companies. The RBI will now sell dollars directly to the 3 state-run oil firms, and thus eliminate their buying in the spot market which drives the USD/INR higher and thus depresses the INR. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 65.48 (upper Bollinger band standard deviation 2), then at 65.00 (psychological support), before 64.50 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 66.00 (psychological resistance), then at 66.50 (psychological resistance), before 67.00 (psychological resistance).

   By Sudeep Jain And Ashutosh Joshi 
 

MUMBAI--The Indian rupee fell to a fresh record low against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, as growing expectations of a U.S. military intervention in Syria pushed investors to seek safety in the dollar.

The rupee fell to as low as 65.93 to the U.S. dollar, down sharply from 64.30 late Monday in Asia.

The rupee's decline led to a sharp selloff in stocks, reversing the gains of the last three sessions.

The Bombay Stock Exchange's S&P BSE Sensex fell 2.4%, to 18110.70 points by Tuesday afternoon. The index has lost more than 5% this month, making it the worst-performing major stock market in Asia.

"Equity markets only look at the currency and nothing else," said Shardul Kulkarni, analyst at Mumbai brokerage Angel Broking Ltd.

The Indian currency has fallen more than 17% against the dollar since the start of May over fears that India will struggle to fund its wide current account deficit if the U.S. Federal Reserve winds down its easy-money policy. Currency dealers say that the Reserve Bank of India likely sold dollars in the previous two sessions to prevent the rupee's slide against the dollar.

On Tuesday, analysts said the dollar was higher against many emerging market currencies. In India specifically, "the passage of the food security bill has also hurt sentiment," said Rajeev Darji, an analyst at XDirect Global Solutions, an online currency trading firm in Mumbai.

India's lower house of Parliament on Monday passed a bill guaranteeing subsidized grain for nearly 70% of India's population. Analysts fear that this would add to the government's spending and could worsen its financial health.

Mr. Darji expects the rupee to weaken to 67.50 to the dollar in coming sessions.

On Tuesday, the dollar was also in demand by oil refiners who typically buy more dollars toward the end of month to settle import bills.

In stocks, banks and financial companies were the worst performers Tuesday, as the further weakening of rupee means the Reserve Bank of India will likely continue with liquidity tightening measures that have significantly increased the lenders' short-term borrowing costs.

Mortgage lender Housing Development Finance Corp was down 7.1% to 691.50 rupees ($10.5), while HDFC Bank was 5.6% lower at 576.00 rupees.

title: DJ 3rd UPDATE: Asian Shares Mixed After Selloff
text:
--Asian markets mixed after sharp selloff

--Shares rebound in Indonesia

--Official efforts to buoy markets calm investors

(Adds information, quotes, updates/adds market levels) 


 
   By Mia Lamar, Prasanta Sahu and Andreas Ismar 
 

Asian stocks were mixed Wednesday following a dramatic two-day selloff across the region that sent governments in the hardest-hit markets rushing to stem further declines.

Indonesia's benchmark Jakarta Composite Index was trading nearly 2% higher late afternoon, bouncing back from a sudden rout that sent the index down 9% in two days. Stocks in India were more volatile, rising as much as 1.8% before slipping into the red.

"India's central bank is adding to its woes by appearing to change its policy goals almost from one day to the next," said Nicholas Spiro, managing director of independent research firm Spiro Sovereign Strategy.

Officials have accelerated efforts to shore up the country's shaky financial markets, which have for days seen the rupee fall to new lows. The country is likely to go ahead with a plan to issue rupee-denominated bonds overseas, a senior government official told The Wall Street Journal Tuesday, in a bid to attract more capital and stem the rupee's decline.

The rupee remained weak Wednesday, trading at 63.73 per U.S. dollar after falling to as low as 64.11 late Tuesday.

State-driven intervention was seen in Indonesia as well. The country's central bank "continues to remain in the market to stabilize the rupiah exchange rate," Deputy Gov. Perry Warjiyo told the Wall Street Journal, confirming the views of money dealers who had suspected the central bank was in the market.

Rising expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will act next month to wind down its $85-billion-a-month bond buying program sparked a global selloff in financial markets this week, hitting Asia's emerging markets the hardest, as they have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the central bank's easy-money policies.

"This is an inflection point for Asia," said UBS economist Duncan Woolridge. "The last five years have been about getting exposure to Asia's debt-led growth story. That idea is probably finished."

Calmer trade in the U.S. bond market helped sentiment. Yields on the U.S. 10-year note edged back from the 3% mark, although strategists noted countries like Indonesia and India still face a tough road ahead.

"Although the Fed's possible liquidity tightening has been blamed, the underlying issue for these countries is a bleak outlook on economic growth for the rest of the year," said Kelly Teoh, market strategist at IG in Singapore.

In Tokyo, shares edged up 0.2% to 13,424.33, shaking off earlier losses after Tokyo Electric Power Co. reported its worst spill of highly radioactive water since the plant suffered a triple meltdown two years ago. Shares of the company, commonly known as Tepco, dropped 9.3%.

Sentiment also improved as the dollar regained strength against the Japanese currency, last changing hands at 97.56 yen versus 97.26 yen late Tuesday in New York.

Stocks in Hong Kong slumped after a bigger-than-expected rise in consumer prices last month. The Hang Seng Index fell 0.7%, led by declines in interest rate-sensitive property stocks.

Trade was choppy in Sydney as investors awaited minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's July policy meeting later in the trading day. The S&P ASX 200 was last up 0.4%.

Shares of local mining giant BHP Billiton fell 2.2% after the company reported its second-straight decline in annual profit.

title: DJ  Asia Takes Strain As Emerging-Market  Currency  Selloff Continues
text:
--Selling pressure on Indian rupee, Indonesian rupiah continues

--Bank Indonesia suspected of taking action to support rupiah, dealers say

--Turkey rate decision due at 1100 GMT

By Clare Connaghan

The selloff in Asian emerging market currencies intensified Tuesday with the Indian rupee plunging to a new life-time low, while the Indonesian rupiah fell to its weakest level since April 2009, amid concerns over how these countries will cope when the Federal Reserve starts withdrawing stimulus measures.

The rupee remained locked in a downward spiral Tuesday, falling to a fresh record low against the greenback of INR64.11. The Indonesian rupiah also felt the pain, slumping to a four-year low of IDR10,700 against the dollar, before the central bank was suspected of intervening to support the currency, dealers said. Bank Indonesia usually doesn't comment on specific interventions. The Thai baht also weakened to a one-year low, as expectations grew that minutes from the Fed's August meeting due Wednesday could signal that it will start pulling back from the stimulus measures that have supported markets for nearly five years, as early as September.

"The action in FX currently is in emerging market currencies, where the selloff continues in earnest," said Societe Generale in a note to clients.

The prospect of the Fed pulling back on its bond purchases has made investors fret that the tide of money that flowed into emerging markets in recent years will diminish. Countries such as India, which have large current-account deficits, reflecting a reliance on inflows of capital, have felt the brunt of investors fleeing emerging market assets.

The rupee has lost more than 5% in value against the dollar so far this month, despite authorites there taking a number measures to support the currency. But unless authories take more steps to bolster foreign-currency reserves that could be used to defend the rupee, the currency is unlikely to stabilize, analysts say. "This will likely require the issuance of either a Non-resident Indian bond or a sovereign bond," said Indranil Sen Gupta, an analyst at Bank of AmericaMerrill Lynch.

Europe's emerging markets were calmer. The Hungarian forint and Polish zloty, regained some ground against the euro following Monday's selloff.

The Turish lira bounced off record lows against the euro and one-month lows against the dollar, ahead of an interest rate decision at 1100 GMT. According to eight economists surveyed by Dow Jones Newswires, the central bank is expected to keep the benchmark one-week repo rate at 4.5%, the overnight borrowing rate at 3.5% and the overnight lending rate of 7.25%.

"I expect Turkey to stay on hold," said Christian Lawrence of Rabobank. But he does not rule out the chance that the lending rate may be raised by 0.5 percentage points.

In the major currencies, investors piled into the perceived safe havens of the yen and Swiss franc, with the former rising to one-week high against the dollar and the latter a one-week high against the euro

Elsewhere, the New Zealand dollar came under pressure against the buck after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand said it will introduce new restrictions on home loans in October.

The Australian dollar also weakened against the U.S. dollar after the central bank said there is the possibility of a further cut in interest rates.

In minutes of its Aug. 6 policy meeting--when the benchmark cash rate was cut to a record low 2.50%--the Reserve Bank of Australia said it will continue to watch economic data to assess the correct level of interest rates.

"Regarding the communication of this decision, members agreed that the bank should neither close off the possibility of reducing rates further, nor signal an imminent intention to reduce rates further," the minutes said.

The Norwegian krone fell to a six-week low against the euro after data showed Norway's economic growth was lower than expected in the second quarter.

At 1030 GMT, the euro was trading at $1.3400 against the dollar, compared with $1.3340, late Monday in New York, according to trading system EBS. The dollar was at Y97.230 against the yen, compared with Y97.57, while the euro was at Y130.27, compared with Y130.11. The pound was trading at $1.5670 against the dollar, compared with $1.5654 late Monday in New York.

The Wall Street Journal Dollar Index, which tracks the U.S. dollar against a basket of major currencies, was at 73.43 from 73.568.

(James Glynn in Sydney contributed to this story.)

title: Indonesia  c.bank say to continue  intervention  to stabilise rupiah
text:
JAKARTA, Aug 20 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank said on Tuesday it would contine interventing in the foregn exchange market to stabilise the rupiah and buy government bonds in the secondary market.

The comments by Deputy Governor Perry Warjiyo followed a third day of sharp falls in Indonesia's financial markets, triggered by concerns of the economy and broader worries about the impact of a cut in the U.S. Fed's monetary stimulus on emerging markets in general.

"In two days, we have bought about 2.6 trillion rupiah ($247.86 million) of government bonds ... (Bank Indonesia) will remain in the market intervening in the forex market to stabilise the rupiah," he told reporters. He did not say how much foreign exchange intervention there had been. Other Applicable Definitions

"IDR Business Day" means a day on which commercial banks and foreign exchange markets settle payments in Tokyo, New York, Singapore and Jakarta.

"IDR Rate" means, in respect of an IDR Valuation Date, the IDR/JPY exchange rate, expressed as the amount of JPY per one IDR, which is calculated by the Calculation Agent in accordance with the following formula and rounded to the nearest five decimal places with 0.000005 being rounded up:

USD/JPY Reference Rate divided by USD/IDR Reference Rate

"IDR Valuation Date" means the day that is five (5) Relevant Business Days prior to the relevant Fixed Rate Interest Payment Date or the Maturity Date, as applicable (a "Scheduled IDR Valuation Date"), or, if such day is an Unscheduled Holiday, the immediately following Relevant Business Day, in which case the related Fixed Rate Interest Payment Date or the Maturity Date, as applicable, shall be postponed to fall five (5) Relevant Business Days after such deferred IDR Valuation Date; provided that, if the IDR Valuation Date has not occurred on or before the tenth (10(th) ) consecutive day after the Scheduled IDR Valuation Date, then the next day after such tenth (10(th) ) day that would have been a Relevant Business Day but for the Unscheduled Holiday shall be deemed to be the IDR Valuation Date.

"Reference Dealers" means five banks active in the USD/IDR or USD/JPY currency and foreign exchange market, as applicable, as selected by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

"Unscheduled Holiday" means a day that is not a Relevant Business Day and the market was not aware of such fact (by means of a public announcement or by reference to other publicly available information) until a time later than 9:00 a.m. local time in the principal financial centre(s) of IDR five (5) Relevant Business Days prior to the Scheduled IDR Valuation Date.

"USD" means United States dollars.

"USD/IDR Reference Rate" means the spot rate of USD/IDR at 11:00 a.m. Singapore time expressed as the number of IDR per one USD and published on the Reuters Screen "ABSIRFIX01" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate) on the applicable IDR Valuation Date, as determined by the Calculation Agent.

In the event that no such quotation appears on the Reuters Screen "ABSIRFIX01" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate), the USD/IDR Reference Rate shall be determined by the Calculation Agent by requesting quotations for mid rate of USD/IDR foreign exchange rate at or about 11:00 a.m. Singapore time on the first (1st) IDR Business Day following the relevant IDR Valuation Date from the Reference Dealers.

If five or four quotations are provided as requested, the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be the arithmetic mean (rounded to the nearest whole IDR, 0.5 being rounded upwards) of the remaining three or two such quotations, as the case may be, for such rate provided by the Reference Dealers, after disregarding the highest such quotation and the lowest such quotation (provided that, if two or more such quotations are the highest such quotations, then only one of such quotations shall be disregarded, and if two or more such quotations are the lowest quotations, then only one of such lowest quotations will be disregarded).

If only three or two such quotations are provided as requested, the USD/IDR Reference Rate shall be determined as described above except that the highest and lowest quotations will not be disregarded.

If none or only one of the Reference Dealers provides such quotation, the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

"USD/JPY Reference Rate" means the mid rate of USD/JPY, expressed as the number of JPY per one USD, published on the Reuters Screen "JPNU" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate) as of 12:00 p.m., Tokyo time on the applicable IDR Valuation Date, as determined by the Calculation Agent. If five or four quotations are provided as requested, the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be the arithmetic mean (rounded to the nearest whole IDR, 0.5 being rounded upwards) of the remaining three or two such quotations, as the case may be, for such rate provided by the Reference Dealers, after disregarding the highest such quotation and the lowest such quotation (provided that, if two or more such quotations are the highest such quotations, then only one of such quotations shall be disregarded, and if two or more such quotations are the lowest quotations, then only one of such lowest quotations will be disregarded).

title: STOCKS NEWS INDONESIA-Telkom rises on Q2 earnings
text:
Shares in PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia rose as much as 3.1 percent after the telecom provider announced its second-quarter results.

Net profit grew 12.7 percent to 10.1 trillion rupiah ($1.01 billion) year-on-year, Telkom said in statement on Friday. The company's shares had the second-highest turnover on the stock exchange.

Indonesian blue-chip stocks rose 0.02 percent, while the broader Jakarta Composite Index was up 0.1 percent.

1510 (0810 GMT)

($1 = 10,060 rupiah)

(Reporting by Andjarsari Paramaditha in Jakarta; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)

***************************************************************  13:30 STOCKS NEWS INDONESIA-Property, utility firms' earnings could beat forecasts-Citi Citi Research expects a weak second-quarter for commodity-related and auto sector companies, while property, media and utility firms could beat consensus estimates, it said in a note on Friday.

Property companies are to benefit from strong pre-marketing sales last year, the note said. Media companies could book higher advertising rates, while utilities would benefit primarily from forex gains.

Plantation's downside could be due to higher labour costs and lower crude palm oil prices, while plunging spot coal prices on weak demand from China and India could hurt mining earnings. Auto firms would also be under pressure due to price discounts linked to competition and a weaker rupiah, the note said.

"We believe the volatility in the market will continue due to fears of QE tapering and slower China growth of around 7 percent," the note stated.

"On the Indonesia-specific front, the central bank has reduced its intervention, letting the rupiah weaken in line with the regional currencies. We expect inflation to peak in July, and see a slight improvement in the current account due to the fuel price adjustment."

Citi's top picks includes property developers Alam Sutera Realty and Bumi Serpong Damai, television operator Media Nusantara Citra, cement maker Indocement Tunggal Perkasa and toll road operator Jasa Marga.

Alam Sutera shares were up 1.77 percent at 780 rupiah.

The broader index was up 0.25 percent.

1328 (0628 GMT)

(Reporting by Andjarsari Paramaditha in Jakarta; Editing by Prateek Chatterjee)

***************************************************************  11:20 STOCKS NEWS INDONESIA-Bahana cuts Bank Danamon to 'reduce'

Bahana Securities downgraded lender PT Bank Danamon Tbk  to "reduce" from "hold", citing earnings pressure due to lower margins and additional provisioning and delay in an acquisition deal.     "Going forward, we believe that margin pressure will persist on the back of higher blended cost of funds and intensifying competition in mass market loans," analyst Teguh Hartanto said in a note on Friday.     The research house also said the delay in an acquisition deal due to pending approval from the central bank has resulted in uncertainties in the outlook on Danamon.     Last month, DBS Group Holdings Ltd said it could review its planned acquisition of a stake in Danamon if the Singapore lender was allowed to buy only a 40 percent share.      "Unfortunately, this has become a controversy issue as BI recently revamped regulation on acquisition, limiting ownership of financial institutions in a bank up to 40 percent, implying share acquisitions of more than 40 percent must be transacted through several stages, subject to BI's reviews on healthiness and GCG rating," Hartanto said.     Bahana also slashed its target price on Danamon's shares to 4,500 rupiah from 5,800 and said the company's weak second-quarter earnings prompted the research house to lower its mass-market loan growth estimates for 2013 and 2014 by 13 and 17 percent, respectively.     The lender's shares dropped 1.75 percent to 5,600 rupiah. The broader index was up 0.37 percent.     1111 (0411 GMT)     (Reporting by Andjarsari Paramaditha, Editing by Anupama Dwivedi)

title: Asian c.banks take differing approaches to stemming outflows
text:
JAKARTA, July 10 (Reuters) - Asian central banks are expected to adopt divergent strategies to protect their economies against weaker growth and scary foreign capital outflows as they hold policy reviews amid a sea-change in international markets.

For much of Asia, the prospect of the U.S. Federal Reserve winding down its easy money policies has removed the headache of asset-inflating inflows, though the speed at which funds have pulled out has created a whole new set of worries for some.

Central banks in Indonesia and India, which rely on foreign capital to fund current account deficits and are therefore more vulnerable to portfolio outflows, have been forced to intervene in the market to defend their weakening currencies.

Bank Indonesia is expected to hike its benchmark policy rate for a second consecutive month at a policy review on Thursday, and could announce surprise measures to counter surging inflation, a declining rupiah currency and falling foreign exchange reserves.

"The limelight is certainly on Bank Indonesia (BI), especially following the recent comment that they have a mix of policies in their toolbox to cope with the recent spike in inflationary pressures," said Gundy Cahyadi, economist at OCBC in Singapore.

But for other Asian central banks, the situation is not as dire as capital outflows and inflation remain manageable.

They are unlikely to immediately tighten broadly easy policy settings in response to the changing Fed outlook.

Thailand's central bank on Wednesday kept its policy rate unchanged at 2.50 percent as expected, after a recent cut to support growth and curb capital inflows.

Malaysia and South Korea were expected also to hold policy rates steady when their monetary policy committees meet on Thursday.

"Asian central banks are generally mercantilist and will pick a weaker currency and higher growth," said Sean Yokota, head of Asian strategy at SEB. "The pace (of a currency's decline) may be open to debate, but the direction is fine with them."

In Indonesia, however, Yokoto noted that inflation was likely to head above 8 percent by year-end. Even if that was not sustained, he said, interest rates at 6 percent and 5-year government bond yields at 6.7 percent were too low.

Indeed, Bank Indonesia last month became the first Asian central bank to hike its benchmark rate since 2011, and was widely expected to follow with another 25-basis-point move to 6.25 percent on Thursday.

"Countries that run current account deficits tend to be more vulnerable because of the pressure in the balance of payments. As a whole though, external liquidity risk in the region remains manageable at least for now," Cahyadi said.

BIG TOOL KIT

Beyond raising its benchmark rate, BI could also hike its overnight deposit facility rate (FASBI) after the central bank indicated it would "strengthen its policy mix" at this week's meeting, analysts said.

BI has also hinted it could soon introduce measures like tradable term deposits and an auction market in foreign exchange swaps to stem the flow of foreign funds.

Analysts believe Indonesia should also introduce macroprudential measures such as a holding period for exporters' profits to slow declining foreign exchange reserves, which dropped to a two-year low of $98.1 billion in June.

Indonesian policymakers were not alone in reviewing their full range of tools in the face of the biggest inflection point for investors since 2008.

India's regulators on Monday toughened rules for derivatives trading in the currency market in a bid to arrest the steep decline of the rupee, which fell to a record low against the dollar this week and is emerging Asia's worst performer this year.

(Additional reporting by Sonali Desai in SINGAPORE, Kitiphong Thaichareon in BANGKOK, Christine Kim in SEOUL and Anuradha Raghu in KUALA LUMPUR; Editing by Simon Cameron-Moore)

If the USD/PHP pair ends the week below 43.54, some upside pressure will ease. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 43.00 (psychological support), before 42.70 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 43.54 (200-week moving average), then at 43.89 (monthly Bollinger mid), before 44.00 (major psychological resistance).

Immediate resistance is at 9,950 (suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention), before 10,000 (major psychological barrier).

Better-than-expected industrial production figures released late Monday could also give the Taiwan dollar room to breathe. The industrial production data for May showed a contraction of 0.07% versus expectations for a 1.46% drop. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 30.110 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 30.000 (psychological support), before 29.920 (20-day Bollinger mid). Immediate resistance is likely at 30.300 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 30.380 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/KRW -- consolidation with upside bias. USD/KRW still appears to be very well-bid, though the pair is slightly overextended on the daily Bollinger band charts. The dollar broke a one-year high Monday after breaching the KRW1,160 psychological barrier, which may now serve as a resistance as the pair opens Tuesday lower at KRW1,159. A mild recovery in the Kospi, currently up 0.1%, appears to be underway and this may help the South Korean won to recoup some losses. However, the won will remain on a path toward weakness unless the USD/KRW pair ends Tuesday below KRW1,142 -- the base of the Bollinger uptrend channel. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is 1,150 (psychological support), then at 1,148 (base of monthly Bollinger uptrend channel), before 1,142 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1,160 (psychological resistance), before 1,170 (psychological resistance).

USD/SGD -- consolidation lower. USD/SGD may slip down to 1.2686, which is the bottom of the daily Bollinger uptrend channel. The long-tailed doji candlestick Monday suggests upside momentum may be approaching exhaustion and thus the next move could be lower. The short-term uptrend bias, however, will remain intact so long as the pair ends the day above 1.2686. In order to nullify the bullish bias, USD/SGD needs to close below the uptrend channel, which could then hint at a move even lower to the 20-day Bollinger mid at 1.2589. The Sing dollar may have gotten a slight boost from Monday's higher-than-forecast CPI reading. Inflation rose 1.6% on year compared with estimates for a 1.2% increase. The Monetary Authority of Singapore uses the Singapore dollar's relative strength to help control imported inflation, and thus may engineer a stronger Sing dollar by intervening in the currency market when the currency falls. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.2700 (psychological support), then at 1.2686 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 1.2600 (psychological support). A sharp move lower could spook the weak holders of long-USD/MYR positions, who would then capitulate and sell the dollar. The external factor to watch for in these risk-sensitive markets may be Chinese stocks -- if another sharp fall occurs, the U.S. dollar could rise again. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is 3.2000 (psychological support), then at 3.1800 (psychological support), before 3.1750 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 3.2200 (psychological resistance), before 3.2500 (major psychological barrier).

Immediate resistance is at 31.06 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud), then at 31.09 (weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), before 31.36 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

title: 4th UPDATE: Asian Shares Sharply Lower On Fed Result, Weak China Data
text:
--Asia down on Fed pullback, weak China PMI

--Chinese banks lower on liquidity concerns

--Dollar hits one year high against peso, ringgit, all-time high against rupee

(Adds information, quotes, updates/adds market levels)


 
  By Daniel Inman 
 

A broad sell-off hit Asian markets Thursday, driving currencies and stock markets to long-term lows following another bearish reading on China's economy and the strongest indication yet that the U.S. Federal Reserve is poised to begin winding down its bond-buying program.

Chinese and China-related stocks tumbled, the Indian rupee hit a record low and gold fell to its lowest price in nearly three years. Stocks in Southeast Asia, where smaller markets are especially vulnerable to outflows of foreign funds, suffered some of the biggest drops. In Indonesia, the Jakarta Composite Index fell 3.7%.

The release of data indicating that China's manufacturing activity contracted again in June accelerated early selling that had begun after the Fed suggested overnight that it would begin cutting back its bond buying by year's end.

"Emerging Asia is in a tight corner, between U.S. monetary policy and their own issues," said Angelo Corbetta, head of Asian equities at Pioneer Investments, which had $197.9 billion of assets under management at the end of October. "And most of the silver bullets have been used already."

Indications that the Fed could start winding down its stimulus have led to heavy outflows from Asian emerging markets in recent weeks and the selling continued Thursday. The Philippines' PSE Composite was last down 2.9% and Thailand's SET fell 3%.

Chinese markets fell sharply after a gauge of manufacturing activity fell to its lowest level in nine months. Also weighing on sentiment was a cash crunch among Chinese banks that has pushed interbank lending rates to the highest levels in two years and made banks more cautious about lending.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index lost 2.9%, its worst decline by percentage since July, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell 3.3%. On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index lost 2.8%.

Chinese banks listed in Hong Kong were big losers. China Construction Bank fell 5.2%, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China lost 3.8% and China Minsheng Banking Corp. dropped 6.3%.

"Liquidity conditions remain tight, while the latest data shows that China's manufacturing activity continues to contract, putting further pressure on the economy," said Zhang Gang, an analyst at Central China Securities. "Due to a lack of positive catalysts, the market will likely continue to find its bottom."

HSBC's preliminary China purchasing managers index for June came in at 48.3, compared to a final reading of 49.2 in May. A figure below 50 indicates a contraction.

Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 dived 2.1%, its biggest fall since May 2012. China is Australia's largest trading partner. The Australian dollar plunged to a 33-month low. It has fallen more than 10% this year due to a combination of slowing growth, slumping commodity prices and expectations of interest-rate cuts.

In Tokyo, companies with strong exposure to China underperformed the broader market. Construction and mining equipment manufacturer Komatsu sank 3.8% and industrial robotics firm Fanuc Corp. dropped 3.2%. The Nikkei Stock Average fell 1.7% despite the U.S. dollar's rise against the yen, which usually benefits Japanese stocks.

The dollar jumped 1.2% against the yen overnight and continued climbing in Asian trading. The dollar was recently at Y98.02, compared with Y96.47 late Wednesday in New York.

Selling of equities helped drive down the region's other currencies, which have been under pressure in recent weeks due to outflows prompted by expectations of stronger growth and rising yields in the U.S. The dollar hit one-year highs against the Philippine peso and the Malaysian ringgit. Indonesia's central bankintervened to prop up its currency.

Spot gold fell 3.4% to $1,304.90 a troy ounce, its lowest price since September 2010. Gold saw some of the biggest gains of any asset in recent years because of the Fed's stimulus program, which many thought would trigger high inflation. Gold is considered a hedge against inflation.

Immediate resistance is at 30.94 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance), then at 30.96 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 31.00 (psychological resistance).

USD/PHP --consolidation lower. USD/PHP is likely to fall back toward the weekly Ichimoku Cloud at 42.60 and then consolidate. The greenback is retreating sharply as risk appetite returns. The market seems to be coming around to the notion that the U.S. Federal Reserve reducing its pace of bond purchases doesn't mean interest rates will be hiked yet. As long as the market believes benchmark U.S. interest rates will continue to be kept low for some time, the greenback will slide back down again. Manila stocks will likely recover strongly from the recent selloff, which will thus help the peso to rebound as well. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 43.00 (psychological support), then at 42.60 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud support), before 42.50 (psychological support). Immediate resistance is at 43.50 (psychological resistance), before 43.87 (monthly Bollinger mid resistance).

USD/IDR -- consolidation lower. Spot USD/IDR slipped a tad after the Indonesian central bank raised the benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.0%, which surprised the market. The rupiah only rose mildly on the policy decision Thursday, but it could get a huge boost from the overnight slump of the U.S. dollar as the market readjusts its expectations of what U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Bernanke will say at next week's policy meeting. The WSJ article--that the Fed might keep rates low even if bond buying eases--boosted investor sentiment overnight and is triggering a selloff in long-USD positions. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 9,800 (psychological support), then at 9,790 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 9,750 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 9,850 (suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention), before 9,900 (psychological resistance).

USD/INR -- downside bias. USD/INR is likely to turn around and slip toward the base of the Bollinger uptrend channel at 56.56, though the 57.00 psychological barrier will likely help prop up the pair in the interim. The chart reversal signal confirmed Wednesday, coupled with the additional long-tailed doji candlestick Thursday, presents a convincing case that the USD/INR pair is overbought and due for a pullback. The overnight fall in the WSJ Dollar Index, due to a change in the way the market perceives the Federal Reserve will act at next week's policy meeting, will help pressure the pair lower. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 57.00 (psychological support), then at 56.56 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 58.00 (psychological resistance), then at 58.50 (psychological resistance), before 58.98 (record high).

title: DJ  Bank Indonesia Surprises With 25-BPs Hike in Overnight Deposit Rate to 4.25%
text:
JAKARTA--Bank Indonesia has raised the interest rate of its overnight deposit facility 25 basis points to 4.25% with immediate effect, to help ease mounting pressures on the rupiah, the central bank said Wednesday.

The central bank is "ready to take any necessary step" to maintain monetary stability following the rupiah's recent depreciation, Bank Indonesia said in a press release.

The surprise hike in the overnight rate comes ahead of the central bank policy meeting Thursday, where analysts have said the bank is likely to hold its benchmark BI rate at 5.75% for the 16th consecutive month.

The pressures on the rupiah intensified recently as foreign investors pulled out from Indonesian bonds and stocks in anticipation of a cutback in the U.S. Federal Reserve's bond-buying program, amid signs of economic recovery there.

The U.S. dollar traded at IDR9,830 late Tuesday among banks in Jakarta, but banks have been selling the greenback to customers above IDR10,000 since Monday. Local stocks fell 3.5% Tuesday, while the yield of government rupiah-denominated bonds rose an average 12 basis points.

Bank Indonesia has been suspected of selling dollars in the market since last month to slow the rupiah's depreciation. The rupiah has fallen nearly 3.5% against the dollar so far this year, also due to concerns over the country's current-account deficit.

Bank Indonesia said last week foreign-exchange reserves fell by about $2.3 billion last month to $105 billion, which economists said was mostly due to its intervention to defend the local currency.

Bank Indonesia said Wednesday it will continue to supply the market with dollars if needed.

The government later this month plans to raise subsidized fuel prices to discourage consumption of such fuels, which in turn will help reduce fuel imports.

Finance Minister Chatib Basri told reporters late Tuesday that he expects the rupiah will appreciate after the government raises subsidized fuel prices.

"The government's plan is clear that subsidized fuel prices will be increased," Mr. Basri said. "The market will welcome the policy."
