title: EM ASIA  FX -Rupiah weak despite c.bank deposit rate rise, outflows hit baht
text:
* Indonesia c.bank makes surprise 25 bps hike in FASBI rate     * Bank Indonesia: ready to supply dollars to support rupiah     * Thai finmin says not worried about fund outflows   (Adds text, updates prices)     By Jongwoo Cheon     SINGAPORE, June 12 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah stayed weak on Wednesday despite the central bank's surprise increase in its overnight facility rate and its pledge to provide more dollar liquidity, while the Thai baht hit a nine-month low on capital outflows.     Bank Indonesia announced late on Tuesday that it was raising the FASBI rate, which it pays commercial banks for deposits, by 25 basis points to 4.25 percent, effective Wednesday.       The central bank on Wednesday said it was ready to ensure large supplies of dollars to support a weakening rupiah and to buy government bonds in the secondary market.        But the rupiah's spot indicative price fell 0.3 percent to 9,850 per dollar.

 The currency traded weaker than that level with some dollar bids seen above 10,000 earlier, according to traders.     "BI apparently felt that they couldn't wait until tomorrow. They wanted to react before things moved too quickly," said Sean Yokota, head of Asia strategy at Scandinavian bank SEB in Singapore, referring to the central bank's scheduled policy meeting on Thursday.     On Tuesday, the rupiah fell below 10,000 to the dollar for the first time since 2009, as dollar liquidity tightened up on speculation that a tapering of monetary stimulus by the Federal Reserve may cause capital flight from emerging Asia.     The central bank was also spotted providing dollars for intervention to support the rupiah.     Indonesia and India are the most vulnerable among emerging Asian markets to capital outflows, triggered by expectations of higher U.S. interest rates, as these countries run massive current account deficits that are financed primarily by foreign portfolio investments.     Notwithstanding a sell-off in the past three weeks, foreigners have not been liquidating Indonesian government bonds too heavily, and they still hold around 34 percent of them, near the record level.     Analysts suspect a large part of the pressure on the rupiah is being felt in currency markets as investors hold onto their high-yielding assets but seek some protection against currency volatility.     Some analysts said Bank Indonesia's efforts may relieve the rupiah.     Reflecting such views, the rupiah forwards recovered earlier losses with one-month dollar/rupiah non-deliverable forwards  a tad lower in the afternoon after rising.     HSBC said the rupiah may find more support if the government finalises a long-awaited reduction in fuel subsidies.     The bank said the central bank's decision to raise the FASBI rate "was unexpected, but a step in the right direction."     "In the next few days, if there is finally an announcement on fuel subsidy cuts, this could give market sentiment towards IDR assets another shot in the arm," it wrote in a client note.     Indonesia has been agonising for months over how to cut fuel price subsidies that are devouring the budget and widening the country's current account deficit. But the reduction is seen accelerating inflation at the same time. An increase in fuel prices is generally expected, but the timing has been uncertain.     Still, the rupiah is not free from speculation about the Federal Reserve tapering monetary stimulus. The expectations have supported the U.S. dollar.     Gundy Cahyadi of OCBC Bank said that how the rupiah fares will depend on how the dollar broadly performs. "If U.S. dollar/Singapore dollar spikes to 1.28 or something, one will expect to see dollar/rupiah much higher despite the FASBI hike."     The city-state's currency barely changed at 1.2552 to the U.S. dollar.


    
    BAHT
    The baht lost 0.7 percent to 31.17 per dollar, its weakest
since Sept. 11, 2012, pressured by outflows from Thai stocks and
bonds.
    Finance Minister Kittirat Na Ranong said he was not worried
about recent capital outflows because they could help balance
flows and the Thai baht. 
    Bangkok stocks hit a near five-month low, while bonds lost
ground.
    The 10-year government bond yield jumped to 4.11
percent, its highest since March 2010. The five-year yields rose
to 3.37 percent, the highest since October last year.
    "The equities and bonds sell-off still continues," said a
senior Thai bank trader in Bangkok, adding that the baht is
weakening to the previous low of 31.25 in the short term.
    
    WON
    The won edged higher on demand from exporters such as
shipbuilders for settlements.
    Earlier, the South Korean currency rose as much as 0.6


percent with Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd 
announcing it had won a 1.46 trillion won ($1.29 billion) order.
 
    The finance ministry also played down market concerns about
a potential surge in capital outflows, saying that foreign
central banks and institutional investors continued to buy local
debt and showed no signs of pulling out. 
    Still, the won gave up most of its initial gains as foreign
investors kept selling Seoul shares. Offshore funds also
reduced won holdings, traders said.
    Foreigners were net sellers for a fourth consecutive session
in Seoul's main stock market. They dumped a combined net
2.2 trillion won during those four days, according to Korea
Exchange Data.
    "Dollar demand from custodian banks and offshore funds stood
out. Investors tried to buy dollar/won whenever it fell," said a
South Korean bank trader in Seoul.

title: DJ   FX  CHAT: USD/IDR Up; IDR Depreciation Healthy Correction-Citi
text:
The USD/IDR is slightly higher at 9,820 in the interbank market vs 9,815 on the greenback's general strength, with suspected Bank Indonesia's intervention slowing the pair's rise. Two dealers suspect the central bank to have sold around $30 million at 9,820 as foreign investors continued to sell local stocks and bonds Monday, exacerbated also by concerns over the country's current account deficit and the government's budget deficit. Although the USD/IDR is gearing toward 10,000, Citigroup says in a report that the IDR's depreciation is still a healthy adjustment. Although the IDR has weakened by about 3.5% vs the USD year-to-date, on a trade-weighted and inflation-adjusted basis, the IDR had in fact strengthened by about 2%, it says; "arguably a weakening of the IDR on real effective exchange rate basis is more desirable to correct the external imbalance." Dealers tip a 9,810-9,840 band for the pair in the session.(i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

text:
[Dow Jones] The USD/IDR is higher at 9,820 vs 9,810 late Friday on the greenback's general strength, but suspected intervention by Bank Indonesia helps to slow the pair's rise, dealers say. Two dealers suspects the central bank to have sold around $100 million in total around 9,810. "Bank Indonesia's intervention helps calm the market but, I don't think Bank Indonesia will fight the dollar's rise," one of the traders says; he tips a 9,810-9,830 range Monday. text:

          Immediate Range Larger Range 
 
 
   USD/CNY       -              - 

USD/TWD 29.890-30.000 29.710-30.200


   USD/KRW   1,20-1,128    1,117-1,130

   USD/PHP  42.00-42.20    41.76-42.31 
   USD/IDR  9,770-9,800    9,720-9,820 
   USD/INR  57.00-57.00    56.48-57.40 
 

(Ranges are calculated using recent highs and lows, information on the placement of option strikes, and technical analysis - Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci levels, trendlines and moving averages.)

USD/CNY - markets are closed today for a holiday.

USD/TWD - consolidation with upside bias. USD/TWD could rise back above the 20-day Bollinger mid and take on a mild upside bias once more if the pair follows the lead of dollar/yen higher. If USD/TWD ends the way above 30.050, where the Bollinger uptrend channel begins, upside momentum could increase. The rise in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, after the slightly better-than-expected U.S. non-farm payrolls report Friday, could mean a stronger greenback this week. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is likely at 30.000 (psychological resistance), then at 30.050 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 30.200 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel and psychological resistance). Immediate support is at 29.890 (20-day Bollinger mid), then at 29.760 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 29.710 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud).

USD/KRW - consolidation with upside bias. USD/KRW gaps up above 1,120 on the back of higher U.S. government bond yields, which are supportive of the greenback. USD/KRW may be headed for the daily Bollinger uptrend channel at 1,128, which could impart a stronger bullish bias to the pair. The Kospi will be keenly watched for signs of weakness, particularly Samsung shares which fell sharply last week and dragged the index down. Poor China export data and industrial production over the weekend could imply a slightly weaker outlook for South Korea's exporters as well. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 1,128 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 1,130 (psychological resistance). Immediate support is 1,120 (psychological support), then at 1,117 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), before 1,111 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud).

USD/SGD - consolidation. USD/SGD may drift in a range of 1.2482-1.2560, bounded by the Bollinger downtrend channel support and the 20-day Bollinger mid. The pair is rising along with USD/JPY at the moment, but whether or not the pair can break out of this range may depend on how equities perform. After Wall Street's gains Friday, Singapore's STI could rally and help support the Singapore dollar. However, poor exports and industrial production data out of China over the weekend could dampen risk appetite in Asia. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.2500 (psychological support), then at 1.2482 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 1.2404 (daily Ichimoku Cloud). Immediate resistance is at 1.2560 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance), then at 1.2600 (psychological resistance).

USD/MYR - upside bias. USD/MYR breaks higher past the psychological resistance at 3.1000 and may soon test the top of the Bollinger uptrend channel at 3.1250. The greenback is rising across the board, led by USD/JPY, after Friday's slightly better-than-expected U.S. non-farm payrolls data. The increase in jobs added led to another selloff in U.S. government bonds that drove the 10-year Treasury yield up again, boosting the greenback. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 3.1100 (weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 3.1200 (psychological resistance), before 3.1250 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate support is 3.1000 (psychological support), then at 3.0870 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 3.0790 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 3.0500 (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud).

USD/THB - upside bias. USD/THB is likely to continue rising toward 30.94, the weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance. The pair looks bullish, supported by the weekly Bollinger mid line at 30.41 and pulled up by the daily Bollinger uptrend channel. The Bank of Thailand's threat of intervention in the event of excessive currency strength may help support USD/THB on dips as investors trim their exposure to the baht. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 30.94 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance), before 31.00 (psychological resistance). Immediate support is at 30.41 (weekly Bollinger mid support), then at 30.00 (psychological support and base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP - upside bias. USD/PHP is likely to follow USD/JPY upward, fuelled by bullish undertones for the dollar. The next target for the USD/PHP pair may be the top of the weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone at 42.60. The market is increasingly leaning toward the possibility that the U.S. Federal Reserve will taper off the pace of its bond purchases soon, which is thus giving the dollar a boost. The U.S. non-farms payroll data on Friday, though not exceptional, gave traders more indication that the labor market is improving and thus less government stimulus may be necessary. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 42.20 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 42.31 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), before 42.60 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud). Immediate support is at 42.00 (psychological support), then at 41.80 (base of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 41.76 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/IDR - consolidation with upside bias. Spot USD/IDR will be stable due to suspected central bank intervention around 9.810, but the USD/IDR NDF market is already pricing a stronger dollar. The 1-month NDF contract, the most liquid one, has breached levels above 10,000--not seen since 2009--and could be on the way to the next major psychological resistance at 10,500 next. The greenback is broadly stronger as traders price in the increasing likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve may start tapering the pace of its asset purchases, which will undoubtedly push U.S bond yields, and thus the dollar, higher as well. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 9,800 (psychological resistance and top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 9,810 (suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention), before 9,820 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate support is at 9,770 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 9,740 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before 9,720 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support).

USD/INR - consolidation with upside bias. USD/INR is likely to maintain its upside bias as the dollar gets a lift from slightly-better-than-expected U.S. non-farm payrolls data Friday. The bullish dollar tone is likely to pull the USD/INR pair even higher past the psychological barrier of 57.00, though the topside could be limited by the top of the monthly Bollinger uptrend channel at 57.40. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 57.33 (June 2012 high), before 57.40 (top of monthly Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate support is at 57.00 (psychological support), then at 56.48 (weekly upper Bollinger band standard deviation 2), before 56.00 (psychological support).

(Ranges are calculated using recent highs and lows, information on the placement of option strikes, and technical analysis - Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci levels, trendlines and moving averages.)

USD/CNY - consolidation. There could be a small uptick in Wednesday's dollar/yuan parity rate as the PBOC's valuation method likely correlates well to USD/JPY, which rose overnight above Y100.00. The blip higher in the WSJ Dollar Index and the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield may trigger mild dollar bullishness which will keep spot USD/CNY supported. The mid- to long-term USD/CNY NDF contracts may however trade with a softer tone due to PBOC governor Zhou Xiaochuan saying on Monday that the time is right for interest rate reform - which will speed up the path toward China liberalizing its currency as well. The market is still keenly betting on another step toward freeing up the yuan trading regime this year. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support for USD/CNY is at 6.1210 (June 3 record low), then at 6.1061 (base of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), before 6.1045 (bottom of weekly Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is likely at 6.1371 (top of daily Bollinger downtrend channel), then at 6.1400 (psychological resistance), before 6.1500 (psychological resistance).

USD/TWD - consolidation. USD/TWD could drift within a range of 29.890-30.050, bounded by the 20-day Bollinger mid support and the Bollinger uptrend channel. If this range breaks, the USD/TWD pair could see follow-through movement. The greenback is firming up on the back of hawkish talk from U.S. Federal Reserve voting member Esther George, who said that some sectors are overly reliant on cheap money funded by stimulus measures. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield also rose overnight to 2.15% from about 2.11%, thus supporting the greenback. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 30.000 (psychological support), before 29.890 (20-day Bollinger mid). Immediate resistance is likely at 30.050 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 30.200 (top of daily Bollinger uptrend channel and psychological resistance), before 30.330 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/KRW - consolidation. The USD/KRW pair will likely face an uphill task of rallying unless it can close above the 1,129 level today. The pair is likely to be trapped within a 1,120-1,129 range, supported by the daily Ichimoku Cloud and capped by the Bollinger uptrend channel. The greenback is rising slightly at the open due to the overnight bounce in USD/JPY, but it remains to be seen if there is any momentum to this move; USD/JPY is still biased lower on the daily charts. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 1,120 (daily Ichimoku Cloud and psychological support), then at 1,116 (20-day Bollinger mid support), before (base of daily Ichimoku Cloud). Immediate resistance is at 1,129 (daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 1,130 (psychological resistance).

USD/SGD - downside bias. USD/SGD still looks slightly bearish under the 20-day Bollinger mid at 1.2546, but an overall firmer WSJ Dollar Index overnight could lift the pair up above this key pivot and negate the downside bias. If however, the Bollinger mid resistance holds, the USD/SGD pair could slip toward the daily Bollinger downtrend channel at 1.2447 next. The market will be focusing on Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls, which could determine how soon the Federal Reserve pulls back from quantitative easing. Dow Jones technical analysis shows immediate support is at 1.2500 (psychological support), before 1.2447 (daily Bollinger downtrend channel). Immediate resistance is at 1.2546 (20-day Bollinger mid resistance), then at 1.2600 (psychological resistance).

USD/MYR - upside bias. USD/MYR continues to trade with a bullish technical bias on the daily charts, guided higher by the Bollinger uptrend channel and propped up by the Ichimoku Cloud support zone at 3.0790. The greenback is inching back up, helped by hawkish comments from U.S. Federal Reserve board member Esther George, who said that businesses may be addicted to cheap funding. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose on her comments, adding to the supportive-USD tone overnight. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 3.0980 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud), then at 3.1000 (major psychological resistance), before 3.1070 (weekly Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate support is 3.0820 (base of weekly Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 3.0790 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), before 3.0730 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/THB - consolidation with upside bias. USD/THB may stay elevated near the top of the Bollinger uptrend channel with the bounce in the WSJ Dollar Index overnight. Further upside for the pair appears likely, though the pace of the move may be slow, since the pair is already at the upper confines of the Bollinger uptrend channel. The next major target for the USD/THB pair could be the 30.95 weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 30.50 (psychological resistance), before 30.95 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance). Immediate support is at 30.40 (weekly Bollinger mid support), then at 30.00 (psychological support), before 29.95 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP - consolidation with upside bias. USD/PHP remains biased higher along the Bollinger uptrend channel which now supports at 41.65. The pair could next target the major resistance at 42.60 that is the top of the weekly Ichimoku Cloud. The dollar is likely to stay well-bid above the 42.00 psychological mark for now, given the blip up in the WSJ Dollar Index overnight. Dollar bulls were encouraged by comments from U.S. Federal Reserve board member Esther George who reiterated her stand against excessive cheap funding engineered by the Fed's quantitative easing. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 42.31 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 42.50 (psychological resistance), before 42.60 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud). Immediate support is at 42.00 (psychological support), then at 41.80 (base of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), before 41.65 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/IDR - consolidation. USD/IDR is likely to trade with a supportive tone, but may not rise very much in the spot market due to the Indonesia central bank keeping a close tab on the rupiah. Bank Indonesia in recent weeks has been suspected of selling dollars in the spot market around 9,800-9,810 to support the rupiah. Traders may instead turn to the unregulated NDF market to express their bullish-USD view. The 1-month NDF premium--the price difference between a spot contract and a 1-month NDF forward contract--should be monitored for a spike which could indicate risk aversion in Indonesia. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 9,760 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 9,735 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 9,800 (psychological resistance), then at 9,810 (suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention), before 9,820 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/INR - consolidation with upside bias. The USD/INR will likely stay well-bid after the rise in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, but the upside may be slightly limited for now as the dollar is already near the top of the daily and weekly Bollinger uptrend channels, which suggests that the market is long dollars. A pullback and flushing out of some of the long-USD positions may be necessary to see a bigger rally in USD/INR. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 57.00 (psychological resistance), before 57.33 (June 2012 high). Immediate support is at 56.43 (daily and weekly upper Bollinger band standard deviation 2), then at 56.00 (psychological support), before 55.60 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 3.0980 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud), then at 3.1000 (major psychological resistance), before 3.1070 (weekly Bollinger uptrend channel). Immediate support is 3.0820 (base of weekly Ichimoku Cloud support), then at 3.0790 (daily Ichimoku Cloud support), before 3.0730 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/THB - consolidation with upside bias. USD/THB may stay elevated near the top of the Bollinger uptrend channel with the bounce in the WSJ Dollar Index overnight. Further upside for the pair appears likely, though the pace of the move may be slow, since the pair is already at the upper confines of the Bollinger uptrend channel. The next major target for the USD/THB pair could be the 30.95 weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance zone. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 30.50 (psychological resistance), before 30.95 (weekly Ichimoku Cloud resistance). Immediate support is at 30.40 (weekly Bollinger mid support), then at 30.00 (psychological support), before 29.95 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/PHP - consolidation with upside bias. USD/PHP remains biased higher along the Bollinger uptrend channel which now supports at 41.65. The pair could next target the major resistance at 42.60 that is the top of the weekly Ichimoku Cloud. The dollar is likely to stay well-bid above the 42.00 psychological mark for now, given the blip up in the WSJ Dollar Index overnight. Dollar bulls were encouraged by comments from U.S. Federal Reserve board member Esther George who reiterated her stand against excessive cheap funding engineered by the Fed's quantitative easing. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 42.31 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), then at 42.50 (psychological resistance), before 42.60 (top of weekly Ichimoku Cloud). Immediate support is at 42.00 (psychological support), then at 41.80 (base of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel), before 41.65 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/IDR - consolidation. USD/IDR is likely to trade with a supportive tone, but may not rise very much in the spot market due to the Indonesia central bank keeping a close tab on the rupiah. Bank Indonesia in recent weeks has been suspected of selling dollars in the spot market around 9,800-9,810 to support the rupiah. Traders may instead turn to the unregulated NDF market to express their bullish-USD view. The 1-month NDF premium--the price difference between a spot contract and a 1-month NDF forward contract--should be monitored for a spike which could indicate risk aversion in Indonesia. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate support is at 9,760 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel), before 9,735 (20-day Bollinger mid support). Immediate resistance is at 9,800 (psychological resistance), then at 9,810 (suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention), before 9,820 (top of weekly Bollinger uptrend channel).

USD/INR - consolidation with upside bias. The USD/INR will likely stay well-bid after the rise in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, but the upside may be slightly limited for now as the dollar is already near the top of the daily and weekly Bollinger uptrend channels, which suggests that the market is long dollars. A pullback and flushing out of some of the long-USD positions may be necessary to see a bigger rally in USD/INR. Dow Jones technical analysis suggests immediate resistance is at 57.00 (psychological resistance), before 57.33 (June 2012 high). Immediate support is at 56.43 (daily and weekly upper Bollinger band standard deviation 2), then at 56.00 (psychological support), before 55.60 (base of daily Bollinger uptrend channel).

"Reference Dealers" means five banks active in the USD/IDR or USD/JPY currency and foreign exchange market, as applicable, as selected by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

"Unscheduled Holiday" means a day that is not a Relevant Business Day and the market was not aware of such fact (by means of a public announcement or by reference to other publicly available information) until a time later than 9:00 a.m. local time in the principal financial centre(s) of IDR five (5) Relevant Business Days prior to the Scheduled IDR Valuation Date.

"USD" means United States dollars.

"USD/IDR Reference Rate" means the spot rate of USD/IDR at 11:00 a.m. Singapore time expressed as the number of IDR per one USD and published on the Reuters Screen "ABSIRFIX01" page (or its successor page for the purpose of displaying such rate) on the applicable IDR Valuation Date, as determined by the Calculation Agent.

If only three or two such quotations are provided as requested, the USD/IDR Reference Rate shall be determined as described above except that the highest and lowest quotations will not be disregarded.

If none or only one of the Reference Dealers provides such quotation, the USD/IDR Reference Rate will be determined by the Calculation Agent in its sole discretion, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.

title: WRAPUP 1-Asian bonds sell off, Bank  Indonesia intervenes
text:
* Fed policy view pushes 10-yr Treasury yld to 13-mnth high

* Asian bond selloff occurs ahead of 5-yr Treasury auction

* Foreigners sell record amounts of Korean bond futures

* Bank Indonesia steps in to buy bonds as yields surge

By Vidya Ranganathan

SINGAPORE, May 29 (Reuters) - A spike in U.S. interest rates triggered by expectations the Federal Reserve will tighten policy soon spurred a massive selloff in Asian bonds on Wednesday and forced Indonesia's central bank to step in to support its bond market.

The selling was triggered by a drop in U.S. Treasuries during Asian trading that took U.S. 10-year yields to 13-month highs, extending the run-up in yields since Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke's testimony last week.

That testimony raised the possibility of the Fed rolling back its extraordinary quantitative easing (QE) program sooner than markets had anticipated.

Foreigners who have been huge buyers of high-yielding Asian debt led the selling, traders said, putting pressure on bond markets in Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, South Korea and Australia.

As Australian bonds dropped, 10-year cash yields jumped to two-month highs at 3.48 percent and the Aussie dollar hit a 19-month low.

"These are the places which have seen the most fund inflows into the bond markets during the search for yield," said Nizam Idris, strategist with the Macquarie Group based in Singapore.

"But when growth seems to be coming back and the Fed could taper or unwind QE, then these flows are reversed.

"And 10-year Treasury yields are now at levels where most of these trades are being repriced."

While the U.S. dollar gained in the past week as concerns mounted over how soon the Fed will withdraw its massive monetary stimulus, bond markets remained largely steady.

Expectations the Fed's policy tightening will be gradual and be accompanied by stronger growth had encouraged foreigners to stay invested.

The fears that yields will rise faster, thereby leading to cash outflows from emerging markets and into dollar assets, intensified after Tuesday's auction of U.S. 2-year notes met with lukewarm demand and drew a higher-than-expected yield. The Treasury department is set to auction 5-year notes on Wednesday.

U.S. 10-year yields were quoted at 2.18 percent at 0900 GMT, and have risen 56 basis points since early May.

In Indonesia, the central bank was forced into defending the rupiah and rare bond-buying intervention after rupiah bonds dived.

Five-year Indonesian government bond yields hit a 2-month high of 5.29 percent, taking the total climb in yields over two weeks to 0.4 percentage points, before the central bank's bond buying pulled yields lower. Traders said the rupiah fell below 9,900 per dollar.

Bank Indonesia (BI) Deputy Governor Perry Warjiyo said the central bank had intervened "..because some short term foreign investors or traders are selling off their bonds."

"We are committed to be in the market to stabilize the exchange rate of the rupiah. Because of it, we intervene both in forex and bonds," Warjiyo said.

FOREIGNERS SELL

Foreigners hold large amounts of dollar and local-currency denominated bonds in Asia. Their largest holdings as a proportion of the total bonds issued are in Indonesia and Malaysia.

Data from Indonesia's debt office showed offshore investors held 305.33 trillion rupiah ($30.8 billion) of government bonds, or 34 percent of the total outstanding as of May 24.

Bank Indonesia's holdings of rupiah government bonds increased from 1.9 trillion rupiah at end of January to 22.6 trillion rupiah on May 24.

In South Korea, foreigners' net selling of leading June 3-year bond futures hit a record 4.5 trillion won on Wednesday.

"This kind of foreign selling is unprecedented, so the repercussions in the coming days could be considerable," said a trader in Seoul.

Yield on the benchmark Korean 10-year government debt rose to its highest level in more than three months, while the won fell half a percent against the dollar.

The Philippine peso hit a 9-month low.

In Malaysia, 5-year yields hit an 8-month high of 3.3 percent. Yields on Thailand's 5-year government bonds were at a one-month high of 3 percent despite Bank of Thailand cutting policy rates on Wednesday to support the economy and deter hot money inflows.

Stock markets weakened, with Hong Kong's shares faring the worst.

Yields on dollar-denominated Indonesian and Philippine credits, which are most vulnerable to U.S. Fed policy because they are priced and quoted at a spread to U.S. Treasury yields, also rose on Wednesday.

The Philippine 2037 bond was quoted at 112 cents and Indonesia's 2043 bond at 93 cents per dollar of bond value, both down four to five cents in the past week. The Philippine peso hit a 9-month low.

"There is now the view that the U.S. recovery story is real and sustainable," said Macquarie's Idris.

Ten-year U.S. yields would have to climb above 3 percent to reach 'escape velocity' or a level that would imply a sustainable economic recovery and therefore higher yields, Idris said, adding he expected markets would only get a green light signal if U.S. jobs data next week was really strong.

"I am riding this move but only cautiously," he said. (Additional reporting by Cecile Lefort in Sydney, Vincent Se Young Lee in Seoul, Rieka Rahadiana and Adriana Nina Kusuma in Jakarta, Umesh Desai in Hong Kong; Editing by Simon Cameron-Moore)

title: INSTANT VIEW 3-Bank Indonesia keeps rate at 5.75 pct, cautious on growth
text:
JAKARTA, April 11 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank kept its benchmark rate unchanged at a record low 5.75 percent on Thursday, as expected, as it sees inflationary pressures easing and is concerned about slowing economic growth.

All 14 analysts polled by Reuters had forecast the rate would be left unchanged, as core inflation eased in March and the government has not made any move yet to cut fuel subsidies.

Bank Indonesia (BI) sounded more cautious on global economic growth prospects than in previous statements, leading some economists to see it keeping rates on hold all year. BI has kept the policy rate unchanged since February 2012, when it was cut by 25 basis points.

KEY POINTS

- BI says rate consistent with inflation targets

- BI says sees inflationary pressures easing

- BI sees slower 2013 economic growth at 6.2-6.6 pct

- BI sees moderate depreciation pressure on rupiah

Graphic for Indonesia inflation, rates:

http://link.reuters.com/nef95s("http://link.reuters.com/nef95s")

COMMENTS:

HAK BIN CHUA, ECONOMIST, BANK OF AMERICA MERRIL LYNCH, SINGAPORE

"Soft commodity prices are starting to slow overall GDP growth. The prospect of higher energy costs if the government decides to ration or adjust subsidized fuel prices may cut growth by another notch.

"The risk of monetary tightening, either via FASBI or the BI rate, will increase in coming months as inflation jumps on a fuel policy adjustment, whether via rationing or a price increase.

"Bank Indonesia has chosen not to be pre-emptive, despite the dangers of an inflation overshoot from fuel prices."

FAUZI ICHSAN, ECONOMIST, STANDARD CHARTERED, JAKARTA

"This was to be expected. We do expect them to keep rates on hold for the rest of the year. Though we think the central bank will increase the FASBI rate by 50 basis points by the second half of this year."

GARETH LEATHER, ECONOMIST, CAPITAL ECONOMICS, SINGAPORE

"The recent sharp rise in inflation increases the chances of a rate hike before the end of the year. However, given the uncertain global outlook and the fact that core inflation remains subdued, we believe interest rates will remain on hold for the remainder of 2013.

"The big question now is how long it will be before BI starts to hike interest rates. The worsening of the current account position, falling foreign exchange reserves, the weak rupiah and continued strong credit growth are all reasons why BI may decide to hike rates sooner rather than later.

"One area on uncertainty concerns the outlook for inflation...so far the pick-up has been driven by temporary factors, which have pushed up food prices. More importantly, core inflation is low, which suggests that underlying price pressures remain relatively subdued. Provided that core inflation remains low, BI is likely to take a relaxed view about the increase in the headline rate.

"With exports set to struggle this year on account of weak global demand, we expect interest rates to remain on hold until the end of 2013, with policy tightening likely to begin next year."

GUNDY CAHYADI, ECONOMIST, OCBC BANK, SINGAPORE

"BI's statement seemed a little more dovish than usual, and certainly the downward revision to the 2013 GDP growth forecast from 6.6 percent to 6.2 percent was a clear indication that the central bank would continue to maintain their accomodative policy as long as they can.

"Indonesia's export growth has been somewhat disappointing in the first 2 months of the year and it seems like the marked recovery that we have been expecting (to happen in H2) may now be delayed.

"Despite the recent uptick in inflation, BI remains confident that inflation pressure will start to moderate again in the future, and thus, they stood by the decision to keep the rate unchanged.

"Having said that, we think that the eagerly awaited result regarding fuel subsidy will be a key event to watch out for. We suspect that some form of fuel price hike is imminent and that this may necessarily mean that BI needs to raise its BI policy rate to anchor inflationary expectations going forward."

MARKET REACTION

- The rupiah spot's indicative prices edged slightly lower after the decision, to 9,695 per U.S. dollar by 0728 GMT.

- Jakarta stocks edged lower after the decision but stayed in positive territory, trading up 0.6 percent.

CONTEXT

- Four polled analysts expected the central bank to tighten policy on Thursday or afterwards by rising the overnight deposit facility rate, or FASBI, to help ease the current account deficit and support the rupiah.

- Bank Indonesia cut its policy rate by 75 basis points in 2011, and by another 25 basis points in February 2012 to help maintain the country's annual economic growth at more than 6 percent.

- Headline inflation hit a nearly two-year high at 5.9 percent in March due to import restrictions on several foods, but core inflation softened to 4.21 percent from 4.29 percent the previous month.

- In 2012, Indonesia had a sizable current account deficit and its first annual trade deficit. The twin deficits put pressure on the rupiah, which weakened about 6 percent against the U.S. dollar during the year.

- There was a trade defict of $330 million in February, as global demand stayed weak amid surging imports.

- Forex reserves declined to $104.8 billion at the end of March from $105.2 billion in February, as Bank Indonesiaintervened in the forex market to support the rupiah.

- Recent data releases show modest optimism about the economy. Retail sales in February were 14 percent higher than a year earlier, while a consumer confidence index was flat at 116.8 due to steady domestic consumption.

(Reporting by Andjarsari Paramaditha and Randy Fabi; Editing by Neil Chatterjee)

title: Indonesia  Finance Minister:  Central Bank  Should Sell More Dollars When  Intervening
text:
JAKARTA--Indonesia's finance minister on Monday said the country's central bank should intervene in the currency market by selling dollars in large amounts, in contrast to its current practice of supporting the ailing rupiah with relatively small manipulations.

Agus Martowardojo, undergoing a vetting process in his bid to become the new chief of the nation's central bank, told lawmakers at the House of Representatives that selling dollars "would be better if not done little by little, as this only makes the market fearful" by suggesting Bank Indonesia is reluctant to defend the rupiah or doesn't have enough dollars.

"Consequently, the rupiah will fall even more and as a result we have to sell more dollars," he added.

The Indonesian currency has been one of Asia's worst performers since last year, dropping more than 8 percent in the past 12 months. The central bank says it intervenes in the market to reduce volatility in the currency.

Mr. Martowardojo, picked by President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono to head the central bank for a five-year term beginning in May, faces a second day of vetting Tuesday, when a House panel will vote on recommending his candidacy before the entire House.

title: ANALYSIS-Bank Indonesia takes precautions to keep rupiah's decline orderly
text:
* Indonesian banks told to stay out of offshore rupiah forward market

* Central bank intervening to cushion rupiah's decline

* Politics lengthens odds of a rise in subsidised fuel prices

By Vidya Ranganathan

SINGAPORE, Feb 14 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank is gradually closing trading loopholes used by global investors in an attempt to exert more control over its weakening currency and prevent a desirable depreciation of the rupiah from turning into a panicky tailspin.

Last week, it reminded domestic banks they are not allowed to dabble in offshore rupiah forward markets. It told them it wants an improvement in onshore trading volume. And it said it will specify the hours during which banks can quote exchange rates for the rupiah.

Looking for motives behind this focus on trading hours and rules in what has been a relatively well-behaved market, analysts suspect Bank Indonesia's aim is to remove room for speculative play before letting the market take the rupiah down slowly.

The central bank has been selling dollars, limiting the rupiah's decline so far this year to around 0.5 percent, but any intention to manage an orderly decline in the rupiah remains unstated.

But, without that intervention, the rupiah would undoubtedly have fallen faster as the currency comes under growing pressure from the country's huge import bills and the risk of capital outflows.

The current account showed a deficit of $24.18 billion in 2012, following a surplus of $1.7 billion in 2011, according to data released on Wednesday.

The rupiah lost around 6 percent against the dollar in 2012, cushioned by constant, yet subtle intervention.

Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono said last month the central bank would use various instruments to maintain the stability of the rupiah, and must from time to time intervene in the currency market to ease the pressure on dollar supply created by large, lumpy payments to meet energy imports.

But Sarwono stressed that Indonesia's balance of payments remained in overall surplus, as the capital account surplus covered the current account deficit.

The current account showed a deficit of $7.76 billion in the fourth quarter of 2012, and the deficit for the full year was $24.18 billion, marking a sharp deterioration from the $1.7 billion surplus posted in 2011, according to data released on Wednesday.

Indonesia ended 2012 with a balance of payments surplus of $165 million, down sharply from $11.9 billion the previous year, though it had a surplus of $3.2 billion in the fourth quarter.

A textbook policy response to pressure on the currency would be for Bank Indonesia to raise interest rates.

That could forestall outflows, crimp domestic consumption, and reduce any rise in payments for dollar-priced imports of refined oil products, machinery and food, particularly after the country suffered its first-ever trade deficit in 2012.

But investors and economists alike suspect authorities in Southeast Asia's largest economy are going to take the more politically acceptable route of letting the rupiah weaken, albeit at a pace that keeps foreign investors comfortable while also boosting the value of exports and making imports expensive.

"What's going to be most palatable is to let the currency drift lower, if that's the way the market is pushing it, with obviously some intervention to slow the pace of depreciation," said Robert Prior-Wandesforde, Asian economist at Credit Suisse.

"That is not the most appropriate response, in my view."

If a massaged depreciation is the ultimate intent, the central bank would probably intervene in a subtle fashion, to avoid unsettling foreign investors or unecessarily draw too heavily on its foreign exchange reserves.

Foreign investors hold about $28 billion, or 33 percent of Indonesia's high-yielding government bonds.

And whereas currency reserves, at $109 billion, and equivalent to six months of imports, appear to be a comfortable amount the bank will want to spend them wisely.

Rupiah markets are not pricing in abrupt swings in the currency, quite the contrary. Economists expect there will be a slow drift down in the rupiah.

ING economist Tim Condon said Indonesia's current account will remain in deficit, as it did before the 1998 Asian financial crisis, resulting in a 3-to-4 percent annual depreciation in the rupiah.

"Hot money investors get used to orderly rupiah depreciation," he warned, adding that investing in Indonesia's fast-growing economy made more sense than investing in rupiah-denominated bonds or stocks.

Investors betting on the economy have been going directly into areas such as mining and transport too. Indonesia received a record 221 trillion rupiah ($22.5 billion) in foreign direct investment in 2012.

RUPIAH AT 10,000

To be fair to the central bank, it has little sway over what would be the most effective policy response to reduce the pressure on the currency, namely hikes in heavily subsided fuel prices.

Southeast Asia's largest economy is growing between 6 and 7 percent a year. The rapid pace of investment and consumption in the economy has driven imports up, whereas external demand for its coal and other commodity exports has been subdued.

Taken together, the trade deficit and the interest payments to foreigners has left Indonesia vulnerable balancing its external books.

"If the current account is not stabilising, they really have to go back to the policy basket and pull out something fresh," said Claudio Piron, a strategist at Bank of AmericaMerrill Lynch.

"That is further policy tightening or allowing more depreciation of the currency. But I think ultimately the issue is the oil deficit, which they can do something about."

The quick fix to the rupiah's woes would be to hike subsidised fuel prices, which on average are responsible for about a billion dollars of the trade deficit each month.

But raising prices would be unpopular with voters, who go to the polls for a presidential election in 2014.

With inflation also comfortably in the middle of the central bank's 3.5-5.5 percent target range, it is reasonable to suppose Bank Indonesia's preferred policy choice is to allow a gentle weakening in the currency.

The tricky part, though, would be for Bank Indonesia to manage the pace of that depreciation in a way that forestalls any panic among foreign investors.

Two factors could unnerve them: extreme volatility or any sign that the rupiah will move more than it has done historically, which is on average 7 to 12 percent a year.

Most immediately, that would mean the rupiah, which is being traded around 9,700 a dollar, does not weaken beyond 10,150 in February.

Barring a brief bout of weakness in January, foreign investors have so far kept their faith. Market pricing of future rupiah volatility is low and stable.

Even the non-deliverable forward (NDF) market, the playground for speculators, belies any sign of concern, with a 3-month pricing for the currency just one percent weaker at 9,800 per dollar.

And that raises the risk that Bank Indonesia will inadvertently stir unease by firing missives at an offshore market whose stability has been reassuring for foreigners, who hedge their rupiah bets in NDFs, instead of focusing on fixing the real issues with the rupiah.

"The irony is that the Indonesian NDF market has been relatively well behaved," said Piron. "So, it may be more harmful than good," he said, referring to the central bank's reminder on the ban on NDF trading last week.

title: Bank Indonesia Dep Gov: Will Increase Dollar Selling if Necessary to Help Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA, Indonesia--Bank Indonesia will, if necessary, increase sales of dollars in the domestic foreign-exchange market to help the local unit, Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono said Friday.

"We will [intervene] in the market at the right time and size--if necessary we will sell [dollars] in large amounts," Mr. Sarwono told reporters.

The rupiah has been under selling pressure since early last year because of worries over the country's widening current-account deficit. This forced the central bank to intervene.

After trading close to 9,900 rupiah last week the dollar eased to IDR9,650 Friday thanks in part to trickling capital inflows and suspected Bank Indonesiaintervention.

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesia c.bank says no plans for new instruments to deal with rupiah
text:
* Bank Indonesia says will intervene in market where necessary

* To maintain rupiah stability with various existing instruments

(Adds comments)

JAKARTA, Jan 25 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia, the central bank, said on Friday it had no plans to introduce new instruments to deal with the decline of the rupiah currency and would continue to intervene in the market where necessary.

Indonesia's rupiah has been one of the world's worst performing currencies over the past year, dragged down in part by concerns over a widening current account deficit. It was trading in late afternoon at around 9,665/85, down on the day, but above lows touched earlier this month.

"We try to maintain the stability of the rupiah with various existing instruments. There is no fundamental change of instruments or anything," the deputy governor for monetary policy, Hartadi Sarwono, told reporters.

"But we know the problem is a shortage of dollar supplies ... from day to day. I need to reiterate this because our balance of payments is still in surplus overall, which means that the current account deficit could still be covered by the capital account."

But the nature of the capital account, in which a major part was from goods and services, meant there was not always enough to cover the shortfall in the trade balance.

"Therefore, BI (Bank Indonesia) must from time to time ... venture into the market to reduce the gap between supply and demand," he said.

He said he expected the current account deficit to improve and that demand for foreign exchange could be met by the market.

"As usual, we will intervene. We'll see how the numbers are now. If there is a huge need for oil and gas imports, we will increase more there. So there is no instrument that has changed, only the amount and timing."

(Reporting by Adriana Nina Kusuma; Writing by Jonathan Thatcher; Editing by Jacqueline Wong)

title: WSJ BLOG/Marketbeat: Weakened Indonesian Rupiah Could Mean Bargains for Bond Investors
text:
The Indonesian rupiah has weakened sharply in recent months, edging close to the crucial threshold of 10,000 to the U.S. dollar due to several factors including a widening current account deficit. But some traders say that the central bank won't let the rate cross that line in the sand, and that the bottoming-out currency could attract foreign bond buyers.

Investors are showing keen interest in an Indonesian bond auction scheduled for Tuesday--with the relatively cheap rupiah providing a draw, on top of the high yield of Indonesia's government bonds--says a Jakarta-based rupiah trader who works for a foreign investment bank.

The dollar-rupiah touched a high of 9,920 last week in Indonesia's "shadow market," the trader says. Before Bank Indonesia apparently intervened on Monday, providing $50 million-$100 million in liquidity, the dollar had been trading around 9,870 rupiah. The unofficial market, which has emerged because Bank of Indonesia restricts its dollar supply, reflects the rupiah's real value more accurately than the official one.

The trader said the central bank probably won't let the dollar-rupiah cross the 10,000 mark, as this could trigger a deluge of rupiah-selling due to automatic orders. He favors the idea of gradually selling dollars on the shadow market.

Bank Indonesia has a limited supply of foreign reserves and usually sells dollars only to market participants who can prove they've sold rupiah assets. For others who are "pre-hedging" and may not have actually sold the underlying assets, there is the shadow market, which operates outside the formal exchange and where the dollar trades at a premium to the official spot rate.

There is also the nondeliverable forward or NDF market, an offshore platform often used by speculators. The NDF market is settled in U.S. dollars using the difference between the contracted NDF rate and the prevailing spot rate, and usually trades at an even higher premium to the official spot rate.

Traders closely watch the premiums for dollar-rupiah NDF contracts as a gauge of fear among investors, as they can be a precursor of more volatility in the spot market. In May 2012, when the one-month NDF premium spiked as high as 200 rupiah, a 3.9% rally in the dollar-rupiah spot rate came days later. Last week's rise in the NDF premiums is creating a reinforcing cycle of rupiah weakness and making some market-watchers think it could depreciate further, the Australia & New Zealand banking group's research team said in a recent note.

However, an NDF trader in a small, Singapore-based foreign investment bank thinks otherwise. He feels the NDF premiums could slide soon as Bank Indonesiaintervenes to quell market instability. He is looking to bet on a drop in longer-term NDF premiums, such as the one-year contract, which currently trades with a premium of 410 rupiah. This could happen if the central bank floods the spot market with more dollars in the coming days.

At current spot levels, the rupiah could start looking more attractive to investors, the Jakarta-based rupiah dealer says, noting the relatively cheap currency makes Indonesia's high-yielding bonds an even better deal. The 10-year Indonesia government bond yields approximately 5.2%, which stands out sharply against a global background of depressed interest rates brought on by round after round of quantitative easing, and is a stark reminder why Indonesia has in the past been a darling of emerging market investors searching for yield.

The rupiah's indicative price softened 0.3 percent to 9,660 to the dollar on exchange pages, but its real market price was a weaker 9,880-9,900 quoted against corporate dollar demand, dealers said.

Indonesia's debt also fell, with yields on 10-year bonds

hitting 5.263 percent, their highest since Dec. 12, and the five-year yield at 4.713 percent, also highest since Jan. 2.

The country aims to raise 7 trillion rupiah ($726.52 million) from a bond auction on Tuesday.

"It looks like investors could be more cautious than the recent auctions, on the back of recent weakening of the rupiah," said Gundy Cahyadi, an economist at OCBC Bank in Singapore.

The rupiah has slid 0.3 percent against the dollar so far this year after being the worst performing emerging Asian currency in 2012 with a loss of nearly 6 percent, Thomson Reuters' data showed.

Worries about the country's current account deficit and inflation, as well as a lack of dollar liquidity, have been putting pressure on the rupiah and curbing foreign investors' appetite for Indonesian assets. [ID:nL4N0AF2TE

The future value for the rupiah has plunged in offshore forward markets, indicating a rush by foreigners to hedge their risks.

Finance Minister Agus Martowardojo said he expected the rupiah to weaken this year on a wider current account deficit and uncertain global economic situation, adding its average exchange rate will be at 9,300-9,700.

The central bank has been spotted selling dollars to support the Indonesian currency, dealers said. On Monday, it provided dollar liquidity between 9,655 and 9,680, they added.

Bank Indonesia also expressed determination to stabilise the currency market.

"Bank Indonesia will always ready to intervene if rupiah depreciates excessively from its fundamental," Bank Indonesia Governor Darmin Nasution told parliament.

Still, some analysts and dealers expect Tuesday's bond auction to attract decent foreign interest, given higher yields.

The rupiah rebounded in the forwards market with one-month dollar/rupiah non-deliverable forwards down 0.4 percent to 9,890.

"By looking at the correction last week and not much trading volume, it means that there were not a lot of foreign outflows," said Handy Yunianto, debt market analyst at Mandiri Sekuritas in Jakarta.

Foreign investors reduced Indonesian bond holdings by 1.29 trillion rupiah in the first four days of last week, but that compared with average daily bond market trading volume of 9.5 trillion rupiah in 2012.

"I think demand at the auction tomorrow will be big," said Yuniato, adding the valuation should be "interesting" with the recent correction.

WON

The won eased on dollar demand from local importers and as some offshore funds booked profits from the South Korean currency.

Investors stayed wary of possible intervention by the foreign exchange authorities.

Still, the won remained in a bullish trend, dealers said.

"Investors appeared to still hold dollar-short positions, but they did not cover those positions actively. I don't think they will aggressively unwind those positions unless the won loses its trend," said a foreign bank dealer in Seoul.

PHILIPPINE PESO

The Philippine peso eased as investors covered dollar-short positions on caution over further central bank interventions.

But real money funds and interbank speculators looked for chances to buy the peso on dips, limiting its downside.

BAHT

The Thai baht edged up on stock inflows and exporters but was also called by intervention worries.

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesia govt sees weaker rupiah, cbank defends 9,700 to the dlr
text:
(Updates with details, dealer comment)

JAKARTA, Jan 14 (Reuters) - Indonesia has downgraded its forecast for the rupiah this year, with a floor of 9,700 per dollar, a level the central bank has defended in recent days as nervous investors put the currency under pressure.

The government had budgeted for a rupiah at 9,300 per dollar in 2013, but expectations that weak commodity exports would continue to fuel trade and current account deficits means real market prices are already being quoted by dealers at around 9,900.

The depreciating currency has weakened sentiment towards the country's stocks and bonds and dented the fast growing G20 economy's appeal as a safe haven for investors.

There has been no big sell-off in rupiah assets so far, with foreign bond ownership rising to record levels at 33 percent of the total and stocks rising 1.4 percent on Monday to near a record record hit earlier this month.

However, a spike in one-month forward prices show foreigners are hedging positions.

The currency's indicative spot price has traded at or below 9,700 per dollar in the past five trading sessions, yet has closed above that level each time at around 9,650, with traders pointing to the central bank intervening by selling dollars.

"Bank Indonesia will always be ready to intervene if the rupiah depreciates excessively from its fundamentals," Bank Indonesia's Governor Darmin Nasution told parliament on Monday.

The rupiah was emerging Asia's worst performing currency last year, shedding nearly 6 percent, and has slipped another 0.3 percent so far in 2013.

It was not clear what the central bank sees as the currency's fundamental level.

This time last year it made the same noises and appeared to be defending 9,200, but it then let the currency weaken and now that level appears to be 9,700.

"That is where the market thinks they are at the moment," said a Jakarta-based currency dealer. "They are trying to manage the currency rate within the government forecast to parliament. They also want to smoothen the curve for gradual depreciation."

Finance Minister Agus Martowardojo told parliament on Monday the rupiah will continue to weaken due to pressures from an uncertain global economic situation and the wider current account deficit, estimated at around $10 billion last quarter.

The finance ministry said in November it was comfortable with the rupiah at around 9,600, as that level may ease the country's trade imbalances by helping exporters and cutting down on surging imports.

The central bank has kept interest rates at a record low to maintain economic growth at above 6 percent.

Analysts are now calling for rate hikes to support the rupiah, but pro-growth policymakers are likely to keep that as a last resort.

Instead, the central bank is likely to use its foreign reserves, built up to $112.8 billion by December from $106.5 billion six months earlier, as firepower to intervene if the 9,700 level is broken.

"They will come at 9,800 and defend it. Then 9,900. They are ready," said the Jakarta dealer.

title: Bank Indonesia Will 'Continue to Be in the Market' - Deputy Governor
text:
JAKARTA--Bank Indonesia Deputy Gov. Hartadi Sarwono said Thursday that the central bank will raise interest rates when the rupiah depreciates "excessively for too long," signaling its readiness to support the local currency.

The rupiah was the worst-performing currency in Asia against the U.S. dollar last year, losing over 6% largely due to worries over Indonesia's wide current account deficit. title: EM ASIA  FX -Won, Taiwan dollar up, but  Indonesia  loses in mixed trade
text:
* S.Korean exporters support won; intervention caution caps

* Taiwan dlr up on inflows of foreign financial institutions

* Rupiah down on corp dlr demand, but bond inflows seen

* Sing dlr dips on market talk of intervention

(Adds details, updates prices)

By Jongwoo Cheon

SINGAPORE, Nov 2 (Reuters) - The South Korean won and the Taiwan dollar edged up on Friday, supported by improving U.S. economic data, but other emerging Asian currencies slipped on expectations of intervention by local authorities to stem the rise of the regional units.

Investors were also cautious ahead of the U.S. Presidential election on Nov. 6 and the challenge of the "fiscal cliff" that Congress must tackle soon after.

A rise in U.S. private sector employment in October and a jump in consumer confidence helped push the won and the Taiwan dollar higher as inflows from foreign financial institutions increased.

But the Indonesian rupiah slid as local corporates sought dollars while the Singapore dollar eased on speculation that local authorities would intervene to prevent it from strengthening past 1.2200 to the U.S. dollar.

Suresh Kumar Ramanathan, head of regional interest rate and FX strategy at CIMB Investment Bank, said he expected emerging Asian currencies to lose ground after the U.S. election.

"Global risk appetite will skew towards cautious tone for the rest of the world post-November 6 Presidential election," said Ramanathan in Kuala Lumpur.

After the election, Congress must deal with a "fiscal cliff" -- up to $600 billion in expiring tax cuts and spending reductions that are set to kick in next year -- which threatens to hurt the U.S. economy.

Investors' immediate focus, however, is the U.S. nonfarm payrolls data due at 1230 GMT, which is expected to show employers added 125,000 jobs in October, with the jobless rate ticking up to 7.9 percent from September's 7.8 percent.

"Any upside surprise on this front, we think, may fuel global risk-taking behavior instead of boosting the dollar across the board," OCBC Bank said in a note.

On the week, Asian currencies have been mixed after most of them enjoyed gains in the previous week.

The won rose 0.6 percent against the dollar and the Taiwan dollar gained 0.3 percent, according to Thomson Reuters data.

The Malaysian ringgit has fallen 0.5 percent with dollar-short covering, while the rupiah has eased 0.3 percent, data for the week showed.

WON

The won gained on exporters' demand for settlements in extremely thin trading, while its upside was tightly limited as investors stayed cautious over possible intervention by the foreign exchange authorities.

The authorities were spotted overnight trying to stem the won's strength via the non-deliverable forwards market, dealers said.

Still, investors expect the South Korean currency to stay firm despite uncertainty over the U.S. election next week, dealers added.

"There are few reasons to push down the won, given continuous exporters' deals and firm stocks. The won will be around the current levels," said a foreign bank dealer in Seoul.

TAIWAN DOLLAR

The Taiwan dollar gained as foreign financial institutions bought the local unit on expectations for strong U.S. jobs data later in the day.

Dealers in Taiwan expected the island's unit to appreciate more regardless of the U.S. election result, although the currency's upside is seen as limited because of the possibility of intervention.

RUPIAH

The rupiah eased on dollar bids from local corporates, but bond inflows relieved the Indonesian currency, dealers said.

But some dealers expect demand for the bonds not to last long, saying the rupiah is likely to stay under pressure.

"These inflows are surprising. But I expect if there are any more inflows, they will be linked to window dressing before the year-end," said a Jakarta based dealer.

Another trader pointed out risks from proposed hikes in electricity tariff next year and a prospective fuel price raise.

On Oct. 23, Indonesia's parliament approved the government's 2013 budget plan and left open the possibility of a fuel price hike. ID:nL3E8LN3TG]

Indonesia does plan to cut power subsidies next year by hiking electricity tariffs by 15 percent, to save 11.8 trillion rupiah ($1.23 billion) that will be used to improve infrastructure.

The trader said the rupiah could weaken to 9,700 per dollar by the end of the year, although the central bank will slow down, especially in December.

title: Emerging Market  Currencies  Mixed On Spain Concerns
text:
Emerging market currencies seesawed Tuesday as investor mood swung to caution on headlines about Spain's plans to seek financial assistance.

A report indicated that Spanish Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy indicated he wasn't considering seeking a credit line to support the debt-laden country. Investors expect Spain eventually will require the help but may delay it as long as it can or at least until its provincial elections in November.

This led to a choppy ride for emerging market currencies. The dollar opened the day lower against the Mexican peso at MXN12.7705 but later rose to MXN12.8419, up 0.3% on the day.

The Mexican currency also received a boost after strong CPI in the U.S. and the strongest level of U.S. homebuilders' confidence since June 2006 left investors with little doubt about the strength of the country's economic recovery. The momentum could bring in buyers and push the currency toward MXN12.6550/12.6650, according to a trader at Standard Chartered.

Some investors are using these dips to go long the U.S. dollar, suggesting that in the coming months they expect the dollar to strengthen in line with the fortunes of the economy.

Currencies such as the Hungarian forint and Czech koruna, though, managed to make sizable gains against both the euro and the dollar. Investors find these higher yielding currencies attractive. The forint is up 0.43% at 277.84 per euro, according to CQG data. Market participants suggest that the euro will trade in a range between HUF277.50 and HUF282.59 in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, the Turkish lira close to new highs, and market participant are looking to buy at the dips ahead of a central bank meeting on Thursday, when the monetary authority is expected to cut overnight lending rates for the second time since February. Turkey, faced with slowing growth, is expected to resort to rate cuts like other emerging economies. The dollar fetches TRY1.8036, down 0.38% on the day.

The stronger buying pace in the morning prompted several central banks to intervene, including Colombia, Peru and Indonesia.

The USD/IDR is trading at 9605, late afternoon New York time, after it dropped below 9600 earlier in the day following the central bank's attempts to hold the currency in that range.

Peru and Colombia regularly intervene to regulate the pace of currency movements. The Peruvian sol is trading almost flat on the day at PEN2.582 per dollar, while the Colombia peso is also unchanged at 1798.8 per dollar, according to CQG data.

In credit markets, Perusahaan Listrik Negara, the state-owned electricity company of Indonesia, sold $1 billion of 30-year notes at a yield of 5.35%. The deal tightened from its initial price.

text:
* Won at 6-1/2 mth high on stock inflows

 * Taiwan dlr up on foreign funds, exporters; c.bank caps

 * Rupiah hits near 7-wk high on bond inflows

 * Philippine peso ease; negative fwds prompt profit-taking 

(Adds text, updates prices)

 By Jongwoo Cheon

 SINGAPORE, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Most emerging Asian currencies extended gains on Monday, enjoying capital inflows to the region after the Federal Reserve's aggressive policy stimulus last week, and the Indian rupee hit a four-month high on the government's reforms.

 The rupee has gained up to 1.2 percent to 53.66, the strongest since May 15, as the Indian government on Friday opened up the country's supermarket sector to foreign retailers  and allowed more foreign investment in airlines and broadcasters, a day after sharply increasing the price of heavily-subsidized diesel. 

 The South Korean won hit a six-and-a-half month high on stock inflows, and the Taiwan dollar touched its peak in more than four months on incoming funds.

 The Indonesian rupiah also hit a near seven-week high on bond inflows.

 "Asian currencies have room to rise further as the Fed did not only pump up money but also let investors buy time," said Jeong My-young, Samsung Futures' research head in Seoul.

 "Most risk currencies, especially the euro, looked technically overbought. But Asian FX may not fall much even though the euro may see corrections, as people will look for chances to buy the currencies against the euro," she added.

 Before this emerging Asian units had weakened versus the euro because the regional units did not reflect the rise in the euro on worries that a slowing global economy would keep hurting export-oriented Asia.

 Still, investors grew more cautious over possible intervention by local authorities to stem their currency gains. The central banks of Taiwan and Philippine were spotted buying dollars, dealers said.

 Most regional units were also seen excessively bought, suggesting they may suffer from short-term corrections.

 The 14-day relative strength indices (RSI) of U.S. dollar/Singapore dollar, U.S. dollar/Taiwan dollar, dollar/rupee and dollar/baht stayed below the threshold 30, indicating those pairs are in oversold territory.

 The RSI of dollar/won, dollar/peso and dollar/rupiah stood above the threshold, but not far from that line.

 The Philippine peso and the Singapore dollar eased.

 TAIWAN DOLLAR

 The Taiwan dollar leaped to 29.198 against the U.S. dollar, its strongest since May 3, on foreign funds inflows and as domestic exporters chased it on expectations of further appreciation.

 But the central ban was spotted buying U.S. dollars around 29.200 to slow down the local unit's strength, while importers joined the bids, dealers said.

 RUPIAH

 The rupiah hit 9,443 to the dollar, the local unit's strongest since Aug. 1 on bond inflows, dealers said.

 The Indonesian currency found a resistance at that level as local banks bought dollars on behalf of their local corporates.

 Still, the rupiah is expected to rise further on more inflows with the Fed's stimulus, dealers said.

 "The QE3 will boost inflows and investor confidence in foreign direct investments here," said a Jakarta-based dealer, adding the rupiah may head to 9,400.

 "The policy would be beneficial for Indonesia as it would strengthen the rupiah without BI having to dig deep into its foreign exchange reserves," said the dealer, referring to Bank Indonesia.

 The central bank had been seen intervening to stem weakness in the rupiah, according to dealers.

 WON

 The won advanced to 1,113.3 per greenback, its strongest since March 2, on demand linked to foreign investors' stock purchases.

 Foreigners bought a net 503.1 billion won ($450.38 million) worth of Seoul shares after absorbing a net 1.28 trillion won on Friday, according to the Korea Exchange data.

 Caution grew over possible intervention by the foreign exchange authorities to stem the won's strength, and domestic importers bought dollars for payments.

 "The authorities may allow more gains if the euro and stocks stay firm, while the speed of appreciation is slow," said a senior foreign bank dealer in Seoul.

 "But they will step in 1,110," he said.

 PHILIPPINE PESO

 The Philippine peso weakened as traders reduced bullish positions with short-term forwards negative and as the central bank was spotted intervening by buying dollars, dealers said.

 The peso started local trade firm at a session peak of 41.33 per dollar, but turned lower. The central bank was seen around 41.35, dealers said.

 "Onshore swap points collapsed and were quoted at negative points. Negative points have a negative carry on long peso positions and make it expensive to hold on to dollar short positions overnight," a foreign bank dealer in Manila.

 Most of the short-term peso forwards from overnight to two-month were quoted at a discount, indicating that it was costlier to hold a short dollar position.

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR

 The Singapore dollar eased on local bank offers around 1.2200 to U.S. dollar with disappointing export data cementing caution over the central bank's intervention.

 Singapore's non-oil exports in August fell more than expected, raising the prospects of the city-state entering into a recession.

title: 3rd UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Leaves Rate Unchanged Amid Weakening Growth, Rupiah Pressure
text:
--Bank Indonesia holds rates steady, governor says inflation under control

--Focus on rupiah, inflationary pressures signal bias toward tightening policy

--Weaker-than-expected growth predicted in 2012 and 2013

--Bank Indonesia may allow onshore banks to swap U.S. dollar bonds for dollars

--Current-account deficit likely widened in second quarter

(Adds context throughout, current-account deficit predictions in 13th paragraph, news of dollar-bond swaps in 14th and 15th paragraphs)

By Ben Otto, I Made Sentana, Joko Hariyanto

JAKARTA--Indonesia's central bank left its policy interest rate unchanged at 5.75% as expected Thursday, as higher inflation and continued weakness in the rupiah kept it from relaxing its stance despite weaker growth forecasts associated with the global economic slowdown.

Bank Indonesia Gov. Darmin Nasution reiterated the bank's commitment to keeping inflation under control and focus on the rupiah. He told reporters that "the current policy rate is consistent with the inflation forecast" and reiterated past comments that inflation "is likely to remain low and can be contained within our target range" of 3.5%-5.5%.

The decision to hold rates at an all-time low comes as Indonesia is facing weakening growth while trying to keep a lid on inflation, and as countries around the region are loosening policy. Bank of Korea unexpectedly cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points Thursday, and China has cut its key rate twice in the past month, but economists say a weak rupiah will keep Bank Indonesia from following suit for the rest of the year.

"As before, Bank Indonesia indicated that it will keep the rupiah in line with the rest of the Asian currencies, suggesting that further intervention to smooth out flows in the market will remain prevalent going forward," OCBC economist Gundy Cahyadi said in an email. "We expect inflation to average around 5.0%-5.5% this year, and that Bank Indonesia will not adjust its monetary policy rate anytime soon."

All 13 economists surveyed by Dow Jones Newswires had predicted the central bank would maintain its overnight rate after inflation accelerated to 4.53% in June from 4.45% in May, stoked by higher prices of basic foodstuffs.

The country's financial markets had little reaction to the news. The rupiah was steady at IDR9,460 against the dollar immediately after the decision, later weakening to IDR9,480 on regional concern and importers' demand for dollars. The stock market closed down 0.9%, a slight recovery from deeper losses earlier in the day.

The central bank also said Indonesian commercial banks increased their loans by 26.3% during the first five months of the year, a sign of continued improvement in their intermediary role. The central bank has been encouraging banks to lend to boost economic growth.

Mr. Cahyadi said strong loan growth amid still robust domestic demand could push inflation to 6.3%-6.5% next year.

Inflation will likely stay elevated in July and August due to the start of a new school year and the high spending associated with the Islamic fasting month of Ramadan.

Gov. Nasution also said the bank had cut growth forecasts for 2012 and 2013. The bank now sees 2012 growth of 6.1%-6.5%, whereas last month it said growth would likely be at the bottom end of its 6.3%-6.7% forecast range due to debt crisis in the euro zone, a fragile U.S. recovery and slowdowns in China and India. He added that the bank projects third-quarter growth of 6.3%.

In 2013 the bank now also predicts expansion 6.3%-6.7%, down from 6.4%-6.8% previously.

The rupiah has clawed back some of its losses recently but remains a regional laggard due to expectations that Indonesia's current account will remain in deficit in the third and fourth quarters. Gov. Nasution said Thursday the current account deficit likely widened in the second quarter.

The bank has said it predicts a current-account deficit of about $3 billion in 2012, but some analysts have said it could be almost three times that amount. The deficit will add more pressure on Indonesia's foreign-exchange reserves, which have decreased by some $10 billion in the last two months, to about $106.5 billion at the end of June, as Bank Indonesiaintervenes in the market to stave off rupiah volatility.

In an unexpected move, Deputy Governor Halim Alamsyah also said the central bank may allow onshore banks to swap U.S. dollar bonds for dollars.

The arrangement would be "marginally positive in terms of providing US dollar liquidity," Barclays said in a research note. "That said, the immediate impact might be limited as banks that have U.S. dollar bonds are more likely to have cash dollars as well, and hence would be unlikely to tap this window."

Dollar liquidity has been a problem in Indonesia, where risk-averse foreigners recently pushed the rupiah the lows not seen in almost four years as they sought dollars to exit the market. Bank Indonesia introduced dollar term deposits in June in a bid to attract more offshore dollars into the currency market.

Still, demand for dollars remains high and the rupiah remains Southeast Asia's worst-performing currency this year, having fallen about 4% year to date and more than 9% in the last 12 months.

Gov. Nasution reiterated the bank's stance that the U.S. dollar would average IDR9,200 this year.

"Prospects for the rupiah will remain poor, given widening trade and current account deficits," Hak Bin Chua of Merrill Lynch said in a research note. "Given weak exports, the current account deficit could widen in excess of $5 billion, or about 2.4% of GDP, in the second quarter. Falling foreign reserves could also restrain Bank Indonesia's intervention efforts to stabilize the rupiah."
