title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Up On Korean Tensions;Resistance At 9,010
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0715 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR sharply higher at 9,000 vs 8,965 as rising Korean tensions drives safe haven USD up vs most Asian currencies, dealers say. "I think 9,010 should be the resistance for today. And if the dollar comes back down, it will likely be supported at 8,985," says dealer. Dealers say no sign of suspected Bank Indonesia's intervention to slow USD/IDR rise so far. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0712 GMT [Dow Jones] News of explosion inside North Korea rattles Asian currencies with USD/SGD pushing up around 30 ticks to just below 1.3200. Trader at local bank expects pair to remain capped at 1.3200 for now, tips likely support at 1.3150. "I think there's still risk in the Korean peninsula that is going to create more uncertainty in the market," trader says. Notes 1.3200 is about 2.5% above estimated MAS NEER mid-point. Pair now 1.3181 vs 1.3092 early. (samuel.holmes@dowjones.com)

0710 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/INR implied volatilities tad higher as spot inches up on Korean tensions, but market still betting against heavy spillover into INR with impact of Korea unlikely very much beyond initial knee-jerk uptick, says trader with foreign bank; 1-month ATMF at 8.90%/9.90% vs 8.70%/9.70% late Thursday. Tips belly, back-end to remain unaffected, although geopolitical cue from Korea could keep front-end supported at current levels. Adds, real story may be on risk reversals, with front-end risk reversals beginning to find firmer bidding interest, which may pick up pace through session. (bijou.george@dowjones.com)

0710 GMT [Dow Jones] Asian local currency bonds are at risk of rising inflation, without taxes, says Morgan Stanley. Says reintroduction of withholding taxes in Korea, Thailand on offshore bond holdings, risks that further restrictions on portfolio flows may be imposed across region merit reassessment of attractiveness of Asian local currency bonds. Notes Korean and Singaporean government bonds sharply down this week. "Most Asian local currency bond markets continue to have very flat curve slopes, which implies that most curves currently offer modest compensation to investors for extending duration beyond the belly of the curve," House says. Recommends reducing duration to front-ends in most markets across Asia. (chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0708 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/CHF erodes the psychologically-important resistance at 1.0, but needs a [daily] close above that level to confirm a positive upside bias, says Commerzbank. "A close above 1.0 will target 1.0329 [the 38.2% retracement of the move down from June] en route to 1.0480, the upside measured target of the base," says technical analyst Karen Anne Jones. USD/CHF trades at 1.0015. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0706 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/CHF is still under pressure and even an expected weakening of the Swiss KOF leading indicator, at 1030 GMT, is unlikely to boost the pair, says Commerzbank. "It's all down to the weakness of the euro, though we've also had positive Swiss trade and employment data recently," says analyst Ulrich Leuchtmann. EUR/CHF trades at 1.3301. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0701 GMT [Dow Jones] HSI down 1.0% at 22,819.17 vs 23,036.18 midday, tracking A-shares' fall (Shanghai Composite last down 0.9%) on lingering tightening worries, which pressured China, HK stocks since higher-than-expected China CPI data out earlier this month, stoking fears of tightening by Beijing. Still, "(we) understand the temptation to 'go defensive' on China as policy starts to tighten, but with a gradual U.S. demand recovery still ahead, the notion that H-shares have already peaked strikes us as jittery," says Macquarie. Adds, with Chinese, HK policymakers steering flows away from stretched property markets, stocks "may relatively benefit." Blue chips' weakness across the board with 42 of 45 index members down, but Li & Fung (0494.HK), not exposed to China, HK risks, +2.0% at HK$46.70, outperforming for second day. Market volume tepid at HK$42.33 billion. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0700 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/HKD higher, tracking USD strength vs EUR, regional currencies; some investors repatriate funds amid rising tensions on Korean Peninsula ahead of planned U.S.-South Korea naval exercises Sunday, says trader at China-based bank. Tips pair in 7.7620-7.7650 band near-term. "I've spotted some overseas banks covering short positions. I expect the pair to rise further." Pair last at 7.7623, vs 7.7588 yesterday. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0646 GMT [Dow Jones] Investor apathy in Singapore stock market persists, keeping overall volume light, STI tad lower. Index off 0.2% at 3152.20, still in tight morning range of 3151-3164. Any further downside not likely to push STI below current November low of 3118 set this week. "We expect the local market to remain rangebound today in a sleepy session," says CIMB. New listing Sabana REIT (M1GU.SG) falls prey to soft market conditions, last at S$1.01 vs S$1.05 IPO price, although off early low of S$0.97. Market breadth negative at almost 2 decliners for each gainer vs neutral by end of morning session. Among blue chips, notable decliners include SembMarine (S51.SG), off 3.0% at S$4.88, CityDev (C09.SG), off 1.3% at S$12.18, ST Engineering (S63.SG), off 1.2% at S$3.24. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com)

0644 GMT [Dow Jones] ASIAN SUMMARY: Regional markets mostly lower; Kospi ends down 1.4%, extending fall after AFP reports North Korea says planned U.S.-South Korea naval exercises would bring peninsula closer to war; Nikkei down 0.4%; S&P/ASX +0.1%; HSI down 1.0%; Taiex down 0.5%; Sensex down 1.1%; Shanghai Composite down 0.9%; STI down 0.2%; Indonesian shares down 0.5%; Philippine shares down 1.1%; SET down 0.5%; NZX-50 flat; KLCI down 0.4%. In FX markets, USD/JPY at 83.90, near 8-week high, vs 83.56 in NY late Thursday, EUR/USD at 1.3292 vs 1.3369, EUR/JPY at 111.51 vs 111.75. PBOC adviser Li Daokui says October interest rate hike signals further rate adjustments likely, priority shifted to containing inflationary expectations over maintaining fast, steady growth. State-run China Securities Journal reports, citing unnamed sources, some Chinese investment banks asked property sector clients to turn to Hong Kong bourse to raise money. State-run Shanghai Securities News reports, citing unnnamed source, China will continue to target 8.0% GDP growth in 2011. Japan October core CPI down 0.6% on-year vs down 1.1% in September, down 0.6% expected. Kyodo reports Japan economic minister Kaieda says worried about consumer spending from next year; not mulling additional stimulus now. RBA Gov. Glenn Stevens says policy settings little tighter than average but appropriate for period ahead. Korea October current account surplus $5.37 billion vs September's revised $3.95 billion. BOK Official says exports to remain robust in November; current account surplus to easily exceed $30 billion this year. Thai Prime Minister reiterates expects Thai GDP to grow close to 8% this year, expects BOT to continue to enter FX market, but only to limit volatility. Singapore October manufacturing output +31% vs revised +26.8% in September, +26.5% expected. Philippines September trade surplus $751 million vs deficit $32 million year earlier. Spot gold at $1,367.90/oz, down $7.20 vs NY close. January Nymex crude oil futures at $83.62/bbl down 24 cents compared with Wednesday's New York settlement. (john.phillips@dowjones.com)

0641 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/JPY may rise, possibly to 87.00 sometime in December on any further gains in U.S. Treasury yields, says Hideki Amikura, deputy general manager at Nomura Trust and Banking. "The main driver for further gains would be continued rises in Treasury yields, particularly in the short zone." Many investors watch spreads between short-dated U.S.-Japan government debt as indicator for direction to take on pair. Says continued tensions on Korean peninsula may also help USD/JPY. While both USD, JPY considered safe havens, investors likely to prefer USD to JPY given Japan's proximity to conflict. "The tensions will probably continue to prompt some global investors to consider trimming their yen holdings further." U.S., South Korea to commence 4-day joint naval exercise in Yellow Sea on Sunday, following North Korea's shelling of South Korean island there earlier this week. USD/JPY last at 83.86 after hitting fresh near 8-week high at 83.92.(andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0639 GMT [Dow Jones] Credit Agricole says PBOC's recent "hawkish" rhetoric reflects mounting price pressures. House expects monetary tightening to accelerate as inflation likely to remain elevated in medium term, rise towards 5% on-year by mid-2011. Revises rate hike call to 100 bps vs 50 bps by mid-2011. Expects 200 bp increase in RRR within same time frame. Revises down end-2011 USD/CNY target to 6.30 from 6.45, says faster CNY rise likely to limit imported inflation. "We believe that the central bank is behind the curve and is only at the beginning of a scramble to control prices." PBOC Deputy Gov. Hu Xiaolian said earlier central bank plans to normalize money, credit growth using rates, required reserve ratio, open market operations. (jean.yung@dowjones.com) [ 11-26-10 0215ET ]

Additional Information regarding the Notes 
1.         The EU has adopted a Directive regarding the taxation of savings 
income (the "Savings Directive").  The Savings Directive requires Member States 
(as defined below) to provide to the tax authorities of other Member States 
details of payments of interest and other similar income paid by a person to an 
individual in another Member State, except that Austria and Luxembourg will 
instead impose a withholding system for a transitional period unless during such 
period they elect otherwise. 
 
The Bank undertakes that it will ensure that it maintains a paying agent in a 
country which is a member of the European Union (a "Member State") that will not

constitutes income from sources outside the United States but will, depending on

            D) Due to a change in law since the date of the Prospectus, the

3.         Noteholders should consult their own tax advisors concerning the 
consequences of owning the Notes in their particular circumstances under the 
Internal Revenue Code and the laws of any other taxing jurisdiction. 
 
4.         Additional Investment Considerations: 
 
The Notes offered by this Pricing Supplement are complex financial instruments 
and may not be suitable for certain investors. Investors intending to purchase 
the Notes should consult with their tax and financial advisors to ensure that 
the intended purchase meets the investment objective before making such 
purchase. 
 
There are various risks associated with the Notes including, but not limited to, 
exchange rate risk, price risk and liquidity risk. Investors should consult with 
their own financial, legal and accounting advisors about the risks associated 
with an investment in these Notes, the appropriate tools to analyze that 
investment, and the suitability of the investment in each investor's particular 
circumstances.  Holders of the Notes should also consult with their professional 
tax advisors regarding tax laws applicable to them. 
 
The Bank will hedge its obligations under the Notes by entering into a swap 
transaction with an affiliate of the Dealer as swap counterparty.  Assuming no 
change in market conditions or any other relevant factors, the price, if any, at 
which the Dealer or another purchaser might be willing to purchase Notes in a 
secondary market transaction is expected to be lower, and could be substantially 
lower, than the original issue price of the Notes.  This is due to a number of 
factors, including that (i) the potential profit to the secondary market 
purchaser of the Notes may be incorporated into any offered price and (ii) the 
cost of funding used to value the Notes in the secondary market is expected to 
be higher than our actual cost of funding incurred in connection with the 
issuance of the Notes.  In addition, the original issue price of the Notes 
included, and secondary market prices are likely to exclude, the projected 
profit that our swap counterparty or its affiliates may realize in connection 
with this swap.  Further, as a result of dealer discounts, mark-ups or other 
transaction costs, any of which may be significant, the original issue price may 
differ from values determined by pricing models used by our swap counterparty or 
other potential purchasers of the Notes in secondary market transactions. 
 
Payment of each Interest Amount and the Redemption Amount will be based on the 
IDR Rate, which is a measure of the rate of exchange between the Indonesian 
Rupiah and the USD.  Currency exchange rates are volatile and will affect the

governmental actions could adversely affect the value of the Notes, as well as

acceleration.  Even in the absence of governmental action directly affecting 
currency exchange rates, political or economic developments in Indonesia or 
elsewhere could lead to significant and sudden changes in the exchange rate 
between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD. 
 
The Indonesian Rupiah is an emerging market currency.  Emerging market

government actions including currency controls, devaluations and other matters 
which could materially and adversely affect the value of the Notes.

title: MARKET TALK: China Govt Bonds Down On Strong CPI, Loans Data
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0220 GMT [Dow Jones] China government bonds lower after data show October CPI, new yuan loans stronger than expectations, strengthening concerns Beijing would introduce interest rate hikes in near term following latest decision to hike banks' reserve requirement ratio by 50 bps, says Shanghai-based trader with local insurer; adds PBOC shifting its moderately loose monetary policy to prudent, likely to further tighten liquidity in 2011. Shanghai Stock Exchange government bond index at 125.96 vs 125.99 last close, tipped in 125.80-126.00 band rest of session. (ming.wang@dowjones.com)

0219 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/TWD down at 30.075 vs 30.600 late yesterday; pair remains weighed by foreign fund inflows, exporters' stop-loss selling, says local bank trader. Pair also weighed by Commercial Times report, which cites Taiwan Vice Premier Sean Chen's comment Wednesday criticizing central bank's intervention. Trader notes exporters, banks "have been complaining about the central bank's policy," as TWD closing level in Taipei doesn't represent real trading conditions. Trader says central bank may taper off its daily intervention. Tips pair to test 30.000 support today. Adds, investors ignore Taiwan legislature financial committee's proposal to impose management fees on speculative funds, as players expect management fee wouldn't stop foreign inflows amid global excess liquidity conditions. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0213 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan stocks off 0.1% at 8444.97, shares tipped consolidate in tight range around current level on uncertainty ahead of local mayoral elections. Some hot money from bonds entering equities market as Taiwan government tightens restrictions on some short-term local currency products, but slowing total foreign inflows, profit-taking on tech shares balancing out upside, says KGI Securities analyst Randy Chang. "Right now, no one expects the G-20 to solve anything. We don't see any kind of consensus, so we don't think it will have much impact on the market," he says. Tips Taiex in 8400-8480 range today. Acer (2353.TW) off 0.8% at NT$89.50 on weak October sales. Hon Hai (2317.TW) off 0.9% at NT$115.50, Formosa Plastics (1301.TW) off 2.0% at NT$92.00 on profit taking. Cathay Financial (2882.TW) +0.3% at NT$48.45, China Airlines (2610.TW) +0.7% at NT$23.30. (paul.mozur@dowjones.com)

0211 GMT [Dow Jones] China October CPI up 4.4% on year, vs 4.0% tipped in Dow Jones poll, September's +3.6%; growth fuels rising worries about inflation, feeding debate between analysts on extent of upward price pressures. China October food prices +10.1% on year, many economists believe food prices main driver, inflation will decline in coming months with autumn harvest. But others see inflation spreading to non-food items, believe it's being driven by ample money, credit conditions. Data come after China raises banks' reserve requirement ratio by 50 bps (effective from next Tuesday), 4th such hike this year, likely aiming to relieve some inflationary pressures; China also hiked interest rates for 1st time in almost 3 years in October to combat inflation, asset bubbles. Some economists say China entering cycle of more rate hikes. Adding to inflation concerns, PPI up 5.0% in October, vs 4.3% rise in September, Dow Jones poll tip of 4.6%, on rising commodity prices globally. (owen.fletcher@dowjones.com)

0211 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares likely higher, tracking gains in many Asian markets after shares in U.S. ended higher overnight, traders say; expect main index to top 3780 after shares ended +0.5% yesterday at fresh record high of 3756.967. But trader at First Asia Capital says "buying won't be as huge as in previous sessions as local funds may take profit after recent gains." Bellwether Telkom (TLKM.JK) may gain after ADRs +1.8% in NY, while car maker Astra (ASII.JK) may rise on bargain buying. Profit-taking likely hit nickel miner Inco (INCO.JK) on lower nickel prices. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0207 GMT [Dow Jones] China's fixed-asset investment, industrial output data show economic growth steady after Beijing launched series of steps earlier this year to cool investment in real estate and other sectors with overcapacity, but inflation worry likely will prompt government to consider more tightening steps, such as further reserve requirement ratio hikes. But any tightening steps may have to be launched prudently to avoid hurting economic growth too much. Urban fixed-asset investment +24.4% on-year in January-October period, vs January-September's +24.5%, in line with economists forecast of +24.4%; October industrial output +13.1% on year, slightly slower vs September's +13.3%, expectation of +13.4%. See: =DATA SNAP: China January-October Urban FAI Up 24.4%; Expected Up 24.4% (victoria.ruan@dowjones.com)

0204 GMT [Dow Jones] MKS Finance says gold market characterized by volatile and choppy trading. "We expect gold to remain choppy in the near-term, closely tied to the moves in the U.S. currency despite renewed concerns over European sovereign debt." Spot gold at $1,402.60/oz, down 80 cents after bouncing off low of $1,383.55/oz overnight. Gold in euros at EUR1,015.70/oz, down EUR3.70 after again failing to surpass its June 7 record close of EUR1,020.50 yesterday. Precious metals wavering on some suggestions Fed's quantitative easing plans could be curtailed if U.S. economic data continues to improve; U.S. new jobless claims fell to better than expected 435,000 in week ended Nov. 6. However Fed's announcement late Wednesday it will purchase $105 billion in Treasurys during next month possibly more resonant for gold bulls. (james.campbell@dowjones.com)

0155 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippines shares tad higher, with investors starting to hunt for bargains after 4-session, 4.5% retreat; bellwether PSEi +0.1% to 4200.85 in light volume, with support pegged at 4150, resistance 4250; market breadth positive, with gainers beating decliners 46 to 23. Leading gainers, Aboitiz Power (AP.PH) +5.0% at PHP30.50, Alliance Global Group (AGI.PH) +2.0% at PHP11.02 and Metro Pacific Investments (MPI.PH) +0.5% at PHP4.03, which all recent decliners; retreaters led by PLDT (TEL.PH), down 0.1% to PHP2,416. "I expect a technical bounce today after the 4-day retreat. The market has fallen too fast, too soon," says SB Equities research head Erwin Balita. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0155 GMT [Dow Jones] China shares open higher, led by coal miners, but concerns about further monetary tightening to rein in inflation, limits index upside. Shanghai Composite Index last +0.1% at 3119.49, may turn lower to test support at 3080 (near 10-day moving average) after release of October CPI due 0200 GMT. Expectations are that China's CPI likely rose 4.4% last month, "if confirmed, it will definitely intensify concerns about a further interest rate hike in the short term," says CSC International analyst Zhang Yuheng. Coal producers rise on expected higher seasonal sales in winter: China Shenhua Energy (601088.SH) +2.3% at CNY29.20, Yanzhou Coal Mining (600188.SH) +3.9% at CNY32.15. Shenzhen Index flat at 1390.00. (rose.yu@dowjones.com)

0154 GMT [Dow Jones] Japan MOF says coupon on 5-year JGBs at auction later in day at 0.30%; Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Katsutoshi Inadome says tender "should meet strong demand." Says buying from Japanese banks with excess liquidity likely robust, also current yield levels of around 0.35% close to fair value, and that's attractive. Lead December futures last up 0.06 at 142.58, 10-year yield last unchanged at 0.990%, 5-year yield last down 0.5 bp at 0.345%.(takashi.mochizuki@dowjones.com)

0152 GMT [Dow Jones] November HSI futures +0.5% at 24,520, indicating cash market may open higher after DJIA's modest rise. Still contract ends yesterday at 93-point discount, suggests HK market may witness further consolidation near-term. November open interest down 1,927 lots at 116,434. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0151 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR falls to 8,885, lowest level since June 6, 2007, vs 8,895 yesterday, as capital inflows continue, partly due to intact bearish sentiment on greenback globally, dealers say. 3 dealers note no indications of Bank Indonesia intervention to slow pair's slide. "I expect Bank Indonesia to start buying the dollar at IDR8,800 to slow the rupiah's appreciation," dealer says; 8,880-8,900 range tipped for day. Unabating inflows of short-term capital have prompted Bank Indonesia to consider imposing further measures to avoid a sudden reversal of these funds, such as possibility of imposing longer a holding period than one month currently required for its money market securities. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com) [ 11-10-10 2120ET ]

Pair also weighed by Commercial Times report, which cites Taiwan Vice Premier Sean Chen's comment Wednesday criticizing central bank's intervention. Trader notes exporters, banks "have been complaining about the central bank's policy," as TWD closing level in Taipei doesn't represent real trading conditions. Trader says central bank may taper off its daily intervention. Tips pair to test 30.000 support today. Adds, investors ignore Taiwan legislature financial committee's proposal to impose management fees on speculative funds, as players expect management fee wouldn't stop foreign inflows amid global excess liquidity conditions. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0213 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan stocks off 0.1% at 8444.97, shares tipped consolidate in tight range around current level on uncertainty ahead of local mayoral elections. Some hot money from bonds entering equities market as Taiwan government tightens restrictions on some short-term local currency products, but slowing total foreign inflows, profit-taking on tech shares balancing out upside, says KGI Securities analyst Randy Chang. "Right now, no one expects the G-20 to solve anything. We don't see any kind of consensus, so we don't think it will have much impact on the market," he says. Tips Taiex in 8400-8480 range today. Acer (2353.TW) off 0.8% at NT$89.50 on weak October sales. Hon Hai (2317.TW) off 0.9% at NT$115.50, Formosa Plastics (1301.TW) off 2.0% at NT$92.00 on profit taking. Cathay Financial (2882.TW) +0.3% at NT$48.45, China Airlines (2610.TW) +0.7% at NT$23.30. (paul.mozur@dowjones.com)

0211 GMT [Dow Jones] China October CPI up 4.4% on year, vs 4.0% tipped in Dow Jones poll, September's +3.6%; growth fuels rising worries about inflation, feeding debate between analysts on extent of upward price pressures. China October food prices +10.1% on year, many economists believe food prices main driver, inflation will decline in coming months with autumn harvest. But others see inflation spreading to non-food items, believe it's being driven by ample money, credit conditions. Data come after China raises banks' reserve requirement ratio by 50 bps (effective from next Tuesday), 4th such hike this year, likely aiming to relieve some inflationary pressures; China also hiked interest rates for 1st time in almost 3 years in October to combat inflation, asset bubbles. Some economists say China entering cycle of more rate hikes. Adding to inflation concerns, PPI up 5.0% in October, vs 4.3% rise in September, Dow Jones poll tip of 4.6%, on rising commodity prices globally. (owen.fletcher@dowjones.com)

0211 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares likely higher, tracking gains in many Asian markets after shares in U.S. ended higher overnight, traders say; expect main index to top 3780 after shares ended +0.5% yesterday at fresh record high of 3756.967. But trader at First Asia Capital says "buying won't be as huge as in previous sessions as local funds may take profit after recent gains." Bellwether Telkom (TLKM.JK) may gain after ADRs +1.8% in NY, while car maker Astra (ASII.JK) may rise on bargain buying. Profit-taking likely hit nickel miner Inco (INCO.JK) on lower nickel prices. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0207 GMT [Dow Jones] China's fixed-asset investment, industrial output data show economic growth steady after Beijing launched series of steps earlier this year to cool investment in real estate and other sectors with overcapacity, but inflation worry likely will prompt government to consider more tightening steps, such as further reserve requirement ratio hikes. But any tightening steps may have to be launched prudently to avoid hurting economic growth too much. Urban fixed-asset investment +24.4% on-year in January-October period, vs January-September's +24.5%, in line with economists forecast of +24.4%; October industrial output +13.1% on year, slightly slower vs September's +13.3%, expectation of +13.4%. See: =DATA SNAP: China January-October Urban FAI Up 24.4%; Expected Up 24.4% (victoria.ruan@dowjones.com)

0204 GMT [Dow Jones] MKS Finance says gold market characterized by volatile and choppy trading. "We expect gold to remain choppy in the near-term, closely tied to the moves in the U.S. currency despite renewed concerns over European sovereign debt." Spot gold at $1,402.60/oz, down 80 cents after bouncing off low of $1,383.55/oz overnight. Gold in euros at EUR1,015.70/oz, down EUR3.70 after again failing to surpass its June 7 record close of EUR1,020.50 yesterday. Precious metals wavering on some suggestions Fed's quantitative easing plans could be curtailed if U.S. economic data continues to improve; U.S. new jobless claims fell to better than expected 435,000 in week ended Nov. 6. However Fed's announcement late Wednesday it will purchase $105 billion in Treasurys during next month possibly more resonant for gold bulls. (james.campbell@dowjones.com)

0155 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippines shares tad higher, with investors starting to hunt for bargains after 4-session, 4.5% retreat; bellwether PSEi +0.1% to 4200.85 in light volume, with support pegged at 4150, resistance 4250; market breadth positive, with gainers beating decliners 46 to 23. Leading gainers, Aboitiz Power (AP.PH) +5.0% at PHP30.50, Alliance Global Group (AGI.PH) +2.0% at PHP11.02 and Metro Pacific Investments (MPI.PH) +0.5% at PHP4.03, which all recent decliners; retreaters led by PLDT (TEL.PH), down 0.1% to PHP2,416. "I expect a technical bounce today after the 4-day retreat. The market has fallen too fast, too soon," says SB Equities research head Erwin Balita. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0155 GMT [Dow Jones] China shares open higher, led by coal miners, but concerns about further monetary tightening to rein in inflation, limits index upside. Shanghai Composite Index last +0.1% at 3119.49, may turn lower to test support at 3080 (near 10-day moving average) after release of October CPI due 0200 GMT. Expectations are that China's CPI likely rose 4.4% last month, "if confirmed, it will definitely intensify concerns about a further interest rate hike in the short term," says CSC International analyst Zhang Yuheng. Coal producers rise on expected higher seasonal sales in winter: China Shenhua Energy (601088.SH) +2.3% at CNY29.20, Yanzhou Coal Mining (600188.SH) +3.9% at CNY32.15. Shenzhen Index flat at 1390.00. (rose.yu@dowjones.com)

0154 GMT [Dow Jones] Japan MOF says coupon on 5-year JGBs at auction later in day at 0.30%; Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Katsutoshi Inadome says tender "should meet strong demand." Says buying from Japanese banks with excess liquidity likely robust, also current yield levels of around 0.35% close to fair value, and that's attractive. Lead December futures last up 0.06 at 142.58, 10-year yield last unchanged at 0.990%, 5-year yield last down 0.5 bp at 0.345%.(takashi.mochizuki@dowjones.com)

0152 GMT [Dow Jones] November HSI futures +0.5% at 24,520, indicating cash market may open higher after DJIA's modest rise. Still contract ends yesterday at 93-point discount, suggests HK market may witness further consolidation near-term. November open interest down 1,927 lots at 116,434. (susanna.tai@dowjones.com)

0151 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR falls to 8,885, lowest level since June 6, 2007, vs 8,895 yesterday, as capital inflows continue, partly due to intact bearish sentiment on greenback globally, dealers say. 3 dealers note no indications of Bank Indonesia intervention to slow pair's slide. "I expect Bank Indonesia to start buying the dollar at IDR8,800 to slow the rupiah's appreciation," dealer says; 8,880-8,900 range tipped for day. Unabating inflows of short-term capital have prompted Bank Indonesia to consider imposing further measures to avoid a sudden reversal of these funds, such as possibility of imposing longer a holding period than one month currently required for its money market securities. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0151 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/JPY may fall to 112.50 if China CPI, PPI for October is strong, fueling speculation that China may take hawkish monetary policy soon, which in turn likely to weigh on share prices, riskier currencies such as EUR, says Tomohiro Nishida, senior dealer at Chuo Mitsui Trust and Banking; China inflation data due 0200 GMT; EUR/JPY last at 113.41. In that scenario, EUR/USD may fall towards 1.3700; pair last at 1.3801.(kosaku.narioka@dowjones.com) [ 11-10-10 2119ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: Indonesia Shares End +0.5%; 3800 Cap Eyed
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0920 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares end +0.5% at fresh record high of 3756.967 in moderate volume, boosted by foreign buying in most telecom, commodity-related stocks amid hopes for strong FY earnings, traders say; expect shares to continue to gain tomorrow, with main index likely testing 3800-resistance level. "Healthy foreign-buying was the main driver for the gain of the main index," says trader at Erdhika Securities. Foreigners net buyers of IDR205 billion worth of shares vs IDR150 billion net buys yesterday. Among gainers, steel maker Krakatau Steel (KRAS.JK) +49% at IDR1,270 on debut, heavyweight Telkom (TLKM.JK) +3.7% at IDR8,450, while nickel producer Inco (INCO.JK) +2.1% at IDR5,000. Profit-taking hits car maker Astra (ASII.JK) down 1.2% at IDR57,450. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0914 GMT [Dow Jones] Nomura expects EUR/CHF to trade higher and says it's therefore bought a three-month EUR/CHF 1.3700 call for 1.04% of EUR face value. "Our first target is a short term (one month) recovery in the cross back to its recent high above 1.38. With time value still in the option, this would broadly cover the premium (with current vol and skew if spot is at 1.38 in one month the call would be worth 1%, almost exactly covering the premium)," it says. "The next target is a move to 1.4150, the mid-point of the late May-early June range. This would provide a 3:1 payout. We allocate $10m within our $100m model portfolio," Nomura adds. Spot EUR/CHF trades at 1.3395. (martin.essex@dowjones.com)

0912 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD slips back a little as investors continue to readjust their positions ahead of this weekend's G-20 summit in Seoul. Rising tensions, fueled by China reporting a larger than expected trade surplus for October, should help the USD as risk sentiment subsides. The EUR is a little higher, with the single currency getting some respite despite continued concerns over a euro zone debt default. The market is now waiting to see if a Portuguese debt auction later in the day fares as well as one did for Greece on Tuesday. The EUR is up at $1.3811 while the USD has fallen a little to Y81.68. The GBP is up at $1.6001 even though there are fears that the Bank of England will give a downbeat assessment of the UK economy in its quarterly Inflation Report later in the day. (nick.hastings@dowjones.com)

0911 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia shares end higher to close at new all-time high; KLCI ends +0.1% at 1528.01."The FBM KLCI is now in uncharted territory. The mid-cap and lower liner stocks have also begun to move, making the current rise a very broadbased one," says Maybank IB. "We believe that the FBM KLCI should now head up towards the 1533 and 1553 target areas." Market breadth positive with 441 decliners vs 420 advancers; YTL Corp (4677.KU) +4.2% at MYR8.39, Malaysian Resources (1651.KU) +3.7% at MYR2.25. Decliners include AMMB Holdings (1015.KU) down 1.6% at MYR6.20, Genting (3182.KU) down 1.1% at MYR10.68, AirAsia (5099.KU) down 1.2% at MYR2.44. (ankur.relia@dowjones.com)

0911 GMT [Dow Jones] There's been a subtle change in USD/JPY's fortunes says Mizuho Corporate Bank's Nicole Elliott. A small spike low and a bullish engulfing candle hints that the spot will hold above its November low of 80.21 for at least another week or two. The spot is currently struggling with its 26DMA around 81.84, however, Elliott expects it to make a fresh interim high, however, she still favors small shorts from 81.85 with a stop above 82.55 for a first downside target of 80.85. USD/JPY now at 81.68 from the day's high of 81.91. (gary.stride@dowjones.com)

0910 GMT [Dow Jones] Irish and Portuguese bond yields continue to widen versus bunds Wednesday ahead of the Portuguese October 2016 and June 2020 bond auctions. "The disastrous performance of Portuguese bonds has everything to do with enormous doubts about the Portuguese Budget, both initially in terms of it being passed, and then in terms of its overall feasibility," says Marc Ostwald, Monument Securities strategist. "That the risks in Portugal have risen sharply in recent months is indisputable, but the chances of a debt rescheduling or default still look to be remote, and as such the heightened risks appear to be more than adequately priced into current yields, and a decent cover should be achievable." The Irish situation shows no signs of improving any time soon, with uncertainty of the December 7 budget passing through parliament adding to EFSF bailout concerns. The 10-year Irish/German yield spread is 4bps wider at 557.5bps and the 10-year Portuguese/German spread is 3.5bps wider at 439bps, according to Tradeweb. (nick.andrews@dowjones.com)

0910 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia's move to drop 3-month certificates, or SBI, in today's auction signifies central bank's concerns on speculative flows, may extend minimum holding period of SBIs, says OCBC; move "is a bid to continue pushing investors to go into the longer-end papers, which in turn is meant to reduce speculative flows in the market." Adds, concerns on sudden outflows remain; "we would not be surprised if they were to implement a longer minimum holding period for SBI bills to 3 months from 1 month" currently. (andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

0908 GMT [Dow Jones] Nomura still reckons GBP will outperform but prefers to remove the directional USD bias inherent in the short EUR/GBP trade it entered on November 2. It argues that EUR/GBP tends to be positively correlated with EUR/USD, so a renewed USD sell-off could hurt the trade. As a result, it is switching to a GBP basket trade, with two thirds invested against EUR and one third against USD. The EUR/GBP trade is closed for a profit of around 1.3% of the amount invested. "We enter this new basket trade at 0.8620 EUR/GBP and 1.5990 GBP/USD. We will run a 1.0% basket stop loss... We allocate $10m within our $100m model portfolio," Nomura says. (martin.essex@dowjones.com)

0907 GMT [Dow Jones] As tensions rise ahead of the G-20 summit starting this Thursday in Seoul, expect the USD to benefit, says Commerzbank. The bank notes that the whole issue of QEII, which had initially hit the USD, has now been pushed onto the back burner, while news of China's even larger than expected trade surplus will fuel discontent. "The USD often benefits if there is tension on the international scene. As a result EUR/USD might ease further initially," the bank says. (nick.hastings@dowjones.com)

0905 GMT [Dow Jones] PREVIEW: China's October industrial production likely +13.4% on-year vs September's +13.3%, according to Dow Jones poll of 12 economists. Survey also shows urban fixed asset investment likely +24.4% in January-October period on-year vs January-September's +24.5%. Survey shows China's industrial output, investment remain relatively stable, despite cooling measures this year such as first ever rate hike in almost three years in October, continuous measures to cool property market. "Industry seems to have achieved a soft landing, but with industrial output growth slightly weaker than during the pre-crisis period," says Capital Economics economist Mark Williams. Data due Thursday. (li.liu@dowjones.com)

0901 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia's real GDP growth likely slowed to 5.6% on-year in 3Q vs +8.9% in 2Q, +10.1% in 1Q says RHB Research; 3Q industrial production growth slows to +4.3% on-year vs +11.1% in 2Q. "Going forward, we expect the global economy to expand at a more moderate pace in 2011," says RHB. Adds, in tandem with slowdown in global demand, country's exports may also slow in 2011 but domestic demand growth may stay resilient but grow at more moderate pace of 5.5% in 2011 vs +5.9% tipped for 2010. House expects real GDP growth to slow to 5.0% in 2011 from +7.3% forecast for 2010. (kwan-por.lee@dowjones.com)

0856 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR lower at 8,895 vs 8,904 late yesterday in line with USD's weakness vs regional currencies, dealers say; no sign of Bank Indonesia's intervention to prevent pair from sliding below 8,900, two dealers say. "I was surprised that Bank Indonesia didn't seem to intervene," one of them says; adds pair may slide further tomorrow, but profit taking evident in local bond market today could limit USD/IDR slide to 8,885; 8,910 resistance tipped. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com) [ 11-10-10 0420ET ]

0855 GMT [Dow Jones] UBS downgrades Sandvik (SAND.SK) to sell from neutral. "We believe the stock should derate going forward with 4Q results or news suggesting weaker commodity prices being potential catalysts for a de-rating," the bank says. Adds that of SKF (SKF-B.SK), Sandvik and Atlas Copco (ATCO-A.SK) it still prefers SKF and thinks it deserves to outperform relative to the other two. Keeps SEK95 target unchanged due to better cash flow offsetting EPS downgrades. Shares -1.9% at SEK111.50. (sven.grundberg@dowjones.com)

0853 GMT [Dow Jones] The December 10-year gilt opened below the 123.81 support level and "a settlement below here will be a further negative, suggesting the directional risk is beginning to skew to the downside once more and that a deeper sell-off is on the cards," says Richard Adcock, UBS technical strategist. "The bearish themes are backed up by the momentum/trending relationship, with the MACD still below its zero line, and we will now look for a closing cross lower in stochastics over the next few days to confirm the resumption of the downside that can test the more important longer term support at 121.93/122.22." Support lies at 123.20, 122.22 and 121.93. (nick.andrews@dowjones.com)

0849 GMT [Dow Jones] Sensex trapped in narrow band, now flat at 20,915.29 on absence of fresh triggers, subdued cues from Asian peers. "Most of the major company results are already out and there are no major events to look forward to," says Prakash Diwan of Networth Stock-Broking. Another analyst tips index in 20,500-21,200 band near-term. Among actives, Tata Motors (500570.BY) +3.3% at INR1312 as 2Q net profit surged to INR22.23 billion, up vs INR217.8 million year earlier. However, Hindalco Industries (500440.BY), which posted lower-than-expected 2Q net profit late Tuesday, down 3.6% at INR223.45 and Cipla (500087.BY) down 1.7% at INR343.70. (swagata.gupta@dowjones.com)

0846 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia's wider balance of payments data is likely positive for IDR and local bond market, analysts say. Indonesia's BOP stood at $6.96 billion in 3Q vs $5.42 billion in 2Q; contributed by $6.48 billion of capital and financial account (vs $4.37 billion in 2Q), $1.31 billion of current account (vs $1.8 billion in 2Q). "The erosion of the current account surplus is happening at a gradual pace...For the near future, portfolio inflows may continue to be rapid especially in the wake of the Fed's QE2," Bank Danamon's Helmi Arman says. ING shares similar view, but warns not getting too excited until inflation subsides. "We will turn bullish on government bonds after the threat of an above-6.0% inflation print has passed." (andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

0842 GMT [Dow Jones] The zloty is higher as foreign investors are moving into Poland with its relatively high interest rates, a trader says. Adds the currency is likely to test EUR/PLN3.8850 level, vital resistance toward further strengthening in anticipation of rate hikes. EUR/PLN is at 3.8901 from 3.9017, USD/PLN at 2.8190 from 2.8398. (marcin.sobczyk@dowjones.com)

0841 GMT [Dow Jones]USD/INR implied volatilities lower on moribund spot, but finding support at current levels from reviving concerns on health of global economy, says trader with foreign bank; 1-month ATMF at 7.50%/8.25% vs 7.75%/8.50% late Tuesday. Also, approaching G-20 meet also adding to demand for protection from currency swings, bolstering front-end of curve, says trader. Adds, some interest on 3-month to 1-year vega neutral spreads, likely to cover gap in risk bucket rather than play on view for curve. (bijou.george@dowjones.com) [ 11-10-10 0410ET ]

title: UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Keeps Rates Steady; Inflows Bigger Concern
text:
(Adds quotes from central bank, economist on liquidity management, inflation)


 
   By Farida Husna and Andreas Ismar 
   Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia Thursday kept its key interest rate unchanged at a historic low of 6.50%, and reiterated that it views a wall of foreign capital inflows as a greater threat than price pressures.

The central bank's stance strengthens market views that it may keep rates unchanged for the rest of this year, while potentially moving to further strengthen liquidity management after already introducing several measures.

The rate decision was in line with market expectations as slowing inflation is providing room for the central bank to keep borrowing costs low. All 13 economists in a Dow Jones Newswires poll expected Bank Indonesia to keep the overnight policy rate at 6.50%, the level it has been at since August 2009, to help spur growth in Southeast Asia's largest economy.

Indonesia's consumer price index edged down to 5.67% on-year in October from 5.80% in September, the official Central Statistics Agency said Monday. On-month inflation eased to 0.06% from 0.44%.

"The Board of Governors underlines that liquidity management is more important amid huge capital inflows and excess liquidity," Bank Indonesia said in a statement.

Bank Indonesia has ordered commercial banks to raise their reserves by 3 percentage points from Nov. 1 to absorb excess funds and help reduce inflationary pressures.

The move was taken after it issued a set of policies in July, including instituting a one-month holding period for its short-term securities, or SBIs, in a bid to curb hot money flows and reducing risk of sudden capital outflows.

Several central bankers in recent weeks have also aired the idea of further lengthening the minimum holding period of SBIs and term deposits.

"The possible implementation of quasi capital controls is likely to be done in a very careful and well communicated manner, so as to keep the stability of the domestic financial conditions intact," OSK DMG economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja said.

"Our end-2010 forecast for the Bank Indonesia rate remains unchanged at 6.50% and possible rate hikes might only start to materialize around the second half" of next year, Tanuwidjaja added. He forecast the policy rate to reach 7.50% by the end of 2011.

Bank Indonesia also announced Thursday that its foreign exchange reserves jumped to $91.8 billion at the end of October from $86.5 billion in September.

"If we look at the significant jump in FX reserves for October, it is also clear that Bank INdonesia has been more interventionist of late, and this is again another sign of concerns over capital inflows," OCBC economist Gundy Cahyadi said.

Bank Indonesia has said inflows totaled IDR115 trillion ($12.92 billion) between January and September.

-By Farida Husna and Andreas Ismar, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 39831277; andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com [ 04-11-10 0919GMT ]

General Information

Additional Information regarding the Notes

1. The EU has adopted a Directive regarding the taxation of savings income (the "Savings Directive"). The Savings Directive requires Member States (as defined below) to provide to the tax authorities of other Member States details of payments of interest and other similar income paid by a person to an individual in another Member State, except that Austria and Luxembourg will instead impose a withholding system for a transitional period unless during such period they elect otherwise.

The Bank undertakes that it will ensure that it maintains a paying agent in a country which is a member of the European Union (a "Member State") that will not be obliged to withhold or deduct tax pursuant to the Savings Directive.

3. Noteholders should consult their own tax advisors concerning the consequences of owning the Notes in their particular circumstances under the Internal Revenue Code and the laws of any other taxing jurisdiction.

4. Additional Investment Considerations:

The Notes offered by this Pricing Supplement are complex financial instruments and may not be suitable for certain investors. Investors intending to purchase the Notes should consult with their tax and financial advisors to ensure that the intended purchase meets the investment objective before making such purchase.

There are various risks associated with the Notes including, but not limited to, exchange rate risk, price risk and liquidity risk. Investors should consult with their own financial, legal and accounting advisors about the risks associated with an investment in these Notes, the appropriate tools to analyze that investment, and the suitability of the investment in each investor's particular circumstances. Holders of the Notes should also consult with their professional tax advisors regarding tax laws applicable to them.

The Bank will hedge its obligations under the Notes by entering into a swap transaction with an affiliate of the Lead Manager as swap counterparty. Assuming no change in market conditions or any other relevant factors, the price, if any, at which the Managers or another purchaser might be willing to purchase Notes in a secondary market transaction is expected to be lower, and could be substantially lower, than the original issue price of the Notes. This is due to a number of factors, including that (i) the potential profit to the secondary market purchaser of the Notes may be incorporated into any offered price and (ii) the cost of funding used to value the Notes in the secondary market is expected to be higher than our actual cost of funding incurred in connection with the issuance of the Notes. In addition, the original issue price of the Notes included, and secondary market prices are likely to exclude, the projected profit that our swap counterparty or its affiliates may realize in connection with this swap. Further, as a result of dealer discounts, mark-ups or other transaction costs, any of which may be significant, the original issue price may differ from values determined by pricing models used by our swap counterparty or other potential purchasers of the Notes in secondary market transactions.

Payment of each Interest Amount and the Redemption Amount will be based on the Applicable Rate, which is a measure of the rate of exchange between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD. Currency exchange rates are volatile and will affect the holder's return. In addition, the government of Indonesia can from time to time intervene in the foreign exchange market. These interventions or other governmental actions could adversely affect the value of the Notes, as well as the yield (in USD terms) on the Notes and the amount payable at maturity or upon acceleration. Even in the absence of governmental action directly affecting currency exchange rates, political or economic developments in Indonesia or elsewhere could lead to significant and sudden changes in the exchange rate between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD.

The Indonesian Rupiah is an emerging market currency. Emerging market currencies may be subject to particularly substantial volatility, as well as to government actions including currency controls, devaluations and other matters which could materially and adversely affect the value of the Notes.

The methodologies for determining the Applicable Rate may result in a Redemption Amount (or Early Redemption Amount, as the case may be) of the Notes, or an Interest Amount on the Notes, being significantly less than anticipated or less than what an alternative methodology for determining the IDR-USD exchange rate would yield.

0930 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR late higher at 8,930 vs 8,920 yesterday as local players take profit after Bank Indonesia's suspected active intervention recently, showing its resolve not to let greenback fall below IDR8,920. "Market expects Bank Indonesia to continue buying around 8,920 in the near term, providing support for the pair," dealer at local bank says; adds pair remains biased down partly due to robust foreign appetite for local stocks, bonds; tips pair to trade in 8,920-8,935 range Tuesday. (andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

0929 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai government bonds higher in lackluster trade. Mild buying demand seen in short-dated notes in early trade. Players hibernating ahead of Bank of Thailand's policy rate decision Wednesday, though they increasingly believe central bank will keep benchmark rate at 1.75%, says local dealer. Adds, if absence of fresh drivers persists, sentiment likely to remain in doldrums Tuesday. Bid/offer yields of issue due December 2015 quoted at 2.43%/2.40% vs 2.44%/2.40% late Friday, November 2016 at 2.55%/2.50% vs 2.58%/2.55%, June 2019 at 2.78%/2.72% vs 2.81%/2.78%. (piyarat.setthasiriphaiboon@dowjones.com)

0919 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares end down 0.8% at 3566.918 in light volume, but off intraday low of 3557.371, as weaker Asian markets inspire local funds to continue to take profit, traders say; expect shares to continue to fall tomorrow; tip support at 3530. "The selloff in most consumer- and select commodity-related stocks drove the main index lower despite healthy inflows," says fund manager at state-owned bank. Profit-taking hits food maker Indofood (INDF.JK) down 2.5% at IDR4,957, consumer goods producer Unilever (UNVR.JK) down 4.4% at IDR17,250. Bucking trend, gas, oil producer Medco (MEDC.JK) +15% at IDR4,225 on news Pertamina will buy a 27.9% stake in Medco. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0914 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia shares end down as investors take profits after recent highs as 2011 budget turns into "non-event" with no major positive surprises; KLCI down 0.6% at 1,480.70; "From the market's standpoint, Budget 2011 is again a non-event," AmResearch says; but adds upside remains as liquidity may continue to flow into emerging markets as additional monetary easing by central banks of developed markets may continue. 0907 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/INR extends gains mirroring EUR's retreat vs greenback while demand from oil importers also supports, dealers say. Pair at 44.37, off low of 44.17 intra-session, 44.12 late Friday. Trader with state-run bank says, pair driven higher as some participants covering short dollar positions despite USD inflows directed at Coal India Ltd.'s up to $3.5 billion share sale, which opened for subscription Monday. Trader tips 44.40 as key resistance for pair. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0858 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/TWD up late at 30.885 vs 30.793 Friday supported by steep drop in local stock market today, Taiex ends off 1.8% at 8060.54. "Regional weakness (in stock markets) and foreign investors selling Taiwan shares today led to a temporary halt in the Taiwan dollar's appreciation," says local trader. 0855 GMT [Dow Jones] GBP/USD has reached an extremely overextended position and risks are now on the downside says BNP Paribas. Fed chairman Bernanke's more cautious approach to QE on Friday triggered a USD correction and puts GBP/USD, which has been a main gainer on the prospects of more US liquidity, as most at risk of a correction. BNP also notes a deterioration in UK fundamentals which will likely lead to both the BOE and governments revising their growth forecasts lower. GBP/USD now trades at 1.5870 and the bank would use any uptick to 1.60 to short with a target of 1.55 and a protective stop around Friday's high of 1.6110. (gary.stride@dowjones.com)

0853 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/HUF climbs higher as markets receive details of Hungary's planned extraordinary tax package for the telecommunication, energy and retail sectors, but market participants expect further details to come later Monday. EUR/HUF is at 276.76 from 273.9 Friday. MKB Bank expects hectic trading during Prime Minister Viktor Orban's speech in parliament at 1100 GMT, adding the pair could rise to 279 if it breaks resistance at 276. Commerzbank says markets especially gauge any news in the speech on long-awaited structural reforms; sees the cross trading between 274.50-278.00. (veronika.gulyas@dowjones.com)

0841 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/CZK trades higher slightly at 24.529-24.549 from 24.51 late Friday as EUR rebounds from last week's losses, in part driven by the weakening of Czech stocks, a local trader says. The cross also follows similar moves on other currencies in the region, the trader says, adding that in all the EUR/CZK is likely to stay in its current range just around 24.500.(leos.rousek@dowjones.com)

0836 GMT [Dow Jones] India interbank call rate inches up by 60 bps Monday as banks scramble to cover cash positions in a week witnessing country's largest share sale plus 3 retail bond sales, says trader with state-run bank. Overnight call rate at 6.75% vs 6.15% Friday close, collateralized lending and borrowing obligation rate at 5.75% vs 6.00% at open. Trader says call rate may gradually move much higher this week as individuals may withdraw heavily to subscribe to share, debt sales. Notes, most lenders borrowed from interbank call market sparingly, instead meeting cash shortfall from RBI's discount window at fixed 6.00%. Banks borrowed INR894.55 billion from RBI Monday. Tips call rate in 6.50%-6.90% band rest of session. Coal India's IPO, which aims to raise up to $3.5 billion, opened for subscription Monday. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0835 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/PHP higher late Monday, tracking EUR retreat against USD. Pair at 43.23 from 43.17 late Friday. Pair likely to stay within 43.15-43.45 range Tuesday with upside risks as market likely to follow EUR movement. "The peso may retreat further as euro might sustain its reversal," says local bank trader. (rhea.sandique-carlos@dowjones.com)

0833 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia shelves painful fiscal reforms for now as government prepares for an election, says HSBC; election has to be called by 2013. "The fact that the new budget proudly includes a plan to construct a MYR5 billion 'Warisan Merdeka' tower--which would trump the already unnecessarily tall Petronas Twin Towers--speaks volumes about just how focused the government is on this front," says HSBC. Adds government target of cutting budget deficit to 2.8% of GDP in 2015 (from 5.6% this year) "would now appear ever more ambitious." Says subsidy cuts so far "largely symbolic" with 2011 subsidy bill at MYR23.7 billion, just over MYR1 billion less than 2010's expected costs; GST implementation postponed without new timeline. "The now-best case is that the government's gamble pays off: that the near-term dangling of carrots (plus postponement of sticks) may just deliver a strong mandate for tough reforms after the elections." (kwan-por.lee@dowjones.com) [ 10-18-10 0530ET ]

"Gold's lackluster performance on Friday may fuel more profit-taking as investors fear that the gold rally may take a breather after the recent meteoric rise in prices," says Phillip Futures. October open interest little changed at 112,944 lots. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

Adds, central bank may step in to slow pair's rise later; as it was suspected of doing so recently. Tips pair in 30.700-30.800 band for day. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

Gainers outnumber losers at pre-open; those bid up at least 2% include Swire Pacific (0019.HK), Hang Lung Properties (0101.HK), Sinopec (0019.HK), Shenhua (1088.HK), China Coal (1898.HK); while HSBC (0005.HK) lone blue chip quoted more than 1% lower. HKEx (0388.HK) indicated flat at HK$180.00 pre-market, while stock very overbought after 47.7% surge since September, any pullback unlikely significant given robust HK market volume. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0141 GMT [Dow Jones] KLCI little changed at 1490.40, supported by gains in plantation stocks. Broader market mixed, with advancers, decliners evenly matched. 2011 budget unveiled by PM Najib Friday failing to make any impression among investors. "Broadly speaking, we see little instantaneous impact from Budget 2011 on our domestic stock exchange as the government's master plan to overhaul the Malaysian economy...may only begin to bear fruit in the medium to longer term," HwangDBS Vickers Research says; pegs immediate resistance at 1495, support at 1465. Among gainers, plantation stocks extend gains amid strong palm oil prices, with Batu Kawan (1899.KU) +7.2% at MYR15.80, Genting Plantations (2291.KU) +0.4% at MYR8.40; among decliners, PLUS (5052.KU) down 0.9% at MYR4.42 as some analysts deem UEM, EPF's MYR23 billion takeover offer unattractive. (benjamin.low@dowjones.com)

0140 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares likely higher, expected to test 1000 as fund inflows continue. If benchmark index rises above that psychological level, it may even extend gains to 1020 technical resistance, says Globlex Securities' Head of Equity Investment Strategy Chakkrit Charoenmethachai. "As the dollar remains bearish, it's likely that the fund relocation to the Asian markets would continue," he says. Expects energy, financial plays to lead advance, though gains likely limited on profit-taking; investors think Bank of Thailand may hold its benchmark rate unchanged at 1.75% at Wednesday policy meeting. Support put at 987. SET Index ended +0.4% at 997.15 Friday. (piyarat.setthasiriphaiboon@dowjones.com)

0133 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore shares slightly higher; STI +0.3% at 3215.13, off 3197 early low, with gainers beating losers 1.7 to 1. Muted gains reflect caution ahead; "(STI) upside is probably limited after the good run we've seen and the market is starting to look a bit tired. The main question is 'did we do enough to warrant the spike above 3200?' I think that question will be answered during the earnings season," says analyst at local brokerage. GLP (MC0.SG) opens at S$2.16 on debut, +10% vs IPO price of S$1.96, gains largely expected after offer 12X subscribed; stock tops volume list. SGX (S68.SG) down 0.8% at S$10.04 after 1QFY11 net profit falls 21% on-year, hurt by lower securities revenue; down 17.1% on-year. China New Town Development (DN4.SG) +5.8%, second most traded stock, on news dual listing in Hong Kong by way of introduction to commence trading October 22. STI resistance tipped at May 2008 peak of 3,267, support at 3,142 last week's low. 271.5 million shares traded so far. (matthew.allen@dowjones.com) [ 10-17-10 2211ET ]

(MER.PH), PLDT (TEL.PH) and Globe Telecom (GLO.PH) may be in investors' focus. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

Benchmark 10-year Treasury yield up 6.1 bps at 2.567% late Friday in New York. Rise came after stronger-than-expected retail sales, manufacturing outlook for New York region dented expectations for bold Fed move, despite earlier speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Bernanke Friday emphasizing readiness for more monetary easing. FOMC meets Nov. 2-3. Ueno says Treasury market "may not see a calm spot until after the early November FOMC meeting passes."(andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

Net foreign investment year-to-date estimated at $411 million, according to National Clearing Co. Adds, "upcoming financial results will also help boost interest in oil, fertilizer and gas companies. 0804 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia's subsidies to various sectors from gasoline to foods likely to rise 22.5% to MYR24.9 billion in 2010 from MYR20.3 billion year earlier, despite recent cuts in subsidies in fuel, sugar, the government says in economic report. "Total subsidy outlay is increasing and is unsustainable," it says, adding recent IMF study finds subsidies "not well-targeted." Of 2010 total, fuel subsidies likely +61.6% on year at MYR10.0 billion due to rising oil prices; assistance for education likely at MYR7.1 billion; other welfare assistance at MYR2.3 billion. Subsidies for interest rate differential, electricity likely MYR1.5 billion, paddy, rice, sugar and flour subsidies total MYR2.3 billion. Subsidies rank as second largest component in government's 2010 operating expenditure. (kwan-por.lee@dowjones.com)

title: UPDATE: Foreign Funds Pour Into Bank Indonesia Notes Despite Curbs
text:
(Adds background)

By I Made Sentana

Of Dow Jones Newswires

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Foreign investors last month raised their investment in notes issued by the Indonesian central bank, in another sign that funds are continuing to pour into the country despite measures aimed at curbing short-term capital inflows.

Like other countries in the region such as South Korea and Thailand, Indonesia has in recent months attracted a flood of foreign funds, pushing up the value of its currency to new highs against the dollar.

Foreigners owned IDR64.7 trillion ($7.25 billion) of central bank notes as of Sept. 30, up from IDR55.0 trillion as of Aug. 30, Bank Indonesia said Thursday.

This means around 26% of its outstanding money market securities was held by non-residents.

Foreign ownership of the securities peaked at IDR83 trillion in April before investors trimmed their holdings in the wake of renewed concerns over euro-zone debt problems to IDR36.4 trillion in May.

But foreign ownership has rebounded, despite the central bank in June introducing several measures to discourage short-term capital inflows, including the implementation of a minimal one-month holding period for the securities, and the introduction of paper with longer maturities.

This increase is part of a wider trend that has seen offshore investors similarly raising their holdings in the government's rupiah-denominated bonds to IDR186.76 trillion as of Tuesday from IDR182.26 trillion as of Sept. 30.

The influx of capital in search of higher yield has lifted the rupiah by around 5% against the dollar so far this year, to its highest level in 39 months.

The appreciation of its currency has made the country's exporters less competitive, a problem also faced by its regional peers, and traders said Bank Indonesia might have intervened in the market on occasions to support the greenback.

-By I Made Sentana; Dow Jones Newswires; 62-21 39831277; I-Made.Sentana@dowjones.com [ 07-10-10 0837GMT ]

"We do expect the unemployment rate to move below 5% - most likely before years end," says Westpac. "The current average monthly gain of 32,000 is comfortably above labor force growth." Aussie unemployment rate currently at 5.1%. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0121 GMT [Dow Jones] HSI likely to consolidate, as profit taking sets in after HK market up in 20 out of last 24 trading sessions, for cumulative gains of 11.4%. UOB KayHian's Steven Leung says blue chips overbought, with HSI's 14-day RSI at 77.76, "a level for consolidation." Still, expects more market upside after consolidation, house's year-end target kept at 26,500 for HSI, 15,500 for H-share index. Any pullback in resources stocks such as Cnooc (0883.HK), PetroChina (0857.HK), Shenhua (1088.HK) may be entry opportunities given strong sector momentum. HSI +1.1% at 22,880.41 yesterday, a new 2010 closing high; volume finally breaches HK$100 billion mark at HK$104.8 billion. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0111 GMT [Dow Jones] AUD/USD sharply higher as Aussie economy adds 49,500 jobs in September vs expected 20,000, with new post-float high likely soon, says Sean Callow, senior currency strategist with Westpac. After trading around 0.9765 just before jobs report, AUD/USD last at 0.9840, its highest level since reaching a post-float high of 0.9850 on July 15, 2008. "In this bounce, we took out 0.9790 and other interim resistance. Beyond this, you're mostly looking at round figures like 0.99 and parity. The only other level watch for resistance is 0.9870," says Callow. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0103 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/PHP tipped lower as other currencies advance vs USD on expectation of further easing measures by the Fed; pair may slide to immediate support of 43.30 after settling at 43.505 late yesterday, a new 28-month low; resistance seen at 43.75. Local bank trader says "only the central bank stands in the way of further peso gains." (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0101 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore government bonds likely higher, tracking overnight gains in U.S. Treasurys amid growing expectations Fed, other central banks will loosen monetary policy further. "The rally in U.S. and some European bonds is likely to push Singapore government bonds higher. The market is currently driven entirely by external factors," says trader at local bank, tips yields to fall 2-3 bps. Yesterday, 10-year government bond yield fell 3 bps to 1.96%, 2-year unchanged at 0.41%. (gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com) [ 10-06-10 2144ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Steady; 8,910-8,930 Range Tipped
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0126 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR steady at 8,920 despite broad USD weakness vs regional currencies, as players see chances of Bank Indonesia continued intervention increasing after IDR's recent sharp gains, dealers say; "But, the tone is still bearish on the dollar because foreigners may still need to buy the rupiah to settle their purchases of Indonesian stocks and bonds done Friday," dealer with foreign bank says. 8,910-8,930 range tipped. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0113 GMT [Dow Jones] Stock selection "makes all the difference" in September, will again be important in October, says local fund manager; notes HSI up 9% in September, which impressive, but even more impressive are Hutchison Whampoa (0013.HK), HKEx (0388.HK), SHK Properties (0016.HK) racking up 26%, 25%, 23% rises last month, vs China Life (2628.HK), Esprit (0330.HK) at other extreme, up 3% and down 3% respectively. Thinks gains will moderate in October, strategy is to buy "strong stocks" on pullback rather than betting on laggards to catch up. Tips HSI to open modestly higher today on Wall Street cues, although profit-taking likely to set in early part of week, if not today. HSI ends Thursday down 0.1% at 22,358.17. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0112 GMT [Dow Jones] 5-year JGB yield briefly falls to 0.240%, lowest level since June 2003, amid growing expectations that BOJ will loosen monetary policy early this week, says trader at Tokyo securities house; adds if speculation persists that central bank will do more to curb trend toward strong JPY, 5-year yield could extend declines, possibly to 0.200%. Adds demand for longer-term JGBs also rising amid persisting concerns that Japan's economy will likely remain sluggish for long time, making yield curve flatter. 5-year yield now at 0.245%, down 0.5 bps; 10-year down 1.5 bps at 0.940%, 20-year at 1.670%, down 2.5 bps. (tomoyuki.tachikawa@dowjones.com)

0109 GMT [Dow Jones] Profit-taking clips EUR's wings after ascent earlier in morning to multi-month highs vs USD, JPY, but EUR may avoid any serious tumbles this week as investors take comments from Chinese PM Wen over weekend as show of support for common currency, says Yuzo Sakai, manager of FX business promotion at Tokyo Forex & Ueda Harlow. In Greece on Saturday ahead of 2-day Asia-Europe Meeting summit starting today, Wen says China will "make a big effort" to stand behind euro zone, continue to support a stable EUR, and will keep buying Greek bonds. "With all the attention that's on Chinese policy, remarks like this can't help but give the euro some support." Adds EUR also likely to get support as recent rises in risk-sensitive commodities prod investors to turn to higher-yielding units such as common currency. EUR/USD last 1.3752, after earlier hitting 1.3809, highest since March 17, while EUR/JPY up to 114.98, highest since May 18. (andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0106 GMT [Dow Jones] Nymex crude likely to consolidate with risks skewed to upside after hitting 2-month high $81.87/bbl this morning, provided support at Friday's $79.70 low doesn't break, Dow Jones technical analysis shows. Daily continuation chart positive-biased as 5-day & 15-day moving averages still rising; meanwhile, MACD & stochastics bullish, but latter at overbought. Resistance at psychological $82.00, then at then $82.97 (Aug. 4 top); breach would expose upside to psychological round-numbered levels from $84 up to $87.00, then $87.15 (May 3 peak). Fall below $79.70 support would temper near-term positive outlook, opening way down $78.04 (previous cap set Sept. 13), then $77.55 (Thursday's low, near 200-day moving average), $76.69 (55-day moving average) and $75.52 (Sept. 27 low, matching 100-day moving average). November crude last down 4 cents at $81.54/bbl on Globex. (jerry.tan@dowjones.com)

0105 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB lower at 30.16-30.18 vs 30.20 late Friday in thin trade amid continued bearish view on greenback. Pair biased down with fund inflows likely to continue. Market expects BOT to step in to curb sharp THB rise. "(The central bank) may not be able to reverse the trend but the market is still hoping it will stem the pace of baht appreciation," says local dealer. Adds panic selling by exporters may ensue if pair slips too quickly early in week, sliding through key 30.00 support. Initial support pegged at 30.10; resistance at 30.22. (piyarat.setthasiriphaiboon@dowjones.com)

0105 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/PHP likely lower, tracking USD weakness vs regional currencies in early Asian trade; pair may slide to 43.75 after settling late Friday at 43.88; support tipped at 43.60, resistance at 44.00. Manila-based trader says if central bank refrains from buying, USD/PHP will likely hit new year-to-date low today. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0059 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares likely to rise a tad in 8200-8300 range after ending +0.1% at 8244.18 on Friday, boosted by foreign fund inflows on hopes local currency to continue rising, says KGI Securities trader Randy Chang. USD/TWD at 31.310 late Friday, off 2-year intraday low. Still, adds volume likely moderate today on lack of firm cues, with China markets shut for National Day holidays. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0055 GMT [Dow Jones] Kospi +0.5% at 1886.33 on Wall Street's gains Friday, with foreign investors extending buying-streak to 14 sessions. "Investor sentiment remains positive as foreign funds are flowing into emerging markets amid a weak U.S. dollar," says HI Investment & Securities' Kim Seung-han. Hopes of more Fed action to stimulate U.S. economy, strong China data, expectations of strong 3Q (local companies') earnings will continue to support market sentiment, analysts say; think Kospi may touch 1900 sometime this week. Recent KRW strength may hurt some exporters, but energy, airline stocks may get boost, analysts say. "Tech shares are under pressure due to foreign-exchange risk (strong KRW) but valuation-wise, it's a good timing to snatch those up," Kim adds. Banks, securities also up on brighter 3Q earnings outlook, recently active stock trades, respectively, analysts say. KB Financial (105560.SE) +1.7% at KRW50,800, Hana Financial (086790.SE) +2.1% at KRW36,000. SK Energy (096770.SE) +2.8% at KRW148,000, Korean Air Lines (003490.SE) +1.0% at KRW78,800, Asiana Airlines (020560.SE) +1.4% at KRW9,630. (jung-ah.lee@dowjones.com)

0051 GMT [Dow Jones] ACCC Chairman Graeme Samuel says competition sensitivity is high in Australian finance sector due to the global financial crisis. "That is an area of constant focus for us in terms of examining potential mergers on a very vigorous basis, and is made even more difficult by not knowing exactly what we are going to see over the next year or two years," he tells the Wall Street Journal. Uncertainties include whether non-bank financial institutions re-enter market with vigor of 2007, and whether foreign banks return despite more stringent capital requirements. ACCC recently blocked National Australia Bank's (NAB.AU) bid for AXA Asia Pacific (AXA.AU), after copping criticism for allowing takeover of BankWest by Commonwealth Bank (CBA.AU), St. George Bank (SGB.AU) by Westpac (WBC.AU) during crisis. But Samuel says that criticism misses the point; increased dominance of mortgage market by big four banks is due to drying up of securitization market that funded smaller, non-bank competitors. "I don't think there is anything that a competition regulator can do to change that or that any government can do. We have got to let this shock of the GFC get out of the system," he says. See "Regulator Weighs Australia's Future" (rebecca.thurlow@dowjones.com)

0044 GMT [Dow Jones]EUR/USD, EUR/JPY down as short-term investors in Asia take profits, says senior FX dealer at major brokerage in Japan. EUR/USD earlier hit 1.3809, highest level since March 17, while EUR/JPY rose to 114.98, highest since May 18. "Those rises put the euro at an attractive level for profit-taking, which should put the brakes on further gains for the rest of today." Says EUR/USD could fall to 1.3710 vs last at 1.3755, EUR/JPY to 114.20 vs last 114.66. (andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0038 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei down 0.2% at 9385.02, after opening in positive territory, as investors stay sidelined ahead of BOJ policy board meeting (Monday-Tuesday). Investors widely anticipate additional monetary easing measures to be announced; today's Nikkei range seen at 9350-9500, analysts say. "It's a chance for the BOJ to take steps before the U.S.," says Cosmo Securities equity strategist Toshikazu Horiuchi, referring to upcoming November FOMC meeting. "But market players are not quite sure about what, specifically, the BOJ can do when it comes to 'stepped-up' measures." 25/33 Topix subindexes lower; banks off 0.9%, consumer finance firms off 0.9%. Among heavyweight shares, Fast Retailing (9983.TO) off 1.1%. Inpex (1605.TO) up 2.2% at Y412,000 on crude gains. Mitsui Fudosan (8801.TO) up 2.1% at Y1,490 on continued BOJ easing hopes after sharp Friday gains. Shinsei Bank (8303.TO) up 3.4% at Y60 on Credit Suisse rating hike. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com) [ 10-03-10 2126ET ]
