title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Lower; 8,900-8,930 Tipped Friday
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

1020 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR falls to 39-month low as foreign funds continue to flow into local debt, stock markets, dealers say. Pair last at 8,920 vs 8,910 earlier, 8,935 late yesterday. "The pair is heavily biased down, and it could have hit 8,900 if the Bank Indonesia didn't intervene," dealer says. Adds, BI may have bought around $200 million to stem IDR's rise. 8,900-8,930 range tipped for Friday. "Near-term, KRW, PHP, IDR and THB may continue to perform well on capital inflows and external balances," says Standard Chartered.(andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

1020 GMT [Dow Jones] December bunds are down 0.05 at 131.76 and Nick Holt, a trader at Morgan Stanley cautions that momentum is showing signs of running out of steam. "If we cannot break back into the up-channel and close above 132.14, then a retrace will be on the horizon," he says. Support is at 131.53, 131.46, and 131.32. Resistance is at 132.00, 132.20, and 132.50. (neelabh.chaturvedi@dowjones.com)

1018 GMT [Dow Jones] The Irish government has repeated its reassurances to Anglo Irish senior bondholders Thursday, but BNP Paribas "can not help thinking that Anglo's senior debt should be subjected to a haircut too." Argues that the benefits to the sovereign ("by putting a stop to the money drain") would indirectly support Bank of Ireland and Allied Irish spreads, outweighing concerns that they too might be subject to a haircut at some stage. CDS written on Anglo Irish's senior debt were 25 bps tighter Thursday at 860 bps, while sub CDS were at 51 points upfront, 7 points higher, according to Markit. (mark.brown@dowjones.com)

1004 GMT [Dow Jones] Sensex +0.8% at 20,107.60 as investors cover short positions ahead of close of derivate expiry for September. "Volumes have picked up sharply in banks and metal shares. These are the real contributors to the benchmark index's rise," says local dealer; adds, "funds are continuing to look for good investments at lower levels and this is one main reason for the short covering." Among gainers, HDFC (500010.BY) +3.3% at INR729.30, ITC (500875.BY) +2.7% at INR178.40, State Bank of India (500112.BY) +2.0% at INR3,256, Sterlite Industries +3.2% at INR166.60. Sensex tipped in 19,800-20,200 range Friday. (raghavendra.upadhyaya@dowjones.com)

1002 GMT [Dow Jones] South Africa's PPI reading for August was a touch higher than consensus expectations, but with little pass-through into CPI this isn't likely to trigger meaningful reaction, says Standard Chartered's Razia Khan. He adds: "It is a small point in favor of rates staying on hold, but PPI was never going to be the make or break factor." Annual PPI was up 7.8% after a rise of 7.7% in July. (robb.stewart@dowjones.com)

0955 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares end +0.6% at fresh 14-year high of 975.30 as capital inflows continue to cheer market sentiment. Strong August economic indicators including private investment, private consumption released earlier today also lend support. Big cap energy plays lead gains. "The SET index is likely to go up further on the back of capital inflows, but its pace would be slowed as profit-taking may emerge while it is approaching the 1,000-mark level," says Capital Nomura Securities strategist Chai Jirasevenupraphund. Notes, Thai shares so far chalked up 22.3% from closing level at end-June. Resistance at 977-980 zone, support at 963-965. Among most active, PTT (PTT.TH) +1.4% at THB297, Banpu (BANPU.TH) +0.9% at THB716, Siam Commercial Bank (SCB.TH) off 0.5% at THB103.50, PTT Aromatics & Refining (PTTAR.TH) flat at THB27.50, PTT Exploration & Production (PTTEP.TH) +1.3% at THB154. (oranan.paweewun@dowjones.com)

0949 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan central bank likely to manage ample market liquidity until 1H 2011 via open market operations (eg. hiking rates on NCDs, CDs) rather than hiking policy interest rates, says JP Morgan economist Grace Ng. "The growing likelihood that the Fed will introduce further quantitative easing would increasingly raise concerns amongst EM policymakers, including the Taiwan central bank, about capital inflow and impact on domestic liquidity going ahead." Adds, Taiwan's 12.5-bp hike today highlights island's solid economic recovery, gradual upturn of CPI. (aries.poon@dowjones.com)

0949 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB drops to 30.37 vs 30.47 late yesterday, tracking general bearish USD tone. Persistent portfolio inflows into local stocks, bonds keep bolstering THB while release of strong August economic indicators also THB supportive. Pair off 30.365 session low, also fresh 13-year low, on suspected intervention by central bank, say two dealers. "Most players are after the baht as all factors are pointing toward a firmer baht. The central bank is believed to have bought several hundred million dollars, just like yesterday," says Bangkok-based dealer. Next support at 30.30 then 30.20, subject to broad USD trend over the weekend, resistance at 30.40. (phisanu.phromchanya@dowjones.com)

0945 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/CHF just made a fresh 30 month low of 0.9730 and Barclays Capital says there's more downside to come. The bank originally had a target of 0.9640, the 2008 low. However given the downside break of a 2-year contracting range and general USD weakness the bank says it cannot rule out a slide to 0.9325 in the 4Q. USD/CHF now at 0.9741. (gary.stride@dowjones.com)

0939 GMT [Dow Jones] The dollar is sinking fast across the board, and its pattern against the yen is no exception. Having dropped to yet another post-intervention low of Y83.16 in earlier European trading, it's still hovering at Y83.30. If the Bank of Japan doesn't step in again soon, in line with its policy of continued vigilance on the currency, it could get messy. "It's playing with fire," says Paul Mackel, an analyst at HSBC. If it doesn't come in soon, the market could pile in, he adds. (katie.martin@dowjones.com)

0937 GMT [Dow Jones] Bunds slip into the red as demand falls at ECB's 6-day refinancing operation. Banks borrowed EUR29.443 billion at the facility, after a take-up of EUR104 billion at the 3-month cash tender Wednesday. With banks repaying EUR225 billion Thursday, lower demand brings down the excess liquidity in the system, while easing concerns about the banking system somewhat. December bunds are down 0.10 at 131.71. (neelabh.chaturvedi@dowjones.com)

0935 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/CZK trades steady at 24.588-24.608 from 24.59 late Wednesday, remaining rangebound, shrugging of euro zone news of Moody's downgrade of Spain, as it had largely been expected, a trader says. "EUR/CZK is only slightly moving above and below 24.6, but if the various indicators from global markets today bring some momentum to markets, we could see EUR/CZK move lower because the koruna is just looking for an impulse to return to stronger levels," the trader adds. (sean.carney@dowjones.com) [ 09-30-10 0620ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: Indonesia Shares Up 0.3% Midday; Timah Leads
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0535 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares by midday +0.3% at 3055.011 in light volume, off earlier low of 3489.812, led by buying in select resources, automotive stocks on hopes for strong 3Q earnings, traders say; tip resistance at 3520. "I think the main index is set to close at another fresh record high in a generally cautious trend," says fund manager at state-owned pension fund. Among gainers: tin miner Timah (TINS.JK) +5.3% at IDR3,000, gold, nickel miner Antam (ANTM.JK) +3.3% at IDR2,350. Profit-taking hits toll road builder, operator Jasa Marga (JSMR.JK), down 3.0% at IDR3,200. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com)

0510 GMT [Dow Jones] Kospi turns lower, down 0.2% at 1862.91 as investors taking breather before 3Q earnings season; "foreigners are buying KRW220 billion worth of domestic stocks and it's keeping the main index from falling further," says Lee Kyoung-min at Woori Investment & Securities. Says if major companies come up with strong 3Q results next month, Kospi may get hefty boost to test 1900 level; 1855-1870 band tipped for today. Stocks helping to limit Kospi's fall include technology, shipbuilding, transport shares. Samsung Electronics (005930.SE) +0.7% at KRW777,000, Hynix Semiconductor (000660.SE) +1.1% at KRW22,100, Hyundai Mipo Dockyard (010620.SE) +1.9% at KRW188,500, Korean Air Lines (003490.SE) +1.8% at KRW77,400. Some shares falling after recent gains: Hyundai Engineering & Construction (000720.SE) down 2.5% at KRW71,800, SK Energy (096770.SE) off 2.3% at KRW148,500, LG Chem (051910.SE) down 1.7% at KRW327,000. (kyong-ae.choi@dowjones.com)

0502 GMT [Dow Jones] China likely to continue using targeted measures such as Wednesday's property curbs to rein in excesses in certain parts of the economy, rather than turning to broad-based tightening such as interest rate hikes; Wednesday's measures only the latest example of this strong policy preference. Consumer prices rose 3.5% in August, but mostly on one-off factors such as higher food prices, and economists almost universally expect inflation to ease in coming months. Inflation rates were also much higher during last round of interest rate hikes, over 6% in 2H 2007 and as high as 8.7% in February of 2008. See: =MONEY TALKS: China To Focus On Property, Not Broad Tightening. (aaron.back@dowjones.com)

0501 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei 225 December futures down 1.3% at 9440, extending morning losses on concerns about firmer yen (USD/JPY at 83.52 and EUR/JPY at 113.59). "In addition to the stronger yen, the decline in banking shares to fresh year-to-date lows is souring overall sentiment," says Hideki Horikawa, chief analyst at Himawari Securities. MUFG (8306.TO) down 4.0% at Y388 and SMFG (8316.TO) off 3.9% at Y2,432; both hit fresh 2010 lows on concerns over consumer lender affiliates and renewed European debt worries. Puts successive futures index near-term support levels at 9400, then 9200. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0447 GMT [Dow Jones] KLCI +0.2% at 1,464.08 midday in range-bound morning session as investors grope for leads from global markets amid dearth of local cues; index caught in tight 6 point range through morning session; Dealer says markets likely to continue to consolidate through rest of session; tips 1,460-1,467 range for rest of session. Immediate resistance at recent high of 1,479.59, with support at Friday low of 1,445.33. Market breadth negative with 348 decliners vs 253 advancers. Advancers led by property, construction stocks with Kimlun Corp. (5171.KU) +1.9% at MYR1.09 on MYR70 million contract win from Malaysian Resources (1651.KU), which +1.4% at MYR2.19; MMC Corp. (2194.KU) +2.0% at MYR3.00. Decliners led by Unisem (5005.KU) down 2.0% at MYR1.98, IOI Corp. (1961.KU) down 1.1% at MYR5.49. (ankur.relia@dowjones.com)

0442 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/JPY briefly falls below 83.50, lowest level since Sept. 15, when Japan's government intervened in foreign-exchange market, amid persistent speculation Fed likely to ease monetary policy further soon, says Yuzo Sakai, senior dealer at Tokyo Forex & Ueda Harlow; adds, selling by Japan's exporters also pushing pair lower. But notes "if the dollar extends falls against the yen, expectations could grow that the government will step into the currency market again to sell the yen, which could discourage investors from actively buying" JPY. Tips support at 83.20 for now; last 83.51 vs session high of 83.81. (tomoyuki.tachikawa@dowjones.com)

0441 GMT [Dow Jones] Action in Singapore stock market notably subdued as investors generally staying on sidelines after digesting solid gains from past weeks. STI +0.3% at 3095.66 midday, but +5.3% since start of September, with support at last week's 3069 low. "The index won't come off too much because everyone knows this year is a good year for the Singapore economy," says dealer at foreign brokerage; "we have had a good month in September. It's time to take a break, have a Kit Kat, as it's the end of the month." Overall market volume light at 894.4 million shares worth S$1.24 billion, with good mix of large, small, mid caps among most active, including Genting Singapore (G13.SG), off 1.1% at S$1.88, Innovalues (591.SG), flat at S$0.17, Genting Hong Kong (S21.SG), off 2.3% at US$0.43, Transcu Group (E15.SG), flat at S$0.125, SingTel (Z74.SG), off 1.0% at S$3.14. (frankie.ho@dowjones.com)

0441 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei down 1.1% at 9450.77 after hitting new intraday low of 9436.59 in afternoon session. "It's futures-led selling; it's not like new selling factors are hitting the cash market," says Japanese brokerage manager, adding Europeans appear to be selling on slightly weaker USD/JPY (now 83.53 vs 83.80 earlier); December Nikkei futures off 1.2% at 9450, in line with cash market. Adds, Nikkei may be supported at 9400. All 33 Topix subindexes in negative territory, with heavily-weighted banks down 3.1% as a group; MUFG (8306.TO) down 2.5% at Y390 on concerns about rising credit default swap levels for consumer lender affiliate Acom (8572.TO). Nintendo (7974.OK) continues fall, now off 9.5% at Y20,820 after slashing FY forecast. Tokyo Electric Power (9501.TO) stabilizing somewhat, off 2.4% at Y2,055 (vs midday close of Y2,031) after announcing details of massive equity capital increase plan. (ayai.tomisawa@dowjones.com)

0440 GMT [Dow Jones] HK market's resilience, with HSI ending midday only down 0.3% at 22,316.98, despite ICBC (1398.HK) stake cut by Goldman Sachs, China's further property tightening, should be taken as sign of market's underlying strength. Market volume strong at HK$46.97 billion at interval, doesn't appear index would slide more; week's lowest of 22,109 likely won't troubled. ICBC down 3.2% at HK$5.78, China Overseas Land (0688.HK) tumbles 3.7% to HK$16.20, China Resources Land (1109.HK) off 4.5% at HK$15.76, but weakness in part offset by rally in Hutchison (0013.HK), big HK developers Cheung Kong (0001.HK), SHK Properties (0016.HK). Overall, given HSI's about 9% gain in September, "we believe the market will enter a period of consolidation over the next few trading sessions," says Celestial Securities. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0429 GMT [Dow Jones] PREVIEW: Hong Kong August retail sales growth likely remained in double digits, but likely slowed vs July on fading base factor. By value, tipped +16.0% on-year in August vs July's +18.9%; by volume +13.2% in August vs July's +16.0%, according to Dow Jones poll of 5 economists. "Domestic demand remains buoyant with the fall in the jobless rate and tourist arrivals continue to be resilient, but the higher base of comparison last year also weighs on the headline figure," Core Pacific-Yamaichi analyst Keith Lo says. Bank of East Asia economist Paul Tang says retail sales growth likely fell to "high single digits" in 4Q due to higher base of comparison, as city's retail sales returned to growth since September last year. Data due 0830 GMT Monday. (chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0424 GMT [Dow Jones] While central banks of South Korea, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia were suspected of intervening in FX markets overnight, following confirmed moves by Japan earlier this month, don't expect Reserve Bank of Australia to do any such thing, say traders and strategists. With surging mining sector, robust banking system, inflation a very real concern, RBA is looking to cool the economy any way it can, with gains in AUD helping central bank. "If the Aussie dollar wasn't as high as it is, we could see more than one rate hike by the end of the year as it's doing some heavy lifting for the RBA. A high Aussie dollar curbs importers and inflation, creating a dampening affect that is exactly what the RBA wants," says JPMorgan Economist Helen Kevans. AUD/USD last at 0.9670 after hitting 26-month high around 0.9730 overnight. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0423 GMT [Dow Jones] Vietnam shares end +0.3% at 454.52, with buying led by foreigners on 3Q earnings hopes, also ahead of key government meeting later this week, though concerns on high interest rates remain. title: Asian Central Banks Keep Up  Intervention  As Dollar Weakens
text:
SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--The central banks of South Korea, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia were suspected of intervening in forex exchange markets Wednesday to contain gains in their currencies, but analysts say the continued weakness of the U.S. dollar means Asian units should extend their rallies.

The wave of intervention, which has continued across the region for most of this year, hasn't been strong enough to reverse the strengthening trend in Asian currencies, as many policymakers are allowing their currencies to rise slowly to limit imported inflation.

That stance was reinforced after China, the top trading partner for key Asian countries, said in June it would let the yuan strengthen against the dollar -- meaning that other Asian countries can maintain their export competitiveness against China even if their currencies rise a bit.

On Wednesday the Thai baht and the Malaysian ringgit hit their highest levels since the 1997 Asian currency crisis, while the Singapore dollar rose to an all-time high.

In a note to investors, Standard Chartered analysts said global dollar weakness, closely tied to market expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve may launch another round of quantitative easing by boosting purchases of U.S. securities, is likely to keep Asian and other emerging market currencies in strong demand. In recent days, the central banks of countries ranging from Russia to Colombia have been suspected of intervening in forex markets because of dollar weakness.

"The prospect of another round of quantitative easing by the Fed in the fourth quarter of 2010 should be seen as broadly negative for the dollar," StanChart said.

Intervention Wednesday was particularly significant in Indonesia, which has attracted a surge of inflows thanks to its solid economic performance and high interest rates.

Jakarta-based traders said the central bank was suspected of buying around $50 million at IDR8,950 in early trade, and then an unspecified amount at IDR8,945. Neither move managed to send the rupiah lower, however, and the dollar last traded at IDR8,935.

"The dollar is still under pressure against the rupiah, as investors' appetite for riskier assets is improving," one dealer in Singapore said.

Intervention by Bank Indonesia has continued for the past two years, but is now likely at its highest volume ever. Bank Indonesia's forex reserves rose 9% in the first three weeks of September, a huge amount even by East Asian standards, mostly due to dollar-buying in forex markets.

The Bank of Thailand and Monetary Authority of Singapore also were suspected of early intervention moves Wednesday. In Bangkok, traders said the BOT was spotted intervening at THB30.50 against the dollar, but the baht rose further and last traded at THB30.46.

In Singapore, the MAS managed to weaken the local dollar slightly after it soared to an all-time high at S$1.3152 against the greenback. The Singapore dollar last traded at S$1.3170.

Seoul traders said intervention by the Bank of Korea was relatively mild, as the Korean won is still some distance away from two-year highs hit earlier this year. The dollar last traded at KRW1,141, having fallen as low as KRW1,139 earlier in the day.

17 Sep 2010 06:41 EDT DJ  Bank Indonesia Official: BOJ Intervention Good For Indonesia Budget

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Bank of Japan's move to weaken the yen is good for the Indonesian budget, Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono said Friday.

"Intervention by Bank of Japan recently is good for Indonesian budget as we have quite a large amount of yen-denominated debt," Sarwono said without elaborating.

The central bank said its currency policy isn't to intervene "at all costs" but only to smooth out volatility.

Sarwono added the central bank will combine instruments to curb inflation and not depend solely on adjusting interest rates.

"A rate hike will further attract capital inflows and add more liquidity into the market," Sarwono said.

Bank Indonesia Governor Darmin Nasution said a rate hike will be counterproductive for the current economy, a further sign that the central bank prefers to keep the rate unchanged as long as possible.

title: UPDATE: Bank  Indonesia  Sees Benefit From Yen  Intervention
text:
(Adds comments, background)


 
   I-Made Sentana and Andreas Ismar 
   of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia will benefit from the Japanese central bank's move to weaken the yen as it makes the country's yen-denominated debt more manageable, Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono said Friday.

Sarwono said Indonesia has "quite a large amount of yen-denominated debt," in a meeting with reporters that was also attended by the central bank governor.

Data from the finance ministry show Indonesia had Y2.68 trillion in yen-denominated debt as of April 30--about 16% of the country's total debt. The country had 22% of debt denominated in the dollar.

Bank Indonesia Governor Darmin Nasution suggested that Indonesia won't follow in the footsteps of its Japanese counterpart, saying Bank Indonesia will only act to smooth out volatility in its currency rather than intervening aggressively to curb the rupiah's gains.

The Indonesian rupiah has climbed nearly 5% against the dollar so far this year, making the country's exports more expensive for overseas markets. But the central bank played down the impact on the export sector.

"At the moment, the rupiah isn't the only currency (in the region) which is strengthening against the dollar. (Thailand's) baht and (Malaysian) ringgit have gained even more, so let's not say that Indonesian exports are no longer competitive," said Nasution.

Policy Combination To Curb Inflation

Sarwono also explained why, despite mounting inflation, the central bank kept its policy interest rate unchanged at 6.50% earlier this month, a level it has been since August 2009.

Consumer prices rose 6.44% from a year earlier in August, the fastest in 16 months, leading the central bank to acknowledge earlier this week that its full-year inflation target of 6.0% would be "hard to achieve."

"A rate hike will further attract capital inflows and add more liquidity into the market," said Sarwono, adding that the authorities will not depend solely on adjusting interest rates to tame inflation.

Investors have been flocking to Indonesian stocks and bonds, attracted by the country's political stability and strong economic growth. But some of those foreign funds flow out whenever global markets get jittery, pressuring the local currency.

In a bid to minimize the damage that could arise from such sudden reversal of fund flows, the central bank issued a set of policies in June, including a month-long holding period for Bank Indonesia certificates and the introduction of longer maturities for these securities.

"That's why we haven't raised the rate but instead issued new policy on primary reserves requirement," he added.

Earlier this month, the central bank said commercial banks must, from Nov. 1, increase their primary reserves at the central bank to 8% of their third-party-funds from the current 5%. Bank Indonesia said the move will likely absorb IDR50 trillion of excess liquidity from the market.

Nasution also said that a rate hike will be counterproductive for the economy, cementing the view that the central bank will keep its policy rate unchanged for as long as it can.

"I think their move on the reserves requirement is quite aggressive in terms of curbing liquidity," OCBC economist Gundy Cahyadi said.

"At the moment we still maintain our forecast for the BI rate to be raised by 50 basis point this year, but their latest move certainly opens up possibilities that they may not need to raise the rate this year," Cahyadi added.


 
   -By I-Made Sentana and Andreas Ismar, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 39831277;andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com

title: FX  ASIA: Japan  Intervention  Could Prompt Copycats Around Asia
text:
SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--A Japanese intervention in forex currency markets might well fail to weaken the yen, but should have a near-term impact on other Asian currencies.

Japanese authorities have ratcheted up their rhetoric against a strong yen as the currency rises steadily, hitting a 15-year high against the dollar Tuesday.

Some analysts say Japanese intervention would embolden other Asian central banks, many of which have intervened heavily so far this year, to increase their own dollar purchases to protect their exporters. Likely candidates for a quick correction under that scenario would be the Taiwan dollar, Korean won and Singapore dollar, all currencies closely watched by their central banks.

Asian central banks "would be more likely to intervene" after a potential Japanese move, as it "would make them more comfortable with intervention," said Sean Callow, a forex strategist with Westpac. "All Asian central banks keep an eye on what the others are doing; they haven't been shy about intervening."

Japanese intervention might become likelier if Ichiro Ozawa, a kingmaker in the ruling Democratic Party of Japan, wins an internal party election Tuesday to replace Naoto Kan as party leader and prime minister. Ozawa has espoused a more activist line to curb the yen and protect Japanese exporters.

That could become a matter of concern for Japan's competitors, including South Korea and Taiwan, which have taken market share from Japanese exporters in fields such as automobiles and electronics.

Over the past two years, as the yen rose 19% against the U.S. dollar, the Korean won has lost 5% against the greenback and the Taiwan dollar has been flat. That has helped those economies -- which grew more than 7% on-year in the second quarter, compared with 1.5% growth in Japan -- to recover faster from the global slowdown.

Westpac's Callow said China's response to any Japanese intervention also would be key, as the Chinese yuan has become an increasingly relevant benchmark for Asian currencies. With Japan hectoring China to intervene less to weaken the yuan, China could react to Japanese intervention by slowing or even reversing the pace of yuan appreciation.

Singapore, where the local dollar rose to an all-time high against the greenback earlier this week, is another candidate to mirror any Japanese intervention. A person familiar with the Monetary Authority of Singapore's thinking said the central bank would be more likely to step in if Tokyo does.

On the other hand, Indonesia could find it hard to increase its intervention. As of last month Bank Indonesia's forex reserves stood at $81.3 billion, up 36% on the year -- among the world's largest gains -- as a result of sustained dollar purchasing in forex markets.

Bank Indonesia has expressed reservations about the quick buildup and announced several measures to increase monitoring of investment inflows in recent months, looking to find other ways to lessen pressure on the rupiah.

That's because Indonesia's high policy rates, now at 6.5%, make it more expensive to keep dollar reserves there than in other countries, as commercial banks must be paid interest in local currency in exchange for keeping dollars with the central bank.

(David Roman, a regional forex reporter, has been a Dow Jones correspondent since 2002, covering economic and corporate news. He can be reached at 65 6415 4045 or by e-mail: david.roman@dowjones.com)

0958 GMT [Dow Jones] Dealers betting Malaysian government may soon lift ban on offshore trading of MYR may be in for disappointment; participants have been speculating Bank Negara may do away with ban after bank last week further liberalized FX rules; but relaxation is administrative in nature, modest step to help companies reduce their exposure to currency fluctuations and lower currency conversion costs. Bank may also want to assess impact of latest rule changes on market before moving towards full currency convertibility, which existed before 1998. If history is any guide, markets shouldn't expect further relaxation of currency trading rules for a few more years. See: =MONEY TALKS: Malaysia Not Ready To Let Ringgit Trade Offshore. (elffie.chew@dowjones.com)

0957 GMT [Dow Jones] Most Thai government bonds down on profit-taking by some foreign banks after recent steep gains. However, offshore players continue to seek medium and long-term notes, limiting downside for day. Foreign investors parked funds in bonds after they piled up THB positions, pushing THB to fresh 28-month high. "Despite profit-taking by some players, persistent capital inflows will continue to keep bonds well-bid and this likely to prevent any sudden yield reversal," says bond trader. Yields expected to move in tight range tomorrow. Bid/offer yields of issue due December 2015 quoted at 2.70%/2.67% vs 2.70%/2.65% late yesterday, November 2016 at 2.77%/2.72% vs 2.73%/2.70%, June 2019 at 2.82%/2.75% vs 2.79%/2.75%. (phisanu.phromchanya@dowjones.com)

0957 GMT [Dow Jones] The spread between Irish and German bond yields remains stable after the Irish government debt agency, NTMA, sold EUR200 million worth of six month T-bills and EUR400 million eight-month T-bills at average yields of 1.978% and 2.348%, respectively. Coverage is 10.1 times in the six-month maturity and 4.1 times in the eight-month maturity. (nick.andrews@dowjones.com)

0955 GMT [Dow Jones] Pakistan shares up on gains in refinery, cement stocks with benchmark KSE-100 index +0.4% at 9589.37. "Cement stocks are in the limelight on expectations that the government will soon start constructing homes, bridges, roads and highways in flood-hit areas, which will boost demand," says local dealer. Says market sentiment aided by foreign investments as data show offshore fund houses invested $1.1 million in equities Wednesday. "There is a likelihood that the IMF (in response to floods) could relax conditions tied to the release of loan installment of $1.56 billion to Pakistan, out of the total aid package of $11.2 billion approved in November 2008," adds local analyst. National Refinery (NRL.KA) +3.9% at PKR192, Attock Cement (ACPL.KA) +1.3% at PKR65.85. (djn.in@dowjones.com)

Tips pair in 32.000-32.100 band for day. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

Orient Securities Futures analyst Ying Haoliang says chart-based factors also lift metals prices after recent declines; adds metals may stage technical rebound over next few sessions, tips Shanghai copper's nearby resistance at CNY58,000/ton. Benchmark December copper last up 1.2% at CNY57,290/ton, benchmark December zinc last up 1.7% at CNY16,945/ton. (yue.li@dowjones.com)

0134 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW off 1,201 high, fails to convincingly break past psychologically key 1,200 mark, amid Kospi's 0.3% gain. Traders note, KRW closely tracking Kospi moves, which continues to lurch in, out of positive territory. Pair at 1,197.5 vs 1,196.0 late yesterday in Seoul. "The pair tried a couple of times earlier to take out the 1,200 mark, but didn't work. And it doesn't look easy," says local bank trader. Adds, if pair succeeds in breaching 1,200 in spite of exporters waiting near there to sell heavily, could exacerbate pair's rise. Another local bank trader tips 1,195-1,205 range rest of day. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0129 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares tipped higher as market awaits 2Q GDP data and likely central bank move to keep rates at low levels; benchmark PSEi may rise to 3570 immediate resistance after last ending 0.7% higher at 3554.14, with support pegged at 3540. "We still see net foreign buying and that would provide support to the market," says Grace Cerdenia, operations head at 2TradeAsia.com; adds "the BSP will most likely retain low interest rates." Property, banking stocks likely to lead market advance after shedding some gains in recent days. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0122 GMT [Dow Jones] Any rebound in HSI, after 4-session 2.1% losing streak, unlikely major, sustainable, as market in short term likely still in correction phase, says KGI Asia's Ben Kwong; tips correction, after HSI peaked at 21,805 on August 8, could last a month, although downside from here may not be too much; adds possible HSI will dip below 20,000 briefly but if that happens, would attract medium-term investors. China Life (2628.HK) set to fall on tepid 1H business performance; more blue-chip results eyed with Henderson Land (0012.HK), China Resources (0291.HK), PetroChina (0857.HK), ICBC (1398.HK), Bank of China (3988.HK), BOC HK (2388.HK) expected today. HSI ends down 0.1% at 20,634.98 yesterday. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0122 GMT [Dow Jones] Korea treasury bonds, bond futures a touch lower in early trade in mild downward correction following recent sharp gains. Analysts, however, don't anticipate big losses as demand for treasuries likely to remain solid amid on-going jitters over global economic recovery, especially after downbeat U.S. new home sales, durable goods data. "Despite the hefty foreign selling in futures yesterday of more than 9,000 contracts in net, bonds held up fairly well, which shows the overall demand for bonds remains solid," says Daishin Securities analyst Jeong Im-bo. Foreign investors' moves will remain key for market, but overall appetite for bonds likely to be kept solid. 3-year yield quoted +1 bp at 3.58%, 5-year yield +2 bps at 4.13%, September futures down 4 ticks at 112.06. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com)

0119 GMT [Dow Jones] Emergence of Chinese-led consortium weighing possible counteroffer to BHP Billiton's (BHP.AU) takeover bid for Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan (POT) has drawn attention to most important agricultural input you've never heard of--potash, key fertilizer ingredient. Canada and Belarus, two biggest producers, have set up cartel-like arrangements to keep prices buoyant, a major irritation for China. For China, food security concerns make potash national level issue as country doesn't produce enough. China's major source of potassium chloride, type of potash, at Chaerhan Salt Lake in Qinghai, one of its most remote provinces. Lake is production base of Qinghai Salt Lake Potash (000792.SZ), in which a Sinofert Holdings (0297.HK) unit held 18.49% stake at end-2009. According to 2009 annual report, QSLP is China's biggest potassium chloride producer with 25% market share; says two-thirds of China's 2009 demand met by imports. Government's efforts to support agricultural sector likely to result in ever-increasing fertilizer demand in coming years. Good for QSLP, but big headache for Beijing's leadership. See: =WSJ BLOG/China Real Time Report: China's Big Potash Appetite (dinny.mcmahon@wsj.com)

0107 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei cuts early gains, narrowly off at 8843.07, on political uncertainty as Ichiro Ozawa, former secretary-general of ruling Democratic Party of Japan, expresses intention to run for Sept. 14 election to pick party president, who would likely become prime minister. "The political risk that Mr. Ozawa's participation will further delay government policies (to stem yen's rise) is weighing on the market," says Masayoshi Yano, senior market analyst at Meiwa Securities. Adds investors also frustrated that policies such as currency intervention and monetary easing unlikely to come out while BOJ Gov. Shirakawa visits U.S. until Aug. 30. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0101 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/JPY last 84.69 after rising to intraday high of 84.89, cap at 85.00 heavy due to selling by non-Japanese funds, says senior dealer at major bank in Tokyo. Says ahead of Fed Bernanke speech in annual Jackson Hole Economic Symposium tomorrow, "investors are reluctant to buy the dollar above the psychological level of Y85.00"; adds investors also see Japan exporters' offers above 85.00. Citibank Japan strategist Osamu Takashima tips strong USD/JPY technical resistance at 84.73, then 84.83, 84.90. (takashi.mochizuki@dowjones.com)

Says U.S. initial jobless claims will be the focus; data due 1230 GMT. Tips key support for AUD/USD is at 0.8780 and it will take a close below there to portend further falls this week. Adds, this recognizes the risk that a jump in expectations for full blow quantitative easing by the Fed could see a broad-based weakening in the USD, supporting AUD. AUD/USD now 0.8847. 0119 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR higher at 8,995 vs 8,975 late yesterday as risk aversion resurfaces, dealers say. No sign of Bank Indonesia intervention to slow pair's rise, but central bank expected to step into market if pair around 9,005. "Trading activity is quite healthy so far," dealer says. 8,980-9,010 range tipped for day. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0109 GMT [Dow Jones] Crude extends losses in electronic trading, after 2.8% drop overnight triggered by unexpected build in U.S. gasoline stockpiles. Upward revision of global oil demand outlook by IEA didn't prop up crude oil prices, as gloomy sentiment on economic recovery drove decline in tandem with equities. "It's true that the U.S. economy is not in a good shape. But it's not all bad either," says Mitsubishi Corporation Futures analyst Shuji Sugata; adds market tends to overemphasize negative factors when sentiment negative. September Nymex crude down 57 cents at $77.45/bbl on Globex. (mari.iwata@dowjones.com)

0104 GMT [Dow Jones] RBNZ likely to hike official cash rate just once more in 2010 before pausing due to weak economic recovery, says Deutsche Bank Chief Economist Darren Gibbs; "we think that developments over the past month have strengthened the case for slowing the rate of policy normalisation to the point where we now think that even one more 25 basis point hike on September 16 is a stretch." Adds locally, data flow has been discouraging relative to what has been expected; "the combination of local and offshore data has caused the market to reduce the probability of a 25 basis point hike at the September meeting to 56%, with only 28 basis points of tightening now priced for the remainder of the year." Says if RBNZ doesn't hike, unlikely to restart normalization cycle before end of year. (lucy.craymer@dowjones.com)

0103 GMT [Dow Jones] Potential negative for AUD/USD is that Aug. 21 election race coming into its final week next week is neck and neck and the balance of power could be held by a few independents, says Greg Gibbs, FX strategist RBS. Says has also been a negative race that offers little in way of a fresh vision or strong mandate. Adds, change of government to Liberal will involve several significant policy shifts, such as scrapping of mining tax, no plans for an emissions trading scheme, significant shift on broadband communication policy. Adds, while a mining tax scrapping may be viewed as potential positive for mining companies and boost for AUD, change of government creates significant uncertainty. Says a close election result with a few independents controlling the balance will create fear of policy inaction. AUD/USD now 0.8977. (james.glynn@dowjones.com)

0103 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/PHP likely higher as investors turn risk averse after sharp losses in U.S. stocks overnight, while EUR weakness expected to weigh on risk-sensitive Asian currencies. Pair may test 45.50 resistance, but if it breaks that level, 45.70 next stop vs 45.235 late Wednesday; support eyed at 45.00. "We're dealing with negative sentiment. The Dow was down over 200 points last night. We may see some banks continuing to cut short positions," says local bank trader; thinks central bank may sell (USD) late if pair rises sharply. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0059 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/TWD likely to extend gains after hitting 1-week high of 31.880 late yesterday, boosted by stronger global USD, says foreign bank trader. Tips 31.800-31.950 band. Says, investors turn risk averse as "the global economy may face obstacles on the road to recovery." Still, suggests pair capped by exporters selling above 31.950. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0058 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P/ASX 200 down 1.0% at 4409.8, hits 3-week low of 4388.0, although its outperforming Wall Street, where S&P 500 fell 2.8% on worse-than-expected U.S. trade data. Follows recent underperformance in S&P/ASX 200 as it reacted to disappointing China imports data. Telstra (TLS.AU) down 7.4% and James Hardie (JHX.AU) down 8.0% on weak earnings guidance, though resources heavyweight BHP (BHP.AU) down just 0.8% and major banks down only 0.9%-1.4%. "But the Australian share market already copped a fair whack after those disappointing import numbers out of China. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0058 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/USD rising as players in Asia cover short positions, pushing pair to 1.2877 from earlier low 1.2830. Move comes after pair marks lowest level since July 23 in early Asia trade at 1.2830. Says further short covering may push pair up to around 1.2900. (andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0053 GMT [Dow Jones] RBS FX strategist Greg Gibbs says it's interesting that in midst of a risk sell-off, USD/JPY hasn't been able to break decisively lower, despite only tepid interest from government to discuss intervention. Notes this suggests market already significantly long JPY, and short USD. Adds USD/JPY should remain relatively stable for now. Says recent economic reports in Japan have been weak, including industrial production, machinery orders; Nikkei has badly underperformed, while the Japanese economy remains highly geared to export-driven demand. As such, says fundamental case for buying JPY is as weak as it is for any of major currencies, if not weaker. Adds JPY outlook mixed and there's not a good risk reward trade there at present; positioning is long, risk appetite will probably see it firm, but it's vulnerable to intervention. USD/JPY now 85.10. (james.glynn@dowjones.com)

0051 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/CNY set to rise following USD's strong gains vs EUR, dollar index's 1.9% rise, largest single-day rise in 2010 overnight. Dollar-yuan central parity likely to be set above 6.7800 vs 6.7768 yesterday; on OTC USD/CNY tipped in 6.7720-6.7800 for session. "We expect the dollar-yuan's trading level won't be as high as the central parity rate, because some trading desks are holding long dollar positions and may want to square them." (joy.shaw@dowjones.com)

0047 GMT [Dow Jones] JGB "yields look likely to come under further downward pressure, perhaps somewhat detached from Japan's own fundamentals" amid U.S. Treasury yield curve bull-flattening rapidly, says Barclays Capital chief strategist Chotaro Morita. 10-year cash JGB yield last down 3.0 bps at 0.980%, lowest level hit since August 14, 2003. 5-, 20-year yields also lower at 0.300%, 1.575% respectively, both lowest since August 2003. Adds, however, pattern since late July that USD/JPY's fall hurting Japan stock prices and lifting JGBs "may not be that simple in the future." With only slight differences in policy target rates between BOJ and Fed, "no one knows how much exchange rates will be affected by differences in the scale of central bank quantitative easing," Morita says. (min-jeong.lee@dowjones.com) [ 08-11-10 2119ET ]

After that, though, economic realities will hit home and support for the U.K. currency will wane. (nick.hastings@dowjones.com)

0716 GMT [Dow Jones] Swedish CPI, excluding interest rate costs, is likely to continue to trend downwards going into '11, says SEB, and expects the figure to be mostly lower than the Riksbank's forecast. Expects the July number to decline 1.6% on the year "mainly due to large base effects from unusually small summer sales on clothes in '09." Notes the stronger krona is a downside risk, but recent signs of less downward pressure on international producer prices on consumer goods in combination with higher commodity prices on food indicate risks now are more balanced than earlier. Sweden's two year bond yield is 0.5 bps lower at 1.4%, while the 10-year bond yield also trades down 0.5 bps at 2.7%. (dominic.chopping@dowjones.com)

0714 GMT [Dow Jones] Switzerland's rate of unemployment in July is expected to have fallen to 3.6%, from 3.7% in June, according to the average forecast of four economists' forecasts compiled by DJN. They predict the rate dropped for a sixth consecutive month as the robust economic rebound, driven by rising exports and consumer demand, persuaded companies to hire more workers. The data are due Friday, Aug. 6 at 0545 GMT. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0712 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR still steady at 8,940 after Bank Indonesia, as expected, leaves policy rate unchanged at 6.50%. "Bank Indonesia's decision was well anticipated given its reluctance to start tightening in order to allow the economy to continue growing," dealer with foreign bank says; adds sentiment on IDR still positive, without suspected Bank Indonesia intervention, pair may have fallen to 8,930. 8,940-8,950 range now tipped rest of day. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0709 GMT [Dow Jones] Foreigners have long been enamored of Indian stocks, but typically not in mood for long-term relationship. That's changing, says Heard on the Street. One indication comes from declining use of participatory notes, which offer foreigners way to avoid registering with Indian authorities. Regulators have never been happy with this arrangement, in part because P-notes give anonymity, an opportunity for wealthy Indians to avoid taxes, encourage speculative capital flows. From SEBI's point of view, drop in use of P-notes is welcome; good news for India's markets is this hasn't discouraged inflows - a reflection of foreigners' growing confidence in New Delhi's intent to further liberalize economy. True, heavy investment by foreigners is always risky, registering as FII doesn't mean global funds won't rush to exit if spooked; but rush could prove less hasty if more foreigners are thinking long-term; win-win here is that market will become more liquid, more efficient; in this fast-changing economy, that's a development worth appreciating. See: "=HEARD ON THE STREET: A Less Fleeting Engagement With India." (harsh.joshi@dowjones.com)

0705 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia keeps policy rate unchanged at 6.50% as expected, blames high inflation in July on seasonal factor. Though statement tone slightly hawkish, it offers little clue when bank likely to start rate hikes, analysts say. "We predict the rate hikes to start in the fourth quarter, with 25 basis points in November and another 25 basis points in December," says Bank Danamon economist Anton Gunawan; previously he expected rate hike to start in January. Meanwhile, OCBC economist Gundy Cahyadi notes BI statement that it wants to manage inflationary expectation going forward indicates "a rate hike should not be ruled out later in the year." 0709 GMT [Dow Jones] Foreigners have long been enamored of Indian stocks, but typically not in mood for long-term relationship. That's changing, says Heard on the Street. One indication comes from declining use of participatory notes, which offer foreigners way to avoid registering with Indian authorities. Regulators have never been happy with this arrangement, in part because P-notes give anonymity, an opportunity for wealthy Indians to avoid taxes, encourage speculative capital flows. From SEBI's point of view, drop in use of P-notes is welcome; good news for India's markets is this hasn't discouraged inflows - a reflection of foreigners' growing confidence in New Delhi's intent to further liberalize economy. True, heavy investment by foreigners is always risky, registering as FII doesn't mean global funds won't rush to exit if spooked; but rush could prove less hasty if more foreigners are thinking long-term; win-win here is that market will become more liquid, more efficient; in this fast-changing economy, that's a development worth appreciating. See: "=HEARD ON THE STREET: A Less Fleeting Engagement With India." (harsh.joshi@dowjones.com)

0705 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia keeps policy rate unchanged at 6.50% as expected, blames high inflation in July on seasonal factor. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0704 GMT [Dow Jones] China poised to accelerate expansion of crude oil, products storage capacity with major implications for oil demand. According to Xinhua News Agency, China's oil product storage capacity may reach close to 500 million barrels by 2015, nearly 50% above last year's level. That's significant as inventory buildup largely unrelated to GDP growth; tanks cannot be left idle due to maintenance costs. Recent oil pipeline explosion, heavy rains in NE China underscore need for greater stockpiling to cover any sudden supply disruptions. IEA members such as U.S. required to hold oil stocks equivalent to 90 days' worth of net imports; in contrast, China's end-June crude oil inventory wouldn't cover two months of net imports. "China cannot afford to allow its oil inventory to be stagnant. It must build oil inventory at a faster pace than demand if China wants to improve its consumption-day coverage," says Paul Ting, U.S.-based independent analyst specializing in China. title: INTERVIEW:  Indonesia Central Bank  To Continue 'Cautious  Intervention ' - Official
text:
(Adds comments from Sarwono on inflows, background)


 
   Andreas Ismar 
   Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank will continue "cautious intervention" to smooth exchange rate fluctuations amid recent strengthening of the local currency, its deputy governor said Thursday.

"We still see inflows to stocks and bonds, which help the rupiah's strengthening," Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono told Dow Jones Newswires.

The comments came after the U.S. dollar nearly fell through the psychologically important IDR9,000 mark Wednesday. The dollar was at IDR9,003 late Wednesday, with traders saying they did not detect any central bank intervention.

"We were quite surprised yesterday as BI did not enter the market, even when the pair came very close to 9,000. A day before, the central bank seemed to only intervene in small amounts. Its moves were not typical," a dealer at a foreign bank said.

Dealers suspect the central bank bought around $30 million Tuesday to curb the rupiah's appreciation. The amount, however, was marginal compared to the hundreds of millions of dollars Bank Indonesia used to trade in order to minimize large forex swings, dealers said.

The dollar stood at IDR9,007 at 0530 GMT. The rupiah has gained about 4.6% against the dollar so far this year.

Inflows Remain Healthy After Hot-Money Curbs

"Foreign flows are still entering the country in an orderly fashion, and (it) has started to shift from SBIs (short-term central bank certificates) to government bonds, as a result of recent policies, specifically the one-month holding period," Sarwono said.

Bank Indonesia last month issued a set of policies aimed at curbing hot money flows and smoothing volatility in the rupiah. The changes include requiring a one-month minimum holding period for SBIs and introducing SBIs with longer maturities of nine- and 12-months in addition to the existing one-, three-, and six-month SBIs.

Other asset classes in the country have rallied so far this year, with the Jakarta composite index reaching a record high at Wednesday's close and bond yields reaching record lows recently.

With improving sentiment toward high-yielding assets, the country's strong economic growth and prospects it will receive an upgrade from rating agencies, foreign flows are likely to continue entering Southeast Asia's biggest economy, analysts said.

Still, strong inflows could suddenly reverse, causing instability.

Sarwono said that Bank Indonesia will "continue to increase foreign exchange reserves to safeguard against reversals" of funds.

He added the central bank's forex reserves stood at $77.6 billion as of July 27, up from $76.3 billion at the end of June.

-By Andreas Ismar, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 39831277; andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com

(Joko Hariyanto contributed to this article) [ 29-07-10 0532GMT ]

title: =DJ  FX  ASIA: Asian  Currencies  To Gain Gradually As Yuan Peg Ends
text:
SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Asian currencies surged Monday as China's decision to drop the yuan's peg to the dollar revived expectations of a regional rally.

Central banks in South Korea, Indonesia and Thailand intervened to curb gains in their currencies, but strategists said Asia's authorities will likely tolerate a gradual appreciation after Beijing said Saturday it will let the yuan move more freely.

Gains in Asian currencies, as central banks tighten monetary policy, will likely be slow and in some cases fitful. Concerns about Europe's sovereign debt-crisis may continue to sap risk appetite, complicating the Asia rally.

The People's Bank of China drove home the message that it will allow only gradual moves in its currency, setting the yuan's central parity rate at 6.8275 to the dollar, the same as Friday's fixing--and a weaker yuan level than the dollar's over-the-counter close Friday at CNY6.8262.

This was the central bank's first operational evidence of its policy of allowing more flexibility in the yuan exchange rate. Beijing had essentially pegged the dollar around CNY6.8300 since July 2008 as an emergency measure to combat the global financial crisis.

"It seems they're trying to avoid being seen as very aggressive," said Frances Cheung, a currency strategist at Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank. She forecasts the yuan will rise 1.5% against the dollar by the end of the year.

Investors, after the surprise fixing Monday morning knocked Asian currencies back from early highs, nonetheless resumed buying yuan and other regional currencies. The dollar dropped to CNY6.8015, its lowest under China's modern exchange-rate system, before rebounding somewhat. At 0650 GMT it was quoted at CNY6.8090.

"At the beginning the market was trying out around the level of Friday's close, but it has since turned to focus on the prospect of yuan appreciation in the near term," said a Shanghai trader at a foreign bank. "Everyone is selling dollars now."

Other Asian authorities are looking to China for cues. As the region's biggest export market with a rapidly growing economy, China is hugely important for other countries in Asia, and each government will likely try to ensure its currency doesn't deviate too much from those of its rival exporters.

Spencer Lin, the head of the foreign-exchange department at Taiwan's central bank, said Taipei will pay attention to movements in Asian currencies after China's currency shift.

Bank Indonesia Deputy Gov. Hartadi Sarwono said, "The rupiah will adjust, as China's new policy will help trigger global economic recovery." Yet, the central bank later intervened to temper the rise in the rupiah, which had jumped to its highest level since May 10. The dollar was at IDR9,065 at 0705 GMT, off its early low of IDR9,030.

The Bank of Korea, warning against "one-sided" currency moves, bought an estimated $1 billion for won, boosting the greenback to KRW1,172 from KRW1,169, Seoul traders said. The dollar remained well below late Friday's KRW1,202.6.

The Bank of Thailand was suspected to have bought a few hundred million dollars to slow the rise in the baht, which is up 3.1% against the dollar year-to-date.

Asian currencies may remain under gentle upward pressure. Barclays Capital expects a roughly 5% yuan rise by the middle of 2011, forecasting the dollar will fall to around CNY6.5000.

Standard Chartered says one way to play a yuan rise is through the New Taiwan dollar, which should benefit from the yuan de-pegging, given cross-strait trade links. The bank recommends selling the U.S. currency via three-month nondeliverable forwards at an outright entry of TWD31.550, targeting a decline to TWD31.000.

"In our view, the Taiwan dollar is likely to catch up with other Asia ex-Japan currencies as the Taiwan central bank is likely to become more tolerant of gradual currency appreciation," the bank said.

ING Bank is most bullish on the won, Taiwan dollar, Singapore dollar and Malaysian ringgit, "based on cheapness on real effective exchange-rate grounds and our assessment of central banks' tolerance for currency appreciation," said economist Tim Condon.

-By Arran Scott, Dow Jones Newswires; +65-6415-4042; arran.scott@dowjones.com

(Shen Hong and Joy Shaw in Shanghai, Alex Pevzner in Taipei, Min-Jeong Lee in Seoul and Joko Hariyanto in Jakarta contributed to this article.)

title: EM ASIA  FX -Won, ringgit lead Asia gains; rupiah up on Moody's
text:
* Won up 2.6 pct vs dlr, biggest pct gain in 14 months

* Ringgit hits near 2-mth high

* Authorities seen intervening to check currency gains

By Cheon Jong-woo

SEOUL, June 21 (Reuters) - China's vow to allow more yuan flexibility boosted Asian currencies on Monday with the won appreciating the most in 14 months as the plan is seen bolstering demand in Asia's second-biggest economy and lifted risk appetite.

Indonesia's rupiah found further support after Moody's Investors Service raised the country's rating outlook.

Foreign exchange authorities in Asia were spotted intervening to check gains, but the currencies are expected to rise further, dealers and analysts said.

"Until we get risk off and the yuan flips above 6.83 again, Asian currencies will continue to rise," a currency dealer in Kuala Lumpur said.

Spot yuan strengthened to 6.8015 to the dollar, compared with Friday's close of 6.8262, even after the People's Bank of China set Monday's mid-point <CNY=SAEC> unchanged at 6.8275 before trading started.

On Saturday, China said it would gradually make the yuan's exchange rate more flexible, indicating it was ready to break a 23-month-old U.S. dollar peg that had come under intense fire.

The move eased tension with the West ahead of a summit of the Group of 20 countries this week, encouraging investors to snap up riskier assets.

(For more on China's currency, see [ID:nSGE65I02M])

WON

The South Korean won <KRW=> posted its biggest daily percentage gain against the dollar in nearly 14 months as China's vow to allow more yuan flexibility boosted risk appetite.

The won found further support from exporters' demand for settlements, which prompted investors to clear dollar-long positions to cut losses, although the foreign exchange authorities were spotted to curb its strength.

The currency ended local trade up 2.61 percent at 1,172.0 per dollar from Friday's domestic close <KRW=KFTC> of 1,202.6.

The percentage gain was the biggest since a 4.58 percent rise on April 30, 2009.

"Support from the yuan's news was stronger than expected. The authorities tried to curb the won's strength around the end of local trade, but the intervention was not strong enough," said a foreign bank dealer.

Seoul shares <.KS11> closed up 1.62 percent with foreign investors buying a net 293.0 billion won worth of stocks on the main exchange.

RINGGIT

The Malaysian ringgit added gains to hit a near two-month high, tracking its Asian peers after China's pledge over the weekend to allow more yuan flexibility.

The ringgit rose as much as 2.31 percent to 3.1780 per dollar, strongest since April 27.

"China's move boosts all Asian currencies. I think USD/MYR may head to this year's low of 3.17, maybe over a course of a week," says a dealer in Kuala Lumpur.

RUPIAH

The Indonesian rupiah <IDR=> rose as Moody's lifted the country's rating outlook to positive from stable, praising its stability and the effectiveness of its fiscal and monetary policies. [ID:nTOE65K03M]

The rupiah was up 0.91 percent to 9,005 per dollar.

The currency is expected to rise further on the brighter outlook for the economy, but market players remain cautious over intervention by the central bank to curb its strength.

"The Indonesian economy fundamentally is in good shape," said a foreign bank dealer in Jakarta. "I want to check 9,000, the last strong support, when Bank Indonesia keeps intervening to protect rapid volatility movements. If it breaks through the level, definitely rupiah will go to 8,900."

BAHT

The Thai baht <THB=> tracked stronger Asian currencies, gaining more than a third of a percent to a near-six-week high of 32.28-30 per dollar after China's move.

"The baht's tone is strong but the Bank of Thailand is actively intervening to hold it at 32.30. If the baht cannot be stabilised at this level, it might firm to as far as 32.00 later," a trader in Bangkok said.

A second trader said dollar selling pressure in early trade came mostly from foreign investors while Thai exporters held back to assess the trend. Dollar/baht was bid at 32.26 against 32.38 late on Friday. The baht has gained 3.29 percent so far this year.

YUAN

Market players are keen to sell dollar/yuan NDFs even with the slight bounce from the lows after the PBOC kept the yuan's mid-point flat, prompting some short-covering in early trade, dealers in Hong Kong said.

Large selling interest was seen on any move up in NDFs <CNYNDFOR=>, with U.S. banks and hedge funds doing the bulk of the selling for now. Trading was concentrated on the one-month and the one-year tenors, but overall volume was not too large.

"Though the pace of the selling has declined sharply from last week, people are still expecting an eventual move on the yuan in the next 1-2 weeks," said a senior NDF trader at a broker in Hong Kong.

One-year NDFs traded at 6.6280. A head trader at a European bank in HK said there was good two-way flow around 6.63 in one-year NDFs and that players were looking for opportunities to sell both USD/CNY NDFs and USD/Asia pairs. CURRENCIES VS U.S. DOLLAR Change on the day at 0605

title: MARKET TALK:  Indonesia Intervention  Likely Ate  FX  Reserves May
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0617 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia says its FX reserves down to $75.6 billion as of May 31 from $78.58 billion April 30, without providing reasons; but analysts say a large chunk of drop may have been due to intervention amid capital outflows sparked by euro-zone debt problems; traders suspect central bank was in market frequently recently, as IDR under pressure, falling 1.7% vs USD in May; Bank Indonesia's acting governor Nasution said yesterday that outflows had abated.(i-made.sentana@dowjones)

0612 GMT [Dow Jones] HK short-selling volume down 24.9% at HK$1.766 billion midday, as percentage of market total drops to 6.1% vs 7.5% at Wednesday's half-day, suggesting bears deterred by HSI's 1.8% rebound following 3-day losing streak. China Mobile (0941.HK) leads with HK$104.11 million, then HSBC (0005.HK) with HK$88.69 million. Next come China Yurun Food (1068.HK) with HK$83.79 million, China Life (2628.HK) with HK$79.04 million, ICBC (1398.HK) with HK$62.48 million. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0608 GMT [Dow Jones] Bullish move in S&P 500 futures signaling traders to get out of bonds, especially in Australia, though one senior trader says it's still a market too much on edge to do anything but trade. "Things are OK on the economic front, but who knows how long that will last? The short-term moves are still so sharp, you can only make a day trade of it. We're not seeing a lot of true investors coming to the table right now." Trader says S&P 500 futures move above its 200-day moving average, acted as catalyst for Aussie bond price drop, with 3-year off 11 ticks at 95.16. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0607 GMT [Dow Jones] The increase in Swiss retail sales in April seems to signal the end of deflationary dangers in Switzerland, says UBS. "The growth gap between nominal and real retail sales has narrowed to virtually nothing, and as such the latest report seems to confirm the end of deflationary trends just now, as hinted by virtually every other Swiss price indicator," according to economist Reto Huenerwadel. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0603 GMT [Dow Jones] Bank Indonesia keeps policy rate unchanged at 6.5%, repeating its mantra that rate consistent with 2010 inflation target of between 4%-6% and efforts to help spur economic recovery. Indonesian markets on midday break but little impact likely as decision widely expected; all 14 economists polled by Dow Jones tipped Bank Indonesia to stand pat. Comments suggest it intends to keep rates unchanged in coming months; OCBC's economist Gundy Cahyadi still expects Bank Indonesia to hike rate to 7.25% by year-end as inflation likely to gain pace. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0545 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares +1.8% midday at 762.77, in tandem with healthy gains in most regional bourses. Volume heavy, suggesting buying interest strong though investors may start to take profit after recent strong rebound. "It's been a fairly good session this morning but I think this might be as far as it may rise today. Without any real catalyst in sight, I don't see the SET rising much from here in the near term," says Bualuang Securities strategist Pongrat Ratanatawanananda. Resistance pegged at 766, 50-day moving average, support at 757. Among most actives, Thanachart Capital (TCAP.TH) +5.0% at THB25, Indorama Ventures (IVL.TH) +2.3% at THB18.10, Banpu (BANPU.TH) +1.7% at THB592, Bangkok Bank (BBL.TH) +3.5% at THB118.50. (phisanu.phromchanya@dowjones.com)

0540 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan government bonds end sharply lower, tracking robust 2.3% gain in local stocks, prompting stop-loss selling by securities houses, says local brokerage trader. "We'll have to watch stocks on Monday as further gains will push yields higher," he says. Yield on reopened 10-year bond ends at 1.4173%, highest since it started when-issued trade, vs previous close at 1.3880%; tipped to test 1.43% resistance Monday. 5-year yield ends at nearly 2-month high of 1.0237% vs 0.9950%, tipped in 1.03%-1.05% band. (alex.pevzner@dowjones.com)

0539 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares end +2.3% at 7360.28 led by big rebound in electronic stocks, tracking gains in Asian bourses, strong Wall Street overnight, says Alex Huang, assistant VP at Mega Securities. Tips main index to consolidate in 7300-7450 band tomorrow, as investor confidence remains weak given sluggish trade. "Europe's fiscal troubles will continue to sideline investors in the near term," he says. Hon Hai Precision (2317.TW) settles +4.6% at NT$125.0 on comments from Apple Inc's (AAPL) CEO Steve Jobs firm isn't a "sweatshop." Chimei Innolux (3481.TW) in Hon Hai group +4.1% at NT$35.60. AU Optronics (2409.TW) +3.0% at NT$30.80, Siliconware Precision (2325.TW) +3.7% at NT$35.45, Acer (2353.TW) +5.2% at NT$79.10 on technical rebounds. (crystal.hsu@dowjones.com)

0537 GMT [Dow Jones] Rallying AUD/USD still has more room to go, says Philip Burke, FX Chief Dealer for JP Morgan in Sydney. "There seems to be some good model buying and a wide range of accounts buying Aussie today," says Burke. In rally, AUD/USD breaks to 0.8500, up from 0.8406 late yesterday, with strong US stock market helping morning gains, strong local data helping in afternoon. "It's a case of that doom and gloom slowly dissipating," says Burke, who sees resistance at 0.8550 and 0.8700, though he thinks first level won't hold. (geoffrey.rogow@dowjones.com)

0533 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P/ASX 200 up 2.4% at 4484, hits 2-week high of 4489.1, albeit on light trading volumes. Financials, materials and energy stocks leading broad-based gains, in line with U.S. and Asian markets. AUD/USD also firm, though S&P/ASX 200 leading the rally. "It appears participants are slowly placing greater emphasis on underlying economic and company fundamentals rather than all the current background noise," says IG Markets strategist Ben Potter. "Confidence has improved to the point where traders are happy to hold positions over the course of the day rather than booking quick profits." Focus turns to tonight's U.S. private sector jobs data, followed by Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls. Traders anxious to see if Wall Street can rise two days in a row, something it hasn't done for 23 trading sessions. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0532 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/JPY climbs to 113.66 vs its day's low of 112.70, as "long-term investors appear to be buying on the cheap on expectations for its further gains" amid stock market rise, says Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking Corp. senior trader Hideaki Inoue. Nikkei +3.2%. Adds, unit may extend gains to 114.00 later in day. "Players' sentiment points to more recovery," which may encourage Europe players to lift unit further later in day if global stock markets track Asia stocks. Attention to jobs data including today's ADP employment data, ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index. Adds, EUR/JPY may rise to psychological key 115.00 if closely-watched Friday's non-farm payrolls data come in higher-than-expected. (miho.nakauchi@dowjones.com)

0528 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares +2.1% midday at 2790.887 in moderate volume with telecommunication, bank blue chips leading gains on hopes for strong 1H earnings, traders say; tip resistance at 2810 vs 2801.203 intraday high. "Gains across Asian markets have inspired investors to buy back recently-battered shares," says trader at Lautandhana Securities; still, expects retail funds to take profit late. Among gainers, Bank Rakyat (BBRI.JK) +4.2% at IDR8,700, Bank Mandiri (BMRI.JK) +2.9% at IDR5,450, while heavyweight Telkom (TLKM.JK) +1.9% at IDR8,000. (edhi.pranasidhi@dowjones.com) [ 06-03-10 0217ET ]

text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0441 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR bounces, now trading at 9,250 from 9,225 intraday low, but still tad below 9,255 late yesterday as local participants buy pair in thin trade, dealers say. "There's no sign of Bank Indonesia intervention as dollar demand is not very strong," a dealer says; 9,220-9,280 still tipped as range for today.(i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0435 GMT [Dow Jones] PREVIEW: Bank Indonesia likely to keep overnight policy rate unchanged at 6.5% Thursday as inflation still benign, despite having picked up in May; all 14 economists polled by Dow Jones expect central bank to keep rate at same level since August to help spur economic growth. "We think Bank Indonesia's tone will remain neutral-to-dovish this Thursday as inflation remains in the low-end of its inflation target range of 4%-6% and uncertainties about euro-zone sovereign problems weigh on the global outlook," says Citigroup economist Johanna Chua; expects hiking to start in 1Q 2011; meanwhile some economists predict rate hike to start as early as in 3Q. ( I-Made.Sentana@dowjones.com)

0427 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/HKD extends gains as weaker local stocks prompt investors to shift funds into U.S. unit, says senior trader at U.S. bank. Tips pair's near-term support at 7.7920, resistance at 7.8000. HSI down 0.4%. "Still, a big rise of the pair isn't likely as the upcoming IPOs might attract inflows, capping the pair at 7.8000 in the near term," trader says. Notes Agricultural Bank of China (AGBC.YY) is expected to raise up to US$30 billion in its IPO in July. Pair last at 7.7944 vs 7.7933 this morning, up from 7.7917 yesterday.(chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0425 GMT [Dow Jones] LME metals seeing some long liquidation in Asia, with sentiment gloomy, at least in short term; 3-month nickel breaks down through $20,000 level for first time since Feb. 24, while copper off 1.2% at $6669/ton with 1,643 lots done, both contracts seeing heavy volume in past hour as EUR/USD testing 1.22 level again, now at 1.2198 vs 1.2263 intraday high. "The investor community is starting to reweight their positions on concerns over near-term Chinese demand and in the knowledge that growth in Europe is going to be anaemic. Consumers might be buying these dips though," says trader at U.S. bank. Tips initial support for nickel at $19,755, neckline of reverse head and shoulders that launched post-February rally; then $19,000. "Anything below $20,000 is in the buy zone for consumers as we are still seeing some good indications from the stainless steel sector," he says. LME nickel at $19,950/ton, down $550 with 233 lots traded. (james.campbell@dowjones.com)

0424 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares end higher, buoyed by bargain-hunting with positive domestic economic news supporting sentiment. Benchmark PSEi ends +0.7% at 3289.56 amid heavy trading. "Geopolitical and (global) financial concerns are still there but domestic investors are in-tuned to positioning themselves into the market," says DBP-Daiwa Securities research head Ron Rodrigo; notes wide expectations by economists that central bank likely to keep policy rates on hold at meeting Thursday also boosting interest in local equities. Says market may continue to advance Thursday even as investors eye overseas developments, next resistance 3300, support 3250. Banco De Oro Unibank (BDO.PH) ends +4.5% at PHP46.50; Ayala Land (ALI.PH) +3.7% at PHP14.00. Ayala Corp. (AC.PH), down 1.5% at PHP325.00; PLDT (TEL.PH) off 0.4% at PHP3,430 limit market advance. (rhea.sandique-carlos@dowjones.com)

0420 GMT [Dow Jones] Nikkei down 0.8% at 9638.49, lower vs (positive) morning close of 9747.54, as enthusiasm following PM Yukio Hatoyama's resignation fades; USD/JPY, EUR/JPY slightly down vs earlier when selling in JPY seen on concerns over increased political turbulence weighed on safe-haven appeal of JPY. "The foreign exchange market has a bigger impact on Japanese stocks," says Yumi Nishimura, senior market analyst at Daiwa Securities Capital Markets. Says Nikkei may trade between 9600-9750 in afternoon. 27/33 Topix subindexes lower; trading houses down on falling crude; Mitsui & Co (8031.TO) off 7.3% at Y1,179, hit by concerns about costs stemming from massive oil spill in Gulf of Mexico. Sony (6758.TO) off 2.3% at Y2,723. (ayai.tomisawa@dowjones.com)

0413 GMT [Dow Jones] India government bonds now mostly flat after weak opening as market anxious over likely RBI rate hike after comments from India PM Manmohan Singh that government will continue to take all steps necessary to ease price pressures. Benchmark 7.80% 2020 bond at 101.94 vs 101.98 last close, second-most traded 8.20% 2022 bond at 102.70 vs 102.82 last close. "The market is in a wait-and watch mode after comments from the Prime Minister and RBI Governor too yesterday that inflation is still higher than it should be," trader says. Tips benchmark 2020 bond in 101.70-102.10 range, 2022 bond in 102.60-102.90 range during session. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0413 GMT [Dow Jones] Japan political turmoil in wake of PM Hatoyama's resignation to continue weighing on JPY in coming weeks ahead of Upper House elections (likely July 11) as uncertainty prompts foreign investors, traders to sell yen, says Masafumi Yamamoto, chief foreign exchange strategist at Barclays Capital in Japan. "The uncertainty until the decision about the next prime minister and finance minister, and even after the new Cabinet is formed, the uncertainty about the election should be a negative for the yen." But says even if current finance minister Kan, seen as less tolerant of JPY strength, becomes next PM as many expect, does not necessarily mean major change in government currency policy. "Kan obviously prefers a weaker yen, but so far the Keidanren (Japan Business Federation) and other business lobbyists are not pushing strongly for government action against yen strength." Says whoever becomes next PM, finance minister, key possible triggers for government verbal, actual intervention would be sharper falls in country's share markets, with many watching Nikkei for any breach of 9,000, and more pressure from business community. On EUR/JPY, says euro zone's own political problems likely to temper any gains in cross; German President Kohler resigned Monday, increasing political concerns in key euro-zone member. (andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0410 GMT [Dow Jones] Vietnam shares end +0.4% at 510.74 after Prime Minister Nguyen Tan Dung yesterday told central bank to urge commercial banks to further lower rates to support economic growth. Dung said Vietnam sticking to GDP growth target of 6.5% for 2010. "Firms are expected to post better results for the second half of the year with banks lowering their interest rates," says trader. Notes foreign and long-term investors buying in blue chips. Volume low with 40.7 million shares valued at VND1.3 trillion traded. Among actives, Ocean Group JSC (OGC.VH) +0.3% at VND32,300, Saigon Thuong Tin Commercial Joint Stock Bank (STB.VH) down 0.9% at VND20,300, Saigon Securities (SSI.VH) down 0.8% at VND37,000. Tips index to stay around 510 for rest of week. (trong-khanh.vu@dowjones.com)

0409 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/TWD falls to 32.294 midday vs 32.418 yesterday, trading in tight 32.250-32.300 band in most of morning session as market lacks cues with Taiex choppy, Korea markets closed, says local bank trader. Volume moderate at US$496 million midday; "traders are cautious over recent global uncertainties" such as euro zone debt problems, he says. Tips pair in 32.250-32.310 band in afternoon. (mason.wu@dowjones.com)

0401 GMT [Dow Jones] Sensex +0.4% at 16,644.07, just off 16,678.09 early high, aided by some short-covering after a 2.2% sell-off yesterday; 22 of the 30 index issues up, with rise led by auto shares after strong May vehicle sales numbers. "The positive opening is on expected lines. There is some short-covering in sectors that were beaten down yesterday like metals and select infrastructure plays," says dealer at domestic fund house. Adds, Sensex could trade range bound for session, with upside capped at 16,700. News flow from Europe, China could provide direction later. Among auto plays, Mahindra & Mahindra (500520.BY) +2.0% at INR575.00, Maruti (532500.BY) +1.8% at INR1,283. Tata Motors (500570.BY) +1.3% at INR735. Among metal plays, Sterlite Industries (500900.BY) +1.1% at INR636.30. Infosys (500209.BY) +0.9 at INR2,648.00, Larsen (500510.BY) +0.8% at INR1,605.50. But, Tata Power (500400.BY) down 1.4% at INR1,242. (gurdev.singh@dowjones.com)

0400 GMT [Dow Jones] NZ shares down 0.6% at 3038.08 in thin volume, following trend of offshore markets, says Hamilton Hindin Greene broker Grant Williamson; "once again we are lacking any domestic news or any stock specific news. It's all extremely quiet." Fisher & Paykel Appliances (FPA.NZ) down 1.8% at NZ$0.55; "investors are still a little bit uncertain regarding Fisher & Paykel Appliances and would like to see proof of a turnaround in demand for their products and earnings." Telecom (TEL.NZ) +0.5% at NZ$1.88 after touching fresh all-time low of NZ$1.85 earlier in session; "It's just bouncing off that low." Says dearth of local drivers mean "all eyes will be on international markets once again." (rebecca.howard@dowjones.com) [ 06-02-10 0041ET ]
