* Indonesia, Taiwan c.banks also seen intervening

* Talk of funds unwinding short euro/Asia positions

(Adds details, analyst comments)

By Jongwoo Cheon

SINGAPORE, Aug 9 (Reuters) - Emerging Asian currencies fell on Tuesday on heavy stock outflows before intervention and a recovery in the share markets helped them cut losses, but the near-term outlook remains cloudy on concerns about the Europe debt crises and U.S. economy.

Asian shares slumped in recent sessions, pulling down their currencies, which had been benefiting from the region's growth story and the reluctance to hold euros due to the ongoing sovereign debt crisis in Europe.

"It looks difficult for sentiment on Asian currencies to revive anytime soon, although they may outperform others, as many investors have given up hopes for a sustained economic recovery," said Jeong My-young, a currency strategist of Samsung Futures in Seoul.

The extreme sell-off in risk assets has forced funds to square-up all risk positions and sell Asian currencies as well.

"Clearly, the risk factor dominates in the near-term, which pressures down Asian rates and FX. I have closed all my recommendations to pay Asian rates," said Frances Cheung, a strategist at Credit Agricole CIB in Hong Kong.

Shares recouped some of their losses, with traders citing speculation that the Fed might make an emergency statement before U.S. market opened as one of the reasons for the rebound, but most players were dismissive of the rumour.

To cushion the impact of a stock sell-off, some of the regional foreign exchange authorities, especially in Indonesia, South Korea and Taiwan, were spotted selling dollars to stem weakness in their currencies, dealers said. The Taiwan dollar, helped by intervention, outperformed most of its Asian peers.

Policymakers are likely to keep providing relief to their currencies, which are expected to stay weak as investors are likely to keep reducing risk exposure in a global rout, analysts and dealers said.

"We are on a slippery slope currently and any volatility that the authorities can control, they will try to," said Sacha Tihanyi, senior currency strategist for Scotia Capital in Hong Kong.

"Given that high financial market volatility increases the negative downside risks to growth outlooks, and the softening in commodity prices, these central banks may be more amenable to entertaining FX weakness. However, stemming volatility will also be a concern."

Investors are now focussing on the Federal Reserve's policy meeting later in the day amid mounting pressures on the U.S. central bank for more actions to revive the economy and relive global markets.

The outlook remains dim.

"It (rebounds in stocks and Asian currencies) might be a bad development actually, with investors lured back to risk assets. But the risk is still to the downside if the ECB and Fed disappoint, for example," said Credit Agricole CIB's Cheung.

WON

The won recovered most of losses as the authorities were spotted selling dollars, especially around the dollar/won's session high of 1,096.1, to check the local currency's weakness.

Exporters also bought the South Korean currency for settlements.

The 14-day dollar/won Relative Strength Index (RSI) still stays above the 70 threshold, indicating the pair is in overbought territory, allowing the market to expect a rebound.

"We may see a sharp rise in the won after seeing such a severe fall. I don't think foreigners will sell stocks more," said a foreign bank dealer in Seoul.

Foreign investors sold a net 1.18 trillion won ($1.09 billion) in stocks, the largest since March 10 and outpacing their net purchases of bond futures of 998.8 billion won.

Bond inflows have also supported the won.

RUPIAH

The rupiah also cut losses as stock trimmed falls and after Indonesian central bank was spotted buying it for intervention.

Earlier, the Indonesian currency slid 0.6 percent to 8,555 per dollar, breaking through the 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of its appreciation since late June.

"The central bank has been actively supplying the dollar to maintain FX volatility," says an Asian bank dealer in Jakarta, adding BI was seen at the moment.

The central bank has been seen using a firm rupiah to fight inflation, but in a statement announcing its rate decision on Tuesday, Bank Indonesia said "it expects the currency to remain stable with a tendency of limited appreciation."

Foreign investors sold a combined net $408.7 million in Indonesian stocks during the previous four consecutive sessions, according to Reuters data.

That compared with a 14-day moving average of net daily sales of $11.2 million.

PHILIPPINE PESO

The Philippine peso recovered most of earlier losses on caution over the central bank's intervention and regional stocks cut falls.

"Both local and foreign names buying this morning, but they are not too keen in pushing spot beyond 42.79," said a European bank dealer in Manila, referring dollar/peso's session high.

The central bank was expected to step in the market, if the peso weakens to 42.80, he added.

RINGGIT

The dollar is testing major resistance against the Malaysian ringgit at 3.0447. This is the 200-day moving average and has thwarted six attempts by the dollar to overcome it in the space of the last two years.

The dollar has not achieved a daily close above this index since 14 July 2009.

A daily close above this average is clearly bullish for the dollar and opens the possibility that its long term downtrend is coming to an end.

Investors still remain complacently long emerging Asian currencies and may be forced to exit their positions as the global stock market rout takes its toll.

The dollar which currently trades at 3.0430 will face further major resistance at 3.0700.

title: EM ASIA  FX -Won, rupiah down on specs' dlr-short covering
text:
* Dlr short-covering, Lone Star rumour weigh on won

* Rupiah dips on corporate dlr demand

* Euro, weakening global economy may slow inflows to Asia

(Updates with text, prices)

By Jongwoo Cheon

SINGAPORE, July 5 (Reuters) - The South Korean won and the Indonesian rupiah eased on Tuesday as interbank speculators covered dollar-short positions with the euro hit by a slew of stop-loss buying, but continuous inflows to Asia helped limit regional currencies' weakness.

"The uncertainty over the euro zone and the global economy may slow inflows to Asia, although flows could be quite volatile depending on sentiment," said Frances Cheung, a strategist at Credit Agricole CIB in Hong Kong.

"With the uncertainty, Asian currencies can suffer from time to time in the near term."

Adding to the uncertainty over the outlook for the second half of the year for emerging Asian currencies, Australia's central bank trimmed its growth outlook for this year, while keeping interest rates on hold, as expected.

Emerging Asian currencies rose in the first half of the year, but their gains slowed in April-June on fears of a potential Greece debt default and signs of a slowing global economy.

But regional units have started the third quarter with a firm tone as foreign investors resumed buying stocks and bonds in the region, encouraged by stronger economic fundamentals than in many developed markets.

Long-term investors are unlikely stop injecting money into Asia as long as its robust growth is maintained, dealers and analysts said.

"The big picture won't be changed and USD/Asia still looks heavy," said a Kuala Lumpur-based dealer.

WON

The won retreated as investors covered dollar-short positions and on a market rumour about dollar demand linked to Korea Exchange Bank's dividend payment to Lone Star.

The U.S. buyout fund is set to secure a $466 million dividend payout from its stake in KEB.

Still, the South Korean currency found relief from shipbuilders' demand for settlements and some investors such as offshore model funds bought it on dips.

"Offshore funds will absorb the won currency assets whenever they have time and money. In longer term, the won's bullish trend remains intact," said a foreign bank dealer in Seoul.

Foreign investors bought Seoul stocks for five sessions in a row.

RUPIAH

The rupiah shed 0.2 percent to 8,540 versus the greenback on dollar-short covering and corporate demand.

Investors also remained cautious over possible dollar-buying intervention by the central bank, with a dealer citing Bank Indonesia's aggressive dollar purchases around 8,518-8,525 in the previous session.

On Monday, the central bank's deputy governor said it sees the rupiah averaging 8,650 per dollar.

Still, the Indonesian currency is seen staying firm despite caution over intervention, said a Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta, adding investors are likely to keep seeking higher yields.

"BI will guard it only when its moves are too volatile," the dealer said.

RINGGIT

The ringgit slightly fell against the dollar as interbank speculators covered dollar-short positions.

Still, rises in dollar/ringgit were capped ahead of some resistances such as 3.0135, around the bottom of the daily Ichimoku cloud.

Its 55-day moving average also stood at 3.0145.

title: DJ UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Deputy Gov: Not Closed To Interest Rate-Hike Option
text:
--Indonesian central bank isn't ruling out raising policy interest rate, even though inflation looks to be on downward trend, says deputy governor

--Room to manage inflation by letting rupiah appreciate isn't as big as before

--Central bank, finance ministry in talks to use foreign exchange reserves to buy back government bonds.

(adds more comments from Hadad from 4th paragraph, remarks from finance minister in 14th-15th paragraphs) 


 
   By I Made Sentana and P.R. Venkat 
   Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Muliaman Hadad Sunday said the central bank isn't closed to the option of increasing interest rates, and cautioned that room to manage inflation by letting the local currency rise is not as "big" as before.

"Indeed we see that inflation is on a downward trend for now. But I don't think we are closed to the option of hiking interest rates" Hadad told Dow Jones Newswires on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum on East Asia.

He added that while the appreciation of the rupiah against the dollar helps to check imported inflation, "the room for maneuvering [inflation through currency appreciation] is not so big as before."

Hadad said that while domestic prices pressures need to be contained, a very strong local currency won't be good for the economy.

The central bank has said it will allow the rupiah to strengthen more against the U.S. dollar to help offset inflationary pressures. The rupiah has risen about 5.7% against the greenback so far this year, making it one the best performing among the major Asian currencies.

Bank Indonesia has held off on raising its policy interest rate even as inflation accelerated earlier this year, for fear of attracting speculative capital inflows. It has raised the rate just once since August 2009, and Thursday left the policy rate unchanged at 6.75%

Hadad also said that any increase in the reserve requirement ratio for commercial banks would depend on the amount of excess liquidity in the system.

The central bank has been using tools other than the policy rate to rein in inflation, including an increase of the mandatory reserve requirement ratio to 8% from 3% to tighten liquidity.

Hadad also said the authorities were looking at ways to develop its bond markets to better manage the large capital flows entering Indonesia.

On intervention by the central bank to sterilize the excess liquidity, Hadad said that such moves are done in consultation with the finance ministry. "We do discuss this [intervention] very closely," he said.

Speaking earlier at a WEF conference, Hadad said Bank Indonesia was optimistic on keeping inflation within target this year.

Indonesia's headline inflation is likely to be slightly more than 5% this year, within the central bank's target range of 4% to 6%, due to lower domestic food prices, an appreciating currency, and a lower chance of the government raising administered prices, Perry Warjiyo, a director at Bank Indonesia had said Friday.

Indonesia's consumer price index rose nearly 7% through 2010.

At the same conference, Indonesian Finance Minister Agus Martowardojo said that his country was not looking at implementing any capital controls and that his ministry was in talks with the central bank to use foreign exchange reserves to buy back government bonds.

He said that the government and Bank Indonesia will sign an agreement that will allow the government to use the central bank's foreign exchange reserves to stabilize the government's rupiah bond prices if investors dump the notes.

Foreigners currently hold around 30% of the government rupiah's bonds, one of the highest ratios in the region.

-By I Made Sentana, and P.R. Venkat, Dow Jones Newswires, 62-39831277; i-made.sentana@dowjones.com

--Andreas Ismar and Linda Silaen contributed to this article.

title: EM ASIA  FX -Rises gather momentum after Fed;  intervention  cited
text:
* Sing dlr at record high; rupiah at 7-yr peak

* Won hits 32-mth high despite intervention, control warning

* MAS, BNM, BI intervention spotted

(Updates with prices, snippets)

By Jongwoo Cheon

SINGAPORE, April 28 (Reuters) - Emerging Asian currencies gathered upside momentum, touching milestones against the dollar on Thursday after the Federal Reserve signalled it would not hurry to tighten policy, cementing expectations for further fund flows into Asia.

The Singapore dollar hit a fresh record high against the greenback and is seen as technically the most overbought since October last year when the central bank widened its trading band for the first time since after Sept. 11, 2001 attacks on the United States.

Foreign exchange authorities from many Asian countries including Singapore and South Korea intervened to check strength in their currencies, but they moved dollar bids lower in line with overall gains in the regional units, dealers said.

Currency market players, such as exporters, did not miss out on buying emerging Asian currencies on dips that resulted from intervention.

The Federal Reserve's first-ever press conference "appeared merely to confirm the market's view that the Fed will complete its QE2 programme and thereafter maintain ultra-loose monetary policy for the foreseeable future. For now at least, there appeared little to trouble USD bears," said Callum Henderson, global head of FX research with Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore.

"The market is clearly short USD, but with USD fundamentals remaining very weak -- weak growth recovery, zero policy rates, high unemployment, rate hikes outside the US, and the terms of trade impact from high oil -- that remains the way to go."

On Wednesday, Chairman Ben Bernanke signaled that the U.S. central bank is in no rush to scale back its support for the economy with the labour market still in a "very, very deep hole." [ID:nN26291565]

Emerging Asian currencies have risen on growing appetite for higher yields, as regional policymakers fight inflation amid economic fundamentals that are stronger than elsewhere.

Abundant global liquidity also helped them as investors have piled into Asian stocks and bonds.

"Asian currencies' gains are really speedy, especially after Bernanke appeared not to have any will to lift the dollar," said Jeong My-young, a currency strategist of Samsung Futures in Seoul.

Investors appeared long on regional currencies against the dollar, but they saw little risks of massive dollar short-covering for the moment.

"Bernanke seems to be rather happy with holding off any tightening move even after completing QE2," said Andy Ji, Asian currency strategist and economist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia in Singapore.

"The Fed thinks both core inflation and inflation expectation are well anchored. So in the short-term, risks of dollar-short cover have diminished somewhat, at least for the next month."

Still, more gains in Asian currencies may come slowly on intervention and given market positions, some dealers said.

Ji expects regional central banks to intensify intervention efforts along with some forms of capital controls.

Seoul warned that it may impose fresh capital controls after data showed short-term foreign borrowing in March jumped the most in 27 months amid expectations for further gains in the won currency. [ID:nL3E7FR5CF]

"From here, we should play short-term because risk of a jump(in USD/AXJ) is high with too many short positions," said a senior dealer in Kuala Lumpur.

The dollar/Singapore dollar's 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI) fell to 16.7, the weakest since Oct. 14 last year when the Monetary Authority of Singapore widened the trading band for the city-state's currency.

The dollar/ringgit 14-day RSI slid to 14.9, the lowest since May 2007, indicating the pair are oversold.

WON

The won strengthened to as firm as 1,071.0 per dollar in Seoul, the strongest since August 2008, and its one-month non-deliverable forward (NDF) also shrank to the lowest since that same month.

The foreign exchange authorities were spotted buying dollars to stem gains in the South Korean currency.

Meanwhile, a central bank official said a firmer won had had little impact exports on so far and domestic companies would be able to bear the levels. [ID:nL3E7FS00H]

RUPIAH

The rupiah hit a seven-year high against the dollar with strong follow-through demand for Indonesia's new dollar bond.

In one of the biggest deals in the dollar space from Asia-Pacific, Jakarta's $2.5 billion medium-term note offering this week was nearly 3 times oversubscribed, with half the issue snapped up by U.S. investors. [ID:nIFR75cDT4]

The rupiah firmed to as strong as 8,572, the strongest since April 2004.

The central bank was spotted buying dollara, initially from 8,600 up to 8,610, but pulled back its intervention lines.

A European bank dealer in Jakarta said Bank Indonesia would allow more appreciation as it is a regional trend.

INTERVENTION

Central banks of Singapore and Malaysia were spotted buying dollars to slow down strength in their currencies, which were seen as more overbought than others.

But they also lowered levels of U.S. dollar bids in line with a slide in the greenback, dealers said.

The MAS was spotted buying the U.S. dollar from 1.2280, but the Singapore dollar strengthened to as firm as 1.2250.

title: DJ US Dollar To Remain Pressured Despite Singapore  Currency  Move
text:
-- Asian central banks unlikely to end dollar recycling

-- Singapore's currency move not likely to herald regional shift in policy

-- U.S. dollar set to remain under pressure By Siva Sithraputhran Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

LONDON (Dow Jones)--The U.S. dollar is set to remain under pressure over the long term because most Asian central banks are seen as being unlikely to slow the pace of greenback sales, even after Singapore signaled that it might do just that.

Asian central banks typically buy the dollar against local currencies to slow any export-denting bouts of strength, but then churn the dollars into euros, Australian dollars, and other currencies to spread the risks, so the greenback falls. This 'recycling' of reserves has been at the heart of the dollar's weakness against a range of currencies--including the euro--over recent years.

That relationship came under scrutiny Thursday after the Monetary Authority of Singapore opened up to more currency strength by raising the trading band of the Singapore dollar, initially boosting the currency to a record high against the greenback and dragging other Asian currencies higher with it. Tellingly though, the immediate reaction from Singapore's closest neighbor, Malaysia, was to intervene in the market to stem the rise of its currency--the ringgit--indicating that there is still lot of resistance to allow local currency gains.

Recycling quickly kicked in, and the U.S. dollar plunged, sinking fast against the euro, the Australian dollar, and other major currencies.

Valentin Marinov, a strategist at Citigroup in London, remains of the opinion that emerging-market currencies will be allowed to rise only gradually, maintaining that pressure on the dollar.

'This set-up could be particularly damaging for the dollar against its liquid alternatives in the G-10 world,' he said. 'We think this should continue to generate sufficient upside momentum for the euro and Australian dollar against the greenback,' he added.

Over the past few months, there have been waves of interventions by the central banks of South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia to arrest the rises of their respective currencies. By keeping their currencies from rising too fast, the central banks want to make sure their exports don't lose competitiveness.

'There is no monetary coordination in Asia, with most policymakers running mercantilist-type policies that favor their own exports via undervalued exchange rates,' Win Thin, New York-based strategist at Brown Brothers Harriman said.

Singapore has been 'more open to currency appreciation in [a] controlled way' than some regional competitors, said Ken Dickson, investment director at Standard Life Investments in Edinburgh, which manages GBP143 billion in assets worldwide.

To some extent, China too has been allowing its currency to rise very gradually as it tries to rein in inflation.

The amount of currency reserves held by Asian central banks has continued to mount, suggesting that the wider market impact of any region-wide change in policy could be huge, even if only a fraction of these reserves are moved in or out of dollars.

At the end of March, China's foreign exchange reserves surged to a record, topping $3 trillion. In Singapore, reserves have been climbing steadily since November, to reach just over $233 billion in March. That indicates that the central banks have been carrying out smoothing operations to keep their currencies within the required trading bands. Data for April will be eagerly awaited for signs that the pace of gains has moderated.

Singapore's move last week means it will be able to trim these smoothing operations, said Dickson at Standard Life.

But as other regional central banks are still loathe to let their currencies rise, the impact of Singapore's action on the U.S. dollar looks set to be drowned out. -By Siva Sithraputhran, Dow Jones Newswires; 44-20-7842-9462; siva.sithraputhran@dowjones.com.

title: DJ Emerging Nations Seen Taking More Subdued Tone On  Currency  Wars
text:
--Emerging nations may be less strident on currency appreciation at coming IMF/World Bank meetings

--Inflation makes emerging countries more open to forex appreciation

--Capital controls, currency battles to remain an issue By Anjali Cordeiro Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

NEW YORK (Dow Jones)--After a year of aggressive moves to beat down their exchange rates, emerging nations are quietly showing a greater acceptance for stronger currencies as they battle rising inflation at home.

Some of that willingness to allow currency appreciation may be reflected in the tone of finance ministers and central bankers from the developing world as they gather for the 2011 Spring meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Washington later this week.

As with previous such meetings, there is still likely to be finger pointing. Developing nations continue to blame loose monetary policy in the U.S. as a cause of potential asset bubbles and currency appreciation in Asia and Latin America. They also face pressure from their exporters to keep currencies weak due to competition from China, which tightly controls the yuan. But those worries are temporarily taking a back seat to local price pressures.

'I wouldn't expect the same stridency around currencies that we have seen in some recent meetings, nor will the issue disappear,' says Mark Malloch-Brown, a former vice president of the World Bank, who is now at FTI Consulting.

For investors, the growing possibility that policymakers will be more flexible makes Latin American and Asian currencies an attractive proposition. The dollar has lost 5.6% against the real and 1.4% against the Indonesia rupiah since mid March. A stronger currency, which reduces the price of imports, can help reduce inflation.

Brazil's Finance Minister Guido Mantega, who used the term 'currency wars' to describe global disagreements on foreign exchange, last year raised taxes on foreign fixed-income investments into the country. But as the real soared over the last month, investors grew hopeful that Brazilian policymakers will take a softer stance.

While Brazil's central bank has continued to build reserves, there have been no stringent capital controls announced. Policymakers there are battling inflation, with data showing a rise in the 12-month inflation rate to 6.3% as of March.

Bank Indonesia's deputy governor said recently that the central bank will continue to fight inflation and prevent the rupiah from being overly volatile. Those comments could suggest the bank might be open to allowing the rupiah to rise somewhat to fight inflation, but it would want any moves to be smooth.

'Indonesia changed their tune,' said David Rolley, portfolio manager at Loomis, Sayles & Co. 'All these central banks had to decide what war to fight. They are now much more interested in fighting inflation than a currency war.'

One issue likely to be hotly debated at the meetings is the efficacy of capital controls and government interventions in currencies. In a reversal of its earlier stance, the International Monetary Fund recently endorsed the use of controls on international cash inflows in certain cases.

But it is still unclear how effective such policy tools have been in curbing currency increases in places like Brazil and South Korea. These currencies have risen even though policymakers have taken steps to curb so-called 'hot money' flows.

Emerging nations are unlikely to completely throw in the towel. Central banks in South Korea, Malaysia and Indonesia appeared to intervene in foreign-exchange market in recent weeks as their currencies jumped, though their main focus appears to be to stem appreciation rather than reverse the direction of their currencies.

Emerging Asian countries, excluding China, intervened in spot currency markets by an estimated $11 billion in March and $15.3 billion in February, according to Barclays Capital. This compares to an average of $22.6 billion per month between August and October last year, when such interventions were more aggressive.

Emerging-market policymakers generally compare their currencies versus others in the developing world. So, they tend to be more comfortable if all emerging market currencies are appreciating at the same time, says Denise Simon, a portfolio manager on the Lazard emerging-markets debt team in New York.

'I don't know if individually countries can do anything' to reverse the upward trend in their currencies, said Simon, whose team likes Asian and Latin American currencies because of the fundamental strength of these economies and widening interest rate differentials.

Emerging world central banks have begun raising interest rates, even as rates in the U.S. and Japan remain near zero. The International Monetary Fund in its World Economic Outlook noted that some emerging economies will need even tighter monetary policies to reduce the risk of a hard landing. In most of these economies, some appreciation of the exchange rate is called for, the IMF said.

Philip Poole, head of macro and investments strategy at HSBC Global Asset Management, says China's recent moves to let the yuan to move a little higher makes it easier for other emerging nations to allow appreciation. Currencies like the Singapore dollar and Korean won look attractive, he feels, and even the Brazilian real could rise some more.

But he doesn't expect any broad consensus or coordination on emerging currencies at the IMF meetings: 'It's each man for himself.' -By Anjali Cordeiro; Dow Jones Newswires; 212-416-2200; anjali.cordeiro@dowjones.com

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesia holds rates for now, using rupiah vs inflation
text:
(Adds details, quotes from central bank and economists)

JAKARTA, April 12 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate at 6.75 percent on Tuesday, as expected, and said it was letting the rupiah rise as part of its efforts to contain inflationary pressures caused by strong domestic demand and high commodity prices.

Economists said those worries about inflation meant interest rates were bound to go higher but Bank Indonesia decided to hold policy on this occasion because inflation dipped in March and the current harvest would help take pressure off food prices.

"In our view, it is wise to probably tighten further, given the economy is still very strong. We saw some ministers said 6.5 percent growth for Q1 -- that's a very strong number," said Wellian Wiranto, an economist with HSBC in Singapore.

"We still think they will hike in second quarter, even as soon as next month. (Our forecast) is they will rise 25 basis points next month and another 25 basis points in June, so a total of 50 basis points in Q2."

The central bank expects economic growth to remain solid in the second quarter, with Governor Darmin Nasution telling a news conference after a policy meeting that he expected an expansion of 6.4 percent from the same quarter last year.

Annual inflation slowed to 6.65 percent in March from 6.84 percent in February, although core inflation, which excludes administered prices and volatile food, edged up to 4.45 percent from 4.36 percent.

The rupiah has strengthened nearly 4 percent against the dollar in 2011. At mid-afternoon Tuesday, it was at around 8,655 to the dollar. In the past week, it has touched its strongest level since May 2004.

Bank Indonesia has intervened in the currency market to put brakes on the rupiah's appreciation, but not aggressively.

"Like other regional central banks, Bank Indonesia recognises the benefit of an appreciating currency in helping to contain inflation pressures," said David Cohen at Action Economics in Singapore.

Any worries about loss of competitiveness from the rise in the rupiah were mitigated by the rise in other Asian currencies, he said. Central bank chief Nasution said competitiveness had not been hurt.

However, to slow the influx of hot money coming into the country, the central bank announced that from May 13 investors would have to hold on to central bank debt (SBI) for six months before selling it, against one month now.

Analysts forecast Bank Indonesia will raise rates to 7 percent by the end of this quarter and to 7.5 percent by the year-end to dampen inflation in Southeast Asia's largest economy.

Rising oil prices may force the government to implement a plan to cut fuel subsidies for private cars, which has been delayed, or increase the retail price of subsidised fuel sometime in the second quarter, which will add to inflationary pressures.

(Reporting by Aditya Suharmoko and Adriana Nina Kusuma; Writing by Alan Raybould)

title: DJ UPDATE: Asian  Currencies  Surge With Euro, Prompting  Intervention
text:
-- Asian currencies surge as euro climbs on ECB, dollar slumps on budget

-- Intervention spotted in Philippines, Malaysia, Korea, Indonesia, Thailand, India, Taiwan

-- Region's central banks buy $7.5 billion, Citigroup estimates

-- Singapore dollar logs record high, Australian dollar highest since 1983 float, Korean won 2.5-year peak

-- No letup seen for dollar weakness until the Fed ends QE2 in June

(Adds estimated total for region, Bank Indonesia comments, Taiwan intervention) 


 
   By P.R. Venkat 
   Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Asian currencies surged Friday as the euro climbed on an interest-rate hike and the dollar languished on a potential U.S. government shutdown, prompting several central banks in the region to intervene to curb their currencies' gains.

Among the sharp gainers, the Singapore dollar broke from its recent stagnancy to pop to a record high against the U.S. currency, the Australian dollar again notched its highest level since being floated in 1983 and the South Korean won hit a two-and-a-half-year high.

Central banks in the Philippines, Malaysia, Korea, Indonesia, Thailand, India and Taiwan apparently bought dollars to keep the advance in their own currencies under control, local traders said. All told, the region's central banks bought $7.5 billion, Ron Ng of Citigroup Global estimated in a research note.

Traders began the day expecting the dollar might rise against Asian currencies, as investors looked set to take profits on recent dollar declines to square their positions heading into the weekend.

Instead, the U.S. currency remained weak as the euro added to gains from Thursday's rate hike by the European Central Bank, its first tightening since 2008. Many Asian currencies take their cue from the euro, which has acted as a barometer of global risk appetite.

The dollar fell against most major and regional currencies as hopes faded that Republicans and Democrats in Washington could agree on a budget deal before the U.S. government runs out of operating cash at midnight Friday.

"The tightening cycle in Europe has clearly started, and the rate-differential argument is pertinent here," while U.S. budget worries weighed on the dollar, said currency strategist Nizam Idris at UBS in Singapore.

Asian central banks may try to cushion the dollar's fall against their currencies but know they can't stop the trend, and are simply trying to keep their export-reliant economies roughly competitive with their neighbors'. The authorities seldom comment on intervention, but officials at several central banks in recent days have said they will act to prevent excessive volatility.

Indeed, Bank Indonesia Deputy Gov. Budi Mulia told Dow Jones Newswires on Friday the central bank will continue to fight inflation, suggesting tolerance of rupiah gains, while preventing the currency's moves from being too volatile.

The region's currencies have surged over the past year as Asia has led the global economic recovery and as low interest rates in the richest countries have spurred a flood of investor capital into Asia seeking higher returns.

Asian currencies also got a boost as the People's Bank of China fixed the tightly controlled yuan higher Friday for a sixth session, setting the dollar's central parity rate at a record low CNY6.5420.

Expectations that Beijing will allow faster yuan gains sent the yuan sharply higher in the market for nondeliverable forwards, an offshore venue where investors can bet on future moves. The 12-month dollar/yuan contract sank to a three-year low bid quote of CNY6.3620, from CNY6.4000.

The region's currency authorities are generally tolerating greater appreciation these days to help them battle rising inflation, said Thomas Harr, head of Asia currency strategy at Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore. The dollar will likely remain weak until at least June, when the Federal Reserve is slated to end its "quantitative easing" policy of buying government bonds, he said.

Friday's euro ascent kick-started the Asia rally. The common currency had come off Thursday's highs as the ECB's quarter-percentage-point rate hike was almost universally expected and central bank chief Jean-Claude Trichet said the ECB hadn't decided to embark on a series of rate increases.

Nonetheless, the euro took off in the Asia morning on the view that the ECB may tighten every quarter, and the currency never looked back.

The euro's rise to a 2011 high above $1.44 spurred accelerating gains among Asian currencies, notably the Singapore dollar. The U.S. dollar had been largely holding above support around S$1.26 for the past two weeks, but the euro's climb helped break through that level. At 0945 GMT, the euro was at $1.4399, and the U.S. currency bought S$1.2571.

"Whoever is long dollar will be suffering here," said Idris.

The ICE Dollar Index, a broad measure of the currency's value against the currencies of America's main trading partners, was at 75.185 late in the Asian session. That was down from 75.534 late in New York and threatened a slide to its November 2009 low of 74.17 in coming weeks.

To tame the peso at five-month highs, the Philippine central bank apparently bought $600 million between PHP43.05 and PHP43.00 in heavy trade, defending the U.S. currency around the psychologically important PHP43.00 line, Manila traders said. Bank Negara Malaysia apparently twice sold the ringgit, which has benefited as a proxy for the rising Chinese currency, Kuala Lumpur traders said. They spotted the central bank buying dollars at MYR3.0210 late in the day after a defense at MYR3.0220 failed.

The Bank of Korea apparently bought an estimated $1 billion as the dollar fell to 1,082.00, its lowest since August 2008, when the global financial crisis was escalating, Seoul dealers said.

In a bid to curb the rising rupiah and baht, Bank Indonesia apparently bought an estimated $100 million at IDR8,653, while the Bank of Thailand apparently bought dollars around THB30.03, local dealers said. After the rupee hit a six-month high, the Reserve Bank of India was seen apparently buying dollars at INR43.98, the first intervention since November, local traders said.

The Taiwan central bank let the local dollar strengthen more than local traders had expected, but they spotted the bank buoying the greenback late in the day at TWD28.903.

-By P.R. Venkat, Dow Jones Newswires; +65 64154 152; venkat.pr@dowjones.com

title: Bank Indonesia: To Keep Inflation Under Control, Prevent Rupiah Volatility
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia will continue to fight inflation and prevent the rupiah from being overly volatile, Deputy Gov. Budi Mulia said Friday.

Mulia's statement could indicate that the central bank remains open to the option of raising interest rates if inflation picks up again, and allowing the rupiah to continue rising to help rein in imported inflation, although it is likely to want the rupiah's appreciation against the dollar to be smooth.

title: MARKET TALK: Oil Traders Should Also Watch USD - GS Caltex
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0550 GMT [Dow Jones] Supply problems in Libya and other oil-exporting states remain the dominant driver of crude's rally, with concerns over election related potential production disruptions in Nigeria supporting benchmark contracts in Asian trade Friday. Nigeria's electoral agency on Thursday announced a third delay in legislative polls in some parts of the country. Traders say any kind of supply problems in Africa's top oil producing nation will likely squeeze an already tight global oil market and trigger a long-term bull signal for crude. Nymex crude for May delivery is up 85 cents at $111.15/bbl after hitting a fresh 2.5-year high of $111.19 earlier in the session. In addition, oil traders should also keep an eye on the USD, says a GS Caltex trader. The USD is weaker against the EUR in Asian trade after the ECB delivered its first rate hike since 2008 Thursday; the greenback's weakness will likely provide extra support for dollar-denominated crude prices. "There are just too many factors pushing oil prices up," says the trader. (philip.vahn@dowjones.com)

0545 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares end 0.1% lower at 8894,54, ending a six-session winning streak, dragged by profit-taking in tech heavyweights HTC (2498.TW) and Hon Hai (2317.TW), although hotel operators soar on news Taiwan will allow Chinese individual tourists to visit by end-June. Diana Wu, an analyst at Capital Securities, tips the Taiex to remain in a 8750-9000 range next week as fund rotation will remain the trading theme, with banking stocks likely outperforming as local interest rates are steadily rising. Among other gainers, Compal (2324.TW) is +4.6% at NT$29.80 on its share buyback and AU Optronics (2409.TW) is up 1.6% at NT$26.00 on improved average selling prices in March. (aries.poon@dowjones.com)

0536 GMT [Dow Jones] The EUR/CHF is likely to appreciate to 1.35 in three months and to 1.40 in six months as financial markets are proving resilient to risk, ING says. "We look for the funding currencies of the U.S. dollar, the yen and the Swiss franc to underperform this year, while the euro and emerging-market currencies should shine," says strategist Chris Turner. The EUR/CHF is at 1.3111. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0531 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/THB slips to 30.03-30.04 from 30.06-30.07 early, and compared with 30.11-30.115 late Thursday in active trade, in line with most regional peers, say traders. The Bank of Thailand is suspected to have bought the dollar since early trade, say two local dealers; they expect the central bank to be around for the entire day to slow the baht's rise. One local dealer adds that continued capital inflows, in addition to exporters' selling, are pushing the greenback lower. Another dealer says the rising interest rate trend amid robust economic growth in Asia is likely to continue to attract more fund inflows. Dealers tip support at 30.00 for today. (piyarat.setthasiriphaiboon@dowjones.com)

0529 GMT [Dow Jones] India's overnight call rate is likely to remain below 6.0% for the next two weeks on a positive banking system cash situation and as the RBI extends the second liquidity facility until March 6, says a dealer with a privately-run bank. The measures were set to expire Friday. The RBI says banks can avail liquidity up to 1.0% of their net deposits and can apply for a waiver if they fall short of the mandated bond-holding ratio due to this measure. "This will flush the banking system with liquidity in the short-term but may not be sustainable in the long-run," the dealer adds. The interbank overnight call rate is at 5.85% unchanged from Thursday's close, while the three-day call rate is at 6.0%. The collateralized borrowing and lending obligation rate or CBLO is at 2.16% from 3.25% at the open. The dealer tips the overnight call rate in a 5.00%-6.00% range in the near-term.(sourav.mishra@dowjones.com)

0523 GMT [Dow Jones] S&P's upgrade of Indonesia sovereign ratings raises expectations the country could get the long-coveted investment grade by the three major ratings agency by 2012, says Standard Chartered economist Eric Sugandi. "One of them could upgrade in 2011," he says. S&P raised its long-term foreign currency sovereign credit and debt ratings to BB+ with a positive outlook from BB. Its ratings are now at par with Fitch's BB+ (positive), and Moody's Ba1 (stable outlook). Analysts don't expect S&P's action to push bond prices much higher after their recent rally. "Bond yields have been very low," Danamon bond analyst Helmi Arman says. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0520 GMT (Dow Jones) The near-term risk for USD/CHF has reverted to the downside, and a retracement into the 0.9025 area is possible, says Commerzbank. "Intraday rallies are likely to find near term resistance at 0.9225 ahead of 0.9300," according to analyst Karen Anne Jones. The USD/CHF is at 0.9101 by 0515 GMT. (neil.maclucas@dowjones.com)

0512 GMT [Dow Jones] An investor sells with-delta one-month USD-call/JPY-put contract with a Y86.00 strike at 10.65% earlier in the day, while some other players sell three-month at-the-money straddles, says a senior dealer at a major Japanese bank. Traded contracts suggest "investors believe the USD/JPY will eventually rise above Y86.00, but not at a speed that the current volatilities suggest now," he says, adding that current USD/JPY volatilities are bit overpriced due to the Japan-quake risk premium. Benchmark volatilities implied by one-month ATM volatilities rise to 10.05%/10.75% from 10.25%/10.55% in New York; the dealer says ongoing concerns about Fukushima nuclear reactors are a part of the reason.(takashi.mochizuki@dowjones.com)

0507 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore STI is up marginally, gaining 2.89 points, or 0.1%, to 3174.54 at lunch after opening weaker as markets in Japan recover smartly from a lackluster start after Thursday's earthquake. "We may see some profit-taking again moving into the weekend. The markets are likely to remain cautious. A lot will depend on how the European markets react to the ECB rate hike," says OCBC analyst Carey Wong. Support for the benchmark is tipped below 3165 and then 3130 and resistance at 3180 followed by 3200. SGX (S68.SG) is among the top gainers, +2.7% at S$8.37 as Australia formally rejects merger plans with ASX (ASX.AU). Sembcorp Industries (U96.SG) is the top gainer, up 3.0% at S$5.51 and its rig building unit Sembcorp Marine (S51.SG) is up 1.2% at S$6.00 on a spurt in crude oil prices. Keppel Corp. (BN4.SG) is up 0.2% at S$12.70. (gaurav.raghuvanshi@dowjones.com)

"Although S&P was behind other ratings agencies its ratings action on Indonesia, it's still good news for Indonesia as now all three major ratings agencies have acknowledged Indonesia's progress," a dealer says; three dealers suspect Bank Indonesia to have bought around $100 million at the 8,653 level to ease volatility. title: Bank Indonesia Likely Bought Total $120M Around IDR8,700 -Dealers
text:
Corrected April 1, 2011 5:27 ET (0927 GMT) [ 01-04-11 0854GMT ]

("Bank Indonesia Likely Bought Total $120M At IDR8,700 - Dealers," at 0906 GMT, misstated the central bank's action in the headline and in the first and second paragraphs. The error also appeared in the flash headline "*Bank Indonesia Likely Sold Total $120M Around IDR8,700 -Dealers" at 0854 GMT. The correct version follows:)

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia likely bought a total of $120 million around IDR8,700 Friday to prevent volatility in the value of the nation's currency, three dealers said.

"Bank Indonesia bought the greenback several times today via state banks," a dealer with a foreign bank said.

The dollar was at IDR8,697 at 0855 GMT, down from IDR8,705 late Thursday.

Without confirming specifically Friday's intervention, Bank Indonesia Gov. Darmin Nasution told reporters that the central bank doesn't want the rupiah to appreciate too fast.

"We don't want the (dollar) to reach IDR8,600 levels from IDR8,700 levels too quickly and suddenly," Nasution said.

Bank Indonesia has mentioned that it would allow the rupiah to appreciate to help contained imported inflation.

-By I Made Sentana, Dow Jones Newswires; +62 21-39831277 [ 01-04-11 0924GMT ]

1044 GMT [Dow Jones] The euro net cash requirement [NCR] is negative in April, with EUR74B in bond supply outweighed by EUR57B in redemptions and EUR27B in coupon payments. France, however, benefits from strongly supportive cash flows in the same month, with EUR19B in supply against EUR18.4B in redemptions and EUR16B in coupons. Spain also benefits, with EUR7.3B in supply offset by EUR15.5B in redemptions and EUR3B in coupons. (nick.cawley@dowjones.com)

Sterling, meanwhile, was under pressure after U.K. manufacturing PMI printed a lower-than-expected number and pushed the pound lower. The euro enjoyed some month-end buying, but is unable to make headway against a buoyant greenback. text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

1003 GMT [Dow Jones] Hong Kong's headline consumer price index rose 3.7% in February on-year compared to January's 3.6% increase, mainly due to the rise in private rents. February's CPI was also above the 3.2% median forecast by seven economists in a Dow Jones poll. Economists say the city's inflation will remain on an uptrend in coming months. "The effect of the higher rents have just started to emerge, there is still a long way to go for the private rents to rise more," says Bank of East Asia economist Paul Tang. He expects CPI to rise 4.7% in 2011, more than government's forecast for a 4.5% increase. (chester.yung@dowjones.com)

0956 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/USD appears to be losing some of its upside momentum, says BNP Paribas. With no further action from the BOJ, and a positive outcome from the upcoming E.U. summit already priced in, it's not clear what will drive the spot above 1.4280 resistance, it adds. Looking ahead, the bank says any more hawkish comments from ECB officials will be discounted as the comments of potential candidates for the top job, while an April rate hike is already largely factored in. Portugal's woes are likely to end with it falling into the arms of the EFSF before next month's elections, while data-wise Friday's German IFO is likely to show a sharp fall in expectations, all of which are EUR/USD negatives says the bank. EUR/USD now at 1.4228. (gary.stride@dowjones.com)

0956 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/THB is lower late at 30.23 vs 30.29-30.30 Monday in tandem with softer USD/Regionals, says a Bangkok-based dealer, as exporters continue to unload USD/THB, while some interbank players start to pile up short USD positions. But the pair is off a 30.21 session low on suspected buying by the central bank around the 30.21-30.25 level, two dealers say. "The dollar/baht looks kind of heavy. With the current sentiment (eased concerns over Japan's nuclear issues), I think the pair is bound to drift lower tomorrow," one dealer says. But any possible intervention by the central bank will limit downside. Next support is pegged at 30.20, with resistance at 30.25. (phisanu.phromchanya@dowjones.com)

0952 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia's five-year government bonds are lower as players sought cheaper notes in the finance ministry's auction held earlier today. "The ministry only took IDR1.5 trillion from IDR4.5 trillion worth of bids for the five-year bond. Expect some of those who did not win bids to enter the secondary market Wednesday," a local trader says. He adds trading is light as players opt for the auction instead of the secondary market. The five-year yield is higher at 7.95% from 7.84% late Monday, the 10-year yield is flat at 8.21%, the 15-year yield is down at 9.07% from 9.13%, the 20-year yield is up at 9.49% from 9.48%. (andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

June gilts are down 0.56 at 117.81. (neelabh.chaturvedi@dowjones.com)

0940 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/PKR is lower Tuesday as exporters' selling in the greenback outweighed bids by importers, a state-run bank dealer says. The pair is at 85.40 vs 85.52 late Monday. The dealer tips the pair in a 85.40-85.50 band Thursday. (djn.in@dowjones.com)

"More local investors are seeking the U.S. dollar, although volume remains mild so far," says one dealer. He tips the pair to come in a 8,770-8,800 range Friday. (andreasismar.sandiwan@dowjones.com)

He adds, "the market had factored in a 25bp hike and the RBI view on anti-inflationary stance may not impact immediately." The one-year premia are at 2.690 from 2.775 late Wednesday. He tips the one-year premia to remain in a 2.68-2.72 band for rest of the session. The overnight call rates are now at 7.65%, off an intraday high of 7.90%. Lower oil prices indicate an easing in inflationary pressure as India imports about 80% of its crude oil needs. (sourav.mishra@dowjones.com)

0949 GMT [Dow Jones]--ING doesn't expect an SNB rate hike before September. The Swiss franc's strong appreciation is a useful tool for the SNB in that it curbs the impact on Swiss prices from higher oil prices, and in a small open economy like Switzerland's, it basically works as a monetary tightening, ING economist Julien Manceaux says. "And as consumers are reacting slowly to the recent rise in employment, the SNB seems to think that the Swiss economy has enough monetary tightening for the time being," Manceaux says. (katharina.bart@dowjones.com)

0948 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai shares end 0.6% lower at 1002.35 in tandem with losses in most regional bourses; trade is moderate. Lingering concerns over Japan's unfolding nuclear crisis are weighing on market sentiment. "As long as Japan's problem remains in focus, the (Thai) stock market direction will track regional markets," says Capital Nomura Securities Chai Jirasevenupraphund. He tips support at 995-990 and resistance at 1010. Among the most active shares, PTT (PTT.TH) is down 0.9% at THB336, Banpu (BANPU.TH) is off 0.5% at THB738, IRPC (IRPC.TH) is flat at THB6.0, Indorama Ventures (IVL.TH) is off 1.0% at THB49.25 and Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF.TH) is up 0.4% at THB25. (oranan.paweewun@dowjones.com)

0945 GMT [Dow Jones--The SNB is leaving all its options open in terms of when and how to raise interest rates, says Hyposwiss's Thomas Stucki. "The SNB has been quite clever in that on the one hand, they highlight the strong economic picture, but on the other hand they have put the strong Swiss franc very much in focus too. They are leaving all their options open in terms of hiking rates," Stucki says. His forecasts call for a 25-basis-point hike in September. (katharina.bart@dowjones.com)

0942 GMT [Dow Jones] The Sensex extends losses, down 1.3% at 18,117.39, after the RBI raises policy rates by 25 bps each and increases its March-end inflation forecast to 8% from 7%. "The rate hike was along expected lines, but the increase in the inflation forecast is not an encouraging sign," says a local dealer. He adds, the RBI has said it will stick to an anti-inflationary stance and that means further rate hikes are likely in coming months. Maruti Suzuki India (532500.BY) is down 4.6% at INR1,167.30 due to concerns the recent sharp rise in the JPY will push up the company's import costs. Housing Development Finance Corp. (500010.BY) is down 4.0% at INR635.00, while Reliance Industries (500325.BY) is 1.5% lower at INR1,028.50. Among gainers, Bharat Heavy Electricals (500103.BY) is 1.9% higher at INR1,962.00. A Dow Jones technical analyst tips the Sensex in a 18,050-18,500 range for the rest of the session. (sudeep.jain@dowjones.com)

0941 GMT [Dow Jones] The zloty is down and could weaken further Thursday, as the Polish currency remains a proxy for the region, a dealer says. "The zloty is still reacting more violently than other regional currencies to any negative global threat," he says. "Newsflow from Japan remains in focus, while the EUR/PLN is seen in a 4.07-4.11 range today." He adds that the end of the week will give some indication of whether this zloty weakening is the beginning of a larger cycle or whether it will play itself out. EUR/PLN now trades at 4.0862 from 4.0458 Wednesday. USD/PLN at 2.9205 from 2.8966. (marynia.kruk@dowjones.com)

0940 GMT [Dow Jones] India interbank call rates are off their highs but continue to remain at elevated levels as system liquidity moves into sharp deficit due to advance tax outflows, says a dealer with a state-run bank. The overnight call rates are now at 7.65% versus an intraday high of 7.90%. "Apart from advance tax, there is also a rush among branches to disburse sanctioned loans before the end of the fiscal year on March 31, which is keeping demand for cash high," he says. He expects the call rates to remain in a 7.50%-8.00% band in the near term, above the RBI's repo rate of 6.75%. The RBI says in its mid-quarter review of monetary policy that liquidity may come under some temporary pressure in the second half of March due to advance tax collections. It however disclose whether it will extend the additional liquidity easing steps--holding a second daily liquidity auction and allowing banks to borrow to an extent of 1% of deposits--which are to expire on April 8. (nupur.acharya@dowjones.com)

0938 GMT [Dow Jones] Pakistan shares trade a tad higher, supported by gains in oil and fertilizer stocks. The benchmark KSE-100 index is up 0.1% at 11,800.58. "Some buying from local financial institutions, mainly in oil and fertilizer plays, are helping the index to stay afloat," says a domestic dealer. He adds, volume is modest as uncertainty in regional markets on the Japan disaster and ongoing crises in the Middle East are keeping sentiment subdued. Foreign funds sold shares worth $2.9 million Wednesday. He says, "the market outlook appears to be depressed as the government has imposed a 15% flood surcharge on income tax of companies, which would crimp earnings of blue chips." He tips the index in a 11,600-11,900 range in the near term. Pakistan State Oil (PSO.KA) is up 0.4% at PKR280.01 and Engro Corp. (ENGRO.KA) is up 1.0% at PKR195.75. (djn.in@dowjones.com)

0938 GMT [Dow Jones] Russian capital outflows are due to surplus capital arriving in the country from high oil prices but not being absorbed by the economy, UniCredit says. "We think the main reason for the continued capital flight is relatively loose monetary policy on top of persistent weak investment demand in Russia, which keeps interest rates low and capital away from the country." Russia has seen around $17B in outflows so far this year, almost half of what it saw in all of 2010. (ira.iosebashvili@dowjones.com)

0937 GMT [Dow Jones] Thai government bonds are higher on lingering worries over the nuclear crisis in Japan. Offshore participants are seen buying, especially long-dated notes. However, "some local players took profit after the recent rally, bringing yields off their lows," says a bond trader. The focus is on how Japan's situation evolves for potential trading cues. Without any fresh factors, yields are expected to remain rangebound in the near-term. The bid/offer yield of bonds due December 2015 are quoted at 3.29%/3.25% from 3.32%/3.30% in late Asian trade Wednesday, the October 2017 yield is at 3.55%/3.50% from 3.60%/3.50% and the December 2021 yield is at 3.75%/3.70% from 3.84%/3.82%. (phisanu.phromchanya@dowjones.com)

0936 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/THB weakens to 30.32-30.33 from 30.41-30.42 late Wednesday in Asia, bucking the regional trend with some exporters seen selling, a Bangkok-based dealer says; trade is moderate. "It seems that liquidity is low and for some reason, with the USD/JPY down a lot, it is having an impact on the USD/THB," he says; he adds, overall, the market remains fairly directionless despite the THB strength. He expects the pair may break through 30.30 Friday, after which it could shift down quickly to 30.25, although the Bank of Thailand may step in around that level to stem the pace of the downside. Resistance is tipped at 30.35. (leigh.murray@dowjones.com) [ 03-17-11 0552ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Higher On Japan Worries; 8,775-8,805 Tipped
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0116 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR is higher at 8,795 vs 8,780 late yesterday as plummeting Japanese stocks trigger selloffs in other regional bourses including Indonesia, dealers say. Two dealers say Bank Indonesia was heard checking rate, but is unlikely to have intervened as the market remains calm and the pair was off the 8,800 intraday high. "Bank Indonesia could sell the dollar if it creeps higher to above IDR8,800," a dealer says; he tips a 8,775-8,805 range. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0113 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/KRW gaining ground as expected, but off its high with some traders suspecting the BOK has sold small amounts of USD to slow KRW's slide above the 1,140 level early today following finance ministry's warning against volatility, say market participants. The pair is last at 1,138.4, off the 1,144.0 high. "Exporters are selling above KRW1,140 and the Kospi is doing better than expected today. There are also expectations that the government wouldn't be happy to see more gains in the pair due to inflation, which will probably be the reason for their (intervention) earlier," says a local bank trader; he tips the pair to be in a 1,135-1,145 band for the rest of day. A foreign bank trader says external uneasiness linked to Japan's nuclear plant problems have escalated and traders are betting on more gains in pair, but such attempts are offset partly by export settlement. (kanga.kong@dowjones.com)

0109 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia government bonds are likely to rise a tad as worries over the global economy in the aftermath of Japan's earthquake may deter any interest rate hikes in the near future, a local trader says. He tips the yields to move 1 to 2 bps lower during the day. On Wednesday, the yield on the August 2014 MGS ends unchanged at 3.38%, the September 2016 MGS yield also closes flat at 3.55%, the September 2017 MGS yield ends down 2 bps at 3.75%, and the July 2021 MGS yield ends 4 bps down at 4.01%. (ankur.relia@dowjones.com)

0108 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/MYR is higher at 3.0610 vs late Wednesday's 3.0490, tracking other Asian currencies after U.S. stocks tumbled overnight as worries mounted that Japan's nuclear crisis would end in reactor meltdowns and a radiation catastrophe, says a local trader. "We are back to risk aversion again today," he adds. He tips the pair in a 3.0500-3.0700 range. (ankur.relia@dowjones.com)

0106 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/PHP may rise as local stocks are expected to fall after Wall Street's decline overnight, while investors continue to fret about the nuclear situation in Japan. The pair may rise to 43.80 after settling at 43.755 in late Asian trade Wednesday; traders peg resistance at 44.00 and support at 43.50. "It's still a 'buy-dollar and sell-Asia' story because of Japan. However, this is mostly sentiment-driven so the trend could quickly reverse. We're also watching out for BSP (central bank) because it could intervene if the dollar moves towards PHP44.00," says a Manila-based currency dealer.(cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0105 GMT [Dow Jones] The HSI is likely to fall taking a cue from Wall Street, but is not expected to test Monday's low of 22,253 which is also 2011's low, says a futures trader, because "the panic sentiment is unlikely to match that of Monday morning's." Tencent (0700.HK) may fall after below-view FY10 results, while China Mobile (0941.HK) is likely to underperform more in the short run on dividend disappointment and higher capex ahead. More blue-chip stocks such as Henderson Land (0012.HK), China Overseas Land (0688.HK), PetroChina (0857.HK) and China Resources Power (0836.HK) are expected to report results later Thursday. The HSI ended +0.1% at 22,700.88. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0105 GMT [Dow Jones] While bargain hunting has buoyed the USD/JPY up from the post World War II low it hit earlier this morning at 76.25, selling by Japan exporters could weigh the pair down to around 75.00 in the near term, says Osamu Takashima, the chief FX strategist at Citibank Japan. "Buying back the dollar may temporarily take precedence" after the sharp fall earlier, Takashima adds. "But given the morning's drop, there are many exporter options that were knocked out, so the exporters' dollar-selling, yen-buying pressure will likely increase further from here." Takashima says for the rest of the global day, the pair's topside will be heavy around its previous record low of 79.75, while it could fall back as low as 78.00, compared with last 79.54. (andrew.monahan@dowjones.com)

0100 GMT [Dow Jones] China shares may extend gains, but any upside will likely be capped on concerns over further interest rate hikes in the short term, analysts say. They expect the Shanghai Composite Index to test 2950 resistance after it ends up 1.2% at 2930.80 yesterday. "With fears about Japan's radiation leak fading, Chinese investors will shift focus back to the domestic economic situation," Shanxi Securities says in a note. Analysts tip negative sentiment towards companies that are involved in the nuclear power industry, such as Dongfang Electric (600875.SH) and Sufa Technology Industry (000777.SZ), after China says late yesterday that it halted approvals for new nuclear power plants pending changes to safety standards. The Shenzhen Composite Index ends up 1.1% at 1307.96. (rose.yu@dowjones.com)

0100 GMT [Dow Jones] PREVIEW: India's central bank may continue its monetary tightening as inflation continues to defy attempts to tame it, economists say. The RBI may raise the key lending and borrowing rates by 25 bps each to 6.75% and 5.75% respectively, according to 14 of the 15 economists polled by Dow Jones. "Since crippling growth is not on the agenda, the RBI will likely adopt a 'go-slow' approach from here on"--raising rates only gradually--"unless sharply higher global commodity prices mess up everything," a CLSA research note says. Only one expects a sharper 50bp increase in both rates as inflation increasingly becomes generalized and the RBI "simply cannot afford to remain behind the curve any longer," Religare Capital Markets says. RBI's rate decision is due 0630 GMT Thursday. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0059 GMT [Dow Jones] The KLCI may open lower tracking weak U.S. stocks overnight as worries mounted about Japan's nuclear crisis, a local dealer says. "Yesterday's rebound was in really low volumes, and we are most likely to see another day of broad selling today," the dealer adds. He tips immediate support at 1485, then the Nov. 2010 low of 1474. Wednesday KLCI ended 0.6% higher at 1492.44. Malaysia Airports (5014.KU), or MAHB, may rise strong traffic growth. (ankur.relia@dowjones.com)

0056 GMT [Dow Jones] The Kospi is down 1.1% at 1937.20, tracking the overnight declines in U.S. stocks. Though the market is fearing over the nuclear crisis in neighboring Japan, the recent corrections also provide good buying opportunities considering the fundamentals of local stocks, says Samsung Securities analyst You Seung-min, who tips 1900 support. Most heavyweight stocks are down, with Samsung Electronics (005930.SE) down 1.5% at KRW874,000, Hyundai Motor (005380.SE) off 1.1% at KRW180,000 and LG Chem (051910.SE) down 1.3% at KRW407,000. But shipbuilders ourperform on new order hopes after Samsung Heavy Industries (010140.SE) says late Wednesday it received a KRW1.25 trillion order to build two drilling ships for an unidentified U.S. firm; Samsung Heavy is up 0.3% at KRW36,900, Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering (042660.SE) is up 2.2% at KRW32,400 and Hyundai Heavy Industries (009540.SE) rises 1.6% at KRW460,000. (jieun.shin@dowjones.com)

0053 GMT [Dow Jones] Longer-dated Singapore government bonds may rise, tracking gains in U.S. Treasurys overnight, flattening the yield curve, as concerns over Japan's nuclear crisis and unrest in the Middle East continue driving investors toward safer assets, a trader with a foreign bank says. "Bonds will likely rise with a flatter curve, given the current global situation. (But) I don't think there will be much movement on the short-end, maybe 2 basis points at most." She tips the 10-year bond yield to slide 5-7 bps. On Wednesday, the two-year bond yield fell 1 bp at 0.37%, while the 10-year yield slid 1 bp at 2.30%. (chunhan.wong@dowjones.com) [ 03-16-11 2116ET ]

title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Reverses Earlier Fall; 8,800 Cap Tipped
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0435 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/IDR reverses earlier losses as the sharp fall on the Japanese bourse triggers outflows from other regional stocks, dealers say; the pair is at 8,785 from 8,765 late Monday, after falling to 8,750 earlier in the day. Three dealers suspect Bank Indonesia sold $100 million at 8,790 to slow the dollar's rise. "Bank Indonesia likely intervened once so far today," a dealer says. A 8,760-8,800 range is tipped for the session; Indonesian shares are down 2.1%. (i-made.sentana@dowjones.com)

0430 GMT [Dow Jones] Vietnam shares end down 2.3% at 468.74 as investors continue selling for a second straight session amid concerns that Japan's earthquake will have an impact on the economy as the Japanese market accounts for more than 10% of total Vietnamese exports. "Many players share concerns that the Japanese disaster will have a significant impact here because Japan has been a major donor to many infrastructure development projects here whose funding is likely to be hurt this year," says a Hanoi-based brokerage trader. Among the most actives Saigon Securities (SSI.VH) ended down 0.4% at VND23,600, Sacombank (STB.VH) closed down 1.4% at VND13,700 and Vietinbank (CTG.VH) finished 1.5% higher at VND27,500. Traders predict more losses Wednesday and tip support for the key index at 460. (phammuoi.nguyen@dowjones.com)

0426 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares end lower, reversing from early session gains, amid a substantial decline in other regional bourses. The benchmark PSEi ends off 0.6% at 3896.31, with 102 decliners and 35 advancers while 36 issues were unchanged. "The declines in other markets are quite huge, causing foreign selling in the local market," says Joseph Roxas, Eagle Equities president. Roxas adds the index may stay within a 3850-3950 range Wednesday as the market watches developments in Japan following last week's massive quake. Among the most active stocks Alliance Global (AGI.PH) ended down 2.0% at PHP11.80, Energy Development (EDC.PH) ended up 1.6% at PHP6.18, and Aboitiz Equity (AEV.PH) ended up 0.8% at PHP41.35. (rhea.sandique-carlos@dowjones.com)

0425 GMT [Dow Jones] A fund manager at Aberdeen International Fund Managers says the gainers from the Japan earthquake will be commodities used for reconstruction in the country, picking up some of the slack as China's economy slows. "If there are any gainers, cynically opportunistic though that may sound, they are likely to lie among resource companies such as Rio Tinto (RIO.AU) and BHP (BHP.AU). Japan will need thermal coal and iron ore to boost non-nuclear power alternatives." (nisha.gopalan@dowjones.com)

0422 GMT [Dow Jones] Australia's S&P/ASX 200 index is down 2.7% at 4500.2 after hitting a 6-month low of 4479.7, following an intraday bounce from 4492.4 to 4544.8. Japan's worsening nuclear disaster is fueling extreme volatility amid expected global liquidation of funds by Japanese investors. Japan's Nikkei futures fell more than 16% intraday after Prime Minister Naoto Kan said that an explosion and fire at the Fukushima nuclear power plant had produced a high level of radiation with the danger of further leakage. "People holding long positions are now seeing headlines suggesting this nuclear disaster is really deteriorating," says IG Markets institutional dealer Chris Weston. "If it does blow out to a full meltdown, all hell will break loose." AUD/USD weakness continues to point to offshore selling, with the currency diving to 0.9962 from 1.0097 this morning. The S&P/ASX 200 index is heading for the next support level of 4469.0 (61.8% retracement of the July 2010-February 2011 rise). Former support at 4451-4464 is now expected to offer resistance. (david.rogers1@dowjones.com)

0421 GMT [Dow Jones] The Sensex opens sharply lower and is down 2.5% at 17,971.34, tracking negative cues from the Asian markets after news of further explosions at a nuclear power plant in Japan, which elevates the risk of a spread in radiation. Japan's Nikkei plunges 12.8%. "Investors across the globe are concerned about the collateral damage caused by the crisis situation in Japan," a local analyst says; he adds, "investors are also worried about crude oil prices shooting up again as they view going ahead, there can be an increase in crude oil imports in Japan with disruption in its nuclear generation capacity." But he expects some value buying toward the later half of the trading session in banking and metal stocks; he tips the Sensex in a 17,900-18,350 range intraday. The Sensex's losses are led by autos and metal stocks. Maruti Suzuki (532500.BY) is down 4.0% at INR1,208.50, Tata Steel (500470.BY) is down 3.6% at INR579.30, Reliance Industries (500325.BY) is down 2.4% at INR994.10, Infosys Technologies (500209.BY) is down 2.6% at INR3,020 and ICICI Bank (532174.BY) is down INR2.5% at INR994. (swagata.gupta@dowjones.com)

0421 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/PHP extends its gains as worries over the latest explosion in Japan's troubled nuclear power plant undermines regional bourses and currencies. The pair is at 43.86 from 43.62 earlier today, and after settling at 43.59 late Monday. Traders peg support at 43.50 and resistance at 44.00. "Renewed concerns over Japan has triggered another round of risk aversion. We might see the central bank start to intervene later today to calm the market," a local bank trader says. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0414 GMT [Dow Jones] The USD/INR is near a three-week high as local stocks open deeply negative on souring risk sentiment as Japan struggles to grapple with a nuclear emergency following radiation leaks from a reactor, says a trader at a state-run bank. The pair is at 45.35 after quickly touching a high of 45.37 in early trading, compared with 45.07 late Monday. The Sensex is down 2.6%. "The pair rose sharply in a wild start and seems to stabilizing now, but a further upside to the dollar cannot be ruled out as the threat of a radiation leak spreading across Southeast Asia lurks," he says. He tips the pair in a 45.25-45.45 band for the session. (khushita.vasant@dowjones.com)

0411 GMT [Dow Jones] The HSI is down 3.8% at 22,449.60 midday, although it has recovered from an intraday low of 22,253.47; market volume at half day spikes to HK$60.95 billion, almost matching HK$65.1 billion all of Monday. "Market sentiment is definitely panicky," according to Alvin Cheung, associate director at Prudential Brokerage, as investors are spooked by concerns over a radiation leak at a Japanese nuclear plant. Still, Cheung adds some bargain-hunting has emerged near the 22,200 level, which may act as an intraday support. "There is no need for Hong Kong investors to over-panic, given what I believe is an undemanding valuation for local stocks," Cheung says; he estimates the HSI is trading at a forward 2011 P/E of 13.7X. But the Nikkei's post-midday-break plunge may spur further selling in the local market; the Nikkei is down 14.4%. All 45 blue chips are down. Among the top three losers, Ping An (2318.HK) tumbles 6.7% to HK$76.25 after its share placement, Hang Lung Properties (0101.HK) falls 6.6% to HK$30.55 and Cosco Pacific (1199.HK) is down 6.3% at HK$14.24. (robert.li@dowjones.com)

0410 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares surrender their early gains, tracking the sharp decline in Japan and other regional markets after the latest explosion at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant. The benchmark PSEi is off 0.5% at 3899.97 in moderate volume as decliners beat gainers 105 to 30. Support for the PSEi is pegged at 3850, with resistance at 3950. "I guess we can no longer ignore the losses we're seeing around the region, particularly the Nikkei," says Jomar Lacson, research head at Campos Lunaza and Co. Leading losers are Alliance Global Group (AGI.PH), down 2.0% to PHP11.80 and DMCI Holdings (DMC.PH), down 0.5% to PHP37.75, and Metropolitan Bank & Trust (MBT.PH), down 2.8% at PHP60.30--all of which were gainers earlier in the trading day. (cris.larano@dowjones.com)

0405 GMT [Dow Jones] The Nikkei is down 13% at 8,365.20, falling below 8,500--its lowest intraday level since April 2009--following a double-digit plunge in futures during the midday break on news of a fire at Tokyo Electric Power's (9501.TO) No. 4 reactor at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant in northeastern Japan. Nikkei 225 June futures are now off 17% at 7,820, while Topix futures have been halted at 774.50. Reports said radiation has spiked near the No. 3 reactor. "It's panic selling. It's not only the foreign investors, but everybody just wants to dump shares," says Retela Crea Securities general manager Yosuke Shimizu, putting the Nikkei's next support level at 8,000. All 33 Topix subindexes are down. Tokyo Electric Power, or "Tepco", remains limit-down, ask-only at an indicative price of Y1,221. Honda Motor (7267.TO) is down 7.2% at Y2,873, Toyota Motor (7201.TO) is off 6.9% at Y672. Construction shares, which had enjoyed a surge of buying on Monday on hopes for reconstruction demand in the earthquake and tsunami-affected regions, are also sharply lower, off 15% as a group; general contractor Kajima Corp. (1812.TO) is down 16% at Y217. Sony (6758.TO) is off 13% at Y2,228. The Topix index is off 14% at 730.76. (kana.inagaki@dowjones.com)

0403 GMT [Dow Jones] Lead June JGB futures are sharply higher, rising more than Y1 on-day in the afternoon session, as the Nikkei plunges over 13%; the contract hit 141.17--the highest level since Dec. 8. The benchmark 10-year cash JGB yield could break below the 1.1% mark this week (vs 1.150% currently) as it's hard to predict how the crisis at the crippled nuclear power plants will end up, boosting demand for safe-haven assets, says Deutsche Securities strategist Makoto Yamashita. Also, "there is a risk that, even if the government tries to provide fiscal help (on post-quake reconstruction), production activities and sentiment (among firms and households) will deteriorate sharply," he adds. (megumi.fujikawa@dowjones.com) [ 03-15-11 0035ET ]

1. The EU has adopted a Directive regarding the taxation of savings income (the "Savings Directive"). The Savings Directive requires Member States (as defined below) to provide to the tax authorities of other Member States details of payments of interest and other similar income paid by a person to an individual in another Member State, except that Austria and Luxembourg will instead impose a withholding system for a transitional period unless during such period they elect otherwise.

The Bank undertakes that it will ensure that it maintains a paying agent in a country which is a member of the European Union (a "Member State") that will not be obliged to withhold or deduct tax pursuant to the Savings Directive.
