title: EM ASIA  FX -Won leads slide; c.banks support rupiah, peso
text:
* Dollar/won NDFs jump, won vols pick up

 * C.banks in Indonesia, Philippines intervene

 * Swiss c.bank intervenes to weaken its currency

 * Investors jittery ahead of U.S. jobs data, G7

 By Kevin Yao

 SINGAPORE, Feb 5 (Reuters) - The South Korean won led Asian currencies lower on Friday as investors dumped riskier assets on jitters over debt problems in Europe, prompting central banks in Indonesia and the Philippines to intervene to support their currencies.

 Asian stocks dipped, while dollar extended its gains from the previous day due to investor anxiety about sovereign debt in Greece, Portugal and Spain sparked a sell-off in the euro.

 But the euro leapt against the Swiss franc as the Swiss central bank intervened to weaken its own currency. The ero earlier plunged to a 15-month low against the franc <EURCHF=>. [ID:nTOE614043]

 Weakness in the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso prompted their central banks to intervene, traders said.

"I would place them in the category of Asian central banks that are genuinely concerned about volatility of their illiquid currencies so would not be at all surprised if they stepped in to calm rupiah and peso on what is a very nervous count-down to payrolls," said Westpaccurrency strategist Sean Callow.

 Asian central banks usually intervene by buying dollars to limit the rise in their currencies to support local exporters, but also step in to smooth sharp currency falls.

 WON

 The spot won <KRW=> tumbled about 2 percent in early trade to 1,176.9 per dollar but later steadied near 1,170.

 The won, which has lost more than 4 percent since Jan. 11, faces further weakness after a dip below the 100-day moving average at 1,162 on Friday.

 Offshore dollar/won NDFs <KRWNDFOR=> jumped amid jitters over sovereign debt risks in Europe, but they later trimmed gains as Korean exporters start selling.

 One-month NDFs steadied near 1,170 after hitting as high as 1,178.6 compared to Thursday's close at 1,174.

 "We see strong selling by exporters, funds are staying aside now. It was a drama last night, with euro collapsing and everything squeezed. I think all want to take a breath before U.S. non-farm payrolls and G7 meeting this weekend," said a Singapore-based NDF trader.

 Manwhile, won's implied volatilities <KRWVOL> hit 15 percent from 14 percent on Thursday as the spot dips.

 "Won vols are well bid as dollar/won moves higher," said an option trader.

 RUPIAH, PESO

 The high-yielding rupiah <IDR=> fell as far as 9,410 per dollar -- down 1 percent from Thursday's close -- as traders spotted official intervention to support the unit.

 "BI (the central bank) is interferring in the market just to stabilise the rupiah -- they are selling dollars at 9,410," said a trader in Jakarta.

 The Philippine peso <PHP=> shed 0.8 percent to 46.53 per dollar.

 "We suspect the central bank was selling dollars at today's high," said a trader in Manila.

After a fairly uneventful US session Monday, the USD and JPY gained strongly in Asia on safety flows amid reports China was putting into place last week's reported lending curbs on certain banks. USD/JPY slumped to a fresh one-month low of 89.53, EUR/JPY a near 9-month low of 126.12 and EUR/USD lost a cent to 1.4071. For Tuesday UK GDP and German Ifo grab attention but keep an eye on equities, the Nikkei shed 1.7%, China 2.4% and Europe is heading toward a 1% loss, all of which could further damage risk appetite and give the JPY and USD more upside potential. title: WRAPUP 1-Asian c.banks scramble to contain  currency  strength
text:
* Intervention seen in S.Korea, Indonesia, India, Singapore

* Korean official vows further action on won, if necessary

* Concerns that rapid currency gains may hurt recovery

By Kevin Yao

SINGAPORE, Jan 11 (Reuters) - Several Asian central banks intervened on Monday in an effort to temper the rally in their currencies as the dollar weakened broadly, highlighting fears that rapid currency rises may hurt economic recovery.

Central banks in South Korea, Indonesia, India and Singapore were spotted buying U.S. dollars to contain their currencies, driven up by the dollar's weakness and expectations that China's strong exports data may prod Beijing to allow the yuan to rise.

"I think Asian central banks are watching the pace of currency appreciation," said Thio Chin Loo, currency strategist at BNP Paribas in Singapore. "They are cautiously optimistic about the economy and don't want to prick the nascent recovery."

In a sign that concerns over strengthening currencies were not unique for emerging markets, the head of Swiss National Bank said on Monday that the central bank will fight any excessive rise of the Swiss franc against the euro, hinting at a possible intervention.

In Seoul, a senior finance ministry official, speaking after the authorities were seen buying dollars, warned that the authorities would act further to temper the won if necessary.

"We are worried that the foreign exchange market is leaning excessively one way," Kim Ik-joo, head of the ministry's international finance bureau, told Reuters.

"We are closely watching foreign exchange rates and we will take proper measures if necessary," Kim said.

Dealers said, the authorities tried to prevent the won from rising past the 1,200-per dollar level, though the currency briefly hit 1,114.9 per dollar, its strongest in more than 15 months, and closed on the stronger side of the 1,200 mark.

The won has gained 4 percent against the dollar so far this month, making it the top performer among nine emerging Asian currencies tracked by Reuters.

The rising won also intensified purchases of Korean bonds by foreigners, along with the view that rate rises will be slower coming in the year ahead, with the buying, in turn, pushing the won further up.

Confronted with a steady stream of investment funds betting that Asia will continue to lead the global economic upturn, the region's authorities have been using both verbal and market intervention to cool of the pressure on their currencies.

Taiwan went a step further last week, unveiling new controls to curb speculative inflows, giving foreign short-term investors betting on currency gains a week to invest their funds in stocks or pull out.

In Indonesia, the authorities were also spotted trying to stem the rise of the high-yielding rupiah, which jumped as much as 1 percent on Monday, and the central bank said it would keep on buying dollars to rein in its currency.

In Singapore, the central bank was also seen buying dollars as the Singapore dollar hit a one-month high and in India, state-run banks were spotted buying the U.S. currency after the rupee rose 1 percent to its highest in more than 15 months.

The rupiah has gained 3 percent against the dollar so far this month, making it the second best performer in Asia. (Additional reporting by Vidya Ranganathan in SINGAPORE, Lee Soo-jung in SEOUL and Swati Bhat in MUMBAI; Editing by Tomasz Janowski)

title: EM ASIA  FX -Ringgit, peso near 16-mth highs on dlr woes, China
text:
* Dollar slide after poor jobs data spurs Asian currencies

* Ringgit jumps over 1 pct, breaks key resistance at 3.35

* Peso gains 0.7 pct to highest since Aug. 2008

* Rupiah's rise sparks official intervention

* Yuan NDFs imply faster yuan rise after trade data

By Kevin Yao

SINGAPORE, Jan 11 (Reuters) - The Malaysian ringgit and Philippine peso hit their highest levels in almost 16 months on Monday as the dollar faltered and Chinese data raised hopes of yuan gains, while Indonesia's central bank intervened to slow the rise in the rupiah.

Asian stocks hit a 17-month high as a strong rebound in China's exports raised optimism about the region's economic outlook, while the dollar suffered its biggest fall in six weeks in the wake of disappointing U.S. jobs data. [ID:nTOE60A009] [IDnSGE60A03L]

RINGGIT

One-month dollar/ringgit non-deliverable forwards <MYRNDFOR=> slid to 3.3320, the lowest since Aug. 2008 and largely at par with the spot, as offshore investors scrambled to shed long dollar positions.

"The market was caught long (on USD) from last Friday," said a Singapore-based dealer.

The spot ringgit <MYR=> jumped as much as 1.3 percent to 3.3325, breaking key resistance at 3.35.

"Investors are squaring their cross/ringgit positions and so far we see only hedging flows on cross/ringgit here," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.

PESO

The peso <PHP=> gained 0.7 percent at 45.48, its highest in nearly 16 months.

"The peso is gaining ground on the strong Chinese trade data. It's likely that successive positive data should have China moving towards strengthening the yuan, and the regionals should follow," said a dealer in Manila.

Traders say the peso was being driven more by fund inflows by institutions as the wave of remittance inflows seen in Dec. has passed.

One-month dollar/peso NDFs <PHP1MNDFOR=> fell from Friday's close of 45.78 to to 45.65, lowst since Aug. 2008.

RUPIAH

Despite suspected intervention by the central bank, the high-yielding rupiah <IDR=> jumped 1 percent to 9,120 per dollar.

"BI (the central bank) does not want the rupiah to move too fast," said a trader in Jakarta.

The currency has gained 3.3 percent against the dollar so far this month, making it the second best preformer among the nine regional currencies tracked by Reuters.

Meanwhile, Indonesian bond yields dropped on falling dollar/rupiah and upbeat comments by PIMCO, the world's biggest fund manager.

Chia-Liang Lian, a fund manager at Pacific investment Management Co, said Indonesian local debt was attractive due to its yield appeal versus other markets. [ID:nTOE60A01T].

YUAN

The benchmark offshore one-year NDFs <CNY1YNDFOR=> fell sharply to a two-month low, implying more yuan appreciation in 12 months after China posted strong foreign trade data over the weekend.

The NDFs hit 6.585, down from Friday's close of 6.607, its lowest level since Nov. 13.

Twelve-month yuan appreciation implied by NDFs rose to 3.70 percent measured from the Chinese central bank's daily mid-point, compared with 3.34 percent implied at Friday's close.

Expectations that Beijing may unshackle the yuan from a dollar peg gained steam after China's data showed exports leapt 17.7 percent from a year earlier, dwarfing the 4.0 percent rise forecast by economists and breaking a 13-month streak of year-on-year declines. [ID:nSGE60A016]

title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Lower Late: May Head Higher Fri
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0854 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR lower at 9,235 in late session vs 9,275 late yesterday on capital inflows, but suspected Bank Indonesia intervention helps slow pair's slide, dealers say; central bank suspected of buying around $10 million earlier today, with acting governor Darmin Nasution saying IDR's recent appreciation "quite fast." "Profit taking against the rupiah may emerge Friday ahead of the weekend, which will lift the dollar higher," says local dealer; 9,220-9,280 range tipped tomorrow. (IMS)

0848 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/HUF is trading in a tight range Thursday, amid lackluster trade, traders say. EUR/HUF is at 269.0 versus 268.50 earlier in the morning, and 268.70 Wednesday afternoon. Commerzbank notes negative news from Iceland leaves HUF unfazed, unlike previous occasions. Raiffeisen says even reviving Greek fiscal worries have failed to depress HUF, unlike at the end of 2009. Both expect tight EUR/HUF trading range to persist, Raiffeisen sees the cross trading between 267.25 and 279.85 Thursday. (MAF)

0846 GMT [Dow Jones] The Turkish lira and bonds are stronger as investors take profits in the stock market and shift to bonds and foreign exchange markets. USD/TRY trades at 1.4730 from 1.4760 Wednesday, while the benchmark August 3, 2011 bond trades at 8.86% from 8.94% Wednesday. Analysts say any developments on a new IMF loan deal and US jobless claims data due 1330 GMT will be important for direction. They forecast TRY to trade between 1.4650 and 1.4820 and the benchmark bond to trade between 8.83% and 8.9%, in the short term. (IHA)

0845 GMT [Dow Jones] French government bonds OAT April 2018 and October 2023, both on offer along with two other series, are likely to be issued in response to dealer demand, and should go well, say Barclays Capital strategist Huw Worthington and Cagdas Aksu. The October 2019 and April 2041 bonds, which are also on offer, are looking "good value" versus their German equivalents, they say. "Overall we expect the auctions to go relatively well." Auction results are due at 0950 GMT. (BEM)

0844 GMT [Dow Jones] The sharp improvement in Hungary's January-September current account will continue in 4Q, a positive for the HUF provided a benign external risk environment, says ING. A 2009 balance of payments surplus will support further cautious rate cuts in January/February, before the expected pause around the April parliamentary elections. Notes imports will eventually bounce back once domestic demand recovers, but with a tighter fiscal policy this shouldn't lead to an excessive current account deficit widening and should also be offset by a recovery in exports. (MAF)

0843 GMT [Dow Jones] The Swiss franc may well have strengthened to a post-SNB-intervention high against the euro overnight; however, Nick Hasting's Forex Focus argues that the franc may start to self-correct without the SNB's help. (GST)

0840 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/PHP lower at 45.83 vs 46.01 late Wednesday, retreating to fresh 16-month low in absence of new market direction; pair may continue range trading Friday, says local bank trader, may stay within 45.75-46.00 band. "I would prefer to buy on dips," adds trader. (RSA)

0838 GMT [Dow Jones] The pound is under pressure again, but this time from politics and not deficit worries. On Wednesday two Labour back-benchers called for a secret ballot on PM Brown's leadership. Standard Bank's Steve Barrow says the news has so far done only collateral damage to the pound but there could be a lot more damage ahead as the political fighting, not to mention infighting, escalates ahead of the upcoming election, which much be held by June 2010. GBP/USD has just printed a fresh one week low of 1.5936, EUR/GBP a one week high of 0.9024. (GST)

0833 GMT [Dow Jones] Societe Generale expects good demand at France's OAT auction Thursday, despite the large amount, EUR7.5 billion to EUR9 billion, to be issued. The Oct. 2019 and April 2041 OATs, both among the OATs on offer, are cheap relative to the curve, it says, adding "we also like the 30-year OAT relative to [Dutch government bond] DSL." Auction results are due at 0950 GMT. (BEM)

0831 GMT [Dow Jones] Newly installed Japanese Finance Minister Naoto Kan makes his presence felt early with comments on his first day in the job that he would like to see a weak JPY. He even went as far as to quote a level, saying that many Japanese firms were in favor of the dollar being around Y95.00, USD/JPY spiked some 60 sen on his comments to the day's high of 92.88, it now trades at 92.73. (GST)

0828 GMT [Dow Jones] Gilts open lower Thursday ahead of the BOE rate decision, due 1200 GMT. Although, no change is expected from the meeting and underperformance is likely to continue, thinks Peter Schaffrik, Commerzbank strategist. "Something is rotten in the state of Great Britain. Again, government credibility is at the heart of the current market fears," he says. Calls for a secret leadership ballot hardly helped on Wednesday and after Pimco's negative comments on the asset class earlier in the week, gilts have few positives. Elsewhere, US jobless claims are due at 1330 GMT but Friday's US nonfarm payrolls is this week's main focus. The gilt yield curve steepens, with the 2-year/10-year benchmark spread widening to +279.1 bps from Wednesday's +277.5 bps. The March gilt futures contract is currently down 0.30 on the day at 113.74. The 10-year benchmark gilt down 0.30 n the day at 103.134, yielding 4.085%. (NKA)

0825 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/INR slips to new 1-year low as exporter selling hits spot, forwards market hard, exporters using every support to dump dollar exposures, says foreign bank trader. Pair at 45.69 vs 45.81 earlier, 45.86 late Wednesday, while 1-year forward premium at 1.06 vs 1.14 late Wednesday "It's a one-way street. There's no telling where this could end," says trader. Notes, pair had nipped above key 45.80 support earlier in session, but large German bank set ball rolling by dumping dollars sparking widespread bout of selling. Adds, pair may find support at 45.60 within session, but may continue to drift lower to test 45.00 over next few sessions. (BIJ) [ 01-07-10 0354ET ]

title: Bank  Indonesia  Likely  Intervenes  To Support Dollar - Dealers
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market Tuesday to support the dollar after the rupiah strengthened sharply, currency dealers said.

Bank Indonesia likely bought a total of $200 million over the morning and afternoon sessions between IDR9,290 and IDR9,320 after inflows to local high-yielding assets boosted the rupiah, the dealers estimated.

title: Bank  Indonesia  Likely  Intervenes  To Support Dollar - Dealers
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market Tuesday to cap a sharp rise in the rupiah as investors bought local assets, currency dealers said.

Bank Indonesia was suspected to have bought $100 million to $150 million between IDR9,290 and IDR9,305 to slow the rupiah's rise, the dealers said.

The dollar regained some ground to trade at IDR9,305 at 0322 GMT. The U.S. currency's session low of IDR9,290 was its weakest since Oct. 15, 2009, according to central bank data. On Monday, the dollar fetched IDR9,340.

The rupiah has strengthened sharply since the New Year break as investors were attracted to local high-yielding assets, such as stocks and the central bank's Sertifikat Bank Indonesia short-term notes.

The investors were buying local assets to bet on a relatively strong domestic economy and low inflation this year, market participants said.

-By Reuben Carder, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 3983 1277; Reuben.Carder@dowjones.com [ 05-01-10 0334GMT ]

title: Bank Indonesia Likely Sells $10M At IDR9,505-IDR9,515 -Traders
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Indonesian central bank likely sold the U.S. dollar in early trade Wednesday to prevent the rupiah from weakening sharply, currency traders said.

Bank Indonesia likely sold around $10 million between IDR9,505 and IDR9,515 as the dollar's overnight gains and dollar buying by local investors to fund year-end payments pushed that currency higher.

The dollar retreated from a high of IDR9,515 following the suspected intervention, and was trading at IDR9,510 around 0125 GMT. The dollar fetched IDR9,495 in late Asian trade Tuesday.

"It looks like they're trying to bring (the dollar-rupiah level) back below IDR9,500," one trader at a foreign bank said.

Bank Indonesia's suspected intervention, he said, was relatively small as liquidity is thin ahead of the holiday period.

Traders said the dollar is likely to trade between IDR9,490 and IDR9,520 for the rest of the day.

-By Reuben Carder, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 3983 1277; Reuben.Carder@dowjones.com [ 23-12-09 0139GMT ]

0941 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia shares end +0.3% at 2474.833 in light volume, off intraday low of 2458.148, tracking gains across Asian markets after stocks in U.S. end higher overnight. "Foreign buying helped improve overall sentiment here despite selling by most local retailers ahead of long weekend," says trader at Valbury Securities; expects shares to gain Monday on year-end window dressing; tips resistance at 2500. Indonesian markets will be closed Thursday and Friday for Christmas holiday. Among gainers: gas distributor Gas Negara (PGAS.JK) +2.0% at IDR3,825, cement maker Indocement (INTP.JK) +3.1% at IDR13,300. Profit-taking hits bellwether Telkom (TLKM.JK) down 1.0% at IDR9,600. (EDH)

0937 GMT [Dow Jones] India interest rate swaps trade lower as market pushes back expectations of potential RBI tightening moves, but no major moves in market as many traders avoid taking on heavy positions in holiday season, says state-run bank trader; 1-year OIS at 5.02%/5.06% vs 5.04%/5.08% last close, 5-year OIS at 6.83%/6.87% vs 6.86%/6.90%. "Rates could well (move) further down as rate hikes now seem relatively further away, but the volumes just aren't big enough to unwind at one go without taking that impact cost," says dealer. Tips rates to slowly drift lower, 1-year OIS may slip by 10 bps over next few sessions unless new cues come in. (BIJ)

0934 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia shares end steady, with benchmark KLCI +0.11 points at 1,260.53 in thin volume of 338 million shares traded. Dealer with local bank backed brokerage says index traded within tight range but mainly in negative territory before mild bargain hunting pushed some heavyweight stocks higher late. Market breadth marginally negative with 282 decliners vs 268 advancers. "The 1,260-1,262 levels (50-day moving average) (turned out) to be a key resistance today... charts indicate further weakness," dealer adds. Tips 1,250-1,265 range tomorrow. Advancers include Hai-O (7668.KU) +4.7% at MYR7.85, Proton (5304.KU) +3.7% at MYR3.95, SP Setia (8664.KU) +2.2% at MYR3.68. Decliners were EON Capital (5266.KU) down 2.9% at MYR6.80, IJM (3336.KU) down 2.9% at MYR4.32, Gamuda (5398.KU) down 1.9% at MYR2.61. (KPL)

0929 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB higher at 33.34 vs 33.255 late yesterday amid broadly positive USD tone. Buying from interbank players helping propel USD, but Bangkok-based dealer says "there are still quite a lot of exporters trying to sell (USD) before year-end." Adds exporters offloading USD at 33.33-33.34 today. Pair remains biased upwards though some expect USD strength to be short-lived; 33.30-33.40 range tipped tomorrow. (LHM)

0926 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan government bond prices will likely plunge tomorrow as government surprises market with larger than expected 1Q issuance of NT$190 billion (expected NT$150 billion), out of which NT$70 billion is in 20-, 30-year bonds, for which demand may come only from insurers, says local bank trader, adds amount for 20-year bond (NT$40 billion) also larger than expected; 30-year bond sale is first since 2004. "I don't think insurers will be able to digest this much and this will be reflected in the yields," he says; expects yield curve to steepen at long end. Yield on benchmark 10-year bond to range at 1.50%-1.55% vs today's close 1.4822%, 20-year may jump to 2.10%-2.17% vs 2.0790%. (ABP)

0922 GMT [Dow Jones] AUD/USD could slide toward 0.85 and NZD/USD 0.67 says UniCredit but such moves will offer a buying opportunity. That's because in the New Year the bank says it expects more risk appetite to favor the Pacific Rim currencies and carry trade strategies. AUD/USD now trades at 0.8755, NZD/USD at 0.70. (GST)

0922 GMT [Dow Jones](An item at 0551 GMT misstated the date when the index last ended higher, while the headline also misstated the index highs. The correct version is as follows:) Taiwan shares settle 0.6% higher at 7,901.50, best settlement since June 20, 2008's 7,902.44, led mainly by electronics titles' 1.0% gain as investors bet shipment growth to remain strong through Lunar New Year holiday, says KGI Securities trader Randy Chang. Index hit as high as 7,910.88, but failed to rise further in part because most foreign investors already on holidays. "People are buying hopes...for a better 2010." Hon Hai (2317.TW) gains 2.9% to NT$144.5 on biggest volume since late October as investors expect company's 2010 profit growth to accelerate with three-way merger of its units Innolux, Chi Mei and TPO. Nanya Technology (2408.TW) limit up 7% at NT$24.90. Daiwa Securities SMBC analysts Jae Lee and Pranab Kumar Sarmah say Nanya among their favorite DRAM names on expectation cyclical recovery in memory-chip industry will continue throughout 2010. For rest of year, Chang tips 7,800-8,000 band. (PEL)

0919 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR slightly higher late at 9,500 vs 9,495 late yesterday, but off 9,515 intraday high after suspected central bank intervention, late USD selling. Bank Indonesia spotted selling total of $15 million-$20 million over both morning and afternoon sessions to cap rise in pair on broad USD strength, year-end USD buying by local corporates; local exporters also eyed offloading excess USD in afternoon session, helping pair ease from highs. Underlying tone to stay bid tomorrow ahead of trading holiday Friday, but Bank Indonesia likely guard upside, limiting pair in narrow 9,490-9,510 range, dealers say. (RLC)

0917 GMT [Dow Jones] Malaysia consumer prices fell 0.1% on year in November on high base effect vs median 0.2% drop expected in Dow Jones poll of 10 economists. "The CPI numbers are very much within expectations...the index will likely turn positive this month" on year-end holiday spending, lower base in December 2008, says economist with local brokerage. Still, inflation "likely benign" in 2010, says economist, with no pressure on central bank to hike rates early. Statistics Department says November's decrease due to lower transportation costs (down 6.8% on year) but food and non-alchoholic beverages +0.9% on year. CPI rose 0.3% on-month in November. For January-November period, index +0.5% on year; economist says full year inflation likely less than official forecast of +1.0%. CPI grew 5.4% in 2008. (KPL)

0914 GMT [Dow Jones] Sterling slips to the day's lows ahead of the 0930 GMT BOE December minutes release. UK press speculation that more QE or a change in the deposit rate may have been discussed are factors weighing on the pound Wednesday. GBP/USD trades at 1.5940, just off Tuesday's 2-month low of 1.5924 while EUR/GBP is just a couple of ticks under Tuesday's one-week high of 0.8945. (GST)

0908 GMT [Dow Jones] USD is hardly changed with a little scattered profit-taking as trading dries up ahead of Christmas. With Japan closed, turnover has slumped but the general mood remains positive with European stocks opening higher. USD is expected to remain well supported with more positive economic news likely later Wednesday, following Tuesday's strong rise in existing home sales. USD is flat at Y91.81 while EUR is also hardly changed at $1.4251. GBP is down at $1.5949 as the market waits for the latest Bank of England minutes. (NEH)

0907 GMT [Dow Jones] French consumer spending in November was mostly supported by the government's car scrapping scheme, says UniCredit's economist Tullia Bucco. She says households made the most of the program, which will end in January. "Today's outcome lifts spending on manufactured goods more than 2% above the 3Q average, pointing to a sizeable contribution to 4Q private consumption." She sees GDP +0.5 to +0.6% in 4Q, after the disappointing performance recorded in 3Q. "However, looking ahead, this pace of GDP growth looks hardly sustainable in the coming quarters, when government stimulus measures will fade or will become decisively less supportive." (GAM) [ 12-23-09 0441ET ]

title: UPDATE: Bank  Indonesia  Has "No Choice" But To Continue With  FX Intervention
text:
(Adds comment from Bank Indonesia's acting governor and background.)

By Reuben Carder and Costas Paris

OF DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia has "no choice" but to continue intervening in the foreign exchange market to stabilize the dollar-rupiah rate, and is likely to raise its policy rate in the first or second quarter next year as price pressures increase, a person familiar with the situation said Friday.

The person told Dow Jones Newswires that the benchmark rate is likely to be raised from the current 6.50% in the first or second quarter of next year. The timing and size of the hikes will depend on inflation, he said, which the central bank anticipates will be driven by rising domestic demand, as well as higher prices for commodities and crude oil.

Separately, Bank Indonesia's acting governor Darmin Nasution said later Friday that inflationary pressures in Indonesia are expected to increase in the second quarter of next year.

Nasution reiterated an earlier forecast that annual inflation this year is likely to be around 2.9%, softer than last year's 11.1%. Indonesia uses the on-year price increase in December as its annual inflation rate.

Besides the high-base effect last year, easing energy and commodity prices around the world as well as the rupiah's appreciation of around 15% so far this year have brought inflation to its lowest levels in many years.

Bank Indonesia officials didn't specify the size of the central bank's foreign exchange interventions. Market participants estimate Bank Indonesia has bought or sold dollars on many occasions this year--often as much as $100 million or more in a single day--to cap sharp dollar-rupiah movements amid volatility in regional currencies. Bank Indonesia doesn't generally target a specific exchange rate.

Indonesia's Chamber of Commerce and Industry has pressured Bank Indonesia to cut rates further from the current record-low level to give extra impetus to the economy, but the central bank doesn't consider there's enough room for more cuts, the person said. The central bank has cut a total of 300 basis points since it started easing in December 2008.

The Chamber of Commerce didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The person added that the central bank is of the view that the high inflation base effect from 2008 has yet to dissipate.

The government in mid-2008 raised retail fuel prices by an average of 30%, sending inflation to multiyear highs. The high base effect, and a downturn in the domestic economy, are likely to reduce Indonesia's inflation rate to a record low of 3.5% or less this year, officials have previously said.

-By Costas Paris and Reuben Carder, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 3983 1277; Reuben.Carder@dowjones.com [ 11-12-09 0819GMT ]

title: Indonesian c.bank  intervenes  to defend rupiah-traders
text:
SINGAPORE, Dec 9 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bankintervened on Wednesday to support the rupiah, trying to set a floor near the 9,500 per dollar level, traders said.

 "BI (the central bank) has been selling dollars from the market opening," said a dealer in Jakarta.

 The high-yielding rupiah <IDR=> fell 0.6 percent to 9,495 to the dollar due to concerns about debt woes for Greece and Dubai, but it later stablised as local exporters also sold dollars, traders said.

 The rupiah is up 16 percent against the dollar this year, making it the best-performing currency in Asia. Indonesian officials have predicted it will strengthen further next year.  (Reporting by Kevin Yao; Editing by Neil Fullick)

title: UPDATE: Bank  Indonesia : Local Dollar Demand Outstrips Supply
text:
(Adds suspected intervention, background)


 
    By I Made Sentana 
    Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Demand for the U.S. dollar in Indonesia's foreign-exchange market is greater than the available supply at the moment, a central bank official said Monday, suggesting that Bank Indonesia won't try to slow capital inflows that have boosted values of local assets this year.

The central bank will, however, guard against volatility in the dollar-rupiah exchange rate ahead of expected capital inflows into emerging-market assets next year, Deputy Governor Budi Mulya said on the sidelines of a seminar when asked whether Bank Indonesia would consider curbing short-term capital inflows.

"The characteristics of our market are different" from those of other countries (that have moved to curb inflows)," he said on the sidelines of a seminar.

"In the local market, there is still excess demand" for dollars, he said.

His remark indicates that the central bank views inflows of capital as necessary to meet market demand for the dollar. U.S. dollar liquidity in the country is quite low due to massive fund outflows that occurred late last year.

The domestic economy's relatively strong performance and improving political stability have, however, attracted capital inflows of late. The rupiah has gained more than 15% against the dollar since January, while the benchmark stock index is up around 80%.

The market was abuzz with speculation last month that Bank Indonesia would move to limit inflows of short-term funds after Deputy Governor Hartadi Sarwono said the central bank would study the pros and cons of limiting foreign ownership in its short-term notes. Sarwono later said that the central bank wouldn't implement such a policy.

Mulya reiterated Monday that Bank Indonesia will maintain its current policy on exchange-rate movements. From time to time, the central bank sells the U.S. dollar against the rupiah, and vice versa, to cap sharp moves in the exchange rate.

Earlier Monday, Bank Indonesia was thought to have sold $25 million to $50 million between IDR9,460 and IDR9,465 to head off weakness in the rupiah as upbeat U.S. November employment data gave the dollar a boost against regional currencies.

A 0.6% fall in local stocks and dollar-buying by local companies to pay year-end debts added to the local unit's weakness, currency dealers said.

The dollar retreated to IDR9,455 following the suspected intervention from an intraday peak of IDR9,465. The dollar fetched IDR9,415 late Friday.

Currency dealers said that the market wasn't affected by Mulya's subsequent remarks on demand for the U.S. dollar as those were in line with market expectations.

-By I Made Sentana, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 3983 1277; I-Made.Sentana@dowjones.com (Reuben Carder contributed to this article) [ 07-12-09 0530GMT ]

title: UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Defends Rupiah; Likely Sold $50m-$100M
text:
(Updates rupiah level, adds background)

By Reuben Carder

Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia was suspected to have intervened to slow the rupiah's fall Thursday when several other regional central banks were reportedly trying to rein in their surging currencies.

Bank Indonesia likely sold between $50 million and $100 million between IDR9,450 and IDR9,460 to prevent the rupiah from falling too sharply during the afternoon session, the dealers said. They attributed the rupiah's weakness to a comeback by the dollar against the majors and a fall in the domestic stock market, which lost 2.8%.

Monetary authorities in the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore and South Korea appeared to sell their currencies Thursday, fending off a slide in the dollar that threatens their export-oriented economies. Their interventions were, however, small, traders said.

The domestic central bank was "just leveling out the movements" in the market rather than protecting a specific level, a dealer said. Dealers said liquidity was thin ahead of an Islamic holiday Friday, exaggerating the market's movements.

Bank Indonesia doesn't target a level for the rupiah, but prefers a stronger local unit to help fight imported inflation and to support capital-goods imports. It intervenes in the market from time to time to cap excess volatility.

The dollar opened the day's domestic trading session at IDR9,365, compared with IDR9,400 in late Asian trade Wednesday. It rose to a high of IDR9,460 during the afternoon session before easing to IDR9,445 subsequently.

One currency dealer said that Bank Indonesia will probably be comfortable letting the dollar fall to around IDR9,200 for now and isn't likely to prop up the dollar as long as it stays above that level.

General Information 
Additional Information regarding the Notes 
1.    The EU has adopted a Directive regarding the taxation of savings income 
(the "Savings Directive"). The Savings Directive requires Member States (as 
defined below) to provide to the tax authorities of other Member States details 
of payments of interest and other similar income paid by a person to an 
individual in another Member State, except that Austria, Belgium and Luxembourg 
will instead impose a withholding system for a transitional period unless during 
such period they elect otherwise. 
 
 
The Bank undertakes that it will ensure that it maintains a paying agent in a 
country which is a member of the European Union (a "Member State") that will not 
be obliged to withhold or deduct tax pursuant to the Savings Directive.

    C) Due to a change in law since the date of the Prospectus, the second

    D) Due to a change in law since the date of the Prospectus, the fourth

3.Noteholders should consult their own tax advisors concerning the consequences

4.    Additional Investment Considerations: 
 
 
The Notes offered by this Pricing Supplement are complex financial instruments 
and may not be suitable for certain investors. Investors intending to purchase 
the Notes should consult with their tax and financial advisors to ensure that 
the intended purchase meets the investment objective before making such 
purchase. 
 
 
There are various risks associated with the Notes including, but not limited to, 
exchange rate risk, price risk and liquidity risk. Investors should consult with 
their own financial, legal and accounting advisors about the risks associated

investment, and the suitability of the investment in each investor's particular 
circumstances. Holders of the Notes should also consult with their professional 
tax advisors regarding tax laws applicable to them. 
 
 
The Bank will hedge its obligations under the Notes by entering into a swap 
transaction with an affiliate of the Dealer as swap counterparty. Assuming no 
change in market conditions or any other relevant factors, the price, if any, at 
which the Dealer or another purchaser might be willing to purchase Notes in a 
secondary market transaction is expected to be lower, and could be substantially 
lower, than the original issue price of the Notes. This is due to a number of 
factors, including that (i) the potential profit to the secondary market 
purchaser of the Notes may be incorporated into any offered price and (ii) the 
cost of funding used to value the Notes in the secondary market is expected to 
be higher than our actual cost of funding incurred in connection with the 
issuance of the Notes. In addition, the original issue price of the Notes 
included, and secondary market prices are likely to exclude, the projected 
profit that our swap counterparty or its affiliates may realize in connection 
with this swap. Further, as a result of dealer discounts, mark-ups or other 
transaction costs, any of which may be significant, the original issue price may 
differ from values determined by pricing models used by our swap counterparty or 
other potential purchasers of the Notes in secondary market transactions. 
 
 
Payment of each Interest Amount and the Redemption Amount will be based on the 
IDR Rate, which is a measure of the rate of exchange between the Indonesian 
Rupiah and the USD. Currency exchange rates are volatile and will affect the

intervene in the foreign exchange market. These interventions or other 
governmental actions could adversely affect the value of the Notes, as well as

acceleration. Even in the absence of governmental action directly affecting 
currency exchange rates, political or economic developments in Indonesia or 
elsewhere could lead to significant and sudden changes in the exchange rate 
between the Indonesian Rupiah and the USD. 
 
 
The Indonesian Rupiah is an emerging market currency. Emerging market currencies

title: MARKET TALK: USD/IDR Higher; Tipped In 9,550-9,650 Range
text:
Contact us in Singapore. 65 64154 140; 
MarketTalk@dowjones.com 
 
 

0145 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR higher at 9,590 vs 9,560 late yesterday as risk aversion resurfaces and foreign players still spooked by talk of possible measures taken by Bank Indonesia to limit short-term fund inflows, dealers say. Barclays Capital says if Bank Indonesia imposes restrictions on foreign holdings of SBI paper, measures would result in moderate, albeit temporary, demand for USD; "however, in our view, the underlying trend will remain IDR positive." Cautions against a sanguine view that Bank Indonesia won't act - for instance, it could prevent foreign investors from rolling existing positions in SBI and entering new ones. Dealers peg USD/IDR in 9,550-9,650 range, expecting Bank Indonesia to intervene later today.(IMS)

0142 GMT [Dow Jones] Korea treasury bonds little moved in early trade, while futures trading with moderate losses as foreigners snap 14-session buying streak and reverse into net-sellers; 3-year yield +1 bp at 4.25%, 5-year yield down 1 bp at 4.77%, December futures down 5 ticks at 109.70, with foreigners selling 1,406 contracts in net so far today. "Other than foreign selling in futures, the overall favorable atmosphere for bonds hasn't changed much, while weaker domestic stocks will likely help sentiment," says Daishin Securities analyst Jeong Im-bo. Tips 3-year yield in 4.20%-4.30% range for day. Notes, longer end bonds may perform well, given their attractive yields. Whether foreigners increase net selling volume in futures or not could be key, though Jeong doesn't expect any aggressive selling. (MJL)

0141 GMT [Dow Jones] Taiwan shares last down 0.4% at 7732.64 on weak U.S., regional shares, led by electronics stocks (down 0.5%) on profit taking, weakness in U.S. techs. LCD maker Chi Mei Optoelectronics (3009.TW) down 1.0% at NT$20.60 after strong gains this week on Innolux Display's (3481.TW) acquisition. Selling only mild; "investors know the government will not let local shares fall much before the municipal government elections (early next month)," says Hua Nan Securities Investment Management trader Henry Miao. Expects main index to consolidate in 7700-7760 band rest of session in absence of major leads. Central bank governor Perng yesterday says up to NT$300 billion worth of foreign money shouldn't remain on island, but "foreign investors may put the money in the bourse, which will help the market instead," says Miao. Formosa Plastics (1301.TW) down 0.6% at NT$65.80 as group's NT$280 billion integrated petrochemical complex expansion project held up because of difficulty in getting larger pollution emissions quota.(JEH)

0136 GMT [Dow Jones] EUR/JPY falling, with Japan exporters eyed selling a lot due to this regular settlement day, in addition to selling by U.S. names in Japan position adjustments ahead of U.S. holiday season, says senior sales dealer at major bank in Tokyo. Adds weak Japan stocks, which often negative for EUR, also fueling selling by short-term players; EUR/USD also down. EUR/JPY may fall to 132.00 vs last 132.60; EUR/USD may fall to 1.4850 vs last 1.4903. AUD/JPY may fall to 80.50 vs last 81.69.(TMO)

0133 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB steady at 33.19 from late yesterday with pair unmoved by weekly U.S. jobless claims, which offered no surprises; BOT suspected of again intervening in market, although only mildly, trader says. "The market should be fairly subdued after there was nothing unexpected overnight and also as we head into the weekend," says local dealer. Pair expected in 33.15-33.25 band.(LHM)

0132 GMT [Dow Jones] Singapore stocks retreat as investors lighten positions amid cautious tone following Wall Street's losses. STI off 0.2% at 2753.84; support tipped at 2727 (Nov. 13 close), with resistance at year-to-date high of 2785. Market breadth at almost two decliners for every gainer, while overall volume light. Dealer at local brokerage says near term downside could be limited, but whether market can attain new highs remains to be seen; "looking at the charts, you'll see that the lows are getting higher and higher while the highs have remained steady. It's now a question of whether the market can go up some more." Top percentage decliners among blue chips include NOL (N03.SG), off 1.3% at S$1.57, ST Engineering (S63.SG), off 1.0% at S$3.13. (FKH)

0132 GMT [Dow Jones] Lead December Kospi200 futures down 0.2% at 213.25, but investors mostly sidelined after yesterday's massive foreign stock buying via program buying in non-arbitrage trade; that "seems to be just a one-off event. It's still not clear why they picked up such a heavy number of stocks yesterday," leaving investors in doubt about sustainability of foreign stock buying, says Moon Ju-hyun at Hyundai Securities. Foreigners' net selling in spot market so far improves market basis, spurring program buying in arbitrage trade now. But lead Kospi200 expected to drift around last close of 213.70 rest of today. (SKS)

0130 GMT [Dow Jones] Philippine shares may retreat on Wall Street, technical cues; benchmark PSEi may slip to initial 3050 support after rising to close +1.0% at 3083.30 Thursday; index +2.4% over last 3 days; expected near-term trading band 3000-3100; "We'll likely see the market move sideways, with a downward bias because of the overdue correction. The market needs a technical breather," says Grace Cerdenia, head of operations at 2TradeAsia.com; blue chip Metropolitan Bank & Trust (MBT.PH), gold producer Philex Mining (PX.PH), among market's recent gainers, may lead market retreat. (SFL)

0130 GMT [Dow Jones] 10-year cash JGB yield likely rangebound in 1.270%-1.370% band over next two weeks, as players unlikely to chase aggressively without further stock falls, JPY gains or increasing speculation over additional BOJ easing steps, says Deutsche Securities strategist Makoto Yamashita; 10-year yield last down 0.5 bp at 1.290%. Says market will closely watch BOJ's view on deflation at Gov. Shirakawa press conference from 0630 GMT, but thinks BOJ chief unlikely to clearly acknowledge Japan entering deflation as says BOJ wants to maintain economic recovery scenario. (MEF)

0125 GMT [Dow Jones] "There is no evidence central banks are diversifying away from USD," says State Street Global Advisors Head of Currency Management Collin Crownover. Notes IMF data which shows FX reserves remain consistent; "there is no other currency right now that has the same credibility as USD," he says. Says EUR not liked as alternative currency due to lack of transparency in institutions, depth of market, uncertainty about future of EU project. CNY also won't be a reserve currency for some time. Says USD weakness fully consistent with cyclical explanation, driven by the relative economic performance and fiscal, monetary policy; "We don't see anything abnormal about USD weakness at this stage of the decline." (EGC)

0121 GMT [Dow Jones] December Nikkei 225 futures down 1.0% at 9450, just off low of 9440, as weak tech stocks hurting cash index; next support around 200-day moving average (now 9341), but futures may fall more next week, with technical support for next week pegged at July 13 intraday low of 9030, says Traders Securities manager Tamotsu Numazaki. While financial stocks higher today on cash market on short-covering, equity financing concerns will linger, he says; adds, if yen remains strong and continues to weigh on exporter stocks, market sentiment unlikely to improve any time soon.(JUO)

title: UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Downplays Talk Of Capital Controls
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia is "comfortable" with how it manages the rupiah's exchange rate and has no immediate plan to limit capital inflows, Deputy Governor Hartardi Sarwono said Wednesday.

Sarwono said that while the central bank is evaluating the impact of limiting foreign ownership of short-term notes issued by the central bank, also known as SBIs, no changes are in the works.

"Bank Indonesia is still comfortable enough with the existing policies, namely intervention (in the market) if there's a big fluctuation in the (rupiah) exchange rate," Sarwono told Dow Jones Newswires.

Some economies such as Taiwan and Brazil recently imposed measures to discourage short-term capital inflows to slow the appreciation of their currencies.

Indonesia is similarly witnessing a surge in hot money inflows following two peaceful elections earlier this year. It is also an investor favourite for being one of the few countries recording growth while others grapple with recession.

Sarwono added that purchases and sales of the central bank's paper by foreign investors remain orderly and haven't caused any sharp fluctuation in the rupiah's exchange rate.

He said that foreign investors currently own IDR47 trillion ($4.98 billion) of the total IDR280 trillion of SBI in the market.

Foreign investors also own around $11 billion of rupiah-denominated government bonds.

Despite of the rupiah rising 17% against the dollar so far this year, several Bank Indonesia officials recently made bullish comments about the local unit. Analysts say the remarks suggest the central bank favors further appreciation to contain inflation, which is expected to accelerate next year.

Standard Chartered Bank economist Eric Sugandi said a stronger rupiah wouldn't severely hurt the Indonesian economy as it isn't heavily reliant on exports, unlike some of its regional peers.

A stronger rupiah will also reduce the cost of capital goods imported by domestic companies, which will give the economy an eventual boost.

He added that Bank Indonesia should be careful in imposing capital controls as such an act could discourage foreign investors from entering Indonesia, hurting the rupiah.

-By Farida Husna and I Made Sentana; Dow Jones Newswires; 62-21 39831277; I-Made.Sentana@dowjones.com [ 18-11-09 0526GMT ]

title: Indonesia  Min: Not Aiming To  Intervene  In  Forex  At Any Particular Level
text:
SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Indonesian Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati said Wednesday that the government isn't looking to intervene in the foreign exchange market at any particular level, but will ensure that any currency moves are smooth.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit here, she said Indonesia isn't seriously affected by the weaker dollar because the country is mainly an exporter of natural resources rather than of manufactured goods.

She said, however, that sudden moves in the foreign exchange market are undesirable that given the recent depreciation of the dollar.

She also said that Indonesia's central bank must take future inflation expectations into account when setting monetary policy.

She cited uncertainty over rising commodity prices and a weaker dollar as possible drivers of inflation.

-By David Roman, Dow Jones Newswires; +65 64154 045; david.roman@dowjones.com [ 11-11-09 0623GMT ]

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesia c.bank to support rupiah if needed -dep gov
text:
(Adds details, quotes)

JAKARTA, Oct 29 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia (BI), will intervene in the market if needed to support the rupiah <IDR=>, deputy governor Hartadi Sarwono said on Thursday.

The rupiah lost 1 percent to 9,700 against the dollar earlier on Thursday, hitting a one-month low, as offshore players took profits on local assets, prompting the central bank to intervene for the second day to support rupiah, traders said.

Despite losses in recent days, the rupiah remained Asia's best performing currency this year, up 13 percent against the dollar so far this year.

"BI will always monitor these developments and will be in the market if needed so that the market won't be panic and conduct transactions in an orderly manner," Sarwono told reporters.

Sarwono said the weakening of the rupiah in the past few days followed selling pressure in the U.S. stock markets as well as worries over possible changes in monetary policy in Asia. He did not elaborate.

"BI doesn't see this as the end of a U.S. dollar weakening, and Indonesia's economic prospects are quite good so that there is still room for the rupiah to strengthen," he added. (Reporting by Adriana Nina Kusuma; writing by Sonya Angraini; Editing by Sara Webb)

0932 GMT [Dow Jones] Indonesia bond market regains some ground as IDR reverses slide; yields now largely steady vs Wednesday after rising 10-15 bps early. "There are genuine flows from offshore, they're buying in the belly of the curve," dealer says; "it looks like the first phase of some real money accounts coming back in and starting to bet against the dollar again." Dealers say FR30 7-year benchmark yield around 9.78% vs 9.7487% Wednesday; FR36 10-year at 10.31% vs 10.1890%. USD/IDR lower at 9,610 late vs 9,690 Wednesday; hit 9,710 earlier but dragged back by suspected heavy intervention from central bank. Stocks also claw back most of their early losses to close down 0.5%.(RLC)

0930 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/INR forward premium falls more amid easing bond yields, overnight index swaps since RBI kept key policy rates unchanged at monetary policy review Tuesday offering comfort that interest rates would remain low at least in near-term; September 2010 premium at 1.25 vs 1.30 while October premium at 1.36 vs 1.42 last close, dealer with private bank tips continuing receiving interest as traders sell spot dollars to enter buy/sell swaps in forwards. Higher USD/INR spot since RBI policy also attracting supplies from exporters, dealer adds. "There was paying interest from some large foreign banks a few times but it could not withstand the continuing exporter supplies," says dealer. (AVK)

0930 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/THB unchanged in late trade at 33.46, with selling from offshore pulling pair back after early rise to 33.51 which came on broad USD strength offshore; pair overall in tight 33.47-33.51 range. "The Bank of Thailand's revision of its GDP forecast didn't really affect the market," says Bangkok-based dealer, because more positive growth is already expected in 2010. Players eyeing U.S. 3Q GDP later for guidance, but expects 33.35-33.50 range for USD/THB tomorrow. (LHM)

0927 GMT [Dow Jones] USD/IDR turns south late after suspected heavy intervention by Bank Indonesia and capital inflows; now 9,610 vs 9,690 late Wednesday, off intraday high 9,725. "BI came in heavily around 9,700 and after that the market turned around by itself," dealer says. Dealers estimate central bank sold $150 million-$200 million. Bank Indonesia deputy governor Hartadi Sarwono says solid economic fundamentals give scope for rupiah to strengthen further, tips dollar to stay under pressure; dealer adds London-based investors sell pair likely to buy local bonds; 9,580-9,650 tipped Friday. (RLC, IMS)

0924 GMT [Dow Jones] KLCI ends off low, down 0.6% at 1241.75 with decliners outpacing gainers 2 to 1 on concerns over pace of economic recovery after poor U.S. economic data, say dealers. "The decline was in tandem with losses in other Asian markets. Foreign funds were all net sellers in some of the big cap stocks but volume traded was moderate," says dealer. Cautions, benchmark KLCI closed below psychological 1250 level, indicating more weakness may be in pipeline. "The performance on Wall Street (tonight) will be closely watched. Further declines may drag the KLCI well below its immediate support at 1233 (30-DMA)," he adds. On upside, expects resistance at 1250. Among decliners, Genting (3182.KU) down 1.5% at MYR7.20, Maybank (1155.KU) down 1.8% at MYR6.63. On upside, Latexx (7064.KU) adds 1.9% at MYR2.65 and SP Setia (8664.KU) +1.3% MYR3.86. (VGB)

0917 GMT [Dow Jones] France Telecom (FTE) 5-year CDS is little changed Thursday, quoted at 54/57bps from Wednesday's close of 54bps, according to Markit. France Telecom posted in-line 3Q results. Barclays Capital says the company's ability to grow organically is under pressure and the bank says its appetite for M&A may increase. "We believe that even relatively small transactions could be sufficient to damage its perception as a 'safe haven'". Keeps its marketweight recommendation on bonds, and is neutral on CDS. (SYC)

0913 GMT [Dow Jones] Greek government bond spreads are wider in mid-morning trade after credit ratings agency Moody's warns of a possible downgrade. "The market has reacted to the Moody's announcement," says a bond trader. title: Indonesia Rupiah Falls Against Dollar; Dollar Hits IDR9,540
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Indonesian rupiah weakened further in afternoon trading Thursday with the dollar breaching the IDR9,500 resistance level to reach IDR9,540, its highest in about two weeks.

Currency dealers said they hadn't detected Bank Indonesia intervening in the market in afternoon trade, although the central bank was suspected to have sold at least $50 million in the morning session to shore up the rupiah.

title: CORRECT: Indonesia Finance Min: Rupiah Needs To Be More Stable
text:
("=UPDATE: Indonesia Finance Min: Rupiah Needs To Be More Stable," published at 0558 GMT, misstated the name of the Indonesian finance minister in the second paragraph. The error was also contained in the article "Indonesia Fin Min: Rupiah Needs To Be More Stable," published at 0311 GMT. The correct version follows:)


 
   By Linda Silaen 
   Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's finance minister said Wednesday that the rupiah and other regional currencies appear to be seeking a "new equilibrium," and said that the government will monitor the local unit closely for signs of volatility to ensure that it trades in a more stable manner against the U.S. dollar.

The rupiah and its counterparts are "in the process of finding a new equilibrium in line with their (underlying) fundamentals" following the global downturn, Sri Mulyani Indrawati told reporters. "The rupiah exchange rate has not yet reached an equilibrium point where it is comfortable."

Her comments echo views among many investors and analysts that the rupiah is retracing back to levels prior to the global economic downturn. The relatively resilient performance of the domestic economy and an improving political climate have boosted investor sentiment in Southeast Asia's largest economy.

The finance ministry and Bank Indonesia have said that a stronger rupiah helps fight imported inflation, but have warned against excessively sharp movements in the exchange rate.

Bank Indonesia often intervenes in the currency market to cap sharp moves but doesn't target a specific currency range and lets the market move relatively freely. The central bank was suspected of intervening to support the dollar several times in recent weeks after it weakened sharply.

The rupiah has risen around 17% since January. The dollar recently traded around IDR9,400, unchanged from its close Tuesday.

-By Linda Silaen, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 3983 1277; Reuben.Carder@dowjones.com [ 21-10-09 0727GMT ]

title: UPDATE: Bank Indonesia: IDR Gains In Line With Regional Peers
text:
(Adds central banker's comments on inflation, loan growth; updates rupiah level; background.)

By Farida Husna and Reuben Carder

Of DOW JONES NEWSWIRES

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The rupiah's recent strong gains against the dollar are in line with the strength of regional currencies and with domestic economic fundamentals, Bank Indonesia Acting Governor Darmin Nasution said Wednesday.

"The rupiah isn't alone. The currencies of other countries around us are also strengthening," Nasution said, adding that Bank Indonesia will work to curb excessive volatility in the exchange rate.

Nasution's remarks came after Bank Indonesia was suspected to have intervened quite heavily to support the dollar last week.

Analysts expect Bank Indonesia to tolerate gains in the rupiah but predict it will step in from time to time to buy the U.S. dollar, to curb intraday falls in the greenback that it deems too sharp. The central bank generally favours a stronger rupiah to help fight inflation, and this concern outweighs that of export competitiveness, analysts say.

Nasution said the central bank aims to prevent local businesses from being adversely affected by sharp currency movements. However, he said Bank Indonesia doesn't consider any particular level for the rupiah against the dollar as "comfortable." Bank Indonesia does consider the impact of currency movements on importers, exporters and the government, he said, without elaborating.

The government uses a forecast average exchange rate to calculate foreign-exchange related costs in the state budget each year. He said the dollar will likely average IDR10,000 or higher against the rupiah this year, despite a significant fall below that level in the second half of the year.

JAKARTA, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The appreciation of Indonesia's rupiah <IDR=> could help contain price pressure in Southeast Asia's biggest economy, the International Monetary Fund's senior resident representative in Indonesia said on Wednesday.

Milan Zavadjil, the IMF's representative, also told Reuters in an email that the central bank, Bank Indonesia (BI), was right to direct intervention to trying to reduce volatility in the rupiah, which is Asia's best-performing currency so far this year.

"In the current situation of strong capital inflows, the appreciation of the rupiah can help contain domestic price rises. BI is right to direct intervention largely at reducing volatility," he said.

Zavadjil noted that the country's exchange rate flexibility has helped it in the past to deal with large capital flows.

"Exchange rate flexibility has served as an important shock absorber for Indonesia," he said.

"During the worse of the global financial crisis, the flexibility of the currency helped absorb large capital outflows, thus avoiding a large loss in reserves and a loss in confidence." (Reporting by Gde Anugrah Arka, Editing by Sara Webb)

title: =DJ  FX  ASIA:Bank Indonesia Will Let Rupiah Rise At Measured Pace
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The rupiah's rally is good for Indonesia's economy and the central bank knows it. That's why it will let the currency rise further - at a measured pace.

The rupiah has climbed nearly 4% against the dollar this month and almost 15% since January as investors have piled into Southeast Asia's largest economy on hopes that an improved political and security environment and the country's new, investor-friendly government will lead to large returns on Indonesian stocks and other investments.

The dollar's broad decline has added to rupiah bullishness.

With its large domestic market, Indonesia relies much less on exports to drive economic growth than many of its Asian peers, so there's not much pressure to drive the rupiah down to get an edge on Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand, its rivals in palm oil, natural rubber, timber, metals and other exports.

Indonesia's exports amount to about one third of gross domestic product and net exports less than 2%. In Thailand, exports make up around two thirds of GDP.

Bank Indonesia has intervened to slow the rupiah's rise, but the dollar-buying clearly isn't aimed at trying to change the market's direction. Acting Gov. Darmin Nasution said earlier this month merely that the central bank doesn't want the rupiah to strengthen "too fast."

Analysts say Bank Indonesia would allow the dollar to fall to IDR9,200-IDR9,300 - the top of a range of IDR8,700-IDR9,300 that prevailed for nearly three years before the U.S. currency spiked last year when the global financial crisis deepened.

The dollar was at IDR9,730 Monday at 0520 GMT.

"The rupiah will be among the top performers in the region - the only limiting factor is the fact that it has strengthened so much this year," said Gundy Cahyadi, an economist at IdeaGlobal in Singapore. Indonesia is "not as dependent on exports as Thailand or Malaysia - that's the advantage."

Cahyadi forecast the dollar will fall below IDR9,500 and could test IDR9,400 by the end of the year.

Fauzi Ichsan, an economist at Standard Chartered in Jakarta, said Bank Indonesia might start buying dollars under IDR9,500 but that it will only look to slow the rupiah's rise, not stop it.

A strong rupiah would keep imported inflation in check, which could be key to curbing price pressures in a world of rising commodity and energy prices.

What's more, Indonesia's newly reelected president, Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, plans to build up the country's infrastructure to lay a firmer foundation for lasting economic growth. A strong rupiah makes imported capital goods cheaper.

Jakarta has pledged to spend more on infrastructure as it aims to bring economic growth up to about 5% in 2010 from an estimated 4.3% this year.

Not all analysts think the rupiah's strength will last. ING forecasts the dollar will rise to IDR10,500 by the end of the year as inflationary expectations turn investors away from local assets.

   OF DOW JONES NEWSWIRES 
 

SINGAPORE (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's trade minister said Monday that the economy is likely to grow 4.0% to 4.5% this year and the central bank stands ready to intervene in the foreign exchange market to curb volatility.

"What is important is to maintain a stable currency and curb volatility ... What we look for is stability in the exchange rate that reflects the underlying macroeconomic fundamentals," Trade Minister Mari Pangestu told Dow Jones Newswires in an interview.

She also said the recent suicide bombings in Jakarta would have a limited impact on markets, including the stock and currency markets, and that economic fundamentals remain strong.

As well, economic growth in the first half was encouraging, despite the contraction in exports and imports and low growth in investments.

"Domestic consumption accounts for 70% of our growth and it was growing at 5.8% and the growth remains strong," Pangestu said.

Indonesia's economy expanded at 4.1% in the first six months of the year, with the inflation rate at 3.65%.

"Inflation is already coming down and we do believe that we can maintain inflation between 5% to 6% this year, and then for the next year, 4.5% to 5.5%," Pangestu said, adding that the economy is expected to grow 5% to 6% in 2010.

On trade, the minister said exports are likely to contract at a much slower pace than her ministry initially estimated.

"In the beginning of the year, we were projecting a 20% to 30% contraction. Now we have revised it to around a 15% contraction," Pangestu said.

She said the recent suicide bombings won't have much impact on portfolio investments in the country, as most investors look at the fundamentals of the economy, which remain strong.

"Of course, we can expect travel and tourism to be affected in the short term (but) Indonesia has demonstrated its resilience ... and we will also be resilient in overcoming this current unfortunate situation."

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Bank Indonesia will remain consistent on monetary policy and will work to support the domestic economy, a central bank official said late Wednesday.

The central bank will support the local economy by "accelerating the absorption of the government's fiscal stimulus package," Wimboh Santoso, Bank Indonesia head of bureau for financial stability, told an awards ceremony.

He said Bank Indonesia's 2.5-percentage-point cut to its policy rate since December should encourage local banks to give more loans, and at lower rates.

SINGAPORE, Feb 5 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah and South Korean won fell on Thursday due to renewed concerns over a dollar liquidity crunch, while other Asian currencies held steady ahead of the European Central Bank's rate decision due later in the day.

 The Indonesian rupiah <IDR=> fell as far as 11,950 per dollar, down almost 1.9 percent, as investors rushed to buy dollars amid fears of a shortage of the U.S. currency.

 "There is not enough dollars in the market," said a Jakarta-based trader, adding that Bank of Indonesia is intervening to support the rupiah but the amount of dollars it sold in the market was small.

 Broad dollar strength as well as rising short-term dollar funding costs were adding pressure on the rupiah, traders said.

 The rupiah has fallen just over 7 percent against the dollar so far this year, the second worst performer in Asia after the South Korean won <KRW=>, which is down almost 9 percent.

 Asian central banks are generally leaning towards tolerating further currency weakness as exports collapsed amid the global downturn, but they still intervene to smooth currency volatility.

 The won <KRW=> fell as far as 1,385.9 per dollar, down half a percent from Wednesday's close, after a senior government official was quoted as saying the country may suffer more foreign currency liquidity shortage. [ID:nSEO42854]

 Much of Asia was affected by a dollar crunch last year caused by the global financial crisis, with South Korea suffering the most as foreign investors pulled out from the country, contributing to the won's 25 percent slide in 2008.

title: UPDATE: Bank Indonesia Surprises With 25 BPs Policy Rate Cut
text:
(Adds details, background, and economists' comments)

JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Indonesian central bank Thursday surprised the market by cutting its benchmark rate by 25 basis points, a move that analysts say highlights its proactive stance in mitigating the impact of the global slowdown on the domestic economy.

"The rate cut to 9.25% is expected to stimulate business activities amid the global economic slowdown," Bank Indonesia said in a press release after a monthly rate-setting meeting.

The central bank added that it expects inflationary pressures to continue easing in the coming months, paving the way for further cuts.

Consumer-price inflation eased to 0.12% on month in November from 0.45% in October, and to 11.68% on year from 11.77%.

Bank Indonesia said that it expects annual inflation to continue sliding to around 6.5% next year thanks to falling commodity and energy prices in the international markets.

Nine out of 12 economists polled by Dow Jones Newswires had expected Bank Indonesia to hold the rate steady, citing concerns about the rupiah, which has lost 24% of its value against the dollar so far this year.

The central bank also cut the overnight repurchase rate it offers to commercial banks to 9.75% from 10.50%, and increased its overnight deposit rate to 8.75% from 8.50% in an effort to "resolve the segmentations in the interbank money market."

Shifting Focus

Analysts said that the cut in the policy rate, the first since December 2007, indicates the central bank's focus is shifting toward spurring growth and away from controlling inflation.

"Not surprisingly, this...decision was justified on the basis of more gloomy domestic and international growth prospects as well as greater confidence that inflation will fall within (if not below) the 6.5%-7.5% target range of the Central Bank," said Robert Prior-Wandesforde, a Singapore-based economist with HSBC.

Growth in Southeast Asia's largest economy slowed slightly to 6.11% on year in the third quarter of the year from 6.39% during the April-June quarter.

Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati said last month that growth would likely continue sliding, to between 4.5% and 5% in 2009 as demand for Indonesia's exports would be hurt by recession in major economies.

Analysts said that the rate decision could also signal that Bank Indonesia is of the view that interest rates are no longer effective in defending the rupiah.

The rupiah was trading at IDR12,050 to the dollar at 0725 GMT, slightly higher than its Wednesday close of IDR12,250 as year-end demand for dollars from local companies eased, dealers say.

"There was no knee-jerk reaction against the rate cut as it is minor compared with the cuts done by other central banks," a dealer with a foreign bank in Jakarta said.

In a sign that it acknowledges the rate cut could make the local currency less attractive, Bank Indonesia said that it will continue to intervene in the foreign exchange market to reduce the volatility in the rupiah.

Bank Indonesia has been actively intervening in the market since October as the rupiah fell to its lowest level in a decade.

Analysts said that Indonesia needs to secure loan commitments from multilateral and bilateral lenders in order to improve confidence in the local unit.

The government has approached the World Bank, Asian Development Bank, Islamic Development Bank, Japan, France and Australia recently, but so far there has been no commitment from those potentials lenders.

-By Farida Husna and I Made Sentana, Dow Jones Newswires; 62 21 39831277; I-Made.Sentana@dowjones.com [ 04-12-08 0809GMT ]

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Undermined by  intervention  worry

SINGAPORE, Jan 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies slipped in holiday-thinned trading on Tuesday, weighed down by profit-taking after their sharp rises in the past week and the anxiety about possible central bank intervention.  

 Markets in Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia were closed for a Muslim festival holiday. That kept trading volumes thin.  

 The won <KRW=> <KRW=KFTC> closed local trade around 982 per dollar, just off Monday's high of 975 which was the currency's strongest level since the Asian financial crisis in 1997.  

 The Philippine peso <PHP=> fell to 52.645 per dollar, off Monday's peak of 52.25 which was its highest level since May 2003.  

 The Thai baht <THB=> gave up some ground, easing to 39.93 from Monday's 8-month high of 39.69 a dollar.  

 "Seems like some players took profit, but when we were back up above 39.90 some exporters came to sell dollars," said a baht trader based in Bangkok.  

 Regional currencies slipped as the dollar staged a slight rebound from three-month lows struck the past couple of sessions against the euro <EUR=> and yen <JPY=>.  

 Also, markets paused to see the extent to which central banks around the region would intervene to cap their currencies, which have risen sharply since the start of the year.  

 South Korean authorities kept up their normal run of comments.  

 The Vice Finance Minister said the won had risen too fast and steps would be taken as necessary, soon after a Bank of Korea official said the currency had risen above an equilibrium range against the dollar but authorities would not force it lower.  

 "Korean authorities clearly are not comfortable with either the pace of the move or the rate of the won," Richard Yetsenga, HSBC's currency strategist, said.  

 "But it unlikely that they will be successful in preventing the won moving at all."  

 Shahab Jalinoos, currency strategist with ABN AMRO Bank, said in a note the comments suggested there would be no concerted attempt to cap the won.  

 "This backs our view that strong growth means Korea will not want to risk the liquidity headaches implied by concerted intervention. Korean intervention in 2006 will be tactical rather than  strategic," he said.  

 That view would be confirmed if the Bank of Korea raised interest rates at its policy meeting on Thursday, he said.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Won down, baht steady, eyeing  intervention
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 10 (Reuters) - The South Korean won and the Taiwan dollar slipped while other Asian currencies held steady on Tuesday in holiday-thinned trading as markets turned wary of central bank intervention.  

Markets in Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia were closed for a Muslim festival holiday. That kept trading volumes thin.  

The won <KRW=> <KRW=KFTC> was quoted around 980 per dollar, just off Monday's high of 975, which was the currency's strongest level since the Asian financial crisis in 1997.  

The Philippine peso <PHP=> was barely changed at levels hugging 52.50 per dollar, just off Monday's peak of 52.25, which was its highest level since May 2003.  

"It's very tight trading. The dollar is up in other markets but not doing much against peso," said a Manila-based trader.  

Traders said the regional currencies slipped as the dollar staged a slight rebound from three-month lows struck the past couple of sessions against the euro <EUR=> and yen <JPY=>.  

Also, markets were taking a breather while watching how far central banks around the region would intervene to cap their currencies, which have risen sharply since the start of the year.  

"With Asian FX having rallied strongly already this year and central banks showing some, though not decisive, intervention appetite, a phase of consolidation today makes sense in this environment," Shahab Jalinoos, currency strategist with ABN AMRO Bank said in a note.  

Markets should also be careful about selling the dollar against the Asians in such holiday trading for central banks could use the opportunity to push their currencies down, he said.  

"The key risk to long Asia positions today is that local central banks decide to take advantage of a modest USD bounce globally to ramp up intervention and literally get more 'bang for their buck'," Jalinoos said.  

"While this will not reverse the longer term USD-Asia downtrend, it would make sense perhaps for them to try this if they are planning to engage only in a tactical as opposed to a strategic intervention policy." CURRENCIES VS U.S. DOLLAR Change on the day at 0226 GMT
