title: Bank  Indonesia  denies dollar buying  intervention .
text:
JAKARTA, June 5 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank on Wednesday denied market talk it was buying dollars saying there was more room for the rupiah to continue its recent surge. 

 The rupiah - the best performing regional currency this year - lost some of its gains after the bank said on Tuesday the market should not over react to the currency's appreciation. 

 Some dealers took those remarks as a signal that the bank would intervene to stem the rupiah's sharp rise. 

 "It is impossible (for the central bank) to buy dollars because there is still room for the rupiah to strengthen," central bank deputy governor Miranda Goeltom told Reuters. 

 Goeltom said a rupiah level of around 8,500-8,600 to the dollar was "appropriate". 

 By 0925 GMT on Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 8,890/8,940 per dollar after touching its highest level since August 21 of 8,440 the previous day.

title: Emerging Asia  FX -Mostly down on yen, rupiah eyes c.bank.
text:
SINGAPORE, June 5 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were 

 down early Wednesday, tracking loses in the yen after 

 the Bank of Japan intervened to sell its currency. 


    For the Philippine peso        and the Indonesian rupiah



, however, domestic factors were more in focus.



    The peso was a little lower on Wednesday on political



worries while the rupiah traded cautiously below a nine-month



high set on Tuesday due to market fears the Indonesian central



bank might intervene.



The Singapore dollar eased to a session low of



1.7890 per dollar, from late Tuesday's 1.7825, weighed down by



yen's losses against the dollar.



Dealers said the BOJ's fourth intervention in two weeks had



raised doubts over nearterm upside for the yen and other



regionals which track Japanese currency as Japan is both a



major market and export competitor for most Asian economies.



Some corporate dollar sales for hedging needs was seen as



likely to support Sing dollar around 1.7880-1.7890, but dealers



said some players were still short of dollars and may opt to



cover those positions.



The Thai baht was down to 42.40, from late Tuesday's



42.29, with Singapore dealers expecting more downside on the



regional yen issue. They said slowing equity and export-related



inflows would also keep the baht depressed.


INTERVENTION HANGS OVER RUPIAH



The Indonesian rupiah strengthened to 8,575 per dollar from



lows around 8.650 seen late on Tuesday but this was still below



a nine-month high set earlier on Tuesday.



Dealers blamed the retreat on central bank comments that



some saw as opening the door to intervention to slow the


currency's appreciation.



Bank Indonesia said it saw more room for the rupiah to rise



this year but said it expected it to stabilise in the short



term.



The central bank's deputy governor Miranda Goeltom warned



that it was important the forex market did not overreact which



could lead to excessive swings and affect economic recovery.



Dealers in Jakarta said players, most of whom were short of



dollars, took the comment as countering last month's statement



when the bank said that exports would remain competitive even



if the rupiah strengthened to 8,500 to the dollar.



The rupiah breached that early Tuesday to touch 8,440 per



dollar - a level not seen since August 21 last year - but the


central bank comments led some players to fear intervention.



MANILA FOCUS ON POLITICS



With Philippine May inflation figures issued in line with



expectations at an annual 3.6 percent, unchanged from April,



analysts said the focus for the peso was on politics.



Samir Goel, market analyst at Bank of America in Singapore,



said economic numbers have taken a back seat after defection of



a Senator John Osmena to the opposition, tilting the balance in



the Senate against President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo.



"This is an example yet again of how quickly political



factors can overtake the optimism on economic reforms in



Philippines, as in much of Southeast Asia," he said.



Goel said opposition gaining majority in the upper house



would heat up the political scene and could potentially delay



the legislative process for some of the key reforms.



    The peso quoted at around 50.60 to the dollar early



Wednesday, against 50.43 close on Tuesday.



    In May the currency hit a 13-month high of 49.20 to the



dollar but it has come under pressure since then on worries



over falling government revenues which could result in a higher



budget deficit.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Ends Higher On Ctrl Bk  Intervention  Talk
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended higher Thursday on rumored intervention by authorities to help push the dollar lower. 

 The dollar closed at IDR9,530, down from IDR9,590 at Wednesday's finish. 

 State banks were heavy sellers of dollars in the afternoon session, helping push the U.S. currency to close at its low for the day. 

 Traders said the state banks were likely acting on behalf of the central bank to help push the dollar lower. 

 The dollar moved higher in the morning on demand from local companies that need the U.S. currency to repay foreign debt or fund imports. 

 The dollar hit an intraday high at IDR9,585 in early trade. 

 But the trend remains dollar bearish as Indonesia has made a number of steps toward reforming its economy in recent weeks which has helped market sentiment. These include selling PT Bank Central Asia to Farallon Capital of the U.S. last month for around $500 million. 

 Adding to positive sentiment is expectations the International Monetary Fund will soon give the go-ahead for the disbursement of the next $340 million loan to Indonesia under its $5 billion program. 

 The market also expects the Paris Club of official creditors to agree - at a two-day meeting which ends Friday - to reschedule $5.5 billion in Indonesian sovereign debt.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Dn As Importers, Comml Bks Buy Dlrs
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah closed lower Thursday as commercial banks covered their short-dollar positions amid fresh bids for the U.S. currency by local importers, dealers said. 

 The dollar closed at 10,215 rupiah, up from its close at IDR10,180 Wednesday. The dollar, however, was off its intraday high of IDR10,260 on suspected intervention from Bank Indonesia. 

 The central bank has said it would intervene in the currency market to defend the rupiah if necessary. It doesn't comment on specific instances of intervention, however. 

 "Fresh bids for dollars from local importers triggered interbank players to square their dollar-short positions," said a dealer with a foreign bank. 

 Dealers expect banks to drive the dollar lower to IDR10,180 when the market reopens Friday before local companies step in to buy the U.S. currency on dips. 

 Besides buying dollars to pay for imports, local companies need dollars to pay maturing offshore debts. 

 Dealers expect the dollar to trade between IDR10,180 and IDR10,250 Friday. 

 In the money market, the overnight rupiah lending rate slipped to 15.75% from 16% earlier in the day on improved liquidity. But the rate was still higher than its usual level of between 15.25% and 15.50%, as the Indonesian Bank Restructuring Agency was suspected to have withdrawn some of the funds it had placed with banks and transferred them to the state coffers.

title: Emerging  FX  - Directionless, market in holiday mood.
text:
SINGAPORE, Feb 11 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were a mixed 

 bag in thin trade late on Monday as players did last-minute 

 position squaring ahead of Lunar New Year holidays. 

     Trading was thinned by local holiday in Japan and Lunar New 

 Year holidays in Korea and Taiwan. Most Asian financial markets 

 will be closed on Tuesday and Wednesday. 

     Markets showed no response to Singapore's official upgrade 

 of its growth forecast while the absence of corporate demand 

 for dollars pushed the Thai baht and the Indonesian rupiah 

 higher. 

 "The market seemed to be paying more attention to what they 

 are going to eat at New Year banquets than to the global or 

 regional outlook today," said a dealer at an Asian bank. 

 The G7 meeting over the weekend hardly affected the market 

 as the meeting passed without any strong comments on 

currencies. 

 The yen bounced off its early lows as players covered short 

 positions in anticipation of fund repatriation by Japanese 

 firms and on expectations of supportive comments ahead of 

 President George W. Bush's visit to Tokyo. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar lingered within a narrow 1.8325-1.8340 

 range in choppy trade. 

 Most players reluctant to take fresh positions ahead of the 

 Tuesday-Wednesday holidays, even as Prime Minister Goh Chok 

 Tong said in a Lunar New Year message the government had 

 revised growth expectations for the year to 1.0 to 3.0 percent, 

 up from minus 2.0 to plus 2.0 percent. 

 Dealers said the upward revision was behind the curve 

 because most analysts had been raising their forecasts since 

 the end of 2001, when exports in most Asian showed signs of 

 bottoming out. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was in a doldrum as players wound up their trading 

 ahead of the holiday. Although Thai financial markets are open 

 during Lunar New Year, a number of Chinese-Thai companies will 

 be closed. 

 Dealers said the baht had been underpinned lately by dollar 

 offers from offshore names in Singapore and Hong Kong, and 

 capital inflows from a Japanese auto maker. 

 Baht funding costs in the offshore market were soft, with 

 the one-month forward rate being quoted at 5/10 satang to the 

 dollar. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended lower at 51.315 to the dollar against 51.220 

 on Friday after corporates stocked up for debt repayment. 

 Turnover picked up to $100.75 million from around $86 million 

 in the previous session. 

 However, analysts expect the peso to strengthen in the 

 medium term on the back of inflows from equity investment and 

 asset sales. 

 In the money market, the country's key Treasury bill rate 

 fell below the benchmark overnight borrowing rate at Monday's 

 government auction to a fresh 15-year low of 7.278 percent, and 

 the government said it hoped the 91-day T-bill would fall 

 further. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah edged higher as local corporates stayed out of 

 the market, allowing interbank players to further trim their 

 long dollar positions. 

 The long dollar liquidation was kicked off after aggressive 

 dollar purchases by state banks sparked talk of central bank

intervention last week. 

     Financial markets in Indonesia will be closed on Tuesday 

 and will reopen on Wednesday.

title: Emerging  FX  - Pulled back on their feet by yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 29 (Reuters) - Asian currencies continued 

 their rise against the dollar late on Tuesday, spurred on by 

 the yen's gains. 

     With the Korean won leading the charge, the regional 

currencies have been steadily inching higher against the 

 greenback since late last week. 

     Still, dealers and analysts said the bearish sentiment 

 towards the yen despite its recent bounce and a lack of 

 interest in the regional markets was preventing Asian 

currencies from making more rapid advances. 

 Given the recent dramatic moves in the major currencies, 

 dealers said players were more interested in trading in the 

 majors, where the gains were bigger and the liquidity more 

 flush. 

 Peter Redward, currency strategist at Deutsche Bank in 

 Singapore, said central bank intervention was also holding back 

 some regional currencies. 

 "That's left the regional currencies in no man's land. With 

 the U.S. recovery underway, most of the regionals should be 

 strengthening. But then we've got central banks taking the 

 opportunity to build up their forex reserves," he said. 

 In recent weeks, most Asian central banks, with the 

 exception of Indonesia and Hong Kong, have reported a rise in 

 their forex reserves. 

 Besides regional developments, the market was also focusing 

 on the two-day Federal Reserve meeting which starts later in 

 the day. While most in the market are not expecting a rate cut, 

 they were waiting to see what the Fed might say about the 

 economy. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar managed to claw back some territory 

 from its U.S. rival, but was held in check by talk the central 

 bank may have been in the market to buy dollars. 

 Some dealers said the central bank was believed to have 

 bought a small amount of dollars around the 1.8315/20 level. 

 They, and others, said the central bank was probably keen to 

 cap the local dollar's gains given the still fragile yen and 

 the weaker euro, both of which are major components in the Sing 

 dollar's trade-weighted basket of currencies. 

 News that Singapore Technologies and Hong Kong's Hutchison 

 Whampoa were seeking to take a combined 70-80 percent stake in 

 Global Crossing Ltd. also weighed on the local dollar. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was up on dollar sales by exporters for month-end 

 needs and on settlement of stock purchases by foreign investors 

 in the past two sessions in which they had picked up a net 449 

 billion won of local shares. 

 Dealers in Singapore said players were encouraged by the 

 correction in the dollar/yen that they believed had created 

 more room for the won to appreciate without resistance from 

 authorities. 

 Korean authorities have shown greater concern over the 

 won's competitiveness in the face of a near-term bearish 

 outlook for the Japanese currency given Korea's overlapping 

 export portfolio with Japan. 

 They said the yen's rebound overshadowed the steeper than 

 expected dip in industrial output for December. The won's 

 upside was expected to be capped around 1,310-1,305 for now, 

 but a steadier yen could allow the won to rack up more gains. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht advanced further against the dollar on the back of 

 the yen's rebound, but its gains were dented by talk of the 

central bank coming in to check prices. 

 The central bank has been in the market regularly lately to 

 pick up dollars below 44, either to top up reserves or to cap 

 the baht's gains against the backdrop of increased capital 

 inflows, dealers said. 

 "They (the central bank) were in the market to check rates, 

 but I'm not sure if they actually bought the dollar today," 

 said a local dealer. 

 Charts showed the dollar/baht was still trapped in a 

 downtrend channel, indicating more gains ahead for the local 

currency. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was firmer, reflecting the regionals' trend. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said corporate players were holding back on 

 dollar purchases on hopes the dollar would dip further. 

 The rupiah was also boosted by news of the IMF approving a 

 US$341 million instalment under Indonesia's $4.5 billion loan 

 programme, and extending the loan for a year. 

 Separately, the IMF said on Tuesday it was confident the 

 divestment of Indonesia's largest retail bank, Bank Central 

 Asia (BCA), would be well managed but said the sale should be 

 wound up swiftly. 

 In the money market, Bank Indonesia kept its intervention

 rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 15.125 

 percent for the overnight rate and 15.875 percent for the 7-day 

 rate. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar held steady but gave up its early gains 

 following a 2.68 percent fall in the local stock market and 

 dollar sales by a foreign bank suspected to be executing an 

 order placed by a foreign equity fund manager. 

 Dealers in Singapore said despite the yen's rebound and 

 some recent positive data flow, stock market losses and 

 wariness over the central bank's repeated dollar-purchase 

interventions has dampened market sentiment and could keep the 

currency in a tight range around the 35 per dollar level. 

 Foreign investors sold a net T$553.5 million of local 

 shares on Tuesday, following net sales of T$463.2 million on 

 Monday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The Philippine peso was locked in a tight range of 

 51.16-51.23, ending the day at 51.165 as it tracked the yen and 

 regional currencies. 

 Trading was brisk with $134.2 million changing hands. 

 Dealers in Manila said bargain-hunting importers swooped in 

 to buy dollars when it fell below 51.20, while exporters wanted 

 to sell the greenback around 51.30. 

 Many importers hedged their dollar requirements in the 

 forward market just before 2002 and have been sitting on the 

 sidelines so far. But dealers said corporates may come back at 

 the right price. 

 Still, they expect the peso to be trapped in its familiar 

 range ahead of the Fed's announcement and economic data 

 including fourth quarter gross domestic product due on 

 Thursday.

title: Emerging  FX  - Mixed in Asia as dollar/yen idles.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies parted ways 

 early on Thursday, with most edging lower or steady, as the 

 dollar dithered just under the 133 level against the yen. 

     The markets remained fixated on the wobbly yen's progress, 

 and any sharp movement in the dollar/yen could trigger a 

 reaction in the regional currencies. 

     But, in keeping with their recent trend, any reaction was 

 likely to be muted. 

     Analysts have attributed the more modest losses of the 

 regional currencies compared to the yen's to a number of 

 factors including recent capital inflows into the region and 

 already substantial falls in the currencies. 

 However, they have reminded the market it would be 

 foolhardy to believe the Asian currencies have cut their apron 

 strings with the yen. 

 "While Asian currencies notable the KRW, TWD and SGD have 

 outperformed the JPY since September 11, they have done so 

 because markets are pricing in a firm rebound in the U.S.," 

 said Mansoor Mohi-uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg in 

 Singapore, said in a note. 

 "If this fails to materialise then Asian currencies are 

 likely to come under renewed pressure against the JPY as well 

 as the USD." 

 On the local news front, both the Bank of Korea and the 

 Philippine central bank will be holding monetary policy 

 meetings later in the day. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged lower in line with the yen, but gains on the 

 local stock market were expected to boost its fortunes. 

     However, players were wary that the authorities, unhappy 

 with the won's surge against the yen, may intervene. 

     Deputy Finance Minister Kim Yong-Duk told Reuters on 

 Wednesday that a weaker won should accompany any more falls in 

 the yen for Korea to maintain export competitiveness. 

     He also said the attempts by Japanese officials to talk 

 down the yen were "undesirable", and warned it could provoke 

 concerns from Japan's neighbours in Asia. 

     The Bank of Korea is expected to keep its key overnight 

 call rate steady at four percent at its monthly monetary policy 

 meeting later in the day. In a recent Reuters poll, economists 

 said expectations of a better economy were likely to encourage 

 the bank to sit pat on rates. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was mostly steady in early trade in a dearth of 

 fresh leads, with most market participants focused on the 

 direction of the dollar/yen and real commercial demand. 

 In the medium term, dealers expected the baht to be 

 well-supported by expectations of capital inflows linked to 

 privatisation, with the state-owned Telephone Organisation of 

 Thailand (TOT) launching its IPO in March. 

 In the offshore market, baht funding costs were hardly 

 changed, with the tom/next rate at 0/5 satang per dollar and 

 the one-month rate at 7/11 satang per dollar. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was marginally weaker, but off its morning 

 low of 1.8520 after some U.S. and European names cashed in on 

 the U.S. dollar gains. 

 But dollar bargain hunting at around 1.8460 would mean that 

 the Sing dollar will trade in a narrow range, with players 

 focused mostly on the dollar/yen direction, dealers said. 

 Analysts said the Sing dollar's downside should be limited 

 in the longer term after the Monetary Authority of Singapore 

 restored a narrow trading band earlier this month. 

 "This implies that the MAS will be less tolerant of Sing 

 dollar weakness against the USD going forward," said Mohi-uddin 

 at UBS Warburg. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO (PHP=) 

 The peso opened at 51.80, edging lower than the previous 

 day's close of 51.56, but dealers in Manila said the 

 government's launch of 15-year global bonds would give a slight 

 boost to the peso. 

 Co-lead manager of the bond issue Morgan Stanley said on 

 Wednesday the Philippines sold $750 million of 15-year global 

 bonds. Dealers said the market was hoping the sale of those 

 bonds might bring fresh dollar inflows into the market should 

 the government choose to inject some of that liquidity from the 

 bond launch into the market. 

     They were mixed on whether the Philippine central bank

 would cut rates later in the day. 

     Dealers in Manila and Singapore expected the peso to trade 

 at an intraday high of 51.50 to the dollar because corporates 

 were buying dollars at that level. 


    TAIWAN DOLLAR



    The Taiwan dollar was barely changed from Wednesday's close



of 35.05 as the market waited for fresh cues from the



dollar/yen.



    Still, the market was reluctant to take any large positions



because volatility was expected to be held in check by the


central bank. Taiwan's central bank boasts some $122 billion in


foreign exchange reserves, and market players say it is



regularly in the market to smooth away volatility.



    The currency was also likely to receive a boost from



continued foreign fund flows into the local stock market.



     INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah drifted around a narrow range of 10,400-10,500



with the market still suffering from the lack of fresh leads.



    While local corporate dollar demand has re-emerged in the



market, dealers in Jakarta said players were reluctant to take



huge positions because of fears of central bank intervention.



    On the macro front, Indonesia's Chief Economics Minister

title: Emerging  FX -Trapped under yen's shadow.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 4 (Reuters) - Asian currencies held onto 

 their recent ranges early on Friday, but the yen's shaky shadow 

 was stretching over regional markets. 

     With little fresh local news to trade on, players have been 

 focused on the yen, which continued to battle the dollar 

 despite the euro's slight retreat. 

     Still, there were local factors that managed to dull the 

 yen's influence. Foreign equity inflows in South Korea and 

 Taiwan's stock markets cushioned some of the negative vibes 

 from the yen, with fear of Taiwan's ever-vigilant central bank

 also doing an effective job of protecting the Taiwan dollar. 

 A bit of jawboning from Thai authorities also aided the 

 baht. And players in Singapore were taking seriously the 

Monetary Authority of Singapore's decision to narrow the 

 trading band for the trade-weighted Singapore dollar as a 

 reflection of improving confidence in the economy. 

 There was some local data expected to trickle in later in 

 the day, including Philippine export numbers for November and 

 December inflation. 

 But both the major and regional currency markets were 

 paying the most attention on U.S. employment report for 

 December due later in the day. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won is firmer against the U.S. dollar, boosted by gains 

 in the stock market, a rebound in the yen and talk of exporter 

 dollar offers. 

 The currency opened a touch lower at 1,313.0 against 

 Thursday's close of 1,312.7 before climbing to its morning high 

 of 1,308.5. 

 Korean shares jumped three percent after the first 

 eight minutes of trading, fuelling hopes for foreign capital 

 inflows. 

 Foreign investors bought a net 211 billion won worth of 

 shares on Korean bourses on Thursday, almost double their net 

 buying the previous day. 

 Dealers said seasonal demand, the yen's direction and local 

 stocks would continue to be major driver in the near-term. 

 Charts show 1,300 is a strong resistance for the won for now. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar opened firmer at 35.003 to the dollar in 

 the onshore market compared with 35.030 at Thursday's close. 

 The currency was supported by a steady yen and hopes for 

 more capital inflows after the local stocks racked up gains at 

 the open because U.S. gains boosted local semiconductor shares. 

     Foreign investors were net buyers of T$5.31 billion (US$152 

 million) in Taiwan stocks on Thursday. 

     The Finance Ministry will release December trade data on 

 Monday. 

     The central bank data show Taiwan's foreign exchange

 reserves rose to a record US$122.211 billion in December, 

 making the sixth straight monthly rise. 

     Although the central bank did not give the reason for the 

 rise, dealers said it had been intervening actively in the 

foreign exchange market in December to curb gains in the Taiwan 

 dollar and support Taiwan's export competitiveness. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar held steady within a tight 

 1.8470-1.8475 range, helped by a steadier yen. 

 But dealers said expected near-term weakness of the yen and 

 talk of dollar bids by local players lined up at around 1.8440 

 would keep Sing dollar's upside limited. 

 Dollar offers were expected at around 1.8500 with most 

 players reluctant to test lower levels after the Monetary 

 Authority of Singapore narrowed its preferred trading band for 

 the currency on Wednesday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso edged slightly higher as interbank players 

 continued to trim their long dollar positions on a steadier 

 yen. 

 However, dealers in Manila said the peso's upside would be 

 limited on an expected rise in demand for dollars by local 

 corporates next week. 

 The market will watch out for the inflation data for 

 December, due to be released later in the day, for clues on the 

central bank's next move on key interest rates. 

 The central bank on Thursday left key overnight rates 

 unchanged with borrowing at 7.75 percent and lending at 10 

 percent. The rates were last lowered by 25 basis points on 

 December 13. 

 The central bank governor said there was room for another 

 25-50 basis point cut in key rates later this month depending 

 on factors like inflation and economic recovery. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was stalling just below the 44 level as players 

 pondered the dollar/yen's next move. 

 Dealers in Singapore said comments by the Thai finance 

 minister and central bank governor that 44 to the dollar was an 

 appropriate level for the baht had a limited impact on the 

 market. 

 Bank of Thailand governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said on 

 Thursday the bank would monitor the exchange rate more closely 

 this year because exports are expected to run into more 

 trouble. 

 Daily charts showed the dollar/baht retracing some of its 

 move up in late December, with 43.95 expected to provide some 

 support because it represents the 50 percent retracement of its 

 December 13-28 rise. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah managed to stay afloat above the 10,400 mark on 

 wariness over possible central bank intervention. 

 With few positive local factors to drive it higher, the 

 rupiah was content to stagnate around these levels as players 

 acted cautiously in case of intervention from Bank Indonesia. 

 A newspaper reported the economy grew by 3.5 percent in 

 2001 according to preliminary figures, slightly beating 

 expectations of 3.01 percent growth.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Lower On Dollar Debt Repayments
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended weaker Thursday as banks bought dollars on behalf of corporate clients that need to repay debt. 

 Negative sentiment was further compounded by demonstrations earlier this week against plans to raise utility costs this year to ease the budget deficit. 

 The government needs to get its deficit - estimated at 3.7% of gross domestic product last year - under control to restore confidence in the economy and the local currency. Failure to do so will leave Indonesia even more dependent on foreign loans to fill the gap. 

 The dollar ended at IDR10,390-IDR10,410, higher than IDR10,380 at Wednesday's close. 

 The U.S. currency traded up to an intraday high at IDR10,430, at this level the central bank was rumored to have intervened by selling dollars. The bank has a policy of intervening to help the rupiah, but never confirms its actions. 

Indonesia's central bank is likely to defend IDR10,450 Friday, making this a key resistance level for the dollar. 

 Although the bank's dollar sales can bring the U.S. unit lower in thin trade, the trend is likely to remain dollar bullish in the near term, traders said. Many foreign exchange players remain on holiday this week after the New Year break. 

 But next week, the dollar may continue to rise amid further demand from local companies that need to repay foreign debt. 

 The government, too, is burdened with huge foreign public debt totaling around $70 billion. Jakarta is likely to have to ask foreign government creditors at a meeting next month to reschedule its debt coming due this year. 

 Without faster sales of assets from the broken banking system - which crashed in 1997 bringing the economy to its knees - the government deficit will remain high, and the rupiah under pressure.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Ends Up;Ctrl Bank  Intervention  Suspected
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended slightly higher on its first trading for the year Wednesday thanks to suspected Bank Indonesia intervention, dealers said. 

 The dollar closed at 10,380 rupiah, down from its close Friday at IDR10,450. Indonesian currency markets were closed Monday and Tuesday for New Year's holidays. 

 The U.S. unit had risen to an intraday high of IDR10,550 earlier in the day as some participants bought the dollar on expectations of corporate demand. 

 However, the central bank was suspected to have entered the market, which triggered the unwinding of the dollar-long positions. Bank Indonesia has a policy of intervening to prevent volatility, but it doesn't comment on individual actions. 

 "Talk that Bank Indonesia was in the market quickly triggered dollar-long liquidation as basically the dollar was already overbought," a dealer with a local bank said. 

 Local companies, which in most recent sessions have been buying dollars for debt servicing, were absent from the market. 

 Fears of intervention by Bank Indonesia protected the rupiah from news that the country's trade surplus in November narrowed to $1.8 billion from $2.46 billion in October. 

 Continued weak data for both exports and imports indicate that economic growth may remain soft this year, and the weaker surplus points to a possible future deterioration in reserves, analysts said. 

 Dealers expect the dollar to trade between IDR10,350 and IDR10,450 Thursday. 

 Separately, the weighted average rate of Bank Indonesia's one-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes edged down to 17.50% in a weekly auction from 17.62% last week. 

 The decline, however, was too little to indicate a softening bias on the part of Bank Indonesia, dealers said.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Down;Local Cos Buy Dlr On Last Day
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah gave up earlier gains to close slightly lower in thin trade Friday as local companies bought the dollar on dips to pay maturing foreign debts, dealers said. 

 After falling to an intraday low of 10,300 rupiah, the dollar closed at IDR10,450, up from its close Thursday at IDR10,410. 

 This means the rupiah depreciated 7.4% this year compared with its close at IDR9,675 to the dollar last year.

 Still, the dollar's slide only proved an invitation for local companies to buy the U.S. currency during the year's last trading day. 

 Trading will be closed Monday as Bank Indonesia won't provide clearing services ahead of the New Year public holiday. The local foreign currency market will reopen Wednesday. 

 Dealers expect the dollar to start the new year with bullish note as local companies will still have to pay maturing offshore debts next year. 

 Moreover, a lack of progress on the domestic economy will continue to deter foreign investment in Indonesia, dealers added.

title: Emerging  FX  - Mixed after Fed cut, wavering yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 21 (Reuters) - Asian currencies slipped early Wednesday, finding cold comfort from Wall Street's disappointment over the Federal Reserve's rate cut and the softer yen. 

 However, regional currency markets were generally long dollars, especially against the Singapore dollar and Korean won. Any turnaround in the yen may convince players to bail out of long dollar positions, giving Asian currencies a short-term boost, dealers said. 

 The Fed cut rates by 50 basis points on Tuesday, bringing the federal funds rate to five percent and the discount rate to 4.5 percent. It also signaled it was ready to take necessary action at any time. 

 A Reuters poll showed 17 out of 25 primary dealers of U.S. government securities polled after the Fed cut expected another 50 basis point by the next Fed meeting on May 15. For the POLL, double click . 

 But the size of the cut disappointed Wall Street, which had been clamouring for a bigger cut. The technology-laced Nasdaq fell by 4.8 percent, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 2.4 percent. 

 Those falls were expected to pressure tech-senstive equity markets in Taiwan and Korea. 

 On the major currency markets, the yen saw early gains slip away and the euro managed to rachet up more gains against the dollar. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was under pressure at around 1.7740, having hit lows of around 1.7760 overnight. 

 Dealers said underpinning the downside was persistent speculation SingTel might drop its bid to buy Australia's Optus . 

 "But until there is clear news here, the market seems unwilling to offload its large U.S. dollar longs," Mansoor Mohi-uddin, regional currency strategist at UBS Warburg in Singapore, said in a research note. 

 Dealers said some U.S. investment banks were unwinding long positions, piled up in the run up to March 16 highs of 1.7780. 

 The Sing dollar has lost 2.5 percent since the beginning of the year, in part because of the weaker yen and other regional currencies. 

 That, analysts say, lessened the market concerns about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won opened lower as disappointment over the size of the Fed's rate cut and concerns over the prospect of a U.S. recovery worked through the local stock market. 

 The weaker yen and bearish economic data also weighed on sentiment. Dealers said the won was expected to consolidate in the near term as the market was very long of dollar. 

 "But the dollar's bullish trend is intact. Charts show the dollar/won is still trapped in the uptrend channel which started on February 20," said a dealer in Singapore. 

 The market was unnerved by news of Korea's fourth quarter growth shrinking on quarter for the first time since the second quarter of 1998, the nadir of the Asian financial crisis. 

 Analysts said although Korea may avoid technical recession as its economy is likely to grow moderately in the first quarter this year, its gross domestic product might contract again the April-June period. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht dangled just above the 44.00 level as the market continued to favour the dollar despite disappointment over the Fed's rate cut. 

 Uncertainty over the U.S. economy, the weak yen and Thailand's gloomy economic outlook all kept a lid on the baht. 

 "There's not much good news around. The dollar looks a bit overbought and we spotted some profit taking at around 44.00. But I expect dollar bulls to pick it up on dips to 43.80," said a dealer at an Asian bank. 

 Dealers said the market's reaction to news that the government would unveil a new fiscal stimulus package in April was muted. 

 "Looking at their fiscal position now, I think there's little room for the government to increase its spending. The delay of value-added tax (VAT) increase would stretch the government's coffer a bit," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bangkok. 

 The one-month forward rate was quoted at 6.9/9.9 satang per dollar offshore and -10.50/-10.25 satang onshore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso eased after the central bank indicated its desire to follow the Fed rate cut with its own. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said he expected the Monetary Board at its meeting on Thursday to ease key overnight rates by 50 basis points. 

 The overnight borrowing rate now stands at 10.5 percent and the lending rate at 12.75 percent. 

 The central bank has cut its key rates by 450 basis points after raising them by 400 basis points in October to defend the weak peso . 

 Dealers said they expected the peso to trade in a range of 48.50-48.80 with the downside capped by expected dollar inflows from exporters. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was holding above 10,500 in a market wary of further central bank intervention. 

 Chief economics minister Rizal Ramli said on Tuesday he had asked the Indonesian bank agency to convert $500 million in asset sales to help the rupiah. He also said he had requested that the central bank act more decisively to support the rupiah. 

 Bank Indonesia has been intervening regularly in the market, either directly or through state banks. It has also recently raised its benchmark one-month SBI rate to 14.97 percent and its intervention rates in the rupiah money market by 50 basis points. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was flat in early trade, as the market puzzled over Wall Street's fall, the indecisive yen, and Taiwan's dimming economic prospects. 

 Charts showed the U.S. dollar was hugely overbought against the Taiwan dollar, with a reading of around 95 at 0047 GMT. 

 However, sentiment towards Taiwan was still bearish given its dependency on exports to the U.S. 

 Looking ahead, Taiwan will release February export order data and industrial output on Thursday. Recent Reuters polls showed economists on average expected a 10.8 percent on year rise in export orders and a 10.73 percent on year rise in industry output.

title: Indonesian Rupiah Problems Purely Political -Ex-IMF Neiss
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- The beleaguered Indonesian rupiah's problems are purely "political" and there is little that the country's central bank can do to shore up the currency, former International Monetary Fund Director Hubert Neiss said Wednesday. 

 Bank Indonesia's recent moves to intervene in the foreign exchange market and raise interest rates, though necessary, won't significantly boost the currency, Neiss told reporters on the sidelines of a banking seminar in Singapore. 

 Neiss is currently Deutsche Bank's (G.DBK) chairman for Asia. 

 Last week, amid increased political uncertainty, the rupiah fell to 11,500 rupiah against the dollar, its lowest level since August 1998. It has since partially recovered and was quoted at IDR10,429 to the dollar at 0628 GMT. 

 Neiss said he doesn't expect Bank Indonesia to keep interest rates high for a long time as this would hurt the country's economy. 

 The former IMF official who was instrumental in formulating the multilateral agency's rescue package for Indonesia, however, declined to comment on whether Indonesia had made any recent progress in economic reforms suggested by the body. 

 "Both sides (Indonesia and IMF) are still engaged in discussion," he said. 

 Replying to questions from seminar delegates earlier, Neiss said though "Indonesia has had a bad press" due to its political situation, it has made "substantial progress in rehabilitating" the domestic banking sector. 

 "The priority of banks (now) should be to fully divest nonperforming assets," he said. 

 Neiss noted that despite Indonesia's woes, its economy was growing, albeit slowly, and has potential for faster growth in the future. 

 Indonesia "is still in a very difficult transition period," he said. 

 Replying to reporters' questions, Neiss said there was no risk of recession in Asia this year. 

 After a rapid 6%-8% growth last year, Asian economies will grow at a slower 2% to 4% rate this year, but that doesn't imply Asia is heading into a recession, he said. 

 Neiss said Asian nations are generally well positioned to avert another 1997-98 type of crisis as they have higher reserves, lower short-term debt and positive current account balances.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Lower As Political Woes Continue
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah closed lower Monday as political and security woes continue to hurt the currency. 

 The dollar closed at IDR10,430, up from IDR10,325 at Friday's close, but off an intraday high at IDR10,500. 

Indonesia's central bank intervened later in the day, selling a small amount of dollars directly to the market, helping the local currency recover some ground. 

 "Dollar resistance remains at 10,500," a local trader said. 

 Traders estimated the amount of direct intervention was at about a few million dollars, much less than that of last week. State banks were also selling dollars Monday, probably on behalf of the central bank. 

 However intervention won't help lift the rupiah in the longer term, as investors remain concerned over moves to impeach President Abdurrahman Wahid, traders said. The likelihood of further violence also concerns investors, they added. 

 A bomb exploded Saturday on a railway line near Jakarta. There were no casualties but the blast led to more negative sentiment on the market. A wave of bombs in the past twelve months have destabilized the country. 

 Stocks also fell, with the JSX Composite Index closing 3.5% lower, a 28-month low of 367.142 points. 

 Rates fell slightly Monday, as the central bank appears to have let the pressure off a tightening cycle, that was aimed at helping the rupiah. 

 Last week, the central bank borrowed rupiah in the interbank market in an attempt to dry up liquidity and help the currency rise from a 30-month low at 11,500. 

 But the central bank seems to be focusing more on intervention rather than on rate policy, as interest hikes have very little effect on the politically-driven rupiah at the moment, analysts say. 

 The overnight interbank rate closed Monday at 12.75%, down from over 13% earlier in the day.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Lower On Bleak Political Outlook
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah closed lower against the U.S. dollar in active dealing Friday, as local companies continued buying the dollar because of the uncertain domestic political situation. 

 After rising to an intraday high of IDR10,375, the dollar closed at IDR10,325, up from its close of IDR10,150 Thursday. 

 Dealers said that local companies bought the dollar in anticipation of foreign debt repayments in two or three months. 

 "Although local companies don't have to repay their foreign debts until the next two or three months, they are buying the dollar now on bleak political outlook," said a dealer with a foreign bank. "Local companies remain skeptical as there are no signs of political truce between President (Abdurrahman Wahid) and his opponents." 

 Bank Indonesia's intervention failed to help the rupiah as the central bank sold the dollar to foreign banks instead of to local companies, dealers said. 

 Dealers estimated Bank Indonesia on Friday sold $40 million in the market, directly and indirectly through state banks and brokers. 

 A statement by senior economic minister Rizal Ramli, that he is optimistic the dollar will fall below IDR10,000 in the near future, failed to calm local companies, dealers said. 

 The interbank money market was steady as Bank Indonesia didn't borrow rupiah from the market to tighten liquidity. The overnight rupiah interbank rate was steady between 12.5% - 12.75%. 

 Bank Indonesia usually tightens rupiah liquidity in the interbank money market to reduce the pressure on the rupiah in the foreign currency market. 

 As dollar demand was healthy Friday, dealers expect the dollar to open Monday around IDR10,500, unless Bank Indonesia intervenes promptly.

title: Asia Markets-Hunt for value helps regional stocks.
text:
HONG KONG, March 15 (Reuters) - Asian investors searched 

 for value amid the carnage of a U.S.-inspired stock market 

 sell-off on Thursday and found enough to bring many regional 

 bourses off their lows by the close of trading. 

     Surprisingly, it was the tech sector which saw some of the 

 better buying with China Mobile in Hong Kong, 

 Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing in Singapore 

 and Korea' Samsung SDI Co all posting gains. 

     "For the moment there is value in Asia, it's just that Asia 

 is being hijacked by external events," said Markus Rosgen, 

 Asian equity strategist for ING Barings in Hong Kong. 

     "In an outright U.S. recession this region would have a 20 

 percent downside, but that would make this region very much the 

 cheapest out of the U.S. or Europe," he said. 

     "There is a lot of value out there now, but there's sadly 

 more downside driven by external factors," Rosgen said. 

     Share prices across Asia were hit hard in early trade by 

 Wall St's across the board pummeling overnight amid fears for 

 the health of Japan's banking system. 

     The key Dow Jones Industrial index sank 317.34 points, or 

 3.08 percent, to 9,973.46 -- it was the Dow's 10th-largest 

 point loss ever. 


    The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index	   closed below



the 2,000 mark for the second time this week to end at



1,972.10, down 42.68 points or 2.12 percent. The Nasdaq index



has now shed 60.9 percent from its high of 5,048.62 in March a



year ago.



During the Asian day a big turnaround in Tokyo's benchmark



Nikkei average emboldened investors in the region to venture



back and bargain hunt.



CHINA PLAYS IN FOCUS



Asia's exposure to a U.S. economic slowdown through its



reliance on exports has many players looking to China as a



defensive play because it is one of the few countries with



robust domestic demand.



    Figures out on Thursday on retail spending showed this



domestic demand continues strong.



    China's retail sales for the January-February period grew



10.6 percent this year over the same period of 2000.



    Since last year the Chinese New Year holiday fell in



February and this year it was in January, the period covered by



the numbers indicates sales were definitely better.



    China's economy remains on track for seven percent growth



this year, according to both official and many private sector



economists. But export growth has already started to slow down



and net exports are starting to drag on the economy.



The government has pledged to counter the impact of



external slowdown with increased state infrastructure spending,



while foreign direct investment is streaming into the country.



Actual FDI flows were around $40 billion last year and have



been surging during January and February this year - rising 24



percent on year ago levels. If that rate is sustained FDI could



exceed $50 billion this year.



    But analysts say there are still sizeable risks involved in



China.



    A risk of policy inertia leading to a slower reform pace



than the market is expecting is one key factor, according to



Chi Lo, Treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank.



    Lo said China is under stress on three fronts. On the

title: Emerging  FX  - Worried by soft yen, regional gloom.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 15 (Reuters) - Asian currencies failed to escape the fury of dollar bulls late Thursday with the yen still faint and the regional outlook remaining decisively gloomy. 

 Despite a bounce in downtrodden Tokyo stocks, concerns over Japan's economic disarray continued to haunt the yen . Ratings agency Fitch placed 19 Japanese banks on negative review on Wednesday, sending investors running for dollar cover. 

 U.S. funds were also reported to be scurrying home after another day of heavy losses on Wall Street, driving some regional currencies lower as they sold off local stocks and converted the proceeds into dollars. 

 Dealers also blamed the weakness in the Indonesian rupiah as damping sentiment towards the region. Local corporate dollar demand kept the ailing rupiah below 10,000, despite wariness over central bank intervention after news Bank Indonesia fined Standard Chartered Bank 9 billion rupiah for violating recently installed foreign exchange curbs. 

 Meanwhile, the euro remained under pressure, faced with not only its inability to capitalise on woes in Japan and on U.S. equity markets, but also falls on European bourses. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was trapped in a tug-of-war between central bank intervention which kept the market cautious, and strong corporate demand for the dollar. 

 Dealers said Bank Indonesia intervened through two state banks which were estimated to have offered up to $20 million before midday. 

 The rupiah was also underpinned by news of the central bank fining Standard Chartered Plc's Indonesian operation for allegedly breaching tough new foreign exchange rules. 

 "That news and wariness of intervention has lent support to the rupiah. People in the market believe the central bank won't let the rupiah fall through 10,200," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Jakarta. 

 "But at the end of the day, you have genuine strong dollar demand, and genuine concerns over a poorly performing leader who refuses to step down. State companies which the government urged to sell dollars are still net buyers," he said. 

 Before the news of the fine spread in the market, dealers said the dollar looked well-bid after local media reported comments by Finance Minsiter Prijadi Praptosuhardjo that the sale of palm oil plantations to Malaysia's Kumpulan Guthrie was not final. He was reported as saying parliament should have been consulted. 

 Expectations that IBRA would convert some $345 million in the market from that sale had helped support the rupiah on Wednesday. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso lurched lower but was still trapped in its recent range, weighed by weak regional currencies and dollar demand from a state utilities company, dealers said. 

 The currency was wedged in a 48.33-48.49 range. Trading volume was relatively brisk, with around $148.50 million traded compared with $66 million on Wednesday. 

 "One state company has been in the market since yesterday to buy the dollar to service debt. The amount was quite big relative to the turnover," said a dealer at a European bank in Manila. 

 The central bank left its key overnight rates unchanged at 10.5 percent for the borrowing rate and 12.75 percent for the lending rate. 

 The bank has cut rates by 450 basis points since December after raising them by 400 basis points in October to defend the peso in the face of a political crisis. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar had little reprieve in afternoon trading, sliding to fresh two-and-a-half year lows around 1.7700. 

 "We've been seeing funds out of New York and Europe sold the Sing dollar moderately to get out of the stock market," a European bank dealer said. 

 The Straits Times Index was off its worst but still near its lowest level since April 1999, having lost around nine percent since the beginning of the month. 

 Dealers said the flow of funds and bleak outlook for the yen pointed to a weak Sing dollar, but fears of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would slow its decline. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht sank to its lowest level since January 2 as corporate and interbank players continued to buy the dollar in the wake of a weak yen, despite high baht funding costs offshore. 

 Dealers said one hedge fund had been asking around for prices, but it was not clear if it took any positions against the baht. 

Central bank governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul said on Thursday the baht was not depreciating too quickly. His remark was interpreted by the market as implying the bank was not disturbed by the baht's recent losses and would let it fall further. 

 Chatu Mongol also said that one bank had been barred from participating in the local repo market - where financial institutions get cheap funds - for 10 days after it breached forex regulations. 

 Separately, Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said Thailand was unlikely to face another economic crisis and fresh baht instability. But his remark failed to stop the market from selling the baht. 

 The one-month forward rate in the offshore market eased to 6/11 satang per dollar from 10/12 satang earlier, but was still high compared to last week's range. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar fell under the weight of the soggy yen, but the central bank helped it off its lows. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the central bank was spotted selling U.S. dollars around the high of 32.615. 

 Local banks in Taipei quickly followed suit, helping bring the Taiwan dollar back to 32.55. 

 But the U.S. dollar remained well-bid on the offshore non-deliverable forward market, with the one-month at 0.125/140 at 0826 GMT against 0.10/13 earlier in the day. 

 "Investors are taking long dollar positions in the NDFs because the fundamentals for Taiwan are expected to weaken," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Taiwan relies heavily on its high-tech exports and is now faced with a limping technology sector, a slowdown in its largest export market - the U.S. - and a weaker currency for one of its biggest competitors - Japan. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was off its lows but still weak after hitting a near two-month trough of 1,290 per dollar on the back of the sagging yen and early losses in Korean stocks. 

 Dealers said further falls were contained by exporter dollar sales and fears of government efforts to limit the won's slide, as was the case when it hit 25-month lows of 1,293 in January. 

 Bargain-hunting in Korean stocks also cushioned the won somewhat, but with foreign investors selling a hefty 55 billion won worth of local shares, dealers expected it to remain weighed. 

 Labour Minister Kim Ho-jin estimated the unemployment rate for February would be five percent or 1.069 million people, but he expected the number of jobless to fall to 980,000-990,000 in March. February data is due next week. 

 Korea's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in January and 3.9 percent in December.

title: Asia Grains-Volatile rupiah defers Indonesian deals.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 14 (Reuters) - Wide currency fluctuations have prompted Indonesian commodity importers, who were eyeing soymeal, wheat and sugar shipments, to defer their buying plans, regional traders said on Wednesday. 

 "No Indonesian buyer is ready to finalise contracts with the rupiah moving up and down," said a Singapore trader. "They are interested in some sugar and small amounts of soymeal but traders are deliberately staying away." 

 The Indonesian rupiah hit 30-month lows on Monday when it lost some 12.5 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar. Since then, it has recovered following central bank intervention. 

 "As it is, Indonesia's meal and beans buying have been slow in the past few weeks because of excess stocks and early arrivals. But now, buyers are totally out of the market due to the rupiah," said a soymeal trader from Jakarta. 

 Indonesia earlier this month bought 20,000 tonnes of soymeal from the United States at about $210 a tonne C&F for late March or early April shipment. Last week, traders were negotiating for another 30,000 tonnes of U.S. meal. 

 "It seems that the deal which was being negotiated has not materialised," said one trader. "The rupiah has been fluctuating since then. Even Indian meal is out of question now because of very high prices. I have not heard of any new contract for Argentine meal also." 

 According to traders, U.S. high-pro meal was offered to Indonesia at about $216 a tonne C&F. Indian meal was offered at $212 a tonne while Argentine low-pro meal was offered at $183. 

 "Even the unclear position of import duties is affecting any possible sales to Indonesia," said one trader. 

 Director General of International Trade Riyanto Yosokumoro said earlier this month Indonesia was considering raising import duties on rice, sugar and soybeans to protect local producers. 

 WHEAT, SUGAR IN SAME BOAT 

 Regional grain traders said wheat import contracts were also at a standstill because of the rupiah volatility. Not only buyers are staying away, but suppliers were also not very keen to aggressively push sales. 

 "The need for wheat in the domestic Indonesian market is still there but who is willing to take the risk at this moment?" asked one wheat trader. 

 Another trader said: "We are hoping that the currency will stabilise soon. Maybe, from next month onwards we will see a few new wheat import contracts getting finalised." 

 Trade officials say Indonesia will likely see solid growth in wheat imports this year as food multinationals, buoyed by reviving growth, plan business expansions. 

 Earlier this month, Indonesia's biggest wheat importer and miller, PT Bogasari Flour Mills said it would buy another 100,000 tonnes of wheat from India in addition to the 100,000 tonnes it bought in January. 

 "One or two sugar cargoes to Indonesia could materialise this week but we are keeping our fingers crossed," said one Singapore-based sugar trader. 

 Traders said there have hardly been sugar sales to Indonesia after India sold three cargoes of 12,000 tonnes each late last month. Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest sugar importer.

title: Emerging  FX  - Struggling along as good news eludes.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 13 (Reuters) - Asian currencies dragged their feet lower in early trade on Tuesday as the beleaguered yen and the battered Indonesian rupiah undermined regional sentiment. 

 The yen, already down 3.0 percent against the dollar this month, pushed to a fresh 20-month low overnight on mounting political uncertainty and Japan's bleak economic outlook. 

 In Indonesia, fears of central bank intervention could provide some support for the rupiah, but in the absence of fundamental change, analysts said they did not expect to see a meaningful turnaround soon. 

 The country's impasse with the IMF involving $400 million in vital funds is far from being resolved. This could jeopardise a $5.8 billion debt rescheduling deal with the Paris Club of official creditors. 

 A fund spokesman said in Washington that it expected to have future discussions with Indonesian authorities but there were still some major issues to be overcome. 

 Analysts and dealers expect regional currencies to retain their bearish tone in the near-term. 

 "Looking forward, we continue to be most bearish on the yen. For Asian currencies, we remain bearish especially on the baht, and the rupiah," said a DBS report. 

 "The Sing dollar will continue to face downward pressure due to a weaker yen and regional currencies," it said. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was underpinned by fears of intervention by the central bank which jumped in to sell up to $12 million in the market on Monday to shore up the sagging currency. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the market was also cautious that the central bank might soon tighten its grip on foreign exchange trading to halt a slide in the rupiah. 

 "I doubt very much if Bank Indonesia would resort to full-fledged capital controls. They might instead do something to force exporters to sell their dollars. The market seems a bit cautious at this point," said a Singapore dealer. 

 "Otherwise, the rupiah could creep lower...it could reach 12,000 because there is no good news whatsoever either from the economic or political front," he said. 

 The Indonesian central bank has repeatedly said it is committed to a free exchange rate regime. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid, whose leadership is being heavily criticised, said on Monday he would not step down, adding that the country would fall apart if he did. 

 Although Indonesia's spat with the IMF drags on, many believe the Fund will not abandon the country. However, it is expected to stick to its guns on reforms. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht pushed below the 43.70 mark alongside other regional currencies as foreign names bought dollars in both spot and forward markets. 

 Dealers said the baht might soon test 44.00 but not without rounds of dollar profit-taking. The dollar was looking overbought with a reading of 76 on the 14-day relative strength index. 

 But it should find some support at around 43.50 where the market is likely to buy the U.S. currency on dips, dealers said. 

 "There is no strong local lead at the moment, so the baht seems to be tracking the regional currencies. The weaker yen and the ailing rupiah have spurred dollar demand and hedging activity," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Singapore. 

 The one-month forward rate was quoted at 1/3 satang per dollar offshore and -11.5/-9.0 satang onshore. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar kept a softer tone to stay just below a three-and-a-half month low of 1.7620. 

 Dealers said investors unloading the Sing dollar because they expected local equities to follow the U.S. stock markets, which again took a dive on Monday. 

 Weakness in regional currencies and the euro compounded its woes, they added. 

 "We see various parties are selling. Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo, everyone," a European bank dealer said. 

 Dealers said 1.7690 was now within sight, a level not seen since September 1998. 

 Analysts said the market was not too concerned about the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) intervening to support the Sing dollar, given that its decline was in line with weakness in the currencies of its trading partners. 

 One analyst said there was growing speculation the MAS would revise their stance to neutral from a tightening bias soon, which meant the central bank would guide the Sing dollar lower. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won was depressed by losses in the local stock market, the weaker yen, and poor economic data. It opened at 1,284.0 against Monday's close of 1,278.4. 

 The benchmark KOSPI , whose performance usually affects sentiment in the currency market, shed 3.14 percent at the open as investors were unnerved by hefty losses in the Nasdaq overnight. 

 Foreign investors sold a net 23.5 billion won worth of shares in early trade. 

 Sentiment was also dampened by bleak current account data. Korea's current account surplus was almost halved in January to a provisional $684.4 million from December's final $1.24 billion. 

 Analysts said the faltering semiconductor sector, a main export component, would keep pressure on the economy in the months ahead. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO The peso opened a tad lower at 48.15 and was expected to stay pressured by weaker regional currencies, with dealers watching how local equities would perform. 

 Another factor upsetting the peso was a $470 million loan held by the central bank which is maturing in April. The central bank has said the bank may simply buy dollars from the market. 

 Dealers expected the peso to creep lower to 48.35, to fill a gap between 48.25 and 48.35. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar made a soft start, briefly dipping past the 32.50 per dollar mark to lows not seen since end-January as the Nasdaq drop triggered selling of local electronics shares. 

 On Monday, the Taiwan dollar fell sharply as recent declines on Wall Street sparked foreign fund outflows, which dealers estimated at US$100 million on Monday. 

 The local dollar's close below 32.40 on Friday prompted speculation the central bank had moved back its line of defence, prompting the market to push it lower, given the sagging yen and declines in tech stocks.

 The yen was spared a selloff in reaction to plummeting Japanese share prices Tuesday, as losses in the benchmark Nikkei 225 were within market expectations, players said. 

 Just how much the foreign exchange market expected the Nikkei to drop wasn't clear, but the benchmark did shed 2.9% to close at 11,819.70, the lowest finish since January 1985. 

 The South Korean won was one of the beneficiaries of the yen's stability. After opening weaker at 1,284.0 won to the dollar, the won strengthened throughout the day closing at KRW1,275.3, up from Monday's close of KRW1278.40.

title: Bk  Indonesia  Plans  Intervention  In Interbank Money Mkt
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia plans to intervene in the interbank money market later Monday to absorb rupiah liquidity, an official with the central bank said Tuesday. 

 The pressure on the rupiah in the currency market is expected to ease if its liquidity in the interbank money market is tightened.

title: Bank Indonesia says will continue helping rupiah.
text:
JAKARTA, March 12 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank said on Monday it would continue to do its best, including intervention, to defend the fast-sliding rupiah. 

 "Bank Indonesia will continue to do its best," deputy governor Miranda Goeltom told Reuters. 

 "We have enough funds to help the rupiah... we will continue to do it (intervention)." 

 The rupiah has fallen around 10 percent from late Friday levels, though by 0627 GMT had recovered some ground and was quoted at 10,400/10,500 to the dollar. 

 Goeltom said she expected rates to rise at Wednesday's auction of short-term central bank paper (SBIs) and said Bank Indonesia had already raised the intervention rate in the money market by 50 basis points. 

 Earlier, senior deputy bank governor Anwar Nasution called intervention in the currency market at the moment like pouring water into the sand, saying an end to political instability was crucial to protect the currency.

title: Indonesian rupiah breaches 11,000 as worries grow.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 12 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah slid past 11,000 per dollar on Monday, extending early losses after the central bank said it had limited ability to defend the currency. 

 Bank Indonesia deputy governor Anwar Nasution's comments that intervention now would be like "pouring water into the sand" drove the rupiah past its earlier low of 10,800. 

 "All this time Bank Indonesia has raised interest rates, intervened, but the rupiah keeps weakening...political reconciliation is a must to gain stability," he said. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 11,100/400 at 0356 GMT, down 10.1 percent from its late Friday levels. It has not broken past 11,000 since September 24, 1998. 

 Dealers said doubts over President Abdurrahman Wahid's leadership and his ability to handle economic and ethnic problems had spurred dollar demand. 

 News that thousands of anti-and pro-government protesters had poured onto the streets of Jakarta also unnerved the market. 

 Bank Indonesia and state banks were the only sellers of dollars in a thin market, dealers said. 

 "Companies and banks are busy covering their short dollar positions while there are few offerers of dollars. It could go to 15,000 before we see any profit-taking on the dollar," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Jakarta. 

 "Bank Indonesia sold a small amount of dollars this morning and stopped. I don't think they can do much at this point," she said. 

 "The fall was exaggerated a bit by thin volume. I think the central bank's recent rules to curb speculation have backfired," she added, referring to the drying up of liquidity following BI's new forex trading curbs.

title: Asia Markets - Gloom here, there, everywhere.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 12 (Reuters) - Asian equity and currency

 markets sank on Monday, overwhelmed by bad news from Wall 

 Street and Japan. 

     On top of that, Southeast Asian currencies, especially the 

 Singapore dollar, were contending with a flailing Indonesian 

 rupiah , which skidded to lows not seen since September 

 1998. 


    The U.S. Nasdaq	   market fell victim on Friday to



investors whose hopes of a deep rate cut from the Federal



Reserve were dashed by positive February jobs data.



    The Nasdaq's 5.35 percent fall, chip giant Intel Corp's



 profit warning, and bad news from other U.S.



technology leaders like Cisco sent Asian tech stocks



reeling.



    Tech-sensitive bourses in Singapore	 , Taiwan	  ,



and Korea all stumbled over the losses on Nasdaq.



    Benchmark indices in Tokyo and Hong Kong	  fell back



as well, with Japan's Nikkei faced with a home-grown



brew of economic and political troubles.



    STUMBLING YEN, MIXED-UP GOVERNMEMT



    Prime Minister Yoshiro Mori's decision over the weekend to



push the elections of his party's president ahead of schedule



seemed to clear Japan's murky political scene.



    But his denial on Monday that he intended to resign muddied



those waters even more.



    Despite slightly better than expected October-December



economic growth data, the market remained deeply pessimistic



over Japan's prospects.



    Analysts shrugged off the 0.8 percent rise in gross



domestic product, saying most indicators still pointed down.



    Those concerns, questions over the country's leadership,



scepticism over the ruling coalition's economic package and the



Nasdaq's fall pushed the Nikkei to a 16-year closing low.



    The yen	  fell below 120, casting a shadow over



regional currency markets that have been under its thumb in



recent sessions.



    "At this point, we're certainly seeing that regional


currency weakness...under the shadow of the yen," said Song Sen



Wun, vice president of regional economics at G.K. Goh Research



in Singapore.



    With sickly markets in Japan and the United States, the



euro was looking quite hale in comparison.



    SUFFERING RUPIAH



    However, the yen's woes paled next to the rupiah's. The



Indonesian currency crashed to a low of 11,210 -- its worst



since September 22, 1998.



    The rupiah managed to claw back from that following verbal



and actual intervention by Bank Indonesia. Dealers in Jakarta



said the bank offered between $5-$10 million in the afternoon,



after it offered $2 million in the morning to no avail.



Indonesia's economic and political woes sideswiped the



rupiah earlier in the day as nervous interbank players bid up



the dollar for fear of the situation getting worse.



Among the chief concerns in the market were those centred



on Jakarta's frayed relationship with the International



Monetary Fund and the leadership of embattled President



Abdurrahman Wahid.



News of protests in Jakarta by pro-and anti-Wahid factions



pushed the market over the edge, as investors fretted over



possible violence between the two sides.



A straw poll of analysts surveyed by Reuters on Monday said



that barring capital controls and a significant turnaround in



the political situation, the rupiah could hit 12,000-15,000 by



the end of June.



"The two things that I'm looking at are the situation with



the IMF and the situation with Wahid... Even if things are



patched up with the IMF, things still will look shaky if Wahid



hasn't stepped down by June," said an analyst at a foreign bank



in Singapore.



The IMF has delayed since December a $400 million loan to



Jakarta over concerns about central bank independence, regional



autonomy and asset sales.



"While the loan itself isn't a lot, it means a lot as far



as investor confidence," said Nizam Idris, regional economist



at IDEAglobal.com in Singapore.



Wahid said on Monday he would not resign, and called upon



hugely popular Vice President Megawati Sukarnoputri to become



more proactive.

title: Emerging  FX  - Depressed by yen, rupiah wretched.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 12 (Reuters) - Asian currencies started the the week on a glum note as doubts over the leadership in Japan and Indonesia came to a head, battering the yen and the rupiah. 

 The rupiah fell past 11,000 for the first time since September 24, 1998 as companies and banks rushed to buy dollars amid mounting concern about the political and economic outlook. 

 Analysts predicted it could slide further, barring capital controls or a significant improvement in the political situation. 

 "If the rupiah continues to go at its current pace, I think the government would come up with fresh measures...ie, one form of capital control or another. In that case, it could pick up to around 10,000," said Andrew Fung, head of Asia Pacific treasury research at Rabobank. 

 "Barring that, there is a possibility that it could go to 13,000. I still think the rupiah should trade above 10,000, but sentiment is driving market dynamics at this point," he said. 

 The Thai baht traded at the lower end of its recent range as good news on the national asset management company, soon to be established to tackle non-performing loans, was clouded by the yen and the rupiah. 

 The Sing dollar slipped past 1.7600 which had been expected to be the Monetary Authority of Singapore's intervention threshold, sparking speculation it could test 1.7650. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar trailed off to three-and-a-half month lows of 1.7620 to the dollar on relatively healthy turnover. 

 Weakness mainly owed to the Indonesian rupiah, which tends to move the Sing dollar when it moves sharply. Singapore and Indonesia have traditionally had close investment ties. 

 Dealers said the lagging stock market following the Nasdaq sell-off and the weaker yen dampened sentiment. They added that Sing dollar selling partly owed to talk of Singapore Telecommunications making a bigger-than-expected bid for Cable and Wireless Optus . 

 Dealers said the Sing dollar was unlikely to fall much beyond 1.7620, a low last seen in late November, due to jitters over intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso trimmed losses to end at around 48.07 per dollar, having fallen to around 48.25 earlier in the day. 

 "That was a knee-jerk reaction to the falling rupiah and the yen. But the sell-off didn't last because we have a relatively stable economy and now the political situation is better off," a trader at a local bank said. 

 He added the peso should settle into a snug range of 47.00 to 48.50 in the short term. 

 "We need to see a firmer stock market, more offshore demand and more foreign investment for the currency to break the range trading," he added. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won continued to be weighed by weakness in the yen and declines in local stocks, gapping down at the open and hitting a an early low of 1,280.1. 

 Exporter and state bank dollar sales near that level kept it from falling any further but dealers expected limited upside as foreign investors remained net sellers of Korean equities for the third straight session. 

 The benchmark KOSPI ended 3.66 percent lower as foreigners unloaded tech shares following the Nasdaq's 5.35 percent drop on Friday. Bank shares were also sold on disappointment with a decision by Korean creditors to support the cash-starved Hyundai Group. Data released on Monday offered little cause for cheer, with the current account surplus almost halving on the month in January to a provisional $684.4 million. 

 Analysts said the faltering semiconductor sector, a main export segment, would keep pressure on the economy. 

 J.P. Morgan said it would cut its 2001 growth forecast for Korea to 3.5 percent or lower from four percent as weakness in the electronics sector remained a concern despite improvements in consumer and business sentiment and industrial output. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hit a 30-month trough, before verbal and actual dollar-selling intervention by Bank Indonesia prompted a bounce. 

 Mounting concerns about the government's inability to contain ethnic violence and revive the economy, and the fate of IMF loans spurred dollar demand from banks and local companies in a thin market. 

 News of the closure of three gas fields by Exxon Mobil Oil Indonesia in northern Aceh on Friday due to security concerns added to the gloom as the Indonesian economy relies heavily on oil and gas exports. 

 The rupiah extended losses after deputy central bank governor Anwar Nasution said BI had limited ability to defend it. 

 That remark was later countered by another BI deputy governor who said the central bank would continue intervening to support the currency and had adequate reserves to do so. 

 Dealers said BI backed its comments with actual dollar sales worth around $5-$10 million, causing the rupiah to bounce above the 11,000 level. 

 "It's almost a one-way market. Bank Indonesia and state banks were among few dollar providers. Exporters are not selling," said a Jakarta dealer. 

 "If it goes on like this, I bet the central bank will do something. I don't think it will be a capital control. They might be looking into ways to force exporters to bring in dollar revenues," he said. 

 Chief economics minister Rizal Ramli said 8,000 was an acceptable level for the rupiah. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was wedged in a narrow 43.55-43.75 range. Investors were reluctant to take profits on the dollar due to gloom in the rupiah and the yen, but they were not willing to build on their already long dollar positions either. 

 The market welcomed news that the soon-to-be-established national asset management company would buy up to 250 billion baht ($5.74 million) of bad loans from private banks at book value net of loan loss reserves. 

 It had earlier said it might absorb as little as 120 billion baht at discounts. 

 "The news seems to be benefitting bank and finance shares more than the baht. I guess people will be watching how efficient and transparent the AMC is and the rate of loan recovery," said a dealer at a European bank in Bangkok. 

 "The baht didn't move much today. The market is already pretty long of the dollar, but at the same time there is no compelling reason to buy the baht either," he said. 

 Baht funding costs offshore nudged up, with the one-month forward rate rising to 1.5/2.5 satang per dollar. TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar slid to its lowest level since January 30, edging closer to 32.50 per dollar on declines in local stocks and a depressed yen. 

 The market was keen to test its downside after Friday's close below 32.40, which prompted speculation the central bank had moved its line of defence back to 32.50. 

 Taiwan shares ended lower for the third straight session as heavyweight electronics shares were hurt by the Nasdaq's drop.
