title: Indonesian Rupiah Ends Flat; Sjahril Effect Short-Lived
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended Asian trade flat Monday after moving higher in the late afternoon following comments by Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin pledging that the central bank will intervene to boost the local unit. 

 Sjahril told reporters the bank will intervene in the market "every day" to support the rupiah, which authorities have repeatedly stressed in recent weeks is undervalued given the improving economy. 

 The governor's comments pushed the dollar to an intraday low just below 8,600 rupiah, but continuing concerns over the Indonesian political situation pushed the U.S. currency up to end at IDR8,608, flat from Friday's close. 

 "If nothing special happens on Tuesday I think we'll see a higher U.S. dollar," said a foreign bank trader in Jakarta. 

 Last month, Sjahril said the central bank would only intervene if it would prove effective. 

 The dollar should trade in an IDR8,600 to IDR8,670 range Tuesday, traders said. At the lower end of the band, local importers are eager to buy dollars, the foreign bank trader said. 

 Among factors hurting the rupiah are concerns that an uncertain political climate is slowing the pace of debt restructuring. 

 Bank Indonesia's major tool to help the rupiah, which has lost 18% since January, is to push up local rates through its weekly auction of Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes. 

 But traders said rates on the one-month notes would have to rise significantly from around 11.13% in recent auctions to halt the currency's slide. 

 With the banking system still on its knees due to huge problem loans, the government won't be keen to raise rates much higher, the foreign bank trader added.

title: Bk  Indonesia  Gov: To  Intervene  In Market To Boost Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin said Monday that the central bank will intervene in to boost the rupiah by selling dollars. 

 "If necessary, we are going to intervene in the market every day," Sjahril told to reporters before making a scheduled appearance before a parliamentary committee on the Bank Bali case. 

 Sjahril, however, declined to disclose the amount dollars that the central bank plans to sell to strengthen the local currency. 

 At 0730 GMT (3:30 a.m. EDT), the dollar was trading at 8,630 rupiah, compared with IDR8,653 in late Asian trading Friday. The rupiah has weakened 18% since early January. 

 Sjahril said the central bank also plans to use the Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes to help boost the rupiah. The notes are auctioned by the central bank every Wednesday . 

 "So far, we only have this (the SBI notes) to help stabilize the rupiah," he added. 

 He didn't explain, however, whether the central bank will raise the interest rates on the SBI notes. 

 The rate on one-month SBI notes rose to 11.13% last Wednesday from 11.07% a weak earlier. 

 Sjahril, in the hearings session Monday, is expected to clarify to the members of the parliamentary committee on whether he was involved in the Bank Bali case. 

 The Bank Bali scandal involved the illegal transfer of funds from the bank to a company linked to the former ruling Golkar party. 

 Separately, Bank Indonesia Senior Deputy Governor Anwar Nasution said that the central bank's Deputy Governor, Subarjo Joyosumarto will resign effective July 1. 

 "Subarjo will then take a post as chief of education and training department of the South East Asian Central Bank Association which is based in Kuala Lumpur," Nasution told reporters. 

 Nasution didn't give further details.

title: Indonesia rupiah buoyed by capital controls talk.
text:
JAKARTA, June 2 (Reuters) - The rupiah was off its intraday highs by late trade on Friday but was still well supported by speculation Indonesia may introduce some form of capital controls in a bid to prop up the beleaguered currency. 

Central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said he was opposed to outright capital controls but would be willing to discuss with the government "grey area" measures such as steps to control the flow of the rupiah. 

 Trade and Industry Minister Luhut Pandjaitan said the idea of capital controls was still being studied, and added that he thought the current foreign exchange regime was too liberal. 

 "The foreign exchange regime is too free, so it needs adjustment," Pandjaitan said. 

 By 0900 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 8,463/8,493 to the dollar, versus 8,640/8,670 in late trade on Wednesday. Jakarta markets were closed on Thursday for a holiday, but the rupiah managed to briefly breach 8,400 in thin offshore trade. 

 The currency ignored bullish April trade data, as well as inflation data from May which was in line with expectations. 

 "It's talk about capital controls that is driving the market," said a dealer at a European bank in Jakarta. "People are suddenly worried about being short of rupiah." 

 Dealers said onshore players actively covered short rupiah positions shortly after the local market open on Friday, boosting the rupiah to a high of 8,410 against the dollar. 

 But they said talk of capital controls remained speculative and may not boost the currency for long. 

 "Many players remain uncertain on what kinds of capital controls the government might be considering. One of the options may be to force the repatriation of exporters earnings back into the country but this is easier said than done," one foreign bank dealer said. 

 In an interview with CNN, Sabirin said the rupiah was undervalued. 

 "On an economic basis I still believe the rupiah should be around 7,000 and perhaps maybe a bit stronger than 7,000," Sabirin said. 

 He said intervention by the Bank of Indonesia to defend the rupiah would depend on the volatility of the exchange rate. 

 "If there is in our view any use for intervention, we do so. But of course we do not want to waste our currency reserves to do intervention that may not be beneficial for the medium-term stability of the curency," he told CNN. ((Andrew Marshall, Jakarta newsroom +62 21 384 6364, Fax +62 21 344 8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesia may consider curbs on rupiah flows.
text:
TOKYO, June 2 (Reuters) - Indonesian central bank governor Syahril Sabirin said on Friday he was opposed to outright capital controls but would be willing to discuss with the government "grey area" measures such as steps to control the flow of the beleaguered rupiah . 

 In a brief telephone interview with CNN from Jakarta, monitored in Tokyo, Sabirin said he believed the rupiah on economic grounds was worth at least 7,000 to the U.S. dollar - more than 17 percent above current levels. 

 "I don't really believe in capital controls for Indonesia but in some grey areas, for example limiting the flow of rupiah and so on..., we may discuss whether or not there is a benefit from that," the central bank chief said. 

 Speculation Indonesia might be on the verge of imposing capital controls gathered momentum on Thursday, aided in part by a comment by the new managing director of the International Monetary Fund, Horst Koehler, that capital controls were not a taboo. 

 But speaking in Bangkok, Koehler said they should be introduced only under special circumstances. 

 Koehler is due to meet Indonesian President Abdurrahman Wahid later on his Asian tour. 

 Frustration with the economic policies of the Wahid administration, especially its perceived failure to accelerate the pace of corporate and legal reforms needed to boost investor confidence, has contributed to a recent slide in the rupiah. 

 Fresh outbreaks of religious and ethnic violence across the sprawling archipelago have also soured sentiment toward the rupiah, which briefly breached the 8,400 to the dollar level on Thursday before falling back to to around 8,450. 

 It was quoted near 8,500 in early Asian trading on Friday. 

 "On an economic basis I still believe the rupiah should be around 7,000 and perhaps maybe a bit stronger than 7,000," Sabirin said. 

 He said intervention by the Bank of Indonesia to defend the rupiah would depend on the volatility of the exchange rate. 

 "If there is in our view any use for intervention, we do so. But of course we do not want to waste our currency reserves to do intervention that may not be beneficial for the medium-term stability of the curency," he told CNN.

title: Bk Indonesia Gov: Interest Rate Rise Wed Due To Weak IDR
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia may have to revise its key macroeconomic forecasts if the rupiah remains weak, central bank Governor Sjahril Sabirin said Wednesday. 

 Speaking at a news conference after meeting parliamentary leaders, Sjahril also said that the increase in interest rates at Wednesday's central bank note auction was an inevitable result of the rupiah's weakness. 

 "This is something that cannot be avoided, this is a result of the weakening rupiah," Sjahril said. 

 He added however, that he doesn't expect interest rates to continue to rising. 

 Interest rates on one-month Indonesia central bank notes jumped four basis points at Wednesday's auction, as yields continued to creep up in the wake of a rate hike in the U.S. and amid the lingering weak rupiah. 

 Traders said the rate increase was an apparent attempt by Bank Indonesia to shore up the flagging rupiah. 

 Sjahril said the central bank was preparing a "pessimistic scenario to face some bad conditions," for all of its key forecasts, including inflation, growth and interest rates. 

 "Now, Bank Indonesia is making preparations in order to revise assumptions, if conditions remain unstable," Sjahril said, although he stressed that the central bank hasn't yet revised any of its forecasts. 

 Bank Indonesia forecasts growth this year of between 3% and 4% and inflation of between 5% and 7%, if the government presses ahead with budgeted fuel price increases. 

 Higher interest rates put direct pressure on the state budget and guiding rates up is something the central bank is clearly reluctant to do. 

 The government has issued IDR309 trillion worth of bonds as of April to recapitalize 25 local banks and is expected to issue a further IDR100 trillion of bonds to recapitalize several state and private banks. 

 The bonds carry fixed and floating rates tied to the average interest rate of Bank Indonesia's three-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes, which currently stands at 10.91%. 

 The government calculates the cost to the budget this year of interest payments on the bonds of 6.5% of gross domestic product. As well as increasing the pressure on Indonesia's recovering economy, hiking rates now would jack up this already massive bond interest payment bill. 

 The rupiah slipped to a seven-month low of IDR8,768 May 12. Although it has since recovered some ground - it ended Asian trade at IDR8,505 Wednesday - the currency remains weak and well off the IDR7,000 to the dollar level on which the 2000 budget is based. 

 Bank Indonesia says the rupiah's weakness is due to political factors, rather than economic issues. It has also sent mixed signals as to whether it would intervene to support the currency. 

 Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Miranda Gultom said earlier that the central bank hadn't intervened Wednesday, although she reaffirmed that Bank Indonesia changes dollars into rupiah on the market as required. 

 Sjahril said he doesn't expect interest rates to continue on an upward trajectory. 

 "I expect the weak rupiah won't be for too long, so interest rates won't keep on increasing," he said. 

 The upward trend in U.S. interest rates has also put Indonesian yields under pressure. Sjahril said he didn't know whether another hike in the U.S. in July would put more pressure on Indonesian rates. 

 "We'll see how the situation is in the market," Sjahril said, adding that the central bank doesn't want to risk raising interest rates.

title: Bk Indonesia - Rupiah Vulnerable To Political Tension
text:
JAKARTA-(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Anwar Nasution said Tuesday the rupiah remained vulnerable to political tensions in the run-up to a special parliament hearing in August at which some lawmakers have threatened to unseat President Abdurrahman Wahid. 

 Anwar said the central bank would intervene if it was considered necessary and effective to defend the currency, which recently slumped to a seven-month low against the dollar. Concerns over friction within Wahid's coalition cabinet fueled that drop. 

 "Bank Indonesia will still intervene in the market as long as it's considered effective," Anwar told reporters. 

 But the central bank isn't likely to guide interest rates higher in order to help the rupiah, as Indonesian rates are higher than in other countries, he said. 

 The bank's one-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia note last Wednesday yielded 10.99%, up from a week-earlier 10.91%. 

 Anwar said that the local currency should strengthen to 7,500 rupiah to the dollar if the government pushed through reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund in the latest letter of intent signed last week. 

 At 0745 GMT, the dollar was trading at IDR8,445, up from IDR8,355 late Monday. 

 -By Simon Montlake; 62 21 3983 1277; smontlake@ap.org

title: Asian  Currencies  Up Late As USD Surge Pauses;S$ Up On GDP
text:
HONG KONG -(Dow Jones)- Most Asian currencies were higher against the U.S. dollar late Friday as the U.S. unit took a pause from its recent rise, the Philippine central bank hiked rates and Singapore's government released stronger-than-expected growth figures. 

 Only the South Korean won stood out as a session loser partly due to the resignation of the South Korean Prime Minister Park Tae-joon, after he admitted to improper property transactions. 

 Dealers also pointed out recent falls in the local stock markets as the main reason for the won's depreciation. Local stock markets have fallen sharply since mid-April due to bearish U.S. markets and worries over the troubled local investment-trusts companies. 

 The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index has fallen 30.7% so far this year, while the over-the-counter Kosdaq index has fallen 46.8%. 

 The dollar was at 1,122.5 won, up from KRW1,118.50 Thursday. 

 Dealers reported only modest trading interest across the board. "It was like a holiday mood," said one dealer at a U.S. bank. Another Singapore trader said the market is waiting to see what Taiwanese President-elect Chen Shui-bien says in his inaugural address Saturday. 

 The upside for the regional currencies will be limited, nonetheless, by the prospects for more rate hikes from the U.S. Federal Reserve in the coming months, said traders. 

 The Singapore dollar was up on news that the city-state's gross domestic product expanded 9.1% on year in the first quarter, above market expectations of just over 7%. 

 The U.S. dollar was quoted at S$1.7285, down from S$1.7333 late Thursday. 

 A rate hike in the Philippines also boosted the peso slightly, with the U.S. dollar trading around 41.64 pesos, down from PHP41.73 late Thursday. With its key overnight rates hiked one half a percentage point, the Philippine central bank was seen as trying to prop up the local unit as the turmoil in the southern Philippines and the U.S. rate hike continued to undermine it. 

 The rupiah was unmoved following the Indonesian central bank's comments, ruling out more support for the country's beleaguered currency. The dollar was quoted at 8,350 rupiah, down from IDR8,550 late the previous day. 

 "Only if needed, Bank Indonesia will intervene in the market; if not (needed) we don't want to intervene," said Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin. 

 However, dealers said continued rupiah-buying by state-run banks helped cap the U.S. dollar at IDR8,500, and is partly behind the gains. 

 Against the Thai baht, the U.S. dollar was also lower, with the U.S. unit quoted at 39.135 baht, down from THB39.245 late Thursday. Dealers said the baht rose in line with other regional currencies. 

 The U.S. dollar was only slightly lower against the Taiwanese currency at NT$30.71, compared with NT$30.730 late Thursday.

title: Indonesian  Central Bank  Rules Out More Rupiah Support
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin said Friday the central bank had no plans to further intervene to support the rupiah. 

 "Only if needed, Bank Indonesia will intervene in the market; if not (needed) we don't want to intervene," Sjahril told reporters. 

 "It takes time to strengthen (the) rupiah because it must be done gradually and depends on the market sentiment." 

 His comments come after he said Wednesday that the central bank had sold less than $300 million to boost the rupiah in the currency market this week. 

 He said Bank Indonesia had spent less than 1% of its foreign exchange reserves to support the currency, but didn't offer more details. 

 Bank Indonesia said that the country's gross international reserves as of May 5, which are net foreign exchange reserves plus outstanding foreign exchange contracts, were at $29.478 billion. 

 The rupiah slumped to a seven-month low last Friday as volatility returned to haunt the currency on a mix of factors that included the expected tightening bias by the Federal Reserve, slow domestic economic reforms and a barrage of confusing comments by senior policymakers. 

 At 0614 GMT, the dollar was trading at IDR8,418, compared with IDR8,350 late Wednesday. The market was closed Thursday for a public holiday.

title: Rupiah boosted by news on IMF letter of intent.
text:
JAKARTA, May 17 (Reuters) - News that the Indonesian government would sign a delayed letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund later on Wednesday boosted sentiment on the rupiah. 

 By 0300 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 8,475/8,500 to the dollar compared with 8,545/8,595 in early trade before the news and 8,500/8,550 in late local trade on Tuesday. 

 "The positive news boosted sentiment on the rupiah. But the upside for the local unit seems to be limited as higher corporate dollar demand emerged at around the 8,450 area," one bank dealer said. 

 The signing of the letter of intent was necessary to release a $400 million loan originally due in April. The IMF delayed release of the loan because of the government's slowness in moving on reforms. 

 Dealers said lingering concerns about President Abdurrahman Wahid's handling of the economy were also likely to limit the rupiah's upside. 

 A decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise borrowing costs by 50 basis points, as expected, its biggest move in five years, surprised no one but helped remove one of the uncertainties hanging over the rupiah, dealers said. 

 "The 50 basis-point hike does help remove one of the negative factors. But concerns remain on the government's poor handling of the economy. Now it no longer has significant external factors to blame," one dealer at a European bank said. 

 Dealers said the market was slow as state banks, which led dollar selling on Tuesday after Wahid asked them to do so, were not yet active in the market in early trade. 

 Wahid on Tuesday asked Bank Indonesia and state banks to help the battered currency which had fallen more than 18 percent against the dollar so far this year. 

 Dealers questioned whether central bank intervention could bring a sustainable recovery in the rupiah - Bank Indonesia has already said it does not regard intervention or interest rate hikes as a viable solution as political factors play a large part in the currency's weakness. 

 Wahid, facing a growing crisis of confidence in his handling of the economy, also ordered his finance minister to review economic projections in this year's budget which are now looking too optimistic. ((Jakarta newsroom +62 21 384 6364, Fax +62 21 344 8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Emerging  FX  - Yen's rebound soothes, but still wary.
text:
SINGAPORE, Dec 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies clawed back 

 some gains late on Friday on the back of the yen's rebound 

 ahead of the weekend and New Year holidays. 

     Financial markets in Hong Kong, Japan, Indonesia, 

 Philippines and Thailand will be closed on New Year's eve while 

currency markets in Taiwan and Korea will operate on Monday. 

     Trading sessions will be shortened in Singapore. Otherwise, 

 most Asian markets will reopen on Wednesday. 

     The yen rebounded to a session high of around 130.75 after 

 the dollar dipped in a bout of dollar profit-taking and 

 option-related sales. 

     By late Tokyo trade, the yen fell again around 131.50 on 

 expectations the Japanese officials would continue to show no 

 sign of tempering their apparent acceptance of a lower yen. 

     The Singapore dollar that touched 11-1/2-year lows at 

 1.8550 early on, bounced back above the 1.8500 level while the 

 Korean won and Taiwan dollar rose above their late Thursday 

 levels. 

 But analysts expected the yen's reprieve to be short-lived. 

 "Moves in the dollar/yen can be vicious at times, and then 

 it is the year end. So most players opted to clear old 

 positions, square out and lock in profits while they can," a 

currency strategist at a Singapore bank said. 

 "But the weak yen story isn't over yet. This retracement is 

 likely to draw in more hedging by corporates and speculators 

 and we'll see more weakness in other Asian currencies." 

 A weaker yen tends to raise competitiveness concerns in 

 Asian regional economies, with Korea, Taiwan and Singapore seen 

 more vulnerable given the similarity of their exports and 

 markets with those of Japan. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar struggled to reach higher ground but 

 was pulled below 1.8500 again by U.S. dollar demand from 

 interbank players who anticipated a weaker yen and bleak 

 economic data next week. 

 The government is scheduled to release its preliminary 

 fourth-quarter GDP data and the whole year's growth estimate on 

 Wednesday. 

 Economists polled by Reuters forecast that the economy this 

 year will contract 2.5 percent year-on-year but grow 1.7 

 percent in 2002. 

 Charts show the U.S. dollar remains heavily overbought 

 against the Sing dollar on the 14-day relative strength index, 

 indicating further correction ahead. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht eked out some gains on last-minute exporter dollar 

 offers, with a minor rebound in the yen providing some support. 

 The market was near to holiday mood and paid little 

 attention to the economic data released by the Bank of Thailand 

 on Friday, dealers said. 

 In November, exports contracted 12.8 percent on the year 

 compared with a year-on-year decline of 14.3 percent while 

 imports shrank 8.7 percent. 

 Despite a drop in trade surplus, the country's current 

 account surplus rose to $537 million from $531 million in 

 October. 

 Further gains in the dollar could be dented by rising baht 

 funding costs in the offshore market, with the one-month rate 

 now quoted at 18/26 satang per dollar against 16/28 late on 

 Thursday. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar regained lost ground and closed higher 

 after 11 straight sessions of decline, drawing strength from 

 the yen's rebound. 

     The currency closed at 35.084 to the dollar on Friday after 

 finishing at a 15-year closing low of 35.127 on Thursday. 

     Dealers in Singapore said players trimmed their long dollar 

 positions while there were no signs of the usually active 

central bank on either side of the market. 

     The market ranged between an intraday low of 35.186 and a 

 high of 35.051. The Taiwan dollar's weakest level this year was 

 an intraday trough of 35.30 in July. 

     Charts showed the dollar was still overbought, with the 

 14-day relative strength index reading at 84.171, but was much 

 lower than 99.183 level seen earlier in the day. 


    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso ended onshore trade lower but was off its early



trough as players covered short peso positions ahead of a long



weekend.



    Monday and Tuesday will be public holidays in Manila and



markets will resume trading on Wednesday.



    Dealers in Manila said importers and corporates pushed the



dollar higher earlier but later took a cue from the yen and



squared out of those positions.



    President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo said she was satisfied



with the level of the peso even if it did not strengthen to 50



as she had previously hoped. The currency was at around 53.61



to the dollar when Arroyo set the target earlier this year.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah slipped to a low of 10,480 before



exports-related inflows pushed it back to around 10,350.



Dealers in Jakarta said the rupiah was under pressure in



early trade from a pick-up in commercial dollar demand, but the



volumes were not large enough to have a big impact on the



rupiah.



Dealers in Singapore said corporates had remained cautious



in recent sessions due to dollar sales by exporters for their



year-end requirements.



In the money market, Bank Indonesia kept its intervention


rates unchanged at 15.125 percent for the overnight rate and



15.875 percent for the seven-day rate.

title: Emerging  FX  - Defiant to yen weakness, inflows watched.
text:
SINGAPORE, Dec 13 (Reuters) - Asian currencies refused to 

 buckle under the yen's weakness in early trade on 

 Thursday, drawing support from seasonal capital inflows and 

 demand for local currencies. 

     Dealers said foreign investors, loathe to report too much 

 cash at the year's end, have been dumping funds into stocks. 

     Dollar offers from exporters and banks seeking to trim long 

 dollar positions ahead of the year end also supported regional 

currencies. 

     The yen sank to a new eight-month low of 126.58 against the 

 dollar overnight on a report by hedge fund group Medley Global 

 Advisory quoting a U.S. official as saying there was no lower 

 limit on the Japanese unit. 

 But the currency clawed back some gains after the Treasury 

 Department said the report did not reflect the agency's 

 position. 

 The market will be watching closely the U.S. November 

 retail sales report due later in the day. It will shed light on 

 consumer spending which accounts for two-thirds of economic 

 activity. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 Gains in some regional currencies, especially the Thai baht 

 and the Indonesian rupiah, provided some psychological support 

 for the Sing dollar. 

 But the currency pared some of its earlier gains after the 

 yen sank back below 126 to the dollar as the Japanese currency

 carries substantial weight in Singapore's trade-weighted basket 

 of currencies. 

 Dealers expected market participants to sell the U.S. 

 dollar on its way to 1.8350 - the level seen as a near-term 

 support for the Sing dollar. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht ran into some resistance at around 43.65 where 

 some players started picking up dollars again, but sporadic 

 dollar sales by exporters and offshore players helped underpin 

 the local currency. 

 Charts show the baht well-supported at 44.10, the 

 38.2-percent retracement of the dollar/baht's October 

 25-December 13 downmove. 

 The market is divided over the direction of Thai interest 

 rates. Some analysts were betting the Bank of Thailand would 

 deliver a long overdue rate cut at its next policy meeting. 

 But others argued there was no point for the central bank

 to cut rates unless the U.S. economy deteriorated further to 

 the point that it was necessary for the Fed to extend its 

 easing cycle. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won managed to defy the yen's gravitational pull and 

 opened slightly higher at 1,272.50, compared with the 

 Wednesday's close of 1,274.4. 

 The local currency was well-supported by expectations of 

 heavy foreign direct investments, but its upside was dented a 

 bit by the yen's weakness and fears of central bank

intervention. 

 Finance Minister Jin Nyum said his ministry was well aware 

 of negative impact of the yen's weakness on the Korean economy 

 and was closely watching its movement. 

 Market sources estimated that December FDI could exceed 

 $2.0 billion. This includes 244 billion won (US$191.5 million) 

 to LG Group's energy units and 155 billion won (US$121.7 

 million) to Shinhan Finance Holding Co . 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was hovering around 10,000 due to recent 

 dollar-selling intervention by Bank Indonesia. Gains were 

 exaggerated by paper-thin trading volumes ahead of the Muslim 

 Eid al-Fitr holiday which marks the end of the fasting month. 

     Corporate players also slowed down buying the U.S. dollar 

 ahead of the year-end. 

     On the macro front, Bank Indonesia said on Wednesday it 

 expected the economy to grow by up to 3.6 percent in the fourth 

 quarter and up to four percent for the full year, but some 

 analysts said these figures were overly optimistic. 

 The central bank's forecasts were roughly in line with 

 earlier official figures, but much lower than the 4.77 percent 

 growth recorded last year.

title: Indonesia  c.bank says  intervening  to prop up rupiah.
text:
JAKARTA, Dec 11 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said on Tuesday Bank Indonesia was in the market propping up the rupiah. 

 "BI (Bank Indonesia) is intervening but only in small amounts," Sabirin told reporters. 

 But he insisted the intervention was not the only factor driving up the currency, one of Asia's most brittle units. 

 "The strengthening of the rupiah has also been due to optimism in the market over the government's privatisation steps," Sabirin said. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 10,125/10.175 by 0935 GMT compared to Monday's level of around 10,200.

title: Emerging  FX  - Hold on but eye wobbly yen, Fed meeting.
text:
SINGAPORE, Dec 11 (Reuters) - Asian currencies held their 

 ground late Tuesday helped by a lack of trading interest in 

 face of a wobbly yen , the Federal Reserve's rate 

 decision and  the approaching holiday season. 

     The dollar gave up its overnight eight-month peaks against 

 the yen, but mounting gloom about the state of the Japanese 

 economy kept it supported. 

     But the yen has been of lesser concern to regional 

currencies of late, with equity-related inflows and rising 

 optimism on a rebound in the U.S. economy, their major export 

 market, instilling some resilience. 

     Though Wall Street's recent losses wiped out part of last 

 week's equity gains across the region, currency players choose 

 to stick to their positions ahead of the Fed's widely expected 

 25 basis point cut in its 2.0 percent fund rate later Tuesday. 

     In local events, Bangkok offered foreign companies tax 

 breaks to set up their regional offices in Thailand as part of 

 an incentive package to attract foreign investment. 

     Korea's import and export prices for November showed a 

 declined from October, suggesting easing demand both at home 

 and abroad. 

     And industrial output in China rose 7.9 percent in 

 November, its lowest in nearly two years, indicating the impact 

 on the broader economy from the global downturn. 


    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won edged up as settlement of local stocks bought by



foreign investors last week resulted in some inflows in the


currency market.



    Dealers in Singapore said news that Korea Telecom plans to



sell up to 15 percent of its stake to foreign investors,



including five percent new shares supported the won.



    That dealers said countered to some extent the impact of



recent net sale of local stocks by foreign investors.



    However, the upside was seen capped by worries that



expectations of a steep fall in the yen could prompt players to



cover their short dollar positions.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso was steady at the close of onshore trade as



corporates kept to the sidelines, while year-end inflows and



remittances from overseas workers capped the downside.



    However, dealers said peso stability was more due to



reluctance to trade ahead of the expected Fed rate cut which is



likely to be followed by a cut of its own by the central bank.



    Media reports have estimated dollar remittances by overseas



Filipino workers, which traditionally accelerate in the last



quarter, were expected to be down by at least $600 million this



year from last year's $6.05 billion.



THAI BAHT



The baht strode higher on the back of dollar offers from



exporters and some U.S. names in the offshore market who had



overhedged their positions earlier this year.



Dealers in Singapore and Bangkok said the local currency


was also underpinned by expectations of wider interest rate



differentials.



While the market is speculating that the U.S. Federal



Reserve will slash key interest rates at its meeting on



Tuesday, it reckons the Bank of Thailand will not follow suit.



Baht funding costs in the offshore market rose slightly to



10/15 satang to the dollar for the one-month rate and 150/171



satang for the 12-month rate.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar ended barely changed at 34.455 after



trading in a tight range of 34.448-34.461, with minimal central



bank intervention.



The market was weighed down by losses in the local stock



market, with foreign investors being net sellers of T$714



billion (US$20.7 million) in domestic shares on Tuesday.



    The market was subdued as players took a wait-and-see



stance ahead of the Fed's meeting later in the day.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah broke past the 10,200 level for the first time



since October 25 thanks to suspected intervention by Bank


Indonesia and fewer dollar bids from local corporates.



    Dealers in Jakarta said trading activity was getting



lighter ahead of the Eid-Al-Fitr holiday this weekend, and most



corporates had fulfilled their dollar requirements ahead of



year-end.



Nevertheless, players hesitated from driving the rupiah



much higher given Indonesia's tricky economic fundamentals.



However, the market shrugged off news that the government



expected to complete this year its merger process for the



country's banks.



SINGAPORE DOLLAR



The Singapore dollar spent the session not far from its



opening levels of around 1.83.



The dollar/Sing found itself confined in a tight range of



1.8293-1.8321. The market struggled first to break the



bottom-side, but ran into the dollar bids. It later tried to



test the upside, only to run into dollar profit-taking.



Dealers said the market was looking for direction, knowing



the weaker yen and the city-state's poor fundamentals were



capping the Sing dollar's upside. However, a stronger euro and



the more confident tone among the regional currencies kept the



local currency from sliding too far.

title: Indonesian Rupiah Ends Higher As State Bks On Sidelines
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended higher Thursday as large state-owned banks, which in recent weeks have been buying dollars for customers, remained out of the market, traders said. 

 State-owned Bank Mandiri and other banks were sidelined, which took the pressure off the rupiah. Indonesian companies need to repay dollar debts by the year-end, which has hurt the local currency in recent weeks. 

 But traders said the debt repayment flow may now be easing. 

 Indonesia's central bank was also rumored to be active Thursday selling dollars, although there was no confirmation of this from the bank itself. Bank Indonesia has a policy of intervening to help the rupiah but never comments on individual actions. 

 The dollar closed at IDR10,425, down from IDR10,470 at Wednesday's finish. 

 But it's still unclear whether debt repayments from companies will stay at lower levels for the remainder of this year. Few banks have a clear idea of exactly what amount of debt companies still have to repay. 

 The dollar moved to an intraday high of IDR10,475 Thursday as players continued to buy the U.S. unit on the belief that Bank Mandiri would be active buying on behalf of corporate clients - mainly state-owned companies. But this buying didn't materialize. 

 The rupiah should remain in a tight range against the dollar for the rest of the year. The dollar remains strongly supported at IDR10,300 due to continued concerns over the country's debt situation.

title: Emerging  FX  - Directionless, local factors rule.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were a mixed 

 bag in late trade on Wednesday as investors looked to local 

 factors for clues on direction. 

     The Thai baht repeatedly failed to break above the key 

 barrier of 44.00 to the dollar amid rumours the central bank

 was in the market to tame its recent rapid rise. 

     The Korean won was dragged down by losses in the local 

 stock market, but it was lifted from its intraday trough by 

 dollar sales by exporters. 

     Meanwhile, the yen clawed back some gains against both the 

 dollar and the euro despite Standard & Poor's downgrading 

 Japan's sovereign rating by a single notch to AA. 

     However, dealers said the single-notch downgrade was better 

 than the two notches many had feared. 

     Going forward, the market will be watching data on U.S. 

 jobless claims due out on Thursday. 

     The Bank of Thailand will release its monthly economic data 

 on Friday, which include trade and current account balances and 

 manufacturing production. 

     SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

     The Singapore dollar found some consolation in the steadier 

 yen, but was thwarted in its attempts to rise by players still 

 bearish over the city-state's economic outlook. 

     Analysts say the Sing dollar has struggled to gain any 

 ground because of the market's view that Singapore still needs 

 to stick to an easy monetary policy to see it through the bad 

 economic times. 

 Unlike other countries, Singapore uses its trade-weighted 

 Sing dollar as its main monetary policy tool rather than 

 interest rates. 

     Dealers said the prevailing market philosophy was to buy 

 dollar on dips, unless the dollar/yen falls past 123.50. 

     KOREAN WON 2 

     The won finished sharply lower against the U.S. dollar due 

 to hefty losses in local stocks and growing fears of a 

 potential war between the United States and Iraq. 

     The won ended at 1,272.1 per dollar against Tuesday's close 

 of 1,265.30. Foreign investors were net sellers of 15 billion 

 won of local stocks. 

     Exporter dollar sales trimmed some losses, but were not 

 enough to lift the won to close in positive territory. 

     On the data front, the October current account surplus came 

 in at $388 million, down from $708 million in September. 


      THAI BAHT



    Talk of the central bank's dollar-buying intervention held



the baht back from breaking above 44 again on Wednesday despite



strong demand for the local currency.



    Charts show 44.30 as the dollar/baht near-term resistance.



    Baht funding costs in the offshore market eased slightly,



with the one-month forward rate quoted at 5/9 satang per dollar



against 7/10 satang earlier.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah struggled to bat off the 10,500 level despite



suspected intervention by the central bank.



    Bank Indonesia was spotted selling around $10 million in



the market early in the session, dealers in Jakarta said.



Nevertheless, state banks were quick to pick up the dollar,



shoving the rupiah to a low of 10,525.



The market remained impervious to news of the government's



attempts to dispose of assets ahead of the year-end. The



government said it will make a decision this week about its



plan to sell a majority stake in state-owned PT Semen Gresik to



Mexico's Cemex. Jakarta has been trying to sell the stake for



three years, and its plan was recently foiled by the West



Sumatran government's take-over of a Gresik unit.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar maintained its poise despite losses on

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Down As Ctrl Bk Stays On Sidelines
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended weaker Tuesday as players covered short-dollar positions after the central bank failed to intervene in the market. 

 Local banks had built up short-dollar positions on expectations the central bank would sell dollars in the market to help buoy the rupiah. 

 This pushed the dollar to an intraday low at IDR10,320. But after the central bank failed to intervene, most players began to unwind positions in the afternoon. 

 The dollar closed Asian trading Tuesday at IDR10,420, slightly higher than IDR10,400 at Monday's close. 

 Bank Indonesia reportedly intervened in the market Monday, helping push the rupiah higher in thin trade. The bank has a policy of intervening, but doesn't comment on specific actions. 

 The dollar should find strong support Wednesday at IDR10,350, with resistance at IDR10,500. 

 In the longer term, Indonesia's currency will remain under pressure as investors are concerned over the country's huge levels of foreign debt. Government foreign debt alone is about $70 billion. 

 Repayment of debt for the rest of this year is likely to keep the lid on any rupiah gains, traders said.

title: Emerging  FX -Slightly hung over from recent rises.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies gave 

 up 

  ground late on Tuesday, wobbling slightly after their recent 

 dizzying rises. 

     As with recent sessions, currencies seeing the most capital 

 inflows into local asset markets fared better during the 

 session. Still, the Korean won, which had led the charge 

 against the dollar, was slightly deflated after the benchmark 

 Korea Composite Stock Price Index ended a touch lower. 

     All in all, though, the yen's nervous state did not have 

 much of an impact on the cheerful tone of the Asian currencies, 

 with the exception of the Singapore dollar. 

     Dealers said regional currencies were benefiting from 

 rising hopes in local markets over the possibility of a U.S. 

 recovery in the second half of next year, which would pull Asia 

 out of its economic doldrums. 

     Some analysts were slightly puzzled as to how regional 

currencies could continue to ignore the yen and focus purely on 

 the U.S. recovery hopes given the fact that Japan is still the 

 region's largest economy. 


    THAI BAHT



    The baht continued to defy the yen, itching to break above



44 to the dollar on exporter dollar offers and dollar sales



from Singapore names.



    Despite strong inflows coming into Thailand recently, the


central bank decided on Tuesday to keep its benchmark 14-day



repo rate unchanged at 2.5 percent.



    Assistant Central Bank Governor Bandid Nijathaworn told a



news conference the ratio of Thailand's foreign reserves to its



short-term debt was at a healthy level of 138 percent.



    He added the central bank was ready to ease monetary policy



if the country's economic outlook worsened.



    Baht funding costs were mostly steady, with the one-month



forward rate quoted at 7/9 satang per dollar and the 12-month



rate at 125/135 satang.



    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won softened slightly after local stocks took a dip and



Korean authorities continued to wag their fingers in



disapproval at the market.



    With the yen and won cross rate nearing lows not seen since



October 2000 according to Reuters data, officials in Seoul



stepped up their campaign in maintaining Korea's export



competitiveness. An official from the finance minister



threatened action if the won continued to rise.



Still, a foreign bank dealer in Singapore said the



authorities were more likely looking to smooth the won's rise



rather than prevent it.



    Foreign investors continued to be net buyers of local



stocks, purchasing 65 billion won of Korean shares on Tuesday.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Singapore dollar shuffled around the 1.8350/60 level



with players still tuning into the yen's travails rather than



the firmness in regional currencies.



    To the Sing dollar's relief, however, dealers described the



market as being exhausted, with few having the energy to push



the dollar/Sing higher. A U.S. bank dealer said there was good



two-way interest in the market.



    That said, if dollar/yen moves much higher overnight, there



could be more losses in store for the Sing dollar.



    Unlike its regional counterparts, the Sing dollar has been



beholden to the yen given the fact that it is managed according



to its trade-weighted basket of currencies, in which the yen



has a large weighting.



    Analysts also add the Sing dollar has not enjoyed the kind



of inflows Korea and Taiwan have in recent weeks.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    Local corporate demand for the dollar drove the peso below



52 in a market unnerved by the fighting in the southern



Philippines.



    Government troops and Muslim gunmen loyal to a rebellious



governor continued their battle on the outskirts of the city of



Zamboanga, leaving at least 28 people dead.



    Dealers in Manila said the violence coupled with the



country's sagging economy drove the peso lower with corporate



dollar bids emerging on any dips below the 52 level.



    A local bank dealer in Manila said power and oil firms have



been strong buyers of the dollar recently.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah was wedged in a narrow range, underpinned by



fears of central bank invention and receding dollar demand from



companies.



    Dealers said one-state oil firm remained a major buyer of



the U.S. currency in the calm market.



    On the fiscal front, Indonesia posted a 16.5 trillion



rupiah ($1.6 billion) budget deficit for the first 10 months,



but most analysts forecast it will not deepen beyond the yearly



target of 54.3 trillion rupiah.



Meanwhile, Bank of Indonesia kept its intervention rates in



the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 15.125 percent



for the overnight rate and 15.875 percent for the seven-day



rate.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar continued to advance against the U.S.



dollar despite some consolidation in the local stock market.



Dealers said the currency was boosted by seasonal exporter



dollar sales and improved earnings outlook for some major



semiconductor companies.



The Taiwan dollar closed at 34.468 to the dollar compared

title: Emerging  FX -Charge higher, but c.banks stand in way.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Asian currencies reclaimed 

 lost ground against the dollar late on Monday, propped up by 

 capital inflows in local asset markets. 

     The Korean won led the charge against the dollar, touching 

 seven-month highs despite verbal intervention by the Korean 

 authorities. Even suspected dollar sales by the authorities 

 failed to dampen the won's high spirits. 

 With foreign funds showing little sign of letting up on 

 their buying spree of Korean stocks, more and more analysts are 

 saying Korea is one of the few bright spots in Asia. 

 But the cheer in Korea was spilling over to other regional 

 markets, with the Thai baht and Taiwan dollar also recouping 

 some ground from the dollar thanks to news of their own capital 

 inflows. 

 While they were temporarily outnumbered, pessimists said 

 the strength in regional currencies was unlikely to last in the 

 long term, especially in view of the weaker yen. They say the 

 recent strength in regional currencies was also largely due to 

 the excessive long dollar positions being held in the regional 

 markets. 

 Some analysts say if weakness in the yen persists, central 

 banks were more likely to step up their efforts to prevent 

 their currencies from rising too much to protect their export 

 competitiveness. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won stole the limelight, rising to levels not seen 

 since March this year on soaring sentiment. 

 Foreign equity inflows and the country's respectable 

 economic performance in the face of the global economic 

 slowdown have helped the won rise steadily in recent weeks. 

 The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index 

 gained 4.55 percent to close at a new 14-month high, with 

 foreign investors net buyers of stocks again. Since 

 mid-October, foreign investors have bought some $2 billion 

 worth of local stocks. 

 Korean authorities tried their best to temper the won's 

 rise, verbally intervening twice during the day by saying the 

currency's strength was not desirable given the current 

 economic climate. Dealers in Seoul said state banks were 

 spotted selling dollars in the market, but to little avail. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht touched a high of 44.07 before coming back down to 

 earth when foreign banks in Bangkok bought back the dollar. 

 Inspired by rises in other regional currencies and recent 

 capital inflows into local markets, the baht came close to 

 testing 44.00 - a level it has not broken since September 17. 

 Dealers in Bangkok said the sell-off in the dollar/baht was 

 spurred by offshore foreign banks, who triggered a number of 

 stop-loss dollar sell orders. But when the baht proved unable 

 to reach the 44.00 level, players across the board began buying 

 the dollar/baht again. 

 Some dealers said there was talk the Bank of Thailand was 

 on the bid for dollar. The central bank has said in the past 

 that one of its priorities was to maintain its forex reserves. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar had a brief moment in the sun, rising 

 above 1.83 before dollar bulls beat it back down again. 

     Still, the currency managed to lengthen its chain to the 

 yen, and resisted serious falls despite the yen's wobbly state. 

     However, dealers said the view on the Sing dollar had not 

 brightened, remaining firmly negative given the city-state's 

 struggling economy. The government's suggestion on Friday that 

 Singapore's closely guarded reserves might be used to help 

 counteract its worst-ever recession only served to highlight 

 the dire straits the economy was in. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah steadied in moderate trade, with corporate 

 dollar bids and central bank dollar offers keeping it within a 

 tight range of 10,410-10.460. 

 After Bank Indonesia's suspected intervention late last 

 week, the market was still holding long dollar positions at the 

 open of trade, dealers in Jakarta said. They added dollar sales 

 from the central bank and the Indonesian Bank Restructuring 

 Agency also helped the rupiah steady itself. 

     However, the rupiah's gains were limited because local 

 corporates were on the hunt for dollar. 

     The government continued to race against the clock in 

 disposing assets before the end of the year to help plug the 

 country's gapping budget deficit. IBRA said it has shortlisted 

 nine bidders for a stake of up tp 51 percent in the country's 

 largest retail bank, PT Bank Central Asia. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso climbed in line with the regional currencies, with 

 a trickle of dollar inflows from overseas Filipino workers also 

 supporting it. 

 But the peso's gains were far from spectacular. Dealers in 

 Manila said players were unwilling to unwind their dollar 

 positions because the dollar inflows were largely a seasonal 

 factor due to Christmas. 

 On the bright side, elections for a new provincial governor 

 in the semi-autonomous Muslim region of the southern 

 Philippines were peaceful, despite fears of violence after a 

 failed revolt against Manila. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 Once again, the Taiwan dollar reclaimed a bit of ground 

 only to cede its gains because of the central bank. 

 Analysts say the central bank, which has been keeping the 

 exchange rate stable amid the island's recession, was unlikely 

 to let go of its reins on the currency ahead of key 

 parliamentary elections on Saturday.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Ends Up On Suspected  Intervention
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The rupiah recouped early losses to end slightly higher Friday on suspected Bank Indonesia intervention. 

 Dealers estimated that the central bank sold around $10 million Friday to help the local unit, which was depressed by dollar demand from local companies. 

 The dollar ended at 10,500 rupiah, down from its close Thursday at IDR10,560. The dollar had risen to an intraday high of IDR10,590 shortly after interbank trading opened and before Bank Indonesia was suspected to have flexed its muscles in the market. 

 "Unlike Thursday, Bank Indonesia's intervention today was successful thanks to the thin trading volume," said a dealer with a foreign bank. 

 Bank Indonesia doesn't comment on suspected intervention, although officials have frequently stated that it will defend the currency if needed. 

 Dealers said dollar demand will continue ahead of the end of the year as local companies have to pay maturing offshore debts and multinational companies here send profits back to their home countries. 

 Bank Indonesia is expected to remain the largest dollar supplier in the market due to the absence of foreign capital inflows, dealers added. 

 The dollar is expected to trade between IDR10,400 and IDR10,600 next week.

title: Asian  Currencies  Mixed Late; Renewed US Dlr Bullishness
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Asian currencies were mixed late Friday, with the Singapore dollar feeling the brunt of the market's renewed bullishness toward the U.S. currency. 

 The euphoria over a slew of better-than-expected U.S. economic indicators - including a drop in jobless claims - and Wall Street's recent rally have fueled hopes that an economic rebound may be around the corner. This, combined with signs of progress in the U.S.-led military campaign against terrorism, have bolstered the dollar this week. 

 As speculation mounts that the U.S. Federal Reserve might reverse its current easing cycle, amid hopes the U.S. economy would recover by the second quarter of next year, the Eurodollar futures market is betting that U.S. interest rates will rise by about a percentage point next year, dealers said. 

 "That is keeping the dollar buoyant against the regional currencies, especially against the Singapore dollar," said a dealer at a European bank. 

 But some analysts said the market is getting carried away. 

 "I don't think they're ready to hike so quickly," said Philip Wee, a market strategist at Singapore's DBS Bank. "The market has forgotten that this is one of the worst times the Fed has had in a long while, in dealing with so many uncertainties." 

 The U.S. dollar was especially strong against the Singapore currency, climbing to S$1.8365, from S$1.8324 late Thursday, after a day of erratic trading. 

 A large local bank had dominated trading, selling the U.S. currency at higher levels while picking it up again at cheaper levels, dealers said. 

 As sentiment toward the U.S. currency turns increasingly positive, a test of the psychologically important S$1.8400 appears imminent, market watchers said. 

 Even a milder-than-expected 21.6% fall in Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in October and comments by the Monetary Authority of Singapore it is unlikely to ease policy further "for now" failed to ruffle the U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 "When we look at monetary conditions, it is currently very easy. Monetary conditions are conducive for recovery. I don't see any need for concern," said Khor Hoe Ee, a managing director at Singapore's central bank. 

 Some market observers have been calling for the MAS to further ease monetary policy in coming months as Singapore sinks deeper into a recession. 

 Singapore's gross domestic product shrank 5.6% in the third quarter from a year earlier, following a 0.5% contraction in the second quarter. 

 The New Taiwan dollar ended barely changed at NT$34.500 against the U.S. currency, compared with NT$34.501 Thursday. 

 The central bank bought an estimated US$150 million throughout the session to offset the appreciating pressures on the local currency from U.S. dollar sales by exporters and foreign fund inflows, dealers said. 

 After the market closed, the government said Taiwan's economy contracted by 4.21% in the third quarter on-year, as the Sept. 11 attacks in the U.S. dealt a fresh blow to the already ailing global economy and demand for Taiwan's products. 

 The government slashed its 2001 GDP forecast to a contraction of 2.12%, from a decline of 0.37%. 

 The New Taiwan dollar will likely show minimal reaction to the GDP data, which wasn't as bad as the market had thought; instead, persistent equity inflows will continue to keep the currency buoyed, analysts said. 

 The South Korean won ended little changed, as foreign equity inflows tapered and with the yen relatively stable, dealers said. 

 The dollar ended at 1,283.0 won, compared with KRW1,283.3 Thursday. 

 Foreigners bought a net KRW1.1 billion in Korean shares Friday, compared with a net KRW100 billion in each of the last two sessions. 

 The Philippine peso strengthened slightly as banks, bracing for more remittance inflows from overseas Filipino workers ahead of the Christmas holidays, trimmed their long dollar positions, dealers said. 

 Bank of America said the peso also found partial support from the government's announcement earlier Friday that U.S. regulators have given the Philippines approval to sell up to US$1.2 billion in global bonds for budget support. 

 The dollar closed at 51.920 pesos on the Philippine Dealing System, down from PHP52.045 Thursday. 

 Dragged by the Singapore dollar, the Thai currency was slightly weaker at 44.475 baht to the U.S. dollar, compared with THB44.445 late Thursday. 

 Light intervention by Indonesia's central bank kept the local currency steady at IDR10,635 rupiah against the dollar, compared with IDR10,625 late Thursday, dealers said.

title: Emerging  FX  - Rangebound, but dollar may advance.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 14 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were 

 stuck in recent ranges early on Wednesday, even as the dollar 

 held reign over the other major currencies. 

     Regional currencies have recently been torn between a 

 softer yen and central banks keen on supporting their 

currencies. Moreover, diminishing interest in these markets 

 have also conspired to hold the currencies hostage to their 

 recent ranges. 

     Trading in the regional currencies may be muted because 

 markets in Singapore were closed for a public holiday. 

     Nevertheless, any major gains by the dollar against the yen 

 could unnerve the Asian currencies. 

     Sentiment towards the dollar received a boost after 

 Northern Alliance fighters in Afghanistan marched into the 

 capital city of Kabul as the ruling Taliban fled. That victory 

 in the U.S.-led campaign against the Taliban prompted players 

 to unwind their safe positions in the European currencies. 

 News, too, that a plane crash in the New York City borough 

 of Queens was likely an accident also becalmed a skittish 

 market. 

     Some in the market warned, however, that the euphoria may 

 be premature, with the U.S. economy still facing tough times. 


    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won firmed slightly thanks to rises in the local stock



market. But any sign of selling by foreign investors could



reverse the won's direction.



    Net foreign stock sales had overshadowed positive news that



Standard and Poor's had raised Korea's foreign currency rating.



    Foreign investors sold a net 68 billion won worth of local



stocks on Tuesday after buying a net of only 11 billion won on



Monday.



    Korea's adjusted unemployment rate rose month-on-month in



October to 3.5 percent from 3.3 percent in September, with the



national statistics office reporting that more people in their



thirties and fifties were seeking jobs.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar held fast to its recent range of around



34.50 despite exporters' dollar sales.



The currency has been unable to muster enough strength to



break free from the 34.50 level because of the central bank's



vigilance. Dealers and analysts say the bank has been in the



market nearly every day to ensure a stable exchange rate.



Faced with the possibility of Taiwan's first full-year



contraction and fragile domestic confidence, the central bank


has been keen to maintain a steady rate.



THAI BAHT



The baht remained firm against the dollar, though it was



starting to look fragile as unwinding of long dollar positions



by offshore names began to slow.



A softer yen prevented the baht from gaining more ground as



foreign players began buying back the dollar to cover their



short dollar positions against the other major currencies.



The market was also wary of possible intervention by the


central bank to block the baht's rise. Some in the market said



the bank was seeking to keep the baht at competitive levels,



and to balance any gains related to inflows for the country's



largest ever initial public offering, the sale of 30 percent of



state oil and gas firm PTT Plc.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah steadied around above the 10,700 level, with



players remaining on their toes over central bank intervention.



But, despite the threat of intervention, sentiment towards



the persistently weak currency was glum given Indonesia's



plethora of economic and political woes.



On the political front, the market was still skittish over



potential violence after a prominent pro-independence leader in



the restive province of Irian Jaya was found dead over the



weekend. Nearly 10,000 people turned out on Tuesday to march



peacefully behind the body of Theys Eluay.



Underlining Indonesia's economic problems, the country's



chief economics minister Dorodjatun Kuntjoro-Jakti said on



Tuesday the country was not considering cutting its already



thin spending for the 2001 budget despite growing concerns over



the country's debt levels.



And dealing the rupiah another blow, foreign investment



approvals in January-September fell to $6.05 billion from



$12.25 billion last year. Frightened by the country's chronic



political instability and the slow pace of reforms, foreign



investors have been avoiding Indonesia for months, which has



caused a dwindling supply of dollars in the market amid growing



dollar demand from local corporates seeking to service or repay



debt.



PHILIPPINE PESO



The peso was trapped between wariness over central bank

intervention and growing fear in the market that this year's



dollar remittances from overseas Filipino workers was not going



to be as strong as the market had hoped.



In fact, analysts say dollar remittances were likely to



slow as many overseas workers may have lost their jobs because



of the global economic downturn. Some analysts argue that the



link between a stronger peso and remittances ahead of Christmas



was always tenuous.



Meanwhile, the central bank said it thought the peso may



firm to 51 to the dollar before the end of the year because of



dollar inflows.



It added that it had not intervened in the currency market



for some time. But, dealers in Manila have said they suspected



that bank had been in the market to defend the peso.

title: Emerging  FX  - Helped by firmer yen, North Asia leads.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies firmed 

 early Friday drawing strength from the yen that gained 

 on the back of a sharp fall in the euro . 

     The yen rose to one-month highs against the dollar which 

 was dragged down by the euro's slide to six-week lows against 

 the Japanese currency after the European Central Bank's 

 larger-than-expected interest rate cut. 

 The 50-basis-point cut failed to boost investor confidence 

 and instead backed views in the market that the ECB was behind 

 the curve. The ECB's minimum bid rate now stands at 3.25 

 percent. 

 The move, however, has raised hopes the combined easing in 

 the U.S. and Europe would help global economy climb out of the 

 severe downturn in coming months. 

 Those hopes and continued equity-related inflows could help 

 Korean won and Taiwan dollar which saw two-month and four-month 

 peaks respectively on Thursday. 

 The won's upmove was also supported by the central Bank of 

 Korea's views that foreign exchange market was expected to 

 maintain stability on sustained dollar oversupply. 

 Players in the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso would 

 continue to focus on flows and central bank moves to aid the 

currencies, mired in domestic economic and political woes. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won gapped higher at the open on the lingering cheer 

 from the Bank of Korea's optimistic outlook for the won, 

 breaking the 1,285 level for the first time since September 12. 

 The Bank of Korea kept rates steady on Thursday because of 

 recent hopeful signs for the Korean economy. And despite 

 issuing a warning about future downside risks, it predicted 

 that the local foreign exchange market would remain steady 

 thanks to dollar inflows. 

     For several weeks, foreign investors have been on a buying 

 spree of Korean stocks. 


    TAIWAN DOLLAR



    The Taiwan dollar edged higher on hopes of continued



equity-linked foreign inflows.



    Foreign investors were net buyers of 2.36 billion Taiwan



dollar worth of local stocks on Thursday, after selling a net



511 million Taiwan dollars on Wednesday.



    The currency touched a four-month high on Thursday before



the central bank pulled it down to the well-worn range around



34.50.



    Analysts said as the Taiwan dollar was seen as a barometer



of investor confidence on the economy, the approaching



elections could mean authorities would look for a measured



appreciation of the local currency.



Given the weak external and domestic conditions such an



appreciation was unlikely to help the economy, an analyst at a



U.S. bank in Singapore warned, saying players should be looking



at buying dollars at dips.



SINGAPORE DOLLAR



The Sing dollar edged slightly lower, hovering just above



1.8200 in early thin trade.



Dealers said the currency was pressured partly by rumoured



purchases of the euro and the baht by local investors, possibly



to invest in assets there.



Local names and U.S. names were also heard buying the U.S.



dollar from 1.8165. However, dealers said the U.S. dollar was



unlikely to sail through 1.8200 without difficulty given



potential profit taking around that level.



THAI BAHT



The baht found a toehold around 44.45 after a stop-loss was



triggered at 44.60 in the previous session, but charts show the



dollar should be well-supported at 44.40.



Dealers said offshore buying of the local currency against



the U.S. dollar and the Sing dollar might be linked to foreign



investors' plans to buy shares of state-owned Petroleum



Authority of Thailand (PTT) later this month.



PTT is expected to raise up to 32 billion baht (US$719



million) from its IPO by offering up to 920 million shares to



the public at 31-35 each during November 15-21.



Dealers said apart from technical factors, the dollar/baht



should also be supported by the fact that baht funding costs in



the offshore market has eased.



The one-month forward rate fell to 6/10 satang per dollar



from around 10/15 earlier this week. The 12-month rate remained



firm at 125/150 satang.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH

News that international donors granted Indonesia $3.73

because it was long expected. Though donors aired their



complaints about Jakarta's haphazard approach to reform, there



was little doubt the aid money would be granted given the



precarious state of Indonesia' stability.



    Moreover, Indonesia is also the world's most populous



nation, adding to its geopolitical importance.



    Still, sentiment towards the currency had yet to turn



around because of the challenges that the government has to



tackle. On top of that, dealers in Jakarta said Bank Indonesia



has been the only supplier of the dollar in recent sessions.



    They said local corporates may look to pick up dollars

They said re-introduction of a tiering scheme for overnight

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Higher As Donors Support '02 Budget
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah closed higher against the dollar Thursday after international donors pledged $3.14 billion to help finance the 2002 budget deficit, traders said. 

 After touching an intraday high of 10,600 rupiah, the dollar closed at IDR10,485 compared with IDR10,638 Wednesday. 

 News that Indonesia will receive the funds from international donors for next year's budget lifted sentiment toward the local currency. 

 Jemal-ud-din Kassum, the World Bank's East Asia and Pacific vice president, said the funds reflect the commitment of the lenders toward Indonesia, under the Consultative Group On Indonesia. 

 However, he said they had also urged the Indonesian government to work quickly on reforms to help spur an economic recovery. 

 "It's very good news for Indonesia," said a trader. 

 Traders said Bank Indonesia also intervened heavily to bring the dollar back below IDR10,500. 

 They said further central bank intervention is expected to keep the pair in a IDR10,400 to IDR10,500 range Friday.

title: Emerging  FX  - Rangebound, focus on central banks,.
text:
SINGAPORE, Nov 8 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were confined 

 to a tight range in early trade on Thursday with many players 

 sidelined ahead of central bank interest rate-setting meetings 

 in Europe, South Korea and the Philippines. 

     Most dealers were expecting the European Central Bank (ECB) 

 to cut interest rates by 25 basis points on the view that it is 

 behind the curve on monetary policy. 

     In Korea, a Reuters poll showed nine out of 10 economists 

 forecast the Bank of Korea's monetary policy committee would 

 leave its key overnight call rate unchanged at 4.0 percent. 

     They said a recent fresh batch of healthy data is likely to 

 take pressure off the central bank to lower borrowing costs for 

 this month. 

     But dealers reckoned the Philippine central bank would cut 

 its key overnight borrowing and lending rates after the Federal 

 Reserve's reduction on Tuesday. 

     The two-day meeting between the Indonesian government and 

 donors, which come under the umbrella of Consultative Group of 

 Indonesia, ends on Thursday. Jakarta is seeking $3-4 billion in 

 fresh aid from its donors. 

     The government's failure so far to sell its assets and 

 privatise state firms to secure much-needed funds to plug its 

 budget deficit has proven to be a contentious issue with donors 

 and lenders who are concerned about the country's fiscal 

 stability. 


    INDONESIAN RUPIAH



    The rupiah was holding up rather well, thanks to suspected


intervention by Bank Indonesia.



    Since Tuesday, when it touched the 11,000 mark for the



first time since July 23, the rupiah has strengthened by some



four percent.



    Dealers in Jakarta said the central bank has spent a



relatively huge amount of dollars to defend the rupiah. A



European bank dealer estimated the bank unloaded over $50



million on Wednesday. Bank Indonesia had $29.46 billion in



international reserves as of the third week of October.



    Still, dealers said local corporates were likely to pick up



dollars around 10,500, adding the rupiah's outlook was still



poor given that the central bank was the only source of dollar



supply. THAI BAHT



    The baht followed the regional currencies in a dearth of



fresh local leads, with dealers expecting it to be confined



within its recent range.



    Charts show that the dollar/baht would run into some



resistance at 44.68 which represents the 38.2 retracement of



the dollar/baht's July 23-September 12 downmove.



    The latest RSI reading indicated the dollar/baht is still



trading in neutral territory, but heading toward the oversold



line of 30.



    Dealers in Bangkok said players were likely to pick up



dollars on its way down below 44.60, given baht funding costs



have eased.



    In the offshore market, funding costs have eased markedly,



with the one-month forward rate at 5/15 satang per dollar.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The Philippine peso opened slightly firmer at 51.87 to the



dollar compared with Thursday's close of 51.88, capitalising on



remittances from overseas Filipino workers.



    Sentiment was also boosted by the government's optimistic



forecast for the third quarter growth.



    Socio-Economic Secretary Dante Canlas said on Wednesday he



expected annual gross domestic product growth in the



July-September period to exceed the initial forecast of 2.8



percent.



Dealers said the market expected the central bank to pare



its benchmark rates further by 25 basis points when they meet



later in the day.



SINGAPORE DOLLAR



The Singapore dollar gained a bit more confidence thanks to



the steady yen, with sentiment also cheered by forthcoming bond



issues by local companies.



Singapore Telecommunications said on Wednesday it planned



to raise the equivalent of $1.5 billion in its debut global



bond offering, though the size, structure, timing, and


currencies were not given.



Singapore Airlines and local rail operator SMRT Corp also



plan to launch bond issues of S$800 million and S$300-S$500



million, respectively.



Dealers said these bond issues would help to support the



local dollar for now, with the market looking to sell the U.S.



dollar on rallies.



TAIWAN DOLLAR



The Taiwan dollar rose slightly on the back of local stock



gains, mindful that the island's central bank was keeping a



close watch over it.



Since late October, the Taiwan dollar has been idling



around 34.52 after trading in an increasingly narrow range in



September.



Dealers in Singapore say the market is reluctant to push



the exchange rate either way given the central bank's almost



daily presence in the market.



    Analysts say the bank is eager to maintain a stable rate to



ensure competitiveness and domestic confidence.



    Indeed, the central bank's efforts have been so successful



that it was able to cut interest rates without moving the



exchange rate much.



    The bank eased key interest rates by 25 basis points to



record lows on Wednesday in a move to further boost domestic



confidence. Analysts say the bank's easing has primarily helped



avert a liquidity crunch given the number of bad loans in the



banking system.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Ends Up On Pft-Taking,  Intervention  Talk
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah rebounded against the dollar in volatile trade Tuesday on profit-taking, spurred by talk of central bank intervention, after the local unit fell to a new three-month low earlier in the day, dealers said. 

 The dollar closed at 10,835 rupiah, down from its close Monday at IDR10,940. The U.S. currency briefly touched IDR11,000 earlier in the day, a level unseen since late July. 

 However, suspected Bank Indonesia's intervention along with profit-taking on the dollar rescued the battered local unit, dealers said. They suspect that the central bank sold between $15 million and $20 million Tuesday. Bank Indonesia's officials weren't available for immediate confirmation. 

 The dollar's slide below IDR10,900 prompted some market participants, who were still holding long dollar positions to sell their dollars back at loss. These dragged the dollar to an intraday low of IDR10,720 before fresh bids by local companies pushed it higher. 

 "We sold around $20 million today (Tuesday) to take profit as the market has been overly long on the dollar," said a dealer with a foreign bank. 

 Underlying sentiment on the rupiah, however, remains bearish as the market doesn't foresee much improvement in Indonesia's economy or investment climate, dealers said. 

 The market will closely watch international creditors' two-day meeting commencing Wednesday in Jakarta. They are expected to pledge new loans of between $3 billion and $4 billion to Indonesia to help finance the 2002 state budget. 

 Dealers expect the dollar to trade between IDR10,750 and IDR10,900 Wednesday.
