title: Bk  Indonesia  Gov:To  Intervene  If Necessary To Aid Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Indonesia's central bank governor said Wednesday the monetary authority stands ready to intervene to help the rupiah if necessary. 

 The rupiah is falling Wednesday as local companies continue to demand dollars for debt repayment. The U.S. currency is at 9,725 rupiah. The dollar was quoted between IDR9,520 and IDR9,560 late Tuesday in Asian trade. 

 Jakarta-based bankers said the central bank sold about $30 million to $50 million Tuesday to help stall the rupiah's slide. But the intervention had little effect given the large corporate demand for dollars. 

 "We will intervene in the market if necessary," Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin told reporters. 

 Indonesia has no plans to immediately follow the U.S. 50-basis point rate cut Monday, Sjahril added. Indonesian inflation remains a problem as a weak rupiah this year has pushed up the cost of imported goods. 

 But rates also are unlikely to rise, he said. Later Wednesday, the central bank will auction one-month SBI notes, which yielded an average 17.66% at last week's auction. 

 "Am not expecting the interest rate to go up again," he said.

title: Bank  Indonesia  says might  intervene  to help rupiah.
text:
JAKARTA, Sept 19 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank said on Wednesday it was considering intervening in the foreign exchange market to prop up the rupiah which has slumped to a seven-week low. 

 "We can start any time. Of course we never say when and how much, but we do have room to do that," deputy governor Miranda Goeltom told Reuters when asked if the central bank would soon intervene soon. 

 She said last week's devastating attacks on the U.S. and a delay in a vital debt rescheduling deal by the Paris Club of creditors had created uncertainty in the market. 

 "But Indonesia has already met all prerequisites for the Paris Club deal so there should be no concern about this." 

 At 0500 GMT, the rupiah was quoted at 9,710/9,750 against the dollar. 

 She also said there was a "likelihood" the benchmark SBI interest rates would fall in Wednesday's weekly auction from 17.66 percent the previous week.

title: Emerging  FX  - Softer, eye Japan moves to curb yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 18 (Reuters) - Most regional currencies

 softened early on Tuesday after the dollar held up despite 

 sharp falls on Wall Street, thanks in part to Japanese efforts 

 to rein in the yen . 

  The Bank of Japan (BOJ) flexed its muscles on Monday, 

intervening for the first time in nearly a year to try and halt 

 a damaging rise in the currency. The intervention also won the 

 tacit approval of U.S. Treasury Secretary Paul O'Neill who said 

 it was appropriate for the Japanese economy. 

     The focus now is the BOJ's monetary policy meeting, which 

 runs from today to Wednesday, with expectations high it will 

 follow the lead of the Federal Reserve and ease further. 

     "I think the BOJ will be serious about taking more action 

 on the yen as, though the U.S. is suffering, Japan's economy is 

 suffering more," said a senior analyst from a U.S. bank. 

     "But it is difficult to tell how successful it (BOJ) will 

 be and what the exact effect would be on the regionals," he 

 said. 

     Efforts to curb the yen coupled with aversion to the U.S. 

 dollar given economic conditions and last week's recent terror 

 attacks could still benefit the euro -- an important component 

 for the Singapore dollar's trade weighted basket, he said. 

     Rate cuts by central banks in the United States, Europe and 

 Canada overnight suggested similar moves by certain countries 

 in the region sometime soon. 

     Hong Kong had already eased by 50 basis points and 

 economists said the Philippines was likely to move soon, 

 possibly followed by South Korea. 

     Taiwan's financial markets are closed for a second day as 

 the island begins a massive clean-up in the wake of Typhoon 

 Nari which flooded the capital and killed at least 30 people. 


    SINGAPORE DOLLAR



    The Singapore dollar headed south to 1.7365 per dollar



following the concerted rate cuts abroad, with market talk



centred on rumours the monetary authority (MAS) had intervened.



    Dealers said the local unit continued to trade at the



strong end of the MAS' assumed trading range and that the bank



was likely to lead the currency lower following rate cuts



abroad.



    "There is talk of official buying of dollars as the Sing



looks as though it has a lot more room to depreciate," said a



dealer from a European bank.



    "With all the central banks cutting rates, the MAS is bound



to weaken the Sing. We're looking for 1.7420 today," he said.



    The currency was likely to trade between 1.7350 and 1.7450



in the coming days if the G3 currencies continued to hover



around current levels, he said.



    KOREAN WON         -2



    The won opened barely changed at 1,298.5 to the dollar



against the Monday's close of 1,298.7 as players took a



wait-and-see stance ahead of the BOJ meeting.



    The currency was likely to move in a narrow range, caught



between hopes of capital inflows and importer hedging activity



after it touched an intraday low of 1,300 the previous session.



    There were unconfirmed rumours that General Motors (GM.N)



would be signing a memorandum of understanding for its



prospective purchase of Daewoo Motors.



    Bank of Korea vice governor Park Chul said the central bank


had no plans to convene a monetary policy board meeting ahead



of its next scheduled meeting on October 11.



    But analysts said central bank policymakers could still opt



for an early rate cut as last week's terror attacks on the



United States, a main destination for Korea exports, were



poised to tip Korea's feeble economy into a downward spiral.



INDONESIAN RUPIAH



The rupiah dipped to a five-week low around 9,400,



triggered by dollar buying from foreign banks and corporates.



    Trading conditions remained thin, with deals largely driven



by commercial needs, exaggerating volatility in the currency.



    Dealers said they expected more intervention by Bank


Indonesia after it appeared to enter the market at the 9,260



level on Monday. As a result, the rupiah was unlikely to fall



much below 9,400 in the near-term.



Indonesia's bank restructuring agency said on Monday that



it plans to sell assets worth $1.04 billion through open



auction before the end of the year to help plug the state's



gaping budget deficit.



THAI BAHT



The baht pulled back to 44.10 per dollar so surrendering



most of MOnday's gains, as the market paused for fresh



directions after the Fed's aggressive rate cut and ahead of the



BOJ's policy meeting.



There was also talk the central bank was in the market on



Monday to buy the dollar below 44.00 after one Japanese bank



which normally deals on behalf of the Bank of Thailand was seen



in the market.



    A strong baht could hurt the country's exports which



account for almost 60 percent of its gross domestic product.



    The one-month forward rate rose to 8/13 satang for dollar



offshore and 1.25/1.75 satang onshore.



    PHILIPPINE PESO

    Players were cautious ahead of a special Monetary Board



meeting later in the day. Central Bank Governor Rafael



Buenaventura said the bank would convene the meeting to discuss



what policy move to take following the Fed's cut, with much



speculation they will deliver an easing of their own.



    The central bank's overnight borrowing rate is currently at

title: Emerging  FX  - Pare early gains after Japan buys dlrs.
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Most regional currencies

 gave up earlier gains fuelled by dollar bears on Monday after 

 Japan's monetary authorities intervened for the first time in 

 nearly a year to try and halt a damaging rise in the yen 

 . 

     The regionals had been p(ushing higher as the dollar 

 suffered across the board but a fall to seven-month lows under 

 117.00 yen sparkled the Japanese into selling yen for 

 dollars. 

     The Bank of Japan was believed to have bought up to at 

 least $1.0 billion to curb the yen's strength, dealers said. 

 But with only limited success since in late trade the dollar 

 had faded back to 117.15 yen from highs around 118. 

     The intervention did not come as a surprise given that 

 Japanese officials had expressed a desire to see a weaker yen 

 to help Japan's economy avoid recession. 

     Falling Asian stock markets ahead of a resumption of trade 

 in U.S. equities later on Monday also weighed on the regionals, 

 dealers said. 

     "Regional currencies have given back most of their recent 

 gains, underscoring the fact that they probably should weaken 

 from here," said an economist from a European bank. 

     "As soon as we see some stability in the United States, the 

 focus will be back on fundamentals in Asia which will remain 

 weak for some time to come," he said. 

     The market is waiting anxiously to see if the Federal 

 Reserve cut rates to boost sentiment, with an imminent easing 

 of at least 25 basis point already factored in, dealers said. 

     Taiwan's financial markets remained shut on Monday as 

 Typhoon Nari pounded the island, killing at least 21 people and 

 bringing floods to the capital Taipei. 


    THAI BAHT



    The baht was a shade firmer against the dollar at 43.98,



but was still struggling to break convincingly above the key 44



mark.



    Investors were selling the dollar against regional


currencies after the yen showed its resilience despite



dollar-buying intervention from the central bank.



    The currency was also supported by second quarter domestic



economic data which fared better than expected.



    The country's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 0.9 percent



quarter-on-quarter during April-June after a revised and



seasonally adjusted 0.1 percent quarterly decline in the



previous quarter.



SINGAPORE DOLLAR



The Sing dollar retained its firm tone at 1.7315 despite



bearish export data, but was trading below its intraday high



due to fears of central bank intervention at 1.7300.



Dealers said the currency was underpinned by its safe haven



status within the region and the view that local companies have



become more risk averse and scaled back on their plans to buy



foreign assets.



Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in August took another



beating, contracting 29.9 percent on the year in norminal terms



and 27.2 percent in real terms, within broad market



expectations.



"But we are afraid that the worst may not yet be over.



Obviously, demand from the U.S. will be affected by the



incidents on September 11. The future of world trade is likely



to suffer should the conflict widen and prolong," said Syetarn



Hansakul, economist at WestLB.



KOREAN WON -2



The won softened after the Bank of Japan's dollar-buying


intervention capped the yen's rapid appreciation.



The local currency ended at 1,298.7 per dollar in thin



trade compared with 1,290.0 at the start and 1,296.3 at



Friday's close.



    Dealers said apart from the yen's strength, there was



little reason to justify further gains in the won.



    The prospect of a combination of much slower growth and



higher oil prices, in the case of sustained U.S. military



action against terrorism, should weigh on Asian economies,



including oil-dependent Korea, they said.



INDONESIA RUPIAH



The rupiah hurtled through the 9,300 level for the first



time since early August as foreign banks and corporates soaked



up dollars partly for genuine commercial needs, dealers said.



One dealer said that foreign banks had bid for dollars



throughout the day despite expectations that Bank Indonesia


would intervene to shore up the rupiah at around 9,200 per



dollar.



    "BI did appear to intervene at around 9,260 today but it



had no impact," said the dealer from a different European bank.



    "People just thought it was a good bet to but dollar/rupiah



though there is no specific news," he said.



    Like stock markets elsewhere, Jakarta sank more than four



percent amid fears that U.S. markets might fall sharply.



    Dealers said they expected the rupiah's downside to be



limited to around 9,400 in the near-term given BI's intent to


intervene.



    PHILIPPINE PESO



    The peso slipped to 51.25 per dollar after a drop in



domestic stocks to a fresh 35-month low combined painfully with



Japan's intervention on the yen.



    Despite the sour tone, the currency remained within the



confines of its recent range.



    Economists said all eyes were on whether the Fed would

title: Indonesian Rupiah Ends Dn; Intervention  Fails To Stem Fall
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah closed lower Monday as strong dollar demand persisted and central bank intervention failed to stem the dollar's rise, traders said. 

 The dollar was quoted between IDR9,310 and IDR9,340 late Monday, compared with IDR9,100 to IDR9,130 Friday. 

 Traders said demand for dollars remains strong as state-owned companies continue to buy the U.S. currency for debt repayments and to cover imports. 

 They said Bank Indonesia intervened with around $20 million to stop the rupiah's slide, but with little success. 

 Traders now expect the rupiah to fall towards IDR9,500 this week on sustained dollar demand from state-owned companies. 

 "We think that Bank Indonesia cannot do anything because the demand is huge," said one dealer with a Jakarta-based foreign bank. 

 Traders said the dollar was traded in a wide range of IDR9,100 to IDR9,340 Monday and could hit IDR9,400 Tuesday, although profit-taking is likely to set in. 

 Traders expect the dollar to trade in a IDR9,300 to IDR9,400 range Tuesday.

title: Emerging  FX  - Stick to safe ranges.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 30 (Reuters) - Asian currencies moved a little to the right and a little to the left, only to end up stuck in their recent ranges late on Thursday. 

 Dealers and analysts blamed their indecisive movements on persistently wobbly sentiment towards the dollar, and the yen's failure to take advantage of that sentiment. Those conflicting factors have sent players to the sidelines. 

 While the Singapore dollar tagged after the yen, other usually yen-sensitive currencies such as the Korean won and Taiwan dollar were cowed by fears of central bank intervention. Both the Korean and Taiwan central banks are believed to be keen on maintaining export competitiveness. 

 The market was waiting for the day's major event - the European Central Bank meeting, which was expected to produce a 25 basis-point cut. A decision is expected at 1145 GMT. 

 A cut aimed at boosting growth in the euro-zone could help the euro rise. That in turn could help the Singapore dollar as the single currency is believed to be a significant component in its trade-weighted basket of currencies. 

 The Philippine peso failed to react to better than expected second quarter gross domestic product data. 

 Looking ahead, Hong Kong will issue its second-quarter numbers and Korea will release July industrial output as well as Auguust consumer price data on Friday. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht extended early losses to trade around 44.30/32, bit was still hanging on to recent highs last seen at end-March. 

 Dealers in Bangkok said light exporter dollar sales around 44.35 limited losses. 

 They said the baht was taking its cue from the yen, with several players on the sidelines waiting for the ECB decision's impact on the yen. 

 Baht gains will be limited to around 44.25/28 where there could be covering of dollar shorts, dealers said. 

 Sentiment was dampened after the central bank cut its growth forecast for this year to 1.5-2.0 percent from a previous projection of 2-3 percent due to a slowdown in exports. 

 Despite the forecast downgrade, the central bank kept its benchmark 14-day repo rate unchanged at 2.5 percent. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso hovered around Wednesday's close of 51.19 supported by dollar selling by three foreign banks which also raised suspicion the central bank was behind the move. 

 Trading was subdued with $55.50 million traded, against $90.30 million on Wednesday. 

 Dealers said the central bank had not only supported the peso in recent weeks but was also buying dollars on dips to fund maturing commitments in the non-deliverable forward market. 

 There was a muted response to second quarter GDP data which showed growth of 3.3 percent on the year, higher than market forecasts of 2.25 percent and the government's estimate of 2.8-3.0 percent. 

 First quarter GDP growth was also revised up to 3.2 percent from the previous 2.5 percent. And the figures encouraged the government to keep its 2001 forecast at 3.3-3.8 percent. 

 Dealers said the market would need consistent improvement in economic data to alter its bearish view on the growth outlook. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won slipped slightly, as concerns over Hynix Semiconductor outweighed exporters' dollar sales. 

 But the currency spent the session wedged in a narrow 1,282.7-1,284.4 range as players wondered whether to follow the firmer yen or the losses on the local stock market, where investors were upset over a 15 percent fall in shares of debt-laden Hynix. 

 Singapore dealers noted state-run banks were spotted buying dollars around 1,284, but did not believe it was on behalf of the central bank. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nudged slightly higher, but was trapped in an increasingly narrow range of 34.572-34.587. 

 Since August 20, the local dollar has kept to a 34.496-34.660 range as the market remained conscious of the central bank's vigilance. The bank actively intervenes to smooth volatility, and has recently been spotted capping the Taiwan dollar's upside to protect the island's export competitiveness. 

 Singapore dealers said the bank was believed to be waiting around the 34.57 level during the session. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar lingered around the 1.75 mark with trade subdued ahead of the ECB decision. 

 The euro, yen and dollar are believed to be major components in the undisclosed trade-weighted basket Singapore uses to manage its exchange rate. 

 Amid a lack of fresh local and regional leads, the market was expected to remain fixated on movements in major currencies. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was lifted off its intraday trough of around 9,200 following suspected intervention by Bank Indonesia which was detected selling up to $25 million. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the central bank was rumoured to have unwound dollars from 9,125 to 9,075 rupiah, both directly and through brokers. 

 Meanwhile, BI kept its intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 15.125 percent for the overnight rate and 15.875 percent for the seven-day rate. 

 Finance Minister Boediono said the government was considering assuming a rupiah rate of 8,000-9,000 to the dollar for next year's budget. The 2001 budget targets a rate of 9,600 rupiah.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Up On Rumored  Central Bank Intervention
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended stronger in thin trade Thursday as the central bank was rumored to have sold dollars to boost the local currency. 

 The central bank didn't comment on the rumored intervention, but Senior Economics Minister Dorodjatun Kuntjoro-Jakti said the authorities would let the market determine the rupiah's level. 

 The dollar closed Asian trade at IDR8,925, much lower than IDR9,175 late Wednesday. The dollar moved in a IDR8,910 to IDR9,140 range. 

 The dollar rose strongly this week on demand for the U.S. currency by state oil and gas giant Pertamina to fund imports, and from local companies with foreign debt. 

 But rumored central bank intervention, though local banks, helped the unit in thin trade. Daily volumes in Indonesia are only around $200 million to $300 million, making it easy for the central bank to move trade if it wants to. 

 The central bank is concerned the rupiah's gains since President Megawati Sukarnoputri came to power in late July might get wiped out if the flows for debt repayment continue. 

 In the second half of the year, some $14.7 billion in government and private foreign debt will come due, according to unofficial Bank Indonesia data. This will put pressure on the rupiah. 

 The dollar fell from its year highs around IDR12,000 when Megawati came to power last month, ending months of political pressure. 

 Investors are now waiting to see how successfully the government can implement asset sales promised in an agreement with the International Monetary Fund this week. 

 Quick sales of assets, including Bank Central Asia, would allow the government to narrow its budget deficit and reduce its reliance on foreign debt funding. 

 The dollar should find support at IDR8,900 Friday, with resistance at IDR9,050.

title: Indonesia 's Econ Min: Won't  Intervene  To Help Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Indonesia's top economics minister said Thursday the authorities won't intervene to help the rupiah currency. 

 "The renewed weakness in the rupiah is temporary due to dollar demand from local private companies," Senior Economics Minister Dorodjatun Kuntjoro-Jakti told reporters before the weekly cabinet meeting. 

 "We aren't going to intervene. Let's leave it to market forces," he added. 

 Still, Jakarta-based bankers said the central bank had sold $10 million early Thursday to help the local currency. 

 The central bank's policy is to intervene to help smooth movements in the rupiah but never to comment on specific actions. 

 The dollar is trading at IDR9,100 Thursday morning, having broken through IDR9,000 resistance this week on continued foreign debt repayments from local companies. 

 Bank Indonesia is keen to ensure that the rupiah doesn't lose its gains since President Megawati Sukarnoputri came to power in late July, ending months of political crisis that had sent the dollar as high as IDR12,000.

title: Asia Markets - Depressed by U.S data, Japan slides.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 29 (Reuters) - Asian stocks stumbled on 

 Wednesday as sentiment was bruised by losses in Japan's stocks 

 and bleak U.S. consumer confidence data which the market feared 

 could translate into less demand for Asia's exports. 


    Tokyo's key Nikkei average         marked a 17-year closing



low, shedding 1.87 percent to end at 10,979.76 after



disappointing comments on banks' bad loans from the nation's



top financial regulator prompted investors to sell bank stocks.



    Finance Services Minister Hakuo Yanagisawa said late on



Tuesday the outstanding balance of bad loans at major banks



would likely remain near current levels through fiscal 2003.



    "We have to remember that for the past two years the market



was running on the promise of restructuring whereas very little



change actually materialise," said Richard Jerram, chief



economist at ING Barings Securities in Tokyo.



    "I think there's still plenty more bad news out there and



as long as the government is not delivering anything



particularly helpful, I don't see any reason to be rushing into



the market at these levels," he told Reuters Television.



    In Korea, growing concerns over credit risk of Hynix



Semiconductor knocked almost two percent off the



benchmark KOSPI which ended at 565.63.



   GRIM ECONOMIC DATA



    The markets expect a batch of fresh economic data from



countries across the region this week, with analysts reckoning



they are likely to confirm views the worst is not over yet.



    South Korea's current account surplus fell for the second



straight month in July as exports continued to fall, stirring



talk in the market the country might need another round of



interest rate cut.



    The Bank of Korea said the surplus declined by nearly half



to a provisional $511 million in July from a revised $1.05



billion in June and a 22-month high of $2.16 billion in May.



    The country is due to release July industrial output on



Friday. A Reuters' poll expected the output to drop 0.9 percent



on the month after a U.S.-led downturn in the global



electronics sector has hit exports from Korea.



    The Philippines will publish the second-quarter gross



domestic product data on Thursday. Some analysts said the



number could surprise on the upside due to growth in farm and



service sectors.



    "In our view, the market is focusing too much on the recent



plunge in exports and discounting the resilience in both the



agricultural and service sector," said a DBS report.



    Economists polled by Reuters forecast an average GDP growth



of 2.25 percent year-on-year in the April-June period, compared



with the first quarter annual growth of 2.50 percent.



    The Bank of Thailand will release its monthly economic data



on Friday which are likely to continue to paint a bleak



economic picture of the country.


Central bank governor Pridiyathorn Devakula said he would



proposed his revised 2001 economic growth forecast of 1.8



percent to the monetary board meeting on Wednesday.



    But despite the economic slowdown, the government appears



reluctant to cut interest rates to spur the economy.



Pridiyathorn said he expected the board to leave the benchmark



14-day repo rate to be left unchanged at 2.50 percent.


CURRENCIES SETTLE INTO RANGE



    Asian currencies were trapped in their recent ranges as the



impact of a weak dollar was diluted somewhat by uncertainty



over the yen direction.



    The yen tested the intraday low against both the euro



 and the dollar after Japanese Finance Minister



Masajuro Shiokawa said he expected the country's April-June GDP



data to be bad.



    He said the need for a supplementary government budget to



support the economy was becoming more evident.



    The rupiah slipped to the wrong side of 9,000 after recent



strong gains due to strong corporate demand for the dollar.



    But its downside was limited by suspected central bank

intervention. Bank Indonesia was rumoured to have sold $20-30



million directly and through brokers from 9,150.



    The baht retained its firm tone as some players continued



to pare long dollar positions before the new forex reporting



rules take effect in September 3.



    But dealers said news that the monetary policy board may



leave benchmark interest rates unchanged was likely to keep the



baht's upside limited.



    Some economists believe lower interest rates will benefit



Thailand more because it will reduce costs of the government's



stimulus programmes, given the government is likely to spend



more to get the economy going.

title: Emerging  FX  - Spellbound by stagnant yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 29 (Reuters) - Asian currencies crawled towards the higher end of their recent ranges as the yen managed to hold the 120 level. 

 But the market was not terribly impressed by the slight move higher as most players stood on the sidelines and waited for the dollar and yen to end their stand-off around the 120 mark. 

 Dealers said while the market still felt a twinge of dollar bearishness, players had become frustrated by the yen's failure to gain further ground on the dollar. 

 However, given the soggy sentiment surrounding the dollar, few players were willing to have a go at building long U.S. dollar positions at current levels. 

 The Indonesian rupiah bucked the trend and headed decisively south as local corporate dollar demand kicked in. But given the thin liquidity in the market, and the restrictions on foreign exchange trade, the rupiah market tends to set its own tone. 

 Looking ahead, investors were waiting for revised second-quarter gross domestic product data from the U.S. due later in the day. 

 On the domestic front, the Philippines will be issuing second-quarter GDP on Thursday and Hong Kong will release its second-quarter GDP results on Friday. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar spent most of the session hugging the 1.7500 level, up from 1.7536 late on Tuesday. 

 Dealers said the Sing dollar had recovered in overnight trade in New York. But with the yen bobbing around just above 120 in Asian trade, the Sing dollar hesitated to make further advances. 

 "We're just playing the range right now," said a European bank dealer. He added the market was content to wait for the dollar/yen to set a decisive tone. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was swept below the 9,000 level by dollar demand from local corporates seeking to service or repay foreign debt, despite suspected intervention by the central bank. 

 Bank Indonesia said earlier in the day it was unhappy with the rupiah's levels, and threatened to intervene in the market. Jakarta dealers said they suspected the bank sold dollars directly in the market as well as through brokers. 

 But they added the intervention was to little avail given the huge demand for dollars by Indonesia's heavily indebted firms. 

 The rupiah had enjoyed a brief spurt of strength thanks to optimism over the new government and the signing of a new letter of intent between Jakarta and the IMF. 

 However, analysts have said its rally would be short-lived given the enormity of the problems the country faces. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht gave up some of its gains after failing to break above 44.10, but it retained a firm bias on the back of dollar unwinding ahead of September 3 when new forex rules take effect. 

 The currency was also underpinned by hopes of more portfolio inflows after the government announced it would contribute to foreign funds set up to invest in the Thai market. 

 News the central bank was unlikely to cut the benchmark 14-day repo rate barely supported the baht, dealers said. Some analysts believe lower rates would benefit Thailand, especially as the government needs to spend more to boost the economy. 

 The baht remains in a broad month-old uptrend channel against the dollar, but dealers attributed this mostly to a dollar correction rather than any improvement in baht fundamentals. 

 Baht funding costs eased in the offshore market, with the one-month forward rate dropping to -5/10 satang to the dollar. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso closed at 51.19, barely changed from Tuesday's close of 51.20. 

 Manila dealers said local corporate demand for dollars emerged around the 51.15 level. But when the dollar/peso touched 51.25, a foreign bank was spotted selling around $10-$15 million, sending players out of their long dollar positions as they suspected the bank was acting on behalf of the central bank. 

 Earlier, the market shrugged off comments by the central bank that it would consider further rate cuts if the peso stabilises. Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura also said he would consider easing liquidity reserve requirements if peso liquidity was too tight. 

 The bank raised reserve requirements twice recently by a total of four percentage points to support the peso. KOREAN WON -2 

 The won trickled back the wrong side of 1,280 per dollar after Tuesday's brief spike ran up against fears of central bank intervention and worries about Hynix Semiconductor . 

 State-run Korea Development Bank said it was not considering measures to help out Hynix, a day after the troubled company said it was pulling out of a government-led debt underwriting programme, stepping up pressure on trusts to roll over its debts. 

 Sentiment was also clouded by news Korea's current account surplus for July nearly halved to a provisional $511 million from $1.05 billion in June as exports fell faster than imports. TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar inched higher, but trade was confined to a well-worn range as players kept a wary eye on the yen and the central bank, which has been active in stamping out volatility in recent sessions. 

 The mood was brightened by a sharp rebound in Taipei shares , which gained 3.2 percent after the government approved a proposal to halve the land incremental tax for two years, its first action of the over 300 recommendations made by an advisory panel at the weekend to boost the economy.

title: Emerging  FX  - Firm yen helps, U.S. worries remain.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Asian regional currencies were mixed late on Friday as the yen's resilience offered support in some quarters while corporate dollar demand weighed elsewhere. 

 The Japanese currency enjoyed broad support, thanks to selling of the euro by local exporters and investors frustrated by its failure to rise. 

 The dollar also failed to make much headway against the yen despite further jawboning by Japanese officials, with the Finance Ministry's Haruhiko Kuroda saying recent currency moves did not reflect fundamentals. 

 Overnight news that U.S. unemployment claims rose 8,000 last week and the number of people remaining on the unemployment rolls reached near nine-year highs only added to pessimism over the likely timing of a U.S. recovery. 

 In Asia, the Singapore and Taiwan dollars took heart from the firm yen while the Thai baht reached near five-month highs as players cut long dollar positions ahead of the imposition of new forex rules on September 3. 

 The Korean won was held back by importer dollar buying and a perception the authorities did not want to see it strengthen further. The Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso gave way to commercial demand for the dollar. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht racked up healthy gains as offshore parties ditched long dollar positions before new forex disclosure rules take effect on September 3, with major U.S. names seen selling actively. 

 The baht was also underpinned by a firmer yen and some other regional currencies. 

 But the market was cautious not to push the baht up too fast, fearing the central bank might step in to buy the dollar on dips to repay IMF debts. 

 Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said on Friday his government would try to stimulate economic growth to above two percent in 2001. 

 His remark came after central bank governor Pridiyathorn Devakula scaled down the 2001 growth forecast to 1.8 percent from 2.0-3.0 percent. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar rode the yen and baht's coat-tails as interbank players cut long dollar positions ahead of the weekend and ventured into some cross plays. 

 But gains were capped by corporate demand for the dollar at around 1.7500, dealers said. 

 The Sing dollar was also weighed by fears that SingTel's deal to buy Australia's second-largest telecoms company could lead to outflows, but analysts said funding for the deal should already be covered. 

 Singapore's consumer price index rose 1.3 percent in July against a year earlier and was up 0.6 percent from June. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah traded around the lower end of its recent range due to local commercial dollar demand. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said it moved in a 8,520-8,720 range, with one oil company spotted buying dollars actively. 

 Energy ministry officials said Indonesia's crude oil output, the country's major foreign exchange earner, was expected to fall by an average 100,000 barrels per day next year due to security disruptions in fields. 

 Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 15.125 for the overnight rate and 15.875 percent for the seven-day rate. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso closed at 51.05 in the onshore market, just above its intraday low as players bought dollars to settle non-deliverable forward contracts. 

 Trading was active, with $107.50 million transacted compared with only $62.30 million on Thursday. 

 Sentiment was also dampened by central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura's remarks on Thursday that the bank was not currently considering further measures to support the peso. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won closed at 1,281.2 - at the higher end of its recent 1,280-1,290 range - thanks to the yen's gains. 

 But Seoul dealers said trading was light given the dearth of domestic news. Indeed, the currency has largely remained within the 1,280-1,290 range for the whole week. 

 The won has been tracking the yen closely as Korea and Japan compete on a number of exports. Singapore dealers said the market has recently been too timid to test the won's upside due to wariness over intervention by the authorities. 

 Korean officials have verbally intervened to stem the won's rise to maintain export competitiveness. Last week, a state bank was spotted buying dollars when the won rose past 1,280, believed to be on behalf of the authorities. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar closed marginally firmer on Friday, supported by the yen and central bank intervention. 

 But its upside was capped by fears of capital outflows as Taipei stocks closed at four-week lows on weak corporate earnings and uncertainty over a weekend economic committee meeting aimed at reviving the battered economy. 

 Foreign investors were net sellers of T$3.65 billion (US$105 million) of local shares on Friday, bringing total net selling to T$9.65 billion over a three-session selling streak.

title: Bank Indonesia Offering 18% To Borrow Overnight Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Indonesia's central bank is offering to borrow rupiah at 18% for overnight tenors early Monday in a bid to tighten the supply of the local currency amid inflation worries, traders said. 

 Bank Indonesia's informal intervention in the money market is pushing interbank borrowing rates higher. The overnight interbank rate is now around 18%, up from 16% earlier Monday. 

 But the central bank didn't change its official intervention rate, which remains at 15.125% overnight. 

 The central bank hopes to reduce the supply of rupiah in the system to counter a growth in consumer prices. Consumer prices posted double-digit on-year growth in recent months due to rupiah weakness pushing up the cost of imported goods. 

 The central bank is seeking to reduce the money supply to 108 trillion rupiah ($1=IDR8,510). It said recently that the base money supply, which includes bank deposits at the central bank and currency in circulation, was at IDR113 trillion as of Aug. 7. 

 Dealers said they expect Bank Indonesia to maintain the 18% overnight rate in the coming days as the base money supply is still well above target.

title: Emerging  FX  - Dollar bulls brow-beaten.
text:
SINGAPORE, Aug 10 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were in bouncy spirits in late trade on Friday as the U.S. dollar fell to multi-month lows against both the euro and yen. 

 Local factors also featured strongly. The Philippine peso racked up 2.32 percent on the day following the central bank's second liquidity reserve requirement hike in three weeks. 

 But the yen's rise against the dollar stalled after the Japanese government's monthly report downgraded its official view of the economy for the sixth time this year. 

 Government pressure on the Bank of Japan to ease its monetary stance could also limit the yen's gains against the weaker dollar, analysts said. 

 This would mean the upside for Asian currencies which tend to track the yen closely, would also be limited in the near-term. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar hit a day high of 1.7630, its best level since March 9, as gains in the yen and euro, major components in Singapore's trade-weighted basket of currencies, set off rounds of short-covering. 

 One U.S. name sold the dollar aggressively from New York trading into Friday's Asian session. Gains were exaggerated by the fact that many players in Singapore were away for a long weekend after Thursday's National Day holiday. 

 There was talk of the Monetary Authority of Singapore checking rates around 1.7600, which deterred dollar sales only briefly. Players continued to pared long dollar positions after the Sing dollar broke clearly above that level. 

 Dealers said the next key level would be 1.7500 which could be broken in London or New York, barring MAS intervention, as the market was still long of the U.S. dollar. 

 Data released on Friday confirmed the growth rate turned negative in the second quarter due to a sharp slowdown in electronics manufacturing. 

 Second quarter GDP fell 0.9 percent on-year and 10.7 percent on an annualised quarter-on-quarter basis. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was unfazed by the central bank's new forex disclosure rules announced late in the day as they were in line with market expectations. 

 It gained almost 0.50 from late Thursday levels, breaching the 45.20 mark for the first time since June 29, mostly because of the sharp rise in the yen. 

 The rules do not require banks to identify non-residents and counterparties. Commercial banks had resisted a central bank proposal to reveal names of counterparties as this would breach confidentiality laws in some countries. 

 But the Bank of Thailand said it would require more details on underlying reasons for forex transfers from October 1. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won kept off its early high of 1,278.5 due to fears of central bankintervention to cap its rise. 

 Rumours of central bank intervention spread when local banks were spotted buying dollars as the won broke above 1,280 for the first time since June 1, when it hit a high of 1,277.5. 

 But a broadly weaker dollar, higher local stocks and talk of foreign direct investment flows to Korean companies underpinned the won. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso breached the 52 mark to touch a seven-week high of 51.70 as commercial banks trimmed their dollar longs following a two percentage point hike in liquidity requirements on Thursday. 

 Dealers in Manila said the peso was supported by export-related inflows but the upmove gathered pace when some foreign banks were seen selling dollars, sparking rumours the central bank was in the market. 

 Eyeing the foreign banks, usually active on behalf of the central bank, corporates seeking dollars moved to the sidelines. 

 The central bank on Thursday raised liquidity reserve requirements of commercial banks by two percentage points to 11 percent to mop up excess liquidity. The rise was in addition to a two percentage point hike on July 27. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar reached its highest point since Monday thanks to the firmer yen, though dealers said its gains were tempered by the central bank. 

 They said the bank had prevented the local dollar from closing above the 34.60 level in recent sessions. It has not finished beyond that point since falling sharply past 34.50 a month ago in what analysts believe was a central bank-engineered depreciation to boost export competitiveness. 

 But there was little cause for cheer on the domestic front, with the overdue loan ratio at domestic banks hitting a record high of 6.47 percent at end-June from 5.89 percent at end-March. 

 Taiwan is due to release second quarter gross domestic product data next Friday. Economists polled by Reuters expected GDP to have contracted for the first time in 26 years due to sluggish private investment, slowing domestic consumption and sharp falls in exports. 

 The survey of 10 economists produced an average forecast of a 0.30 percent on-year decline in second quarter GDP after growth of 1.06 percent in the first quarter. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Verbal and rumoured actual intervention by Bank Indonesia lifted the rupiah to a day high of 9,090, but it failed to firm past the 9,000 level due to strong corporate demand for dollars. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said BI was believed to have sold $10-15 million through state banks to capitalise on recent gains inspired by the improved political situation. 

 "We believe the central bank was behind the dollar sales this morning," said a dealer at a European bank in Jakarta. 

 "After that, corporate players were in the market to buy dollars on dips and pushed the rupiah back to 9,140 before it recouped some lost ground later in the day," said the dealer. 

Central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said the rupiah, already up more than 20 percent since a change in leadership nearly three weeks ago, could hit 8,000 per dollar.

title: Bank  Indonesia : Didn't  Intervene  To Help Rupiah Monday
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia's Deputy Governor Miranda Gultom said Tuesday the central bank didn't intervene in the market Monday to help the rupiah. 

 However, Miranda didn't comment on whether Bank Indonesia was selling dollars Tuesday to help the local currency's climb, as the rupiah hit a 2001 high of IDR9,280 to the dollar. 

 Dealers suspect state-owned banks were selling dollars on behalf of the central bank. 

 Miranda also said the stronger currency won't necessarily lead to interest rate cuts. 

 "It won't cause interest rates to go down automatically," Miranda told reporters. 

 The rate on one-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes fell marginally to 17.15% at a weekly auction last Wednesday. 

 The dollar had started its fall earlier Tuesday, before the state banks stepped in, on optimism that President Megawati Sukarnoputri will name a credible team of economic ministers. The announcement is expected Thursday. 

 Dealers expect the dollar to fall to IDR9,000 later Tuesday, although sporadic dollar demand by local companies could slow the fall.

title: Emerging  FX -Yen losses hurt, politics grip rupiah.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 28 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were caught in the yen's downdraft late on Monday, which provided players with an excuse to add to their long dollar positions, dealers said. 

 The euro strengthened at the expense of the yen after talk of central bank intervention kept investors on alert in a market thinned by holidays in London and New York. 

 Political concerns also added to the region's woes. Indonesian President Abdurrahman Wahid warned in a nationally televised speech that any attempts to oust him would break Southeast Asia's most populous country apart. 

 In Thailand, the interest rate tussle between the government and central bank dragged on. A local newspaper reported that the government was preparing to order the central bank to force up deposit rates by 1.5 percentage points to spur spending. 

 But Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra denied the report, saying he had never ordered the central bank to do so. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah wilted past 11,500, briefly hitting one-month lows of 11,720, as Indonesia's leadership crisis dragged on. 

 The market showed little reaction to President Wahid's comments, which stopped short of carrying out his threat to declare a state of emergency. 

 Wahid is scrambling to save his presidency as parliament is set to meet on Wednesday to decide whether to press ahead with a special impeachment session of the top legislative body. 

 Jakarta dealers said the rupiah escaped further losses because local corporates had little appetite for dollars around these levels and state banks were also spotted selling dollars around 11,650. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht settled in a well-worn 45.56-45.62 range, caught between buying by government-linked exporters and selling from offshore banks, Bangkok dealers said. 

 The continuing battle between the government and central bank over interest rates weighed on sentiment. 

 Finance Minister Somkid Jatusripitak said the government would decide on the best level for interest rates after the central bank reports on its policy review on June 4. 

 Deposit rates currently stand at around two to three percent, with lending rates at seven to eight percent. Thai banks are unwilling to lend given their mountain of non-performing loans. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar struggled in the wake of poor economic data, hitting 32-month lows of 34.50 as the central bank let up its usual dogged defence in late trade. 

 Singapore dealers said the central bank sold up to $1.5 billion to slow the currency's fall, beginning its intervention early in the session around 33.495. But it later let the local dollar go in the face of heavy demand for dollars and the disappointing economic data. 

 After the close, the bank said it would enter the market to "maintain order" if necessary, attributing the local dollar's sharp fall to "untrue rumours". 

 While it had been bracing for bad news, the market was still glum over first quarter gross domestic product data issued after the close on Friday. The economy grew by a mere 1.06 percent on year, against forecasts of 3.25 percent. 

 The top economic planning agency said earlier in the day the economy slowed in April with no recovery in sight. Its index of leading indicators in April slipped 0.5 percent on month to 93.3. 

 Looking ahead, the Taiwan dollar could see some relief as the market is heavily long of dollars. Charts showed dollar/Taiwan looking hugely overbought, with a 14-day relative strength index reading of 98. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso dipped against Friday's 50.50 close, though it was off its day's low of 50.96. Local corporates seeking to repay foreign debt bought the dollar on dips towards 50.60. 

 Manila dealers said it was also weighed by ongoing political uncertainty coupled with weekend news of gunmen believed to be Muslim rebels seizing 20 people in a tourist resort in the southern Philippines. 

 The market was also eyeing a special Congressional session to debate a key power reform bill, viewed as a litmus test of the government's commitment to reform. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar was in limbo, stuck in a tight 1.8080-1.8118 range over the course of the day, but dealers said the mood was hurt by growing tension in Indonesia and the Philippines. 

 Local banks and U.S. names were offering the dollar at around 1.8110, stirring jitters about possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, which admitted it had intervened in the market earlier this month to support the Sing dollar. 

 "At any rate, people want to buy the dollar with all sorts of reasons from the Philippines, Indonesia to Taiwan, but they can't because of intervention fears," a European bank dealer said. 

 Given such fears, dealers expected the Sing dollar was unlikely to weaken beyond 1.8180 in the near term. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won closed near the top end of its Monday trading range of 1,293.2-1,298.0 despite the yen's retreat, buoyed by exporter dollar offers and some fund inflows. 

 But the upside was capped amid caution ahead of major economic data this week, including April industrial output on Tuesday and the May consumer price index on Thursday. 

 Economists polled by Reuters forecast industrial output fell 0.6 percent last month from March because of dwindling exports and sluggish domestic demand. 

 Inflation is expected to be tame due to seasonal factors. 

 "We expect negative month-on-month headline inflation for the first time this year. Declines in fruit and heating oil prices are likely to be the main course," Salomon Smith Barney said. 

 "Quite stable CPI figures should be favourable to the bond market. But headline inflation tends to be modest in May because of the seasonal stabilization in agricultural food prices," the bank said in a report.

title: Emerging  FX -Tread familiar ground as yen stalls.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 23 (Reuters) - Most Asian currencies were nestled comfortably in their recent ranges early Wednesday as the dollar stalled against the yen. 

 With expectations the yen would remain in the 120-125 per dollar range for now, regional currencies were not in a hurry to go anywhere. 

 Markets in Asia were also looking for further clues as to where the U.S. economy was headed in the coming quarters. 

 While there has yet to be solid evidence of a pick-up in growth in the U.S., sentiment on Wall Street seemed to brightening, and could spill over to Asia. 

 Several Federal Reserve officials expressed optimism late Tuesday about the economy, predicting an increase in growth in the second half one the recent Fed cuts start kicking in. 

 However, analysts warned against following Wall Street's example given weaker growth, local political risks in Southeast Asia and other threats to emerging markets. 

 "Apart from U.S. growth continuing to be weak, there also remain key risks from the other emerging markets especially Brazil and Argentina while the political situation in Indonesia is likely to weigh on Southeast Asian currencies for the next few months," Mansoor Mohi-uddin, currency strategist at UBS Warburg in Singapore. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was still shaky, though the central bank was capping the dollar's gains at 33.50. 

 Dealers said despite the central bank intervention, dollar/ Taiwan continued to be well-bid, especially given recent poor economic data. 

 Both April industrial output and export orders came in worse than expected on Tuesday at 5.85 percent and 6.6 percent on year, respectively. 

 Analysts said the government is running out of options in spurring the economy, despite the central bank's recent six rate cuts. They added the central bank has little interest in seeing a stronger currency. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won ticked up taking its cue from a steadier yen and a firmer local bourse with stop-loss sales triggered at the open. 

 Singapore dealers said the Nasdaq's sixth rise in a row and continuing talks about the sale of Daewoo Motor and Hyundai Investment Trust & Securities would keep the sentiment buoyed and may limit the downside. 

 But they added a poor economic outlook and lingering uncertainty over recovery in the global tech sector would cap any significant gains. 

 They said dollar demand was expected to grow stronger around 1,285 level. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar firmed from late New York levels of 1.8100-1.8115 on early dollar offers from local banks. 

 Dealers said given the lack of fresh domestic leads, the Sing was likely seek direction from the yen and other regionals. 

 The near-term downside was seen capped around 1.8120-1.8130 on lingering fears of central bank intervention. 

 They said some interbank players were spotted buying U.S. dollars around 1.8080-1.8090 and stronger dollar bids from local corporates were likely to emerge around 1.8050-1.8060. 

 The April consumer price data is due later Wednesday but dealers said it may not have a huge impact unless it surprises the market. The March consumer price index rose 1.8 percent on-year, and was up 0.2 percent from February. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was resting in a well-worn range, having avoided a break of support around 45.66. 

 Bangkok dealers said trading was extremely thin with sporadic dollar offers from exporters supporting the baht. 

 On Tuesday, the cabinet approved a finance ministry proposal to cut corporate tax for listed firms, part of a capital market stimulus package adopted by the government to help revive the bearish Thai stock market. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso opened a tad firmer at 50.60 against Tuesday's close of 50.64. 

 Manila dealers said local banks took profit on their long dollar positions as the yen edged higher. They expected players would buy the dollar on dips around 50.50. 

 Finance Undersecretary Juanita Amatong said late Tuesday the government planned to issue as much as $1 billion worth of bonds in the United States, Japan and Europe next month. 

 She said the government aimed to raise between $500 million and $700 million from the bond float and added Manila was willing to issue more if there was demand. 

 The Philippines' gross international reserves fell slightly to $14.44 billion at the end of April from the previous month's $14.67 billion. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was idling around the 11,400 level, trapped by local corporate dollar demand in a market heavily long on dollar. 

 With few solid leads in the market and Indonesia's political crisis off the boil, the rupiah has been caught between a narrow 11,075-11,560 since May 11, according to Reuters data. 

 Jakarta dealers said if President Abdurrahman Wahid resigns before the impeachment process is kicked off, there was a chance the rupiah could spike higher. But the likelihood of a resignation was dim. 

 Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia said it was unable to intervene "too much" to help the rupiah, without elaborating. Indonesia has $28 billion in foreign exchange reserves compared to Thailand's $32.1 billion aand Taiwan's $111 billion.

title: B. Indonesia  says cannot  intervene  too much for rph.
text:
JAKARTA, May 22 (Reuters) - Indonesia's central bank said on Tuesday it could not intervene too much in the foreign exchange market at the moment to prop up the rupiah, which has lost more than 15 percent of its value on the year. 

 "There are times when we sell more dollars, but right now we cannot intervene too much," bank governor Sjahril Sabirin told reporters. 

 Sabirin did not elaborate. The rupiah has been under pressure from the country's growing political instability and regular demand for dollars to meet foreign debt repayments.

title: Emerging  FX -Boosted by Wall St,  central bank  moves.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 17 (Reuters) - Asian currencies edged higher in early trade on Thursday as strong gains on Wall Street provided a psychological boost by raising hopes for more inflows. 

 The Dow Jones Industrial average rose 34.95 points or 3.15 percent to close above the key 11,000 mark for the first time since September 14. 

 Market participants were also reluctant to buy the dollar against some currencies as they were unnerved by recent actions by central banks. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed to a local newspaper on Wednesday that it had intervened in foreign exchange markets last week to support the Sing dollar. 

 In Thailand, the central bank said on Wednesday it would tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2 to curb speculation on the local currency. 

 And Bank Indonesia said it expected to keep conducting "prudent and measurable" intervention in the foreign exchange market to prevent excessive hikes in interest rates which are already at 21-month highs. 

 BI has been gradually raising rates in a largely unsuccessful attempt to stem the rupiah's losses. But critics said such moves would hurt the state budget and the troubled banking sector. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was trading around two-week highs after the central bank said it would soon take more steps to stave off speculation. 

 Dealers said players rushed to pare long dollar positions, although some bargain hunting was likely to emerge below 45.20. 

 They said the next key target for the baht is 45.06 which it has failed to breach since April 19. 

 On the credit rating front, Fitch IBCA, Duff & Phelps said on Wednesday it had no plans to change Thailand's sovereign ratings and stable outlook despite the regional and global slowdown. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar climbed above 1.8100, thanks to scattered buying by interbank players early in the morning. 

 Dealers were ever more wary of further intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, given its rare confirmation that it sold the U.S. dollar last week. Finance Minister Richard Hu also spooked dealers by saying the amounts involved in recent overseas acquisitions by local companies were not large enough to move the Sing dollar. 

 That fear helped the Sing dollar clamber back to 3-= week highs, off 11-year lows of 1.8265 hit last week. 

 And some dealers expected further liquidation of long dollar positions after the issue of April non-oil exports data, due at 0430 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters expected on a 1.8 percent rise against a 2.1 percent contraction in March thanks to a low base effect and the weaker Sing dollar. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah was loitering around the 11,300 level with players reluctant to trade given the country's volatile politics. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid said earlier in the week he expected to be impeached, though he added that he would continue fighting and would also run for the 2004 presidential polls. His spokesman later denied he had said he expected to be impeached. 

 Meanwhile, Indonesian political leaders have said an impeachment session seemed inevitable. 

 On the economic front, Finance Minister Prijadi Praptosuhardjo said on Wednesday the cabinet would discuss changes to the 2001 budget and submit them to parliament soon. 

 Those revisions were expected to be handed down to parliament in mid-May, and need to be ratified for the IMF to review Jakarta's progress on reforms and resume lending. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO The peso edged up to 50.09 against Wednesday's local 50.14 close, helped by firmer regional currencies and the yen. 

 Manila dealers said energy and power companies were looking to buy the dollar at around 49.80, otherwise staying on the sidelines to wait for more attractive levels. 

 Dealers said the prospect of a rate cut by the central bank also helped lift the mood. 

Central bank governor Rafael Buenaventura said the Monetary Board was biased to cut key interest rates following the U.S. rate cut. The board holds its weekly meeting later on Thursday. 

 The Philippines' overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 A firmer yen lifted the Taiwan dollar, which ended at a six-week low of 32.957 on Wednesday, pushing it back the right side of 32.90. 

 The market was viewing the central bank's recent dollar-buying as an effort to guide the currency lower in order to maintain Taiwan's export competitiveness amid slowing demand. 

 For the past few weeks, the bank has kept the local dollar in a tight range of 32.85-90, but allowed the currency to close past 32.90 for the first time since April 30 on Tuesday. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won recovered some ground thanks to the firmer yen. 

 An early rally on the local bourse also lifted sentiment towards the won with the market hoping for further foreign funds' equity-linked inflows. 

 Even though Korean shares ended lower on Wednesday, foreign investors were net buyers, purchasing a net 16.6 billion won worth of shares. They bought a net 5.2 billion won worth of shares in early trading on Thursday. 

 However, the won was unable to hold onto its earlier high of 1,301.5. For the past two sessions, it has been unable to break resistance of around 1,302 convincingly as local importers sought dollars on dips.

title: Emerging  FX -Fed cuts soothe some, but yen weighs.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were mostly firmer in late trade on Wednesday after interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve raised hopes of economic recovery in the world's major growth locomotive. 

 In a statement that followed the cut, the fifth 50 basis point reduction so far this year, the Fed repeated concerns about falling investment spending and weak corporate profits. 

 But the positive impact of the cut was countered by a weaker yen which retraced to its two-week lows around 124 amid talk of Japanese investor demand for overseas assets. 

 Local factors also played a key role in lifting some currencies, particularly the Singapore dollar and the Thai baht. 

 The Sing dollar made strong gains after the Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed it intervened last week to offset the impact of strong M&A outflows. Dealers said the confirmation, which is unusual, served as a notice that it would not tolerate further slippage in its trade-weighted currency. 

 The Thai baht lurched higher after the Bank of Thailand said it would further tighten disclosure rules on the baht to stave off speculation. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht lept above 45.40 on news the central bank was planning to further tighten disclosure rules on baht trading for non-resident accounts from July 2. 

 Bank of Thailand spokesman Bandid Nijathaworn said financial institutions would need to give more information about spot, forward, and swap transactions, derivative transactions, equity or debt instrument deals between them and non-resident accounts. 

 Bangkok dealers said market participants rushed to cut losses by unwinding long dollar positions after the baht breached above 45.40, although the dollar retracement was met promptly by demand from companies and importers. 

 Baht funding costs in the offshore market also eased further as demand to borrow the baht to fund dollar holdings ebbed. The one-month forward rate was quoted at 9.5/17.0 satang per dollar, but there was not much trade done as the spread was wide. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Singapore dollar firmed as local banks offloaded U.S. dollars following comments from authorities reaffirming their commitment to a tightening monetary bias. 

 The Monetary Authority of Singapore confirmed, in the local press, it intervened last week to offset the impact of an M&A inspired hike in corporate demand for the U.S. dollar. 

 Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament the amounts involved in recent overseas acquisitions by local companies were not large enough to move the Sing dollar. 

 Dealers said local banks led the U.S. dollar sales and were followed by players already seeking to trim long positions. 

 "The near-term trading range could be 1.8100-1.8140 but that is contingent to the yen not weakening significantly beyond 124," a chief dealer of a European bank in Singapore said. INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hovered around 11,400 with the market eyeing warily President Aburrahman Wahid's comment that he would not quit and would in fact fight the next presidential polls in 2004. 

 On Tuesday, Wahid told a seminar he expected to be impeached by parliament but on Wednesday his spokesman denied he made the comment. 

 Jakarta dealers said trading conditions were thin with most activity led by state banks active on both sides of the market. 

 However, most players kept to the sidelines as heads of parliamentary factions met to discuss a possible change in leadership and timing of any impeachment hearing against Wahid. 

 Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia said it would continue to intervene to support the rupiah and avoid excessive hike in interest rates. 

 The central bank also said the Fed rate cut could have an impact on its weekly SBI certificate auction, which saw the one-month rate reach 16.31 percent from 16.26 percent last week. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged lower in line with the falling yen, touching a two-week low of 1,310.2, where some export and equity-related inflows capped the downside. 

 Dealers said hopes of foreign direct investment inflows from the potential sale of Daewoo Motor Co. and Hynix Semiconductor to foreign investors kept sentiment supported. 

 The consumer confidence survey for April also came in better than the previous month but dealers in Singapore said they were more worried about the economy of Korea's biggest export market. 

 With a recovery in the U.S. still unclear despite the Fed's aggressive rate cuts, the won was expected to stay depressed. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended at 50.14 after reaching a high of 50.06 from lows of 50.21. 

 Manila dealers said local banks bought the peso earlier, but foreign banks and IT companies were looking to buy the U.S. dollar at 50.10-20. 

 The government said the preliminary January-April budget deficit was 36.717 billion pesos, lower than its target of 38.3 billion for the period. 

 President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo said the Philippines was aiming to bring down its budget deficit to 130-145 billion pesos this year from its initial estimate of 225 billion pesos. 

 Analysts said the government needs to consolidate its chronic deficit urgently, otherwise it would inflict more damage on the economy given that total public sector debt is approaching 80 percent of GDP. 

 The central bank said it would consider the inflation trend in deciding whether to lower its overnight rates following the U.S. rate cut. The overnight borrowing rate is currently at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar fell to six-week troughs of 32.996, tracking the yen lower. Dealers said U.S. investment houses bought the dollar following the TAIEX's poor showing. 

 Taiwan's central bank is expected to cut its interest rates, following the Fed's move on Tuesday. 

 In April, the central bank cut key interest rates by 0.125 percentage points, bringing the discount rate to 4.0 percent and the collateral rate to 4.375 percent.

title: Emerging  FX -Rupiah falls past 12,000,others wary.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 26 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah toppled over the key 12,000 mark early Thursday, threatening to ruffle other Southeast Asian markets. 

 The rupiah's slide past 12,000 per dollar was prompted by increasing jitters over the country's messy economic and political scene. Among the currencies most vulnerable to shocks from the rupiah were the neighbouring Singapore dollar. 

 Dealers said there was no sign of Bank Indonesia intervention. 

 Emerging markets in Asia were also vulnerable to the latest events in Argentina, where rumours continue to circulate about a debt default and a currency devaluation. 

 The latter took a step towards reality when Argentina's President Fernando de la Rua earlier named an interim head of the central bank. The current central bank governor Pedro Pou had come under increasing fire for refusing to ease strict monetary policies, including the Argentine peso's one-to-one peg. 

 On the bright side, U.S. data issued on Wednesday showed the key housing sector surprisingly resilient and helped dispel some of the gloom over the U.S. economy's prospects. That data fed into a more upbeat mood on Wall Street. 

 The yen was treading water as the market waited for the new Japanese cabinet line-up, while the euro was also stuck with investors keeping watch over the European Central Bank's meeting later in the day. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 With the fate of international loans in the air, Jakarta has been scrambling to fill in its budget shortfall, usually papered over by loans from international lenders. 

 The government announced on Wednesday that it would issue its first ever rupiah deficit bonds, with the expectation that wealthy local governments would buy them. 

 Analysts, however, said the move was cosmetic and did not address the main cause of Indonesia's budget shortfall - an unwillingness to cut expenditures, namely costly fuel subsidies. 

 Markets in Jakarta were also girding themselves for a potentially violent showdown between embattled President Abdurrahman Wahid's supporters and opponents. 

 Parliament is widely expected to issue a second censure of Wahid over two financial scandals, which may spark violent protests from his more fanatical supporters. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht was trapped in a narrow range of 45.50-45.70 in subdued trade. Dealers expected the dollar's upside to be limited as the market was already quite long. 

 Players were also reluctant to actively bid for the U.S. currency because they were wary of further tightening of forex trading regulations. 

 Assistant central bank governor Chettavee Chareonpitak told Reuters in Bangkok that the Bank of Thailand was making an internal study on whether to tighten reporting requirements to help it monitor and curb speculation on the baht by non-residents with access to the currency. 

 "We are looking at additional reporting on non-resident baht accounts, such as information on currency conversion by accounts owners," he said. 

 Charts show dollar/baht confined in a consolidative triangle which could break any time soon. 

 "I think people will be taking profits on the dollar in the near-term because the market is quite long. That should prepare the dollar for another rally," said a dealer at a European bank. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was cowering at 1.8160 after an offshore rout knocked it down to two-week lows of 1.8180 from 1.8100. 

 Underlying weakness stemmed from murky regional political picture, anticipation for further M&A-related flows and little improvements on economic fundamentals, dealers said. 

 Local banks, U.S. investment banks were covering its short U.S. dollar positions, but the Sing dollar's fall came to a halt at 1.8180, level where the authorities were said to have intervened earlier this month. 

 Analysts said a decisive break of 1.8180 would lead to stop-loss U.S. dollar buying orders at 1.8200 then 1.8225, risking a return to decade lows of 1.8235 hit on April 2. 

 March manufacturing output is due out later on Thursday. In February it rose 13.3 percent but analysts anticipate weakness ahead given a downturn in the global technology sector. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won made slight gains with the help of the steady yen, but its rise was capped by importers seeking dollars. 

 Analysts said the yen remained the main driver of the won's direction as Korea and Japan compete on a number of key exports. They added, however, month-end exporters' dollar sales may serve to give the won a short-term boost. 

 The market was keeping watch over March industrial output numbers due at 0300 GMT. A recent Reuters poll showed economists on average expected a 0.2 percent decline on month, mainly due to sluggish electronics exports. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso opened a touch weaker at 50.60 in the onshore market, compared with the Wednesday's close of 50.55, with interbank players and importers bidding for the dollar. 

 Dealers said the arrest of former president Joseph Estrada had limited impact on the market, although some said lack of mass support for him was good for political stability. 

 "The market is closely watching the regionals and developments in Argentina for direction," said a Manila dealer. 

 "I don't think the peso would poke above 50.40 in the near-term because that is where lots of people are going to buy the dollar on dips," he said. 

 The market drew little support from Finance Secretary Alberto Romulo's remark, saying this year's budget deficit could be at 132 billion pesos, lower than the government's official target of 145 billion. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR The Taiwan dollar ticked up to 32.87 from 32.90 late on Thursday but was expected to come under pressure given weaker regional currencies. 

 Dealers said trading would remain lucklustre with offshore players looking to square positions ahead of Japan's Golden Week Holiday which starts this weekend. 

 They also said exporters were likely to come in to sell the U.S. dollar at around 32.95, and equity-related capital inflows would support 33 mark, with the benchmark TAIEX up 0.5 percent after the overnight gains on the Nasdaq. 

 The market showed no immediate reaction to U.S. President George W. Bush reaffirming the U.S. policy on Taiwan. 

 He told Reuters the United States would help Taiwan defend itself against China but said he hoped Taipei and Beijing will resolve their differences peacefully.

title: UPDATE 1-Rupiah falls to 12,000 amid Indonesia woes.
text:
(Adds comments by dealers, analysts and World Bank, latest price action) 

 SINGAPORE, April 26 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah hit 12,000 per dollar in Thursday trade as worries about the country's political and economic outlook mounted, according to Singapore-based sources. 

 After days of fending off the psychological 12,000 level, not seen since September 11, 1998, dealers said the currency finally succumbed in the face of a worsening economic scenario. 

 It was quoted at 12,050/150 at 0232 GMT, down over one percent from levels seen late on Wednesday. Dealers in Jakarta noted that the bid/ask spread was fairly wide, indicating an unwillingness to trade at these levels. 

 They also said the rupiah has so far hit a low of 12,250, and state banks were spotted selling dollars around 12,200, which prompted some profit-taking in a market heavily long on dollar. 

 Charts showed the dollar/rupiah in overbought territory with a 14-day relative strength index of around 89. 

 Dealers added that Bank Indonesia had not been spotted intervening in the market yet, despite its threats to do so. 

 Analysts were hesitant to forecast the next level the dollar may be headed towards, though some said it could hit 13,500 - a level last seen in August 1998 according to Reuters data. 

 Increasingly poor liquidity combined with actual and feared intervention have kept it clear of the 12,000 mark despite a hefty seven percent drop on April 20. 

 But fears of violence in Jakarta ahead of an April 30 parliamentary session, expected to result in a second censure of President Abdurrahman Wahid, and growing anxiety about Indonesia's budget deficit undermined the rupiah. 

 Dealers said the market was disappointed an IMF mission left Jakarta without indicating when it planned to release a stalled but much-needed $400 million loan. 

 Instead, it warned the budget deficit could blow out to six percent of gross domestic product from the targeted 3.7 percent unless urgent measures were taken. 

 Dealers said the market was increasingly sceptical over how long the central bank could continue to prop up the rupiah. 

 Indeed, analysts said Bank Indonesia's current efforts to stem the rupiah's bleeding has so far proved ineffectual. 

 "Bank Indonesia has already tried the two most conventional ways to help the rupiah - hiking interest rates and intervening - but this clearly has not worked," said Thio Chin Loo, regional currency strategist at BNP Paribas in Singapore. 

 She added that given its recent clampdown on speculation, there was little else the central bank could do to address genuine dollar demand from Indonesia's debt-laden corporates. 

 The World Bank's country director for Indonesia, Mark Baird, also said the higher interest rates, which are at 21-month highs, were only a partial defence for the rupiah. He added Indonesia's economic fundamentals do not justify the exchange rate. 

 Analysts stressed that the rupiah's outlook will remain hobbled as long as the current political turmoil continues. 

 "Indonesia craves stability," said Simon Flint, senior currency strategist at Bank of America in Singapore, citing the country's political strife as blocking progress in much-needed economic reforms.
