title: Emerging  FX  - Mixed, glimmer of hope in yen.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 20 (Reuters) - Asian currrencies gave mixed signals early Friday, despite the weaker dollar. 

 While the firmer yen was likely to pull the North Asian currencies higher, the Singapore dollar was still struggling under commercial demand for the U.S. unit. The Philippine peso was also expected to come under pressure with import season underway. 

 And the Indonesian rupiah was floundering after President Abdurrahman Wahid warned parliament on Thursday of further violence from his supporters if efforts to oust him continued. 

 U.S. markets' wildly differing reactions to the Federal Reserve's recent surprise rate cuts left investors in Asia scratching their heads over what exactly the growth prospects for the U.S. and the region were. 

 Wall Street was gleeful about the cuts, taking them as proof that the Fed was pulling out the stops to avoid a recession, but Treasuries despaired that the economy was on the path towards overheating and rising inflation. 

 And forex markets agonised as to whether the Fed's move meant the U.S. economy was in worse shape than previously thought, leaving the dollar limp against the yen and euro . 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won edged lower from its Thursday close of 1,298, though a firmer yen helped limit its fall. 

 Fund inflows were also expected to lend support to the won, after foreign investors bought a whopping net 671.6 billion won in local stocks on Thursday. Foreign investors have bought a net 7.95 billion won in stocks so far on Friday. 

 But local importers and interbank players continued to bid up the dollar, pushing the won just under the 1,300 level. That level is around the 50 percent retracement of the dollar's rise from February 21 to April 4. 

 Charts also showed the dollar/won was headed into oversold territory with a relative strength index reading of around 32. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 Political unrest and growing economic problems left the rupiah languishing beyond the 11,000 mark. 

 Local corporate dollar demand on Thursday forced interbank players to scramble for dollars in an illiquid market, shoving the rupiah past the key psychological level of 11,000. 

 Despite Bank Indonesia's persistent intervention and rate hikes, analysts said the rupiah would continue to languish ahead of April 30, when parliament reconvenes and is expected to issue a second censure of the embattled President. 

 On the macroeconomic front, the World Bank warned that Indonesia's budget deficit may rise to 5-6 percent this year from a projected 3.7 percent. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar reversed course overnight to hit lows of 1.8095 after solid performance in equities pushed it to highs of 1.7970 on Thursday from 1.8085. "People are not convinced by the rise in regional currencies (on Thursday)," a European bank dealer said. "Things may not be out of the woods." 

 The Sing dollar has repaired less than a third of the damage caused by a steep four-percent fall to decade lows of 1.8230 on April 2 from the beginning of the year. 

 Nevertheless, others expected it to show resilience in the face of 1.81 thanks to expectations for firmer stocks due to overnight gains on Wall Street. 

 They added the reaffirmation of a tightening monetary stance by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong on Thursday also discouraged bears to build massive long positions. 

 Lee said Singapore would maintain its policy of a gently appreciating band for the Sing dollar. 

 Dealers said an immediate support for the Sing dollar lies at 1.8080-90 and a resistance at 1.7970. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR The Taiwan dollar was expected to trade nervously around 32.78-85 after the central bank was spotted intervening to weaken the currency on Thursday. 

 The central bank is expected to cut its rates by 0.125 percentage point following the Fed's surprise cut on Wednesday. 

 Taiwan last cut rates on March 29, lowering the discount rate to a historic low of 4.125 percent. 

 But a senior Taiwan central bank official said on Thursday the bank would not immediately follow suit as it had to monitor the effects of the last rate cut on the domestic financial system and the economy. 

 Economists said the central bank's aim in a rate cut would not be to inject liquidity into the market, but rather to bring about a slow depreciation of the Taiwan dollar. 

 But some argued a pro-growth market might think lower rates would help revive demand and boost the stock market, attracting further capital inflows and hence buoying the currency. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was likely to stay under pressure from rising dollar demand by importers ahead of the import season but a steadier yen would provide some support on the downside. 

 The central bank's monetary board on Thursday cut its key overnight rates by 50 basis points, matching the move a day earlier by the U.S. Federal Reserve. 

 The overnight borrowing rate now stands at 9.5 percent and the lending rate at 11.75 percent. 

 The rate cut would boost peso liquidity but dealers said the move was likely to soothe sentiment as monetary easing is needed to spur domestic consumption and investment. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht retreated against the U.S. dollar as euphoria surrounding the Fed's rate cuts on Wednesday was upstaged by strong dollar demand from importers and onshore companies. 

 Dealers said some oil companies had actively bid for dollars, taking advantage of easing oil prices and a steadier baht. They expected dollar profit taking to emerge around 45.50. 

 On the monetary front, the central bank on Thursday kept its benchmark 14-day repo rate unchanged at 1.5 percent despite the Fed's interest rate reduction. 

 It also cut its forecast for economic growth this year to 2.5-4.0 percent from 3.0-4.5 percent in January, and trimmed core inflation expectations to 1.5-2.0 percent from 1.5-2.5 percent projected months ago.

title: Bank  Indonesia  defends rates,  intervention  policy.
text:
JAKARTA, April 20 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia said the ailing rupiah, which fell 3.4 percent earlier on Friday, said the currency "could go anywhere" without it intervening in the market and hiking interest rates, already at 21-month highs. 

 "Those are not useless. If Bank Indonesia did not do those things, the exchange rate could go anywhere ...," central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin told reporters when asked if intervention and hiking interest rates were effective. 

 The rupiah extended its losses late on Friday, hitting lows of 11,500 in the face of active corporate dollar demand, dealers said. The rupiah lost 3.4 percent from its late Thursday levels, hitting a low of 11,500 per dollar, its weakest since September 14, 1998, according to Reuters data. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said it was driven down by local companies seeking dollars for imports and debt servicing amid expectations of further weakness in the rupiah.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends At 31-Mo Low On Political Fears
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah extended its loss and hit a new 31-month low Friday as panic-stricken local companies rushed to buy dollars ahead of a parliamentary session at the end of this month, dealers said. 

 The dollar closed at IDR11,925, up from IDR11,095 Thursday, despite intervention by Bank Indonesia. Dealers said the central bank sold an estimated $30 million to support the beleaguered local currency. 

 Parliament will meet April 30, during which it is expected to issue a second censure to President Abdurrahman Wahid. The move is a further step toward impeaching the president. 

 Fears were heightened after retired military commander Gen. Wiranto warned Friday that a protracted political feud between Wahid and his foes could trigger a new wave of chaos and violence. 

 His statement follows a warning by Wahid Thursday that around 400,000 people are ready to defend him if parliament seeks to impeach him. 

 "People were scrambling to buy the dollar," said a dealer with a European bank. "Bank Indonesia seemed to be the only dollar seller today." 

 Dealers said a Japanese company operating in Indonesia bought a large amount of dollars. 

 Elsewhere, Indonesian shares fell 1.9% to 342.858 points due to the rupiah's weakness and fears of unrest. 

 Dealers said the dollar may jump to IDR12,000 when it starts trading Monday as many participants are still nervous. The U.S. unit is expected to continue its journey to IDR12,300 before taking a breather.

title: Asia Markets-Rally on U.S. rate cut, capped by concerns.
text:
HONG KONG, April 19 (Reuters) - Asian asset prices rallied 

 on Thursday, buoyed by a 50 basis point cut in U.S. interest 

 rates, but with upside capped by some suspicions that the 

 surprise move implied that the U.S. economy may be in worse 

 shape than feared. 

     "I think the markets are trying to work out whether this 

 cut is really good news or bad, that is, is there worse to 

 come?" Li Lian Ong, regional economist at Macquarie Bank in 

 Hong Kong said. 

     Retail investors, still counting their losses from the 

 region's 1997/98 economic crisis, were especially nervous. 

     "I had HK$600,000 invested in the stock market. Today it's 

 worth about $125,000. I have no more money to invest," said an 

 executive with a large container shipping company in Hong Kong, 

 who declined to be identified. 

 "For the average man on the street in Hong Kong, this rate 

 cut changes nothing. People are still poor, jobs are being lost 

 as industry relocates to China, and property prices are still 

 depressed," he said. 

 But economists said the U.S. Federal Reserve's cut - the 

 fourth in as many months that have brought key short term 

 borrowing rates down 200 basis points to 4.5 percent - was 

 positive for Asia. 

 "To the extent that this cut could help the U.S. economy 

 turn around faster, this is positive for the export oriented 

 economies of Asia," Ong told Reuters. 

 Institutional investors followed that logic. 

 Stocks surged around the region with India's Bombay 

 benchmark index leading the charge, up around five percent in 

 late trade. Hong Kong's Hang Seng charged 4.4 percent higher. 

 Japan's bellwether Nikkei 225 chalked up a second 

 successive session of gains, hitting an intra-day high of 

 14,099.49 before easing back at the close, still 1.7 percent 

 higher and adding to the previous day's gain of 4.4 percent. 

     Singapore led the way in Southeast Asia, with the Straits 

 Times Index gaining 2.5 percent. 

     "It did offer a strong boost to local equities today...we 

 think that the Fed rate cuts do give central banks across the 

 region room to ease monetary policy further to bolster their 

 slowing economies," Paul Schymyck, an economist at financial 

 analysts IDEAglobal.com in Singapore, told Reuters Television. 

     But recent history does not offer much hope of a sustained 

 recovery in stock prices. 

     The Hang Seng, the Asian market most closely correlated to 

 the U.S., fell the morning after the last Fed rate cut on March 

 20 and had lost about two percent of its value since then 

 before Thursday's rally. 

 Singapore, heavily dependent on electronics exports to 

 trading partners including the U.S., has tracked a similar 

 path. 

     The STI dropped at the open on March 21 and had lost seven 

 percent in the interim before this rally. 

     And this is against a backdrop of very weak fund inflows. 

     In the first three months of this year, U.S. mutual fund 

 investors withdrew about $800 million from Asia and invested 

 only $300 million to create net outflows of about $500 million. 

CURRENCIES CHEERED BY FED 

     Asian currencies were cheered by hopes that the Fed's cut 

 would prevent the growth engine of the world's biggest economy 

 from stalling. 

     A firmer yen and the Nasdaq's overnight rally also helped 

 regional units distance themselves from recent lows. 

     The yen poked above 122 to the dollar and the euro was firm 

 at three-week highs against the dollar as the market digested 

 the Fed's move. 

     Analysts said the Fed's decision to lower its federal funds 

 rate to 4.5 percent, the lowest since 4.25 percent in May 1994, 

 may help the regionals in the short term. 

     As expected, the Philippine central bank matched the Fed's 

 50 basis-point rate cuts at its policy-setting meeting. 

     But Taiwan's central bank said it would not immediately 

 follow the Fed's suit, while the Bank of Thailand was not 

 expected to immediately cut rates. 

     The rupiah bucked the firmer trend, suffering from a gloomy 

 political outlook. Despite Bank Indonesia's intervention, it 

 slipped through the key psychological 11,000 mark. 

     BOND SPREADS NARROW 

     Asian dollar bonds sprang to life with selected sovereign 

 spreads 10-15 basis points tighter to U.S. Treasuries as the 

 Fed's rate cut lit a fire under U.S. equity markets and revived 

 interest in risk assets. 

 "The rate cut shows the Fed will take strong action to 

 revive demand, particularly capital spending. Since Asia is a 

 producing region, any revival in capital spending will benefit 

 this region," Raja Visweswaran, head of Asia securities 

 research at Bank of America in Hong Kong, told Reuters. 

 Korea's 8.875 percent sovereign bonds due in 2008 were 

 quoted some 15 bps tighter to Treasuries at 185 bps over. 

 Malaysian '09s were also quoted 15 bps tighter at 210 bps over. 

 The Malaysian sovereign has been attracting bargain hunters 

 lately, Visweswaran said. It widened to 240 bps over Treasuries 

 a week and a half ago on expectations Kuala Lumpur may be 

 planning another sovereign bond issue. 

 "The view now is that any new issue is more likely to be a 

 euro issue or a yen-denominated issue which would offer a much 

 cheaper way to raise money than a dollar bond," Visweswaran 

 said. 

 Asian corporate bonds lagged sovereigns though, tightening 

 by about five bps over Treasuries across the board.

title: Emerging  FX  - Buoyed by Fed cut, but rupiah suffers.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 19 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were buoyed on Thursday by the U.S. Federal Reserve's surprise rate cut overnight, raising hopes that the U.S. growth engine will keep ticking over. 

 A firmer yen and the Nasdaq's overnight rally also helped the regionals distance themselves from recent lows. 

 As expected, the Philippine central bank matched the Fed's 50 basis-point rate cuts at its policy-setting meeting. 

 But Taiwan's central bank said it would not immediately follow the Fed's suit, while the Bank of Thailand was not expected to cut rates at its meeting later in the day. 

 And the rupiah continued to suffer from a gloomy political outlook. Despite Bank Indonesia's intervention, it slipped through the key psychological 11,000 mark. 

 Analysts said the Fed's decision to lower its federal funds rate to 4.5 percent, the lowest since 4.25 percent in May 1994, may help the regionals in the short term. 

 But the Fed's sudden move also raised concerns over the depth of the U.S. downturn that necessitated the second round inter-meeting cuts so far this year. 

 The yen poked above 122 and the euro was firm at three-week highs against the dollar as the market digested the Fed's move. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht rose to an intraday high of 45.07, its best level since April 2, on the back of the Fed's rate cuts and a steadier yen before onshore dollar demand set it back. 

 Bangkok dealers said local banks bought dollar actively above 45.10 for customers and importers. 

 "I don't think the baht would move beyond or stand convincingly above 45.00 in the immediate term because commercial demand for the dollar is still quite strong," said a dealer at a European bank in Bangkok. 

 The Bank of Thailand's monetary policy board is expected to keep its key 14-day repo unchanged at 1.5 percent at its meeting later Thursday despite the Fed's cuts. 

 Offshore baht funding costs eased, with the one-month forward rate quoted at -3.00/-0.00 satang per dollar. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won leapt with the firmer yen and rallying local stocks, climbing above the 1,300 per dollar level for the first time since March 21. But it failed to hold onto earlier, more impressive gains. 

 Local stocks closed 4.23 percent higher on the back of the Fed's rate cuts and the Nasdaq's overnight gains. Foreign investors bought a net 671.6 billion won in shares, their largest net purchase since March 3, 2000. 

 But dealers in Singapore said the dollar was well-bid after selling by U.S. funds brought the dollar to a low of 1,293.5. 

 Local importers bought dollars around that level, spurring local banks to cover their dollar positions. 

 Dealers were unsure as to how long the won would be able to hold onto its gains, given the slowing Korean economy. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The ailing rupiah sank below the 11,000 level for the first time in five weeks due to immense dollar demand from local banks and companies. 

 Bank Indonesia was spotted selling dollars when the rupiah slipped to 11,035, with the size of the intervention estimated around $15-20 million. The central bank sold a similar amount of dollars on Wednesday. 

 BI also threatened to increase its intervention in the foreign exchange market. The currency has lost around four percent in one week. 

 But dealers doubted if its persistent intervention - both through direct dollar sales and money market operations - would turn around the rupiah's course in the face of persistent political and economic woes. 

 The market has become increasingly nervous about potential violence in Jakarta ahead of April 30 when parliament is expected to issue a second censure of President Abdurrahman Wahid. 

 Wahid earlier reminded parliament of his support, saying thousands of his backers were ready to come to the capital. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar edged higher to just above 1.80 from Wednesday's lows of 1.8085, thanks to the firmer yen and other regional currencies. 

 But dealers emphasised the volume was thin with little genuine demand for the Sing. Many dealers said the Sing owed its rise to profit-taking on dollars. 

 The market did not react much to comments by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong that the Monetary Authority of Singapore would maintain its monetary policy of a gently appreciating band for the Sing on a trade-weighted basis. 

 "His comment could be an indication from the MAS that it will not change its monetary policy no matter what the Fed does," a currency analyst said. "That's a valid arguement and helps the MAS maintain its credibility." 

 Nevertheless, dealers said Singapore would not be immune to the regional and U.S. slowdowns, furthering the case for a lower Sing dollar. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso firmed to a day's high of 49.96, but later trimmed its gains to stay below 50. 

 Manufacturers and other importers were buying dollars to meet their requirements for April and May, which is the import season. 

 The Phillipine central bank followed the Fed and cut its benchmark overnight borrowing and lending rates by 50 basis points, bringing them to 9.5 percent and 11.75 percent, respectively. 

 Dealers welcomed the move as an effort to spur domestic demand, but noted that the Philippine economy would still suffer if the U.S. slowdown lingers. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar rose in line with the yen, with rises in local stocks also boosting sentiment towards the currency. 

 However, it failed to hold onto its intraday high of 32.785, with the market speculating that the central bank would come in to stem the local dollar's rise. 

 Taiwan's central bank has been in the market recently to cap its currrency's rise in order to maintain Taiwan's export competiveness. 

 The bank said earlier in the day it would not immediately follow the Fed's rate cuts. Taiwan's central bank last cut rates on March 30.

title: UPDATE 1-Indonesian rupiah falls to 5-week lows.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 19 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah slipped through the 11,000 per dollar level for the first time in five weeks in the face of heavy corporate demand for dollars, dealers in Jakarta said on Thursday. 

 It fell to a low so far of 11,035 against 10,915 late on Wednesday, bringing its losses for the week to around four percent. By 0530 GMT, it was quoted at 11,000/020. 

 Dealers said companies and local banks actively bid for the dollar from 10,930 to settle import bills and to repay foreign debts due to fears the local currency could drop further. 

 "Political tensions have risen, with spats between President Abdurrahman Wahid and the parliament appearing to escalate," said a dealer at one European bank in Jakarta. 

 Some dealers added that with Bank Indonesia the sole supplier of dollars, the market was susceptible to panic dollar buying on any sign of local corporate dollar demand. 

 Bank Indonesia was spotted in the market when the rupiah slipped to 11,035, selling around $15-$20 million. The bank also intervened on Wednesday to shore up support for the ailing rupiah. 

 But dealers doubted whether the bank's persistent intervention would turn around the rupiah's fortunes in the face of Indonesia's unrelenting political and economic woes. 

 "Temporarily, intervention may help. But how long can they keep this up?" said a dealer at another European bank in Jakarta. 

 "But they have no choice, or the rupiah would slide further." 

 In an effort to discourage further selling, Bank Indonesia has said it would continue intervening if needed to stem the rupiah's fall and raise rates on its benchmark certificates (SBIs). 

 The one-month SBI rate rose to 15.93 percent at Wednesday's auction from 15.82 percent the previous week. 

 However, analysts said the central bank might have to reconsider its current policy given the currency's persistent weakness. 

 "Official intervention to support the rupiah has merely been able to stem the pace of the decline rather than stop it. High local interest rates have also failed to provide adequate support and are unlikely to do so in the near term," said Standard Chartered Bank in a research note. 

 The bank said the authorities faced tough policy decisions as a weaker rupiah would impact external debt and persistently high interest rates would make the government's budget deficit target tough to meet. 

 "Unfortunately, the current one is looking increasingly stale," it added. 

 The rupiah last breached 11,000 on March 12, when it hit a low of 11,210 after the central bank said it had limited ability to defend the currency.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Ends Lower, Clouded By Domestic Politics
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended at a five-week low Thursday as the market grew increasingly nervous ahead of a parliamentary session on April 30, dealers said. 

 Parliament is expected to issue a second censure to President Abdurrahman Wahid that day, moving another step closer to impeaching the president who rose to power in October 1999. 

 After touching an intraday high of IDR11,105, the dollar closed at IDR11,095, up from IDR10,960 Wednesday. 

 The dollar had failed to break the key psychological level of IDR11,000 earlier in the day, but Wahid's statement that 400,000 followers were ready to fight on his behalf if parliament impeaches him fueled panic dollar buying, dealers said. 

 "The statement made the market more nervous," said a dealer with a foreign bank. "Wahid's statement didn't do any good for the rupiah at all." 

 During the day, Bank Indonesia intervened to help the rupiah by selling an estimated $40 million. 

 But the market continued defying the central bank, knowing the bank's limited capabilities. Bank Indonesia has only around $28 billion in gross foreign exchange reserves. 

 Dealers said the market is getting more disillusioned with prospects for the disbursement of the International Monetary Fund's next loan to Indonesia. 

 An IMF mission is in Jakarta to complete a review of Indonesia's economic program, but it's still unclear when it will release the $400 million installment. 

 In a move to tighten the supply of the rupiah that could be used to buy the dollar, Bank Indonesia Thursday also raised the money market intervention rates by 50 basis points. 

 Elsewhere, Indonesian share prices fell 1.9% to a 29-month low partly due to the rupiah's sustained fall. 

 After successfully maintain its close above IDR11,000, the dollar is expected to test IDR11,300 Friday, dealers said. Meanwhile, the IDR11,000 is expected to serve as a solid support for the U.S. unit.

title: Bk Indonesia Raises Money Mkt Rates 50 BPs

JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia Thursday raised its money market intervention rates by 50-basis points for all maturities between one-day and one week. 

 Bank Indonesia said the overnight rate is now 13.125%, the rates for maturities between two to six days are 13.375% and the one-week rate is 13.875%. 

 The rate hike follows an increase in the benchmark weighted average rate of the one-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes to 15.93% Wednesday from 15.82%. 

 Bank Indonesia has been raising rates to defend the rupiah, which is clouded by the country's bleak political outlook. 

 Bank Indonesia's money market intervention rates are the rates it offers to banks if they put their funds with the central bank. 

 The higher rates are expected to tighten liquidity, which can be used to speculate against the rupiah in the currency market.

title: Emerging  FX  - Easier in holiday-thinned trade.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 16 (Reuters) - Asian currencies were easier late on Monday, but activity was confined to familiar range as holidays in several centres kept interest thin and volumes low. 

 Most Asian markets reopened after a three-day break but Hong Kong, Sydney and much of Europe were still closed for the Easter break. Thai markets were also still shut for Songkran. 

 Analysts expected volumes to pick up from Tuesday, but the overall trend remained unchanged. 

 "Until the market is convinced that risk of the yen falling to much weaker levels is over, most players in the region will prefer to stay long of dollars," a chief dealer of a European bank in Singapore said. 

 Japan competes with key Asian countries in export markets and also absorbs a chunk of the region's exports. 

 Analysts said the release of poor economic data in line with the expected slowing of exports and growth across the region was also likely to keep sentiment depressed. 

 Singapore is due to release March non-oil domestic exports data on Tuesday after lowering its growth forecast for the year last week. Most analysts expect exports to contract after a 5.4 percent rise in February. 

 The Bank of Japan's downgrade of its view of the economy in its April report had little impact on the yen as the view had been widely expected. 

 Both the yen and euro were also rangebound in a holiday-thinned market with the dollar getting some marginal support from tension in the Middle East after Israel's air raid on Syrian positions in Lebanon earlier in the day. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah led regional loosers on Monday as dollar sales by state banks were badly upstaged by strong corporate demand. 

 Jakarta dealers said state banks sold around $10-15 million but that was not enough to halt the rupiah's slide. 

 One oil company was heard placing a big dollar buying order while foreign banks were also active in bidding for the dollar, they said. 

 Optimism over a potentially positive outcome from the IMF visit was overshadowed by news of the World Bank scrapping a $300 million loan to the country, partly due to its failure to meet certain requirements. 

 "Now the market hopes that the IMF visit would lead to the disbursement of its loans for the sake of other creditors' confidence in Indonesia. The country's public-debt profile is in virtual default," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia kept its indicative intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged at 12.625 percent for the overnight rate and 13.375 percent for the seven-day rate. The intervention rates are among the central bank's tools to influence liquidity in the market. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was stuck in a tight range just beyond the 50 mark, with regional weakness keeping the dollar well bid while a lack of corporate dollar demand capped the downside. 

 Dealers in Manila said with a holiday in Bangkok and lack of a clear signal from the yen, most corporates preferred to stay on the sidelines. 

 Meanwhile, the central bank said key policy rates were likely to stay unchanged until the release of inflation data on May 5 and the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting on May 15. 

 The bank's overnight borrowing rate is currently at 10.0 percent while the overnight lending rate is at 12.25 percent. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht came off its lows in late trade after being wedged in a tight range for the whole session as the onshore market was closed for the four-day Songkran holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday. 

 The dollar retained its bid tone, although market participants were reluctant to push or mark it up too high against the baht, fearing the central bank's latest disclosure requirements would further dent dollar demand. 

 The central bank has said that from May 1, banks will have to provide details on foreign debt exposure and repayment obligations when their clients buy dollars from them. 

 The one-month offshore forward rate was quoted at 10/15 satang per dollar while the onshore rate was quoted at -9.9/-9.0 satang. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won held off its lows as fears of central bank support and possible equity-linked fund inflows limited the downside, but the soft yen left players keen to buy the dollar on dips. 

 Foreign investors remained net buyers of Korean shares on Monday, picking up a net 1.3 billion won worth, but their purchases were well below Friday's 69.1 billion won as the Easter holiday and expectations of a softer Nasdaq dampened interest. 

 Dealers said there was no sign of direct or indirect central bank intervention on Monday, but the market remained on guard after the authorities' recent aggressive efforts to curb the won's fall. 

 Data released on Monday showed forex reserves fell to $93.64 billion on April 15 from $94.44 billion at end-March, partly due to a $300 million repayment to the IMF. 

 But the central bank declined comment on whether the drop in reserves was also due to recent intervention, which dealers estimate at around $700-$800 billion. 

 On the economic front, the seasonally adjusted jobless rate held steady at 4.2 percent in March and analysts said it could stay above four percent for the year as the economy slows and corporate restructuring continues. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR 

 The Sing dollar was overshadowed by lingering pessimism over the yen and expectations of poor trade data, due on Tuesday. 

 Analyst forecasts for the March data ranged from marginal gains to a contraction, with a Reuters poll producing an average forecast of a 2.87 percent on-year drop in non-oil domestic exports after February's nominal 5.4 percent rise. 

 Dealers said overall the market still favoured the U.S. dollar, but it was wary of central bank intervention after the central bank said earlier this month it was sticking to a tightening bias. 

 The impact of $5.8 billion DBS-Dao Heng acquisition deal ran out of steam as the market awaited further developments. One dealer said DBS had bought dollars actively in the past few weeks, indicating it might have already covered most of the cash required for the planned takeover. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar nudged lower in line with the yen and won but dealers in Singapore said fears of the central bank, which was believed to be active in early trade kept the currency in its recent tight range. 

 They said the central bank intervention at around 32.95 was not aggressive but was enough to signal its intention. 

 A dealer at a European bank in Singapore said the Taiwan dollar was unlikely to break the 32.88-32.98 range in the near term unless the yen made a major move. 

 A lower finish on the local stock market and last week's downgrade of the trade outlook kept sentiment depressed.

title: Emerging  FX  - Lifted by firmer yen before holiday.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 12 (Reuters) - The firmer yen bumped Asian currencier higher in light trade late Thursday ahead of the Easter break. 

 This report will not appear on Friday, April 13, due to the Easter holiday in most of Asia and the Songkran holiday in Thailand. Please see and for reports on the Korean won and Taiwan dollar. 

 The yen extended its recent gains, taking advantage of speculation over U.S. Treasury Secretary Paul O'Neill's commitment to the strong dollar policy. Those gains lent particular support to the North Asian currencies. 

 The dollar was earlier upset by media reports the U.S. National Association for Manufacturers will meet with O'Neill later this month to complain about the strong dollar. 

 In the meantime, the euro edged slightly higher. 

 However, analysts said the outlook for the yen and regional currencies was still cloudy at best, given slowing external demand and the limping tech sector. 

 On the domestic front, Korea's finance ministry said earlier it would expand its foreign exchange reserves and use dollar/won forwards to stabilise the forex market. 

 And the Bank of Thailand said it was content with the current level of the baht. 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won extended its gains alongside the yen, with wariness over possible central bank intervention also helping. 

 Dealers in Singapore said stop-loss dollar sales were triggered around 1,330 and 1,322. "The market was quite long on dollar anyway. So the yen and the concerns over the central bank are good reasons to bail out of these positions," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore. 

 Korean authorities continued to harden their line towards the foreign exchange market. The Finance Ministry said it would push local banks to repay borrowings owed to the central bank in order to boost reserves. 

 It did not elaborate how it intended to use dollar/won forwards to stabilise the forex market, nor whether that included the offshore non-deliverable forward market. 

 But dealers said the market largely ignored the rhetoric, given the lack of detail. A currency analyst also said the onshore forward market was relatively small. 

 Separately, Finance Minister Jin Nyum said the government would not step into the market to support the won unless it saw panic or speculation, adding however that it would coordinate any action with the central bank. 

 THAI BAHT 

 The baht traded in a tight range with low volumes for most of the day as players avoided taking aggressive positions ahead of a long weekend. 

 Financial markets in Bangkok will be closed from April 13-16 to celebrate the Songkran festival that marks the Thai New Year. They will reopen on Tuesday. 

 Dealers in Bangkok said a firmer yen and fear of central bank intervention kept most players from taking long dollar positions. 

 But analysts said poor fundamentals and continuing equity outflows suggested the baht will weaken in the medium term. 

 The Bank of Thailand's assistant governor Chetthavee Charoenpitaks said the central bank was satisfied with the current level and stability of the baht, which he attributed to stability in the yen. 

 He declined to respond when asked whether a recent strengthening of the baht was due to central bank intervention. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar extended gains to above 1.8030 with trading volume picking up in the afternoon after U.S. names sold dollar/Sing as the yen probed two-week highs. 

 Dealers said investment banks and local banks were keen to buy the dollar at 1.8025-30, with others squaring their positions ahead of the long weekend. 

 The market will now focus on the release of non-oil domestic exports on Tuesday, with a poor figure expected to hound the Sing dollar to decade troughs of 1.8235 hit on April 2. 

 But analysts said despite no improvement in the grim economic outlook, fears of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore would support the downside at 1.8180 for now. 

 In February, non-oil domestic exports rose a worse-than-expected 5.4 percent on year from nine percent in January. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso was a shade higher from late Wednesday levels after touching a low of 50.15 in light and sporadic offshore trade. 

 Markets in Manila were closed for the Easter break and will reopen on Monday. 

 Dealers in Singapore said only a few banks were squaring their positions before the Easter holidays and given low volumes, the moves were exaggerated. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar rode the yen's coat-tails, poking above 32.90 as players trimmed long dollar positions after the yen probed two-week highs against the dollar and the euro. 

 Dealers said they had not heard of any central bank intervention in the Taiwan market on Thursday. 

 Recent gains in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index , which is taken as a strong barometer for the island's exports, also boosted sentiment, they said. 

 Foreign fund buying of local stocks also underpinned the currency. On Wednesday, they bought shares worth a net T$1.961 billion, ending an eight-session net selling streak of T$21.751. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah came off an intraday high of 10,380 due to dollar demand from a multi-national company and state banks in a thin pre-holiday market. 

 But its downside was underpinned by hopes the IMF team's visit to Jakarta would lead to the disbursement of a $400 million loan delayed since last year. 

 "We do not think this visit will result in an LOI (letter of intent), but are encouraged that the likelihood of one is increasing," said an IDEAglobal report. 

 "However, the overall picture still remains tenous...IMF is also concerned about budget deficit and says market may not have priced in possibility of deficit running out of control," it said. 

 The rupiah's steadier tone has eased pressure on the central bank to directly or indirectly prop up the local currency. 

 Bank Indonesia on Thursday kept its intervention rates in the rupiah interbank money market unchanged. The intervention rates are among the central bank's tools to manage liquidity.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Ends Higher On Ctrl Bk  Intervention
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended higher Tuesday on intervention by the central bank, traders said. 

 The U.S. currency moved up to an intraday high of 10,830 rupiah in the morning, versus IDR10,820 at Monday's close, on concerns over the shaky political situation in the country. 

 However the central bank intervened to sell about $20 million through brokers, pulling the dollar back to close Asian trading at IDR10,685, below its Monday close. 

 Still, the dollar remains well supported at these levels due to continued political concerns, traders said. 

 Players expect the dollar to rise as a debilitating political standoff between President Abdurrahman Wahid and the Parliament continues. 

 The Parliament has said it wants to impeach Wahid over two financial scandals, while the president denies any wrongdoing. 

 Even as the political situation stagnates, separatist fighting and ethnic violence across the country continues to keep foreign investors on the sidelines. 

 Indonesia's currency, currently at 29-month lows, is unlikely to recover the lost ground of the past weeks unless the political situation improves, analysts say. 

 Further, foreign debt repayment by local companies is fueling demand for the dollar and keeping it on an upward path, they add.

title: Emerging  FX -Yen weighs,  central bank  fears help.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 6 (Reuters) - Asian currencies came under renewed pressure on Friday as the yen's three-day winning streak against the dollar ran into some resistance. 

 The yen stumbled as a much-awaited economic package by the Japanese ruling coalition failed to impress the market, but renewed jawboning boosted it in late trade. 

 The Finance Ministry's Haruhiko Kuroda said it was hard to justify recent moves in the dollar/yen as there had been no big change in Japan's fundamentals and that Japan would take action in currency markets if current trends continued. 

 Most regional currencies opened higher on the back of the yen's overnight gains but a reversal of those gains sparked covering of short dollar positions. 

 But central banks in Korea and Indonesia intervened while the fear of that in Singapore kept the won, rupiah and Sing dollar off recent lows. 

 With Bangkok closed for a holiday, the baht was not so lucky and slipped to a fresh 37-month low in offshore trade. 

 Analysts said central bank threats and actions could temporarily ease some pressure on the currencies but the outlook remained weak on slowing growth and exports. 

 Fresh trading cues were likely to emerge from the U.S. March employment report due at 1230 GMT. 

 Economists polled by Reuters on average expect a higher unemployment rate, up to 4.3 percent from February's 4.2 percent. They also forecast 58,000 new jobs were created outside the farm sector in March, compared with 135,000 in February. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar kept a soft tone as the yen eased. 

 Dealers said local banks placed sizeable U.S. dollar orders in the afternoon, which pushed it down to session lows of 1.8184. 

 But the market turned wary as the Monetary Authority of Singapore was suspected to have defended that level late on Wednesday. This allowed the Sing dollar to avoid a damaging break of 1.8200 which would expose it to decade lows of 1.8230 hit on Monday. 

 But the market saw no signs of aggressive action by the authorities, which again spurred speculation the MAS had already shifted its monetary stance to neutral from a tightening bias. 

 The MAS has said it would review its monetary policy in the middle of the year. 

 Dealers said the market would focus on a revised growth forecast for 2001 and preliminary growth figures for the first quarter due for release on Tuesday. 

 The government estimates the economy will grow between five to seven percent this year, but economists suspect worsening external conditions could slow growth to as low as 4.8 percent. 

 THAI BAHT 

 Offshore players took advantage of a holiday in Bangkok to push the baht to a 37-month low of 45.72. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the dollar crawled higher in ultra-thin trade, which exaggerated the impact of relatively small deals. They added U.S. names were spotted buying up dollar/baht when the yen fell past 125. 

 "With Bangkok on holiday, that means no Bank of Thailand. So you might as well take adventage of that," said a dealer at a European bank, referring to the central bank's suspected intervention to shore up the baht earlier this week. 

 Charts showed the dollar/baht had wandered deeply into overbought territory with a reading of 84.863 on the 14-day relative strength index. 

 Offshore baht funding costs were still firm at 41/52 satang per dollar against 40/50 satang late Thursday. 

 KOREAN WON -02 

 The won was propped up by the Bank of Korea as it tried to track the yen's retreat against the dollar. 

 Dealers estimated the central bank had directly sold about $150-200 million at around 1,358 won in late morning trade, intervening again in the afternoon. 

 Both times the won rose to around its session high of 1,339.9 where importers and offshore players were seen buying dollars. 

 Hong Kong dealers said the intervention, which came after weeks of verbal threats and recent state bank dollar sales, was not as aggressive as expected, given the $1.5 billion average daily turnover in the won market. 

 They said fears the central bank was probably testing the depth of the market and might come in more strongly later, kept players cautious. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar was firmer, but did not venture very far from Thursday's close of 32.979 as the yen wavered. 

 For the past several weeks, the Taiwan dollar has been tracking the yen closely as Taiwan and Japan compete on electronics exports. 

 Consumer inflation data showed a slight 0.44 percent on-year rise in March against February's 1.02 percent fall. Analysts said the slight rise meant inflation was still benign and may provide more room for the central bank to cut rates. 

 On the Taiwan dollar NDF market, the six-month rate was at 0.560/610 and the one-year was at 0.850/900. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah dipped to a near four-week low of 10,930 as early dollar buying by some state and foreign banks sent local corporates scrambling for dollars. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the central bank pumped in around $10-30 million from around 10,930 all the way to 10,850, but they added that local corporate demand for dollars was strong in the 10,750-10,800 range. 

 The market was unimpressed by news an IMF review mission would start its work in Jakarta on Wednesday as conditions of the visit had been met. 

 Dealers said the market was likely to wait for a formal resumption of IMF lending before pushing the rupiah higher. 

 However, Bank Indonesia governor Sjahril Sabirin said he expected the IMF visit to help boost sentiment in the rupiah which could give the central bank room to lower interest rates. 

 The mission's visit should pave the way for a new $400 million loan from the IMF which has been delayed since late last year due to a dispute between Jakarta and the Fund over key reforms. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso ended at 50.200, slightly below its Thursday close after hitting a session low of 50.50 in line with weakness in other regional currencies. 

 Dealers said oil importers and some foreign banks were seen bidding the dollar up in early trade but inflows from overseas workers ahead of a long weekend capped the peso's downside. 

 Manila's financial markets will be closed on Monday for the Day of Valour.

title: Bank  Indonesia  says to  intervene  to help rupiah.
text:
JAKARTA, April 6 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia said it would continue to intervene into the currency market to help stem further falls in the rupiah, seen testing the psychological barrier of 11,000 to the dollar in early trade on Friday. 

 "We will always continue to make policies in line with what is needed such as by raising interest rates and by selling foreign exchange reserves," central bank deputy governor Miranda Goeltom told reporters. 

 "We will continue selling foreign exchange reserves," she said when asked whether the central bank needed to intervene to help prevent the rupiah weakening further. 

 "(Intervention) is not unusual," Goeltom said. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 10,905/10,935 against the dollar by 0230 GMT. It has come under strong pressure recently due in part to high dollar demand for foreign debt repayment purposes and growing domestic political uncertainty.

 Still, central bank intervention was able to pull the dollar back from its highs, traders said.

title: Emerging  FX -Stumble on weak yen, U.S.-China woes.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 4 (Reuters) - Asian currencies buckled under a heap of negative factors, ranging from a weaker yen, U.S.-China tensions over a U.S. spy plane, and increased risk aversion towards the region as the global economy cooled on Wednesday. 

 Analysts said the dollar remained a preferred currency despite sustained losses in U.S. equities, a sharp decline in U.S. interest rates, and easing oil prices. 

 "Longer-term structural optimism for the U.S. economy triumphs for now over shorter-term cyclical pessimism with respect to the value of dollar," said a Salomon Smith Barney report. 

 It suggested that investors continue to stay long of dollars against the regional currencies. 

 The yen retained its bearish tone after a much-hyped package of emergency measures for Japan's ailing economy was delayed. Dealers said the dollar might consolidate briefly around this level before moving higher toward 127 yen. 

 The standoff between Washington and Beijing over a U.S. spy plane and its crew also kept the market nervous. 

 China has adopted a hardline, blaming the U.S. for Sunday's mid-air collision between the spy plane and a Chinese fighter over the South China Sea, demanding an apology and holding on to the 24 crew. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR The Sing dollar trailed off to lows of 1.8158 in quiet afternoon trade, with sporadic U.S. dollar bids countered by unwinding of long positions. 

 There was renewed talk of Singapore's Changi airport looking to buy Sydney Airport after the Australian government said last week it would complete the sale in the second half of 2001. The Sydney Airports Corp has said its book value is A$3.25 billion. Dealers said prospects of further capital outflows related to more M&A activities were handicapping the Sing dollar. 

 A disappointing 1.2 point dip in Singapore's Purchasing Manager's Index in March reinforced concerns about the slowing economy, analysts said. The figure represented the second month of contraction since January 1999. 

 However, one currency strategist said the downside was well supported at 1.8180 and then 1.8230, levels where she said the Monetary Authority of Singapore had intervened in London on Monday, when the Sing dollar fell to decade lows. 

 She said her calculation showed the Sing dollar nominal exchange rate was bobbing out of the policy band, which the MAS uses to manage the economy. 

 "Bears think they can pressurise the Sing forever, but stop and think about it. This is way out of the band," she said. 

 "I think the MAS is waiting for a big jump (in dollar/Sing) to intervene in the market again." 

 KOREAN WON -2 

 The won slid to a fresh 30-month closing low of 1,365.2 as the yen stumbled past 126, despite the Korean government's pledges to introduce measures aimed at stabilising the currency. 

 Dealers said trading was initially cautious as the market remained wary over central bank intervention. The Bank of Korea was rumoured to have intervened via state banks on Tuesday. 

 However, the won later succumbed as the dollar gained more ground on the yen and foreign investors sold a net 177.4 billion won worth of stocks. 

 Authorities said earlier they were working on a package of measures to stabilise the market. They also repeated warnings that they were watching the market closely. 

 On the offshore non-deliverable forward market, one-month dollar/won was at 1,358.5/59.5 against 1,344.5/45.5 late Tuesday and the three-month was at 1,362.5/64.5 against 1,347.3/48.3. 

 THAI BAHT The baht turned tail to hit fresh three-year lows of 45.47, despite official efforts to talk it up. 

 Local banks joined a selling spree with banks in Singapore and foreign banks in Bangkok, dealers said. 

 The market had been wary about possible intervention by the Bank of Thailand after talk circulated authorities sold U.S. dollars via a Singapore-based bank at 45.40 late on Tuesday. 

 But bears regained confidence in trouncing the baht after Finance Minister Somkid Jatusripitak said the BOT had not intervened to support the baht. 

 He said the baht's weakness was caused by external factors and it did not suggest the Thai economy was not sound. The central bank said the baht has been too volatile versus regional currencies and that it was ready to act. 

 "They are trying to find ways to slow the pace of the decline," a currency analyst said. "They don't mind the decline. They mind the pace of the decline." 

 He said firmer offshore baht funding costs provided the only solace for the baht. The one-month forward rate stood at 50/70 satang per dollar against 50/60 earlier. 

 INDONESIAN RUPIAH 

 The rupiah hit a three-week low of 10,600 as demand for dollars from local corporates spiked despite sporadic intervention by Bank Indonesia. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said with an increase in the flow of bad news from the economic front, in addition to currency weakness across the region, most corporates were staying long of dollars. 

 A dealer at a European bank said the central bank pumped in about $25 million and finally succeeded in defending the 10,600 mark and propping it up to 10,560. 

 The dealer said early intervention had little impact as the bank sold dollars in small amounts, at different levels. 

 Governor Sjahril Sabirin said BI would continue intervening as the rupiah would get worse without the intervention. 

 Meanwhile chief economics minister Rizal Ramli warned the 2001 budget deficit could overshoot the target of 3.2 percent of gross domestic product to slightly over five percent. 

 The defence minister said violence could get worse if political tensions do not ease. 

 PHILIPPINE PESO 

 The peso eased to a low of 50.17, not seen since mid-January, as importers chased the dollar up expecting more pressure from other regional currencies in the coming days. 

 Dealers in Manila said most exporters were holding back their earnings while importers were trying to lock in their dollar needs before the peso slipped lower with the regional downturn. 

 A dealer at a U.S. bank said support for the peso was likely to come in at around 50.20 while its upside was capped at 49.80. 

 TAIWAN DOLLAR 

 The Taiwan dollar tripped over the weaker yen, but resisted the 33 level thanks to wariness over central bank intervention. 

 Dealers in Singapore said the central bank was speculated to be selling dollars when the Taiwan dollar edged to 32.995. But they added the market was expected to test that level again, especially if the yen showed further weakness. 

 Outflows from foreign investors also hobbled sentiment towards the local dollar as Taiwan stocks closed lower for the fourth straight session. Foreign investors sold a net T$5.132 billion in Taiwan shares on Tuesday. 

 Taiwan was also coping with anxiety over the stand-off between the U.S. and China over a U.S. surveillance plane. China regards Taiwan as a renegade province and has been perturbed by the Bush administration's more openly pro-Taiwan stance and possible U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.

title: Rupiah to get worse without  intervention - Indonesia .
text:
JAKARTA, April 4 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia said on Wednesday it would continue intervening in the foreign exchange market to help the ailing rupiah, added the currency would get worse without intervention. 

 "Without intervention, (the rupiah) will clearly get worse," Bank Indonesia governor Sjahril Sabirin told Reuters. 

 Asked if that meant the bank would continue intervening despite some criticism that intervention had done little to stem the rupiah's fall, Sabirin said: "Yes." 

 Sabirin also said the central bank had so far no plan to ease rules requiring commercial banks to achieve a minimum of eight percent capital adequacy ratio (CAR) and a maximum of five percent non-performing loans (NPLs) by year-end. 

 Bankers and analysts had expressed concerns the weak rupiah and high interest rates would hit bank earnings, raise non-performing loan levels and eventually erode their fragile capital base, making it more difficult to meet the requirements.

title: Asia Markets-Mixed as domestic factors rule sentiment.
text:
SINGAPORE, March 28 (Reuters) - Asian share markets were 

 mixed on Wednesday with domestic factors overtaking an earlier 

 upbeat mood stemming from improving U.S. consumer confidence, 

 while currencies sat tight and waited for fresh cues. 

     The U.S. Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 

 in March, beating analysts' forecast for a fall. 

     The data caught most the market by surprise, driving U.S. 

 equities higher and fueling hopes that Asian exports might not 

 see a severe drop-off in demand. 

     However, domestic concerns hit Taiwan and Korea in 

 particular. Investors in Korea fretted over an expected debt 

 write-off for Hyundai Engineering and Construction, pushing the 

 benchmark Korea Composite Index lower. 

 Concerns over the general health of Taiwan's economy and a 

 disappointing dividend payment by United Microelectronics Corp 

 sent Taiwan shares lower. 

 But Tokyo share prices firmed slightly on the back of 

 cautious optimism that the Japanese government will muster 

 together policies to help the economy. 

 Talk that foreign investors were increasing their exposure 

 to Japanese equities bolstered the yen as well, 

 providing underlying support to regional currencies. 

 The market was also speculating that the Bank of Japan's 

 keenly watched tankan survey of business sentiment, due on 

 Monday, may be better than expected. 

     Hong Kong's Hang Seng also climbed, led by gains in China 

 Mobile and HSBC. 

     ARBITRAGE TALK ROCKS SING DOLLAR 

     While the steady yen kept the dollar reasonably tame 

 against regional currencies, Asian currencies were not able to 

 get close to their resistance levels. 

     The Singapore dollar slipped to a low of 1.7955, its lowest 

 level since August 31, 1998, a few days after Singapore 

 Telecommunications Ltd announced its successful bid to buy 

 Australia's Cable & Wireless Optus. 

     Dealers said the Sing dollar sank as hedge funds sought to 

 arbitrage between the shares of SingTel and Optus. 

     The market was abuzz with talk that SingTel was only 

 halfway through meeting its dollar requirements for the deal. A 

 dealer at European bank said a local bank, believed to buying 

 on behalf of SingTel, had probably bought $2-$3 billion. 

 "The Sing dollar market is relatively small, and to meet 

 all the requirements for this deal at once will really upset 

 the market," said the dealer, adding that daily turnover in the 

 local forex market was between $1-$2 billion. 

 Even though there has been scant sign of the Monetary 

 Authority of Singapore despite the Sing's rapid decline, 

 analysts said the authorities were unlikely to change their 

 policy stance of a gradually stronger currency. 

 "The MAS has always been very clear that they regard the 

 exchange rate as a tool to fight inflation, not as a way to 

 compete on exports," said Gerard Teo, regional economist at 

 ABN-AMRO in Singapore. 

 He pointed out that while the Sing dollar has weakened 

 significantly, it was still within its trading band of its 

 trade-weighted basket of currencies. 

 INDONESIA'S PARADE OF WOES 

 The rupiah was once again at the mercy of Indonesia's 

 volatile politics, though wariness over central bank

intervention kept it well behaved. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the market was also reluctant to 

 push the dollar higher in case the Indonesian Bank 

 Restructuring Agency converted more of a total of $500 million 

 from recent asset sales. 

 However, the rupiah remained on the backfoot as President 

 Abdurrahman Wahid responded to a parliamentary censure of him 

 over two financial scandals. 

     Wahid apologised for any "inappropriate behaviour" but 

 remained steadfast in his rejection of the censure. 

     Fears of violence between Wahid's supporters and opponents 

 were brewing in Jakarta, threatening to roil the country's 

 already fragile markets and currency.

title: Bk Indonesia's Gov: Interest Rates To Continue Rising
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Indonesia's Central Bank Governor Sjahril Sabirin said interest rates would continue to rise given the weakeness in the rupiah. 

 Bank Indonesia will also continue to intervene by selling foreign exchange reserves to help the ailing currency, which has hit 30-month lows this year, he told reporters. 

 The central bank pushed up rates to 15.24% on its one-month note Wednesday. The rates have risen by almost half a percentage point in two weeks. 

 But the rate hikes and intervention won't help the rupiah, analysts say, as the currency's woes are politically driven.

title: B. Indonesia  says no plan to cut rph  intervention .
text:
JAKARTA, March 22 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia said on Thursday it had no plan to reduce intervention in the foreign exchange market to prop up the rupiah even though foreign reserves had dropped slightly. 

 When asked whether the central bank would reduce intervention because of the drop, senior deputy governor Anwar Nasution told reporters: "No. No." 

 Bank Indonesia has said the country's foreign exchange reserves fell to $28.57 billion as of the second week of March from $29.12 billion in the previous week. 

 The central bank said the fall was due partly to foreign debt repayments, but foreign exchange dealers said a significant portion was likely to have been used for intervention. 

 By 0830 GMT the ailing rupiah was being quoted at 10,340/10,370 to the dollar.

title: Emerging  FX  - Easier on Fed's aggressive hike.
text:
SINGAPORE, May 17 (Reuters) - A widely expected aggressive 

 tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve overnight pressured most 

 Asian regional currencies against the dollar in early Wednesday 

 trade. 

     The Fed raised its key rates by half a percentage point, 

 bringing the federal fund rate for overnight loans between 

 banks  to 6.5 percent and the more symbolic discount rate to 

 six percent. 

     The Philippine central bank responded to the move by 

 raising its key overnight rates by a similar half percentage 

 point. 


    But the Philippine peso	  opened the day weaker,



dragged down by other regional currencies and concerns over



violence in the southern Mindanao region.



    "Given that growth in these countries (is) still very



nascent and external risks are increasingly building towards a



slowdown in the U.S. economy...it is very likely that



governments in these countries will steer towards weaker Asian


currencies," said Thio Chin Loo, currency strategist at BNP



Paribas Group in Singapore.



Dollar/yen firmed following the Fed's announcement



but pared some gains as interbank dealers unwound long



positions.



PHILIPPINE PESO



The peso edged down to a 23-month low despite the central



bank's decision to raise overnight rates by 50 basis points



with immediate effect.



A bank official told Reuters the hike would take the



overnight borrowing rate to 9.5 percent and overnight lending



to 11.75 percent.



    The rate hike was on top of the Philippines' move to raise



rates by 25 basis points on May 2.



    But dealers said the currency was likely to slide further



on weak regional currencies and worries over violence in



Mindanao.



    A dealer in Manila said the peso support level stays at



41.70, adding that the central bank would have to intervene to



keep it from plunging to 41.80.



    KOREAN WON	   -2



    The won was slightly softer as players sought to buy the



dollar after it strengthened against the yen in early trade.



    A foreign bank dealer in Seoul said dollar/won would likely



face resistance at around 1,116 won, where some dollar sales



from foreign investors buying local stocks were expected.



    Foreign investors bought a net 90.23 billion won worth of



shares on the Korea Stock Exchange on Tuesday.



    Dealers forecast the won to move between 1,114 and 1,116.5



for the day.



    INDONESIAN RUPIAH	



    The rupiah remained hobbled around 8,600 per dollar,



looking set to test recent lows again despite President



Adurrahman Wahid's call on Tuesday for Bank Indonesia and state



banks to rescue the ailing currency.



    Dealers questioned whether central bank intervention could



bring a sustainable recovery in the rupiah.



    Bank Indonesia has already said it does not regard


intervention or interest rate hikes as a viable solution, as



political factors played a large part in the rupiah's weakness.



    Dealers said trading in the rupiah would remain thin, as



the confidence crisis grew.



    "With all the problems there, no one wants to be short



dollars, though we could see some (dollar) profit-taking at



around 8,650," a dealer at a European bank said.



    THAI BAHT	



    The baht edged down in sympathy with other regional


currencies, and some dealers said it looked set to test the



39.50 support.



    The dollar is in favour after the Fed raised borrowing



costs by 50 basis points, dealers said.



    The central bank governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul said on



Tuesday that the central bank would not intervene in foreign



exchange markets unless its movements became too volatile.



    He also said the central bank would keep a low interest



rate policy to keep economic recovery on track. The move could



lead to a weaker baht.



    SINGAPORE DOLLAR	



    The Sing dollar eased slightly, pressured by a softer yen



in early Asian trade. The Sing is managed against a



trade-weighted basket of currencies of which the yen is



believed to represent a substantial portion.



Dealers said dollar demand was still strong after the Fed's



decision to raise borrowing costs by a widely-expected 50 basis



points.



    But the currency was seen supported by possible


intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore at 1.7350.



    It resistance was pegged at 1.7270.



    TAIWAN DOLLAR	



    The Taiwan dollar rebounded on the back of dollar profit



taking after falling to a nearly two-month low on Tuesday.



    Players were cautious about pushing the currency much lower



as the central bank was heard defending it at around T$30.799.



    Dealers expected Wall Street-inspired gains to help



underpin the currency despite some political uncertainties



ahead of the the presidential inauguration on May 20.

title: Rupiah down but U.S. rate hike reduces uncertainty.
text:
JAKARTA, May 17 (Reuters) - Indonesia's rupiah edged down early on Wednesday on lingering concerns about President Abdurrahman Wahid's handling of the economy, dealers said. 

 A decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise borrowing costs by 50 basis points, as expected, its biggest move in five years, surprised no one but helped remove one of the negative factors affecting the rupiah, dealers said. 

 "The 50 basis-point hike does help remove one of the negative factors. But concerns remain on the government's poor handling of the economy. Now it no longer has significant external factors to blame," one dealer at a European bank said. 

 By 0150 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 8,545/8,595 to the dollar versus 8,500/8,550 in late local trade on Tuesday. 

 The rupiah was traded in a range of between 8,545 to 8,675 rupiah in morning trade and was likely to remain in that range the rest of the day, another dealer said. 

 Dealers said local corporates were largely on the sidelines, but they were likely to enter the market when the dollar fell below 8,500. 

 Dealers said the market was slow as state banks, which led dollar selling on Tuesday after Wahid asked them to do so, were not yet active in the market in early trade. 

 Wahid on Tuesday asked Bank Indonesia and state banks to help the battered currency which had fallen more than 18 percent against the dollar so far this year. 

 Dealers questioned whether central bank intervention could bring a sustainable recovery in the rupiah - Bank Indonesia has already said it does not regard intervention or interest rate hikes as a viable solution as political factors play a large part in the currency's weakness. 

 Wahid, facing a growing crisis of confidence in his handling of the economy, also ordered his finance minister to review economic projections in this year's budget which are now looking too optimistic. ((Jakarta newsroom +62 21 384 6364, Fax +62 21 344 8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Indonesian Shares End Up 3.4% On Tech Rebound,Stronger IDR
text:

 JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian shares ended higher Wednesday on a technical rebound in blue chips, lifting the main index off a 13-month low reached Tuesday. 

 The JSX Composite index ended up 3.4%, or 17.032 points at 514.851. Gainers led decliners 127 to 22, with 41 stocks unchanged. 

 Volume was 375 million shares valued at 729 billion rupiah (IDR). 

 The dollar was trading at IDR8,395, compared with IDR8,535 late Tuesday. 

 Jakarta shares opened higher Wednesday after Wall Street brushed off the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's 50 basis-point interest rate hike, the head of research at a local brokerage said. 

 He said there was also a sharp increase in the afternoon session after the Indonesian government signed its letter of intent to the International Monetary Fund, which should pave the way for the release of a $400 million loan installment next month. 

 The market was also boosted by a rebound in market heavyweight Telkom after the stock fell IDR200 Tuesday to its lowest level in more than seven months. Telkom ended up IDR225, or 7.6%, at IDR3,175. 

 The head of research at another local brokerage also said intervention by Bank Indonesia in the weakening rupiah helped strengthen the currency and had a positive effect on the stock market. 

 Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin said Wednesday the central bank has sold nearly $300 million to boost the rupiah this week. 

 "People can see now that the government has a strong will to intervene," the head of research said. 

 The research head said a technical rebound across most sectors also helped lift the main index from Tuesday's fall below the key 500 point support level. 

 Blue chips led the recovery, with cigarette stocks regaining lost ground after recent heavy losses. 

 Gudang Garam ended up IDR375, or 3.2%, at IDR12,075, while rival cigarette producer HM Sampoerna added IDR300, or 2.5%, to IDR12,325. 

 International call operator Indosat was also stronger, with its shares closing IDR375 higher, or 3.8%, at IDR10,275. 

 There was also a technical rebound in retail stocks, with Ramayana ending up IDR200, or 4.8%, at IDR4,400, and Matahari adding IDR50, or 5.9%, to IDR900. 

 But automaker Astra International bucked the trend, falling sharply as company employees rushed to offload shares that the company will be grant as options next week. 

 Astra ended down IDR200, or 6.3%, at IDR2,975.

title: Indonesian rupiah off lows on Wahid comments.
text:
JAKARTA, May 16 (Reuters) - Indonesia's rupiah was off its lows on Tuesday as dealers covered short rupiah positions after President Abdurrahman Wahid asked Bank Indonesia and state banks to help the battered currency. 

 By 0910 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 8,500/8,550 to the dollar versus a low of 8,725/8,745 in morning trade ahead of Wahid's comments and 8,460/8,510 in late local trade on Monday. 

 The rupiah has fallen just over 18 percent so far this year and dealers said if the rupiah strengthens above 8,500, dollar buying will almost certainly return. 

 "Under the law Bank Indonesia is not under the supervision of President Wahid, but still players are worried about being short of rupiah," one foreign bank dealer said. 

 Dealers questioned whether central bank intervention could bring a sustainable recovery in the rupiah - Bank Indonesia has already said it does not regard intervention or interest rate hikes as a viable solution as political factors play a large part in the currency's weakness. 

 Wahid, facing a growing crisis of confidence in his handling of the economy, also ordered his finance minister to review economic projections in this year's budget which are now looking too optimistic. 

 Wahid himself gave a rosy outlook for economic growth this year, saying GDP was expected to grow up to 5.5 percent following two years of deep recession. 

 The Indonesian statistics bureau, however, offered a less rosy outlook. On Monday it said growth this year could be as low as 1.54 percent in the worst case, well below previous estimates of around four percent. 

 Dealers said the rupiah's rebound on Tuesday was led by state banks. Local corporates, meanwhile, mostly stood to the side. 

 "They are largely on the sidelines waiting for better rates. More corporate dollar buying is likely to emerge when the dollar falls to below 8,500," one said.

title: Indonesian Rupiah Ends Almost Flat On Wahid Remarks
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- The Indonesian rupiah ended almost unchanged Tuesday after President Abdurrahman Wahid called for action to support the currency, arresting the dollar's earlier appreciation. 

 Wahid said he would ask state banks and the central bank to take action to shore up the local currency, in contrast to anti-interventionist comments Monday from Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Miranda Gultom. 

 The dollar ended Asian trading at 8,535 rupiah, against IDR8,540 late Monday. 

 Dealers said Wahid's remarks lent some support to the rupiah and prompted some participants to take profit after earlier pushing the dollar to IDR8,740. 

 Wahid also said he had asked the finance minister to look into the impact the weak currency would have on the budget. 

 However, the market is still seeking clarity on monetary policy and in particular, how much pressure Wahid is putting on Bank Indonesia to support the currency. The central bank was made independent last year. 

 Wahid's assertion that the economy could grow up to 5.5% this year also confused the market. His comments came after the Central Statistics Bureau said Monday that the economy would grow by only 1.5% if current conditions persist. 

 Dealers said the rupiah would take its lead Wednesday from the results of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting on interest rates.

title: Indonesia  Must Weigh Downside Of  Currency Intervention
text:
SINGAPORE -(Dow Jones)- Of the Southeast Asian nations considering central bank intervention to shore up their faltering currencies, Indonesia may well be at the head of the queue. 

 But such meddling in the market is never without its costs, and Indonesia probably would suffer the harshest side effects by doing so, analysts say. 

Currencies across the region have been trending downward for several weeks in the face of broad-based dollar strength associated with rising interest rates in the U.S. In the case of Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines, the pressure has been exacerbated by a host of local factors weighing on the currencies. 

 For Indonesia, the road has been perhaps the roughest, with the currency experiencing wild swings amid growing investor uncertainty about the Jakarta government's ability to push through reforms and keep the economic expansion on track. 

 President Abdurrahman Wahid and his top advisors haven't helped matters by issuing confusing statements about exactly what the government was prepared to do to keep the rupiah from falling further. 

 Wahid's latest jawboning Tuesday appeared to provide some stability for the currency as the dollar fell to about 8,500 rupiah after trading as high as IDR8,720 earlier in the day. 

 "I have asked the finance minister to persuade state banks to help (boost the rupiah)," Wahid said at a news conference. 

 "I have also asked Bank Indonesia to take necessary action to stop the rupiah weakening," he added, in a clear effort to prod intervention by the supposedly independent central bank. 

 But with limited foreign currency reserves, the central bank would be limited by the amount it could spend defending the rupiah, said Steve Brice, treasury economist for Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore. 

 With a huge debt level more than 100% of GDP, Indonesia can ill afford to squander its reserves in what would likely be an ill-fated attempt to stop a stampeding market, analysts say. 

 Such a move also would go against the advice of the International Monetary Fund, which has been providing the discipline keeping Indonesia on the path to reform, Brice added. 

 "The IMF has been keeping Indonesia pointed in the right direction. The only way we'll see the rupiah strengthen is through a massive change in international investor confidence that comes with continued reform," he said. 

 Other possible quick fixes available to Indonesia, such as capital controls or a currency board, also would do more harm than good because they would take the pressure off the government to stick with the tough IMF-prescribed reforms, Brice said. 

 John Dodsworth, the IMF's Indonesia representative, made the institution's position clear in comments Monday. 


"We don't think the government should spend the money on defending an
exchange rate when it has so many other choices to spend the money on,"
he said in Brussels.
  - - 16/05/00 09-38G



In contrast to Indonesia, government officials in Thailand and the
Philippines probably are not overly concerned about the recent
depreciation of their currencies, analysts said.



They might even quietly invite a certain amount of slippage to help
the competitiveness of their exports, as long as inflation remains under
control, analysts said.



Merrill Lynch's forecast for the Thai baht rests mainly on the
performance of domestic inflation.



"As long as inflation does not exceed 4%, we believe that the Bank of
Thailand can tolerate some baht weakness," said Supavud Saicheua, head
of Thailand economics for Merrill Lynch.



Thailand, which last week became the first financial crisis victim to
emerge from IMF oversight, was rumored to have supported the baht
through central bank intervention when the dollar rose above the
THB39.000 level.



But the central bank's motivation needs to be carefully examined,
Supavud said in a research paper.



"We believe the BOT's intervention in the foreign exchange market to
push the baht back below 39 per dollar does not signal an attempt to
defend the baht at that level," he said. It appeared to be more of an
effort to prevent excessive volatility and deter speculators from
attacking the currency, according to Supavud.



The Bank of Thailand's main objective is to keep the Thai economic
recovery from stalling, and to do so it needs to keep interest rates low
and the baht competitive against other regional currencies, he said.



The Philippines similarly probably will tolerate a certain amount of
peso depreciation to keep its economic expansion moving forward, Brice
said. The currency has been under pressure lately from expectations of
higher U.S. interest rates and government fighting with separatist
rebels in the southern Philippines.



The dollar closed Tuesday at 41.630 pesos, its highest level since
late October 1998.



Economic fundamentals, including the Philippines' improving budget
situation, should be encouraging investment there, Brice said.



"Unfortunately for the authorities, the market is not looking at
that," he said.



The central bank will probably remain on the sidelines as long as the
depreciation of the peso occurs in an orderly fashion, Brice said.



"If the dollar hits 42 pesos over the coming week I don't think they
will be worried at all."
