title: FOCUS - Indonesian markets weaken, rupiah plunges.
text:
JAKARTA, Aug 13 (Reuter) - Indonesia's markets went through another harrowing session on Wednesday with the rupiah plunging to a record low before recovering on central bank intervention and the stock market closing markedly weaker. 

 The fallout from continuing weakness in South East Asian currencies drove the rupiah to a historic low against the dollar for the second time in four weeks, forcing Bank Indonesia to intervene in the market, dealers said. 

 The Jakarta stock market composite index closed down 0.66 percent at 658.60 points in response to the weaker currency and higher interest rates announced by Bank Indonesia in a vain bid to stem currency speculation, brokers said. 

 The index has fallen by more than 50 points since the beginning of the month on a combination of high interest rates, new controls on margin finance and a slew of rights issues. 

 The rupiah fell to a low of 2,682 to the dollar in the afternoon despite the higher rates before recovering on the intervention to 2,650/80. 

 The bank's intervention band, the parameters outside of which it will enter the market, was maintained at 2,378/2,682 at the daily fixing, indicating authorities were not immediately considering any change in policy. 

 There was no indication of how much money the bank had pumped into the market. Analysts said it could well be a losing battle given the continuing weakness in all South East Asian currencies and their susceptibility to contagion. 

 "It's useless for the central bank to intervene in a bearish market," said Jimmy Koh, regional economist for the I.D.E.A. research consultancy. He noted that the Malaysian central bank had spent some $8.8 billion in intervention measures when the ringgit was under attack earlier this month, but with little to show for its efforts. 

 The ringgit slumped to a 42-month low of 2.7930 against the dollar on Tuesday and continued to be weak on Wednesday. Its weakness has spread to Indonesia, compounding earlier contagion from the Thai baht, analysts said. 

 "First it was the tom yam effect," said Koh. "Now it's the asam laksa effect," referring to a fiery Thai soup and popular Malaysian noodles-in-soup dish. The fallout from currency turmoil in Thailand and Malaysia has hit all regional markets. 

 Earlier, Bank Indonesia raised interest rates for central bank certificates of all maturities by 100 basis points. The move makes it more expensive for investors to borrow rupiah, which could then be used for speculation. 

 But Koh said the raising of rates could only be used as a short-term measure and forecast a further fall in the rupiah as domestic corporates began to hedge their currency risks. 

 "Corporates here are not used to hedging risk, but with things the way they are, they have no option," Koh said. "That will affect the rupiah further." 

 Dealers in Jakarta said the contagion effect was exacerbated by a newspaper report quoting a leading local economist as saying that the rupiah should be allowed to find its own level. 

 Sjahrir, an economist and brokerage firm owner, told the Kompas daily that Bank Indonesia need not intervene and that the market would ultimately decide a fair value for the rupiah. 

 "According to me, just let the rupiah fall to 2,700 or 2,800. The central bank does not have to do anything. Once they (speculators) realise the central bank hasn't done anything, the dollar is already overvalued," Sjahrir was quoted as saying. 

 The rupiah's previous historic low was 2,665 on July 21. 

 Donald Hanna, an economist with Goldman Sachs in Hong Kong, said raising interest rates was however a sensible move to curb the rupiah volatility. 

 "The economy is not as weak as in Thailand," he said. "There is more resilience to higher interest rates. There is no fundamental reason for the rupiah to weaken."

title: BANK INDONESIA DEFENDS BAND, RUPIAH STABILISES.
text:
JAKARTA, Aug 13 (Reuter) - Bank Indonesia defended its intervention band on Wednesday after the rupiah fell to a historic low, erasing much of the currency's losses by the close of the day, dealers said. 

 They said the central bank intervened by selling dollars in the spot market although some said the bank was also seen in the one-month forward market. 

 The rupiah bounced back sharply to 2,620 from a historic low of 2,682 before easing back to 2,650/60 at 0945 GMT at the close of trading in Jakarta. The rupiah opened at 2,643/50. 

 Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,644/54 and 2,665/68, respectively. 

 Bank Indonesia kept its dollar-rupiah intervention band unchanged on Wednesday at 2,378/2,682 but raised its conversion band to 2,629/2,677 from 2,616/2,664 on Tuesday. 

 Dealers said the market had speculated that the band would be widened or possibly removed altogether after the rupiah plunged before recovering on the intervention. 

 Dealers said they were not clear how much money the central bank had pumped into the market to calm nervous operators. 

 "But for sure we are going to see a tightened money market on Friday. The move will result in rupiah scarcity," one said. 

 The local bank dealer said operators had immediately locked in longer-term liquidity available now. 

 Dealers said the central bank was trying to defend the band with the help of the short-term interest rate policy. 

 The bank raised interest rates for bilateral central bank certificates (SBIs) of all maturities by 100 basis points. Overnight rates were raised to 15.0 percent, two-to-six day SBIs to 16.0 percent, one-week to 10.5, two-week to 11.0, one-month to 11.625, three to 11.5, six to 12.125 and one-year to 12.75. 

 The central bank also remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market. 

 The central bank cut its bilateral SBI rates for papers above one-week by 50 basis points last Friday after the foreign exchange market showed signs of stabilisation. 

 However, renewed pressure spilling over from neighbouring countries knocked the rupiah down further, forcing the central bank to impose a tighter money policy to contain speculation. 

 Dealers said heavy selling of the rupiah on Wednesday was triggered on contagion effect from the Singapore dollar and the Malaysian ringgit and on comments by a local economist. 

 Sjahrir, an economist and brokerage firm owner, was quoted in the Kompas daily as saying the market would ultimately decide a fair value for the rupiah. 

 "According to me, just let the rupiah fall to 2,700 or 2,800. The central bank does not have to do anything. Once they (speculators) realise the central bank hasn't done anything, the dollar is already overvalued," Sjahrir was quoted as saying. 

 But an economist with one of the country's state-owned banks said the central bank was likely to continue defending the band. 

 "We all know that there is nothing wrong with the economy or the country's fundamentals. But speculators keep trying. The bank has to give some certainty for the people," the economist said. 

 "There is little use of pointing to fundamentals. We just have to wait until the storm is over," he said. 

 Dealers said swap rates remained high as the central bank was seen mainly in the spot market. 

 Overnight swap was at 1.05/1.25 and tom/next at 1.5/1.8. 

 One local bank dealer said offshore operators were seen biddish in one-week and one-month swaps, pushing them to end at 7.5/8.5 and 30.0/40.0 points, respectively. 

 Two-month swap was at 55.0/61.0, three at 72.0/78.0 and six at 130.0/136.0 points. 

 Overnight money was last at 20.0/25.0 percent. 

 The central bank had intervened last month in the forward market with some one billion dollars.

title: Bank Indonesia's Defense Of Embattled Rupiah Seems Futile
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Currency speculators Wednesday pushed the Indonesian rupiah through the weak end of Bank Indonesia's intervention band and sparked numerous - though unconfirmed - reports that the central bank spent upwards of $200 million intervening in defense of its currency. 

 This apparent action did succeed in pushing the rupiah back within its 12% band, but traders in Singapore and Jakarta remain convinced an eventual second attack on the rupiah's band is inevitable. 

 Many economists assert a defense of the rupiah is justified on grounds it's undervalued, but also concede the speculative fervor currently in the market likely makes such a defense futile. 

 "The Indonesian authorities are in a very difficult situation with no real answers," said Don Hanna, a regional economist at Goldman Sachs & Co. in Hong Kong. "We certainly believe the rupiah is fairly valued within its current band. But at the same time, we don't want to see Indonesia falling on its own sword defending it." 

 Pressure on the rupiah has been felt all week on the back of continued speculative attacks against regional currencies and a strengthening of the dollar globally. 

 But early Wednesday, the attack intensified, as traders at offshore banks began selling the rupiah for dollars as rumors swept the Singapore market that Bank Indonesia was preparing to abandon its current intervention band in favor of a freely floating currency. Indonesian companies were also seen buying dollars to hedge against rupiah exposure. 

 Bank Indonesia responded by raising the rates of its Sertifikat Bank Indonesia, or SBI, money-market paper across the board by a full percentage point. But little support was seen. 

 The currency market grew bolder hours later on news Indonesia's central bank governor and finance minister had scheduled a lunch-time news conference. Speculation centered on the possible announcement of a free-floating policy, but the meeting turned out to be a tutorial for the local media on coverage of the rupiah's woes. The foreign press was barred from the meeting. 

Central Bank Governor Soedradjad Djiwandono instructed the chief editors of local papers to be less alarmist and speculative in their reporting, according to those in attendance. But in a comment that could be perceived as a tip-off, he also said the government "would use all of its monetary tools" to stabilize the nation's currency. 

 At around the same time, the dollar penetrated the top of its trading band against the rupiah, reaching a high of 2,682 rupiah. It was the first time the top end of the band has been broken during the recent spate of regional currency attacks. 

 Just a half an hour later, however, the dollar plunged to an intraday low of 2,630 rupiah on what traders said was a massive Bank Indonesiaintervention, involving the sale of around $200 million. Other traders believe that Bank Indonesia spent as much as $500 million. 

 The dollar gradually began to trend upward to the weak end of the rupiah band, which was again set by Bank Indonesia at 2,378 rupiah to 2,682 rupiah. The dollar closed Asian trading Thursday at 2,670 rupiah. 

 The dollar's quick rebound after the central bank's intervention supports the belief of many market participants that another run on the rupiah is imminent. 

 They note that Indonesia is now the only member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nation's "Big Four" - which includes Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines - that hasn't moved to a freely-floating currency. This view holds that a further deprecation of the rupiah is necessary to keep Indonesia in line with its regional competitors. 

 But many economists differ, asserting that Indonesia's economy is actually much sounder on a fundamental basis than these three neighbors. This strength is particularly evident in recent trends in the balance of trade and inflation. For example,  Indonesia last week registered its strongest performance in trade and inflation for the year. Indonesia's May trade surplus totaled $970 million, and non-oil exports - long a source of concern for economists - grew 13% to a record $3.61 billion. 

 At the present rate, Indonesia's current-account deficit is seen improving upon the 4% of gross domestic product projected earlier in the year. Annual inflation is poised to improve upon the 6.5% registered last year. 

 Indonesia's fiscal and monetary management has also been widely lauded. Economist note that Bank Indonesia is the only central bank in the Asean four preemptively to widen it currency trading band in anticipation of recent turmoil. 

 In light of these strong fundamentals, many economists believe a defense of the rupiah may be justified. They note that if Bank Indonesia is forced to float its currency, the market may distort the rupiah's true value, sending inflation and debt-servicing costs higher. 

 "In the current environment you could see the market undercut the rupiah's true value by 12% to 15%," said William Belchere, the Singapore head of fixed-income research at Merrill Lynch. "In this case, would I say an attempt to defend the currency is worthwhile? Yes."

 The dollar was trading at 2,665 rupiah in the spot market at 1010 GMT (6:10 a.m. EDT), compared with Tuesday's close at 2,648 rupiah. 

 Dealers said that the rupiah broke through the upper band of the trading band at 2,682 rupiah as the market buzzed with speculation about the closed-door meeting between the Finance Minister, the Bank Indonesia Governor and chief editors of local media. 

 The meeting turned out to be just a briefing on the current situation in the domestic and regional currency markets, and was not a policy statement. 

 But, Bank Indonesia still had to intervene in the spot market to show its commitment to defend the rupiah, dealers said. That intervention drove the dollar down to an intraday low of 2,630 rupiah. 

 Officials with Bank Indonesia were not available late Wednesday for confirmation, but market participants believed that the nation's central bank might have spent between $100 million and $500 million in the intervention. 

 Earlier in the day, Bank Indonesia raised the rates of the Sertifikat Bank Indonesia (SBI) across the board by 100 basis points in a move to defend the rupiah. 

 After the dollar broke the upper band, market speculation was rife that the band could be widened. Bank Indonesia, however, left the band unchanged at 2,378 rupiah-2,682 rupiah.

title: INDONESIAN RUPIAH TUMBLES ON CONTAGION EFFECT.
text:
JAKARTA, Aug 19 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah tumbled to 2,646/49 against the dollar at 0145 GMT on Tuesday from an opening of 2,610/20 on falls in the Malaysian ringgit and the Singapore dollar, dealers said. 

 They said falls in the ringgit and the Singapore dollar spilled over to the rupiah at the opening, driving the rupiah down to a low of 2,655 before it recovered on local dollar selling. 

 "It's the contagion effect again. The market is a bit nervous, with spreads trending to widen again. But volume was moderate," one foreign bank dealer said. 

 He said stop-loss limits were triggered after the rupiah fell through the 2,620 level. 

 The dealer said operators remained nervous and cautious, waiting for further developments on the ringgit and the Singapore dollar. 

 The Singapore dollar dipped briefly to 1.50 to the U.S. dollar after an official of the country's de-facto central bank said the currency's exchange rate was at an appropriate level. 

 An official of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said the Singapore dollar's level was appropriate to what was happening in the market. 

 The official said the U.S. dollar had been rising in currency markets recently and the Singapore dollar had depreciated by about five percent against the U.S. unit since the start of 1997. 

Indonesia's central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,588/2,636 on Monday from 2,573/2,621 on Friday.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Higher Vs Dlr; Offshore Buying Interests
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's rupiah continues to strengthen Thursday against the U.S. dollar on strong offshore buying interest, dealers said. 

 Dealers note as well that domestic buying of dollars - needed in recent weeks to cover offshore dollar debt - has diminished, also supporting the rupiah. 

 The U.S. unit is being bought at 2,587 rupiah in the spot market at 0517 GMT (1:17 a.m. EDT) Thursday, slightly lower from Wednesday's close of 2,588 rupiah. The dollar fell to a low of 2,581 rupiah at 0122 GMT (9:22 p.m. EDT) Thursday before rebounding. 

 'The market realizes the demand for buying dollars is subsiding,' said Pardi Kandy, a foreign exchange dealer at PT Mitsubishi Bank Buana in Jakarta. 'Offshore funds are now coming back into the market to take advantage of the attractive fixed-income yields in Indonesia.' 

 Bank Indonesia continues to keep an extremely tight money policy, with Surat Bank Indonesia money market intervention contracts still yielding an attractive 14% to investors. The central bank also continues to restrict issuances of its Surat Berharga Pasar Uang contracts. 

 But traders say money market rates are starting to trend down in anticipation of Bank Indonesia eventually loosening its stance. Overnight rupiah deposits have come down to 15% from 20% Wednesday, as have overnight swap rates. 'The market is keeping one step ahead of the central bank,' Pardi said. 

 Because of this renewed interest in the rupiah, traders see the dollar trading Thursday in a range between 2,570 rupiah and 2,590 rupiah.

title: INDONESIAN RUPIAH STRENGTHENS, LIQUIDITY EASES.
text:
JAKARTA, Aug 7 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah strengthened against the dollar amid improved money market liquidity in early trading on Thursday, dealers said. 

 They said confidence seemed to have returned and sentiment on the rupiah turned upbeat after a central bank meeting with foreign bank representatives on Wednesday did not discuss foreign exchange controls. 

 "This seems to have given a boost to market sentiment," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding further uptrend in the rupiah was likely later in the day. 

 The bank confirmed talks between its governor and foreign bank representatives late on Wednesday, but the talks were not about controls of swap transactions. 

 It said they were exchanging views about the foreign exchange market. Currency dealers said the market was rife with rumours that the central bank was planning to introduce similar steps as taken by the Malaysian central bank to limit swap transactions which were not trade related. 

 One Japanese bank dealer said the confirmation gave the market confidence that the central bank had no plan to introduce radical steps and would be content with existing instruments. 

 Bank Indonesia had widened its intervention band as signs of possible speculative attacks brewed. The early anticipation helped safe the country's valuable reserves. 

 The bank later tightened rupiah liquidity and raised short-term interest rates to contain speculative dollar buying. 

 Treasurers said the high short-term interest rate policy would be temporary and perhaps eased as foreign exchange markets stabilised. 

 Spot rupiah rose to 2,581.5/83.0 at 0210 GMT from an opening of 2,586.0/91.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,580.5/82.0 and 2,580.0/81.5, respectively. 

 The U.S. bank dealer said he expected the rupiah to range between 2,575 and 2,590 for the rest of the day. 

 "We see foreign players continuing to unload dollars while domestic purchases have declined," he said, adding that some big local banks were also unloading dollars despite improved money market liquidity. 

 Overnight money ranged between 15.0 and 17.0 percent, compared with 25-30 percent on Wednesday morning. 

 "If domestic dollar purchases ease and the region's markets continue to stabilise, the market will be trying to break the 2,570 barrier very soon and the central bank will loosen its short-term interest rate policy," another dealer said. 

 Dealers said swaps were lower, with and tending to ease after the central bank meeting on Wednesday suggested there were no plans to copy Malaysian or Thai measures of swap controls. 

 Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 1.2/1.3. 

 One-month swap was at 18.0/22.0, two at 37.0/42.0, three at 55.0/62.0 and six at 118.0/125.0 points. 

 The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,572/2,620 on Wednesday from 2,576/2,624 on Tuesday.

title: Indonesia Mins See Exports Boost From Rupiah Fall -Newspaper
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--The Indonesian government hopes a recent drop in the value of the rupiah, Indonesia's currency, can boost its non-oil exports, especially natural resources-based products. 

 Tuesday's Jakarta Post quoted two ministers as saying non-oil exports will reach a target of $55 billion this year because of the weakened rupiah. 

 'Depreciation (of the rupiah against the dollar) has a positive impact on our exports,' said Hartarto Sastrosoenarto, coordinating minister for production and distribution. 

 Meanwhile, Minister of Industry Tunky Ariwibowo said the weaker rupiah would particularly help exports of agricultural and forestry products and minerals. 

 However, it also would affect exports of products with a high import content, especially manufactured products like machinery components and steel products. 

 Tunky said non-oil exports grew by only 9% in the first five months of this year, 1 percentage point lower than the growth in the same period last year. 

 'With this depreciation, we are optimistic about achieving our non-oil exports target of $55 billion for this year,' said Tunky. 

 Soedradjad Djiwandono, governor of Bank Indonesia, the country's central bank, has warned that speculation in the rupiah would continue for some time until tranquility returns to the region's financial markets. 

 He expressed hope that the assaults on the region's currencies will die down when the Thai baht stabilizes. 

 Bank Indonesia had to spend about $1 billion last month intervening in currency markets to support the value of the rupiah, as it bottomed at 2,662.50 rupiah to the dollar.

title: Indonesia forex intervention  at $1.0 bln - report.
text:
JAKARTA, July 30 (Reuter) - Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank sold one billion dollars in the forward market last week to stabilise the rupiah during a recent speculative attack. 

 Djiwandono was quoted by the Jakarta Post daily as saying the amount was less than the Thai and Philippines central banks sold to defend their currencies because the bank had taken pre-emptive action by widening the dollar-rupiah band. 

 Bank Indonesia widened its intervention band to 12 percent from eight percent on July 11. The band allows the central bank to intervene in the market if rates fall out of the band. 

 Djiwandono said the dollars were sold in the forward market and not in the spot market in order to protect the country's foreign exchange reserves. These were estimated at $21.08 billion at the end of June.

title: Bk Indonesia: Dlr Range Of 2,555-2,610 Rupiah OK - Paper
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia central bank Deputy Governor Paul Soetopo said that a U.S. dollar trading range of between 2,555 rupiah and 2,610 rupiah against the Indonesian rupiah is reasonable in light of the continued instability in Southeast Asian currencies, Indonesia daily Bisnis Indonesia reported Wednesday. 

 The paper quoted Soetopo as saying that the rupiah's exchange rate is basically determined by economic fundamentals, but that it is also being determined by technical factors that affect supply and demand. 

 Soetopo added, however, said that under the current situation, it is almost impossible to determine the rupiah's equilibrium based solely on economic fundamentals. 

 'The equilibrium level of between 2,555 rupiah and 2,610 rupiah is reasonable for the short-term,' Soetopo said. He added that Bank Indonesia will tolerate this level as long as the rupiah remains within Bank Indonesia's intervention band. 

 Earlier Thursday the intervention band remained set at 2,378 rupiah to 2,682 rupiah. At 0323 GMT (10:35 p.m EST) the U.S. dollar is trading at 2,537.50 rupiah, down from an opening of 2,578 rupiah. 

 He said that Bank Indonesia will not set a fixed figure for the market equilibrium, as it could only fuel more speculative attacks against the rupiah, the report said.

title: Indonesian Money Market Rates Up Early On Fear Of Bank Runs
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian money market rates were mostly higher in cautious dealings early Tuesday as banks limited their lending in the interbank market on fears that the delay of bank recapitalization may spark a run on banks, dealers said. 

 Dealers added that some large depositors Monday transferred their deposits from local banks to foreign banks. As a result, foreign banks are enjoying good liquidity, while some medium-and small-sized local banks are facing liquidity shortage. 

 On Friday the government delayed the announcement for two weeks of a bank recapitalization program, which included planned closures of banks ineligible for recapitalization. A reason given, among others, was to give banks a chance to improve their business plans. 

 "Depositors are afraid that their banks can't afford the current negative spread (between lending and deposit rates) any longer and may face closure," said a dealer with a joint venture bank. 

 At 0220 GMT, the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was between 32% and 33% for foreign and secured joint venture banks, unchanged from Monday. Secure local banks are bidding for the overnight rupiah at between 34% and 35%, up from between 33% and 34% Monday. Less secure local banks are paying overnight rates between 50% and 55%, up from between 48% and 50%. 

 In the foreign exchange markets at the same time, the dollar was trading at 8,870 rupiah (IDR), little changed from IDR8,875 late Monday in Asia. 

 Earlier, Bank Indonesia injected IDR2.820 trillion rupiah into the money market. The injection represents the reversal of a Bank Indonesia's recent intervention in the money market. 


In its daily intervention, the central bank kept the overnight rate at
30%; two, three and six day rates at 33%; and one week rate at 34%.

title: Indonesian Money Market Rates Fall On Increased Liquidity
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian money market rates were mostly lower early Thursday as liquidity increased after the central bank released a net 1.90 trillion rupiah (IDR) into the market earlier in the day. 

 At 0310 GMT, the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was between 31% and 34%, down slightly from between 32% and 35% Wednesday. 

 Bank Indonesia's liquidity injection came from the expiration of Sertifikat Bank Indonesia notes it had absorbed in previous money market interventions totaling IDR13.401 trillion. Meanwhile, the settlement of the central bank notes auctioned Wednesday absorbed IDR11.5 trillion back out of the system. 

 Apart from Bank Indonesia's liquidity injection, foreign banks as well as some joint-venture and local banks received deposits being transferred from ailing banks seen targeted for closure Saturday. 

 "We have been witnessing increased transfer of funds from smaller banks since early this week," a dealer with a joint-venture bank said. 

 In order to absorb excess liquidity, Bank Indonesia is conducting money market operations. It keeps the overnight rate at 30%; four-, five-, and six-day rates at 33% and one-week rate at 34%. 

 In the foreign exchange market early Wednesday, the dollar was trading at IDR8,800, down a touch from IDR8,820 late Wednesday in Asia.

title: Indonesian Money Market Rates Flat; Banks Reduce Lending
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian money market rates are mostly steady early Monday as liquidity stays easy although banks reduced their lending to other banks ahead of the bank closure Saturday. 

 Dealers said banks, which are expected to be shut down, are facing difficulties in finding rupiah from other banks and therefore they are bidding for liquidity at much higher rates than safe banks. 

 Bank Indonesia's Governor Sjahril Sabirin told Dow Jones Newswires late Friday that he expected less than 40 banks will be shut down. 

 At 0151 GMT (8:51 p.m. EST Sunday), the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was between 32% and 34% for foreign, joint venture and safe local banks, unchanged from Friday. Whereas, those banks seen targeted for closure are bidding for the overnight rupiah rate at between 50% and 60%, dealers said. 

 "I think until the end of the month banks will remain cautious in lending their rupiah to other banks," said a dealer with a local bank. "I expect interest rates to climb to the run up of the bank closure announcement." 

 Earlier, Bank Indonesia injected 3.018 trillion rupiah (IDR) into the money market. The injection represents the reversal of Bank Indonesia's daily intervention in the money market. 

 The central bank, Monday, kept the overnight rate at 30%, two, three, and four day rates at 33%, and one-week rate at 34%.

title: Indonesia's Rupiah Ends Flat On Profit-Taking On Dollar
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Indonesian rupiah closed flat against the dollar in range-bound dealings Thursday as profit-taking against the U.S. unit saved the local currency from its earlier losses. 

 After trading between 8,750 rupiah (IDR) and IDR8,990, the dollar closed at IDR8,775 in the spot market, unchanged from its close Wednesday. 

 "Offshore participants sold back their dollars after Bank Indonesia checked the exchange rate," said a dealer with a local bank. "Bank Indonesia, however, didn't intervene." 

 Bank Indonesia's move protected the rupiah against the spill-over of the yen's slide against the dollar Thursday. 

 At 1026 GMT (5:26 a.m. EST), the dollar was trading at Y119.73, compared with Y118.90 in New York late Wednesday. 

 Market participants see the dollar trading between IDR8,600 and IDR9,000 Friday. The weekend mood is expected to leave trading thin and quiet. 

 The currency market has so far ignored the government's plan to close around 40 banks on Feb. 27. 

 The government, however, drove money market rates up as banks prefer to place their money at the central bank rather than lend to other banks, on fears that the borrowers could be shut down. Small banks bid the overnight rupiah at 60%, but they didn't succeed in attracting funds, dealers said.

title: Indonesian rupiah clambers upwards, progress slow.
text:
JAKARTA, Feb 2 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah struggled higher against the dollar on Tuesday but trade was particularly thin and uncertainty about the future still hung over the currency, dealers said. 

 They said a weaker dollar yen and improving confidence in the domestic political situation had helped lift the rupiah. 

 The currency was likely to stay between 8,600 and 9,000 to the dollar over the week, possibly edging towards the firmer end of the range if students continued to hold off on fresh mass protests against the government, dealers said. 

 By 1000 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 8,800/8,900 to the dollar, unchanged from its morning levels and firmer than the 8,875/8,925 quoted late on Monday in Jakarta. 

 "The market is quiet, but quiet is good for the rupiah," said one dealer at a U.S. bank in Jakarta. "There is still a lot of uncertainty, but for the moment Jakarta is quiet and that will help the rupiah." 

 Indonesia's central bank governor said interest rates were likely to remain steady despite the strengthening in the rupiah in recent days. 

 Asked if the interest rate level would be cut now that the rupiah had strengthened through 9,000 to the dollar, Syahril Sabirin said: "I think we will maintain it. For the time being this is reasonable." 

 The central bank holds its next auction of one-month paper on Wednesday. Last week, the auction yielded a weighted average interest rate of 36.53 percent, up from 35.89 percent the previous week. 

 Year-on-year inflation fell to 70.66 percent in January from 77.63 percent in December, data from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) showed. 

 The BPS said January month-on-month inflation was 2.97 percent, the highest since September, when prices rose 3.75 percent. 

 It said Indonesia's trade surplus rose to $1.61 billion in November from $1.38 billion the previous months. November exports were $3.90 billion, up from $3.77 billion the month before, while imports fell to $2.29 billion from $2.4 billion. 

 Dealers said the impact of concerns over the financial stability of Brazil and China, which knocked the rupiah in recent weeks, had also largely faded. 

 An agreement reached last week on new political laws to pave the way for parliamentary elections on June 7 has soothed the market, dealers say. Some had feared failure to agree would mean the elections would be postponed, sparking fresh violence. 

 But the election campaign is widely expected to be violent, and this is keeping many foreign investors out of the country, dealers say. 

 On Tuesday, Home Affairs Minister Syarwan Hamid was quoted as saying political parties would be banned from taking to the streets and holding mass outdoor rallies during the election campaign, which has been set for May 18 to June 6. 

 "Political parties will not be allowed to mobilise the masses in open fields and party supporters will be barred from taking to the streets," the Jakarta Post newspaper quoted him as saying. 

 "These measures are meant to prevent clashes and violence like in the past." 

 Bank Indonesia said last week it would continue with "small intervention" to try to lift the rupiah to 8,000 to the dollar. Indonesia's 1999/2000 budget forecasts an average exchange rate of 7,500 to the dollar. ((Andrew Marshall, Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364; Fax +6221 344-8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: SE Asian  Currencies  -3: Rupiah Strength Capped

At the moment, there is no evidence of foreign capital inflows into Indonesia, with only the central bank and state banks the sellers of U.S. dollars."

title: ASIA  FOREX  - Regionals little changed, rupiah firms.
text:
0900 GMT - Asian regional currencies ended little changed 

 on Friday with the firmer dollar putting on the pressure, but 

 the rupiah managed to claw back some of its recent losses. 

     The dollar firmed amid optimism about the outlook for the 

 U.S. economy and pessimism about the prospects for European and 

 Japanese growth. 

     *** The rupiah was a rare bright spot in very thin trade 

 and managed to get back the right side of 9,000. 

     Calm on the streets of the capital Jakarta and the 

 expectation that Bank Indonesia will come in and try to give 

 the rupiah's upward momentum a boost kept the currency firm. 

Central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin said the rupiah's 

 weakness was temporary and "small" amounts of intervention to 

 support it were continuing. 

     Bank Indonesia said it did not intervene in the rupiah 

 market today. 

     The market was relieved by the parliament's approval of 

 sweeping political reforms on Thursday, clearing the way for 

 the June elections. 

     The new laws include a reduction in the number of 

 parliamentary seats reserved for the military to 38 from 75, an 

 end to restrictions allowing only three political parties and a 

 proportional representation system for voting. 

 Indonesia's top economics minister Ginandjar Kartasasmita 

 told Reuters Television on Thursday independence for the 

 disputed territory of East Timor could come as early as next 

 year if parliament approved it. 

     *** The Thai baht was steady but traders are still 

 targeting a drop to the wrong side of 37 per dollar. 

     The Bank of Thailand cut its bank rate to 7.0 percent from 

 12.5 percent effective February 1. 

     The bank rate is that at which the central bank charges on 

 its short-terms loans to private financial institutions. 

     It was the first change in the rate since July 2, 1997, 

 when the baht was devalued and the central bank raised the rate 

 to 12.5 percent from 10.5 percent. 

     Thailand's November currency account surplus was $1.12 

 billion with the trade surplus at $1.02 billion. 

     Reserves as at January 22 totalled $29.4 billion against 

 $29.6 on January 15 and $29.8 on January 8. 

     *** The Korean won was barely changed with state run 

 Export-Import Bank of Korea (Exim) soaking up dollar supplies 

 from exporters and foreign stock funds. 

     Exim Bank officials denied market talk that is was acting 

 on behalf of authorities. 

     "We bought dollars to meet our needs," an Exim official 

 said. "We didn't even buy very much dollars today". 

     He said the bank was preparing for dollars to convert 500 

 billion won raised through issuing bonds. Exim bank planned to 

 issue the won-denominated bonds soon to help finance domestic 

 exporters. 

     *** The Philippine peso was steady and ignored GDP data for 

 last year. 

     The country's 1998 gross domestic product was down 0.5 

 percent on the previous full year due to the combined effects 

 of the Asian currency crisis and the El Nino phenomenon. 

     The economy last registered negative full-year GDP growth 

 in 1991 after a series of natural disasters. 

     Quarterly data showed a hefty decline in the economy 

 through the course of last year: GDP contracted 1.9 percent 

 between the fourth quarters of 1997 and 1998.

title: Rupiah advances, mounts attack on 9,000/dollar.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 29 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah advanced in early trade on Friday and mounted an assault on 9,000 to the dollar, spurred by dollar selling in the forward market in Singapore and improved confidence in domestic political stability. 

 The currency traded as high as 9,000 to the dollar and was quoted at 8,900/9,000 at 0230 GMT, although dealers said no trades had been done at firmer levels than 9,000. 

 "Some people think 9,000 will hold but that doesn't look likely now," one dealer said. 

 "There has been relief that the capital has been quiet, we had all expected more trouble this week. So that has changed the outlook of some people in the market and people are selling one-year (dollars) outright in Singapore." 

 Dealers said they had seen no early signs of Bank Indonesia intervention. 

 But they said the bank - which did not attempt to stand in the way of the downward trend earlier in the week despite pledges by the governor to support the currency - was likely to step up the amount of dollars it was selling to boost the rupiah's bounce. 

 "The central bank know they can't stop the currency falling when that's the way the market is pushing it, but this is their chance to help jack it up," one dealer at a U.S. bank in Jakarta said. 

 Bank Indonesia Governor Syahril Sabirin said on Thursday the rupiah's recent weakening was temporary and intervention to support the currency was continuing. 

 "This is temporary," Sabirin told reporters when asked about this week's weakening of the rupiah. 

 "Small intervention is continuing." 

 Sabirin said earlier this week the central bank would try to lift the rupiah back to the 8,000 level. 

 The central bank has helped prop up the rupiah over recent months by converting $5-15 million a day of aid and loan dollars into rupiah, usually through state banks. 

 Indonesia's 1999/2000 budget assumes an average rupiah rate of 7,500 to the dollar. ((Andrew Marshall, Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364; Fax +6221 344-8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Bank  Indonesia  says "small"  intervention  continues.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin said on Thursday current weakness in the rupiah was temporary and intervention to support the currency was continuing. 

 "This is temporary," Sabirin told reporters when asked about the recent weakening of the rupiah. 

 "Small intervention is continuing." 

 Sabirin said the central bank would do its best to support the local currency. He gave no further details. 

 He said earlier this week the central bank would try to lift the rupiah to 8,000 against the dollar. Indonesia's 1999/2000 budget assumes an average exchange rate of 7,500 to the dollar. 

 The rupiah edged lower against the dollar on Thursday as the U.S. currency gained against the yen, with dealers watching parliament to see whether laws paving the way for elections set for June would be passed. 

 Indonesia's political parties, after weeks of wrangling, have agreed most of the main points of new laws which will form the basis of parliamentary elections scheduled for June 7, but a row over the role of civil servants in politics caused a delay in a vote on the laws on Thursday. 

 By 1010 GMT the rupiah was quoted at 9,175/9,250 compared with 9,120/9,220 late on Wednesday. ((Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364; Fax +6221 344-8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Bank  Indonesia /Rupiah -2: Futile To  Intervene  In  Forex  Mkt
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--It would be futile for Bank Indonesia to intervene in foreign exchange markets to support the rupiah against the dollar given that it's being hurt by external factors, central bank governor, Sjahril Sabirin, said Tuesday. 

 "It's not right if we fight the market, as (the rupiah is weaker) because of external factors," Sjahril told reporters, adding that concerns that China would devalue its currency, the yuan, had hit the rupiah. 

 Global currency markets were rattled on Monday by speculation that China would devalue the yuan following Brazil's decision last week to let the real float freely. 

 A series of Chinese pledges not to devalue - including a promise by Chinese premier, Zhu Rongji, Monday not to weaken the Chinese unit this year - have gone some way towards quashing market fears.

title: Indonesian Money Mkt Up; Bk Indonesia Borrowing Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Despite ample liquidity, Indonesian money-market rates were mostly higher early Tuesday, as the central bank is paying banks higher than its regular intervention rates if they place their rupiah with the central bank. 

 As well as its regular operation to borrow rupiah at predetermined rates, Bank Indonesia Monday afternoon borrowed rupiah at rates determined by the market. 

 Dealers said Bank Indonesia paid 32% interest on overnight money - higher than its intervention rate of 30%. 

 An official at Bank Indonesia confirmed that it paid 32% for overnight rupiah. Bank Indonesia will continue to do so Tuesday, in order to absorb excess liquidity from the market, he added. 

 "The amount of base money in circulation increased sharply during the (Muslim) Idul Fitri holiday last week," the official said. "We have to absorb the excess." 

 At 0206 GMT (9:06 p.m. Monday EST), tracking Bank Indonesia's rate, the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was between 31% and 32%, up from between 30% and 31% Monday. 

 Earlier Tuesday, Bank Indonesia injected 4.308 trillion rupiah (IDR) into the money market, as previous days' borrowings from the market matured. 

 In the foreign-exchange market at 0206 GMT, the dollar was trading at IDR9,163, down from IDR9,300 late Monday. 

 In the swap market, the overnight swap rate inched up to IDR5.50-IDR6.50, from IDR5-IDR6 Monday, tracking money-market rates.

title: Indonesian Rupiah Ends Lower On Offshore Selling Pressure
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Indonesian rupiah bucked the trend of some other currencies in the region Thursday, ending Asian trade lower against the dollar, largely the result of pressure from offshore participants to push the rupiah down. 

 "The market was quite volatile," said a trader with a foreign bank in Jakarta. "Some Singapore buyers tried to squeeze the market to push the rupiah lower." 

 The rupiah (IDR) was quoted at IDR8,675 to the U.S. dollar at the end of the day, down from IDR8,470 late Wednesday in Singapore. The Jakarta market was closed Wednesday for a national holiday. 

 "Most of the locals are still on holidays; this was the offshore players," the trader said. 

 Many Indonesians are on vacation this week following the two day muslim Idul Fitri holidays Tuesday and Wednesday. 

 Traders said offshore participants had sought to push the rupiah lower citing outbreaks of rioting and unrest in some parts of the country. 

 Religious violence spread in eastern Indonesia on Thursday when rioting among Christians and Muslims flared for a third straight day. At least 24 people were killed in bloody clashes on two islands and fighting erupted on a third, police said. 

 Dealers said Bank Indonesia hadn't been seen intervening in the market to support the rupiah. The central bank said last week that it would step into the market if necessary, but there has been no evidence of this. 

 Bank Indonesia's auction of one-month central bank notes Thursday resulted in an increase in interest rates, marking the second consecutive week of an increase in one-month rates after months of steady decline. 

 Dealers said allowing interest rates to rise was the more likely route Bank Indonesia would take in order to support the rupiah. 

 "We don't see any central bank intervention at the moment," said the trader at the foreign bank. "I guess one of the ways to slow down the weakening of the rupiah is to let rates rise."

title: Indonesian Money Market Rates Ease After Two-Day Holiday
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian money market rates are slightly lower Thursday on ample liquidity as the demand for funds eases after the two-day Muslim Idul Fitri holiday. 

 At 0221 GMT, the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was at 30%, lower than the average of 34% last week during which strong demand for rupiah-denominated funds for the holiday pushed up market rates. 

 Dealers said the market was flush with liquidity Thursday because banks last week did not aggressively bid for the central bank notes at the weekly auction. 

 Instead, they kept the rupiah funds handy in anticipation of the pre-holiday demand for cash. 

 Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia has set the daily intervention interest rates, part of the central bank's open market operation to absorb excess funds, at levels close to the market. 

 The intervention rate is 29% for overnight funds, 32% for four to six days and 33% for seven-day funds. 

 The central bank will hold its weekly auction of one-month central bank notes today (Thursday) with a target amount of IDR12.7 trillion. 

 The auction was postponed from Wednesday because of the Idul Fitri holiday. 

 In the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was fetching IDR8,600, up from IDR8,470 late Wednesday in Asia. 

 In the offshore swap market, the premium on the overnight forward contract was IDR5.5/6.6, reflecting an implied interest rate of about 29% to 30%, close to the market level while the one-month premium was at IDR230/270.

title: EMERGING MARKET  FX -Asia stands firm despite Brazil.
text:
LONDON, Jan 15 (Reuters) - Mounting concern that Brazil will be forced into a further real devaluation sent a shiver through many emerging market currencies on Friday although Asian markets were shielded by a sagging U.S. dollar, analysts said. 

 "I think we're beyond the stage where you going to get a full blown currency crisis in Asia just as a result of Brazil," said Tim Fox, currency strategist at Standard Chartered in London. 

 "The U.S. dollar has been affected more than anything and this in a sense protecting the Asian currencies," said Fox. 

 The Brazilian real remained near the top of its new trading band at just under 1.32 per dollar on Friday but the market was expecting further pressure when U.S. markets opened. 

 Media reports estimated between $1.5 billion and $1.8 billion left Brazil on Thursday. 

 Capital flight depletes the country's vital foreign currency reserves - used to defend the real and pay foreign currency debt - and makes a further devaluation or a move to a free-floating currency more likely, analysts said. 

 The U.S. dollar fell across the board in early European trade as traders speculated about the effects of another Brazilian real devaluation on U.S. economic and financial links with Latin America's largest economy. 

Currencies in Asia were generally insulated by the yen's firmer tone of around 112 against the dollar. 

 The Taiwanese dollar and the Korean won saw small gains although the Thai baht and the Philippine peso weakened slightly against the dollar. 

 A firmer yen has allowed the crisis-hit region to lower interest rates sharply over recent months. 

 "Asia's economies have undergone much of the reform that Brazil is now charged with although you can make an argument that interest rates there have some room to be back up in some cases," said one trader. 

 The big loser among Asia's currencies was the Indonesian rupiah which slid through the 9,000 per dollar level to around 9,200, equalling an early November low. 

 The governor of Indonesia's central bank has said the bank may intervene to keep the rupiah above the 8,000 per dollar mark. 

 But traders said no government intervention had been seen yet and the market was eyeing the possibility of fresh unrest after next week's Eid al-Fitr holidays. 

 Indonesia's 1999/2000 fiscal year budget forecasts an average rupiah rate of 7,500 per dollar. 

 The South African rand, seen as vulnerable to Brazilian jitters due to the country's weak curent account position, held at weaker early levels after recovering from a four-month low of 6.33 per dollar in New York trade. 

 Eastern European currencies were generally weaker with the polish zloty opening at 5.31/4.94 firmer than its trading band centre versus 6.45/6.25 in late Thursday trade. 

 The zloty can fluctuate in a band of 12.5 percent either side of its parity rate, set daily by the centrak bank based on a currency basket comprising 55 percent of the euro and 45 percent of the U.S. dollar. 

 The Czech crown opened weaker and was seen trading in a narrow range of between 35.8 to 36.2, local traders said.

title: ASIA MARKETS - Mixed and relaxed about Brazil.
text:
SINGAPORE, Jan 15 (Reuters) - It was a mixed day on Asian 

 markets on Friday in spite of the gloomy news from Brazil, with 

 stock markets also shrugging off a sharp overnight drop on Wall 

 Street. 

     The markets were trading thinly because of a holiday in 

 Japan but the firmer tone of the yen against the dollar helped 

 underpin the regional currencies. 

     Stocks were still the main focus but currency traders kept a 

 close eye on the equity side of things again to watch for 

 overseas investor cash pulling out of the region. 

     DOLLAR SOFT IN ASIA ON BRAZIL WORRIES 

     The dollar remained on a soft footing as traders began to 

 speculate that Brazil's financial woes might prompt the Federal 

 Reserve to ease U.S. interest rates to cushion the Dow. 

     "There's talk of a possible Fed easing because the U.S. 

 stock market will be hard hit if we see a further impact from 

 Brazil," said a Japanese bank dealer. 

     But some felt the Dow's recent losses might not be a source 

 of great concern to the Fed. 

     "I think they would like to take a little bit of heat out of 

 the Dow. It's been roaring ahead since the start of the year," 

 said Peter Whitley, foreign exchange manager at State Bank in 

 Sydney. 

 TAIWAN STOCKS GET A BOOST 

 Taiwan's market got a bit of an artificial boost when the 

 government's huge stabilisation fund weighed in towards the end 

 of the session targeting shares which form a large part of the 

 weighted index. These were mainly financial stocks. 

     But bargain hunters were also seen scooping up electronics 

 shares. 

     Taiwan's weighted index finishing up over 3.4 percent for 

 the day. 

     KOREA STOCKS STILL DOING WELL BUT HANG SENG WOBBLES 

     In Korea, the KOSPI also had a better session, rising more 

 than 1.5 percent as retail investors took advantage of the lower 

 prices after Thursday's post-Brazil sell-off. 

     In Hong Kong, the market was more worried by developments 

 overseas and shares started off very weak, although in later 

 trading prices recovered most of their losses. 

     SINGAPORE CONFUSION 

     In Southeast Asia, there was some early confusion in 

 Singapore when the Straits Times index plunged 5.5 percent at 

 the opening because of a wrongly keyed transaction. 

     A trader put in a wrong price for OCBC bank and one player 

 bought one lot at 30 cents. 

     It was this error which caused the initial five percent 

 plunge in the index. 

     OCBC was quoted at S$8.25 in late business. 

CURRENCIES QUIET AND MIXED 

     It appears Brazil might have done Asia a favour by showing 

 the region is in better shape than Latin America at the moment 

 -- although there are people who think things might take a turn 

 forthe worse at any tie. The strength of the yen pretty much 

 underpinned all the regional foreign exchange markets, with the 

 notable exception of the rupiah. 

     RUPIAH SLIPS GRADUALLY LOWER 

     The rupiah slid past the 9,000 level per dollar at one point 

 on worries about trouble on the streets after a forthcoming 

 public holiday. 

     Although the central bank has vowed to step in and defend 

 the rupiah, there has been no sign of intervention yet. 

     Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin has said the central 

 bank would seek to keep the rupiah firmer than 8,000 to the 

 dollar. Indonesia's budget for the next fiscal year is based on 

 an average rupiah rate of 7,500. 

 But the fear is that when Ramadan ends and the festivities 

 associated with it are over trouble will return to the streets 

 of Jakarta. 

 Students have already pledged to resume mass anti-government 

 protests after the Eid al-Fitr Moslem festival on Tuesday and 

 Wednesday next week. 

 SINGAPORE DOLLAR REGAINS SOME LOST GROUND 

 The Singapore dollar managed a small rise as dealers 

 reported an unwinding of the long baht/short Sing positions put 

 on in recent weeks. 

 The low level of interest rates in Singapore has prompted 

 investors to borrow Singapore dollars and convert them to other 

currencies and much of this cheap funding went on in Sing/baht. 

 THAI BAHT EASES 

 The Thai baht was easier and back through 37 to the dollar 

 despite news that commercial bank lending is expected to grow 

 seven percent this year after contracting five percent last 

 year.

title: ASIA  FOREX  - Regionals weak but off lows.
text:
0850 GMT - Asian regional currencies were mostly easier in 

 late trade despite the yen's firmer tone against the dollar. 

     But trade was thin, with Japan closed for a holiday and 

 widespread uncertainty over the impact of Brazil's devaluation. 

     Traders are increasingly nervous that Brazil might be 

 forced to float its currency following a Standard & Poor's 

 ratings downgrade and as net dollar outflows reached an 

 estimated $1.14 billion on Thursday. 

 But for the time being, Asian stock markets kept their 

 composure despite Wall Street's 2.45 percent drop and that 

 helped limit losses in regional currencies. 

 *** The dollar was easier as traders began to speculate on 

 the possibility of a U.S. interest rate cut if the Dow 

 continued to be pummelled by concerns about Brazil. 

     But dealers expected dollar bids to resurface near 112 yen 

 due to lingering fears of Bank of Japan intervention. 

     *** The rupiah remained weak after sliding through the 

 9,000 per dollar level as traders worried about the possibility 

 of fresh unrest after next week's Eid al-Fitr holidays. 

     It reached a low of 9,200, its lowest since November 5, and 

 traders expected further falls amid concerns of a delay in 

 June's planned general election if parliament fails to push 

 through political reform laws in time. 

     Although the central bank has vowed to step in and defend 

 the rupiah, intervention has yet to be seen. 

     Bank Indonesia Governor Syahril Sabirin has said the 

central bank would seek to intervene to keep the rupiah firmer 

 than 8,000 to the dollar. Indonesia's budget for the 1999/2000 

 fiscal year forecasts an average rupiah rate of 7,500. 

 *** The Korean won stood out with a small gain as local 

 companies unwound dollar positions in the face of a rising yen 

 and the local stock market's resilience to Wall Street's drop. 

 The central bank said the number of firms whose bank 

 accounts were closed after defaulting on their debt dropped to 

 862 in December from 903 in November and 3,197 a year earlier. 

 It attributed the decline to the improving financial health 

 of local firms due to falling interest rates and increased 

 lending to small and medium-sized companies. 

 *** The Singapore dollar was also higher, largely because 

 of an unwinding of the long baht/short Sing positions put on in 

 recent weeks. 

 The low level of interest rates in Singapore prompted 

 investors to borrow Singapore dollars and convert them to other 

currencies and much of this cheap funding went on in Sing/baht. 

     Singapore corporates have also been seen buying into 

 Thailand. 

     *** The baht was some 0.5 percent down from late Thursday 

 levels on that cross play with the Sing dollar. 

     The central bank said local commercial bank lending was 

 expected to grow by seven percent this year. Latest data show a 

 5.3 percent year-on-year contraction in bank lending for the 

 first 11 months of 1998. 

 Foreign reserves rose to $29.8 billion as at January 8 from 

 $29.5 billion on December 30. The Bank of Thailand said it had 

 net forward foreign exchange sales contracts of $6.2 billon to 

 buy Thai baht as at January 8, against $6.6 billion on December 

 30.

title: Rupiah ends weaker but bounces back from 9,000/dlr.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 15 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah mounted a late fightback on Friday from a low of 9,250 against the dollar but still ended weaker with dealers predicting fresh attacks on the beleaguered currency after a market holiday next week. 

 The Indonesian currency was quoted at 8,800/8,900 in late Jakarta trade compared with 8,675/8,725 late on Thursday. It began the week at around 8,000. 

 Bank Indonesia will not be running clearing and foreign exchange operations on Monday and is closed on Tuesday and Wednesday, but dealers said more pressure on the rupiah was likely when the market re-opened. 

 "We all know that the problems in Brazil so far are the tip of the iceberg. But in Indonesia we also have so much uncertainty, there is the chance of messy elections, and this is contributing to very negative sentiment," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Jakarta. 

 "We have seen some panic dollar buying and this could get worse." 

 The currency fell to a three-month low of 9,250 before clawing back some ground, though dealers said there had been no sign of significant central bank intervention propping up the currency. 

 "The state banks came in around lunchtime, but they did not release a significant amount of dollars. The recovery we have seen was really more a technical retracement, but we expect further weakness next week," the dealer said. 

 Dealers said this week's weakness had been sparked by financial instability in Brazil, but magnified by growing concerns about Indonesia's political stability as crime and unrest spiral and a general election looms. 

 Talk that parliamentary deadlock over new election laws could cause a delay in the election added to the rupiah's weakness. The head of the government-appointed team in charge of the election laws later said there was no chance elections would be delayed. 

 Dealers said that if 9,200 was breached again, the next resistance would be at 9,700 and then the psychological 10,000 level. 

 "If 10,000 goes, then you've got 15,000," one dealer said. "There would be panic buying of dollars, much more than we've seen already." 

 Dealers say concerns that violence and instability will increase in the run-up to elections will cast a shadow over the rupiah in the months ahead. 

 Students, behind much of the anti-government protests which helped topple former President Suharto in May and which caused mayhem in the capital late last year, have already pledged to hit the streets again from next week. 

 There are also concerns that a row between parliament and the government over the country's 1999/2000 budget could scupper desperately needed economic reforms. 

 Indonesia's central bank has been helping support the rupiah for months by converting millions of dollars in foreign loans and aid to rupiah. It has been converting $5-15 million a day. 

 Bank Indonesia Governor Syahril Sabirin said on Tuesday the central bank would seek to intervene to keep the rupiah firmer than 8,000 to the dollar. Indonesia's budget for the 1999/2000 fiscal year forecasts an average rupiah rate of 7,500. 

 But there was little sign of central bank intervention on Friday. 

 Dealers said Bank Indonesia may be waiting until the initial storm subsides before stepping in to try and nudge the rupiah higher. They also pointed out that the inflow of funds the central bank has been converting may be running dry. title: Indonesia Rupiah Lower Late On Brazil And Domestic Politics
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesia's rupiah (IDR) was trading lower against the U.S. dollar in subdued dealings late Thursday. The rupiah was the hardest hit of regional currencies by the domino effect of Brazil's effective currency devaluation Wednesday. 

 Brazil's central bank chief, Gustavo Franco, resigned Wednesday and his successor, Francisco Lopes, announced a widening of the trading band for the country's currency, the real. The currency immediately plunged 8.2% to BRR1.32 to the dollar, the floor of the new expanded trading band. 

 The combination of this and the country's high social and political risk dragged the rupiah down, revisiting levels seen two months ago. 

 After falling to a low of IDR8,800 to the dollar, the rupiah was trading at IDR8,675 to the dollar in the spot market at 0955 GMT (4:55 a.m. EST), down from its close Wednesday at IDR8,550 to the dollar. 

 "Singapore-based speculators are still bidding for the dollar in late trading, anticipating a follow through of selloffs on the rupiah during the London and New York trading hours," said a dealer with a joint venture bank in Jakarta. 

 Dealers said they didn't hear of Bank Indonesia intervening in the market Thursday, despite the central bank's warning to the market that it will safeguard the rupiah. 

 The dollar's rise in the spot market, however, was slowed by declines in onshore swap rates, dealers said. 

 One month swap rates declined to IDR250/IDR300 late Thursday, from IDR300/IDR400 late Wednesday. 


The rupiah's direction Friday will hinge on developments in Brazil,
dealers said. They see the dollar trading between IDR8,500 and IDR9,000
Friday. Offshore participants are expected to keep long dollar positions
during the weekend on growing nervousness about a possible outbreak of
social unrest in the country, after a relatively quiet period during the
Muslim Ramadhan holiday.

text:

 "We will continue the intervention to keep the rupiah under (firmer than) 8,000," central bank governor Syahril Sabirin told reporters ahead of a parliamentary hearing.

title: FOCUS-Rupiah slides on mounting political fears.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 13 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah dropped more than five percent against the dollar on Wednesday on regional weakness, fears of fresh domestic unrest and wrangling over the new budget. 

 The rupiah's sudden fall sent tremors through the stock market, where a firmer currency is crucial for scores of debt-ridden firms. The bourse fell 3.92 percent to 419.10 points. 

 By the end of Jakarta trading the rupiah was quoted at 8,550/8,650 to the dollar, after trading as low as 8,650, its lowest in more than two months. 

 Dealers said the rupiah's problems were set to continue. 

 "Support at 8,600 has been taken, I don't see anything standing in the way of 9,000 now," said one trader at a European bank in Jakarta. 

 The rupiah had a brief respite after central bank governor Sjahril Sabirin pledged to step in to help the currency recapture the 8,000 level. But there was no sign of intervention, and the decline soon picked up steam again. 

 Dealers said the rupiah's slide had been sparked by a general weakening in regional currencies against the dollar as investors cut back on their positions amid concerns about a deepening financial crisis in Brazil. 

 "The initial cause was probably Brazil," one said. "Later, when Bank Indonesia said it would intervene the rupiah firmed to 8,300, but because there was no action from Bank Indonesia the market recovered its positions." 

 Dealers and analysts said numerous other worries had contributed to the rupiah's decline. 

 "There have been things building up for a few weeks, and maybe today, given the relatively strong dollar, was the day to take advantage of that," said Clifford Tan, forex strategist at Warburg Dillon Read in Singapore. 

 "The primary concern is about what happens after Ramadan is over. What will happen to the pace and the fervour of political protest across Indonesia? That's issue number one." 

 Indonesian students have vowed to resume mass anti-government rallies after the Eid al-Fitr festival on Tuesday and Wednesday which marks the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan. 

 A series of bloody clashes between security forces and students came to a halt last month when students stopped their protests for the Moslem fasting month. 

 Analysts said a battle between the government and parliament over Indonesia's 1999/2000 budget had also rattled markets. 

 Parliament said this week the government should cut the amount of money it is spending on the crucial bank recapitalisation scheme and revise some budget estimates. 

 "The parliamentary infighting over the budget - that's new for Indonesia, given that it was a rubber-stamp body in the past," Tan said. "In other countries like Mexico the political cost of paying for these large recapitalisations has often become quite a large issue." 

 Dealers said concerns that the beleaguered armed forces could disintegrate was also weighing on the currency. 

 Bank Indonesia has been converting $5-15 million a day of aid and loan money into rupiah in recent months, giving a significant boost to the currency. 

 Analysts said the thin market meant Bank Indonesia intervention could be relatively effective, but warned the funds to be converted into rupiah could soon start drying up. 

 "They have to (defend the rupiah), but we think that the trend is going to be more for a depreciation," said Mangal Goswami, economist at ABN AMRO in Singapore. 

 "Official aid money is going to taper off, the current account is going to fall.... These are all factors that are going to go against the rupiah."

title: Rupiah tumbles more than five pct against dollar.
text:

 He said activity in the swaps market suggested there was more rupiah weakness to come: "It may continue because if you look at the swaps it looks like overseas players are building up long positions. So they might be attacking the rupiah again." 

 Dealers and analysts said numerous other worries had also contributed to the rupiah's decline. 

 "There have been things building up for a few weeks, and maybe today, given the relatively strong dollar, was the day to take advantage of that," said Clifford Tan, forex strategist at Warburg Dillon Read in Singapore. 

 "The primary concern is about what happens after Ramadan is over. What will happen to the pace and the fervour of political protest across Indonesia? That's issue number one." 

 Indonesian students have vowed to resume mass anti-government rallies after the Eid al-Fitr festival on Tuesday and Wednesday which marks the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan. 

 A series of bloody clashes between security forces and students came to a halt last month when students stopped their protests for the Moslem fasting month. 

 Analysts said a political battle between the government and parliament over Indonesia's 1999/2000 budget had also rattled markets. Parliament said this week the government should cut the amount of money it is spending on the crucial bank recapitalisation scheme and revise some budget estimates. 

 "The parliamentary infighting over the budget - that's new for Indonesia, given that it was a rubber-stamp body in the past," Tan said. 

 "In other countries like Mexico the political cost of paying for these large recapitalisations has often become quite a large issue." 

 Bank Indonesia Governor Syahril Sabirin said the central bank would step in to try to keep the rupiah firmer than 8,000 to the dollar. 

 The central bank has been converting $5 million to $15 million a day in aid and loan dollars to rupiah in recent months, providing a significant boost for the currency in thin market conditions. 

 Analysts said the thin market meant Bank Indonesia intervention could be relatively effective, but warned the funds to be converted into rupiah could soon start drying up. 

 "They have to (defend the rupiah), but we think that the trend is going to be more for a depreciation," said Mangal Goswami, economist at ABN AMRO in Singapore. 

 "Official aid money is going to taper off, the current account is going to fall.... These are all factors that are going to go against the rupiah." 

 He said ABN AMRO forecast the rupiah dropping to 9,000 in March and 10,000 in June, before returning to 9,000 in September. 

 Indonesia's budget for the fiscal year to end-March 2000 assumes an average exchange rate of 7,500 to the dollar. 

 "The real level is 8,000 to 10,000," one senior foreign bank dealer said. "Below 8,000 is unrealistic due to the political outlook."

title: ASIA  FOREX  - Regionals weak in early trade.
text:
0010 GMT - Asian currencies were showing an easier bias in 

 early deals as the dollar firmed slightly against the yen, 

 though the market remained nervous about driving it down 

 sharply following the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) interventions on 

 Tuesday. 

     U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin repeated his 

 preference for a strong dollar overnight, saying it had 

 underpinned the still solid U.S. economy. 

     He dismissed suggestions that the administration had been 

 willing to let the dollar slip against the yen to help 

 embattled U.S. manufacturing and steel industries out of a 

 bind. 

     His remarks helped lift the dollar, but analysts said the 

 dollar could face further downside in the face of continuing 

 concerns about Brazil and Japanese repatriations ahead of the 

 fiscal year end in March. 

     *** The Thai baht was among the worst hit by the yen's 

 fall, with worries the central bank might buy dollars to settle 

 its forward obligations contributing to its soft tone. 

     Signs of further interest rate cuts at Thai banks also 

 weighed on the baht, with Krung Thai Bank announcing a 50 basis 

 point lending rate cut, effective today. 

     This brings its minimum lending rate to 11.25 percent and 

 its minimum retail and overdraft rates to 11.75 percent. 

     Bank of Asia cut its its minimum lending rate to 13.25 

 percent from 13.75 percent on Monday. 

     Thailand's main opposition New Aspiration Party is due to 

 submit censure motions in parliament against Finance Minister 

 Tarrin Nimmanahaeminda and two other top ministers. 

     Tarrin will be questioned in a parliamentary debate at the 

 end of the month for alleged lack of transparency in managing 

 the sales of assets belonging to closed finance companies. 

     Analysts see little actual political risk in Thailand, but 

 the launch of the censure motions is likely to keep markets a 

 bit edgy. 

     The state-run Financial Restructuring Authority signed 

 contracts to sell some 156 billion baht of financial and 

 commercial assets left by 56 defunct finance firms with seven 

 groups of bidders. 

 *** The Korean won also took a bit of a knock from the 

 yen's fall, fears of further intervention by the Bank of Korea 

 and profit-taking in the stock market. 

     Seoul stocks started firm, but quickly headed south as 

 investors took profit on recent gains. 

     Commerce Minister Park Tae-young said Korea's economy was 

 expected to return to robust growth of five percent in 2000 as 

 economic restructuring takes effect. 

     Park said 1998 GDP showed an estimated 6.1 percent 

 contraction from the previous year, but was expected to return 

 to growth of 2.1 percent this year. 

     The government has officially projected 1999 full-year 

 growth at 2.0 percent, but an internal central bank report has 

 estimated growth will be as high as 3.2 percent. 

     Park also said the trade surplus would begin shrinking from 

 1999 due to a rise in imports as the economy picks up. This 

 year's trade surplus is projected to reach $25 billion from a 

 provisional $39.9 billion in 1998. 

 *** The rupiah fell further as dollar demand picked up 

 ahead of next week's Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivities, but 

 dealers said thin volumes and fears of central bank

intervention would limit its decline. 

 Bank Indonesia said on Tuesday it would temporarily allow 

 banks to extend credits to non-affiliated parties up to a 

 maximum of 30 percent of their capital from 20 percent 

 previously. 

 The central bank said it was easing the restriction to help 

 banks cope with the economic crisis, and the new ruling applies 

 to credits extended between end-December 1998 and the end of 

 2001.

title: Rupiah falls through 8,000, support seen at 8,100.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 11 (Reuters) - The Indonesian rupiah weakened through 8,000 to the dollar on Tuesday but dealers said it was unlikely to fall below 8,100 due to expectations the central bank would step in at that level to defend the currency. 

 The rupiah was quoted at 8,025/8,055 in late Jakarta trade compared with 7,940/8,040 late on Monday. 

 "We saw demand from local and especially state banks today, buying dollars again, and that pushed the rate over 8,000," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Jakarta. 

 "We still see 8,100 as being well held because of fears that the central bnak might step in." 

 Dealers said there had been higher demand for dollars in recent weeks to cover increased imports ahead of the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr on January 19/20, but this had already been largely satisfied. 

 They said the market was likely to remain quiet in the run up to the festival. 

 Bank Indonesia Governor Syahril Sabirin said on Monday the central bank was prepared to step in to defend the rupiah if necessary. 

 "We are trying our best to make it stable. If some intervention is necessary we will do so. We do not want to see the rate fluctuate in a wider band," he told Reuters Television in Hong Kong ahead of a meeting of central bankers. 

 "But in my view the current rate can be sustained," Sabirin said. "There is still room for the exchange rate to be stronger than the current level but the current level already is all right." 

 For months the central bank has been converting around $5-15 million a day in aid and loan dollars into rupiah. Analysts say this has been a significant factor in the currency's strength. 

 Indonesia's budget for the fiscal year to end-March 2000, released last week, assumes an average exchange rate of 7,500 to the dollar. 

 Because of thin market conditions and a lack of speculative traders, Bank Indonesia intervention can be extremely effective in supporting the rupiah, analysts say. ((Andrew Marshall, Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364; Fax +6221 344-8404, jakarta.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Indonesian Money Mkt Rates Down Slightly On Flush Liquidity
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--Indonesian money market rates were slightly lower in quiet dealings early Wednesday as the market remains flush with liquidity ahead of the weekly auction of the central bank's one-month note later in the day. 

 At 0146 GMT (8:46 p.m. Tuesday EST), the overnight interbank rate - considered the benchmark rate - was at 29.5%, down slightly from 30% a day earlier. 

 "Overnight rate fell slightly as there were a lot of offers for overnight maturity," said a dealer with a local bank. "Banks want to secure their rupiah back Thursday in case their bids for (Bank Indonesia notes) are accepted." 

 Bank Indonesia is inviting bids for its one-month Sertifikat Bank Indonesia to absorb 7 trillion rupiah (IDR). The settlement of the auction will be completed Thursday. 

 At last week's auction, SBI was yielding 35.52%, up from 35.28% a week earlier. 

 Earlier Wednesday, Bank Indonesia injected IDR4.740 trillion into the system. 

 To absorb excess liquidity as well as to prevent the rates from falling sharply, Bank Indonesia is intervening by borrowing the rupiah from the market for tenures between one and seven days. 

 It sets the overnight rate at 28%; for tenures between two and five days at 31%; and seven days at 32%. 

 In the foreign exchange markets Wednesday morning, the dollar was trading flat at IDR7,850. 

 In the swap market, the premium on the overnight swap was unchanged at IDR5.50-6.00.

title: Indonesian rupiah firmer vs dollar, helped by euro.
