title: Indonesian rupiah ends weaker on baht spillover.
text:
JAKARTA, July 23 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah ended weaker against the dollar on Wednesday after a volatile day. 

 The rupiah strengthened to a high of 2,530 from an opening of 2,570/80 but fell back to 2,582/87 at the close. 

 Dealers said the rupiah was on the way to recovery before fresh pressure on the baht spilled over to the rupiah and other regional currencies and pushed rates lower against the dollar. 

 The rupiah was trapped in range trading throughout the day, with minor intervention by the central bank seen helping provide direction to the market, but new jolts in Thailand eroded Bank Indonesia's initiative. 

 Dealers said central bank intervention was seen at the 2,580 level which helped boost the rupiah to 2,540 level in late morning, but the baht slump weakened the rupiah. 

 Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,585.25/95.25 and 2,570.50/80.50, respectively. 

 "Sentiment has turned bearish on the rupiah after opening with bullish sentiment, with attempts to break the 2,500 resistance level," one U.S. bank dealer said. 

 A slump in the Thai baht seemed to have pulled the region down into another round of jittery although it was less rough. 

 One local bank dealer said the market remained volatile, reflected by a wide spread and perception that the turbulence was not over yet although the rupiah had recovered somewhat. 

 Dealers said the spillover triggered operators to buy swaps, whose rises were limited because the market had been long. 

 One-month swap was at 18.0/20.0, two at 37.0/42.0, three at 60.0/66.0 and six at 118.0/125.0 points. 

 "The tone is also biddish on longer-term swaps. But short-term swaps are cheap due to ample rupiah supply," one said. Overnight swap was at 0.1/0.3 and tom/next at -0.1/par. 

 Overnight rupiah closed at 13.0 percent after the central bank raised its one-to-two day bilateral papers (SBIs). 

 The central bank continued to keep short-term rates high to reduce speculative dollar buying using cheap rupiah. 

 Dealers said the bank raised overnight SBIs rates to 13.0 percent from 12.0 percent and that for two-week papers to eight percent from 7.5 percent. 

 The bank kept all other rates unchanged. 

 The bank offered five-to-six day SBIs at 12.0 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent. 

 One market analyst said there was still a lot of volatility in the market and it was difficult to read whether any move in the market was based on flows or real corporate orders. 

 One dealer said earlier if the rupiah could break the 2,500 resistance level, then there was potential for a strong comeback. But if it fell below the 2,600 level, speculators would launch an attack to test the band again. 

 The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,549/2,597 on Wednesday from 2,576/2,624 on Tuesday.

title: Indonesia  Rupiah Rebounds 2.1% Late;  Intervention  Confirmed
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's rupiah made a significant rebound versus the U.S. dollar in trading late Tuesday, buoyed by Bank Indonesiaintervention and profit-taking from local and offshore investors, dealers said. 

 The U.S. unit is being bought at 2,580 rupiah in the spot market at 0904 GMT (5:04 a.m. EDT), a 2.1% fall from Monday's close of 2,635 rupiah. 

 The dollar has now fallen significantly back from the weak end of the rupiah's trading band, which is currently set from 2,378 rupiah to 2,682 rupiah. The market, however, is still struggling to find its own trading range, with dealers offering a wide band of 2,560 rupiah to 2,620 rupiah for near term transactions. 

 Bank Indonesia confirmed intervening on in the one-month forward market to support the rupiah. The central bank's foreign exchange director Djakaria told Dow Jones that Bank Indonesia wanted to see the dollar fall below the 2,600 rupiah support level. Dealers said the move was effective, eventually leading the dollar down to the 2,580 rupiah level. 

 Traders note that speculators are likely to take a more cautious approach toward the rupiah ahead of an Asia Pacific central bankers meeting to be held in Shanghai on Friday, July 25. Depending upon the results of the meeting, dealers say another speculative attack against the rupiah could take place - although it's doubtful. 

 'I personally see the market returning to the rupiah's fundamentals,' said a Singapore-based rupiah trader at a European bank. 'On this basis, the rupiah shouldn't be trading this week. I see it strengthening to the 2,500 rupiah level.' 

 On the swap markets, the overnight rupiah Jakarta Interbank Offered Rate moved down to around 13% from 15% earlier Tuesday.

title: Bk  Indonesia / Intervening  -2: Wanted To Break 2,600 Rupiah
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, confirmed that it intervened in the currency market Tuesday by selling the U.S. dollar in the one-month forward swap market. 

 The head of Bank Indonesia's Foreign Exchange Department, Djakaria, told Dow Jones that the intervention was done in order to help push the dollar below its support level of 2,600 rupiah in the spot market. 

 'The dollar seemed to be supported at 2,600 rupiah,' Djakaria said. 'We helped the market to push the dollar down (through 2,600 rupiah). We hope the intervention will also calm down the market.' 

 Djakaria, however, declined to disclose the value of its transaction. 

 After closing Monday's trading at 2,635 rupiah, the dollar dipped to a low of 2,569.50 rupiah in the spot market at 0633 GMT (2:33 a.m. EDT) following Bank Indonesia's intervention. It has since strengthened to its current level of 2,583 rupiah at 0710 GMT.

title: Indonesia: Shrs End Sharply Lower; Rupiah Concerns Persist
text:
JAKARTA (Dow Jones)--The Jakarta Stock Exchange (JSX) index ended 11.598 points, or 1.6% lower at 712.402, Monday as a wave of panic selling hit the market over the fall in the value of the rupiah versus the U.S. dollar,. 

 Losers lead gainers 113 to 38, with 55 stocks unchanged. Volume stood at 204 million shares valued at 394 billion rupiah, according to a local securities company. 

 A dealer said the sharp fall in the rupiah has hurt sentiment on the equities market. 

 Following the current rising trend in the dollar, some investors switched out of their stock portfolios to buy dollars. This pushed the share index to a lower close, market participants said. 

 'After Thailand and the Philippines, the Indonesian currency is under pressure,' which caused foreign fund managers to release their holdings of the rupiah and locals followed suit, another dealer said. 

 The rupiah touched an all-time-low of 2,662.50 against the dollar at 0407 GMT (12:07 a.m. EDT) Monday. 

 By 0925 GMT (5:25 a.m. EDT), the rupiah stood at 2,637.50 rupiah against dollar amid rumors that Indonesia's central bank has been intervening to support the rupiah. 

 Dealers said the declining trend on the JSX index will depend on the movement of the rupiah. 

 If the rupiah stages a recovery, the stock market could perform better Tuesday, a dealer said. 

 Market leader PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia fell 100 rupiah to 3,925 rupiah on 3.8 million shares traded. Cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakasa lost 200 rupiah at 4,250 rupiah on 2.2 million shares traded.

title: Indonesia Rupiah/Amplifier -2: Domestic Hedging Drives Mkt
text:
Indonesian companies with large foreign currency borrowings or that have large import requirements would be most exposed to the rupiah's plunge. Local banks or financial institutions were also hedging against a rupiah drop. 

 'There was a tremendous amount of hedging going on in Indonesia,' said a Singapore-based foreign exchange director at a major European bank. 'And as often the case, if a currency is going to break it will happen from domestic forces. The power of hedge funds is limited.' 

 Analysts say they are unsure to what extent major Indonesian corporates are hedged, but Monday's action suggests many still needed to put such protection in place. 

 The action was also reflected in swap rates. Although rupiah liquidity remained adequate at the short end, swap rates rose substantially in the longer tenors as Indonesian banks sought to cover their short dollar positions, both in the spot market and through forwards. U.S. dollar/rupiah one-month swap rates rose to 35/40 rupiah late Monday from 20/24 rupiah early in the day. 

Currency dealers said Bank Indonesia was sighted intervening Monday to defend the currency - even though the central bank has indicated previously it would only need to intervene at the limits of the trading band. 

 One local trader said he was receiving rupiah buy orders from Bank Indonesia at 2,650 rupiah/dollar, while another said he received orders to buy rupiah in the three-month and six-month forward markets. Bank Indonesia didn't, however, resort to significantly increasing its money-market rates. 

 Despite the potential threat to its currency trading band, analysts said Bank Indonesia's move earlier this month to widen the rupiah trading band - in the midst of currency turmoil elsewhere in Asia - has been shown as farsighted. 

 By pre-emptively widening its currency trading band to 12% from the previous 8%, the central bank avoided the need to spend billions of dollars defending the rupiah - since the currency's move Monday would have burst the limits of the old 8% band. 

 Bank Indonesia's foreign currency reserves stood at $21 billion at the end of May, good for 5.6 months of imports. Though that's healthy in comparison with the Philippines, recent events have shown that speculative attacks can quickly push reserve levels down to unacceptable levels. 

 The Bank of Thailand, with reserves of more than $30 billion, was forced to abandon its defense of the baht earlier this month.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Plunge Puts Cntrl Bk In Dilemma: Amplifier
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank's relative isolation from Southeast Asia's currency turmoil ended abruptly Monday with a wicked 5.7% plunge in the rupiah, its steepest one-day fall ever. 

 The rupiah's fall buffeted Jakarta's stock market, with the key market index closing 1.6% lower, and is forcing financial analysts to re-evaluate Indonesia's economic prospects. And with the weak end of the rupiah's trading band now less than 40 rupiah away, Bank Indonesia is now grappling with the same dilemma already faced by its humbled Asean neighbors - whether to draw a line in the sand and try to stop a further weakening in its currency. 

 Many currency analysts doubt that the central bank would be able to defend its present currency band for long. 

 'Bank Indonesia said it would defend the rupiah (at the weak end of the band), but this probably isn't sustainable,' said Rajeev Malik, regional economist at Jardine Fleming in Singapore. 'Either they will have to widen the band again, or possibly not announce a new band but still allow the rupiah to fall to a speculative attack.' 

 Bank Indonesia set its intervention band Monday at 2,378 rupiah to 2,682 rupiah. Malik said Bank Indonesia could possibly widen the band to as much as 20% from its current level of 12%. 

 The dollar's rise Monday was fast and furious, jumping more than 100 rupiah to an Asian close of 2,645 rupiah, up from 2,510 rupiah at the close Friday. The rupiah weakened as far as 2,662.50 rupiah per dollar Monday, a drop of 5.7%, before reports of Bank Indonesia intervention caused it to rebound from its lows. 

 The rupiah has now fallen nearly 12% since the beginning of the year, well above Bank Indonesia's 'managed depreciation' target of 4%-5%. 

 But unlike selling pressures on the rupiah last week - said largely to be from offshore speculators - Monday's fall came largely from domestic players, dealers said. Panicked with the prospects of accumlating massive foreign exchange losses, locals move quickly to cover their rupiah exposure.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Plunges 5.4% Vs Dlr; Nears Weak End Of Band
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's rupiah plunged 5.4% versus the U.S. dollar in trading Monday due to heavy selling pressure coming both from domestic corporations and offshore speculators, dealers said. 

 Monday's plunge places the Indonesian currency now less than 40 rupiah away from the weak end of the central bank's intervention band, and sparked reports of Bank Indonesia, the nation's central bank, buying rupiah in the spot and forward markets. 

 Dealers said they expect the dollar to trade higher again Tuesday as speculators test the weak end of the rupiah band which increased by one rupiah Monday to 2,378 rupiah to 2,682 rupiah. 

 The U.S. unit is being bought at 2,645 rupiah in the spot market at 0912 GMT Monday (5:12 a.m. EDT), after closing Friday at 2,510 rupiah. 

 'The central bank has committed to intervene, and it appears that speculators will see if they can take them out,' said the head of foreign exchange dealing at a European bank in Singapore. 'They have already done it in Thailand and the Philippines.' 

 Traders see strong support for the dollar now at 2,630 rupiah with a resistance level squarely set at the weak end of the intervention band, 2,682 rupiah. 

 Dealers noted that Bank Indonesia's short-dated money market rates trended upwards Monday, in line with a central bank move to defend the currency.

title: Indonesian rupiah weakens on dollar short-covering.
text:
JAKARTA, July 16 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the U.S. currency on short-covering in dollars in moderate early trading on Wednesday , dealers said. 

 One U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah strengthened at the opening to 2,453 from 2,455 and the New York closing of 2,458/59, but slid back to 2,457/78 at 0225 GMT. 

 "I think it's a combination of dollar short-covering ahead of Thursday's public holiday and ample liquidity," the dealer said, adding volume was relatively high. 

 All markets will be closed on Thursday for the birthday of Prophet Muhammad and reopen on Friday. 

 Dealers said trading was not as dramatic as Monday, but the market remained edgy on on-going volatility in the region. 

 They said operators were not fully comfortable and remained cautious of a possible spillover if sentiment changed. 

 However, one Japanese bank dealer said spreads were narrowing, suggesting improved confidence in the market. 

 "There is good demand from both local and foreign side but supply is also sufficient. People don't want to be caught too long or too short if other markets turn naughty on Thursday," another dealer said. 

 Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,455.25/56.50 and 2,454.75/56.00, respectively. 

 Liquidity was ample for now, with overnight rates traded at around 8.0/9.0 percent in the morning. Overnight swap was at 0.3/0.4 and tom/next at 0.6/0.7 points. 

 The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates were edging up after easing at the opening, suggesting some volatility remained. 

 But he said local operators were taking profits on foreign selling, limiting sharp declines in swap premiums. 

 Offshore operators had stocked up rupiah with swaps previously to prepare for a possible squeeze by the central bank to fend off speculation. 

 But the bank had pursued an unchanged monetary policy, generating arbitrage opportunity for local players with cheap rupiah funds to fill foreign appetite for swaps. 

 "Now local players are cashing out and limited a quick adjustment in swap rates," one Japanese bank dealer said. 

 He said offshore operators had to lift swap prices higher before they could unload their positions, otherwise the losses were too large.

title: Indonesian rupiah stable as swaps up slightly.
text:
JAKARTA, July 15 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in calmer late trading on Tuesday but swap premiums edged up on offshore purchases, dealers said. 

 One Japanese bank dealer said the market was calmer as offshore players re-entering the longer-term swap market. 

 "Some are looking for good levels to sell the dollar. I think the rupiah could stage a gradual recovery when the regional markets calm down," the dealer said. 

 "But some offshore players are buying longer-term swaps, causing rates to increase slightly from early lows," he said. 

 But the dealer said some offshore players might have to boost swap rates because they were too long in the swap market. 

 "I don't think they can cut their heavy long positions now. They have to raise them to higher levels before they could sell. Otherwise the losses are too large," he said. 

 One local bank dealer said local players were seen delivering the amounts needed by those offshore because they could make good profits out of arbitrage from the money market. 

 He said money market rates were so low that local players could fill the offshore appetite for swaps.

title: Indonesia's rupiah feels regional heat.
text:
JAKARTA, July 14 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah was on a roller-coaster against the dollar on Monday morning, rattled by continued speculative attacks on other regional currencies. 

Currency dealers said the rupiah was not a direct target of fund managers but was affected by the attacks on the Malaysian ringgit and the Philippine peso. 

 Spot rupiah weakened to an intra-day low of 2,469.0 per dollar on Monday morning from an opening of 2,453.0 before it recovered to 2,445.0 and settled at 2,455.0 around midday. 

 "For the rupiah, the issue is definitely the spillover from the peso and the ringgit," Edwin Png, country treasurer of Bank of America, told Reuters. 

 "It's not because of the fundamentals of the rupiah," he said, adding that fund managers were taking advantage of Southeast Asian currency movements. 

 "They want to buy it up as high as possible. But the rupiah situation is not that bad because the central bank only widened the band last week," Png said. 

 Bank Indonesia, the central bank, surprised the market on Friday by widening the dollar-rupiah band to 12 percent from eight percent following recent de facto devaluations of the Philippine peso and the Thai baht. 

 The move helped the rupiah strengthen briefly to 2,410.0 on Friday but it gave up ground to close at 2,438.0 a dollar in Jakarta as speculators maintained their assault on regional currencies. 

 Friday's widening was the eighth since 1992. The bank widened its band to 2,374-2,678 rupiah to the dollar. 

 Since 1992, Bank Indonesia has widened the intervention band in steps to give more room for price fluctuations to absorb external and internal shocks. 

 "They are smart to do that. Fortunately, they didn't let it float like the peso and just widened the band," Png said, adding a float could have a wider impact on the rupiah. 

 However, economists remained comfortable with the rupiah's levels. 

 Daragh Maher, an economist at ING Barings, said earlier any effect on the rupiah due to a spillover from other currencies would be short-lived. 

 He said stable economic growth, the long-term nature of the country's foreign debt and controllable short-term private debt were among the factors helping to shield the rupiah from speculation. 

 Png said the top side of the dollar was expected to be at the 2,470 level because of overseas selling interest. 

 "If you take the depreciation, it's very small compared to other currencies," he said. He added the turbulence could last for a couple of weeks but was confident of Bank Indonesia's ability to handle the situation. 

 "I think the central bank is very well prepared compared to other central banks. They are more controlled in the sense that for the past 12 months the rupiah was always under attack." 

 "The market is somehow already used to that. The central bank is already used to that, unlike others," Png said. 

 "Somehow the economy is not really out of hand. I think they are doing a good job so far to control the economy and also the currency movement."

 He said stable economic growth, the long-term nature of the country's foreign debt and controllable short-term private debt were among the factors helping to shield the rupiah from speculation. 

 Kobus van der Waht, regional treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore, told Reuters Financial Television the band widening was a pre-emptive move. 

 "Bank Indonesia doesn't want to be part, or doesn't want to be in the same trap as happened in Thailand and to an extent in the Phillippines over recent weeks or months," he said. 

 "Taking pre-emptive action (on band) and saying the past policy of depreciation is very much intact. 

 "Decision making is over to the market and there is not going to be a situation where a specific level is defended at the cost of losing very valuable reserves," van der Waht said. 

 Png said the top side of the dollar was expected to be at the 2,470 level because of overseas selling interest. 

 "If you take the depreciation, it's very small compared to other currencies," he said. He added the turbulence could last for a couple of weeks but was confident of Bank Indonesia's ability to handle the situation. 

 "I think the central bank is very well prepared compared to other central banks. They are more controlled in the sense that for the past 12 months the rupiah was always under attack." 

 "The market is somehow already used to that. The central bank is already used to that, unlike others," Png said. 

 "Somehow the economy is not really out of hand. I think they are doing a good job so far to control the economy and also the currency movement."

title: Indonesian rupiah recovers at close, swaps lower.
text:
JAKARTA, July 14 (Reuter) - The rupiah recovered against the dollar and swap rates fell in late trading after being jolted earlier on regional currency volatility, dealers said. 

 One U.S. bank dealer said the market seemd to quiet down, with the Indonesian currency seen recovering from a morning assault, while swaps also dropped across the board. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,445.0/50.0 at 0915 GMT. The rupiah fell to an intra-day low of 2,469.0 from an opening of 2,453.0 before it bounced back to 2,445 and settled at 2,455 at midday. 

 "It's volatile day. You are either making or lost a lot of money with this jumpy market," the U.S. bank dealer said. 

 The dealer said swap premiums fell sharply from early high levels as the currency was driven into turbulence. 

 One-month swap fell later to 20.0/25.0 from 28.0 points, two to 41.0/51.0 from 55.0/60.0, three to 60.0 from 80.0 and six to 115.0 from 140.0 points. 

 The U.S. bank dealer said state banks were seen initiating another wave of dollar selling in late afternoon which saw some follow-through from offshore operators. 

 "They also launched broad swap selling with the rupiah flush in the money market," he said, adding that overnight rates nose-dived to four percent from 20 percent. 

 The dealer said this suggested the central bank was comfortable and had no plan to squeeze the market or take other action. 

 One Japanese bank dealer said he could not predict where the rupiah rates were heading in the very short-term because the regional environment was still so uncertain. 

 "There is no clear trend in the market. We are too much exposed to the region," one Japanese bank dealer said. 

 "But I think the present levels in the spot and swap markets could not hold on for long. They are not at equilibrium levels," he said. 

 "I think the situation is short-lived and will be subject to a correction once things settle down," he said, adding the current spot and swap levels were in equilibrium. 

 The central bank offered repurchase of one-week papers at 13.75 percent which helped banks with SBI certificates. 

 The bank also offered seven-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at seven percent, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent, three- and six-month at 10.50 and 11.25 percent and one-year at 12.0 percent. 

 The Japanese bank dealer said there was also no indication of a dollar tightening in the overnight market. 

 "Dollars are abundant in the market. Overnight rates are hovering at around 5.75/6.00 percent which are quite normal." 

 Dealers said the market did not react to a statement by State Secretary Murdiono who said a wider dollar-rupiah intervention band was to strengthen the Indonesian economy. 

 "Our economic fundamentals are strong. The decision to widen the intervention band will make the economy even stronger," he told reporters. 

 "What we decided on Friday is a precautionary step. We are aware of attacks from everyhwere, but any speculation on the rupiah will fail," Murdiono said. 

 Bank Indonesia, the central bank, surprised the market on Friday by widening the dollar-rupiah band to 12 percent from eight percent following recent de facto devaluations of the Philippine peso and the Thai baht. 

Currency dealers said the rupiah was not a direct target of fund managers but was affected by the attacks on the Malaysian ringgit and the Philippine peso. 

 Kobus van der Waht, regional treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore, told Reuters Financial Television that Friday's surprise move had certainly given a signal. 

 "Bank Indonesia doesn't want to be part, or doesn't want to be in the same trap as happened in Thailand and to an extent in the Phillippines over recent weeks or months," he said. 

 "Thereby basically taking pre-emptive action (on band) and saying the past policy of depreciation is very much intact. 

 "Decision making is over to the market and there is not going to be a situation where a specific level is defended at the cost of losing very valuable reserves," van der Waht said. 

 He said the market will not run away and investors, speculators and participants generally were giving Bank Indonesia the benefit of the doubt. 

 "They have been ahead of the curve in the past following a very prudent depreciation policy over many years and I thnk that is now giving them a big favour," van der Waht said. 

 He said there could be some rupiah weakening as one could expect in a nervous environment but not a run-away situation. 

 Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,375/2,679 and the conversion band to 2,433/2,481 on Monday.

title: Indonesia Widens  Currency 's Trading Band After Manila's Move
text:
JAKARTA -(Dow Jones)- Bank Indonesia Friday widened its dollar-rupiah intervention band to 12% from 8%, creating even greater flexibility to its exchange-rate mechanism. 

 The head of the Foreign Exchange Department of Bank Indonesia, Djakaria, said that the intervention band is now set 2,374 rupiah to 2,678 rupiah to the dollar. Prior to the widening, the band was at 2,430 rupiah to 2,622 rupiah. 

 Bank Indonesia's move followed the Philippine central bank's move earlier Friday to widen its own currency trading band. The Philippine peso has been under attack from foreign-exchange speculators in recent weeks, following a move by the Bank of Thailand to float the baht July 2. 

 Unlike the Philippine government's move, however - which caused the peso to fall over 10% in trading Friday - the Indonesian rupiah lost only about 0.5% in volatile trading, ending trading in Asia at 2,445.50 rupiah to the dollar, down from 2,432.75 rupiah Thursday. 

 The rupiah has been virtually free from speculative attacks over the last two months, while neighboring currencies in Thailand, the Philippines, and Malaysia have been battered. All three countries have been forced to shell out billions of dollars defending their currencies, while Bank Indonesia has been able to stay comfortably on the sidelines. 

 The fact that Bank Indonesia took the prudent steps last year to widen the rupiah's trading band to 8% from 3% had been a major reason for the rupiah's stability. By removing itself from regulating the rupiah's value, Indonesia's central bank effectively transferred the risk to the market. 

 Market players said the bank's move was pre-emptive, and that by widening the rupiah's trading band to virtually a free float, offshore speculators will find it harder to galvanize a concerted attack against the rupiah. 

 "Bank Indonesia made a very smart, prudent policy move by deciding to widen and caught most in the market off guard," Daniel Lian, the head of currency and fixed-income research at NatWest Markets in Singapore, said. "With over a 300 (rupiah) band to deal with, I don't know how offshore players could effectively launch a cohesive attack." 

 Traders pointed to Indonesia's stronger economic fundamentals - as well as its already flexible currency band - as the reason for the rupiah's strength to date. Friday's move continued a liberalization of Indonesia's exchange-rate mechanism that economists had been hoping for. 

 "Pressure was building up against the rupiah, though many see Indonesia as a much different story than Thailand," Lian said. "But with the Philippines and Thailand out of the way, it wasn't impossible speculators would focus on Indonesia." 

Currency analysts noted that in a tightly regulated currency system - such as those previously held in Thailand and the Philippines - speculators can easily coordinate attacks against currencies as they know exactly the level to go in at and where central bank support will be. A wider band, however, offers that much more uncertainty for any speculator, and that much more risk. 

 "It is nearly impossible to speculate with a 12% band, as traders have to drive down the value that much more to see profits," said Neil Saker, Singapore-based economic research head at Socgen-Crosby Securities.

title: Indonesia/Rupiah Calm -2: Proactive Economic Policies
text:
The currency band has been widened in stages from as little as 2% in late 1995. Despite a slew of political shocks in the interim - such as rioting in the capital last year and concerns over President Suharto's health - the central bank has been able to keep the currency comfortably within the band. Usually it has traded near the stronger end. 

 'When traders look at the rupiah, they see it at the strong end of the band, with 8% downside, that's a lot of risk' for a speculator, Belchere said. 'No one is willing to bet on that.' 

 The same kind of prompt action has been seen on the economic policy front. 

 The Bank of Thailand resisted floating the baht because of fears of the effects a currency depreciation would have on the financial sector, already suffering from excessive lending to the depressed property sector. 

 Bank Indonesia, in contrast, has been much more proactive in stemming excessive property speculation and in limiting offshore borrowing by Indonesian companies - though economists concede that some pressures remain. 

 In response to growing concerns over property lending, Bank Indonesia Monday put a moratorium on lending to property companies engaged in land purchases or land development. And Bank Indonesia Governor Soedradjad Djiwandono said Wednesday that the country's tight monetary policies will remain in place. 

 That has helped Indonesia avoid the kind of currency volatility, and the need for regular market intervention, that has been seen in Malaysia, for example. 

 Bank Indonesia's stated policy of depreciating the rupiah by about 5% per year allows investors to know exactly where the market is headed. 

 'It's normally a severe punishment when Bank Negara (Malaysia) intervenes in the market - they always do it aggressively and market participants get bruised,' said Pardi Kendy, head of the treasury at PT Bank Buana Indonesia. 'It's the opposite script in Indonesia. The rupiah is very stable and the central bank has never been harsh to market players.'

title: Indonesia Rupiah Calm Amid Sea Of  Currency  Speculation
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Amid a wave of speculative attacks on the neighboring currencies of Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines during the past few months, the Indonesian rupiah has enjoyed a pleasant respite. 

 As the Thai baht has plunged in the wake of Thailand's July 2 decision to float the currency, both the Malaysian and Philippine currencies have come under renewed attack, prompting central bank intervention and interest rate hikes to defend them. 

 But Bank Indonesia, the central bank, has been able to stay on the sidelines. A chart of the dollar/rupiah rate since early June is more or less flat - a period of extreme turbulence in the other Southeast Asian currencies. 

 Indeed, with the dollar currently at 2,431.23 rupiah, the Indonesian currency is very close to the strongest level it can reach within the central bank's current trading band of 2,430 to 2,622 rupiah. 

 The reason? Strong economic fundamentals, for one, foreign exchange traders say, as well as prompt steps by the central bank to head off worries about economic overheating. But maybe even more important has been Bank Indonesia's well-timed moves to widen the rupiah's trading band and thus take a less prominent role in guiding the currency's day-to-day movements. 

 'Indonesia has listened to its advisors and instituted some extremely prudent moves regarding its exchange rate mechanism,' said Bill Belchere, head of fixed-income research at Merrill Lynch & Co. in Singapore. 'At 8%, they now have one of the most flexible exchange rate systems in the region, which has put them in extremely strong position.' 

 The trading band was widened to 8% in September, from the previous 5%. 

 There has been some speculation recently that the band will be widened further, though many economists say that's unlikely since it would probably only encourage further rupiah strength. 

 The central bank has a policy of depreciating the rupiah by around 5% annually in order to encourage non-oil exports. So far this year, the currency has fallen 2.8%.

title: Indonesian rupiah stable after Thai shock.
text:
JAKARTA, July 2 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Wednesday after the market recovered from an early shock generated by turmoil in the baht. 

 Thailand set a fresh foreign exchange policy on Wednesday by letting its currency float against the dollar, prompting a slew of baht selling and sending jitters through the region. 

 However, the rupiah emerged unscathed from the turbulence, staging a strong comeback with an upward trend. 

 Dealers said the market shrugged off a possible spillover effect as economists hailed strong fundamentals shown by the country's latest macroeconomic indicators. 

 Spot rupiah, due next Monday following a public holiday in the United States on Friday, was quoted at 2,433.0/33.25 against the dollar at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,432.5/33.5. The rupiah tumbled to a low of 2,445 on selling by offshore players on rumours of a baht devaluation. It recovered after Thailand announced its managed float policy. 

 Analysts said the Indonesian economy was stronger than that of Thailand, with the country enjoying a healthy trade surplus, sufficient foreign exchange reserves, a manageable current account deficit, low inflation and an eight-percent central bank intervention band. 

 They said those indicators helped the central bank to comfortably absorb external shocks and internal uncertainty induced during the May general elections. 

 "I am quite surprised how well the rupiah held up," said Daragh Maher, an economist at ING Barings, adding that previous pressures on the rupiah were election-related. 

 "Over the last two to three months when other currencies in the region were under a lot of pressure by virtue of the baht, actually the pressure we have seen on the rupiah had been more election-related," Maher said. 

 He said with the election out of the way people were more comfortable with rupiah risk and that helped explain the relatively strong rupiah performance. 

 Economists said the rupiah might gradually drift towards the strong end of the central bank's intervention band when the Thai baht settles. 

 One U.S. bank dealer said there was also speculation in the market of a possible dollar-rupiah band widening ahead of the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) donor meeting in Tokyo later this month. 

 The World Bank, which coordinates the CGI, said in a report on Indonesia last month that some countries had a wider intervention band but did not specifically suggest that Jakarta follow suit. 

 But central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said it was not good sense to follow what other people were doing. 

 "This kind of argument is weak. That is not good economic policy that just because other poeple have 15 percent we have to go to 15 percent," Djiwandono said. 

 Dealers said the rupiah remained firm, also shrugging off excess rupiah supply in the money market. Overnight rates fell to four percent from 11.0/12.0 percent in the morning. 

 Dealers said overnight dollars had also stabilised to six percent. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,432.00/32.35 and 2,433.5/34.00, respectively.

title: Indonesia Central Bank  Won't Widen  Intervention  Band Soon
text:
WASHINGTON (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank is unlikely to widen the intervention band for the rupiah in response to the recent steady depreciation of the local currency, according to Bank Indonesia governor Soedradjad Djiwandono. 

 In an interview with Dow Jones last week, Soedradjad countered recent market speculation that rupiah weakness could give the central bank room to expand its currency intervention band, currently 8%. 

 Some analysts argue the rupiah weakness gives the central bank a window of opportunity to widen the band, without triggering the capital inflows and rupiah appreciation that accompanied the band widenings last year. 

 The central bank is well on track to achieve its policy of depreciating the rupiah by 3-5% annually, in order to help the country's non-oil exports. That may give it room to widen the band still further, some analysts say. 

 But Soedradjad says that isn't the case. 

 'I don't want to rock the boat when things are working. I know that this has been the concern of the markets,' Soedradjad said. 

 Interviewed in Washington during the spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, Soedradjad emphasized that he is happy with the rupiah's band as things stand. 

 Just because the rupiah has already fallen substantially in 1997, it doesn't mean that 'we have to jump now' to widen the currency band, Soedradjad said. 'It's not as mechanistic as that,' the governor added. 

 The dollar started 1997 at 2,365.00 rupiah but has risen to trade at 2,427.75 rupiah at present, a rupiah depreciation of around 2.6% and somewhat faster than the central bank's target. The intervention band for the rupiah is currently set between 2,407 to 2,599 rupiah per dollar.

title: Indonesian rupiah weakens in late trading.
text:
JAKARTA, April 23 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar late on Wednesday on high liquidity and worries over the coming election campaign, dealers said. 

 One U.S. bank dealer said reports of a strike by some 10,000 workers under contract to Nike Inc and flush rupiah supply in the afternoon boosted sentiment on the U.S. currency. 

 Some 10,000 of the 13,000 workers at a factory under contract to Nike marched from their plant in Tangerang on Jakarta's outskirts to the local parliament on Tuesday to demand a wage increase. They were granted a pay rise after staging a mass strike and protest, Antara news agency reported. 

 "The tone is still biddish on the dollar. But there is a lot of fight at the 2,420 level," the dealer said.

 One currency dealer in Singapore said the tone seemed to be biddish on the dollar, with the brief response to the Nike demonstration reflecting only general caution ahead of the campaign starting on Sunday for the May 29 elections. 

 The rupiah strengthened briefly in the morning following a report in a local daily quoting a university professor and an unnamed official as saying the central bank was planning a band widening in the near future. But the report was later ignored by the market as operators switched focus to politics. 

 A noted economist said the central bank was unlikely to widen its band in the short- or medium-term because there was no fundamental reason to back it up at present. 

 "The rate is hovering at a healthy level below the mid-rate of the intervention band and moderately higher than the floor rate. I don't see any reason to act now," the economist said. 

 He said the central bank had implemented a new reserve rate of five percent only last Wednesday which should help contain money supply growth, which exceeded targets in 1996. 

 The economist said there was no immediate reason to act and the effect of the new reserve rate had to be disgested first. 

 "Political issues are taking the lead for now. People are worried over possible riots and things like that as we enter the campaign period," the Singapore dealer said.

title: Indonesian rupiah volatile on band and politics.
text:
JAKARTA, April 23 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah was volatile against the dollar in moderate trading at midday on Wednesday, dealers said. 

 They said the rupiah strengthened at mid-morning following a report in a local daily quoting a university professor and an unnamed official as saying the central bank was planning a band widening in the near future. 

 Spot rupiah rose to a high of 2,417.5 from an opening of 2,418.5/19.5 on the back of the report, but was later ignored by the market as operators switched focus to politics. 

 A noted economist said the central bank was unlikely to widen its band in the short- or medium-term because there was no fundamental reason to back it up at present. 

 "The rate is hovering at a healthy level below the mid-rate of the intervention band and moderately higher than the floor rate. I don't see any reason to act now," the economist said. 

 He said the central bank had implemented a new reserve rate of five percent only last week which should help contain money supply growth, which exceeded the government target in 1996. 

 The economist said there was no immediate reason to act and the effect of the new reserve rate had to be digested first. 

 Meanwhile, operators switched focus to political issues as the campaign for general elections on May 29 will start Sunday. 

 One currency dealer in Singapore said the tone had turned biddish for the dollar after the lunch-break. 

 "Political issues are taking the lead for now. People are worried over possible riots and things like that as we enter the campaign period," the dealer said. 

 Spot rupiah weakened to 2,420.0/21.0 at 0545 GMT. 

 One local bank dealer said there could be more upside for the dollar after it broke the resistance level of 2,420.0. 

 Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,403/2,595 and the conversion band at 2,403/2,451 on Tuesday.

title: Indonesian rupiah stable in range trading.

title: Indonesian rupiah weakens on dollar short-covering.
text:
JAKARTA, April 17 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in late trading on Thursday following some short-covering in the U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 "I think it's mainly short-covering which is driving the dollar higher. We haven't heard anythin yet in the market," one currency dealer in Singapore said, adding some dollar buying at the London opening helped push the rate up further. 

 Spot rupiah fell to 2,412.0/12.5 at 0840 GMT from an opening of 2,407.75/08.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,411.75/12.25 and 2,407.75/08.50, respectively. 

 Dealers said the sudden dollar upturn was not linked to a small protest by supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri as there was no violence. 

 About 100 supporters of Megawati marched one km from the office of her chief lawyer to the Central Jakarta State Court to lodge a lawsuit against her ouster. 

 One local bank dealer said excess rupiah supply in the afternoon seemed to have aided increased dollar buying. 

 Overnight money dropped to seven percent from 14.0 percent at the opening. 

 "Operators tend to go slightly long over the extended weekend. They just want to play safe," the dealer said. The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday. 

 He said short-covering by both local and foreign players boosted the dollar and sustained a bullish dollar tone. 

 "Sentiment now appears to be bullish on the dollar. It might proceed until the election," another said. Indonesia will hold general elections on May 29. 

 Dealers were cautious in the morning, one day after a new bank reserve requirement rate of five percent was made effective. 

 But the market appeared to be flush on ample central bank supply and on adequate anticipation by banks. The central bank announced the new requirement last year.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals mixed in thin trade.
text:
SINGAPORE, April 16 (Reuter) - Regional currencies were mixed on Wednesday with trading subdued ahead of the 0930 GMT speech by Eisuke Sakakibara of Japan's Ministry of Finance. 

 The Indonesian rupiah firmed slightly against the dollar after a weaker open, with the focus on liquidity due to the new bank reserve requirement rate, effective on Wednesday. 

 Dealers were worried whether the market could absorb the fall-out of the new reserve rate, which is estimated to drain between five and eight trillion rupiah from the system. 

 "We feel a light increase in rupiah demand. But dollar supplies seem to be enough," a Japanese bank dealer said, adding he did not detect any rush to buy today dollars. 

 "We saw some uptrend in the morning. Overnight money is crawling up, thus driving the dollar a bit lower," a dealer based in Jakarta said. 

 "We haven't got a clear picture yet. People are trying to test the market first," he said, adding that early injection of 3.359 trillion rupiah by the central bank helped calm operators. 

 At 0400 GMT, spot rupiah was at 2,407.75/08.25 compared with an opening of 2,407.5/08.5. 

 Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band to 2,401/2,449 on Tuesday. 

 Dealers in Singapore pegged rupiah support and resistance at 2,407 and 2,408.75 to a dollar. 

 The Thai market resumed trading after a four day public holiday but a directionless dollar/yen market limited trading. 

 The Thai baht weakened against the dollar as the greenback made marginal gains against the Japanese currency, dealers said. 

 At 0400 GMT, the baht was at 26.084/089 a dollar against 26.067-26.072 late on Friday. 

 The central bank set the midrate at 26.09 baht per dollar. 

 "There may be little selling (of baht) this morning because people think the dollar trend is going stronger against yen," said a dealer at Siam City Bank Plc. 

 Liquidity was expected to tighten as banks prepared to meet central bank reserve requirements on April 22 and finance firms were due to meet their reserve requirements on Thursday. 

 Ringgit sales from U.S. funds pushed the ringgit to test 2.5120 for a second time, but dollar sales from Kuala Lumpur prevented a decline, dealers said. 

 "Some people are simply buying up dollar/ringgit. It seems like someone is building a huge position against ringgit since last week," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore. 

 He said some U.S. funds, mostly margin players, were involved in the dollar accumulation. "The position could be a few yards (billion dollars)," he added. 

 Ringgit hit a low of 2.5140 a dollar overnight on selling in London, but fell back on rumours that Bank Negara was selling dollars, dealers said. About $30-40 million was traded. 

 "Stop-losses at 2.5120 increased activity in London time and brought down dollar/ringgit," a Malaysian bank dealer said. 

 Singapore dollar was range-bound at 1.4405/35 to the U.S. currency. One chartist said if the Singapore dollar were to breaks 1.4450, 1.4530 would be re-tested.

title: Indonesian rupiah softens, swaps ease on liquidity.
text:

title: Indonesian rupiah firms on liquidity concerns.
text:
JAKARTA, March 25 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in active late trading on Tuesday on concerns over money market conditions, dealers said.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Flat Early; Looking For  Central Bank  Move
text:

title: Indonesian rupiah stable after discount rate cut.
text:
JAKARTA, March 12 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate early trading on Wednesday following a cut in a key discount rate, dealers said. 

 "The cut surprised the market but many operators had already expected the discount rate cut to take place in February or March after a cut in December," one state bank dealer said. 

 Bank Indonesia on Wednesday cut its key discount rates for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points for all maturities. 

 Spot rupiah was generally stable and was last quoted at 2,395.75/96.25 at 0340 GMT from 2,395.80/96.80 at the opening.

 The dealer said the discount rate cut had been expected following recent declines in rates of SBIs (securities issued by the central bank to absorb liquidity). 

 "The cut has been expected after months of generally ample rupiah liquidity and declines in SBI rates" another dealer said. 

 One Japanese bank dealer said the discount rate cut did not have an immediate impact on the rupiah as it was generally stable. 

 Dealers said the SBPU cut was seen as a signal from the central bank that interest rates were expected to be on the downward trend in the future. 

Central bank director C. Harinowo told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday that the discount rate cut decision was based on an improved outlook inflation in Indonesia. 

 Dealers said the rate cut, however, was not likely to push the rupiah further down, as demand for the local currency was expected to strengthen ahead of financial year reporting session in late March.

title: Indonesia's Rupiah -2: 1.511 Tln Rupiah Injected
text:

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht eases on dollar gains.
text:
* Thai baht eases on dollar's overnight gains versus majors. Positive economic data underpins currency, keeping it below central bank's mid-rate. 

 * Singapore dollar remains soft but subdued after overnight sales on news of Brunei finance minister's resignation. 

 * Malaysian ringgit under pressure from dollar's rise. 

 * Indonesian rupiah driven by liquidity conditions. 

 SINGAPORE, Feb 27 (Reuter) - The Thai baht subsided in line with the dollar's overnight gains versus the majors following comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan suggesting a U.S. interest rate hike might be in the offing. 

 The baht was quoted at 25.893-25.898 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 25.842/25.852 late on Wednesday. 

 But dealers said it remained below the central bank's daily fixing of 25.91 for most of Thursday's morning session after the Finance Ministry leaked relatively positive economic data on Wednesday. 

 "I believe the baht is now returning to its normal footing, tracking the dollar/majors. The data yesterday might be viewed by some as still depressing. But if you put it into context, it showed a positive trend," said a UK bank dealer in Bangkok. 

 The data showed Thailand's December trade deficit narrowed to 22.3 billion baht from 24.2 billion baht in November. 

 The Finance Ministry said exports growth for 1996 contracted 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent contraction forecast by the Bank of Thailand earlier. 

 An SBC Warburg analyst said the chance that investors might be moved into a baht selling spree again was minimal after the ministry's release of the data. 

 The central bank is due to officialy release its key economic indicators on Thursday at 0800 GMT. 

 "I see this as an improvement. Of course, some investors might want to see the trade deficit narrow because of strong improvement in exports rather than of the substantial drop in imports. But at the end of the day, it is the trade balance figure that affects the currency." he said. 

 "And I don't think any speculator who recently took losses from the Bank of Thailand's intervention will have more risk appetite to speculate on baht devaluation again soon," he said. 

 Elsewhere, the Singapore dollar remained under pressure after reaching an overnight low of 1.4280 to the U.S. dollar. 

 Dealers said funds had sold the Sing dollar following news that Brunei's Finance Minister had resigned and been replaced by his brother, the Sultan of the tiny oil kingdom. 

 The news spurred speculation Brunei might want to weaken its currency or de-link it from the Singapore dollar, dealers said. 

 "There were rumours Brunei wanted to bring up its non-oil exports. One way to do that would be to weaken the Brunei dollar, which is pegged against the Sing dollar," said a local bank dealer. 

 He said there was some buying of dollar/Sing by interbank players in the morning but it looked capped near its overnight highs. "There's no real interest from customers. They're probably all speculative buys," he said. 

 Dealers said the dollar/Sing was likely to trade a 1.4240-1.4290 range for the day. It was quoted at 1.4267/77 at 0405 GMT. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit remained under pressure from the dollar's overnight rise but dealers said strong dollar selling interest around the 2.4925 level would limit the ringgit's fall. 

 The ringgit was quoted at 2.4833/43 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 2.4810/20 at its Kuala Lumpur close on Wednesday. 

 "Dollar/ringgit's looking biddish after last night. But it'll probably trade a 2.4840-2.4900 range today," said a Singapore-based dealer. 

 The Indonesian rupiah was easier as the market continued to focus on liquidity conditions in the absence of other leads. 

 Spot rupiah was at 2,391.5/92.0 at 0405 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,391.0/92.0. 

 Dealers said short-term swaps fell, while longer-term rates were stable, suggesting the temporary nature of the current ample conditions. 

 Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,381/2,573 and the conversion band 2,381/2,429 on Wednesday after raising them by one point on Tuesday.

title: Indonesia Rupiah Up Vs. Dlr On Central Bk Widening Rumors

title: Indonesian rupiah weakens on ample liquidity.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 23 (Reuter) - The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in volatile early trading on Thursday on the back of excess rupiah supply, dealers said. 

 But some foreign bank dealers said there could be a light spillover from early turbulence in the Thai currency market.

title: Central Bank  defies rumours of rupiah band change.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 13 (Reuter) - Indonesia's central bank continued to defy foreign speculation on a widening of the rupiah's intervention band and snapped up dollars to keep the rupiah from rising too high, currency dealers said on Monday. 

 Offshore currency operators had bought rupiah on Friday, speculating that a widening of the intervention band was imminent. Past widenings of the band had caused the rupiah to appreciate sharply. 

Currency dealers said the speculation continued on Monday. 

 "It's less vigorous than Friday, but enough to maintain upward momentum for the rupiah," one currency dealer said. 

 At 0850 GMT, spot rupiah fall back slightly to 2364.40/5.40, after opening on Monday at 2,363.75/64.10. 

 The central bank raised its intervention band by one point late on Monday to 2,364/2,556. 

 The intervention band is an optimal rupiah-dollar exchange range set daily by the bank. If the rupiah rises or falls out of the band, Bank Indonesia intervenes in the foreign exchange market to keep the currency stable. 

 The band has become the market focus since the central bank widened its band to eight percent from five percent last September. 

Currency dealers in Jakarta said the central bank was estimated to have absorbed at least $1.1 billion last Friday to keep the rupiah from rising out of the intervention band. 

 They said the impact was felt in the market, with swap premiums tumbling across the board on expectation of ample rupiah liquidity on Tuesday induced by central bank dollar-buying. 

 Swap rates are premiums which allow operators to roll over positions established in the cash market. 

 One local bank dealer said offshore operators were still challenging the central bank on Monday to widen its band after they failed last Friday. 

Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono shrugged off market speculation last week by saying monetary policy would be kept flexible and adjusted whenever necessary. 

 However, he also said the rupiah exchange rate would be kept at a realistic level without anti-export bias. 

 Dealers said there were rumours in the market that the central bank might try to teach speculators a lesson by tightening the allocation of central bank papers (SBIs) this week. 

 SBIs are central bank instruments used to tighten liquidity in the money market and are also options for offshore investors to park their funds temporarily. 

 "If the rumours come true, people with ample rupiah might be squeezed if they haven't placed their rupiah yet. Interbank rates this morning have given the signals," the dealer said. 

 He said he doubted offshore operators had found alternate rupiah investments, which may result in further roll-overs of existing short dollar positions. 

 "This is a tug-of-war. I don't know how long they can hold. They are now being squeezed on the swap side," he added. 

 The dealer said some offshore operators appeared to have given up for now, which was reflected in the dollar's slight recovery since Friday. 

 The dollar dropped three points below the central bank intervention band last Friday on heavy band speculation. 

 Dealers said offshore operators might be forced to buy back dollars if they started to calculate the value of their speculation. 

 Dealers said offshore operators were seen mainly sustaining short dollar positions as reflected in declining tom/next swap rates, which were traded below par levels. 

 "If they can't find adequate rupiah investments and cannot get out of the swap market, they will buy back," another said. 

 Dealers in Jakarta said offshore operators seemed to be trying to launch another attack on the band by spreading rumours of a band widening on Wednesday. 

 They said Wednesday was selected as the day because some players usually went short on dollars on Wednesdays and bought them back on Thursdays to enjoy weekend rupiah premiums.

title: Speculation on Indonesia's rupiah band continues.
text:
JAKARTA, Jan 10 (Reuter) - Speculation on another widening of the Indonesian central bank's dollar-rupiah intervention band lifted the rupiah against the dollar in volatile Friday trading, currency dealers said. 

 They said many operators shrugged off the speculation but offshore fund managers kept unloading dollars which led some players to believe a widening was imminent. 

Central Bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono was close-mouthed on the issue when he met reporters and bankers this week. 

 "Our monetary policy is eclectic and pragmatic. We keep adjusting whenever it is necessary. But I can't say when it's necessary," he said on Wednesday. 

 "Our policy is flexible. I can't take the mystery out from the market," he added. 

 "The rupiah exchange rate will be maintained at a realistic level without anti-export bias," Djiwandono told bankers at an annual bankers' dinner hosted by the central bank on Wednesday. 

 A state bank economist said the governor's explicit comments were sufficient to indicate an imminent widening was unlikely. 

 "A band widening now would strengthen the rupiah further which is then violating the export policy," the economist said. 

 Market analysts said, however, that "creative currency players" had spread rumours. Market talk had ranged from a band widening on Friday afternoon, to imminent action because the bank was holding a meeting, and a news conference had been called. 

 The central bank denied any meeting was in progress or that a news conference was planned. 

 The rupiah, meanwhile, continued to appreciate. 

 It surged to a high of 2,359.0 to the dollar at midday, four points outside of the Bank Indonesia's intervention band of 2,363/2,555 set on Friday. 

 The central bank intervenes in the foreign exchange market to stabilise the rupiah if the dollar-rupiah rate moves outside of the intervention band, which is set by the bank on a daily basis. Many currency dealers in Jakarta said they did not believe the central bank would bow to market pressure. 

 Dealers also noted that shrinking interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah, due to declining Indonesian inflation, suggested the potential for a narrowing of the intervention band. 

 The central bank had also said short-term capital inflows of less than one year, accounted for only five percent of the total capital inflow of $10.5 billion in 1996. 

 Dealers said rumours of a band widening had been in the market since October after currency dealers were caught by surprise by the central bank's unexpected move in September. 

 Bank Indonesia widened the band to eight percent from five percent on September 11, after widening it to five percent from three percent on June 13. 

 Since then, dealers have consistently speculated on another widening because of sustained capital inflows, due to interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah.

title: Indonesia/Dlr-Rupiah Trading Band -3: Aware Of Rumor
text:
Speaking at a seminar, Soedradjad added that he is aware of the rumor being spread around the market that Indonesia's central bank will widen the band soon. 

 'It's the game that financial analysts and players are playing now,' he stated. He added that such a rumor has made some players confused and suffer losses. 

 'But that's the nature of the game: someone's gain is other people's loss. What we want is for someone's gain not to be Bank Indonesia's loss,' he said. 

 Soedradjad, however, said that Bank Indonesia will widen the band again when it thinks it is necessary. 'We are not going to do that if we think it isn't necessary yet,' he stated. 

 Soedradjad outlined that one of the purposes of widening the dollar-rupiah trading band is to protect foreign exchange reserves from the volatility in the currency market. 

 Bank Indonesia has had to intervene in the past when the dollar was trading beyond the trading band. It had to intervene by selling the dollar three times last year when the dollar traded above the upper-end of the trading band. 

 At that time, the spread of the trading band was only 44 rupiah. The first intervention was in January 1995 following the crisis of Mexico's peso. The second intervention was in April 1995 as the yen's sharp rise against the U.S. dollar was seen inflating Indonesia's foreign debt. The third one was in August 1995 when the rupiah was attacked by unfounded devaluation rumors. 

 But so far this year, Soedradjad said Bank Indonesia has not had to sell the dollar to the market, thanks to a wider trading band. He said such an intervention was not necessary although the rupiah was under great pressure against the dollar in July following news of President Suharto's health and political riots in Jakarta on July 27. At that time, the spread of the trading band was 116 rupiah.

title: Indonesia says  forex  band widening helps debt.
text:
JAKARTA, Nov 26 (Reuter) - Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Tuesday the widening of the central bank's dollar-rupiah trading band was positive for foreign debt payments. 

 "The strengthening of the rupiah does not put a burden on our principal and interest debt payments. The effect was instead positive because we only need less rupiah to repay debts," Mar'ie told parliament. 

Indonesia widened its dollar-rupiah trading band, or so-called intervention band, to eight percent in September from five percent. This band allows the central bank to intervene in the foreign exchange market if the rate falls outside its limits. 

 The band widening had caused the rupiah to strengthen sharply against the dollar in the past. 

 The World Bank has previously said Indonesia's foreign debt stands at about $100 billion.

title: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals ease on dollar strength.
text:
* Regional currencies under pressure from dollar rise versus majors after news of Italy's re-entry into Exchange Rate Mechanism. 

 * Indonesian rupiah eases on ample liquidity, with upward pressure seen. Support pegged at 2,344/45 and resistance at 2,347/48. 

 * Baht hit by firmer dollar/majors. Support seen at 23.443/44. 

 * Malaysian ringgit eases on heavy dollar/mark buying by U.S. funds. 

 SINGAPORE, Nov 25 (Reuter) - Regional currencies were hit by the dollar's gains against the majors on Monday after news of Italy's re-entry into the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM). 

 In Indonesia, dealers said ample liquidity also weighed on the rupiah, causing players to buy the dollar and sell forward swaps down. 

 Spot rupiah fell to 2,346.00/47.00 at 0450 GMT from the open of 2,343.50/44.50 on sustained bullish dollar sentiment. 

 Overnight swap declined to 0.22/0.26 from 0.25/0.35 points on flush money market liquidity, dealers said. 

 One local bank dealer in Jakarta said cheap local funds continued to sustain further buying interest in the dollar. 

 "The buying is seen driven mainly by local operators, which forces offshore operators to reduce short dollar positions," he said, adding that the momentum was still prevalent. 

 "We are now some points above the central bank band. There is more room to trade now. We believe the central bank would not widen the band in the medium-term," the dealer said. 

 One economist said earlier the present central bank depreciation policy suggested that it did not plan to widen its band in the medium-term. 

 Offshore operators had been putting pressure by going short on the dollar, triggering speculation of another band widening by the central bank on the back of heavy capital inflows. 

 But the central bank has been resisting the pressure and had even challenged the market. 

 The local bank dealer said he would maintain a long dollar position as long as the central bank maintained its three- to four point rupiah depreciation each week. 

 Another dealer said operators were also seen buying dollars in anticipation of narrowing interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah after the central bank seemed to loosen its monetary policy recently. 

 Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,340/2,532 and the conversion rate to 2,340/2,388 on Friday. 

 In Thailand, concern over the new finance ministry post weighed on the baht. It was quoted at 25.443-25.447 to the dollar at 0450 GMT. 

 Dealers said dollar/baht was likely to be dictated by the dollar/majors, mainly the dollar/mark after mark/lira weakened on Italy's re-entry into the ERM. 

 They said the market ignored the Thai central bank governor's call on banks to cut their minimum loan rates to boost the economy, but instead focused on the new cabinet lineup. Activity was also driven by this month's reserve requirement. 

 "Banks began to keep funds for the next reserve requirement. The interbank rate is likely to stand above 10 percent this week," said one dealer at a foreign bank in Bangkok. 

 "I think the market is expecting liquidity to tighten due to the maintenance period and this is supporting the six month-forward rate at the 44/45 level," a Singapore dealer said. 

 In Malaysia, the ringgit broke out of its recent range to head south on heavy dollar/mark buying in early Tokyo, dealers said. 

 They said the ringgit was just tracking the trend in major currencies and was likely to ease further. 

 "There is too much pressure. It is hard to be short dollar this morning," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore. 

 Dealers said the dollar faced resistance at the 2.5220 level, which if broken, could see the ringgit falling to 2.5280. 

 "Ringgit is expected to retreat for a while, if not today, in the next few days. So it is a good opportunity to buy dollars at any dip," a dealer with a Kuala Lumpur bank said. 

 At 0450 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5235/45 to the dollar against 2.5194/04 late on Friday.

 Singapore's Economic Development Board said on Monday evening the city-state's total manufacturing output fell an unexpected 7.6 percent year-on-year in August, far worse than analysts had forecast. 

 The data encouraged several economists to revise downwards their forecasts for the country's economic growth for the year, with some saying growth may be around 6.5 percent in 1996 from 8.8 percent in 1995. 

 "This morning there was a knee-jerk reaction to the overnight data showing an industrial production decline," said a Singapore-based dealer. "But the U.S. dollar was never able to challenge the 1.4120 level and the Sing kept bouncing back." 

 One dealer said some major players appeared to be trying to push the Singapore dollar down below 1.4120 to try to trigger stop-loss selling. 

 "But there is some very big comercial buying at that level and the Sing looks well supported," he said. 

 The Malaysian ringgit was almost unchanged against its southern neighbour at 0.5642 Singapore dollars. 

 "Manufacturing figures were down, so they were buying ringgit and selling the Sing," said a Kuala lumpur-based U.S. bank dealer. 

 Against the U.S. dollar, the ringgit was at 2.5010/20, almost unchanged from its local close on Monday. 

 "On dollar/ringgit, we saw some people trying to push it below the 2.50 level, but quite a lot of buying interest came into the market every time it got there," said another. 

 Dealers said the ringgit was likely to stay within a fairly narrow 2.4990-2.5040 range until the release sometime over the next two weeks of Malaysia's trade figures, widely expected to show a surplus. 

 The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar in slow early trading. 

 One local bank dealer said some offshore operators were trying to push the dollar down at the opening but met strong support at the 2,321.25 level, which helped the dollar rebound to the 2,321.75/22.25 level. 

 Spot rupiah was traded at 2,321.30/1.80 at 0430 GMT against an opening of 2,322.50/23.00. 

 "The pressure was short-lived. Somebody wanted to test the downside but support was strong for the dollar because of the central bank's floor rate," the local bank dealer said. 

 Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,318/2,510 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,318/2,366 on Monday. 

 A dealer in Singapore said the bank was expected to raise soon the floor of its intervention rate further to 2,322. 

 The Thai baht edged up to 25.437-25.442 to the dollar by 0430 GMT, from 25.451-25.454 late on Monday but still appeared to be headed down. 

 "It appears some foreign funds began to flow out after (the) recent sell-off in the stock market," said one currency dealer. 

 The Thai stock index has fallen by 14 percent over the past five trading sessions as foreign funds reduce their investment weight on Thai shares by selling off most blue-chip bank and finance stocks, analysts said. 

 Dealers said dollar buying in the early morning was also because the U.S. unit was believed to have reached its support level against other major currencies.

title: Indonesian rupiah returns to favour with investors.
text:
JAKARTA, Sept 12 (Reuter) - The high-yielding Indonesian rupiah is once again returning to favour among emerging market currencies after the central bank's loosening of intervention controls, foreign exchange analysts said on Thursday. 

 The rupiah, which surged sharply against the dollar on Wednesday after Bank Indonesia widened the intervention band to eight percent from five percent, ticked up slowly on Thursday and analysts saw more rises in coming months. 

 The rupiah jumped to 2,326 against the dollar on the central bank announcement on Wednesday from an opening of 2,349 before settling back at about 2,330. On Thursday, it was trading at about 2,325.50/6.00 in the late afternoon. 

 "A lot of people are establishing outright positions," said Edwin Png, country treasurer at Bank of America. "A lot of hot money is coming in. Look at the problems in Thailand. Where else can you put your money? 

 "I thing the rupiah is still very attractive to foreign investors." 

 The central bank's new band, which marks the perimeters outside of which it will intervene in the market, was set at 2,309/2,501 on Wednesday and analysts said they saw the rate creeping to the lower end of the band by the end of the year. 

 "Right now, the market has room to play," said Jimmy Koh of the I.D.E.A. economic consultancy. "In the longer term, we see the rate heading back toward the lower end of the band. Perhaps by the end of the year. 

 "Further measures to liberalise rupiah movement and introduce a managed float can be expected over the medium term to avoid the problem of the spot rate converging with the lower end of the intervention band," Koh added. 

 "This merely reaffirms our preference for long rupiah positions, which now offer capital gains on top of a highly attractive (yield)." 

 Bank Indonesia said it widened the intervention band to contain the overheating economy and control capital inflows. 

 "It is an open question whether a wider band will be any more effective at slowing inflows (or curbing their effect) this time than in the past," said Peregrine Fixed Income in a commentary received by Reuters. "Unless the band is continuously widened, it has only a temporary effect. Nor have past band widenings appeared to have struck much fear into the hearts of foreign investors." 

 The rupiah has been in a continuous uptrend since the beginning of the year except for slight hiccups in June on unfounded rumours that President Suharto had suffered a heart attack and again in July when riots broke out in Jakarta. 

 But sentiment on the currency has been restored after Suharto made a trip to Germany where doctors gave him a clean bill of health and the crackdown in the aftermath of the riots. 

 The strengthening, however, appears to have scuppered Bank Indonesia's stated target of depreciating the rupiah by five percent annually to help exports, analysts said. 

 Peregrine estimated that the rupiah would need to depreciate at an annual rate of 8.15 percent from now until April 1 to achieve a four percent depreciation over the 1996-97 (April-March) fiscal year. 

 Koh said Indonesian authorities needed to look to other measures to boost exports. 

 "For the export side we believe the government will probably (need to) introduce more deregulation", he said. "Export competitiveness needs more than just a weakened rupiah. They've got to deal with the structural problem."

title: Rupiah jumps after Indonesia's surprise move.
text:
JAKARTA, Sept 11 (Reuter) - The rupiah rose sharply against the dollar on Wednesday after Indonesia's central bank suprised the market and widened its intervention band for the second time this year. 

 The widening effectively gives the market more flexibility to set its own rate, a move which met with approval as the rupiah soared against the dollar immediately after the announcement. 

 Spot rupiah soared to a high of 2,326.0 against the dollar by midday, compared with an opening of 2,348.50/49.50. At 0919 GMT, it was quoted at 2,329.00/31.00 

 The rupiah was fixed by the central bank at 2,309/2,501 rupiah against the dollar on Wednesday against 2,344.0/2,462.0 on Tuesday, or a spread of eight percent against five percent. 

 The central bank said in a statement obtained by Reuters that the move was in line with policies to contain a overheating economy, to reduce speculative trading, to strengthen the ability of the bank to control currency fluctuations and to give more solid ground for monetary control. 

 The band, fixed daily by the central bank, sets the limits outside of which the central bank will intervene in the foreign exchange market. 

 "The timing caught the market by surprise," Edwin Png, country treasurer of Bank of America, told Reuters. 

 "It shows that the central bank has the determination to let the market decide what is the right level of the currency." 

 He added that that the central bank was quite encouraged by the last move since the market had been trading within the band. Bank Indonesia last widened its intervention band in June this year to five percent from three percent after the rupiah came under persistent upward pressure. 

 "I think the market is mature enough to accept this. The market is pretty professional in that there was not much panic after the announcement," Png said. 

Currency dealers said Wednesday's rise was in line with gains after previous widenings of the intervention band. They said prevailing market sentiment that the rupiah was a high-yielding currency also helped the gains. 

 Png said the rupiah was likely to remain strong until the end of the year because of its attractive yield compared with Thailand's baht or other regional currencies. 

 The central bank also announced that that banks' minimum reserve requirement ratio would be increased to five percent from three percent, effective April 16, 1997. 

 The reserve requirement is the amount of deposits banks must place with the central bank. Bank Indonesia last raised its reserve requirement to three percent from two percent in February. 

 The central bank said all other existing reserve requirements would remain unchanged, including calculations and reporting methods. 

 It said the increase in the reserve ratio and the widening of the intervention band would enable the government to contain loan growth and overall liquidity in the market as well as increase the effectiveness of monetary management.

title: Indonesia central bank  widens  intervention  band.

 The expiration of Bank Indonesia certificates, Sertifikat Bank Indonesia (SBI), added 835 billion rupiah into the system. However, the expiration of the money market certificates, Surat Berharga Pasar Uang (SBPU), absorbed back 141 billion rupiah, in addition to 400 billion rupiah through the settlement of new SBIs. 

 The overnight Jakarta Interbank Offered Rates (JIBOR) early Thursday fell slightly to 13% from 14.5% Wednesday, dealers said. 

 Meanwhile, the premium of the dollar-rupiah swaps early Thursday slid to 0.55/0.60 from 0.60/0.65 Wednesday, dealers added. 

 Bank Indonesia left unchanged its dollar-rupiah indication rate at 2,324 rupiah - 2,370 rupiah, and its intervention band at 2,324 rupiah - 2,442 rupiah. Bank Indonesia late Wednesday cut both the indication rate and trading band by one rupiah following the dollar's slide against the other major currencies.

title: Indonesia  Central Bank / Forex  -2: Political Concerns Seen
text:
JAKARTA (AP-Dow Jones)--Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, hasn't intervened in the foreign exchange market to support the rupiah despite some weakness in the currency, J. Soedradjad Djiwandono, governor of Bank Indonesia, said Tuesday, according to the state news agency Antara. 

 Indonesia's rupiah fell nearly 1% last Friday following reports that President Suharto would fly to Germany for medical examinations of his heart and kidney. 

 'The situation (in Indonesia) is safe, and even on Monday the situation is better,' Soedradjad said.
